js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\nA comprehensive template for AI-driven JavaScript/TypeScript development with full CI/CD pipeline support.\n\nThis repository publishes the real test package\n`@link-foundation/example-package-name` so the template release pipeline is\nvalidated end to end with npm trusted publishing.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Multi-runtime support**: Works with Bun, Node.js, and Deno\n- **Universal testing**: Uses [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) for cross-runtime tests\n- **Automated releases**: Changesets-based versioning with GitHub Actions\n- **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Docker images can be published after the matching npm version is visible\n- **Universal app example**: React UI for the package API with GitHub Pages, Electron, and Capacitor build paths\n- **Code quality**: ESLint + Prettier with pre-commit hooks via Husky\n- **Package manager agnostic**: Works with bun, npm, yarn, pnpm, and deno\n- **Broken link checks**: Automated link validation with [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action) and Web Archive fallback suggestions\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Using This Template\n\n1. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `package.json` with your package name and description\n4. Install dependencies: `bun install`\n5. Start developing!\n\n### Development\n\n```bash\n# Install dependencies\nbun install\n\n# Run tests\nbun test --timeout 30000\n\n# Or with other runtimes:\nnpm test\ndeno test -A --parallel\n\n# Lint code\nbun run lint\n\n# Format code\nbun run format\n\n# Check all (lint + format + file size)\nbun run check\n\n# Build the universal React example app\nnpm install --prefix examples/universal-app\nnpm run example:web:build\nnpm run example:desktop:package\n\n# Try the CLI locally\nnode bin/example-package-name.js add 2 3\n```\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .changeset/           # ESLint configuration\n├── .prettierrc           # Prettier configuration\n├── bunfig.toml           # Bun configuration\n├── deno.json             # Deno configuration\n└── package.json          # Node.js package manifest\n```\n\n## Design Choices\n\n### Multi-Runtime Support\n\nThis template is designed to work seamlessly with all major JavaScript runtimes:\n\n- **Bun**: Primary runtime with highest performance, uses native test support (`bun test`)\n- **Node.js**: Alternative runtime, uses built-in test runner (`node --test`)\n- **Deno**: Secure runtime with built-in TypeScript support (`deno test`)\n\nThe [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) framework provides a unified testing API that works identically across all runtimes.\n\n### Package Manager Agnostic\n\nWhile `package.json` is the source of truth for dependencies, the template supports:\n\n- **bun**: Primary choice, uses `bun.lockb`\n- **npm**: Uses `package-lock.json`\n- **yarn**: Uses `yarn.lock`\n- **pnpm**: Uses `pnpm-lock.yaml`\n- **deno**: Uses `deno.json` for configuration\n\nNote: `package-lock.json` is not committed by default to allow any package manager.\n\n### Universal App Example\n\nThe template includes `examples/universal-app`, a Vite React app that imports\n`add` and `multiply` from `src/index.js` and renders a visual calculator UI.\nThe same static build is used by:\n\n- GitHub Pages (`npm run example:web:build`)\n- Electron desktop packaging (`npm run example:desktop:package`)\n- Capacitor Android/iOS sync (`npm run example:mobile:sync`)\n\nThe example app has its own `package.json` and lockfile so template users can\nopt into the frontend stack without adding React, Electron, or Capacitor to the\nlibrary package itself.\n\nSee [examples/universal-app/README.md](examples/universal-app/README.md) for",

[2026-11-01T11:23:13.751Z] [INFO]         "content": "286 /tmp/research-ui/associative-tech-stack.md\n# Associative technology stack\n\nFormal AI stores inspectable knowledge as a links network with Links Notation as its portable text representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In\n`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument\nvector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.\n`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded\nexecution timeout and process cancellation. This is the execution boundary for\nexternal agent commands; it does not itself provide reasoning or link storage.\nThe manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native\nhost facility, not a browser subprocess API.\n\n### `web-capture`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under\n`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in\n`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and\n`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.\nThis supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;\nfailed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.\n\nThe browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture\nadapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base\n(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall\nback to a direct CORS fetch. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. [2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+former local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+import/export projection. Its",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+transitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+reasoning layer.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### `links-notation`",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### `command-stream`",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+vector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+The manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+host facility, not a browser subprocess API.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### `web-capture`",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+This supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+failed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+The browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+adapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+back to a direct CORS fetch. The adapter preserves the target status and bytes,",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+including target HTTP errors; a target error must not be misrepresented as a",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+successful discovery. This browser HTTP boundary is distinct from compiling the",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+native Cargo dependency into WASM.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### `web-search`",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository: [link-assistant/web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search)",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+There are two direct package integrations, with versions governed by their",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+respective manifests:",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- Native: `rust/Cargo.toml` declares `web-search` without default features and with",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  `merge`, under `cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` converts provider rankings to `SearchResult`,",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  configures `MergeOptions` with the shared reciprocal-rank-fusion constant and",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  calls `web_search::merger::merge_results`.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- JavaScript: `package.json` declares `@link-assistant/web-search`.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  `js/web-search-component-entry.js` imports and actually calls",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults`. Its merge uses reciprocal rank",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  fusion and duplicate removal; its HTTP adapter supplies captured pages.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Search discovers candidate evidence; capture obtains it; ranking merges the",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+candidates. Formal AI still owns the reasoning and verification needed to turn",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+those observations into supported statements. Neither package substitutes for",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+that reasoning, proves the content true, or provides a link-store dependency.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+## Architecture and protocol components",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+These repositories explain protocol lineage, compatibility, or design context.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Unless a component is explicitly described as a direct dependency above, it is",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+not linked into the Formal AI runtime.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### Browser storage: `doublets-web`",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### Query dialect supplied by `link-cli`",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+links the Rust library in-process and does not launch an external CLI binary.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### Reasoning model: `relative-meta-logic`",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Repository:",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+is the architectural reference, not a linked crate.",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+code is not linked into the Formal AI runtime.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+## Development and orchestration components",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+These tools exercise or coordinate the system during development. They are not",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+The Agent CLI is an external development-time client for OpenAI-compatible",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+prove that the symbolic agent loop can inspect a worktree, call tools, edit",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+### Hive Mind",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+Hive Mind is development-time orchestration around issue-solving agents and",

[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+the system being driven. Hive Mind does not participate in knowledge storage,",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+parsing, reasoning, or responses in a shipped Formal AI process.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+## Keeping this map accurate",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+When an integration changes, update this guide from executable evidence:",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- `Cargo.toml` and its feature table define Rust runtime dependencies;",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- `package.json` defines the web bundle's direct packages;",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- `rust/src/link_store.rs`, `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, `rust/src/document_formats.rs`,",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  `rust/src/calculation.rs`, `rust/src/main.rs`, and `js/i18n.js` show the integration",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  boundaries; and",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+- compatibility or conceptual repositories must remain in the architecture",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+  section until their code becomes an actual manifest dependency.",
[2026-11-01T11:23:20.461Z] [INFO]                 "+",

[2026-11-01T11:24:16.475Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Associative technology stack\n\nFormal AI stores inspectable knowledge as a links network with Links Notation as its portable text representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In\n`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument\nvector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.\n`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded\nexecution timeout and process cancellation. This is the execution boundary for\nexternal agent commands; it does not itself provide reasoning or link storage.\nThe manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native\nhost facility, not a browser subprocess API.\n\n### `web-capture`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under\n`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in\n`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and\n`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.\nThis supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;\nfailed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.\n\nThe browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture\nadapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base\n(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall\nback to a direct CORS fetch. The adapter preserves the target status and bytes,\nincluding target HTTP errors; a target error must not be misrepresented as a\nsuccessful discovery. This browser HTTP boundary is distinct from compiling the\nnative Cargo dependency into WASM.\n\n### `web-search`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search)\n\nThere are two direct package integrations, with versions governed by their\nrespective manifests:\n\n- Native: `rust/Cargo.toml` declares `web-search` without default features and with\n  `merge`, under `cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`.\n  `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` converts provider rankings to `SearchResult`,\n  configures `MergeOptions` with the shared reciprocal-rank-fusion constant and\n  calls `web_search::merger::merge_results`.\n- JavaScript: `package.json` declares `@link-assistant/web-search`.\n  `js/web-search-component-entry.js` imports and actually calls\n  `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults`. Its merge uses reciprocal rank\n  fusion and duplicate removal; its HTTP adapter supplies captured pages.\n\nSearch discovers candidate evidence; capture obtains it; ranking merges the\ncandidates. Formal AI still owns the reasoning and verification needed to turn\nthose observations into supported statements. Neither package substitutes for\nthat reasoning, proves the content true, or provides a link-store dependency.\n\n## Architecture and protocol components\n\nThese repositories explain protocol lineage, compatibility, or design context.\nUnless a component is explicitly described as a direct dependency above, it is\nnot linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n### Browser storage: `doublets-web`\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)\n\n`doublets-web` is the browser-side Links Platform store and a compatibility\ntarget, not a bundled JavaScript dependency. `js/memory.js` uses an\nIndexedDB implementation with the same event-to-doublets projection and reports\nthe `doublets-web` backend when a compatible global runtime is available. This\nkeeps browser data portable without claiming that the upstream package is\nalways loaded.\n\n### Query dialect supplied by `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nBesides the native storage APIs used directly above, `link-cli` defines the\nlink query and substitution command conventions. Formal AI adapts those\nconventions in `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `rust/src/links_substitution_query/`; it\nlinks the Rust library in-process and does not launch an external CLI binary.\n\n### Reasoning model: `relative-meta-logic`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic)\n\nRelative Meta Logic models claims relative to contexts instead of forcing one\nglobal truth value. Formal AI has an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/relative_meta_logic.rs`, integrated with `rust/src/world_model.rs` for\ncontext-relative facts, contradictions, and queries. The upstream repository\nis the architectural reference, not a linked crate.\n\n### Conceptual model: `meta-theory`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-theory](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory)\n\nMeta Theory is a conceptual foundation for describing languages and theories as\ndata. It informs Formal AI's data-first approach to rules, syntax, and\nreasoning, but there is no `meta-theory` runtime dependency in the manifests.\n\n### Transformation model: `transformer`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer)\n\nTransformer is a related model for graph transformations. Formal AI's current\nsubstitution engine is an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/substitution.rs`, where `.lino` rules match and rewrite link patterns on\nCRUD events. The repository is useful for comparison and vocabulary, but its\ncode is not linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n## Development and orchestration components\n\nThese tools exercise or coordinate the system during development. All language CI now uses the same entry workflow.\n\n![introduction](./docs/comparison/comparison.svg \"json, xml and lino comparison\")\n\nThis library gives you an ability to convert any string that contains\nlinks notation into a list of links and back to the string after\nmodifications are made.\n\nLinks notation is based on two concepts references and links. Each\nreference references other link. The notation supports links with any\nnumber of references to other links.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### C&#35;\n\n```csharp\nvar parser = new Link.Foundation.Links.Notation.Parser();\nvar links = parser.Parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\");\n```\n\n### JavaScript\n\n```javascript\nimport { Parser } from \"links-notation\";\nconst parser = new Parser();\nconst links = parser.parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\");\n```\n\n### Rust\n\n```rust\nuse links_notation::parse_lino;\nlet links = parse_lino(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\").unwrap();\n```\n\n### Python\n\n```python\nfrom links_notation import Parser\nparser = Parser()\nlinks = parser.parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\")\n```\n\n### Go\n\n```go\nimport lino \"github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/go\"\nlinks, _ := lino.Parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\")\n```\n\n### Java\n\n```java\nimport io.github.linkfoundation.linksnotation.Parser;\nParser parser = new Parser();\nList<Link> links = parser.parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\");\n```\n\n### PHP\n\n```php\nuse LinkFoundation\\LinksNotation\\Parser;\n$parser = new Parser();\n$links = $parser->parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\");\n```\n\n### C++\n\n```cpp\n#include \"links_notation.hpp\"\nstd::vector<links_notation::Link> links = links_notation::parse(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\");\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n### Links notation (lino)\n\n#### Doublets (2-tuple)\n\n```lino\npapa (lovesMama: loves mama)\nson lovesMama\ndaughter lovesMama\nall (love mama)\n```\n\n#### Triplets (3-tuple)\n\n```lino\npapa has car\nmama has house\n(papa and mama) are happy\n```\n\n#### Sequences (N-tuple)\n\n```lino\nI'm a friendly AI.\n(I'm a friendly AI too.)\n(linksNotation: links notation)\n(This is a linksNotation as well)\n(linksNotation supports (unlimited number (of references) in each link))\n(sequence (of references) surrounded by parentheses is a link)\nparentheses may be ommitted if the whole line is a single link\n```\n\n#### Indented Syntax\n\nLinks can also use indented syntax for better readability:\n\n```lino\n3:\n  papa\n  loves\n  mama\n```\n\nThis is equivalent to:\n\n```lino\n(3: papa loves mama)\n```\n\n#### Multi-line Groups\n\nA parenthesized group opens a *nested context*: its body starts fresh at\nindentation level zero and follows the same rules the root document does, so a\nline break inside parentheses is structure rather than decoration.\n\n```lino\nvalue (\n  id \"1\"\n  label \"one\"\n)\n```\n\nThis reads as `(value ((id 1) (label one)))` - two children, each a link of its\nown - and not as one flat list in which the boundary between `id` and `label`\nwould be lost. Indentation works inside a group exactly as it does at the root,\nand a body that stays on a single line still collapses to a single link, so\n`(a b c)` is unchanged.\n\nAll eight implementations agree on this. `experiments/issue-282/parity` parses\nthe document above with each of them and fails if any one reads it differently.\nThe complete rules are in the [grammar](docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md).\n\n#### Comments\n\nA `#` hides the rest of the line it stands on, so a document can carry prose\nabout itself:\n\n```lino\n# the machines this deploys to\ndeploy: staging # only staging, for now\n```\n\nThat is the single link `(deploy: staging)`: both comments are gone by the time\nthe document is read. A `#` only opens a comment where a reference could begin,\nso a `#` inside a token (`issue#1047`) and a `#` inside a delimited reference\n(`\"#\"`) stay ordinary characters.\n\nA formatter keeps the same rule from the other side: a reference that begins\nwith a `#` is written quoted (`'#tag'`), so a document it writes reads back as\nitself.\n\nComments are on by default in every implementation, and every parser can be\ntold to read `#` as an ordinary character again for documents written before\ncomments existed - see the parser options in the language READMEs.\n\nSo that means that *this* text is also links notation. So most of the\ntext in the world already may be parsed as links notation. That makes\nlinks notation the most easy an natural/intuitive/native one.\n\n## What is Links Notation?\n\nLinks Notation (Lino) is a simple, intuitive format for representing\nstructured data as links between ~~entities~~ references to links.\nIt's designed to be:\n\n- **Natural**: Most text can already be parsed as links notation\n- **Flexible**: Supports any number of references in each link\n- **Universal**: Can represent doublets, triplets, and N-tuples\n- **Hierarchical**: Supports nested structures with indentation\n\nThe notation uses two core concepts:\n\n- **References**: Points to other links (like variables or identifiers)\n- **Links**: Connect references together with optional identifiers\n\n## Streaming\n\nEvery maintained implementation can parse arbitrary chunks incrementally,\nincluding one-symbol and one-line chunks. A stream emits a top-level record only\nafter its indented children, multiline quoted references, and parenthesized\ncontexts are complete. The canonical parser validates each completed record, so\nstreaming and whole-document parsing have the same syntax and output.\n\n| Language | Push API | Lazy/native adapter |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| C# | `LinkParsed` event | `IEnumerable` / `IAsyncEnumerable` |\n| JavaScript | `link`, `error`, and `end` events | sync / async iterables |\n| Rust | link and error callbacks | `Iterator` |\n| Python | link callback | generator / async generator |\n| Go | callback and `io.Writer` | `iter.Seq2` |\n| Java | `Consumer<Link>` | `Stream<Link>` |\n| PHP | callable | `Generator` |\n| C++ | `on_link` / `on_error` callbacks | `ChunkedLinks` / `parse_chunks` |\n\nAll variants expose write/feed and finish operations, absolute position\ntracking, reset/drain controls, and an unresolved-record size limit. Collection\nis enabled by default; disable it when callbacks or lazy iteration should keep\nmemory bounded. See the [cross-language parity experiment](experiments/issue-197/README.md)\nand each language README for runnable examples.\n\n## Documentation\n\nFor detailed implementation guides and API references, see the\nlanguage-specific documentation:\n\n- **[C# Documentation](https://link-foundation.github.io/links-notation/csharp/api/Link.Foundation.Links.Notation.html)**\n  \\- Complete API reference\n- **[PDF Documentation](https://link-foundation.github.io/links-notation/csharp/Link.Foundation.Links.Notation.pdf)**\n  \\- Complete reference for offline reading\n- **[C# README](csharp/README.md)** - Installation and usage guide\n- **[JavaScript README](js/README.md)** - Modern web development guide\n- **[Rust README](rust/links-notation/README.md)** - High-performance parsing guide\n- **[Python README](python/README.md)** - Python package guide\n- **[Go README](go/README.md)** - Go package guide\n- **[Java README](java/README.md)** - Java/Maven package guide\n- **[PHP README](php/README.md)** - PHP/Composer package guide\n- **[C++ README](cpp/README.md)** - C++17/CMake library guide\n\nAdditional resources:\n\n- [Grammar](docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md) - The notation in EBNF, with the indentation\n  and nested context rules spelled out ([syntax diagrams](docs/grammar/syntax-diagrams.md))\n- [Test Case Comparison](TEST_CASE_COMPARISON.md) - Test-by-test coverage comparison across all eight language implementations\n- [Links Theory 0.0.2](https://habr.com/en/articles/895896/) - Theoretical\n  foundation that Links Notation fully supports\n\n## Test Coverage & Implementation Parity\n\nAll eight language implementations (C#, JavaScript, Rust, Python, Go, Java, PHP, C++) maintain\n**equivalent core functionality**, and the overlap is verified test by test rather than asserted:\n\n<!-- test-counts:start -->\n| Language | Tests | Test categories |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Python | 247 | 24 |\n| JavaScript | 316 | 29 |\n| Rust | 401 | 29 |\n| C# | 295 | 27 |\n| Go | 139 | 17 |\n| Java | 185 | 16 |\n| PHP | 235 | 23 |\n| C++ | 346 | 29 |\n<!-- test-counts:end -->\n\nThe table is written by `scripts/create-test-case-comparison.mjs`, which reads the test files\nthemselves and also produces [TEST_CASE_COMPARISON.md](TEST_CASE_COMPARISON.md) - the full matrix\nof which implementation has which test, each cell linking to the test. The `docs` workflow runs\nthat script with `--check` on every pull request, so a test added in one language and forgotten in\nthe others shows up as a gap in the matrix instead of as a README that quietly went stale. It used\nto be a hand-written list, and had drifted to six languages and six wrong counts.\n\n### Known Implementation Differences\n\nSome language-specific features are intentional:\n\n- **`LinksGroup`** - a parsed group of links kept as one object - exists in\n  [JavaScript](js/src/LinksGroup.js), [C#](csharp/Link.Foundation.Links.Notation/LinksGroup.cs),\n  [Java](java/src/main/java/io/github/linkfoundation/linksnotation/LinksGroup.java) and\n  [C++](cpp/include/links_notation/links_group.hpp). Python, Rust, Go and PHP expose the same\n  structure as nested `Link` values instead.\n- **Tuple conversion** - building a link from a language tuple - is offered where the language has\n  the syntax for it: [C#](csharp/Link.Foundation.Links.Notation/Link.cs) via implicit operators and\n  [Rust](rust/links-notation/src/lib.rs) via `From` implementations.\n\nThese differences are by design and do not affect core parsing/formatting functionality.\n\n## Binary links notation\n\nThe [version 1 specification](docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md) defines\nshared packets and a LiNo document mapping. JavaScript, Python, Rust, C#, Go,\nJava, PHP and C++ provide codecs beside their text parsers; all check the same [golden vectors](docs/protocol/binary-links-notation-vectors.txt).\nSee the [cross-language example](examples/binary/README.md) for encoding options\nand byte-for-byte interoperability.\n\nExact Unicode identifiers and values round-trip with the [reference literal contract](docs/protocol/reference-literals.md)\nintroduced in 0.24.0, including mixed quotes, empty strings, controls and multiline text.",

[Overview](#overview)\n2. [EBNF Grammar](#ebnf-grammar)\n3. [Grammar Explained](#grammar-explained)\n4. [Syntax Diagrams](#syntax-diagrams)\n5. [Examples](#examples)\n\n## Overview\n\nLinks Notation (Lino) is a simple, intuitive format for representing\nstructured data as links between references. The notation supports:\n\n- **References**: Simple identifiers, or quoted strings\n- **Links**: Connections between references with optional identifiers\n- **Nesting**: Parenthesized expressions for inline nesting\n- **Indentation**: Hierarchical structure through indentation\n- **Comments**: `#` hides the rest of the line it stands on\n\nExact Unicode references can use [version 1 UTF-8 hex literals](../protocol/reference-literals.md),\nintroduced in 0.24.0. The prefix `~[0-9]+{` is reserved at reference\nboundaries; quote an existing reference with that spelling.\n\n## EBNF Grammar\n\nThe following EBNF grammar formally defines the Links Notation syntax:\n\n```ebnf\n(* Links Notation (Lino) Grammar - EBNF *)\n(* Version: 0.24.0 *)\n\n(* === Document Structure === *)\ndocument            = skip_empty_lines, links, whitespace, EOF\n                    | whitespace, EOF ;\n\nskip_empty_lines    = { horizontal_whitespace, newline } ;\n\nlinks               = first_line, { line } ;\n\nfirst_line          = SET_BASE_INDENTATION, element ;\n\nline                = skip_empty_lines, CHECK_INDENTATION, element ;\n\nelement             = any_link, PUSH_INDENTATION, links\n                    | any_link ;\n\n(* === Comments === *)\n(* A comment is taken out before the rules above are applied: each of its\n   characters is replaced with a space, so what follows keeps the position it\n   was written at, and a line that held only a comment becomes whitespace *)\ncomment             = comment_start, { any_char - newline } ;\n\n(* Only a \"#\" at the start of the document or after a space, a tab or a line\n   break opens a comment *)\ncomment_start       = ? start of document ?, \"#\"\n                    | whitespace_char, \"#\" ;\n\n(* === Link Types === *)\nany_link            = nested_group, eol\n                    | indented_id_link\n                    | single_line_any_link ;\n\nsingle_line_any_link = single_line_link, eol\n                     | single_line_value_link, eol ;\n\n(* === Nested Groups (Parenthesized) === *)\n(* A group opens a nested context that starts fresh at indentation level\n   zero and follows the same rules as the root document *)\nnested_group        = \"(\", ENTER_NESTED_CONTEXT, nested_group_body,\n                      EXIT_NESTED_CONTEXT ;\n\nnested_group_body   = skip_empty_lines, links, whitespace, \")\"\n                    | whitespace, \")\" ;\n\n(* === Single Line Links === *)\nsingle_line_link    = horizontal_whitespace, reference,\n                      horizontal_whitespace, \":\", single_line_values ;\n\nsingle_line_value_link = single_line_values ;\n\nsingle_line_values  = { horizontal_whitespace, reference_or_link }- ;\n\n(* === Indented ID Link === *)\nindented_id_link    = reference, horizontal_whitespace, \":\", eol ;\n\n(* === Reference Types === *)\nreference_or_link   = nested_group\n                    | reference ;\n\nreference           = reference_literal\n                    | delimited_reference\n                    | simple_reference ;\n\n(* A simple reference cannot start with the reserved prefix ~[0-9]+{. *)\nsimple_reference    = reference_symbol, { reference_symbol } ;\n\n(* Decode the hex as Single-Line Value Link\nA sequence of references on a single line without an explicit identifier:\n```lino\npapa loves mama\n```\nThis creates an anonymous link with three values: `papa`, `loves`, `mama`.\n#### 2. Single-Line Named Link\nA link with an explicit identifier, using the `:` separator:\n```lino\nfamily: papa mama son daughter\n```\nThis creates a link named `family` with four values.\n#### 3. Nested Group (Parenthesized Link)\nLinks enclosed in parentheses can span multiple lines:\n```lino\n(family:\n  papa\n  mama\n  son\n  daughter)\n```\nA parenthesized group opens a **nested context**: its body starts fresh at\nindentation level zero and follows exactly the same rules as the root\ndocument, so indentation is structural inside parentheses too:\n```lino\narray (\n  a\n    b\n  c\n    d\n)\n```\nThe body above produces the same four links the root produces for\n`a`/`  b`/`c`/`  d`, nested under `array`.\nA group body that produces a single link collapses to that link, so\n`(a b c)` stays a single link. The only exception is a body that is itself a\nsingle parenthesized group, which keeps `((a b))` distinct from `(a b)`.\n#### 4. Anonymous Nested Group\nAnonymous parenthesized links:\n```lino\n(papa loves mama)\n```\n#### 5. Indented ID Link\nA named link where children are defined by indentation:\n```lino\nfamily:\n  papa\n  mama\n  son\n```\n### Indentation Rules\nIndentation is significant in Links Notation for defining hierarchical\nstructures:\n1. **Base Indentation**: The first content line sets the base indentation\n2. **Child Elements**: Must be indented more than their parent\n3. **Sibling Elements**: Must have the same indentation level\n4. **Spaces Only**: Only space characters count for indentation\n```text\ndocument\n├── first_line (sets base_indentation)\n├── line (must be >= base_indentation)\n│   └── children (must be > parent indentation)\n└── line (sibling, same level)\n```\n### Nesting\nLinks can be nested in two ways:\n#### Inline Nesting (Parentheses)\n```lino\n(outer: (inner: value1 value2) value3)\n```\nParentheses may also be broken across lines, in which case the indentation\ninside them is structural:\n```lino\n(outer:\n  (inner:\n    value1\n    value2)\n  value3)\n```\n#### Hierarchical Nesting (Indentation)\n```lino\nouter:\n  inner:\n    value1\n    value2\n  value3\n```\nBoth produce equivalent structures.\nEach line beneath an indented ID becomes one of its values. A named line keeps\nits name, so `file: path` is the value `(file: path)`. A nested indented ID\nrecursively gathers its own lines before it becomes a value.\nA bare value may also have indented lines. They form an anonymous nested link\nwith that value first. [2026-11-01T11:24:40.828Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Lino Protocol Parser for JavaScript\nJavaScript implementation of the Links Notation parser using Bun and\nPeggy.js parser generator.\n## Installation\n### Installing from npm\nInstall the package using your preferred package manager:\n#### Using npm (Node.js)\n```bash\nnpm install links-notation\n```\n#### Using Bun\n```bash\nbun add links-notation\n```\n#### Using Deno\n```typescript\nimport { Parser, Link } from 'npm:links-notation@^0.6.0';\n```\n#### In browsers\nThe package has no runtime dependencies and imports no Node.js built-in\nmodules, so bundlers need no polyfills. For example, esbuild bundles it with\n`esbuild entry.js --bundle --platform=browser`. Before 0.27.1, `StreamParser`\nimported Node's `events` module, and browser bundles needed the `events`\npackage installed as a polyfill.\n### Local Development Setup\nFor contributors working on the source code:\n#### Using Bun (recommended)\n```bash\ncd js\nbun install\n```\n#### Using npm\n```bash\ncd js\nnpm install\n```\n## Build\nCompile the Peggy.js grammar:\n```bash\nbun run build:grammar\n```\nBuild the project:\n```bash\nbun run build\n```\n## Test\nRun tests:\n```bash\nbun test\n```\nWatch mode:\n```bash\nbun test --watch\n```\n## Usage\n### TypeScript Support\nThis package includes TypeScript type definitions for improved developer experience with IntelliSense, autocomplete, and compile-time type checking.\n```typescript\nimport { Parser, Link, FormatOptions } from 'links-notation';\n// TypeScript provides full type checking and autocomplete\nconst parser = new Parser({\n  maxInputSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,\n  maxDepth: 64,\n});\nconst links: Link[] = parser.parse('(source: type target)');\n```\n### Basic Parsing\n```javascript\nimport { Parser, Link } from 'links-notation';\n// Create parser\nconst parser = new Parser();\n// Parse Lino format string\nconst input = `papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\nson lovesMama\ndaughter lovesMama\nall (love mama)`;\nconst result = parser.parse(input);\nconsole.log(result);\n// Access parsed structure\nresult.forEach((link) => {\n  console.log(link.toString());\n});\n```\n### Working with Links\n```javascript\nimport { Link } from 'links-notation';\n// Create links programmatically\nconst link = new Link('parent', [new Link('child1'), new Link('child2')]);\nconsole.log(link.toString()); // (parent: child1 child2)\n// Access link properties\nconsole.log('ID:', link.id);\nconsole.log('Values:', link.values);\n```\n### Advanced Usage\n```javascript\n// Handle nested structures\nconst input = `parent\n  child1\n  child2\n    grandchild1\n    grandchild2`;\nconst parsed = await parser.parse(input);\n// Work with groups\nimport { LinksGroup } from 'links-notation';\nconst group = new LinksGroup(parsed);\nconsole.log(group.format());\n```\n### Indented Text Documents\nUse `parseIndentedDocument` and `formatIndentedDocument` for text parents and\ntheir answers or options:\n```javascript\nimport { parseIndentedDocument, formatIndentedDocument } from 'links-notation';\nconst input = `What is your experience?\n  I have worked with JavaScript\n'Question with \"quotes\": and colon'\n  Answer\nSkills\n  JavaScript\n  Python\n`;\nconst answers = parseIndentedDocument(input);\nconsole.log(answers.get('What is your experience?'));\n// I have worked with JavaScript\nconsole.log(answers.get('Skills')); // ['JavaScript', 'Python']\nconsole.log(formatIndentedDocument(answers));\n```\nA parent with no children maps to `[]`, one child maps to a string, and multiple\nchildren map to an array. Repeated parent lines accumulate children in order.\nTo read multiple child lines as multiline text, pass\n`{ multipleValues: 'join' }`. These helpers accept the same parsing options as\n`Parser`, including `comments`, `maxInputSize`, and `maxDepth`.\nThe formatter uses two spaces of indentation and adds a final newline to a\nnonempty document. Ordinary single-space prose stays unquoted. Quotes are\nescaped by doubling the enclosing delimiter. Structural characters, comment\nstarts, reserved literal prefixes, and significant whitespace are quoted.\nEmpty strings and control characters use the versioned reference literals\nintroduced in 0.24.0. A multiline string is encoded as one reference with its\nexact line endings; an array is written as separate child references. Parsed\nIDs are already unescaped.\nThe text format does not distinguish a one-element array from a single string;\nboth read back as a string. Use a multiline string to distinguish one\nmultiline answer from several options. The helpers reject grandchildren and\nnamed links with values instead of discarding their structure.\nFor arbitrary indentation trees, `Parser.parseGroups(input)` returns existing\n`LinksGroup` instances. Each group's `element` is the `Link` on that line, and\n`children` contains its immediately indented groups. Parenthesized values retain\ntheir usual `Link` structure:\n```javascript\nimport { Parser } from 'links-notation';\nconst [group] = new Parser().parseGroups('Question\\n  Answer\\n    Detail');\nconsole.log(group.element.getValuesString()); // Question\nconsole.log(group.children[0].element.getValuesString()); // Answer\nconsole.log(group.children[0].children[0].element.getValuesString()); // Detail\n```\n`Parser.parse()` continues to return the existing list of links and expanded\npaths. `parseGroups()` preserves indentation even for the `name:` syntax.\n`escapeReference` and `unescapeReference` are exported functions and static\nmethods on `Link`. Use minimal mode only for whole text lines; default escaping\nstill quotes spaces so references can be used inside tuples:\n```javascript\nimport { Link, escapeReference, unescapeReference } from 'links-notation';\nLink.escapeReference('plain text'); // \"'plain text'\"\nescapeReference('plain text', { minimal: true }); // 'plain text'\nunescapeReference(\"'it''s ready'\"); // \"it's ready\"\n```\n`unescapeReference` decodes a complete serialized reference, including n-quote\ndelimiters, doubled escapes, and versioned literals. It rejects incomplete\nquoted input and malformed literals, and preserves literal backslashes. Do not\ncall it on already decoded `Link.id` values.\nSee the [Q&A document example](../examples/js_indented_document.js).\n### Streaming Parser (for Large Messages)\nThe `StreamParser` allows you to parse Links Notation incrementally, processing data as it arrives without loading the entire message into memory. This is ideal for:\n- Large files that don't fit in memory\n- Network streaming (TCP/HTTP)\n- Real-time processing of incoming data\n```javascript\nimport { StreamParser } from 'links-notation';\nconst parser = new StreamParser({ collect: false, maxBufferSize: 1024 * 1024 });\n// Listen for parsed links\nparser.on('link', (link) => {\n  console.log('Parsed link:', link.toString());\n});\n// Listen for errors with location information\nparser.on('error', (error) => {\n  console.error(\n    `Error at line ${error.line}, col ${error.column}: ${error.message}`\n  );\n});\n// Feed data incrementally (e.g., from network chunks)\nparser.write('papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\\n');\nparser.write('son lovesMama\\n');\nparser.write('daughter lovesMama\\n');\n// Finish the last record. Links are not retained when collection is disabled.\nparser.end();\n```\n`StreamParser.parse(chunks)` and `StreamParser.parseAsync(chunks)` expose native\nsync and async iterables. The parser also provides `position()`, `drain()`,\n`reset()`, and a maximum unresolved-record size. See the\n[streaming parser example](../examples/js_streaming_parser.js).\n### TypeScript Usage Examples\n```typescript\nimport {\n  Parser,\n  Link,\n  FormatOptions,\n  FormatConfig,\n  formatLinks,\n} from 'links-notation';\n// Create parser with options\nconst parser = new Parser({\n  maxInputSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,\n  maxDepth: 32,\n});\n// Parse with full type safety\nconst links: Link[] = parser.parse('(id: value1 value2)');\n// Create links programmatically\nconst link = new Link('parent', [new Link('child1'), new Link('child2')]);\n// Use formatting options\nconst formatOptions = new FormatOptions({\n  lessParentheses: true,\n  maxLineLength: 80,\n  indentLongLines: true,\n  maxInlineRefs: 3,\n  groupConsecutive: false,\n});\n// Format with type-checked options\nconst formatted: string = link.format(formatOptions);\n// Format multiple links\nconst output: string = formatLinks(links, formatOptions);\n```\n## Syntax Examples\n### Doublets (2-tuple)\n```lino\npapa (lovesMama: loves mama)\nson lovesMama\ndaughter lovesMama\nall (love mama)\n```\n### Triplets (3-tuple)\n```lino\npapa has car\nmama has house\n(papa and mama) are happy\n```\n### N-tuples with References\n```lino\n(linksNotation: links notation)\n(This is a linksNotation as well)\n(linksNotation supports (unlimited number (of references) in each link))\n```\n### Indented Structure\n```lino\nparent\n  child1\n  child2\n    grandchild1\n    grandchild2\n```\n### Multi-line Groups\nA parenthesized group opens a _nested context_: its body starts fresh at\nindentation level zero and follows the same rules as the root document, so a\nline break inside parentheses is structure rather than decoration.\n```lino\nvalue (\n  id \"1\"\n  label \"one\"\n)\n```\nThe document above parses to `(value ((id 1) (label one)))` - two children, each\na link of its own - rather than to one flat list in which the boundary between\n`id` and `label` would be lost. A body that stays on a single line still\ncollapses to a single link, so `(a b c)` is unchanged.\n```javascript\nimport { Parser, formatLinks } from 'links-notation';\nconst links = new Parser().parse(`value (\n  id \"1\"\n  label \"one\"\n)`);\nconsole.log(formatLinks(links)); // (value ((id 1) (label one)))\n```\n### Comments\nA `#` hides the rest of the line it stands on, so a document can carry prose\nabout itself:\n```lino\n# the machines this deploys to\ndeploy: staging # only staging, for now\n```\nBoth comments are gone by the time the document is read, leaving the single\nlink `(deploy: staging)`. A `#` only opens a comment where a reference could\nbegin, so a `#` inside a token (`issue#1047`) and a `#` inside a delimited\nreference (`\"#\"`) stay ordinary characters.\nA formatter keeps the same rule from the other side: a reference that begins\nwith a `#` is written quoted (`'#tag'`), so a document it writes reads back as\nitself.\nComments are on by default, and a parser can be told to read `#` as an ordinary\ncharacter again, for documents written before comments existed:\n```javascript\nimport { Parser, formatLinks } from 'links-notation';\nconst document =\n  '# the machines this deploys to\\ndeploy: staging # only staging, for now\\n';\nconsole.log(formatLinks(new Parser().parse(document))); // (deploy: staging)\nconst plain = new Parser({ comments: false });\nconsole.log(formatLinks(plain.parse('# a b\\n'))); // (# a b)\n```\n## API Reference\n### Classes\n#### `Parser`\nMain parser class for converting strings to links.\n- `constructor(options)` - Create a parser; `options.comments` set to `false`\n  reads `#` as an ordinary character instead of the start of a comment\n  - `options.maxInputSize` - Maximum input size in bytes (default: 10MB)\n  - `options.maxDepth` - How deep links may nest (default: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`,\n    64). Every parenthesized group and every indentation level is one level,\n    and a document nested deeper is refused with a `ParseError` rather than\n    recursed into until the stack runs out\n- `initialize()` - Initialize the parser (async)\n- `parse(input)` - Parse a Lino string and return links\n- `parseGroups(input)` - Read an indentation tree as `LinksGroup` instances\n#### `Link`\nRepresents a single link with ID and values.\n- `constructor(id, values = [])` - Create a new link\n- `toString()` - Convert link to string format\n- `id` - Link identifier\n- `values` - Array of child values/links\n- `escapeReference(reference, options)` - Quote a reference; `minimal: true`\n  allows ordinary prose on a text document line\n- `unescapeReference(reference)` - Decode a complete serialized reference\n#### `LinksGroup`\nContainer for grouping related links.\n- `constructor(links)` - Create a new group",

The avatar supports both **2D SVG rendering** (scalable to any screen size) and **3D WebGL/Three.js rendering** with synchronized styles. It features natural animations like blinking, head movement, and various expressions, making it ideal for AI-powered applications where a visual character representation is needed for voice interaction or chat interfaces.\n\nThe avatar includes:\n\n- **Fullscreen Immersive Design**: Avatar fills the entire screen for maximum impact\n- **Mobile-First Responsive UI**: Hamburger menu with glassmorphism semi-transparent settings panel\n- **2D SVG Mode**: Highly detailed scalable vector graphics with anime-style eyes, detailed hair with highlights/shadows, and sailor uniform\n- **3D WebGL Mode**: Three.js-powered 3D avatar with procedural geometry and animated falling petals\n- **Cherry Blossom Background**: Beautiful animated background scene with trees, falling petals, fence/bridge, and cityscape silhouette\n- **Color Customization**: Real-time color changes with preset themes\n\nFuture planned features:\n\n- Voice input (Speech-to-Text) and output (Text-to-Speech)\n- Local AI model integration for in-browser AI responses\n- Export compatibility with Unreal Engine and Blender\n\n## Features\n\n### Visual Design\n\n- **Highly Detailed 2D Avatar**: Anime-style SVG with detailed eyes (iris patterns, multiple highlights, reflections), hair with highlights and shadows, and authentic sailor uniform\n- **Full Body Mode**: Optional full body view with legs, socks, and shoes (Genshin Impact style)\n- **Configurable Detail Levels**: Adjustable detail from 1 (minimal) to 10 (maximum) controlling shape budgets for performance optimization\n- **Modular SVG Architecture**: Separate React components for each body part (face, eyes, hair, body, legs, background) allowing independent testing and customization\n- **Procedural 3D Avatar**: Three.js avatar with detailed anime head, hair, eyes with blush, and sailor uniform body\n- **Cherry Blossom Background**: Full scene with cherry trees, animated falling petals, wooden fence/bridge, and cityscape silhouette\n- **Dual Render Modes**: Switch between 2D SVG and 3D WebGL rendering\n\n### User Interface\n\n- **Fullscreen Immersive Experience**: Avatar fills the entire viewport for maximum visual impact\n- **Glassmorphism Settings Panel**: Semi-transparent settings panel with backdrop blur effect\n- **Mobile-First Design**: Hamburger menu that slides in from the right on mobile devices\n- **Responsive Layout**: Adapts seamlessly from mobile to desktop\n\n### Animations & Interactivity\n\n- **Multiple Animations**: Idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised expressions\n- **Random Animation Cycling**: Animations play randomly at configurable intervals for natural behavior\n- **Talking Mode**: Lip-sync animation for AI speaking scenarios\n- **Natural Blinking**: Random blinking with configurable timing for realistic appearance\n- **Animated Falling Petals**: Cherry blossom petals fall continuously in both 2D and 3D modes\n\n### Customization\n\n- **Configurable Appearance**: Customize skin, hair, eye, and clothes colors in real-time\n- **Preset Themes**: Quick appearance changes with built-in color presets (Schoolgirl, Blonde, Dark, Pink)\n- **3D Model Support**: Load external GLTF/GLB models with automatic color customization\n\n### Developer Experience\n\n- **Separate Test Pages**: Dedicated pages for testing 2D and 3D modes independently\n- PR, CI, and related investigation data into `docs/case-studies/issue-42`.\n- Search online for relevant facts and established tooling behavior.\n- Report related template issues if the same issue is Online References\n\nOfficial npm documentation confirms that publishable packages are identified by the `name` and `version` fields in `package.json`, and that `name` plus `version` form the package identifier:\nhttps://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json\n\nThe `npm view` command reads registry metadata for a package specifier, so checking the wrong package specifier can produce a false \"already published\" result:\nhttps://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-view\n\nThe release workflow uses trusted publishing. npm's trusted publishing documentation describes GitHub Actions OIDC publishing and the `id-token: [REDACTED] permission requirement:\nhttps://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers\n\n## Root Cause\n\nThe root cause was duplicated package identity. `package.json` already defines the package name and version, but several release scripts copied the package name into hard-coded constants. During template adoption, `package.json` is naturally updated first; script constants are easy to miss.\n\nThe reported script, `scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs`, used the hard-coded name for:\n\n- the `npm view <package>@<version> version` already-published check;\n- post-publish registry verification;\n- output and logging.\n\n# Contributing to js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\n## Development Workflow\n\nUse Node.js 24 with npm 10.9 or newer for development and release tooling.\nChangesets 3 requires a supported Node.js 22.11, 24, or 26+ runtime.\n\n1. **Fork the repository** and clone your fork\n2. **Create a feature branch**: `git checkout -b feature/my-feature`\n3. **Install dependencies**: `bun install` (or `npm install`)\n4. **Make your changes**\n5. **Run local checks**: `bun run check`\n6. **Create a changeset**: `bun run changeset`\n7. **Commit and push** (pre-commit hooks will run automatically)\n8. **Create a Pull Request**\n\n## Code Standards\n\n### File Size Limits\n\n**Maximum 1500 lines per file** (enforced via ESLint `max-lines` rule and CI `check-file-line-limits` job).\n\nThis benefits both AI and human developers by ensuring files remain readable and maintainable.\n\n### Formatting and Linting\n\nAll code must pass:\n\n```bash\n# Check formatting\nbun run format:check\n\n# Check linting\nbun run lint\n\n# Run all checks\nbun run check\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hook runs automatically, but you can also manually format and fix:\n\n```bash\n# Auto-fix formatting\nbun run format\n\n# Auto-fix lint issues\nbun run lint:fix\n```\n\n### Testing Requirements\n\nTests should:\n\n- Cover critical paths\n- Work across all runtimes (Node.js, Bun, Deno)\n- Use the [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) framework\n\n```bash\n# Run tests\nbun test --timeout 30000\nnpm test\ndeno test -A --parallel\n```\n\n## Version Management with Changesets\n\nThis project uses [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) to manage versions and changelogs. This eliminates merge conflicts that occur when multiple PRs bump the version in `package.json`.\n\n### Adding a Changeset\n\nWhen you make changes that affect users, add a changeset:\n\n```bash\nbun run changeset\n# or\nnpm run changeset\n```\n\nThis will prompt you to:",

             | Description                      |\n| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- |\n| `npm run dev`          | Start development server         |\n| `npm run build`        | Build for production             |\n| `npm run preview`      | Preview production build locally |\n| `npm test`             | Run tests once                   |\n| `npm run test:watch`   | Run **ESLint** for code linting with React-specific rules\n- **Prettier** for consistent code formatting\n- **Husky** for pre-commit hooks to ensure code quality\n- **Vitest** for fast unit testing with React Testing Library\n\n## Test Pages\n\nThe archived demo (`/archive`) includes dedicated test pages for isolated testing of each render mode:\n\n- **2D Test Page**: `/archive/test-2d.html` - Test SVG rendering independently\n- **3D Test Page**: `/archive/test-3d.html` - Test WebGL rendering independently\n\nBoth test pages include the full configuration panel and navigation between modes.\n\nThe Avatar Studio (`/`) has its own in-app test harness, reachable via the\n`Tests` view in the top bar (or `?view=tests`).\n\n## Roadmap\n\nThis prototype serves as a foundation for more You are free to use, modify, and distribute this code without any restrictions.\n# Anime Avatar - Development Roadmap\n\nThis document tracks the development progress of the Anime Avatar project, including completed work and planned features.\n\n## Completed Features\n\n### Core Rendering System\n\n- [x] **2D SVG Rendering** - High-quality scalable vector graphics avatar with anime-style design\n- [x] **3D WebGL Rendering** - Three.js-powered 3D avatar with procedural geometry\n- [x] **Dual Render Mode** - Seamless switching between 2D and 3D modes\n- [x] **Modular Component Architecture** - Separate components for head, face, eyes, hair, body, legs, background\n\n### Visual Design\n\n- [x] **Anime-style Eyes** - Detailed eyes with iris patterns, highlights, reflections, sparkles\n- [x] **Detailed Hair** - Hair with strands, highlights, shadows, ahoge\n- [x] **Sailor Uniform** - Complete school uniform with collar, bow, skirt\n- [x] **Full Body Mode** - Optional legs with socks and shoes (Genshin Impact style)\n- [x] **Cherry Blossom Background** - Trees, falling petals, cityscape, fence\n\n### Configuration System\n\n- [x] **Color Customization** - Skin, hair, eye, clothes colors\n- [x] **Detail Levels (1-10)** - Progressive complexity control\n- [x] **Color Presets** - Schoolgirl, Blonde, Dark, Pink themes\n- [x] **Model Scale** - Adjustable scale for 3D mode\n\n### Animation System\n\n- [x] **Natural Blinking** - Random blinking with configurable timing\n- [x] **Expression Animations** - Idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised\n- [x] **Talking Mode** - Lip-sync animation for AI speaking\n- [x] **Animation Cycling** - Automatic random animation playback\n\n### User Interface\n\n- [x] **Fullscreen Immersive Design** - Avatar fills entire viewport\n- [x] **Mobile-First Responsive** - Hamburger menu for mobile devices\n- [x] **Glassmorphism Settings Panel** - Semi-transparent with backdrop blur\n- [x] **Component Testing Page** - Individual component testing with dropdown\n\n### Developer Experience\n\n- [x] **Test Pages** - Standalone 2D and 3D test pages\n- [x] **ESLint + Prettier** - Code quality tooling\n- [x] **Husky Pre-commit Hooks** - Automated code checks\n- [x] **Vitest Testing** - Fast unit tests\n- [x] **GitHub Pages Deployment** - Automated CI/CD\n\n## In Progress (Issue #14)\n\n### Synchronization & Consistency\n\n- [x] **2D Character Scaling** - Added `characterScale` setting to match 3D `modelScale`\n- [x] **Camera Centering** - Both 2D and 3D cameras centered on avatar head/face\n- [x] **Legs by Default** - `showLegs` defaults to `true`\n- [x] **Background Label Rename** - Changed from \"Show Cherry Blossom Background\" to \"Show Background\"\n\n### Model Selection System\n\n- [x] **Background Model Selector** - Dropdown for background scene selection\n  - Road surrounded by cherry blossoms (default)\n  - (Prepared for future models)\n- [x] **Character Model Selector** - Dropdown for character selection\n  - School girl (default)\n  - (Prepared for future models)\n\n### Component Testing Enhancement\n\n- [x] **Quick Access Link** - Link to component testing page from main app settings\n\n### Bug Fixes\n\n- [x] **2D Rendering Size** - Fixed rendering size issue at lowest detail levels\n\n### Site Reorganization (Issue #41)\n\n- [x] **Avatar Studio at `/`** - The standalone multi-format Avatar Studio (previously at `/new`) is now the top-level entry point\n- [x] **Previous version at `/archive`** - The earlier React component demo is archived under `/archive`\n- [x] **Single-build deploy** -
