Being dev-only, it does not affect what we ship. |\n\n---\n\n## Recommendations\n\n### A. Build on these (permissive, healthy, aligned)\n\n1. **Links Notation as the single source of truth**, with lossless conversion\n   to the closest standard in each domain:\n   - **DTCG 2025.10** for tokens (via **Style Dictionary** transforms to CSS,\n     Swift, Kotlin and JS);\n   - **WAAPI / Lottie** for animation;\n   - **Vega-Lite** for charts;\n   - **Mermaid / DOT** for diagrams;\n   - **A2UI / Adaptive Cards / JSON Forms** for UI trees;\n   - **Custom Elements Manifest** for component metadata.\n\n   \"Every other framework is just LiNo\" then becomes concrete: each one has an\n   importer and exporter.\n2. **Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements)** as the reference\n   vanilla-JS renderer. Generate **React and Vue wrappers** with a Stencil-like\n   output-target approach, so one implementation serves all web frameworks.\n3. **Zag.js-style state machines** (adopt Zag.js, or reimplement its machines\n   described in LiNo) for component behaviour and accessibility. Use **React\n   Aria** and WAI-ARIA APG as the acceptance criteria. **Floating UI** for\n   positioning.\n4. **Three-layer tokens** (reference → semantic → component), with\n   **material-color-utilities** for palette generation. **Material, Fluent and\n   Apple (HIG-guided) themes** plus \"classic\" themes as alternative token sets\n   and control templates. Use **Ionic's modes** and **XAML control templates**\n   as the model, and **Open UI** research for canonical component and part\n   names.\n5. **Visualisation:** D3 modules plus our own LiNo chart grammar\n   (Vega-Lite-like). Renderers: **ECharts** (broad charts), **Cytoscape.js**,\n   **Sigma.js/Graphology** and **force-graph/3d-force-graph** (links networks),\n   **xyflow** (editable node graphs, React), **Dagre** (default layout).\n6. **Animation:** our own LiNo keyframe and spring and state-machine model,\n   compiled to **WAAPI / View Transitions**, **Motion** (MIT) on web, and\n   SwiftUI and Compose natively. **rrweb** as an optional DOM-level session\n   recorder. **Playwright** for turning recordings into tests.\n7. **Designer and dev mode:** our own, over the LiNo tree. Copy the panel\n   architecture from **GrapesJS / Puck / Visual Studio**, the runtime-overlay\n   inspector from **React DevTools / Live Visual Tree**, the variants matrix\n   from **Xcode Previews / Storybook**, and the timeline from **Theatre.js**\n   (design only). Use **Puck** (MIT) or **GrapesJS** (BSD-3) only for a\n   throw-away early prototype if speed matters.\n8. **Native:** **SwiftUI** (SwiftPM) and **Jetpack Compose / Compose\n   Multiplatform** renderers that interpret the same LiNo. **React Native New\n   Architecture** (0.82+) with **Expo** for demos, and **React Native Web** to\n   show RN components on the docs site. **Tauri** for a desktop designer shell\n   that can use the Rust associative stack (`doublets-rs`, `link-cli`).\n9. **Assets:** our own icon and illustration set under **CC0-1.0**. Default\n   third-party sets: **Lucide** (ISC), **Material Symbols** (Apache-2.0),\n   **Fluent System Icons** (MIT), **Phosphor / Tabler** (MIT), **Health Icons /\n   Kenney** (CC0). Keep attribution records in LiNo modelled on **Iconify's\n   per-set metadata**, with **SPDX** IDs, a **REUSE 3.3** compliant repo\n   (`REUSE.toml`), and **ScanCode** license scanning in CI.\n\n### B. Only interoperate with (import, export or optional adapter; no core dependency)\n\n- **Figma** (Dev Mode, Variables, Code Connect) and **Penpot** (MPL-2.0;\n  DTCG tokens). Token sync and component mapping only.\n- **MUI, Radix, shadcn/ui, Base UI, Headless UI, Fluent UI React,\n  Ionic.** Migration converters (theme to tokens, component-name mapping) and\n  a **shadcn-registry export** so agents can install our components.\n- **A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms, DivKit, json-render.** Importers and\n  exporters, plus learning their catalog and versioning models.\n- **Lottie / dotLottie** for animation exchange. **Mermaid / Graphviz DOT /\n  Vega-Lite** for diagrams and charts.\n- **ELK.js (EPL-2.0)** and **Graphviz WASM (EPL)**. Optional, separately\n  licensed plugin packages only.\n- **OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0)**, **Twemoji (CC BY 4.0)**, **game-icons\n  (CC BY 3.0)**. Optional packs with the required credits.\n- **Skip** (LGPL libraries), **Capacitor**, **Electron**. Optional delivery\n  routes.\n- **SF Symbols and SF fonts.** Reference by name at runtime on Apple platforms\n  only.\n\n### C. Avoid (license or maintenance conflicts)\n\n- **GSAP.** Its \"Standard No Charge\" license is proprietary and explicitly\n  forbids use in no-code visual animation tools that compete with Webflow,\n  which is our designer. Webflow can also revoke or change the terms.\n- **tldraw SDK.** Production requires a license key (since 4.0), with a\n  watermark on hobby licenses. Incompatible with public-domain redistribution.\n- **Theatre.js Studio (AGPL-3.0)**, the **Plasmic `platform/` code (AGPL)**,\n  **ToolJet (AGPL)**, **Qt/QML** and **Slint** (GPL/commercial) as\n  dependencies. Learn from their designs only.\n- **Rive editor and `.riv` as the core format.** Closed editor and format,\n  though the runtimes are MIT.\n- **Remix Icon** (custom license since January 2026) and **SF Symbols / SF Pro\n  / Segoe UI** (restricted) in any bundled package.\n- **Commercial-only libraries** (GoJS, yFiles, Highcharts, amCharts, AG\n  Grid/Charts Enterprise, MUI X Pro, JointJS+, Remotion) in core.\n- **Material Web (MWC)** as a dependency, because it is in maintenance mode.\n  Use material-color-utilities and the M3 token specs directly.\n- **Heavy code generation as the primary architecture** (lesson from Airbnb\n  Lona, and Mitosis' slow progress). Prefer a runtime LiNo interpreter plus\n  thin native renderers, and use codegen only for wrappers and types.\n\n### D. Open questions to verify before writing issues\n\n- Current stable version of A2UI (0.8 versus 0.9/1.0) and its component\n  catalog schema.\n- Compose Multiplatform for Web stability (Beta or Stable in 2026?).\n- Exact license of the open-sourced Skip engine (skipstone).\n- Fluent UI Web Components v3 stable date.\n- Remix Icon License v1.0 text.\n- Licenses of Adaptive Cards (MIT expected), Onlook, Terrazzo, Tokens Studio\n  plugin, Custom Elements Manifest and mdui. Confirm each in the repo's\n  LICENSE file.\n- Whether link-foundation standardises on Unlicense or CC0 for code. Check\n  `links-notation` and sibling repos.\n\n---\n\n## Sources\n\nDeclarative UI and server-driven UI:\n- Adaptive Cards renderer spec: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/adaptive-cards/rendering-cards/implement-a-renderer\n- Adaptive Cards in Copilot Studio (schema 1.6 host support): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/adaptive-cards-overview\n- A2UI: https://a2ui.org ; Files and Code Sections:\n\n**konard.github.io: settings system (src/settings/)**\n\n- `schema.js`\n  - SECTIONS are a list of `{id, column, title:{en,ru}, lead, fields, when(settings), tabs}`.\n  - FIELDS is the flat list of all fields.\n  - `RULES` maps key → `{d, min, max, u, o (options), c (color)}`.\n  - `CSS_RULES` excludes fields marked `css:false`.\n  - `DEFAULTS` and `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS` are exported.\n  - The DEFAULT_LOOK overlay comes from `schema.defaults.js`.\n  - The sections are motion, nebula, stars, grid, beams, rain, sound, the skins, ui, and theory.\n  - The theory section's `theory.notation` select is L→L² (draft 0.0.2) or R→R² (draft 0.0.3).\n- `schema.defaults.js`: DEFAULT_LOOK is the JSON the user pasted in issue #45 (\"That is defaults.\").\n- `fields.js`\n  - Field factories, each producing a flat object `{key, type, d, label, ...}`:\n    - `range(key,d,min,max,step,label,extra)`\n    - `toggle`\n    - `select(key,d,options,label)`\n    - `color`\n    - `option(value,en,ru)`\n  - `formatValue(field,value)` formats %, × and ° units.\n- `store.js`\n  - Uses `useSyncExternalStore`.\n  - localStorage key `settings` stores only the diff from defaults, so improved defaults still reach users who never changed that setting.\n  - Other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.\n  - API: `setSettings(patch)`, `resetSettings(keys)`, `changesOf`.\n  - `openSharedLook()` applies a `#settings=` hash, keeps the previous look as a saved \"Before the link\" preset, then strips the hash.\n- `apply.js`\n  - `normalize(rules, stored)` clamps numbers, validates options, and checks colors against `#rrggbb`. It also contains a migration (`future.surface:'transparent'` becomes solid with opacity 0).\n  - `applySettings(root, rules, settings)`:\n    - numbers and colors become CSS variables (`liquid.blur` → `--liquid-blur: 18px`)\n    - selects and toggles become `data-*` attributes on `<html>` (`skin.name` → `data-skin-name`)\n    - also derives the corner-radius fallbacks, `--ui-accent-rgb`, an SVG feTurbulence noise data-URI, and `data-surface-invisible`\n  - Both functions are serialized as text into `SETTINGS_SCRIPT` in vite.config.js and run before first paint, which prevents a flash of the wrong theme:\n    ```\n    export const SETTINGS_SCRIPT = `(function(){try{${inline(normalize)};${inline(applySettings)};var r=${inlineJSON(CSS_RULES)};applySettings(document.documentElement,r,normalize(r,JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('settings')||'{}')))}catch(e){}})();`;\n    ```\n    The `themeBeforePaint` Vite plugin injects it head-prepend together with THEME_SCRIPT.\n- `presets.js`\n  - `COMFORT` lists settings that presets, links and random never change: `['motion.mode','sound.on','sound.volume','theory.notation','ui.transparency']`. The idea comes from konard/immortality src/settings.ts.\n  - Functions: `cleanLook`, `applyLook`, `isLook`.\n  - PRESETS: default \"Matrix universe\", glass-universe, calm, matrix, deep-space, warp, neon (Tron), liquid, blueprint, and fast (\"Light and fast\", for slow phones).\n  - `before45()` rebases older presets onto the previous defaults.\n  - `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on any heavy key (count, fps, blur, glow and similar).\n  - Saved looks live under localStorage `settings-presets` as `[{name, look}]`, with `withSaved`, `withoutSaved`, `withImported` and `renamed`.\n  - Sharing: `shareLink` and `lookOfHash` use the `#settings=` prefix with URL-encoded JSON.\n- Remaining schema files:\n  - `schema.ui.js`: control height, padding, border, opacity, menu height and width, slider size and track, border style, and per-corner radii where −1 means \"follow the skin\".\n  - `schema.skins.js`: 12 PALETTES from immortality, SKINS `['glass','liquid','futuristic']`, CORNER_SHAPES (square, cut, tall, wide, round, scoop, notch), CORNER_LINES (none, gap, line, accent, bracket).\n  - Also schema.background.js, schema.layers.js, schema.materials.js and schema.sound.js.\n  - There are about 114 field-factory call sites, with many fields generated in loops; the code itself says \"hundreds\" of fields are script-only (`css:false`).\n\n**konard.github.io: pages and components**\n\n- `src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx`\n  - The /settings/ page is generated from the schema.\n  - Each row is a grid of label | control | value | reset (↺). Changed rows are marked with an `is-changed` class.\n  - Tabs mark the active layer with a dot.\n  - Each section has its own Reset button; there is also \"Reset everything\".\n  - The \"Look at the background\" peek mode hides the panels.\n  - A \"Your changes\" box shows the diff JSON, with Copy plus a textarea to paste and Load either settings or `{presets:[...]}`.\n  - Sounds can be previewed with ▶.\n  - The page is the live preview. It includes InterfacePreview, UiSamples, MaterialPresets and CornerTiles (tile previews of corner shapes).\n  - Columns are explicit because CSS multicol was buggy in Safari.\n  - Other settings-related files: Presets.jsx, InterfacePreview.jsx, UiSamples.jsx, CornerTiles.jsx.\n- `src/components/`\n  - Owned controls:\n    - Select.jsx: portal popup, WAI-ARIA APG keyboard behaviour, typeahead, reads `ui.menuHeight`/`ui.menuWidth`\n    - ColorInput.jsx: hex field plus RGB chooser plus palettes from colorPalettes.js; the popup is portaled and kept on screen\n    - NumberInput.jsx, Tooltip.jsx, PrefSwitches.jsx, Sound.jsx, Glyph.jsx\n  - Layout.jsx: shared frame with the cosmic background, navigation and footer settings link. It imports all skin CSS and fonts.\n  - numericKeys.js: consistent arrow, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End and Shift×10 stepping, with a Safari focus fix.\n  - panelVisibility.js: an IntersectionObserver plus MutationObserver limit how many backdrop-filter surfaces are live.\n  - Charts: ContributionCalendar, ContributionsChart, LanguagesChart, LanguageCloud, StatTiles, Timeline, EcosystemMap (orbit diagram), ProblemSolvingDiagram, NetworkGallery, SourceLines, SocialEmbed, HabrCards, Cosmos, LiquidRefraction, MetaTheory.\n- `src/i18n/prefs.js`\n  - Language order: `?lang` → stored → navigator → en.\n  - THEMES are auto/light/dark, using small `useSyncExternalStore` stores with no provider.\n  - Texts are written as `{en, ru}` objects; plural.js handles plurals.\n- `src/sound/`\n  - engine.js is a Web Audio bus: tone shelf → compressor → convolution reverb, with random detune and pointer panning. It was ported from immortality src/sound.ts (Unlicense).\n  - The AudioContext is created only after user interaction.\n  - interactions.js: document-level listeners map interactions to sounds, and a `data-sound` attribute overrides the default.\n  - Also library.js and options.js.\n- `src/visuals/`: the canvas background layers nebula.js, stars.js, rain.js (\"digital rain\" of link glyphs) and beams.js.\n  - governor.js: an FPS governor lowers resolution, then fps, never back up (SLOW_GAP 45 ms, MIN_SCALE 0.4).\n  - size.js handles sizing.\n- `src/skins.frames.js` plus the generated `skins.frames.css` (84 KB)\n  - The frame and corner definitions are written once and generate both the CSS and the preview tiles (`npm run build:frames`; a test keeps the CSS in sync).\n  - Uses `@property` typed lengths and per-selector `:where()` for performance.\n  - Other skin stylesheets: skins.glass/liquid/future/materials/palettes.css.\n\n**konard.github.io: links network (src/links/)**\n\n- `configurations.js`\n  - Defines the doublet network code: link 0 is \"nothing\", N real links, written as 2N digits in base N+1. A code looks like \"01 20\", or \"s,t;s,t\" for more than 9 links.\n  - Functions: `decode`, `encode`, `codeAt`, `indexOf` (BigInt), `randomCode`, `mathNotation` (subscripts), `linksNotation` → `(1: 0 1)`.\n  - Counts classes up to relabelling with Burnside's lemma (`classCount`, `representatives`), and supports a \"real-only\" mode.\n- `edit.js`\n  - Parsers for the theory notation `λ = {1 ↦ (0, 1)}`, pairs, the N-ary number `0120₃` with its decimal index, and links notation.\n  - Errors are returned as `{en, ru}`.\n  - **parseLinks uses a hand-rolled regex `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g` instead of the official links-notation npm parser.** A grep found no `links-notation` import anywhere in src; it appears only as data or text.\n- `notation.js`: `toReferences` (L→R), `notate`, and `useNotation()`, which reads the `theory.notation` setting.\n- `glyph.js`\n  - The network is drawn as one symbol following the links-visuals blueprint. Each link is one continuous cubic-Bézier curve: a bar at its source, its middle, and an arrow at its target. Other links refer to it by touching its middle. A reference to 0 is a free end; a self-reference is a loop, so (1: 1 1) becomes ∞.\n  - Constants and options:\n    - `SIZE=100`, `STROKE=2.4`\n    - a 9-colour COLORS palette\n    - MARKERS bar, arrow, triangle, tail, dot, circle, square, diamond, none\n    - a SHAPE options object covering placement, order, frame, forces, rotation, spread, padding, bendMode and more\n- `placement.js`: circle, grid (square), hex, dice, playing-card, spiral and d3-force layouts.\n- `style.js` and `style-geometry.js`\n  - STYLE_SECTIONS reuse the settings field helpers.\n  - Six link palettes: site, neon, pastel, warm, cold, print.\n  - `normalizeStyle`; `styleToParams`/`styleFromParams` keep only non-default values in the query string.\n- `render.js`\n  - `networkSvg` builds a single standalone SVG string used for both the preview and every export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen.\n  - XML is escaped and values are normalized to block injection.\n  - Supports backgrounds (solid, linear, radial), a card, and captions in the chosen notation.\n- `export.js`\n  - Downloads SVG, PNG, JPEG and WebP by rasterizing the SVG on a canvas.\n  - Also exports a links-notation file, clipboard copies, the Web Share API, and social share URLs.\n- Overlap reduction:\n  - collisions.js, collision-gaps.js and collision-symmetry.js do automatic spacing.\n  - `solver-job.js` and `collision-worker.js` run it in a cancellable Web Worker.\n  - `useCollisionSolver` ensures that keyed results never replace a newer drawing.\n- Pages:\n  - `NetworkPage.jsx`: the /network/?code=…&style-params editor, with sections Notations, Links, Style and Share. DEFAULT_CODE is '11 22 12'.\n  - `useNetworkHistory.js`: debounced URL history that pauses while a slider is being dragged; debug flag `localStorage network.debug`.\n  - Also NetworkEditor.jsx (LinksTable, per-link cards for colour, turns and gaps), NetworkStyle.jsx, NetworkShare.jsx and NetworkGaps.jsx.\n  - The gallery is at /art/#symbols (NetworkGallery).\n\n**konard.github.io: build and quality**\n- `scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`: hard limit of 1500 lines per file, warning above 1350.\n- Many `experiments/issue-N-browser.mjs` Playwright suites.\n- Every issue gets a case study under docs/case-studies.\n\n**konard.github.io: issues**\n- 24 issues total; #47 is OPEN: \"The left upper corner is not transparent, as well as top bottom. PRs #2, #4, #6 and #8 were merged.\n\n   **anime-avatar** (Unlicense; homepage https://konard.github.io/anime-avatar/; JavaScript; created 2026-01)\n   - Site layout: `/` serves the Avatar Studio from public/index.html and public/studio/*. `/archive` serves the older Vite React demo from src/ and archive/*.html. Both ship from one `npm run build`.\n   - The README mostly documents the archive. It loads the plain JS helpers first, then the Babel-transpiled JSX (ui, Editor, Tests, App). It uses the development React builds.\n   - public/studio/App.jsx:\n     - cfg lives in localStorage under key `acs_B` and is merged over `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`.\n     - `window.__acs = {cfg,setCfg,probe}` exposes state to the test harness.\n     - The view (editor, tests, split or none) is held in the `?view=` URL param and in localStorage `acs_view`. Split view degrades on mobile.\n     - The editor is always mounted so the tests can drive it.\n   - public/studio/defaults.js: a flat cfg with heavily commented semantics.\n     - Model: vrmUrl, modelPresetId, modelUrl, modelFormat, modelKind, pose.\n     - Rig: rot{bone:{x,y,z}}, scale{}, expr{}.\n     - Gaze: a large set of look* params (follow camera, mouse or random; eye and head amounts; smoothing; cone; fallbacks; saccade intervals).\n     - Materials: matGlobalTint, matTintAmount, matSaturation, matEmissive, matPerMesh.\n     - Scene: bg, ground and floorGrid.\n     - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color plus intensity.\n     - Cameras: cameraFov, Dist, Height and Inertia; a separate set of svgCam* values.\n     - Misc: autoRotate, mirrorArms, showFPS, and the experimental joint gizmo flag.\n   - public/studio/constants.js:\n     - Bones: ACS_HUMANOID_BONES (VRM superset), ACS_BONE_GROUPS, ACS_BONE_LIMITS (degrees, citing ROM references), ACS_clampBoneRad and ACS_SCALE_BONES.\n     - Presets and maps: ACS_POSE_PRESETS, ACS_STANDARD_EXPRESSIONS and ACS_MIXAMO_RIG_MAP.\n     - ACS_ANIMATION_PRESETS: Samba and Mixamo idle from the three.js examples CDN, and Gangnam Style from V-Sekai. Connect Telegram, VK, WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, X, LinkedIn, email, GitHub, Upwork, PeoplePerHour and job boards (career.habr.com, hh.ru, superjob.ru and more), and work every conversation from one app. Local-first and open source: your messages, contacts and keys stay in a store you own, with encrypted backups and no cloud in between.\n### Built for\nOur [product vision](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md) takes UI styling and configurability\nlessons from [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code), and uses Telegram\nclients as the baseline for familiar messaging features across providers.\n[Source references and inspiration](docs/CHAT-REFERENCES.md) record the comparisons;\nthe feature matrix describes what is currently supported.\n| Who / what        | How meta-sovereign helps                                                                                                                                      |\n| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **Individuals**   | All your chats in one place, reconnect with people gone quiet, remember what was said (facts), one CV on every job site.                                      |\n| **Sales**         | Leads from every network in one CRM, audiences by rule, mass-personal outreach that sends each message once and politely, follow-ups, fast replies.           |\n| **Marketing**     | Broadcasts to audiences, posts to Telegram channels, LinkedIn and X, community members kept fresh, an opt-out list every automated send honours.              |\n| **User support**  | One Operator queue of unread conversations, answers from a VK community or Telegram Business account, auto-replies as safe drafts, a knowledge base of facts. |\n| **Organisations** | The same tools for a brand, a shop or a project: its accounts, its contacts, its data on its own machine. Team mode (several operators) is on the roadmap.    |\nWhat works for each scenario today, what is partial and what comes next is in the roadmap: [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md).\n## Try it now (no install)\nOpen <https://link-foundation.github.io/meta-sovereign/> in any modern browser. The web app boots immediately, runs entirely in your browser, and writes to local storage by default — nothing leaves your device until you point it at a server.\n> If the link is not yet live, the GitHub Pages workflow (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`) publishes it on the next push to `main`.\nWithout a server the hosted app runs in **browser-only mode**: contacts, patterns and broadcasts work from the browser store, while imports, automations, sync, CV sync and greetings wait for a local server. A notice shows the command to start one and a **Check again** button.\n## Desktop app\nDownload the installer for your system from <https://link-foundation.github.io/meta-sovereign/download/>, or from [GitHub releases](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/releases): Linux (AppImage, deb, tar.gz), macOS (dmg, zip) and Windows (installer, portable), each for x64 and arm64. The desktop app bundles the server, so every feature works without starting one yourself. First-launch steps for unsigned builds, checksums and update notes are in [`docs/USER-GUIDE.md` §4](docs/USER-GUIDE.md#4-install-the-desktop-or-mobile-app).\n## Run a local server (recommended for sync)\nTo sync between devices, keep encrypted backups, and unlock the full feature set, start a local server next to the SPA. Two backends are available; both implement the same wire protocol (see [`docs/SERVER-PARITY.md`](docs/SERVER-PARITY.md)).\n### Rust server — single binary, no runtime, but limited\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign\ncd meta-sovereign\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p meta-sovereign-server -- serve\n```\n> **Rust server limits.** It keeps links **in memory only**: nothing is written to disk, so everything is gone when the server stops. It has **no source adapters**: no live fetches from Telegram, VK, GitHub, Upwork or similar, no outbound HTTP or TLS client (email only ingests archives), and no automations, CV sync, browser auto-import, backups or `/api/export-encrypted`. Pick the JS server or the desktop app for real use. The route-by-route list is in [`docs/SERVER-PARITY.md`](docs/SERVER-PARITY.md).\n### JavaScript server — full feature set (Node/Bun/Deno), from source\nThe package is **not published on npm yet** (the registry answers 404), so `npx -y meta-sovereign serve` does not work today. Run the server from a source checkout (needs Node.js and npm):\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign\ncd meta-sovereign\nnpm install\nnode js/bin/meta-sovereign.js serve\n```\nAfter updating, repeat `serve` while the original host stays running: it keeps serving while the replacement warms up, then transfers the single store writer and retains the public listener/certificate. Failed replacements roll back automatically. Older single-process installations need one initial restart to adopt this host. See [rolling server upgrades](docs/ROLLING-SERVER.md).\nLarge archives use packed cold payloads, bounded suggestion caches and paced, streamed snapshots. See [server CPU and memory](docs/SERVER-RESOURCES.md) for retention limits and the constant-cost memory fields in `/api/health`.\nOnce the package is published to npm, `npx -y meta-sovereign serve` (or `npm install -g meta-sovereign && meta-sovereign serve`) will work. Until then, the desktop app (above) is the way to run the server without a toolchain.\nEither backend listens on <http://127.0.0.1:8787> by default. The JS server answers the hosted app's origin (`https://link-foundation.github.io`) with CORS headers; allow other origins with `meta-sovereign serve --allow-origin=<origins>` or `MS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`. Safari does not let `https` pages reach `http://127.0.0.1`, but it allows `https://127.0.0.1`; the server also answers HTTPS on the same port with its own certificate for localhost — run `node js/bin/meta-sovereign.js trust` once (macOS adds it to the login keychain; other systems print the certificate path), or open `https://127.0.0.1:8787/trust` in Safari and follow the prompts, and the hosted app connects directly. Before trusting, the notice names the server and offers **Trust the server** (<https://127.0.0.1:8787/trust>); it links a localhost UI only if that UI was explicitly enabled. `--tls=false` / `MS_TLS=off` turns HTTPS off. Safari uses the hosted app through the trusted local HTTPS API; the localhost UI is optional. The hosted SPA discovers the local server automatically through `discoverServer()` (saved override → `127.0.0.1` ports). If your browser does not auto-connect, open the in-app **Settings → Server** prompt and paste the URL the binary printed.\nThe hosted app is the default UI: `serve` prints its address, <https://link-foundation.github.io/meta-sovereign/>, and the app finds the server on our port 8787 by itself (it also looks at 8788, 7001, 7002 and 3000; on another port `serve` says to set it in **Settings → Server**), so the server does not have to host a web site. By default `/` redirects to GitHub Pages and the server serves only its API, sync transports and connection helpers. To opt into a localhost web app for offline use, run `serve --local-ui=true` (or set `MS_LOCAL_UI=on`); that copy is then available at <http://127.0.0.1:8787>. Desktop shells explicitly enable their bundled UI. `--ui-url=<url>` (or `MS_UI_URL`) names another hosted copy, such as a fork's Pages, and allows its origin.\nOn macOS, interactive `serve` now handles the full setup: it protects this installation’s TLS key with Secure Enclave, detects existing certificate trust, requests trust only when needed, and opens the GitHub Pages app. For a headless launch use `node js/bin/meta-sovereign.js serve --trust=true --open=true`. `--trust=false` and `--open=false` opt out. The Swift helper needs the macOS Command Line Tools; `--hardware-key=false` explicitly opts into a file key on unsupported Macs. Hardware protection applies to the key on disk; Node uses it in memory. See [local server setup and security](docs/LOCAL-SERVER-SECURITY.md) for the exact access rules and limits.\nOpen conversations load first. History loads automatically on scroll, with a compact indicator inside the message list while requesting or retrying; no history status panel or manual loading button is shown. Earlier history loads automatically on scroll in Chat and Operator. Message selection and menus work across the full row; unread cards use refreshed Telegram counters and retain cached data during connection failures. All / Private / Groups / Channels filters remain available inside every Telegram folder. Drag the vertical dividers to resize columns; widths are remembered. Calls is in the main menu after Chat, and Telegram account editing is under Profile. The default dark controls use white line icons. Buttons and action links have nonzero spacing and aligned control padding. Stories is off by default; Settings → Stories enables its display and requests. The JS server keeps its store under your OS user: `~/Library/Application Support/Meta Sovereign/store` on macOS, `%APPDATA%/Meta Sovereign/store` on Windows, and `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/Meta Sovereign/store` on Linux. Starting `serve` from an older checkout migrates its `.meta-sovereign` store once, preserving messages, contacts, sessions, media and certificate; a compatibility link preserves old paths. Restarts and a different working directory reuse the same store. `--store` or `META_SOVEREIGN_STORE_DIR` override it. See [chat readiness and data storage](docs/CHAT-READINESS.md).\n## Connect the SPA to your server\nThe SPA picks a server in this order ([`js/src/web/discover.js`](js/src/web/discover.js)):\n1. **Same origin** — when you serve the SPA from the JS or Rust server directly.\n2. **Saved override** — `localStorage.metaServer`. Set via the in-app **Settings → Server** prompt.\n3. **Runtime shell candidates** — Electron and Capacitor inject the embedded server URL.\n4. **`127.0.0.1` ports** — the default local-server port is probed automatically.\n5. **Caller-supplied LAN candidates** — passed programmatically.\nIf nothing answers, the SPA falls back to **offline mode**: writes go to the local browser store ([`createBrowserStore`](js/src/storage/browser-store.js): IndexedDB → localStorage → in-memory) and replay automatically through [`OfflineClient`](js/src/web/client.js) the next time a server appears.\nThe full user-facing flow — install nothing, install Rust server, install JS server, install desktop / mobile app, encrypted export, troubleshooting — is in [`docs/USER-GUIDE.md`](docs/USER-GUIDE.md).\n## What it does\n- **Unified inbox** across VK, Telegram, X, WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, email, GitHub, Upwork, PeoplePerHour and job boards, with live updates where the network allows (Telegram, the VK Long Poll, incremental IMAP, GitHub) and full-size archive imports for the rest.\n- **Chat that behaves like Telegram's own apps**: each message sent once, delivery ticks, live updates and catch-up after a gap, read marking, cloud drafts, retries that survive a reload. How the open-source Telegram, Signal and Element clients do it, pinned to the commits we read, is in [`docs/CHAT-REFERENCES.md`](docs/CHAT-REFERENCES.md).\n- **CRM**: everything known about a contact in one view, the same person across networks, communities and memberships, search, audiences by rule (`friends:vk & chat:vk:… - list:blocked`).\n- **Contact imports**: preview and import macOS Contacts (including synced iCloud accounts) or vCard exports from any platform; repeated imports keep stable identities. The directory updates during sync and includes people without messages. See [contact imports](docs/CONTACTS-IMPORT.md).\n- **Saved edit history**: the running local server preserves observed versions while the browser is closed; view them from Chat, Operator or deleted messages, even after the service removes the content. Already downloaded Telegram attachments are retained too. See [capture and retention limits](docs/MESSAGE-HISTORY.md).\n- **Outreach, broadcasts and automations**: who to message, when, on what conditions and with which text; a preview of who gets what; safe drafts by default or paced auto-send with quiet hours, a per-chat cooldown, daily caps and an opt-out list. Every automated send goes through one outbox, so it happens at most once and an unclear result is never retried by itself ([`docs/USER-GUIDE.md` §11](docs/USER-GUIDE.md#11-automations-message-people-by-rule-safely)).\n- **Work accounts**: manual sign-in and saved profile snapshots for Upwork, Fiverr, PeoplePerHour and Wellfound in Connections and Profile. [Setup and initial support limits](docs/WORK-ACCOUNTS.md).\n- **Operator queue and replies**: walk unread messages chat by chat, reply suggestions from your own past answers (Tab takes one), patterns and reply variations, auto-replies on a matching message.\n- **Business and community accounts**: a VK community token runs the Bots Long Poll; Telegram Business quick replies, greeting and away messages, hours and chatbots.\n- **Memory**: structured `question → answer` facts captured from conversations, checked in the chat.\n- **Greetings**: open dialogs on VK, Telegram, WhatsApp, Messenger, X and email with a \"hi\" or a greeting sticker, the way [konard/vk-bot](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot) does ([`docs/GREETINGS.md`](docs/GREETINGS.md)).\n- **CV synchronisation** across LinkedIn, hh.ru, Habr Career, Naukri, VietnamWorks, TopCV and SuperJob through your own browser, field by field ([`docs/CV-SYNC.md`](docs/CV-SYNC.md)).\n- **Your data, safe**: a crash-safe local store ([Doublets](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs) binary + [Links Notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) text), automatic schema migrations ([`docs/DATA-MIGRATIONS.md`](docs/DATA-MIGRATIONS.md)), streamed encrypted backups, full-disk handling, encrypted secrets, a local server that refuses other sites.\n- **Everywhere you are**: the hosted web app, a desktop app with the server inside, mobile shells, WebRTC sync between your own devices, offline writes replayed later; a pure-Rust server variant shares the on-disk format.\n- **Four languages**: the app and every document are in English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese.\nEvery feature, network by network, with what is supported, partial or not supported and whether it is reachable by API or web app: [`docs/FEATURES.md`](docs/FEATURES.md). Every requirement with its evidence: [`docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`](docs/REQUIREMENTS.md).\n## Status\nRequirements R-A to R-Z24 are done and checked in CI on Node, Bun and Deno across Linux, macOS and Windows, with browser end-to-end tests in Chromium. Tests use fakes: nothing is sent from a real account in tests, and only Telegram's message display was also checked against a real store. The scenario-by-scenario state and the next steps (live verification, guided sign-in, team mode, a sales pipeline, campaign results) are in [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md).\n## Repository structure\n`meta-sovereign` is multi-language. Each language tree mirrors the corresponding [link-foundation AI-driven-development pipeline template](https://github.com/link-foundation):\n- **JavaScript** lives under `js/`: `js/src/`, `js/tests/`, `js/scripts/`, `js/bin/`, `js/electron/`, `js/examples/`, and `js/experiments/`.\n- **Rust** lives under `rust/`: `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/Cargo.lock`, and the `rust/crates/` workspace (`meta-sovereign-server`, `meta-sovereign-core`, `meta-sovereign-wasm`).\n- **Native shells**: `js/electron/` (desktop), `mobile/` + `capacitor.config.json` (iOS/Android), `docker/` (web + WebRTC microservices).\n- **Operations**: `.github/workflows/` (CI/CD), `.changeset/` (release management), `docs/` (this guide and case studies).\n```\n.\n├── .changeset/           # Changeset configuration\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD (release.yml, links.yml, pages.yml)\n├── .husky/               # Git hooks (pre-commit)\n├── docker/               # Web + WebRTC microservice Dockerfiles\n├── docs/                 # REQUIREMENTS, USER-GUIDE, SERVER-PARITY, case studies\n├── js/                   # JavaScript tree (src, tests, scripts, bin, electron)\n├── mobile/               # Capacitor mobile shell\n├── rust/                 # Rust workspace manifest, lockfile, and crates\n├── bunfig.toml           # Bun configuration\n├── capacitor.config.json # Capacitor mobile config\n├── deno.json             # Deno configuration\n└── package.json          # Node.js package manifest\n```\n---\n## Developer reference\nEverything below is for contributors. End-users do not need to read it.\n### Inherited features (CI/CD baseline)\n- **Multi-runtime support**: Works with Bun, Node.js, and Deno.\n- **Universal testing**: Uses [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) for cross-runtime tests.\n- **Automated releases**: Changesets-based versioning with GitHub Actions.\n- **Code quality**: ESLint + Prettier with pre-commit hooks via Husky.\n- **Package manager agnostic**: Works with bun, npm, yarn, pnpm, and deno.\n- **Broken link checks**: Automated link validation with [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action) and Web Archive fallback suggestions.\n- **GitHub Pages publishing**: `pages.yml` deploys the SPA on every push to `main` (this PR).\n### Quick Start\n```bash\n# Install dependencies\nbun install\n# Run tests\nbun test\n# Or with other runtimes:\nnpm test\ndeno test --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-net --allow-sys js/tests\n# Run the real-browser e2e (opt-in; needs Playwright + Chromium)\nRUN_BROWSER_E2E=1 npm run test:e2e:browser\n# Run the Rust workspace tests\ncargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace",

Prefer a runtime LiNo interpreter plus\n  thin native renderers, and use codegen only for wrappers and types.\n\n### D. [2026-11-01T11:38:28.161Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Architecture (proposal)\n\nThis document is the target architecture of the associative UI framework\nplanned in [issue #1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1). It is a\n**proposal**: every part of it is delivered by a roadmap issue listed in\n[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), and each roadmap issue may refine it. The evidence\nbehind each decision is in the\n[issue 1 case study](case-studies/issue-1/README.md).\n\n## Principles\n\n1. **Links first.** Every UI concept (element, property, style rule, design\n   token, theme, behaviour, data binding, animation, recording, configuration\n   override, asset licence) is a link in a links network. Links Notation\n   (LiNo, [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation))\n   is its only canonical text form. JSON, CSS, JSX, XAML, SwiftUI and so on are\n   import or export formats, never the source of truth.\n2. **One dialect.** Structure, configuration, styles, tokens, animations and\n   recordings use one LiNo vocabulary (the _UI dialect_), so any other UI\n   framework can be described as a LiNo document in that dialect.\n3. **Sharable by default.** A UI, a theme, a set of overrides or a recording is\n   a plain LiNo text that can be pasted into an issue, a chat with an agent,\n   or a URL.\n4. **Runtime interpreter, thin renderers.** One platform-neutral core\n   interprets the links network. Each platform (DOM, React, Vue, React Native,\n   SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose) has a thin renderer. Code generation is used only\n   for wrappers, types and optional \"eject to code\" exports.\n5. **JavaScript first.** As required by [`javascript-first.md`](javascript-first.md),\n   the JavaScript implementation and shared conformance fixtures come first.\n   Swift and Kotlin ports must pass the same fixtures.\n6. **Everything editable at runtime.** Every rendered element keeps a stable\n   link ID that maps back to its LiNo source. This is what makes the\n   development/configuration mode and the WYSIWYG designer possible on any\n   site built with the framework.\n7. **Public domain.** Code is released under the [Unlicense](../LICENSE). Our\n   own non-code assets are dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0).\n   Third-party assets are allowed only with a machine-readable record of the\n   source, copyright holder, licence (SPDX ID) and attribution text.\n\n## Layers\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph Sources[\"LiNo sources (sharable text)\"]\n    Doc[\"documents<br/>(structure)\"]\n    Tok[\"tokens & themes\"]\n    Sty[\"styles\"]\n    Ani[\"animations & recordings\"]\n    Cfg[\"configuration overrides\"]\n    Ast[\"asset records\"]\n  end\n  Sources --> Core[\"ui-core<br/>parse · validate · project · diff/patch\"]\n  Core --> Store[\"links store<br/>(in-memory network, transactions, undo/redo,<br/>IndexedDB / doublets-web persistence)\"]\n  Store --> Config[\"configuration layers<br/>defaults < theme < site < user < session\"]\n  Config --> Engine[\"style & token resolver,<br/>behaviour state machines, animation engine\"]\n  Engine --> DOM[\"DOM renderer<br/>(custom elements)\"]\n  DOM --> React[\"React adapter\"]\n  DOM --> Vue[\"Vue adapter\"]\n  Engine --> RN[\"React Native renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Swift[\"SwiftUI renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Kotlin[\"Compose renderer\"]\n  Store --> Dev[\"dev/configuration mode<br/>(inspector overlay)\"]\n  Dev --> Designer[\"WYSIWYG designer\"]\n  Dev --> Export[\"export overrides as LiNo<br/>(agent hand-off, share URL)\"]\n```\n\n| Layer                 | Package (working name)         | Responsibility                                                                                                                       |\n| --------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| Dialect specification | `docs/spec/`                   | Vocabulary, grammar of the UI dialect on top of LiNo, conformance fixtures shared by every implementation.                          |\n| Core                  | `@link-foundation/ui-core`     | Parse LiNo (via `links-notation`), project links into an element tree, validate against the dialect, format back, diff and patch. |\n| Store                 | `@link-foundation/ui-store`    | Mutable links network with stable IDs, change events, transactions, undo/redo, persistence (IndexedDB; `doublets-web` compatible). |\n| Configuration         | `@link-foundation/ui-config`   | Layered configuration and overrides; export of overrides as LiNo patches.                                                           |\n| Tokens and themes     | `@link-foundation/ui-tokens`   | Design tokens in LiNo; export to CSS custom properties, DTCG 2025.10 JSON, Swift and Kotlin.                                        |\n| Styles                | `@link-foundation/ui-style`    | Style rules as links (selectors, states, responsive conditions) resolved against tokens.                                            |\n| DOM renderer          | `@link-foundation/ui-dom`      | Reference renderer with custom elements and incremental updates.                                                                    |\n| Framework adapters    | `ui-react`, `ui-vue`, `ui-react-native` | Thin bindings over the core and DOM renderer (React Native renders natively).                                               |\n| Native ports          | `ui-swift` (SwiftPM), `ui-kotlin` (Gradle/KMP) | SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose renderers of the same dialect.                                                         |\n| Components            | `@link-foundation/ui-components` | Controls, layout, chat, charts, diagrams, links-network visualisation; behaviour as state machines described in LiNo.            |\n| Animation             | `@link-foundation/ui-animation`  | Keyframe/spring/timeline model, player (Web Animations API), recorder (timestamped LiNo events).                                  |\n| Dev mode              | `@link-foundation/ui-devmode`    | Runtime inspector overlay, property editing, persistence, \"make these the defaults\" export.                                      |\n| Designer              | `@link-foundation/ui-designer`   | Visual Studio-like WYSIWYG designer built with the framework itself.                                                             |\n| Converters            | `@link-foundation/ui-convert`    | Importers (HTML/DOM, JSX/MUI, Vue SFC, Mermaid, Vega-Lite, Lottie, DTCG) and exporters.                                          |\n| Assets                | `assets/` + `assets.lino`        | Own CC0 assets and third-party asset records with SPDX licences.                                                                 |\n\nPackage names are working names; the monorepo issue decides the final ones.\n\n## The UI dialect (sketch)\n\nThe samples below are in\n[`case-studies/issue-1/samples/`](case-studies/issue-1/samples/) and are\nchecked by [`experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs):\n`links-notation` 0.27.1 parses every sample and formats it back to an equal\nlinks network.\n\nA document (structure, configuration and behaviour in one place):\n\n```lino\n(app: document\n  (title 'Links UI demo')\n  (theme material3)\n  (body: stack\n    (direction vertical)\n    (gap (token space.medium))\n    (greeting: text 'Hello, links')\n    (ok: button\n      (label 'OK')\n      (variant filled)\n      (on press (navigate home)))))\n```\n\nTokens and themes:\n\n```lino\n(material3: theme\n  (extends base)\n  (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n  (token space.medium 16px)\n  (token motion.duration.short 150ms))\n```\n\nAnimation and a recording:\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n(recording-1: recording\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nConfiguration overrides produced by the dev mode (what a user hands to an\nagent with \"make these the defaults\"):\n\n```lino\n(user-overrides: overrides\n  (layer user)\n  (base app)\n  (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n  (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n```\n\n### Links Notation parse shapes\n\nThe experiment\n[`experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs)\nshows that `links-notation` 0.27.1 returns **different link structures** for\nthe same element depending on how it is written:\n\n- `(ok: button (label 'OK'))` on one line gives one nested link;\n- the same text split over several lines inside parentheses, and the indented\n  form `ok: button` / `  label 'OK'`, are returned by `Parser.parse()` as\n  expanded path links such as `((ok: button) (label OK))`;\n- `Parser.parseGroups()` keeps the indented form as an explicit tree.\n\n`ui-core` therefore defines one **tree projection** that accepts all three\nforms and produces the same element tree. The dialect specification issue\nfixes this projection and its conformance fixtures.\n\n## Configuration layers and agent hand-off\n\nEvery value an element uses is resolved through ordered layers:\n\n1. `defaults` — the component's own defaults (shipped in the package);\n2. `theme` — the active theme(s), which may be nested per subtree;\n3. `site` — the application's committed LiNo configuration;\n4. `user` — overrides saved in the browser (IndexedDB);\n5. `session` — temporary overrides made in dev mode and not yet saved.\n\nDev mode writes only to `user` or `session`. \"Make these the defaults\" exports\nthe difference between the top layers and `site` as an `overrides` LiNo\ndocument, a share URL, and a ready-to-paste agent instruction. The agent then\napplies the patch to the committed `site` configuration.\n\n## Development/configuration mode and designer\n\n- Enter dev mode with a keyboard shortcut, a `?ui-dev` URL parameter, or a\n  `<ui-dev-mode>` element. Sites can disable or restrict it.\n- Hovering highlights elements and clicking selects them. The inspector shows\n  the outline tree (links network), the property grid (resolved value plus the\n  layer it came from), styles, tokens, animations and the LiNo source.\n- The WYSIWYG designer reuses the inspector and adds a toolbox, canvas drag\n  and drop, alignment guides, multi-select, undo/redo, docked panels,\n  two-way source sync and a timeline. It is built with the framework itself.\n\n## Themes and other frameworks as LiNo\n\nA theme is a LiNo package of tokens, style rules and component templates\n(the XAML control-template idea). Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG-guided and\n\"classic\" themes (deepcase versions, konard.github.io styles, retro desktop\nlooks) are just alternative packages. Migration from MUI, Fluent UI, shadcn/ui\nand other frameworks is a converter plus a mapping table into the same\ndialect.\n\n## Platforms\n\n- **Web:** custom elements (plain JavaScript), React and Vue wrappers over the\n  same core.\n- **React Native:** a renderer that maps dialect elements to React Native\n  primitives (New Architecture).\n- **Swift:** a SwiftPM package with a SwiftUI renderer. It reads LiNo with a\n  Swift parser (an upstream `links-notation` port, or a port created by the\n  roadmap if none exists).\n- **Kotlin:** a Gradle/Kotlin Multiplatform package with a Jetpack Compose /\n  Compose Multiplatform renderer, with the same parser condition.\n\nAll implementations run the shared conformance fixtures from `docs/spec/`.\n\n## Associative technology stack usage\n\n| Component                                                                      | Use in this framework                                                     |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)           | Canonical text format; parser and formatter for every implementation.    |\n| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)   | Strict encoding and decoding of object-shaped configuration.              |\n| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)           | CLI, environment and `.lenv` configuration of tools (converters, build).  |\n| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)                     | Localisation catalogs for every component and the designer.               |\n| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)             | Lossless CST networks for importing source code (JSX, Vue SFC, HTML).     |\n| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)                       | Query and substitution conventions for selectors and patches.            |\n| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)                 | Compatibility target for browser persistence of the links store.         |\n| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) | Context-relative values (per theme, per user, per device) as a model.    |\n\nThe full mapping, including which components are direct dependencies, is in\nthe case study.\n"

               | `@link-foundation/ui-core`     | Parse LiNo (via `links-notation`), project links into an element tree, validate against the dialect, format back, diff and patch. |\n| Store                 | `@link-foundation/ui-store`    | Mutable links network with stable IDs, change events, transactions, undo/redo, persistence (IndexedDB; `doublets-web` compatible). |\n| Configuration         | `@link-foundation/ui-config`   | Layered configuration and overrides; export of overrides as LiNo patches.                                                           |\n| Tokens and themes     | `@link-foundation/ui-tokens`   | Design tokens in LiNo; export to CSS custom properties, DTCG 2025.10 JSON, Swift and Kotlin.                                        |\n| Styles                | `@link-foundation/ui-style`    | Style rules as links (selectors, states, responsive conditions) resolved against tokens.                                            |\n| DOM renderer          | `@link-foundation/ui-dom`      | Reference renderer with custom elements and incremental updates.                                                                    |\n| Framework adapters    | `ui-react`, `ui-vue`, `ui-react-native` | Thin bindings over the core and DOM renderer (React Native renders natively).                                               |\n| Native ports          | `ui-swift` (SwiftPM), `ui-kotlin` (Gradle/KMP) | SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose renderers of the same dialect.                                                         |\n| Components            | `@link-foundation/ui-components` | Controls, layout, chat, charts, diagrams, links-network visualisation; behaviour as state machines described in LiNo.            |\n| Animation             | `@link-foundation/ui-animation`  | Keyframe/spring/timeline model, player (Web Animations API), recorder (timestamped LiNo events).                                  |\n| Dev mode              | `@link-foundation/ui-devmode`    | Runtime inspector overlay, property editing, persistence, \"make these the defaults\" export.                                      |\n| Designer              | `@link-foundation/ui-designer`   | Visual Studio-like WYSIWYG designer built with the framework itself.                                                             |\n| Converters            | `@link-foundation/ui-convert`    | Importers (HTML/DOM, JSX/MUI, Vue SFC, Mermaid, Vega-Lite, Lottie, DTCG) and exporters.                                          |\n| Assets                | `assets/` + `assets.lino`        | Own CC0 assets and third-party asset records with SPDX licences.                                                                 |\n\nPackage names are working names; the monorepo issue decides the final ones.\n\n## The UI dialect (sketch)\n\nThe samples below are in\n[`case-studies/issue-1/samples/`](case-studies/issue-1/samples/) and are\nchecked by [`experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs):\n`links-notation` 0.27.1 parses every sample and formats it back to an equal\nlinks network.\n\nA document (structure, configuration and behaviour in one place):\n\n```lino\n(app: document\n  (title 'Links UI demo')\n  (theme material3)\n  (body: stack\n    (direction vertical)\n themes:\n\n```lino\n(material3: theme\n  (extends base)\n  (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n  (token space.medium 16px)\n  (token motion.duration.short 150ms))\n```\n\nAnimation and a recording:\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n(recording-1: recording\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nConfiguration overrides produced by the dev mode (what a user hands to an\nagent with \"make these the defaults\"):\n\n```lino\n(user-overrides: overrides\n  (layer user)\n  (base app)\n  (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n  (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n```\n\n### Links Notation parse shapes\n\nThe experiment\n[`experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs)\nshows that `links-notation` 0.27.1 returns **different link structures** for\nthe same element depending on how it is written:\n\n- `(ok: button (label 'OK'))` on one line gives one nested link;\n- the same text split over several lines inside parentheses, and the indented\n  form `ok: button` / `  label 'OK'`, are returned by `Parser.parse()` as\n  expanded path links such as `((ok: button) (label OK))`;\n- `Parser.parseGroups()` keeps the indented form as an explicit tree.\n\n`ui-core` therefore defines one **tree projection** that accepts all three\nforms and produces the same element tree. The dialect specification issue\nfixes this projection and its conformance fixtures.\n\n## Configuration layers and agent hand-off\n\nEvery value an element uses is resolved through ordered layers:\n\n1. `defaults` — the component's own defaults (shipped in the package);\n2. `theme` — the active theme(s), which may be nested per subtree;\n3. `site` — the application's committed LiNo configuration;\n4. `user` — overrides saved in the browser (IndexedDB);\n5. `session` — temporary overrides made in dev mode and not yet saved.\n\nDev mode writes only to `user` or `session`. \"Make these the defaults\" exports\nthe difference between the top layers and `site` as an `overrides` LiNo\ndocument, a share URL, and a ready-to-paste agent instruction. The agent then\napplies the patch to the committed `site` configuration.\n\n## Development/configuration mode and designer\n\n- Enter dev mode with a keyboard shortcut, a `?ui-dev` URL parameter, or a\n  `<ui-dev-mode>` element. Sites can disable or restrict it.\n- Hovering highlights elements and clicking selects them. The inspector shows\n  the outline tree (links network), the property grid (resolved value plus the\n  layer it came from), styles, tokens, animations and the LiNo source.\n- The WYSIWYG designer reuses the inspector and adds a toolbox, canvas drag\n  and drop, alignment guides, multi-select, undo/redo, docked panels,\n  two-way source sync and a timeline. It is built with the framework itself.\n\n## Themes and other frameworks as LiNo\n\nA theme is a LiNo package of tokens, style rules and component templates\n(the XAML control-template idea). Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG-guided and\n\"classic\" themes (deepcase versions, konard.github.io styles, retro desktop\nlooks) are just alternative packages. Migration from MUI, Fluent UI, shadcn/ui\nand other frameworks is a converter plus a mapping table into the same\ndialect.\n\n## Platforms\n\n- **Web:** custom elements (plain JavaScript), React and Vue wrappers over the\n  same core.\n- **React Native:** a renderer that maps dialect elements to React Native\n  primitives (New Architecture).\n- **Swift:** a SwiftPM package with a SwiftUI renderer. It reads LiNo with a\n  Swift parser (an upstream `links-notation` port, or a port created by the\n  roadmap if none exists).\n- **Kotlin:** a Gradle/Kotlin Multiplatform package with a Jetpack Compose /\n  Compose Multiplatform renderer, with the same parser condition.\n\nAll implementations run the shared conformance fixtures from `docs/spec/`.\n\n## Associative technology stack usage\n\n| Component                                                                      | Use in this framework                                                     |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)           | Canonical text format; parser and formatter for every implementation.    |\n| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)   | Strict encoding and decoding of object-shaped configuration.              |\n| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)           | CLI, environment and `.lenv` configuration of tools (converters, build).  |\n| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)                     | Localisation catalogs for every component and the designer.               |\n| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)             | Lossless CST networks for importing source code (JSX, Vue SFC, HTML).     |\n| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)                       | Query and substitution conventions for selectors and patches.            |\n| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)                 | Compatibility target for browser persistence of the links store.         |\n| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) | Context-relative values (per theme, per user, per device) as a model.    |\n\nThe full mapping, including which components are direct dependencies, is in\nthe case study.\n"

[2026-11-01T11:38:28.230Z] [INFO]     "content": "# Architecture (proposal)\n\nThis document is the target architecture of the associative UI framework\nplanned in [issue #1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1). It is a\n**proposal**: every part of it is delivered by a roadmap issue listed in\n[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), and each roadmap issue may refine it. The evidence\nbehind each decision is in the\n[issue 1 case study](case-studies/issue-1/README.md).\n\n## Principles\n\n1. **Links first.** Every UI concept (element, property, style rule, design\n   token, theme, behaviour, data binding, animation, recording, configuration\n   override, asset licence) is a link in a links network. Links Notation\n   (LiNo, [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation))\n   is its only canonical text form. JSON, CSS, JSX, XAML, SwiftUI and so on are\n   import or export formats, never the source of truth.\n2. **One dialect.** Structure, configuration, styles, tokens, animations and\n   recordings use one LiNo vocabulary (the _UI dialect_), so any other UI\n   framework can be described as a LiNo document in that dialect.\n3. **Sharable by default.** A UI, a theme, a set of overrides or a recording is\n   a plain LiNo text that can be pasted into an issue, a chat with an agent,\n   or a URL.\n4. **Runtime interpreter, thin renderers.** One platform-neutral core\n   interprets the links network. Each platform (DOM, React, Vue, React Native,\n   SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose) has a thin renderer. Code generation is used only\n   for wrappers, types and optional \"eject to code\" exports.\n5. **JavaScript first.** As required by [`javascript-first.md`](javascript-first.md),\n   the JavaScript implementation and shared conformance fixtures come first.\n   Swift and Kotlin ports must pass the same fixtures.\n6. **Everything editable at runtime.** Every rendered element keeps a stable\n   link ID that maps back to its LiNo source. This is what makes the\n   development/configuration mode and the WYSIWYG designer possible on any\n   site built with the framework.\n7. **Public domain.** Code is released under the [Unlicense](../LICENSE). Our\n   own non-code assets are dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0).\n   Third-party assets are allowed only with a machine-readable record of the\n   source, copyright holder, licence (SPDX ID) and attribution text.\n\n## Layers\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph Sources[\"LiNo sources (sharable text)\"]\n    Doc[\"documents<br/>(structure)\"]\n    Tok[\"tokens & themes\"]\n    Sty[\"styles\"]\n    Ani[\"animations & recordings\"]\n    Cfg[\"configuration overrides\"]\n    Ast[\"asset records\"]\n  end\n  Sources --> Core[\"ui-core<br/>parse · validate · project · diff/patch\"]\n  Core --> Store[\"links store<br/>(in-memory network, transactions, undo/redo,<br/>IndexedDB / doublets-web persistence)\"]\n  Store --> Config[\"configuration layers<br/>defaults < theme < site < user < session\"]\n  Config --> Engine[\"style & token resolver,<br/>behaviour state machines, animation engine\"]\n  Engine --> DOM[\"DOM renderer<br/>(custom elements)\"]\n  DOM --> React[\"React adapter\"]\n  DOM --> Vue[\"Vue adapter\"]\n  Engine --> RN[\"React Native renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Swift[\"SwiftUI renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Kotlin[\"Compose renderer\"]\n  Store --> Dev[\"dev/configuration mode<br/>(inspector overlay)\"]\n  Dev --> Designer[\"WYSIWYG designer\"]\n  Dev --> Export[\"export overrides as LiNo<br/>(agent hand-off, share URL)\"]\n```\n\n| Layer It is a library of imports and also a deep package (its links are in `deep.json`).\n   - Core libraries: Next.js 14 (peer dependency), React 18, Chakra UI v2 with Emotion, framer-motion, Cytoscape, Monaco through `@monaco-editor/react`, Slate (WYSIWYG), and rjsf (JSON-schema forms).\n   - Other libraries: recharts, amcharts5, d3 / d3-force-3d, react-d3-cloud, aframe plus aframe-forcegraph (the 3D work is commented out), react-grid-layout, re-resizable, i18next, react-icons, xterm, peerjs, emoji-picker-react, yandex-maps, react-hook-form.\n\n   **Apps around it**\n   - deepcase-app (v0.1.0-beta.41, Unlicense) is a shell built on the deep-foundation SDK. It ships to the web as a Next.js app, to Android and iOS through Capacitor, to desktop through Electron (Capacitor community), and as a Chrome extension. Docker and a Helm chart are also included.\n   - Its pages:\n     - `pages/index.tsx` is the main graph.\n     - `pages/client-handler.tsx` opens a handler full-tab, e.g. `/client-handler?props={\"linkId\":..,\"handlerId\":..}`.\n     - The others are `editor`, `card`, `component`, `message` and `cyber`.\n   - It is wrapped in providers in this order: StaticProviders → Provider(gqlPath) → DeepNamespaceProvider → MinilinksProvider → DeepProvider → Connector → AutoGuest → Content.\n\n   **Client handlers (UI stored as links)**\n   - The link pattern is: a `Handler` link goes from `clientSupportsJs` to a `TSX` code link, and a `HandleClient` link goes from a Type to that Handler.\n   - Handler source looks like `({deep, require}) => { const React = require('react'); ... return Component }`.\n   - `evalClientHandler` in deeplinks uses `eval(value)` and expects a function back. It calls that function with `{deep, gql, ...input}`, where `require` is a whitelisted map (`r.list`). `DeepClient.resolveDependency` lazy-loads heavier modules.\n   - `deep._findHandler({handlerId, context})` queries the `handlers` table, filtered by JSExecutionProvider. With no handlerId, it matches a `@deep-foundation/deepcase` `Context` link from the context ids.\n   - Errors are caught by `CatchErrors` (an error boundary) and shown as a Chakra Alert with a reset button.\n   - `deep.json` defines these handlers:\n     - asyncFileClientHandler\n     - stringClientHandler (for Join, PackageQuery and Contain)\n     - queryClientHandler\n     - editorClientHandler (for SyncTextFile and TSX)\n   - It also defines the types `Traveler` (from Any to Query, symbol 🧳), `ContextToken` and `Context`.\n\n   **HandleCyto (graph handlers)**\n   - The package `@deep-foundation/handle-cyto` provides `HandleCyto`. A handler of this kind returns Cytoscape `elements` and `stylesheets` for links of a given type, so per-type graph rendering is itself stored as links.\n   - It can be switched on and off per rule (`useCytoHandlersRules`). `HandleCytoContainInvisible` is one example.\n\n   **Space / Focus / Opened model (window state stored as links)**\n   - `useSpaceId` and `useContainer` are kept in the query store, i.e. the URL.\n   - Node positions are `Focus` links (from the space to the link) whose value is `{x, y}`. \"clear focuses\" and \"unlock\" remove them.\n   - Opened windows are links from `@deep-foundation/deepcase-opened`: an `Opened` link goes from the space to the link, and an `OpenedHandler` link goes from that Opened link to the handler. Both are contained by the space.\n   - In code, `useOpenedMethods()` in `cyto/opened.tsx` provides `open(id, handlerId)`, `close(id)` and `isOpened(id)`.\n   - Handler windows float as React overlays anchored to graph nodes. `CytoReactLayout` (`cyto/react.tsx`) syncs a div's transform to Cytoscape pan/zoom and node positions through cy events (`render`, `add`, `layoutstop`, `data`, `pan zoom`, `position bounds`).\n   - Each window header has:\n     - a handler picker popover (`CytoReactLinksCard`)\n     - an \"open new full tab\" button\n     - a close button\n\n   **Graph**\n   - `cyto/graph.tsx` uses react-cytoscapejs with these plugins:\n     - dagre\n     - cola\n     - d3-force\n     - cytoscape-deep-d3-force (custom)\n     - a custom fork of cxtmenu (`cyto/cxtmenu.tsx`)\n     - edge-connections\n     - edgehandles\n   - Layouts are in `cyto/layouts.tsx`:\n     - `cola` uses edgeLength = 100 + 10 × (number of connected edges).\n     - `deep-d3-force` uses manyBodyStrength -2000, linkDistance 100, alpha 0.8 and infinite: true. This is the default, stored in localStore 'layout'.\n   - A link is drawn as a node plus edges, styled in `cyto/stylesheets.tsx`:\n     - `.link-from` edges have a 'tee' arrow.\n     - `.link-to` edges have a triangle arrow.\n     - `.link-type` edges are dashed [5,5] with a triangle arrow.\n     - `.link-node` is 30×30, white, with a label.\n     - Hover draws a blue underlay (#0080ff).\n     - `.focused` draws a border-width 4 in blue.500.\n     - Query nodes (`.query-link-*-node`) are small, at 8 or 16 px.\n     - `:parent` compound nodes are gray at 0.1 opacity.\n   - Node label format (`cyto/elements.tsx`): `id\\ntype:Name\\nname:Name\\nvalue (truncated to 20 chars as 11+...+9)\\n\\n symbol`. The symbol comes from the type's Symbol link and defaults to 📍. Missing endpoints are auto-added as id-only nodes.\n\n   **Context menus**\n   - The node radial menu has radius 108, activeFillColor rgba(0,128,255,0.75), and opens on cxttapstart or taphold. Its items are: editor, unlock, delete, delete down, insert, update, login, space, container, traveler (n), readme.\n   - The background (core) menu has: insert, center, query.\n\n   **Traveler**\n   - The Traveler sub-menu (`cyto/traveler.tsx`) toggles query links that pull in related links. Its directions are: types, out, in, up, down, to, from, typed, and all/by-type. A Traveler link points to a Query link that is Active and Contained by the space.\n\n   **Top menu**\n   - The top menu is `cyto/menu.tsx` and is animated with framer-motion.\n   - It shows attached ButtonGroups for:\n     - auth (linkId, with an X to log out)\n     - space id (X)\n     - container id (X)\n     - copy token / paste token / login token\n     - gql\n     - editor\n   - Its switches are: autofocus, focus, opened, debug, types, traveler, breadcrumbs, cytoHandlers, animation.\n   - It also has a layout selector, a search box (`MenuSearch`), \"clear focuses\", a Travelers popover and a CytoHandlers popover.\n   - Elsewhere on the screen:\n     - the version text sits bottom-left\n     - the dark-mode toggle is a sun/moon animated button fixed top-right (`switch-mode.tsx`)\n     - a \"packager\" button opens `PackagerInterface` (npm search plus install and uninstall tabs)\n     - a \"connector\" button opens the connection portal (local docker/engine)\n   - UI state lives in `@deep-foundation/store`: `useQueryStore` (URL), `useLocalStore` and `useCookiesStore`.\n\n   **Editor**\n   - `CytoEditor` (`cyto/editor.tsx`) is a Monaco modal with tabs stored in localStore 'editor-tabs' and 'editor-tab', and draft values kept in localStore 'editor-values' with a 500 ms debounce.\n   - `EditorTab` holds `{id, saved, active, loading, initialValue}` and shows an unsaved indicator.\n   - `EditorGrid` gives two columns (or a VerticalSash split): Monaco on the left, and on the right a switch between Preview, Handlers and Results areas.\n   - The preview has a fillSize toggle, a language list (`editor-lang-list`) and TS diagnostics options.\n   - `DeepWysiwyg` (`deep-wysiwyg.tsx`) is a Slate rich text editor with Mark and Block buttons (bold, italic, underline, code, headings, quote, lists, align) and HTML serialization through slate-serializers. `useStringSaver` saves to the link's string value.\n\n   **Theming**\n   - Key Technical Concepts (findings so far):\n\n**LiNo syntax** (docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md, EBNF v0.24.0; grammar also expressed in LiNo at docs/grammar/grammar.lino):\n- A link is a sequence of references, written `(id: v1 v2 …)`. The id is optional.\n- Parentheses can be omitted when a whole line is a single link.\n- Indented ID link:\n  ```\n  family:\n    papa\n    mama\n  ```\n- A bare value with indented children forms an anonymous nested link: `root:\\n child1\\n child2\\n  grandchild` becomes `(root: child1 (child2 grandchild))`.\n- Indentation counts spaces only. The first line sets the base indentation, and children must be indented more than their parent.\n- Multi-line groups (issue #282): `value (\\n id \"1\"\\n label \"one\"\\n)` becomes `(value ((id 1) (label one)))`. A group body opens a nested context that starts at indentation level 0. A single-line body collapses, so `(a b c)` is unchanged, while `((a b))` stays distinct from `(a b)`.\n- References:\n  - Simple references exclude whitespace, `(`, `:` and `)`.\n  - The delimiters `\"`, `'` and `` ` `` behave identically.\n  - N-quoted runs: a run of 2N delimiters inside the body means N literal delimiters.\n  - A bare pair `\"\"` is the empty reference.\n  - Version-1 lossless literals `~1{hex UTF-8}` exist since 0.24.0. The prefix `~[0-9]+{` is reserved.\n- Comments (issue #301): `#` starts a comment only at the start of the document or after whitespace. `issue#1047` and `\"#\"` stay literal. Comments are replaced by spaces, so positions are preserved. They are on by default; `comments:false` turns them off. Formatters quote references that begin with `#` (`'#tag'`).\n- Streaming parsers exist in all 8 languages, with push events plus iterators.\n- A binary links notation v1 exists (docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md), originating in link-cli PR #106. It has golden vectors and a 0x1_ header byte.\n\n**Implementations** (all hand-written; JS is defined first; parity is checked via parity/text-fixtures.json):\n\n| Language | Package / access | Version / status | Tests |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| JS | npm `links-notation` (Peggy grammar; TS types; no runtime deps; browser-safe since 0.27.1, which fixed #351 events polyfill) | 0.27.1 | 316 |\n| Rust | crate `links-notation`, `parse_lino`, plus `links-notation-macro` 0.1.2 with a `lino!` compile-time macro | 0.27.1 | 401 |\n| C# | NuGet `Link.Foundation.Links.Notation` (Pegasus) | 0.27.1 | 295 |\n| Python | PyPI `links-notation`, `from links_notation import Parser` | 0.27.1 | 247 |\n| Go | `github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/go`, `lino.Parse` | v0.27.1 | 139 |\n| Java | `io.github.link-foundation:links-notation` | not published to Maven Central (open issue #192) | 185 |\n| PHP | `link-foundation/links-notation` | not on Packagist (#192) | 235 |\n| C++ | CMake release archive | 0.27.1 | 346 |\n\n- There is no Swift or Kotlin implementation.
