19, 25, 26, 28, 31, 36, 39, 41).\n\n### 1.3 Links Notation usage\n\nNeither repo uses Links Notation. There are no `.lino` files and no `links-notation` dependency or reference in either repo. All configuration is TypeScript/JS objects, serialized as JSON to localStorage, to a URL hash (immortality) or to a downloaded `acs-config.json` (anime-avatar). Both formats are flat or two-level key/value maps, so they map directly to links (see section 9).\n\n## 2. Configurability model\n\n### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n\n`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n\n- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Examples: `PALETTES` (12), `SURFACES` (13 panel materials), `FRAME_STYLES` (9), `BACKGROUNDS` (21), `BACKDROP_GRADIENTS` (7), `FONTS`, `TITLE_STYLES`, `TEXT_EFFECTS`, `INTROS`, `CHART_STYLES`, `CURSORS`, `TABLE_STYLES`, `SCROLLBAR_STYLES`, `ENTRANCES`, `SOUNDS` (26). Id union types are derived with `(typeof X)[number]['id']`, so adding an option updates the types.\n- **Reference registry.** `REFERENCES: Record<ReferenceId, {label, url}>` cites the design source of each option (Arwes, thegridcn, Soul Extract, glitchy.website and others). The panel renders these as links next to each axis.\n- **Axes.** `AXES` has 49 entries:\n  `Axis = ChoiceAxis {kind:'choice', options, display?:'buttons'|'select'} | ToggleAxis {kind:'toggle'} | RangeAxis {kind:'range', min, max, step, unit}`.\n  The shared base is `{key, label, group, description?, sources?}`. `SETTING_GROUPS` defines 8 groups: Color, Panels, Type & text, Scene, HUD & charts, Controls & data, Motion, Audio.\n- **Pure functions over the schema:**\n  - `coerceAxisValue` and `coerceSoundList` validate one value.\n  - `mergeSettings(base, raw)` accepts untrusted input and drops invalid keys.\n  - `diffSettings` and `diffFromDefaults` compute what changed.\n  - `parseStoredSettings` and `migrateLegacySettings` handle storage. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n  - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n  - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`--corner`, `--border-width`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`, `--font-scale`, `--chart-line`, `--bg-speed`, `--motion-scale`, `--bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n  - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n  - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `--fill` variable.\n  - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n  - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n  - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\n### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n\n- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n  - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n  - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n  - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n  - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.\n  - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color and intensity.\n  - Scene and cameras: `bg`, ground, `floorGrid`, `camera*`, a separate `svgCam*` set.\n  - Toggles: `autoRotate`, `mirrorArms`, `showFPS`, and an experimental joint gizmo.\n- `App.jsx` keeps cfg in React state, persists it to localStorage key `acs_B` merged over defaults, and keeps the view (`editor|tests|split|none`) in `?view=` and `acs_view`. It exposes `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}` so in-app tests can drive the UI.\n- There is no schema. Each control is hand-wired in `Editor.jsx` using `Studio.Section/Row/Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle` from `ui.jsx`. Ranges, steps and labels live inline in JSX.\n- Every `Section` has a randomize button and a reset button. `randomizers.js` implements per-group randomize and reset, and respects `ACS_BONE_LIMITS`.\n- Config I/O: Export downloads `acs-config.json`. Import does `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(text)}` and reports errors with `alert`.\n- Engine binding: `apply.js` `ACS_applyAll` runs every frame and pushes cfg into three.js state (pose merge, idle, gestures, look-at, expressions, blink, materials, grid, debug helpers). This is a declarative-state to imperative-scene reconciler.\n\n### 2.3 anime-avatar archive\n\n- `ConfigPanel.jsx` holds about 17 props: skin, hair, eye and clothes colors, blink interval, animation speed, idle and blink toggles, background, `detailLevel` 1 to 10, legs, 3D, shadows, LOD, scale, `modelUrl`.\n- `useAnimationCycle({minInterval, maxInterval, animationDuration, excludeFromCycle})` picks a random named animation (idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised) on a timer.\n\n## 3. Animation and 3D\n\n### 3.1 immortality (2D UI motion)\n\n- **Text effects** (`textEffects.ts`): `revealOrder`, `decipherFrame` and `sequenceFrame` are pure functions of `(text, t, seed)`. A component only supplies the clock. This makes them deterministic, testable and easy to record. Ported from Arwes (MIT) and re-implemented from Soul Extract ideas (GPL, ideas only).\n- **Entrances and staggering** are CSS animations scaled by `--motion-scale`. A fixed bug is documented in [case study issue-7](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7): `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels after the animation and made borders look glitchy. It is now `backwards`.\n- **Backgrounds** (`Starfield.tsx`): 21 canvas renderers with `seededRandom`, `parseColor` and `useReducedMotion`. One background (\"resonance\") reacts to sound cues via `onSoundCue`, an event bus from `sound.ts`.\n- **Pointer-reactive glow** in `Frame.tsx` writes `--mx/--my` directly on the element, with no React state.\n- **Overlays** (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) use `pointer-events:none`. The old `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was replaced with a smooth breathing glow, a photosensitivity fix.\n- **Sound as part of motion**: `sound.ts` has 10 UI events (hover, click, toggle, select, scan, open, close, type, intro, notify), up to 6 sounds per event, and random, cycle or layer modes. The bus is tone shelf, then compressor/limiter, then convolution reverb send, with pointer-positioned stereo. The AudioContext is created lazily because of autoplay rules. `throttledScan` limits repeated scan sounds.\n- No recording or timeline. All motion is either CSS or a clock-driven pure function.\n\n### 3.2 anime-avatar (3D character motion)\n\n- **Clip playback**: three.js `AnimationMixer`. `retargetMixamoToVRM(asset, vrm)` in `animations.js` maps Mixamo bone names through `ACS_MIXAMO_RIG_MAP`, rebuilds `QuaternionKeyframeTrack` and `VectorKeyframeTrack` data, scales hips by rig height, and flips axes for VRM0.\n- **Procedural gestures**: `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` in `gestures.js` is stateless and returns `{rot, exprs}` deltas.\n  - Gestures are `ACS_GESTURE_PRESETS` (wave, nod, shake, bow, each with duration, expression and peak).\n  - Moods are `ACS_MOOD_PRESETS` (`ampScale`, `speedScale`, expression, weight).\n  - Easings are `ACS_EASINGS` (linear, sine, quad, cubic, easeOut, easeInOut, backOut).\n  - Bell and sustained envelopes shape each gesture.\n- **Additive layering**: [case study issue-28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28) established that all motion sources (pose, idle, gestures, look-at, text-motion, mouse force) add relative deltas each frame instead of replacing each other, which removes snaps at gesture start and end. `ACS_mergePose` sums pose and manual rotations, and `mergeExpressionDeltas` sums expressions.\n- **Anatomical constraints**: `ACS_BONE_LIMITS` gives per-bone, per-axis ranges in degrees, citing range-of-motion references. `ACS_clampBoneRad` applies them, and sliders show degrees.\n- **Gaze**: smoothed look-at follows the camera, the mouse or random targets, with a cone, saccades and separate eye and head shares.\n- **Text to motion** (`textMotion.js`): a regex command table (slowWalk, run, happyWalk, stealth and others) maps to GR00T modes and procedural bone deltas, and declares resource requirements. `gearSonic.js` fetches real GEAR-SONIC reference motions (joint_pos, root_pos, root_quat at 50 fps) and a Unitree G1 MJCF/STL robot, and can call a backend.\n- **Speech** (`ipaSpeech.js`): an English-to-IPA lexicon produces a phoneme timeline, which drives VRM mouth expressions and the jaw.\n- **Text to model** (`textToModel.js`): a TRELLIS backend client. With no URL configured it returns `{status:'no-backend'}`, so the feature degrades cleanly.\n- **Editing**: an experimental TransformControls joint gizmo (one joint at a time, hover or tap to switch, off by default).\n- **Export**: GLB (`-edited.glb` via GLTFExporter) and SVG (`ACS_vrmToSVG` projects triangles with back-face culling and depth sort). The SVG export has its own camera settings.\n- **Loading**: `modelLoader.js` handles glTF/VRM, FBX, OBJ, STL, PLY and MMD (PMX/VMD), including zip, rar and 7z archives (fflate and libarchive WASM). `ACS_normalizeModelURL` rewrites GitHub `blob/` and `raw/refs/heads/` URLs to raw download URLs, and `ACS_detectModelFormat` infers the format.\n- **Archive demo**: CSS `@keyframes` (talk, breathe, headSway) on SVG parts, plus a parallel three.js part tree.\n- **Recording**: absent. Screenshot or video export, custom pose saving and a scene editor are only listed in `ROADMAP.md`. There is no MediaRecorder use and no user-editable keyframe timeline.\n\n## 4. Assets and licensing\n\n### 4.1 immortality: zero-asset, cite-everything\n\n- It ships no images or audio. Everything is generated: canvas, SVG, CSS gradients, `feTurbulence` noise and Web Audio. Fonts are OFL `@fontsource` packages.\n- Each option and each sound carries provenance. `OptionDef.source` points into `REFERENCES {label,url}`, and `SOUNDS` entries have `{character, sourceLabel, sourceUrl}`. Sounds have neutral names; the source names say what inspired them.\n- License decisions are recorded per source in [`docs/case-studies/issue-7`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7):\n  - Arwes is MIT, so code was ported with attribution in comments (`frameShapes.ts`, `textEffects.ts`).\n  - Soul Extract is GPL-3.0, so only ideas were re-implemented and no code was copied.\n  - thegridcn has no license, so it was used as a visual reference only.\n- Library choices were weighed by size. Tone.js (about 77 KB) was rejected for plain Web Audio, and the Select was hand-rolled with downshift as the fallback. The framework should keep this habit of recording rejected alternatives.\n\n### 4.2 anime-avatar: per-asset metadata and conditional attribution\n\n- `ACS_MODEL_PRESETS` entries have the shape `{id, label, url, format, kind, credit, license, flipped?, attributionRequired?}`. Examples:\n  - pixiv VRM1 sample and Seed-san: VRM Public License 1.0.\n  - Alicia Solid: Niconi Commons, attribution required, `flipped`.\n  - V-Sekai girl: \"See repository\".\n  - Khronos Duck: CC-BY 4.0.\n  - DamagedHelmet: CC-BY-NC 4.0.\n  - Unitree G1: NVIDIA.\n- `ACS_ANIMATION_PRESETS` (Samba and Mixamo idle from the three.js examples, Gangnam Style from V-Sekai) carry `credit` and `license: 'Mixamo terms (free use with your avatar)'`.\n- `attributionRequired(vrmMeta, preset, animMeta)` in `Editor.jsx` decides attribution in this order:\n  1. VRM `creditNotation`.\n  2. The preset flag.\n  3. The animation flag.\n  4. A license-string heuristic (CC-BY, Niconi, \"attribution\").\n  `AttributionOverlay` shows a credit on the stage only when attribution is required ([issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)). The Metadata section shows the loaded VRM meta.\n- **Risks.**\n  - `ACS_GF2_MMD_MODEL_ARCHIVES` hot-links about 70 proprietary SUNBORN Girls' Frontline 2 MMD archives from the publisher CDN, with license text \"Official GF2 Exilium art page download\".\n  - DamagedHelmet is non-commercial.\n  - \"See repository\" and \"CC-ish\" are not license identifiers.\n  - Assets are loaded at runtime from third-party URLs (unpkg, three.js examples, GitHub raw). Availability and integrity are not pinned; there is no SRI.\n  - None of these assets may enter a public-domain framework asset set.\n\n## 5. Components inventory\n\n| Component / module | Repo | Kind | Reusable for the framework as |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `settings.ts` axis schema, presets, migration, diff, share | immortality | data and logic | **Core config model** (to re-express in Links Notation) |\n| `SettingsPanel` + `AxisControl` | immortality | generic panel | Auto-generated \"configuration mode\" inspector |\n| `Select` (WAI-ARIA select-only combobox, type-ahead, edge flip) | immortality | control | Base dropdown |\n| `Frame` + `frameShapes.ts` (9 frames, chamfer, glow, material layer) | immortality | container | Themed panel/\"window chrome\" primitive |\n| `FxText` + `textEffects.ts` | immortality | text | Animated text primitive |\n| `Starfield` (21 canvas backgrounds) | immortality | background | Theme backdrop plugins |\n| `Overlays` (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) | immortality | overlay | Theme post-effects |\n| `sound.ts` (26 voices, 10 events) | immortality | audio | UI sound theme layer |\n| `LineChart`, `DataTable` (accessible twins), `Gauge`, `StatTile`, sparkline | immortality | data viz | Chart widgets with an a11y table fallback |\n| `HudBar` (UTC clock), `Intro` (boot sequence) | immortality | chrome | Theme chrome |\n| `useElementWidth` (ResizeObserver), `useReducedMotion`, `motionAllowed` | immortality | hooks | Platform utilities |\n| `Studio.GlassPanel`, `ConfigDrawer`, `Section` (randomize/reset), `Row`, `Slider`, `ColorPick`, `Select`, `Chips`, `Toggle`, `Stage`, `useIsMobile` | anime-avatar | panel kit | Second panel kit; plugin candidates |\n| `modelLoader.js`, `svg.js` | anime-avatar | IO | 3D asset plugin; vector export idea |\n| `AttributionOverlay` + `attributionRequired` | anime-avatar | licensing UI | **Core attribution component** |\n| Archive `AvatarSVG`, `Avatar3D`, `ConfigPanel`, `useAnimationCycle` | anime-avatar | demo | Reference only |\n\n## 6. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **One declarative schema per configurable surface.** Declare every setting once as `{key, label, group, kind, options|min/max/step/unit, description, sources}`. Validation, defaults, the panel, presets, randomizer, diff, sharing, migration and tests all derive from it (immortality `AXES`). In the framework this schema should itself be a Links Notation document.\n2. **Option catalogs with ids, labels, descriptions and provenance.** Derive types from the catalog (`(typeof X)[number]['id']`), so adding an option to a theme is a one-line data change.\n3. **Store and share only the diff from defaults.** `diffFromDefaults`, plus a version tag (`v:2`), makes share links short, survives default changes and supports \"N customized\" counters.\n4. **Treat all external config as untrusted.** `mergeSettings(base, raw)` coerces each value and drops unknown keys. Apply this to imports, URL hashes and storage (anime-avatar currently does not).\n5. **Versioned persistence with intent-preserving migration.** Keep only what the user changed from the old defaults, so the new defaults still take effect.\n6. **Comfort settings stay local.** When applying a shared look or preset, keep the viewer's accessibility and comfort keys (motion, sound, volume). Lock the same keys from randomization.\n7. **Presets are partial overrides over a base**, with `isPresetActive` detection and source citations.\n8. **Randomize and reset per group and globally, with an injected RNG**, respecting constraints (bone limits) and locked keys. This makes visual exploration safe and reproducible.\n9. **Project theme state to `data-*` attributes and CSS variables** instead of re-rendering. This is cheap, framework-agnostic and works the same for plain JS, React and Vue. A test then checks that every option has a CSS rule (`styling.test.ts`).\n10. **High-frequency visuals bypass the component tree.** Pointer glow (`--mx/--my`), canvas backgrounds and the per-frame `apply.js` loop write directly to the DOM or scene.\n11. **Animations as pure functions of time** (`decipherFrame(text,t,seed)`, `ACS_gestureDelta(name,t,mood,easing)`). They are deterministic, so they can be recorded, replayed, scrubbed and tested. This is the natural basis for the framework's animation recording: record the clock and inputs, not the pixels.\n12. **Additive animation layers.** Each source contributes deltas that are summed each frame, with envelopes for start and end, so nothing snaps (anime-avatar issue-28).\n13. **Named easing and envelope catalog** (`ACS_EASINGS`, bell and sustained) shared by every animation.\n14. **Domain constraints as data** (`ACS_BONE_LIMITS` in degrees, with references), used for clamping sliders, randomizers and gizmos alike.\n15. **Reduced motion and photosensitivity by default.** Use `motionAllowed()` (the setting combined with `prefers-reduced-motion`), and avoid hard flashes, which is the reason the flicker was replaced.\n16. **Accessible panel conventions**: a non-modal docked drawer, Escape to close, focus return, arrow-key tabs, `aria-pressed` toggles, `<output>` for ranges, an `aria-live` change counter, and a clipboard fallback.\n17. **Accessible data twins**: every chart has a table equivalent, `role=img` and a text summary.\n18. **UI sound theme** as a separate configurable layer: an event-to-sounds map, modes (random, cycle, layer), master bus, lazy AudioContext, throttling, and a cue event bus that visuals can subscribe to.\n19. **Zero-binary assets.** Generate visuals and sounds procedurally so the framework's own assets are trivially public domain.\n20. **Provenance on every borrowed item** (`source`, `sourceUrl`, `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired`), with license decisions recorded per source (MIT port, GPL ideas only, no license means reference only).\n21. **Conditional attribution UI**: show credits only when the asset's metadata or license requires it, and always expose a Metadata/Credits view.\n22. **Dev mode exposes a state handle** (`window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`) plus an in-app test runner that does not autostart, can be stopped and keeps its scroll position (issue #19). This fits a \"configuration mode\" well.\n23. **View state in the URL** (`?view=`, `#ui=`), consumed and then cleaned with `replaceState`, and listening to `hashchange`.\n24. **Graceful optional backends**: AI features return a typed `{status:'no-backend'}` instead of failing.\n25. **URL normalization for user-supplied resources** (GitHub `blob/` to raw) and per-asset fix-up flags such as `flipped`.\n26. **Case-study per issue** (requirements table, root causes, rejected libraries). Both repos already do this, and link-foundation/ui should continue it.\n\n## 7. Duplication candidates\n\nBoth repos independently built the same subsystems. They should become single framework modules:\n\n| Concern | immortality | anime-avatar | Unified module |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Settings schema | `AXES`, typed | implicit in `defaults.js` and `Editor.jsx` JSX | Links Notation schema with `choice/toggle/range/color/vector/list` kinds |\n| Panel controls | `AxisControl`, `Select`, range with `<output>` | `Studio.Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle/Row` | One control set rendered from the schema |\n| Drawer and panel chrome | `SettingsPanel` drawer, `Frame` | `ConfigDrawer`, `GlassPanel` (inline styles) | Themeable panel primitive |\n| Group randomize and reset | `randomizeSettings`, Restore defaults | `randomizers.js`, per-`Section` buttons | Schema-driven randomize/reset with locks and constraints |\n| Persistence | `loadSettings/saveSettings`, versioned key, migration | `localStorage` `acs_B` shallow merge | One store with versioning, migration, and a diff codec |\n| Share and export | `#ui=` hash of the diff | `acs-config.json` download and import | Links Notation text for both URL and file |\n| Easing and timing | CSS timing functions, text-effect clocks | `ACS_EASINGS`, envelopes | Shared easing catalog usable in CSS and JS |\n| Motion preference | `motionAllowed`, `useReducedMotion` | none in the studio (idle, auto-rotate and gaze always on unless toggled) | Platform motion policy |\n| Responsive helpers | `useElementWidth` | `useIsMobile` (720 px) | Shared breakpoint and size utilities |\n| Provenance metadata | `REFERENCES`, `source`, `sourceUrl` | `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired` | One attribution record, using SPDX ids where possible |\n| Visual regression | `experiments/preset-gallery.js` screenshots, `styling.test.ts` | canvas fingerprint, `probeDiff`, PR #17 image compare | Shared screenshot and fingerprint test harness |\n| Canvas backgrounds | `Starfield` (21) | scene background and grid, archive petals | Background plugin interface |\n\n## 8. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 8.1 immortality\n\n1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n\n### 8.2 anime-avatar\n\n1. **No build step in production**: Babel standalone transpiles JSX in the browser on every load, React runs in its development UMD build, and dependencies come from unpkg without SRI. This is slow, fragile and unsafe for a framework.\n2. **Global namespace modules** (`window.ACS_*`, `window.Studio`, `window.__acs`) with implicit load order in `index.html`.\n3. **Monoliths**: `Editor.jsx` is 2381 lines in one component, and `apply.js` is 1316 lines. All styling is inline style objects, so there is no theming.\n4. **Two divergent apps** in one repo (studio in `public/` and the archived Vite app in `src/`). The README mostly documents the archive, and the archive's 2D and 3D part trees (`components/svg/*`, `components/three/*`) duplicate each other.\n5. **Weak config validation**: import does a shallow `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse}`. Nested `rot/scale/expr` are not validated, unknown keys persist, errors use `alert`. There is no storage version or migration, and the key `acs_B` is opaque.\n6. **No schema**: ranges and labels are duplicated between `Editor.jsx` and `randomizers.js`.\n7. **Licensing**: the proprietary GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, and vague license strings (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\"). The license-string heuristic in `attributionRequired` can miss cases.\n8. **Bugs called out in [issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)** (since addressed): the Alicia model loaded back-to-front, GitHub `blob/` URLs failed, loading errors never auto-hid, tests autostarted and could not be stopped, the test log forced scroll to the bottom, split view was shown on mobile, and copyright was shown unconditionally.\n9. **Bugs called out in [issue #28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/28)**: an unnatural wave, non-anatomical slider ranges shown in radians, and gestures replacing look-at instead of adding to it, which caused snaps.\n10. **No animation recording** and no keyframe editing. The Mixamo retarget only plays existing clips. Pose, scene editor and video export are only on the roadmap.\n11. **Open requests** show demand for more model sources and mocap: [#18](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/18) (VRoid Hub, CharacterStudio), [#21](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/21) (kalidokit), [#22](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/22) (webaverse), [#23](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/23) (airi), [#24](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/24) (GitHub miner), [#38](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/38). [PR #17](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/pull/17) (image-comparison e2e) is still open.\n\n## 9. Migration notes\n\n### 9.1 Representing both configs in Links Notation\n\nAn immortality axis declaration could become:\n\n```lino\n(axis surface\n  (label \"Panel material\")\n  (group panels)\n  (kind choice)\n  (display buttons)\n  (options glass carbon brushed-metal hologram ...)\n  (sources arwes thegridcn))\n(option glass (of surface) (label \"Glass\") (source arwes))\n(reference arwes (label \"Arwes\") (url \"https://arwes.dev\"))\n```\n\nA user's settings would be the diff from defaults:\n\n```lino\n(settings (version 2)\n  (palette ares)\n  (frame octagon)\n  (glow 0.6)\n  (sounds (click soft-tick glass-tap)))\n```\n\nThe anime-avatar cfg, including nested bone rotations:\n\n```lino\n(cfg (version 1)\n  (model (preset seed-san))\n  (rot (rightUpperArm (z -80)) (rightLowerArm (x -90)))\n  (expr (happy 0.4))\n  (light (key (color \"#ffffff\") (intensity 1.2))))\n```\n\nThe asset provenance record:\n\n```lino\n(asset alicia-solid\n  (url \"...\")\n  (format vrm)\n  (credit \"DWANGO Co., Ltd.\")\n  (license (spdx LicenseRef-Niconi-Commons))\n  (attribution required)\n  (fixup flipped))\n```\n\n### 9.2 Steps\n\n1. **Port the `settings.ts` engine first.** Keep `coerce`, `merge`, `diff`, `migrate`, `encode/decode`, `applySharedLook` and `randomize` as framework-neutral pure functions, but read and write the schema and values as Links Notation. Swap the JSON share hash for a Links Notation hash and keep a JSON v2 reader for old links.\n2. **Extend the axis kinds** to cover anime-avatar: `color`, `vector3` (bone rotation with per-axis limits and units), `map` (per-bone, per-mesh, per-expression), `list` (sounds per event), `asset` (URL plus format plus provenance), and `action` (buttons such as gestures and export).\n3. **Add rendering hints to the schema** (`render data-attr|css-var|engine`), so `Shell`, the test assertions and engine bridges (`apply.js`-style reconcilers) are all generated.\n4. **Generate the configuration-mode inspector** from the schema. It should merge `AxisControl` (a11y, sources, display hints) with the `Studio` kit (per-section randomize/reset, color pickers, chips, mobile full-screen drawer). [2026-11-01T11:39:02.918Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Research: konard/konard.github.io and konard/links-visuals\n\nSource research for [link-foundation/ui#1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1).\nIts goals are:\n\n- an associative UI framework that is fully configurable and representable in Links Notation\n- a DOM-like language\n- animation recording\n- a WYSIWYG configuration mode\n- classic UIs available as themes\n- bindings for JS, React/React Native, Vue, Swift and Kotlin\n- public-domain assets\n\nThe two repositories were read from sparse, blob-filtered clones. Only the code was read; none of it was\nexecuted. In the paths below, `K:` means `https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/` and `L:`\nmeans `https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Overview\n\n### 1.1 konard/konard.github.io\n\n- **Purpose.** A personal site with a CV, experience, repositories, research, blog, art and an associative\n  stack. It has also become the testbed for a configurable UI. Issue #39 says so directly: *\"all our UI\n  elements must be owned by us ... We later once successfully make full configurability of our system will\n  make our own UI configurable framework.\"* That framework is link-foundation/ui.\n- **Stack.**\n  - React 19 and Vite 8, built as a multi-page app: each page is its own Vite entry and a real URL, with no\n    client router ([K:src/pages/pages.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/pages.js),\n    [K:vite.config.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/vite.config.js)).\n  - d3-force for layout.\n  - `@fontsource` fonts: Orbitron, Electrolize, Chakra Petch, Share Tech Mono.\n  - Testing: Vitest plus Testing Library, and Playwright suites per issue in `experiments/` that run on\n    Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.\n  - Linting and checks: eslint, prettier, secretlint, husky, ruff and shellcheck.\n  - Requires Node 24 or later. Deployed to GitHub Pages by GitHub Actions.\n- **License.** **None.** There is no LICENSE file and the GitHub API reports `license: null`. This blocks\n  copying code into a public-domain framework until the author relicenses it. The sound engine and palettes\n  are ported from konard/immortality, which is Unlicense.\n- **Size.** About 372 MB. Most of it is `docs/case-studies/`, `dev/`, `ci-logs/` and `public/archive/`; the\n  source is small. There are 24 issues, and #47 is open.\n- **Key paths.**\n  - Settings engine: [K:src/settings/](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/main/src/settings)\n    - `schema*.js`, `fields.js`, `store.js`, `apply.js`, `presets.js`\n  - Owned controls: [K:src/components/](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/main/src/components)\n    - `Select.jsx`, `ColorInput.jsx`, `NumberInput.jsx`, `Tooltip.jsx`, `PrefSwitches.jsx`, `Sound.jsx`,\n      `numericKeys.js`, `panelVisibility.js`, `edges.js`\n  - Settings UI: [K:src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx)\n    - `Presets.jsx`, `InterfacePreview.jsx`, `UiSamples.jsx`, `CornerTiles.jsx`, `LinkSetting.jsx`\n  - Links network engine: [K:src/links/](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/main/src/links)\n    - `configurations.js`, `edit.js`, `notation.js`, `glyph.js`, `placement.js`, `style*.js`, `render.js`,\n      `export.js`, `collision*.js`, `solver-job.js`\n  - Network editor: [K:src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx)\n    - `NetworkEditor.jsx`, `NetworkStyle.jsx`, `NetworkShare.jsx`, `NetworkGaps.jsx`, `useNetworkHistory.js`,\n      `useCollisionSolver.js`\n  - `engine.js`, `interactions.js`, `library.js`, `options.js`\n  - i18n and prefs: [K:src/i18n/prefs.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/i18n/prefs.js),\n    `plural.js`\n  - Skins:\n    - [K:src/skins.frames.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/skins.frames.js)\n      generates `skins.frames.css` (1067 lines, about 84 KB)\n    - `skins.glass.css`, `skins.liquid.css`, `skins.future.css`, `skins.materials.css`, `skins.palettes.css`,\n      `ui.css`, `panels.css`\n  - Line-limit guard: [K:scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh)\n    fails at 1500 lines and warns at 1350.\n\n### 1.2 konard/links-visuals\n\n- **Purpose.** A laboratory for drawing *one link*, and networks of links, as a single continuous curve\n  where other links can point at a link's middle. This is the \"blueprint\" visual language that\n  konard.github.io later adopted for its network glyphs.\n- **Stack.**\n  - Plain HTML pages plus ES modules in `js/`.\n  - **D3 v7 is loaded at runtime** through `https://esm.sh/use-m`, as `use('d3')`.\n  - SVG rendering with an optional Canvas mode.\n  - A Bun `serve.ts` dev server.\n  - Unit tests with `node --test`; e2e tests with Playwright / browser-commander.\n- **License.** Unlicense ([L:LICENSE](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/LICENSE)), so it\n  can be adopted directly. The repo is about 5.5 MB.\n- **Key paths.**\n  - Pages:\n    - [L:index.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/index.html): one draggable link\n    - [L:blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/blueprint.html): a 9-point spline blueprint\n    - [L:animated-blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/animated-blueprint.html): IK bending and looping\n    - [L:grid.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/grid.html): 1–64 links on an infinite grid\n    - [L:draw.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/draw.html): freehand strokes become links\n    - `H-fractal.html`, `fabrik.html`, `fabrik-horizontal.html`, `distance-constrained-blueprint.html`, `tests.html`\n  - Modules in [L:js/](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/tree/main/js):\n    - `zoom-pan.mjs`, `grid.mjs`, `markers.mjs`, `blueprint-link.mjs`, `draw-link.mjs`, `ik-pure.mjs`,\n      `ik.mjs`, `path.mjs`, `geometry.mjs`, `control-points.mjs`\n    - `state.mjs`, `render-mode.mjs`, `canvas-render.mjs`, `hud.mjs`, `panels.mjs`, `sliders.mjs`,\n      `animation.mjs`, `resize.mjs`, `svg-setup.mjs`, `constants.mjs`\n  - History of earlier attempts: [L:docs/links-visuals-history.md](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/docs/links-visuals-history.md)\n  - `failed-attempts/`: 76 HTML snapshots\n  - Case studies: `docs/case-studies/issue-{15,21,27,28}`\n  - 13 issues, all closed\n\n---\n\n## 2. Configurability model (konard.github.io)\n\nThis is the most mature part of the two repos and the strongest candidate for the core of link-foundation/ui.\n\n1. **The schema is a list of sections of flat fields.**\n   - Defined in [K:src/settings/schema.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/schema.js).\n   - A section is `{id, column, title:{en,ru}, lead, fields, when(settings), tabs}`.\n   - A field is created by a factory in [K:src/settings/fields.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/fields.js):\n     - `range(key, d, min, max, step, label, extra)`\n     - `toggle(...)`\n     - `select(key, d, options, label)` with `option(value, en, ru)`\n     - `color(...)`\n   - Keys are dotted paths such as `liquid.blur`, `skin.name`, `ui.cornerTL`. They are already link-like\n     (`section.key`) and would map one-to-one onto Links Notation doublets.\n   - The sections are:\n     - motion, nebula, stars, grid, beams, rain, sound\n     - skins: glass, liquid, futuristic, materials, palettes, corners\n     - ui: control sizes, borders, per-corner radii (−1 means \"follow the skin\"), menu size, slider track\n     - theory: `theory.notation` chooses L→L² or R→R²\n   - Split files: `schema.ui.js`, `schema.skins.js`, `schema.background.js`, `schema.layers.js`,\n     `schema.materials.js`, `schema.sound.js`.\n   - There are about 114 factory call sites; loops generate hundreds of fields, many of them script-only\n     (`css:false`).\n2. **One rule table.**\n   - `RULES` maps each key to `{d, min, max, u, o, c}`: default, limits, unit, options, colour flag.\n   - `CSS_RULES` is the subset that is projected into CSS.\n   - `DEFAULTS` and `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS` are exported.\n   - [K:src/settings/schema.defaults.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/schema.defaults.js)\n     holds `DEFAULT_LOOK`, the JSON the owner pasted in issue #45 (\"That is defaults.\").\n3. **Normalization and migration.**\n   - Lives in [K:src/settings/apply.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/apply.js).\n   - `normalize(rules, stored)` clamps numbers, drops unknown options and validates `#rrggbb` colours.\n   - It also migrates old values, for example `future.surface: 'transparent'` becomes a solid surface with\n     opacity 0.\n4. **Projection into the DOM, without the framework.** `applySettings(root, rules, settings)` writes:\n   - numbers and colours as CSS variables on `<html>` (`liquid.blur` becomes `--liquid-blur: 18px`)\n   - selects and toggles as `data-*` attributes (`skin.name` becomes `data-skin-name=\"glass\"`)\n   - derived values: corner-radius fallbacks, `--ui-accent-rgb`, an SVG `feTurbulence` noise data-URI, and\n     `data-surface-invisible`\n\n   All styling is then plain CSS that keys off these variables and attributes.\n5. **Before-paint script.**\n   - `normalize` and `applySettings` are serialized with `Function.toString` into `SETTINGS_SCRIPT`.\n   - The `themeBeforePaint` Vite plugin prepends it into `<head>` together with `THEME_SCRIPT`\n     ([K:vite.config.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/vite.config.js)).\n   - This avoids a flash of the wrong theme or skin, and it is the same code as at runtime, not a copy.\n6. **Store.**\n   - [K:src/settings/store.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/store.js)\n     is built on `useSyncExternalStore`. It has no context provider.\n   - **Only the diff from defaults** is stored, in localStorage `settings`. Users who never touched a key\n     therefore get improved defaults automatically.\n   - Other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.\n   - API: `setSettings(patch)`, `resetSettings(keys)`, `changesOf`.\n7. **Looks (presets).** Defined in [K:src/settings/presets.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/presets.js).\n   - Built-in presets: Matrix universe (default), glass-universe, calm, matrix, deep-space, warp,\n     neon (Tron), liquid, blueprint, and \"Light and fast\" for slow phones.\n   - `before45()` rebases old presets onto `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS`.\n   - `COMFORT` lists keys that presets, shared links and Random never change:\n     `motion.mode`, `sound.on`, `sound.volume`, `theory.notation`, `ui.transparency`. These are\n     accessibility and preference keys; the idea comes from immortality's `src/settings.ts`.\n   - `randomLook()` never goes above the default cost on any heavy key (counts, fps, blur, glow).\n   - Saved looks are stored as `[{name, look}]` under `settings-presets`, with add, remove, import and rename.\n   - Sharing: `#settings=<urlencoded JSON>` (`shareLink`, `lookOfHash`). When a shared link is opened,\n     `openSharedLook()` applies it, saves the previous look as a \"Before the link\" preset, and strips the hash.\n8. **Preferences outside the schema.** [K:src/i18n/prefs.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/i18n/prefs.js)\n   - Language is resolved as `?lang`, then the stored value, then `navigator`, then `en`.\n   - Theme is auto/light/dark.\n   - Each is a tiny external store.\n   - All UI text is written inline as `{en, ru}` objects, and `plural.js` handles Russian plural forms.\n9. **The network editor's local style model.** [K:src/links/style.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/style.js)\n   - `STYLE_SECTIONS` reuses the same field factories.\n   - `normalizeStyle` validates; `styleToParams` and `styleFromParams` put **only non-default values in the\n     query string**.\n   - There are six link palettes: site, neon, pastel, warm, cold, print.\n   - The network uses the same configuration grammar as the site settings, but it is scoped to a document\n     (the URL) instead of the user (localStorage).\n10. **Settings page as live designer.** [K:src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx)\n    - The page is generated from the schema. Each row is `label | control | value | ↺ reset`, and changed\n      rows get an `is-changed` class.\n    - Layer tabs show a dot when that layer is active.\n    - There is a Reset button per section plus \"Reset everything\".\n    - \"Look at the background\" is a peek mode that hides the panels.\n    - The \"Your changes\" box shows the diff JSON with Copy, and has a paste area that loads either settings\n      or `{presets:[...]}`.\n    - Sounds have ▶ preview buttons.\n    - The page itself is the preview: it includes `InterfacePreview`, `UiSamples` (small samples of every UI\n      element, from #45), `MaterialPresets` and `CornerTiles`.\n    - Columns are explicit because CSS multicol was buggy in Safari.\n    - This is the closest existing thing to the \"VS-designer configuration mode\" the issue asks for, though\n      it edits global tokens, not per-element instances.\n11. **Testing every setting.** Issue #15 asked for proof that every setting is applied.\n    [K:src/settings/applied.test.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/applied.test.js)\n    and `settings.test.js` iterate the schema and assert that each field has an effect.\n12. **Skins and frames.**\n    - [K:src/skins.frames.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/skins.frames.js)\n      defines corner shapes and corner lines once:\n      - shapes: square, cut, tall, wide, round, scoop, notch\n      - lines: none, gap, line, accent, bracket\n    - `npm run build:frames` generates `skins.frames.css` from it, and the same definitions draw the\n      `CornerTiles` previews. A test keeps the generated CSS in sync.\n    - The CSS uses `@property` typed lengths and `:where()` to keep specificity at zero.\n    - `schema.skins.js` has 12 palettes (from immortality) and the skins `glass`, `liquid`, `futuristic`.\n    - Owner requirements from issues:\n      - #39: a single transparency setting for all backgrounds; matte, glossy and liquid glass presets; no\n        rounded corners in the futuristic look by default; rounded corners following t3code practice\n      - #45: one per-side border configuration shared by panels, blocks, buttons and other elements; top\n        highlight width set separately from corner/side widths; the corner layer above or below content;\n        colours picked from palettes\n\n---\n\n## 3. Visualizations\n\n### 3.1 Single link (links-visuals)\n\n| Page | What it shows | Tech / notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| [index.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/index.html) | A diagonal line with a cross (source) and an arrow (target), draggable endpoints, fullscreen, a coordinates panel | D3 + SVG markers |\n| [H-fractal.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/H-fractal.html) | Recursive H subdivision with straight arrows | Recursion demo |\n| [blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/blueprint.html) | A configurable link spline with 9 control points (start, p1–p3, center, p4–p6, end) on a grid | `path.mjs` converts Catmull-Rom to cubic. Points are colour-coded: start green, end red, center black, others blue. Dashed `4 2` outline |\n| [distance-constrained-blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/distance-constrained-blueprint.html) | Fixed segment lengths | Constraint experiment |\n| [fabrik.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/fabrik.html), `fabrik-horizontal.html` | FABRIK inverse kinematics | IK experiment (Freya Holmér and argonaut are credited in the README) |\n| [animated-blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/animated-blueprint.html) | IK-driven bending and looping animation | `ik-pure.mjs` uses a pure constant-curvature sweep solver with `IK_SEG_COUNT=4` |\n| [tests.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/tests.html) | Gallery of geometry cases | `test-cases.mjs` |\n\nMarkers ([L:js/markers.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/markers.mjs)):\n\n- The cross and arrow use `viewBox 0 0 100 100` and `markerUnits=\"strokeWidth\"`, so they scale with the line.\n- Their proportions use the golden ratio.\n- They are hardcoded black.\n\n### 3.2 Networks (links-visuals)\n\n- [grid.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/grid.html)\n  - 1–64 coloured links placed on grid cells, with a link-count slider, Reset and snapping.\n  - Proportions are shared with single-link mode through `blueprint-link.mjs` (fixed in #23 and #28).\n- [draw.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/draw.html)\n  - Freehand input through Pointer Events: Apple Pencil, touch and mouse, with `touch-action:none`.\n  - A stroke is simplified into a link whose center is the 50% arc-length point.\n  - An endpoint dropped near another link's center snaps and pins to it. Pins are re-resolved at render time\n    by `applyCenterAnchors`, so links follow when their target moves.\n  - Select and Draw modes; links persist in localStorage (#27).\n- Infinite grid ([L:js/grid.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/grid.mjs)): SVG\n  `pattern` tiles of minor and major lines over a 1e6-sized rect (#15).\n- Zoom and pan ([L:js/zoom-pan.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/zoom-pan.mjs))\n  - The wheel zooms about the pointer with factor `0.999^delta`, scale 0.1–20.\n  - Listeners sit on `document`, which fixed the \"zoom does not work far from the center\" bugs (#19, #21).\n  - `?debug=zoom` turns on a debug overlay.\n- [L:docs/links-visuals-history.md](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/docs/links-visuals-history.md)\n  surveys earlier attempts:\n  - LinksPlatform web UI prototypes; doublet and triplet circle symbols\n  - Cytoscape issue #1217 (edges to edges), declined, and its compound-node workarounds\n  - GoJS label nodes; dmx cytoscape-edge-connections\n  - Deep.Case Cytoscape (link node plus from/to edges) and A-Frame 3D\n  - DeepVisual (Python); doublets-web SVG; react-deep-tree\n\n  It ends with the open goal: *\"stable identity, arbitrary source/target references, self-reference and\n  cycles, understandable recursive structure, and layout that stays readable as links move.\"*\n\n### 3.3 Networks as symbols (konard.github.io)\n\n- **Encoding.** [K:src/links/configurations.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/configurations.js)\n  - A doublet network of N links (plus the 0 link meaning \"nothing\") is written as 2N digits in base N+1,\n    for example `01 20`. With more than 9 links it is written as `s,t;s,t`.\n  - Functions: `decode`, `encode`, `codeAt`, `indexOf` (BigInt), `randomCode`, `mathNotation` (subscripts),\n    `linksNotation` (gives `(1: 0 1)`).\n  - Classes up to relabelling are counted with Burnside's lemma (`classCount`, `representatives`), and there\n    is a \"real references only\" mode.\n- **Five editable notations that stay in sync.** These are in `Notations` in\n  [K:src/pages/NetworkEditor.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/NetworkEditor.jsx):\n  - theory notation, e.g. `λ = {1 ↦ (0, 1)}`, in L→L² or R→R² form ([K:src/links/notation.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/notation.js))\n  - pairs\n  - the N-ary number, e.g. `0120₃`\n  - its decimal index\n  - Links Notation\n\n  The parsers are in [K:src/links/edit.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/edit.js)\n  and return bilingual errors. While the user types, the text stays as typed and the other notations follow.\n- **Glyph.** [K:src/links/glyph.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/glyph.js)\n  - Each link is one cubic-Bézier curve: a bar at the source, a middle, and an arrow at the target. This is\n    the links-visuals blueprint.\n  - Other links refer to a link by touching its middle.\n  - A reference to 0 is a free end; a self-reference is a loop, so `(1: 1 1)` renders as ∞.\n  - Constants: `SIZE=100`, `STROKE=2.4`, a 9-colour palette.\n  - Markers: bar, arrow, triangle, tail, dot, circle, square, diamond, none.\n  - `SHAPE` options: placement, order, frame, forces, rotation, spread, padding, bendMode, and more.\n- **Placement.** [K:src/links/placement.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/placement.js)\n  offers circle, square grid, hex, dice, playing card, spiral, and d3-force.\n- **Overlap reduction.**\n  - `collisions.js`, `collision-gaps.js` and `collision-symmetry.js` add spacing automatically.\n  - The work runs in a cancellable Web Worker (`collision-worker.js`, `solver-job.js`).\n  - [K:src/pages/useCollisionSolver.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/useCollisionSolver.js)\n    keys each result so a stale one never replaces a newer drawing.\n- **Render and export.**\n  - [K:src/links/render.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/render.js):\n    `networkSvg` builds one standalone SVG string. It is used for the on-screen preview *and* every export.\n    XML is escaped and values are normalized. It supports solid, linear and radial backgrounds, a card, and\n    captions in the chosen notation.\n  - [K:src/links/export.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/export.js)\n    exports:\n    - SVG, plus PNG, JPEG and WebP by rasterizing on a canvas\n    - a `.lino` file (Links Notation)\n    - clipboard copies of text and images\n    - the Web Share API and social share URLs\n- **Editor page.** [K:src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx)\n  - URL: `/network/?code=…&<non-default style params>`, with `DEFAULT_CODE='11 22 12'`.\n  - Sections: Notations, Links (a table plus per-link cards for colour, turns and gaps), Style, Share.\n  - `useNetworkHistory.js` keeps debounced URL history and pauses it while a slider is being dragged.\n    `localStorage network.debug` enables debugging.\n  - The gallery is at `/art/#symbols` (`NetworkGallery.jsx`).\n- **Other data visuals.** These are hand-built SVG/React components:\n  - `ContributionCalendar`, `ContributionsChart`, `LanguagesChart`, `LanguageCloud`, `StatTiles`, `Timeline`\n  - `EcosystemMap` (an orbit diagram), `ProblemSolvingDiagram`, `MetaTheory`, `Cosmos`, `LiquidRefraction`\n- **Animated backgrounds.** [K:src/visuals/](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/main/src/visuals)\n  - Layered canvases: nebula, stars, beams, and rain (a \"digital rain\" of link glyphs).\n  - [K:src/visuals/governor.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/visuals/governor.js)\n    is an FPS governor. It lowers resolution first and then fps, and never raises them again\n    (`SLOW_GAP` 45 ms, `MIN_SCALE` 0.4).\n\n---\n\n## 4. geometry expressed as fractions of `gridSpacing` |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **One rule table per key**: `{default, min, max, unit, options, isColor}`. It drives normalization,\n   validation, the generated UI, CSS projection and tests. It translates naturally into a Links Notation\n   schema, e.g. `(liquid.blur: range 18 0 40 px)`.\n2. **Store the diff from defaults, never the full state.** Defaults can then improve for everyone, and saved\n   looks and share links stay small.\n3. **Project settings into CSS variables and `data-*` attributes on the root.** Theming then works without\n   any framework, and the same tokens can be emitted for SwiftUI and Compose as constant tables.\n4. **Run the same `normalize` and `apply` before first paint**, serialized from the real functions rather\n   than copied. There is no theme flash and no second implementation.\n5. **Comfort keys.** Accessibility and preference keys (reduced motion, sound, volume, transparency,\n   notation) are excluded from presets, shared links and randomization.\n6. **Looks as data.** Built-in presets, saved presets, import/export JSON, `#settings=` share links, and an\n   automatic \"Before the link\" backup when a shared look is applied.\n7. **Bounded randomization.** `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on heavy keys, so Random is safe\n   on slow devices. There is also an explicit \"Light and fast\" preset.\n8. **The settings page is the live preview.** Each row has a per-field ↺ reset and changed rows are marked.\n   There are section resets, a peek mode, a diff box with copy and paste, and sample tiles of every UI\n   element. Extending this to per-element editing gives the WYSIWYG configuration mode.\n9. **One source generates both CSS and preview tiles** (`skins.frames.js`), and a test fails if the\n   generated CSS is out of date.\n10. **One renderer for preview and export.** A single SVG string (`networkSvg`) is reused for PNG, JPEG and\n    WebP export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen. The same idea fits animation recording: record\n    the frames of the model, not screenshots.\n11. **URL state holds only non-default parameters** (`styleToParams`), with debounced history that pauses\n    while a slider is dragged.\n12. **Several synchronized notations of one model**, with typed-text preservation and bilingual errors. This\n    shows the framework's \"DOM-like language and Links Notation as two views of one tree\" in miniature.\n13. **Expensive layout in a cancellable worker**, with keyed results that cannot overwrite newer state\n    (`solver-job.js`, `useCollisionSolver.js`).\n14. **Performance governors.** The FPS governor degrades resolution and then fps, and `panelVisibility.js`\n    limits live `backdrop-filter` surfaces. Both belong in the framework runtime.\n15. **Owned, ARIA-compliant controls.** Select follows the APG patterns, numeric keys are shared, and popups\n    are portaled and clamped to the viewport. #39 says \"all UI elements must be owned by us\".\n16. **Declarative sound.** A `data-sound` attribute on any element plus document-level role mapping, so\n    components do not hard-code audio.\n17. **Language and theme stores built on `useSyncExternalStore`, with no provider.** This ports cleanly to\n    signals or observables in Vue, Swift and Kotlin.\n18. **Pointer-centred zoom with document-level listeners** and an infinite pattern grid (links-visuals #15,\n    #19, #21). These are designer-canvas basics.\n19. **Arc-length center anchors for links that point at links.** An anchor is pinned and re-resolved at\n    render time (`applyCenterAnchors`), which is the core of drawing associative links, not just node graphs.\n20. **Pure geometry and IK separated from rendering** (`ik-pure.mjs`), so they can be unit-tested and ported\n    to Swift and Kotlin.\n21. **A test suite per issue** (`*-NN.test.js`, `experiments/issue-N-browser.mjs` on three browser engines),\n    a case study per issue, and a hard 1500-line file limit.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Duplication candidates (move into link-foundation/ui)\n\n| Concern | Current location(s) | Proposed framework module |\n|---|---|---|\n| Settings schema, field factories, normalize/apply, store, presets, share links | K:src/settings/*; the `COMFORT` idea from immortality `src/settings.ts` | `config` core: language-neutral schema plus adapters for JS, React, Vue, Swift, Kotlin |\n| Field factories reused for the network style | K:src/links/style.js reuses fields.js | Same `config` core with scopes: user (storage) and document (URL or `.lino`) |\n| Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip, switches, numericKeys | K:src/components/* | `controls` package |\n| Palettes (12 skins, 6 link palettes, colour chooser palettes) | `schema.skins.js`, `style.js`, `colorPalettes.js`, immortality | `themes/palettes` |\n| Skins and corner frames generator | `skins.frames.js` and `skins.*.css` | `themes`: classic UIs become additional skins |\n| Sound engine and interaction mapping | K:src/sound/* (ported from immortality `src/sound.ts`) | `sound` package |\n| Canvas backgrounds and FPS governor | K:src/visuals/* | `effects` package with `governor` in the runtime |\n| i18n `{en,ru}` objects, plurals, language and theme prefs | K:src/i18n/*, inline in every component | `i18n` with message catalogs, ideally in Links Notation |\n| Link geometry, glyph, markers, placement, collisions | K:src/links/* **and** L:js/* (the same blueprint idea implemented twice) | `links-view`: a single renderer for one link and for networks |\n| Notation parsers and encoders | K:src/links/edit.js, configurations.js, notation.js | Use the official `links-notation` package; keep the code/index maths as a utility |\n| Export (SVG, rasters, `.lino`, clipboard, share) | K:src/links/export.js | `export` utility, reused by animation recording |\n| Zoom/pan, infinite grid, HUD, panel toggle | L:js/zoom-pan.mjs, grid.mjs, hud.mjs, panels.mjs | `canvas` primitives for the designer surface |\n| SVG markers and their Canvas re-implementation | L:js/markers.mjs, canvas-render.mjs; K:glyph.js MARKERS | One marker definition rendered by both back ends |\n| Inline per-page CSS (navy translucent panels) | Every L:*.html page | One theme stylesheet |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Problems, bugs and limitations observed\n\n### konard.github.io\n1. **No license.** The code cannot legally be copied into a public-domain framework until it is relicensed\n   (for example to Unlicense, like links-visuals and immortality).\n2. **Links Notation is hand-parsed.** `parseLinks` in `edit.js` uses the regex\n   `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g`, and `links-notation` is not imported anywhere in `src/`.\n   It only accepts numeric doublets and does not handle nesting, names or multi-line input.\n3. **Settings are JSON, not Links Notation.** This applies to localStorage, the `#settings=` hash, the\n   diff box, and import/export. It contradicts the framework goal of representing everything in Links\n   Notation.\n4. **Bilingual text is hard-coded** as `{en, ru}` objects inside components, including long templated\n   sentences in `NetworkEditor.jsx`. Adding a language means editing every component; there is no catalog.\n5. **Configuration is global only.** The tokens style every element of a kind. There is no per-instance\n   override and no element tree to select from, so it is not yet a WYSIWYG designer.\n6. **React-bound.** The store, pages and controls are React components; only `apply.js` and `src/links/*`\n   are framework-free.\n7. **Open issue #47.** The top-left corner and the top and bottom edges are not transparent by default,\n   although every other element is. These are still border/corner layering bugs from the #45 redesign.\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #13: the rain sometimes scaled up too much on refresh.\n   - #45: some border configurations clipped overflowing content or broke transparent backgrounds and\n     selection.\n   - CSS multicol was unreliable in Safari, so columns are explicit.\n   - Safari needed a focus fix in `numericKeys.js`.\n9. **Heavy generated CSS.** `skins.frames.css` is about 84 KB / 1067 lines, and a very large number of\n   fields (hundreds) costs payload and maintenance.\n10. **Repo weight.** About 372 MB, from case studies, logs and archives committed to the repo, so it is\n    slow to clone. Sparse clones are needed.\n11. **Migrations are ad hoc** (`before45()`, special cases in `normalize`). There is no versioned schema\n    migration mechanism.\n\n### links-visuals\n1. **CDN at runtime.** D3 is fetched from `esm.sh/use-m` on every load. It does not work offline, it is\n   unpinned and therefore a supply-chain risk, and it is not reproducible.\n2. **Global mutable state** in `state.mjs` (module singletons with setters). Two views cannot share a page.\n3. **Duplicated renderers.** `canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG markers and paths by hand, and the\n   two can drift apart.\n4. **A rAF loop runs every frame even when idle** (`animation.mjs`), which wastes battery.\n5. **Inline CSS is copied into every HTML page**, with no theming. Markers are hardcoded black, and only\n   grid.html and draw.html have colour.\n6. **Experiments are not composable.** Each page wires modules differently, and `failed-attempts/` holds 76\n   HTML snapshots instead of git history.\n7. **Limits of the network model.** grid.html places links in cells without real references. Only draw.html\n   has link-to-link anchors, and only to centers (no source/target-to-endpoint semantics, no layout engine).\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #1/#3: start-point snapping.\n   - #15: the grid was not infinite.\n   - #19/#21: zoom failed away from the center because the hit area was the SVG; listeners were moved to\n     `document`.\n   - #23/#28: grid proportions were inconsistent with single-link mode.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n\n1. **Licensing first.** links-visuals is Unlicense and can be ported now. For konard.github.io, ask the\n   owner to add an Unlicense LICENSE before any code is moved. The sound engine and palettes are already\n   Unlicense through immortality.\n2. **Schema in Links Notation.** Express each RULES entry as links, for example:\n   ```\n   (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (unit px))\n   (skin.name: (type select) (default glass) (options glass liquid futuristic))\n   ```\n   Then generate the JS and TS rule tables, and the Swift and Kotlin constants, from it. Store user diffs as\n   Links Notation too: `(liquid.blur 24)`. Keep JSON import for backward compatibility with existing\n   `settings` and `settings-presets` values and `#settings=` links.\n3. **Keep the projection contract.** Write `--section-key` CSS variables and `data-section-key` attributes,\n   and keep the before-paint injection for web targets. Native targets get the same normalized map as an\n   observable store.\n4. **Scopes.** Keep the user/document split (localStorage vs URL or `.lino`), and add an element scope so the\n   designer mode can override tokens per node in the DOM-like tree.\n5. **Controls.** Port Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip and numericKeys with their tests (`*.test.jsx`)\n   as the first `controls` set. Keep WAI-ARIA APG behaviour and the Safari fixes.\n6. **Links view.** Merge the K:src/links glyph, placement, collisions and render code with the L:js\n   zoom-pan, grid, anchors and IK into a single renderer:\n   - one marker set, with SVG and Canvas back ends generated from it\n   - no global state; instance objects instead\n   - D3 bundled and pinned, or dropped where `d3-force` alone is enough\n   - an idle-stopping animation loop\n7. **Parsing.** Replace the regex parser with the official `links-notation` package. Keep `configurations.js`\n   (code and index maths, Burnside counting) as a pure utility.\n8. **i18n.** Move the `{en, ru}` literals into per-language catalogs keyed by id, preferably in Links\n   Notation, and keep `plural.js` rules per language.\n9. **Themes.** Treat `glass`, `liquid` and `futuristic`, plus the 12 palettes and the corner/frame generator,\n   as the first theme pack. Classic UIs (Windows 9x, Aqua and so on) become more theme packs on the same\n   tokens. Fix #47-style corner and edge transparency in the generator, not in per-skin CSS.\n10. **Animation recording.** Reuse the export pipeline: one model goes to a standalone SVG and then to a\n    raster, over a timeline of settings and link diffs. The IK animation in links-visuals and the canvas\n    backgrounds are the first recording targets.\n11. **Process.** Adopt the per-issue test files, the three-engine Playwright runs, a case study per issue,\n    and the 1500-line limit. Do not commit logs or archives, so the framework repo does not grow to hundreds\n    of megabytes.\n"

Nothing was added, committed or pushed, and none of the downloaded code was run.\n\n**What the two repos are**\n- **immortality** (Unlicense): a React/Vite/TypeScript life-expectancy dashboard with a fully configurable sci-fi look. It ships no images or audio: everything is drawn on canvas, in SVG or CSS, and the 26 interface sounds are synthesized.\n- **anime-avatar** (Unlicense code): a browser \"Avatar Studio\" for loading, posing, animating and exporting 3D characters. It has no build step and pulls three.js and React from a CDN. The same repo also holds an older, separate demo app.\n- **Links Notation:** neither repo uses it. All settings are JSON in local storage, a URL hash (immortality) or a downloaded config file (anime-avatar). Section 9 shows how both would map to Links Notation.\n\n**Strongest ideas to adopt (26 are listed in section 6)**\n1. **One settings schema drives everything.** In immortality, 49 typed settings in 8 groups produce validation, defaults, a generic accessible settings panel, 12 presets, randomize, reset, version migration and share links. This is the closest existing model for the framework's \"configuration mode\".\n2. **Only the difference from defaults is stored and shared.** External input is treated as untrusted and invalid values are dropped. Accessibility settings (motion, sound, volume) stay with the viewer when someone applies a shared look.\n3. **Themes switch without re-rendering.** Settings become `data-*` attributes and CSS variables, which would work the same in plain JS, React and Vue. A test checks that every option has a CSS rule.\n4. **Animations are pure functions of time**, such as the text decipher effect and the avatar gestures. Combined with layering where every motion source adds to the others (no jumps), this is a natural basis for animation recording: save the clock, the inputs and the seed, then replay.\n5. **Every borrowed item carries its source and license.** immortality records a decision per source: MIT code ported with credit, GPL code used for ideas only, unlicensed sites used only as visual reference. anime-avatar shows a credit overlay only when an asset's license requires one.\n6. **Constraints are data.** Joint rotation limits in degrees feed the sliders, the randomizer and the on-model rotation handles alike. There are also a shared catalog of easing curves, a separate layer for interface sounds, and an in-app test runner with a state handle for development.\n\n**Duplicated work across the two repos (section 7):** the settings schema and panel controls, per-group randomize and reset, saving, sharing and export, easing curves, reduced-motion handling, mobile and size helpers, source/license records, screenshot tests and canvas backgrounds. Each should become a single framework module.\n\n**Problems and risks (section 8)**\n- **anime-avatar:**\n  - It compiles its code in the browser on every load, runs React's development build, and loads libraries from a CDN without pinning or integrity checks.\n  - The editor is one 2,381-line component styled entirely inline.\n  - Imported config is barely validated, there is no versioning, and errors appear as browser alert pop-ups.\n- **Licensing risk in anime-avatar:**\n  - It links to about 70 proprietary Girls' Frontline 2 model archives.\n  - One sample model is non-commercial (CC-BY-NC).\n  - Some license strings are vague (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\").\n- **No animation recording in either repo.** anime-avatar only lists screenshot and video export, custom pose saving and a scene editor on its roadmap.\n- **immortality:**\n  - A single 3,359-line stylesheet holds every theme.\n  - The list of settings that become `data-*` attributes is copied by hand into a test.\n  - The panel is React-only, share links are long JSON strings, and there is no translation support.\n- **Past animation bugs to keep as regression checks:** an animation fill setting that left panels clipped and glitchy, a hard white-flash flicker (a photosensitivity issue), and the issues in anime-avatar #19 and #28.\n\n**Migration plan (section 9):** port the immortality settings engine as plain functions that read and write Links Notation, add value kinds that anime-avatar needs (colors, rotations, maps, lists, assets, actions), and generate the inspector and theme modules from the schema. Recordings would be Links Notation timelines. Every third-party asset would need a license record checked in CI, and the in-browser compilation, unpinned CDN loading and global-variable modules should not be carried over."

Grammar in Links Notation Format\nThe grammar can also be expressed using Links Notation itself:\n```lino\ngrammar:\n  document:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence skip_empty_lines links whitespace EOF)\n      (sequence whitespace EOF))\n  skip_empty_lines:\n    (zero_or_more (sequence horizontal_whitespace newline))\n  links:\n    (sequence first_line (zero_or_more line))\n  first_line:\n    (sequence SET_BASE_INDENTATION element)\n  line:\n    (sequence skip_empty_lines CHECK_INDENTATION element)\n  element:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence any_link PUSH_INDENTATION links)\n      any_link)\n  any_link:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence nested_group eol)\n      indented_id_link\n      single_line_any_link)\n  single_line_any_link:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence single_line_link eol)\n      (sequence single_line_value_link eol))\n  nested_group:\n    (sequence \"(\" ENTER_NESTED_CONTEXT nested_group_body\n      EXIT_NESTED_CONTEXT)\n  nested_group_body:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence skip_empty_lines links whitespace \")\")\n      (sequence whitespace \")\"))\n  single_line_link:\n    (sequence horizontal_whitespace reference\n      horizontal_whitespace \":\" single_line_values)\n  single_line_value_link:\n    single_line_values\n  single_line_values:\n    (one_or_more (sequence horizontal_whitespace reference_or_link))\n  indented_id_link:\n    (sequence reference horizontal_whitespace \":\" eol)\n  reference_or_link:\n    (alternative nested_group reference)\n  reference:\n    (alternative delimited_reference simple_reference)\n  comment:\n    (sequence comment_start (zero_or_more (not newline)))\n  comment_start:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence start_of_document \"#\")\n      (sequence whitespace_char \"#\"))\n  simple_reference:\n    (one_or_more reference_symbol)\n  delimiter:\n    (alternative '\"' \"'\" '`')\n  delimiter_run:\n    (one_or_more delimiter)\n  delimited_reference:\n    (alternative n_quoted_reference empty_reference)\n  n_quoted_reference:\n    (sequence delimiter_run (zero_or_more any_char) delimiter_run)\n  empty_reference:\n    (one_or_more (sequence delimiter delimiter))\n  reference_symbol:\n    (not (alternative whitespace_char \"(\" \":\" \")\"))\n  whitespace_char:\n    (alternative \" \" \"\\t\" \"\\n\" \"\\r\")\n  horizontal_whitespace:\n    (zero_or_more (alternative \" \" \"\\t\"))\n  whitespace:\n    (zero_or_more whitespace_char)\n  newline:\n    (alternative \"\\r\\n\" \"\\n\" \"\\r\")\n  eol:\n    (alternative:\n      (sequence horizontal_whitespace (alternative newline EOF))\n      nested_group_end)\n  nested_group_end:\n    (sequence inside_nested_context horizontal_whitespace\n      (lookahead \")\"))\n```\n## Grammar Explained\n### Document Structure\nA **document** consists of zero or more links. Empty documents (containing\nonly whitespace) are valid.\n```text\nDocument\n├── Skip empty lines at the start\n├── Parse links (hierarchical structure)\n├── Allow trailing whitespace\n└── End of file\n```\n### References\nReferences are the atomic building blocks of Links Notation. A reference is\neither simple or delimited:\n| Type      | Syntax       | Example         | Description                         |\n|-----------|--------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|\n| Simple    | `identifier` | `papa`, `mama`  | Alphanumeric and special            |\n| Delimited | `\"text\"`     | `\"hello world\"` | Any text between matching runs      |\n| Empty     | `\"\"`         | `(\"\" 1)`        | A bare delimiter pair holds nothing |\n**Simple Reference Characters:**\n- Valid: Letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `!`, `?`, `@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, etc.\n- Invalid: Space, tab, newline, `(`, `:`, `)`\n- A `#` is valid inside a reference (`issue#1047`) but opens a comment where a\n  reference could begin, so a reference cannot start with one unless it is\n  delimited (`\"#\"`)\n**Delimiters:**\nThe three delimiters `\"`, `'` and `` ` `` behave identically, so `\"text\"`,\n`'text'` and `` `text` `` are the same reference. Nothing else delimits: `«`,\n`[`, `|` and the like are ordinary characters of a simple reference.\n**N-Quoted References:**",

Two\nthings follow. A position reported for a document is the position in the\ndocument as it was written, so a parse error still points at the column it\nbroke at. And a line that held nothing but a comment becomes a line of\nwhitespace, which separates links the way an empty line does and does not end\nan indented block, so a comment can stand on a line of its own inside one:\n```lino\nparent\n  # what the child is for\n  child\n```\nreads as `parent` with the single child `child`.\nWriting a document follows the same rule from the other side: a reference that\nbegins with a `#` is written quoted (`'#tag'`), so a document a formatter writes\nreads back as itself. A `#` that cannot open a comment needs no quotes, so\n`issue#1047` is written as it stands.\nEvery implementation reads comments by default and can be told to read `#` as\nan ordinary character instead, for documents written before comments existed.\n### Link Types\n#### 1. Single-Line Value Link\nA sequence of references on a single line without an explicit identifier:\n```lino\npapa loves mama\n```\nThis creates an anonymous link with three values: `papa`, `loves`, `mama`.\n#### 2. Single-Line Named Link\nA link with an explicit identifier, using the `:` separator:\n```lino\nfamily: papa mama son daughter\n```\nThis creates a link named `family` with four values.\n#### 3. Nested Group (Parenthesized Link)\nLinks enclosed in parentheses can span multiple lines:\n```lino\n(family:\n  papa\n  mama\n  son\n  daughter)\n```\nA parenthesized group opens a **nested context**: its body starts fresh at\nindentation level zero and follows exactly the same rules as the root\ndocument, so indentation is structural inside parentheses too:\n```lino\narray (\n  a\n    b\n  c\n    d\n)\n```\nThe body above produces the same four links the root produces for\n`a`/`  b`/`c`/`  d`, nested under `array`.\nA group body that produces a single link collapses to that link, so\n`(a b c)` stays a single link.
