Architecture: links-as-UI and client handlers\n\n### 2.1 UI stored as links\n\nA UI component is a **code link** plus **binding links**:\n\n```\n(handler: Handler clientSupportsJs -> tsxCodeLink)      # \"this code runs in the browser\"\n(handleClient: HandleClient SomeType -> handler)        # \"render links of SomeType with it\"\n```\n\n- The code link (type `TSX`, `@deep-foundation/core`) holds a string value of the form\n  `({deep, require}) => { const React = require('react'); ... return Component }`.\n- `deep._findHandler({ handlerId, context })` (deeplinks `imports/client.tsx` ~L2277) queries the\n  `handlers` table filtered by the JS execution provider. Without `handlerId` it matches a\n  `@deep-foundation/deepcase` `Context` link among the context ids — i.e. handler choice is\n  context-sensitive and itself a link query.\n- `evalClientHandler` (deeplinks `imports/client-handler.tsx`) runs `eval(value)`, expects a\n  function, calls it with `{deep, gql, require, ...input}`, and renders the returned component.\n- `require` is a **whitelist map** (`r.list` in deepcase `imports/client-handler.tsx`) of\n  packages: react, chakra, framer-motion, monaco, cytoscape, recharts, d3, etc. Heavier modules\n  are resolved lazily through `DeepClient.resolveDependency`.\n- `CatchErrors` is an error boundary that renders a Chakra `Alert` with a reset button.\n  Perception replaces it with `ClientHandlerErrorComponent` (modal, src/dist toggle, FinderButton).\n- `ClientHandlerRenderer` props: `fillSize`, `onClose`, `linkId`, `handlerId`, `context`.\n\n### 2.2 Package-defined handlers (`deep.json` of deepcase)\n\n| Handler | Bound to types |\n|---|---|\n| `asyncFileClientHandler` | AsyncFile (image/video/file preview) |\n| `stringClientHandler` | Join, PackageQuery, Contain |\n| `queryClientHandler` | Query |\n| `editorClientHandler` | SyncTextFile, TSX |\n\nOther types declared: `Traveler` (Any -> Query, symbol 🧳), `ContextToken`, `Context`.\n\n### 2.3 HandleCyto — graph rendering as links\n\n`@deep-foundation/handle-cyto` defines `HandleCyto`: a handler that returns Cytoscape `elements`\nand `stylesheets` for links of a given type (`imports/cyto-handler.tsx`). Example:\n`HandleCytoContainInvisible` hides Contain edges. Rules can be toggled per handler\n(`useCytoHandlersRules`). So **per-type visual representation is data**, not code in the shell.\n\n### 2.4 State stores\n\n`@deep-foundation/store` provides one hook API over three backends:\n`useQueryStore` (URL query, shareable), `useLocalStore` (localStorage), `useCookiesStore`.\nExamples: `useSpaceId`, `useContainer` (query store); `layout`, `editor-tabs` (local store).\n\n### 2.5 Perception (second generation)\n\n- `perception-imports/imports/go.tsx` (927 lines): `GoI`, `GoProvider`, `useGo` — navigation as a\n  chainable cursor (`go.focus`, `go.do`, `go.parents`) with `History` / `HistoryHandler` links.\n- `perception-imports/imports/react-handler.tsx`: `ReactHandler`, `ReactHandlersProvider`,\n  `createComponent` — handlers usable as plain React components.\n- `perception-app/pages/index.tsx`: the **whole app shell is a handler** —\n  `<go.Handler handlerId={deep.idLocal('@deep-foundation/perception-links','Layout')} Auth={...} Status={...} ColorMode={...}/>`.\n  The shell supplies only slot components (auth slide-out panel, status indicator, color mode).\n- Also: Telegram web-app script, regenerable `preloaded.json` (handlers bundled offline).\n\n### 2.6 The 2025 rewrite (`deep-foundation/deep`)\n\nNext 15 app router, MUI 6 dark theme (`src/theme.tsx`) with a **per-JS-value-type palette**\n(`types.value/symbol/undefined/promise/boolean/string/number/bigint/set/weakSet...`, each with\nmain/light/dark), black canvas page rendering an echarts graph (`src/app/page.tsx`,\n`src/components/echarts.js`).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Graph visualization\n\n**Library:** Cytoscape via `react-cytoscapejs` (`imports/cyto/graph.tsx`).\nPlugins: dagre, cola, d3-force, custom `cytoscape-deep-d3-force`, custom fork of cxtmenu\n(`imports/cyto/cxtmenu.tsx`), edge-connections, edgehandles (drag to create links).\n\n**Layouts** (`imports/cyto/layouts.tsx`, chosen in top menu, stored in local store `layout`):\n\n| Layout | Parameters |\n|---|---|\n| `deep-d3-force` (default) | manyBodyStrength -2000, linkDistance 100, alpha 0.8, `infinite: true` (continuous simulation) |\n| `cola` | edgeLength = 100 + 10 * connectedEdges |\n| `dagre` | hierarchical |\n\n**Encoding a link** (`imports/cyto/elements.tsx`): every link is a node; `from`, `to` and `type`\nbecome separate edges from that node. Missing endpoints are auto-added as id-only nodes.\nLabel: `id\\ntype:Name\\nname:Name\\nvalue(11 chars + \"...\" + 9 chars)\\n\\n symbol`; symbol from the\ntype's `Symbol` link, default 📍.\n\n**Stylesheet** (`imports/cyto/stylesheets.tsx`):\n\n| Selector | Style |\n|---|---|\n| `.link-node` | 30x30, white, label below |\n| `.link-from` | edge, `tee` arrow |\n| `.link-to` | edge, triangle arrow |\n| `.link-type` | dashed `[5,5]`, triangle arrow |\n| `:hover` | underlay #0080ff |\n| `.focused` | border-width 4, blue.500 |\n| `.query-link-*-node` | small 8px / 16px dots |\n| `:parent` | compound nodes, gray, opacity 0.1 |\n\n**Interactions**\n- Radial context menu on node (`cxttapstart` / `taphold`), radius 108, activeFillColor\n  `rgba(0,128,255,0.75)`: editor, unlock, delete, delete down, insert, update, login, space,\n  container, traveler (n), readme. Core (background) menu: insert, center, query.\n- Double click opens the type's handler as a floating window; drag positions get saved as Focus.\n- Edgehandles: drag from a node to create a link (type picked afterwards).\n- Traveler (`imports/cyto/traveler.tsx`): per-node sub-menu toggling query links that pull in\n  neighbours: types, out, in, up, down, to, from, typed, all / by-type. A `Traveler` link points\n  to an active `Query` contained in the space.\n- Search (`MenuSearch`), \"clear focuses\", per-handler HandleCyto toggles.\n\n**Perception graph** (`perception-app/imports/graph.tsx`): declarative React components\n`<Graph>`, `<GraphNode>`, `<GraphEdge>`, `<GraphStyle>` over cytoscape, with\n`cytoscape-node-html-label` (HTML labels in nodes), cola and dagre.\n\n**Keyboard orientation** (`perception-app/imports/orientation.tsx`): `NavDirection` values\ncurrent, close, delete, edit-from, from, type, to, edit-to, out, typed, in, up, down, prev, next,\nparents, contains, insert, value, results. Each has a left/up/right/down mapping — a spatial\nkeyboard map over link relations.\n\n**3D**: aframe + aframe-forcegraph code exists but is fully commented out; 3D mode requested in\ndeepcase-app #159.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Windows / frames / tabs model\n\nAll window state is **links in the space**, so a layout is persistable and shareable:\n\n| Concept | Representation |\n|---|---|\n| Space (workspace) | a link id in URL (`useSpaceId`), \"enter space\" via radial menu |\n| Container (where inserts go) | link id in URL (`useContainer`) |\n| Node position | `Focus` link (space -> link), value `{x, y}`; \"unlock\" deletes it |\n| Open window | `Opened` link (space -> link) from `@deep-foundation/deepcase-opened` |\n| Which handler in the window | `OpenedHandler` link (Opened -> Handler) |\n| Visible neighbours | `Traveler` -> `Query` links |\n\n- API: `useOpenedMethods()` in `imports/cyto/opened.tsx` -> `open(id, handlerId)`, `close(id)`,\n  `isOpened(id)`.\n- Windows are React overlays anchored to graph nodes: `CytoReactLayout`\n  (`imports/cyto/react.tsx`) applies a CSS transform to a div synchronized with Cytoscape\n  `pan zoom`, `render`, `add`, `layoutstop`, `data`, `position bounds` events.\n- Window header (`imports/cyto/hooks.tsx` ~L640-710): handler picker popover\n  (`CytoReactLinksCard`), \"open in new full tab\" button, close button.\n- Full tab: `/client-handler?props={\"linkId\":..,\"handlerId\":..}` (deepcase-app\n  `pages/client-handler.tsx`) renders any handler as a standalone page.\n- Modal windows: editor (`CytoEditor`), packager (`PackagerInterface`: npm search + install /\n  uninstall tabs), connector (local docker/engine portal).\n- Top menu (`imports/cyto/menu.tsx`, framer-motion animated) — attached ButtonGroups:\n  `auth <id> x`, `space <id> x`, `container <id> x`, copy token / paste token / login token,\n  gql, editor; switches: autofocus, focus, opened, debug, types, traveler, breadcrumbs,\n  cytoHandlers, animation; layout select; search; clear focuses; Travelers popover; CytoHandlers\n  popover. Version text bottom-left; sun/moon toggle fixed top-right (`imports/switch-mode.tsx`).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Editors\n\n1. **Code editor modal** — `CytoEditor` (`imports/cyto/editor.tsx`, 656 lines):\n   - Tabs persisted in local store `editor-tabs` + active `editor-tab`; drafts in `editor-values`\n     (500 ms debounce). `EditorTab` = `{id, saved, active, loading, initialValue}` with unsaved dot.\n   - `EditorGrid` (`imports/editor/editor-grid.tsx`): two columns or VerticalSash split; left\n     Monaco, right switchable area (`editor-switcher.tsx`): **Preview** (runs handler on the link,\n     `fillSize` toggle), **Handlers** (which handlers bind this code), **Results** (handler/\n     promise results). Language list `editor-lang-list`, TS diagnostics options.\n2. **WYSIWYG** — `DeepWysiwyg` (`imports/deep-wysiwyg.tsx`): Slate with Mark buttons (bold,\n   italic, underline, code) and Block buttons (h1/h2, quote, numbered/bulleted list, align),\n   HTML (de)serialization via slate-serializers; `useStringSaver` writes the link's string value.\n3. **Forms** — rjsf JSON-schema forms and react-hook-form for structured values.\n4. **Graph editing** — insert / update / delete via radial menu and edgehandles.\n5. **Perception editor** — Monaco plus CodeMirror (`@uiw/react-codemirror`) for mobile.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Theming\n\n**deepcase theme** (`imports/theme/theme.tsx`): Chakra `extendTheme`, `cssVarPrefix: 'deepCase'`,\n`initialColorMode: 'light'`.\n\n| Token / color | Light | Dark |\n|---|---|---|\n| body bg | gray.100 | cyDark `#141214` |\n| backgroundModal | blue.50 | blue.900 `#19202B` |\n| editorPreviewBackgroundGrid | `#e5eefc` | `#404040` |\n| primary | `#0080ff` | `#0080ff` |\n| text | grayText `#3a3a3a` | whiteText `#ebf8ff` |\n| other | whiteBg `#fcfcfc`, gray.10 `#eee`, gray.900 `#111720` | |\n\nSemantic tokens: [REDACTED], borderColor, backgroundModal, buttonBackgroundModal, switchOn/Off,\neditorPreviewBackground, editorPreviewBackgroundGrid, whiteGray, bgColor, siteBg.\n\n**perception theme** (`perception-imports/imports/theme.tsx`): `initialColorMode: 'dark'`,\n`useSystemColorMode: true`; `deep` palette 50 `#EBF8FF`, 100 `#BEE3F8`, 400 `#4299E1`,\n600 `#2B6CB0`, 700 `#2C5282`, 800 `#1B2535`, 900 `#19202B`, 950 `#0000004d`; `danger` palette;\nactive `#00438F` (light) / cyan (dark); splash `#0D1117`; tokens deepBg, deepColor, deepBgHover,\ndeepBgActive, deepLine, deepLinkNodeBg; `ColorMode` button component.\n\n**deep (2025)** (`src/theme.tsx`): MUI dark, neutral primary `#cccccc`, per-value-type colors\n(value `#64B5F6`, symbol `#FFD54F`, undefined `#90A4AE`, promise `#4DB6AC`, boolean `#F06292`,\nstring `#81C784`, number `#7986CB`, bigint `#9575CD`, set `#4DD0E1`, ...), black canvas.\n\nGraph colors live separately in Cytoscape stylesheets (not in Chakra tokens) — a source of\nlight/dark bugs (see section 10).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Classic UI versions worth reproducing as themes\n\n1. **\"DeepCase classic light\" (0.1.0-beta, deepcase-app issue #76 screenshot)**\n   - Full-screen pale gray-blue canvas (`#edf2f7`-like, Chakra gray.100); hundreds of small\n     emoji nodes (⭐ Type, 📍 default, 🔥 Operation, 📎 Value, 🌲 Tree) with multi-line labels\n     `75 / type:Type / name:Schedule`; thin gray edges with arrowheads.\n   - Row 1: attached outlined button groups `auth 376 x | space 182 x | container 182 x |\n     copy token | paste token | gql | editor`; blue `packager` button top-right.\n   - Row 2: switches autofocus (on, blue), focus, debug, types, promises, traveler, breadcrumbs;\n     search input below; version `0.1.0-beta.2` bottom-left.\n2. **\"DeepCase dark + radial menu\" (issue #299)** — `#141214` canvas, selected node white circle\n   with blue ring and emoji avatar, large faded label `1044 type:User`, dark gray pie menu with\n   rotated wedge labels (editor, traveler (0), container, space, login, update, insert,\n   delete down, delete, unlock); blue active wedge.\n3. **\"DeepCase handler windows\"** — floating Chakra cards anchored to nodes, header with handler\n   picker / new tab / close; Monaco editor modal with tab strip and Preview/Handlers/Results.\n4. **\"Perception dark\"** — `deep` palette (`#19202B`/`#1B2535`), cyan active, HTML labels inside\n   nodes, keyboard-orientation navigation, slide-out auth panel, status dot.\n5. **\"deepcase.github.io landing\"** — `DeepFrame` (`imports/deep-case-frame/deep-frame.tsx`):\n   framer-motion spring tilt card (rotateX/rotateY +/-15 deg, perspective 450) with DeepCaseMini\n   inside, play button, toggler; flying words, typist effect.\n6. **\"Deep 2025 echarts\"** — black canvas, MUI dark, nodes colored by JS value type.\n7. **\"RTS / game mode\"** (deepcase-app #116, #112, #114) — UI \"inspired by RTS games\",\n   edge-scrolling, keyboard scroll, fullscreen; must be switchable back to \"boring\".\n8. **\"3D / VR force graph\"** (#159, commented-out aframe-forcegraph code).\n\nEach can be captured as a nested Links Notation theme: tokens (colors), graph style rules\n(selector -> properties), chrome layout (which menus/rows/switches exist), interaction profile\n(radial vs linear menu, mouse vs keyboard).\n\n---\n\n## 8. Patterns worth adopting (concrete)\n\n1. **Type-bound renderers as links**: `HandleClient(Type -> Handler)`; renderer lookup is a\n   query, so adding a renderer never touches the shell.\n2. **Context-sensitive handler selection** via `Context` links (same link, different view per\n   context: graph node, window, full tab, list row).\n3. **Separate visual-in-graph handlers** (`HandleCyto`) from content handlers — two binding kinds:\n   \"how it looks as a node\" vs \"how it looks when opened\".\n4. **Window state as links**: `Opened(space -> link)` + `OpenedHandler(opened -> handler)`.\n5. **Positions as links**: `Focus(space -> link) = {x, y}` — layout is data; unlock = delete.\n6. **Workspace = link** (space) and **insertion target = link** (container), both in the URL.\n7. **Traveler**: neighbourhood expansion as stored, toggleable queries (types/in/out/up/down/...).\n8. **Overlay sync**: HTML windows positioned by graph pan/zoom transform (`CytoReactLayout`).\n9. **Declarative graph DSL** (`<Graph><GraphNode/><GraphEdge/><GraphStyle/></Graph>`) — maps\n   1:1 to nested Links Notation.\n10. **Keyboard orientation map**: relation -> arrow-key direction table (`orientation.tsx`).\n11. **One store API, three backends** (URL / local / cookie) — shareable vs private state.\n12. **Semantic tokens with light/dark values** (Chakra semantic tokens, `cssVarPrefix`).\n13. **Require whitelist** for user code and lazy dependency resolution.\n14. **Error boundary per handler** with reset and source/dist view.\n15. **Layout picker** with layout parameters as data (force, cola, dagre).\n16. **Full-tab URL for any (link, handler) pair** — deep linking into any view.\n17. **Editor = tabs + code + Preview/Handlers/Results**; drafts autosaved with debounce.\n18. **WYSIWYG for string values** with HTML serialization.\n19. **App shell itself as a handler** (perception `Layout` link with Auth/Status/ColorMode slots).\n20. **Per-value-type color palette** (deep 2025) as a theme dimension.\n21. **Link label template** (`id / type / name / value / symbol`) and **type Symbol** (emoji\n    icon per type) as default node rendering.\n22. **Radial context menu** for link operations; linear alternative for readability (#299).\n\n---\n\n## 9. Duplication candidates\n\n| Duplicated thing | Locations | Suggested single home |\n|---|---|---|\n| ClientHandler / evalClientHandler / CatchErrors | deepcase `imports/client-handler.tsx`, deeplinks `imports/client-handler.tsx`, perception-imports `react-handler.tsx` | one renderer core in link-foundation/ui |\n| Chakra theme | deepcase `imports/theme/theme.tsx`, perception-imports `imports/theme.tsx`, deep `src/theme.tsx` (MUI) | theme as Links Notation, adapters per toolkit |\n| Color mode toggle | `switch-mode.tsx`, `color-mode-toggle.tsx`, perception `ColorMode` | one component |\n| Graph wrapper | deepcase `cyto/graph.tsx`, perception-app `imports/graph.tsx`, deep echarts | one declarative graph DSL with renderer backends |\n| Editor | deepcase `cyto/editor.tsx`, perception-imports Editor (Monaco + CodeMirror) | one editor component |\n| Wysiwyg | deepcase `deep-wysiwyg.tsx` and copies in other packages | one |\n| Platform shells | deepcase-app and perception-app (Capacitor, Electron, Next) | one shell template |\n| Stores | `@deep-foundation/store` used plus ad-hoc localStorage in editor | one store API |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Problems, bugs, limitations\n\n**Architectural**\n- `eval` of TSX strings: no sandbox, full DOM/network access; whitelist only limits `require`\n  (deepcase #85 proposes renaming to \"unsafe\" handlers and adding safe ones).\n- Handlers tied to React + Chakra + browser; no React Native / Swift / Kotlin path.\n- Handler dependency resolution and paths (#60, #63, #64 `import.meta`), MUI in handlers (#72/#74).\n- Graph styles live in Cytoscape stylesheets, outside theme tokens -> dark/light mismatches\n  (#22 icons disappear in dark mode; deepcase-app #234/#80/#296 light-theme readability).\n- No label LOD: tiny/overlapping text is rendered (#37, #47); no pagination (#36).\n- Performance: too many re-renders (#65), slow/crashes after 24 h (#24), freezes/white screen\n  (deepcase-app #226/#123), iPadOS nodes disappear (#235), edges disappear when moving (#320).\n\n**Layout**\n- d3-force with `infinite: true` is unstable and wanders (#51, #52, deepcase-app #269/#218/#191);\n  cola cannot accept positions (#27); auto-place over the whole screen requested (#56);\n  Any-Any link treated as node (#28).\n\n**Windows**\n- z-index of handler window over modal (deepcase-app #290); handler not fully visible in preview\n  (#297); handler link floats (#53); double click opens twice (#30); handler not reopened /\n  freeze with duplicate handlers (#282/#281); remember last opened handler (#292); draggable\n  widget header requested (#198).\n\n**Editor**\n- State/tab bugs (deepcase-app #243, #238, #231, #178, #171, #170, #138, #137, #240), random\n  links opened (#45), splitter not remembered (#54), code lost when switching tabs (#43),\n  links unsorted (#84), no warn-before-update (#44), cannot set empty string (#35), clicking a\n  code file runs it (#3).\n\n**UX**\n- Rotated radial menu text unreadable (#299); browser context menu conflicts (#57/#87/#95);\n  search case / trailing space bugs (#110/#99/#245); drag & drop broken (#293).\n- Requested: user-configurable themes (#300, #247) and backgrounds/animated handlers (#301),\n  multilingual UI (#274), linear.app-style keyboard (#228), graph aggregation / filters / time\n  sort / PNG-PDF export (#89, Linkurious/Ogma references), zoom-into-space (#82), return to last\n  space (#83), pinning (#41), graphical undo/snapshots (#8), 3D (#159), voice/sounds (#155-#158).\n- Build/OS: Vite/bun (#9/#10), many build/OS issues (deepcase-app #31-#41).\n\n---\n\n## 11. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n\n1. **Replace eval'd TSX with Links Notation component trees.** A handler becomes a LiNo tree\n   (element / props / children / bindings) interpreted by per-platform renderers (DOM, React,\n   React Native, Vue, SwiftUI, Compose). Keep an explicit \"unsafe code\" escape hatch, sandboxed.\n2. **Keep the binding links** (`HandleClient`, `HandleCyto`, `Context`) as LiNo relations:\n   `(render: Type -> view)`, `(renderNode: Type -> nodeStyle)`, `(inContext: view -> context)`.\n3. **Map theme tokens to LiNo theme links**: e.g.\n   ```\n   (theme deepcase-classic\n     (mode light (bg gray.100) (primary #0080ff) (text #3a3a3a))\n     (mode dark (bg #141214) (modal #19202B) (text #ebf8ff)))\n   ```\n4. **Map Cytoscape selectors to LiNo style rules**\n   (`(style link-type (line dashed 5 5) (arrow triangle))`) so graph and chrome share tokens.\n5. **Window/space state** (`Opened`, `OpenedHandler`, `Focus`, `Traveler`) maps directly to\n   nested/tabbed LiNo documents — a saved workspace is just a LiNo file; this also gives\n   animation recording (timestamped Focus/Opened changes) and undo snapshots (#8).\n6. **Convert `deep.json` packages** (types, handlers, symbols) to LiNo; preserve type Symbols\n   (emoji) as the default icon set.\n7. **Chrome as data**: top menu rows, switches, radial menu items, keyboard orientation table —\n   all declared in LiNo so classic themes (section 7) are reproducible configurations.\n8. **Avoid inherited bugs**: bounded force simulation (stop/settle), label LOD, single z-index\n   layer manager for overlays vs modals, editor state keyed by link id, horizontal radial labels\n   with icons.\n"

The repos around it are the deepcase-app shell (web, Capacitor mobile, Electron, Chrome extension), a second generation called perception (perception-imports and perception-app), the deepcase.github.io landing site, and a 2025 rewrite `deep-foundation/deep` (MUI dark theme, echarts graph). Which handler is used is chosen by a database query that can depend on a `Context` link. The code is run with `eval`; only the libraries it may `require` are whitelisted. A second binding kind, `HandleCyto`, stores how each type is drawn in the graph, also as links.\n- **Window state is links too:**\n  - The workspace (space) and the insertion target (container) are link ids kept in the URL.\n  - Node positions are `Focus` links holding `{x, y}`.\n  - Open windows are `Opened` and `OpenedHandler` links.\n  - Neighbour expansion is `Traveler` links pointing to Query links.\n  - Any link plus handler can open as a full tab at `/client-handler?props=...`.\n\n  This maps almost directly onto nested Links Notation documents, and could also support animation recording and undo.\n- **Graph:**\n  - Each link is drawn as a node, with separate edges for from, to (with arrowheads) and type (dashed).\n  - Layouts are d3-force (the default), cola and dagre, with a node and background radial context menu.\n  - Perception adds a declarative `<Graph>/<GraphNode>/<GraphEdge>/<GraphStyle>` component set and an arrow-key map over link relations.\n- **Editors:** a Monaco modal with persisted tabs, autosaved drafts and a Preview/Handlers/Results side pane; a Slate rich-text editor for string values; JSON-schema forms.\n- **Theming:** the report records colour tokens for deepcase (Chakra, light/dark), perception (dark \"deep\" palette) and the 2025 rewrite (MUI, colours per JS value type). API:\n     - `Parser().parse()` expands indented or multi-line-paren children into path links such as `((ok: button) (label OK))`;\n     - `parseGroups()` preserves the tree as `{element, children}`;\n     - `Link(id, values)` with `.format()` and `.equals()`;\n     - `parseIndentedDocument` / `formatIndentedDocument`;\n     - `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH` is 64.\n   - Other npm packages: lino-objects-codec 0.9.4, lino-i18n 0.5.0, lino-arguments 0.4.0.\n   - Associative tech stack (formal-ai doc): links-notation, lino-objects-codec, link-cli (doublets-rs), meta-language, link-calculator, lino-arguments, lino-i18n, command-stream, web-capture, web-search, doublets-web (IndexedDB compatibility target), relative-meta-logic, meta-theory, transformer, Agent CLI, Hive Mind.\n   - Proposed architecture:\n     - runtime interpreter with thin renderers; JS-first; stable link IDs;\n     - layered config: defaults < theme < site < user < session;\n     - overrides exported as LiNo patches for agents;\n     - Web Components as the reference renderer, with React and Vue wrappers;\n     - Zag-like state machines, Floating UI positioning;\n     - DTCG 2025.10 tokens via Style Dictionary;\n     - Web Animations API (WAAPI) and Motion for animation; rrweb optional;\n     - SwiftUI and Compose renderers; shared conformance fixtures;\n     - assets: own CC0, third-party recorded with SPDX IDs, REUSE.toml.\n   - Licensing to avoid: GSAP (proprietary, forbids competing no-code animation tools), tldraw SDK (license key), Theatre.js Studio (AGPL), Remix Icon (custom license since Jan 2026), SF Symbols/SF fonts, Material Web (maintenance mode). [2026-11-01T11:41:32.290Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Links Notation (LiNo) ecosystem: research for the associative UI framework\n\nResearch input for [issue #1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1).\nIt covers the notation the whole framework (DOM-like structure, config, styles,\nanimations, the WYSIWYG editor and the links-network visualizer) is meant to be\nwritten in. Data was collected on 2026-11-01 from GitHub and package registries.\nSources: shallow/sparse checkouts of the repositories listed below and `gh api`.\nNo downloaded code was executed.\n\nPrimary sources:\n\n- Repository: <https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation>\n- Grammar (EBNF, v0.24.0 grammar, current packages 0.27.1):\n  [`docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md),\n  and the same grammar written in LiNo itself:\n  [`docs/grammar/grammar.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/grammar/grammar.lino)\n- Reference literals: [`docs/protocol/reference-literals.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/protocol/reference-literals.md)\n- Binary form: [`docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md)\n- Cross-language parity corpus: [`parity/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/tree/main/parity) (`parity/text-fixtures.json`)\n\n## 1. Syntax summary\n\nA **link** is an ordered sequence of references, written `(id: v1 v2 ...)`.\nThe id is optional, and so is everything else. A **reference** is either a\nsimple token or a delimited (quoted) string. Values can themselves be links,\nso nesting goes as deep as you like.\n\n### 1.1 Links and ids\n\n```lino\npapa loves mama                 # anonymous link with three values\nfamily: papa mama son daughter  # link with id \"family\" and four values\n(papa loves mama)               # same as line 1, explicit parentheses\n(outer: (inner: v1 v2) v3)      # inline nesting\n```\n\nThe id is a **single** reference followed by `:`. `a b: c` is not a link with a\ntwo-word id.\n\n### 1.2 Indentation (hierarchy without parentheses)\n\n```lino\nfamily:\n  papa\n  mama\n```\n\nThis is `(family: papa mama)`. A value line that has indented children forms a\nnested link:\n\n```lino\nroot:\n  child1\n  child2\n    grandchild\n```\n\nThis is `(root: child1 (child2 grandchild))`. The rules:\n\n- The first content line sets the base indentation.\n- Children must be indented more than their parent, and siblings must be\n  indented equally.\n- Only spaces count; tabs do not.\n\n### 1.3 Multi-line groups (nested context, issue #282, v0.14.0+)\n\n```lino\narray (\n  a\n    b\n  c\n)\n```\n\nA `(` opens a nested context that starts again at indentation level 0, so the\nindentation inside it is structural. A body that yields a single link collapses\nto that link, so `(a b c)` is one link. `((a b))` stays distinct from `(a b)`.\n\n### 1.4 References and quoting\n\n- Simple reference: any characters except whitespace, `(`, `:` and `)`. So\n  `button.primary`, `@space.3`, `$accent`, `8px`, `100%`, `0.25` and `-1` are\n  all plain simple references.\n- Delimiters: `\"`, `'` and `` ` `` behave identically. N-quoting works as\n  follows: a run of N delimiters opens and closes, and a run of 2N delimiters\n  inside the body stands for N literal delimiters. Example: `\"\"say \"\"hi\"\" \"\"`.\n- `\"\"` is the empty reference. Formatters write it explicitly so it round-trips.\n- Lossless literal, v0.24.0+: `~1{hex UTF-8}`, for example `~1{e282ac}` for the\n  euro sign. Any string, control characters included, round-trips exactly. The\n  prefix `~[0-9]+{` is reserved.\n\n### 1.5 Comments (issue #301)\n\n```lino\n# the machines this deploys to\ndeploy: staging # only staging, for now\n```\n\n- `#` opens a comment only at the start of the document or after whitespace.\n  `issue#1047` and `\"#\"` are literal.\n- Comment characters are replaced by spaces, so error positions stay correct.\n- Comments are on by default and can be disabled (`comments: false`) for legacy\n  documents.\n- Formatters quote references that start with `#` (`'#tag'`).\n\n**Consequence for UI:** CSS hex colours (`#3390ec`) must be quoted, otherwise\nthey are read as comments. URLs and CSS pseudo-classes contain `:`, so they\nmust be quoted too (`\"https://...\"`, `\":hover\"`).\n\n### 1.6 Other forms\n\n- **Streaming parsers** exist in all 8 languages: push events (`link`, `error`,\n  `end`) plus iterators. Useful for large documents and live editing.\n- **Binary Links Notation v1** (`docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md`,\n  originating in link-cli PR #106) has golden vectors. It is a candidate wire\n  and storage format between a UI runtime and a doublets store.\n\n## 2. Implementations\n\nAll implementations are hand-written. JS is the reference, and the others are\nheld to it by the shared parity corpus (`parity/text-fixtures.json`) and golden\nround-trip tests. `.parse(text)` returns `Link[]`.\n  - `.parseGroups(text)` returns a `LinksGroup` tree. `LinksGroup` exists only in\n    JS, C#, Java and C++.\n- `new Link(id, values)`, with `.format(options)` and `.toString()`.\n- `formatLinks(links, { lessParentheses, maxLineLength, indentLongLines, maxInlineRefs, groupConsecutive })`.\n- `parseIndentedDocument` / `formatIndentedDocument` (JS and C++ only).\n- `escapeReference(ref, { minimal })` / `unescapeReference(ref)`.\n- `StreamParser`: events `link`, `error` and `end`, plus `position()`, `drain()`\n  and `reset()`.\n\n### 2.2 Round-trip guarantees\n\n| Guarantee | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| `parse -> format -> parse` yields the same link tree | Yes, in every language, tested against the golden corpus |\n| Any Unicode string survives as a reference | Yes, via quoting or the `~1{}` literal |\n| Same tree across languages | Yes, via the parity fixtures |\n| Comments survive | **No.** They are dropped during parsing |\n| Original layout survives (indentation vs parentheses, quote style, blank lines) | **No.** The formatter re-chooses the layout |\n| Quoted vs bare distinction is visible in the tree | **No.** `\"1\"` and `1` are the same reference string |\n\nFor a WYSIWYG editor that edits the user's `.lino` file, the last three rows\nmatter most. See section 5.\n\n### 2.3 Open and relevant issues (links-notation)\n\n- Open: [#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)\n  (publish Java and PHP) and #350 (dependabot). The repository is otherwise\n  quiet and stable.\n- Closed but relevant to UI:\n  - #301 (comments)\n  - #282 (nested context for multi-line groups)\n  - #332 (lossless reference literal)\n  - #351 (browser bundling)\n  - #313 (formatter / empty reference)\n  - #184 (multi-reference values)\n\n## 3. What a UI dialect needs that LiNo already has\n\n| UI need | Existing LiNo feature |\n| --- | --- |\n| Tree of elements (DOM-like) | Indentation and nested groups. `parseGroups` keeps the hierarchy |\n| Element identity | Link id (`save:`). Ids are single references, globally addressable |\n| Graph, not just tree (reuse, references between elements and tokens) | A reference is just a name, so `@token` / `$name` / an element id can point anywhere in the document. This is native to the associative model |\n| Attributes / props | `(key value)` sub-links, the lino-objects-codec convention |\n| Text content with any characters | Quoting, N-quoting and `~1{}` literals |\n| Comments in hand-written files | `#` comments (read side only) |\n| Big documents, live editing | Streaming parsers, `position()` for error locations |\n| One spec for many targets | 8 implementations with a parity corpus. Rust compiles to WASM |\n| Typed config objects | lino-objects-codec (quoted = string, bare = number/bool/null) |\n| i18n strings | lino-i18n catalogues and React adapter |\n| Settings resolution | lino-arguments (pure build for browser) |\n| Import of existing HTML/CSS | meta-language HTML/CSS importers with lossless CST |\n| Storage as a links network | doublets-web (WASM), link-cli, binary LiNo |\n| Visualizing the network | link-cli workbench and doublets-web playground graph views (prior art for the issue's \"LiNo -> links network UI\" converter) |\n\n## 5. Gaps and open questions\n\n1. **Typed values.** The core tree has only strings, and `\"1\"` and `1` produce\n   the same reference. The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.\n\n   Recommendation: (b) for dimensions, durations and colours, with (a) as the\n   fallback for free-form props. Also ask upstream for a `quoted` flag on\n   parsed references, which would remove the need for a second reader.\n2. **Units and colours.**\n   - `8px`, `0.2s`, `50%` and `1.5rem` are valid bare references, but they are\n     strings until a schema parses them.\n   - Hex colours must be quoted because of `#` comments.\n   - Alternative: `rgb(...)` / `oklch(...)` as links, for example\n     `(oklch 0.62 0.19 255)`, which is better for the associative model and for\n     theme maths.\n3. **`:` in values.** URLs, CSS pseudo-classes (`:hover`), media queries and\n   ratios (`16:9`) need quoting. Prefer structured links instead:\n   `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))` and `(aspect 16 9)`.\n4. **Comments and formatting are lost on round trip.** A WYSIWYG editor that\n   writes back to `.lino` will strip the user's comments and reflow the layout.\n   Options:\n   - (a) A CST mode upstream (trivia and spans, as meta-language already does\n     for CSS).\n   - (b) Make comments first-class links, for example `(note \"...\")`.\n   - (c) Patch-in-place edits using parser positions.\n\n   This needs an issue upstream in links-notation.\n5. **Ordering.** Link values are ordered, which is good for children and\n   keyframes. Property order, however, should be insignificant. The dialect\n   must state which parts are sequences (children, keyframes, transitions) and\n   which are sets (props). It must also define the meaning of a duplicate key:\n   last wins, as in lino-store logs.\n6. **Ids and scoping.** Ids are document-global strings, and nothing prevents\n   duplicates. Questions:\n   - Do we need namespaces (`login.save`) or nested id scopes per component?\n   - How do ids map to doublet numeric addresses, and are they stable across\n     edits? The editor needs stable ids for selection, undo and collaboration.\n7. **References for styles and tokens.** There is no built-in reference sigil.\n   A convention is needed:\n   - `@token.path` for design tokens\n   - `$param` for component parameters (the linksql / transformer convention)\n   - a bare id for elements and keyframe tracks\n\n   Open questions: resolution order (component, then theme, then base),\n   cycles, and fallbacks (`(or @color.accent \"#3390ec\")`).\n8. **Schemas and validation.** lino-schema is only a stub. The dialect needs a\n   schema (which props an element accepts, their types and defaults) for:\n   - the editor's property panel\n   - validation\n   - codegen to React, Vue, React Native, SwiftUI and Compose\n9. **Expressions and bindings.** Event handlers, data bindings and conditional\n   rendering need a small expression vocabulary, for example\n   `(on press (emit save))`, `(bind value $draft.text)` and\n   `(when $sending (show spinner))`. Decide whether this reuses the linksql\n   substitution syntax.\n10. **Missing languages.**\n    - Swift: no implementation exists.\n    - Kotlin: blocked by the unpublished Java package (#192).\n\n    Options: native targets either ship a parser or consume a precompiled\n    form (JSON or binary LiNo) produced by the JS/Rust toolchain.\n11. **Security.** The parser has `maxDepth = 64` and `maxInputSize`. User-supplied\n    themes must never contain executable code. Event handlers are names, not\n    code.\n\n## 6. Proposed sketch of a UI dialect in LiNo (PROPOSAL, not an existing format)\n\n> Everything in this section is a **proposal for discussion**. It is not\n> implemented anywhere. It only uses syntax the current grammar (0.27.1)\n> accepts. The meaning of every name is defined by the proposed dialect\n> schema, not by LiNo itself.\n\nConventions used:\n\n- An indented id link (`save:`) declares an element, token set or animation.\n  Its first value is the **kind** (`button`, `stack`, `theme`, `animation`).\n- Props are `(key value...)` sub-links. Their order does not matter.\n- Children, keyframes and transitions are ordered.\n- `@a.b.c` is a design-token reference. `$name` is a component parameter. A\n  bare id is an element or animation reference.\n- Quoted text is a literal string. Bare values are interpreted by the property\n  schema (number, dimension, duration, enum).\n- Colours are quoted hex or structured `(oklch L C H)`.\n\n### 6.1 A button\n\n```lino\nsave:\n  button\n  (label (t \"composer.send\"))          # i18n key, resolved by lino-i18n\n  (variant primary)\n  (size md)\n  (icon send)                          # public-domain icon set, by name\n  (disabled $draft.empty)              # binding to a parameter\n  (on press (emit message.send))       # handlers are names, never code\n  (style\n    (background @color.accent-fill)\n    (color @color.on-accent)\n    (radius @radius.control)\n    (padding @space.2 @space.3)\n    (state hover (background @color.accent))\n    (state pressed (scale 0.97)))\n  (enter bubble-in)                    # reference to an animation below\n```\n\n### 6.2 A layout\n\n```lino\nchat-screen:\n  split\n  (direction row)\n  (resizable true)\n  (remember-size \"chat.columns\")\n  (children chat-list conversation)\n\nchat-list:\n  list\n  (virtualized true)\n  (item-height 3.5rem)\n  (min-width 16rem)\n  (items $chats)\n  (template chat-row)\n\nconversation:\n  stack\n  (direction column)\n  (max-width @size.chat-column)\n  (children\n    (header (title $chat.name))\n    (messages (items $messages) (group-by sender) (follow bottom))\n    composer)\n\ncompact-layout:\n  breakpoint\n  (when (max-width 640px))\n  (override chat-screen (direction column) (children conversation))\n```\n\n`children` holds element ids, so the same element can sit in several layouts.\nThat reuse is the graph property the associative model gives for free. Inline\nanonymous children (`(header ...)`) are also allowed.\n\n### 6.3 A theme token set\n\n```lino\nbase:\n  theme\n  (space (1 0.25rem) (2 0.5rem) (3 0.75rem) (4 1rem))\n  (radius (control 8px) (bubble 15px))\n  (size (control-h 2.25rem) (chat-column 44rem))\n  (motion (fast 120ms) (normal 200ms) (easing standard))\n\ntelegram-light:\n  theme\n  (extends base)\n  (mode light)\n  (color\n    (bg \"#ffffff\")\n    (text \"#000000\")\n    (accent \"#3390ec\")\n    (accent-fill \"#2a7bd0\")              # darkened for 4.5:1 contrast\n    (on-accent \"#ffffff\")\n    (bubble-out \"#e3fee0\")\n    (bubble-in \"#ffffff\"))\n  (radius (bubble 15px))\n\ntelegram-dark:\n  theme\n  (extends telegram-light)\n  (mode dark)\n  (color (bg \"#212121\") (text \"#ffffff\") (bubble-out \"#8774e1\") (bubble-in \"#212121\"))\n```\n\nThe token names were chosen so that meta-sovereign's existing CSS custom\nproperties (`--bg`, `--accent`, `--accent-fill`, `--bubble-out`,\n`--bubble-radius`, `--control-h`, `--chat-column`) map onto them one to one.\nA theme compiles to `:root[data-theme=...]` CSS variables on the web and to\nplatform theme objects elsewhere. The colour values above are illustrative.\n\n### 6.4 An animation keyframe track\n\n```lino\nbubble-in:\n  animation\n  (duration @motion.normal)\n  (easing \"cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)\")  # quoted because it has parens\n  (fill both)\n  (keyframes\n    (at 0 (opacity 0) (translate-y 8px) (scale 0.98))\n    (at 0.6 (opacity 1))\n    (at 1 (opacity 1) (translate-y 0) (scale 1)))\n  (reduced-motion (duration 0ms))        # honours prefers-reduced-motion\n\ntyping-dots:\n  animation\n  (duration 1.2s)\n  (iterations infinite)\n  (tracks\n    (track dot-1 (keyframes (at 0 (opacity 0.3)) (at 0.5 (opacity 1)) (at 1 (opacity 0.3))))\n    (track dot-2 (delay 0.15s) (same-as dot-1))\n    (track dot-3 (delay 0.3s) (same-as dot-1)))\n```\n\n`keyframes` is an ordered sequence of `(at offset props...)`. `tracks` lets one\nanimation drive several targets, which suits a timeline editor in the WYSIWYG\ntool. Targets: CSS `@keyframes` / the Web Animations API, React Native\n`Animated`, SwiftUI `keyframeAnimator` and Compose `keyframes`.\n\n### 6.5 Open decisions for this sketch\n\n- Should the kind be the first value (`save:\\n  button`), or should the id\n  carry it (`button.save:`)? The first keeps ids clean. The second makes\n  queries such as \"all buttons\" a prefix match.\n- Should `style` be inline, or always a reference to a named style link? The\n  latter deduplicates better, can use deduplino, and maps better to doublets.\n- Should a document be decoded through lino-objects-codec (typed) or through\n  the core parser plus a schema (strings)? Both are viable. The schema route\n  keeps one parser across all 8 languages.\n"

[2026-11-01T11:41:44.043Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Research: link-assistant/formal-ai web UI\n\nScope: the browser-facing UI of [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai).\nThat covers the `js/` folder, the static HTML pages, CSS, i18n through `lino-i18n`, IndexedDB memory,\nthe web-search component, the chat interface, settings, and trace and links-network visualization.\nWe read it as input for the associative UI framework planned in\n[link-foundation/ui#1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1).\n\nMethod:\n\n- A sparse, blob-filtered shallow clone of `js/`, `ts/`, `packages/`, `package.json` and `docs/`. The repo is about 1 GB and was not fully cloned.\n- Issue bodies and titles fetched with `gh`.\n- All downloaded content was treated as data and never executed.\n\nURL bases:\n\n- `FA` = `https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/`\n- `I` = `https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/`\n\n---\n\n## 1. Overview\n\n### 1.1 Stack\n\n| Layer | Technology (version pinned in `package.json`) |\n|---|---|\n| Chat app (`/app/`) | React 19.3.1, written as JSX, no TypeScript at runtime |\n| Component library | `@chakra-ui/react` ^3.37 with `@emotion/react`. Adoption is incremental (issues [#541](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/541), [#550](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/550)), configured with `preflight: false` and empty `globalCss` |\n| Markdown / sanitising | `marked` 18.1.1 and `dompurify` 3.4.17 |\n| Diagrams | `mermaid` 12.2.0, loaded on demand (`mermaid.bundle.js`) with `securityLevel: strict` |\n| OCR | `tesseract.js` 7, loaded on demand (`ocr.bundle.js`, experimental setting) |\n| i18n | `lino-i18n` 0.4.0, bundled into `vendor.bundle.js` and exposed as `FormalAiVendor.LinoI18n` |\n| Web search | `@link-assistant/web-search` 0.11.1, using RRF merge and dedup, plus a web-capture HTTP adapter |\n| Code parsing in browser | `@babel/parser` |\n| Syntax highlight | `js/syntax-highlight.js`, a dependency-free highlighter that emits `hljs-*` classes |\n| Engine | WASM worker (`js/formal_ai_worker.wasm` from `js/wasm-worker/src/lib.rs`) plus JS worker modules (`js/worker/`, listed in `js/worker-modules.js`) |\n| Bundling | `bun build` into IIFEs: `vendor.bundle.js`, `web-search-component.bundle.js`, `ocr.bundle.js`, `mermaid.bundle.js`, `app.js`. plus a preferred language |\n| Mode | `chat`, `agent`, `fullAuto` |\n| Thinking detail | `brief`, `standard`, `detailed` |\n| Min message animation | Default 2 s; motion should honour reduced-motion ([#672](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/672) F3) |\n| Reasoning knobs | temperature, guess probability, follow-up probability, definition fusion, blueprint composition |\n| Misc | experimental OCR, location, assistant name, demo mode, diagnostics |\n\n### 2.4 Theming\n\n- **Tokens.** `--fa-*` custom properties are defined in `01-tokens.css`. Dark values come from `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback.\n- **Selector counts.** About 248 `[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and 244 `[data-theme=\"light\"]` selectors across the CSS. Most dark overrides live in `06-dark-theme.css`.\n- **Chakra bridge.** `theme.js` maps tokens 1:1, e.g. `fa.surface.card → var(--fa-surface-card)`. Chakra components therefore follow the same CSS variables without a parallel theme object.\n- **Root-class composition.** Skins, chat styles, composer styles and icon packs are orthogonal root classes. The CSS combines them, e.g. `.ui-skin-glass.composer-style-glass-clear`.\n\n### 2.5 i18n\n\n- **Runtime.** `js/i18n.js` is an IIFE exposing `window.FormalAiI18n`. It calls `loadCatalogs([...])` and `createI18n({locales, defaultLocale:'en', fallback:['en']})`, then dispatches `formal-ai:i18n-ready`.\n- **Catalog format.** Nested Links Notation blocks (`en` / `buttons` / `key \"...\"`) with `\"\"\"` multiline strings ([#117](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/117)).\n- **CI checks.**\n  - Key parity across all locales (`tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`).\n  - A lint against hardcoded natural language ([#659](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/659), R379).\n- **Gaps.**\n  - `PUBLISHED_RUNTIME_SOURCE = \"lino-i18n@0.3.0\"` in `i18n.js`, while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n  - The vanilla pages use their own JS `LABELS` dicts instead of the catalogs.\n\n### 2.6 Preferences & memory\n\n- **Preferences (`preferences.js`, 123 lines).**\n  - A hand-rolled Links Notation reader/writer with root `demo_preferences` and indented `key \"value\"` lines. Booleans are stored as `on`/`off`.\n  - API: `[REDACTED] {load, save, format, parse, STORAGE_KEY, ROOT}`.\n  - Every page shares the `formal-ai.preferences.v1` key.\n  - It does not use the `links-notation` parser.\n- **Memory (`memory.js`).**\n  - IndexedDB database `formal-ai-demo`, store `events`, root `demo_memory`, bundle header `formal_ai_bundle`, `LINK_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION \"0.2.0\"`.\n  - Events are append-only. `EXPORT_FIELDS` include `kind`, `role`, `intent`, `tool`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `content`, `attachments`, `sentAt`, `evidence`, `accessCount`, `writeCount`, `conversationId` and `conversationTitle`.\n  - It exports `formal-ai-memory.lino`. Import, reset and purge sit behind confirmations ([#196](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/196)).\n  - It reports a `doublets-web` backend only if that global runtime is present.\n\n### 2.7 Web search component\n\n- **Ranking.** `getDefaultProviderIds()` selects the providers, and `mergeResults` merges their results with the `rrf` strategy and `removeDuplicates`.\n- **Capture adapter.** Fetches `/fetch?url=…` from a configurable base (default `http://localhost:3000`, 2,000 ms deadline). On transport failure it falls back to a direct CORS fetch.\n- **Output.** Results are pushed as evidence strings into the trace. [#153](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/153) asks for a unified, deduplicated search-result template.\n\n### 2.8 Accessibility snapshot\n\n- **ARIA.** About 89 `aria-*` attributes: `aria-label` ×26, `aria-hidden` ×14, `aria-pressed` ×11. Also 9 `role=status`, plus `radiogroup`/`menu`/`menuitem`/`option` roles and 2 `aria-live` regions.\n- **Focus.** `:focus-visible` styles appear in `02`, `03`, `06` and `07`.\n- **Reduced motion.** `prefers-reduced-motion` appears only 3 times, all in `04-message-content.css`.\n- **Keyboard.** The resizer supports keyboard steps (40 px, 16 px with Shift).\n- **Audits.** No systematic audit (axe or similar) exists in CI. Open bug [#447](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/447): the left panel cannot be scrolled with the mouse.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Associative tech stack usage plan for the UI framework\n\n| Component | What for in the UI framework | How (based on formal-ai evidence) |\n|---|---|---|\n| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) parser | Canonical text form of every UI artefact: component trees, themes, tokens, skins, layouts, settings and recorded animations | Replace hand-rolled readers like `js/preferences.js` with the official JS parser. Keep a `.lino` file per artefact so it can be diffed and reviewed, as formal-ai does with catalogs, example prompts and memory exports |\n| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec) | Typed (de)serialization of props, theme objects and config at strict boundaries | Use the codec's indented-format parser to validate on import, mirroring `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `associative_package.rs`. Run strict decoding on paste/import of themes or layouts, and canonical encoding on export so round-trips are byte-stable |\n| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) | All user-visible strings in every binding (JS, React, Vue, RN; Swift and Kotlin through generated tables) | Reuse formal-ai's nested and multiline catalog layout, `loadCatalogs`/`createI18n` with an `en` fallback, a ready event, CI key parity and a hardcoded-language lint. Forbid per-page JS `LABELS` tables |\n| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) | Layered configuration: defaults, `.lenv`, env, URL params and CLI flags, merged into a single UI config | Used today only at the Rust CLI boundary. In the framework, use it for the dev server/CLI and a small browser adapter that reads URL query and localStorage in the same precedence. Expose the result as one Links Notation config document (generalizing `formal-ai.preferences.v1`) |\n| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web) / IndexedDB | Persistent store for UI state, WYSIWYG edit history and animation/interaction recordings | Copy the `memory.js` model: an append-only event log projected to doublets, IndexedDB fallback, and `doublets-web` reported only when present. Every WYSIWYG edit becomes an appended event, which gives undo/redo, replay and animation recording for free (matches #672 F4) |\n| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language) | Lossless CST/AST of UI documents: component source (JSX/Vue SFC/SwiftUI/Compose) and markup | Use it as formal-ai uses it in `rust/src/coding/cst.rs` and `document_formats.rs`: parse, check a full match and reconstruct text losslessly. This enables WYSIWYG edits that write back to source in each binding's language, plus translation between bindings (as formal-ai's `js` to `ts` mirror does) |\n| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli) query / substitution dialect | Selecting and rewriting UI links: theme rules, skin overrides, migrations, codemods | Theme and skin application becomes \"match link pattern, substitute values\", like `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `links_substitution_query/`. The native store (link-cli plus doublets-rs) can back a desktop or server-side design registry |\n| [web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search) / [web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture) | Optional components: search box and results with RRF merge; page capture for previews or documentation | Ship as opt-in packages. Reuse the unified result template requested in #153 and the capture adapter's timeout and CORS fallback |\n| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) (concept) | Context-relative values: a token resolves differently by context (theme, platform guideline, locale, density) | Model \"token X in context dark/iOS/ru\" as relative statements instead of flat override files; this addresses the 1,097-line dark override sheet |\n| [transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer) (concept) | Transformations between representations: Links Notation to React/Vue/RN/SwiftUI/Compose | Vocabulary for binding generators; formal-ai's `substitution.rs` shows `.lino` rules rewriting link patterns |\n| [link-calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator) | Optional: computed layout values and expression fields in WYSIWYG mode | Evaluate expression properties (e.g. `spacing * 2`) with an inspectable Links Notation trace |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **CSS-token → component-library bridge.**\n   - One set of `--fa-*` CSS variables is the source of truth.\n   - Chakra semantic tokens point at `var(--…)` (`theme.js`).\n   - The framework should generate both from one Links Notation token document.\n2. **Orthogonal appearance axes as root classes.** Skin × chat style × composer style × icon pack × theme combine freely and are applied as root classes plus CSS vars. This maps directly to a \"theme = set of axis values\" model.\n3. **Icon-pack abstraction.** Each action has a semantic name, mapped per pack (font name, short name, shape), with a `names` text-only fallback. Use this as the basis for public-domain icon handling.\n4. **Priority-based responsive overflow.** `data-menu-priority` moves top-bar actions into the drawer as width shrinks. #388 asks for measured sizes; generalize this into a layout primitive.\n5. **Collapsible sections with isolate.** An isolate button plus Shift+click \"expand only this\".\n6. **Per-setting reset and reset-all** using a default-detection helper (`settingIsDefault`).\n7. **Shared preferences contract** across separately built pages: one storage key, Links Notation format, `data-theme` on `<html>`.\n8. **Natural-language interface commands.** The UI can be configured through chat (`interface-commands.jsx`), a natural fit for an associative, notation-driven config.\n9. **Issue reporting with user context.**\n   - A prefilled GitHub issue within the URL budget, embedding UI state (skin, theme, viewport, language, mode).\n   - Use it as a framework-level \"report UI bug\" component.\n10. **Append-only event log** for memory, giving export/import as `.lino` and destructive actions behind confirmation and export prompts.\n11. **Quality gates in CI.**\n    - i18n key parity and a hardcoded-language lint.\n    - A UI-boundary lint (no business logic in view code).\n    - Per-locale and per-theme screenshots.\n    - A cross-org duplication scanner (`cross-org-duplication.yml`).\n12. **Stable test hooks.** Systematic `data-testid` (`setting-*`, `composer-*`, `conversation-*`) and `window.FormalAi*` page APIs for E2E.\n13. **Security defaults.** A strict CSP on static pages, DOMPurify on rendered markdown, Mermaid with `securityLevel: strict`, and cache-busting asset versions.\n14. **Reasoning-trace presentation.** A hierarchical step view with fade gradient, last-paragraph preview and an animation budget; a candidate reusable \"process/trace\" component.\n15. **Terminology rule.** Say \"links network\", not \"graph\" (#664), so the framework's visualization components use consistent vocabulary.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Duplication candidates\n\n| Duplicate | Where | Recommendation |\n|---|---|---|\n| `h()` hyperscript, `segmentedControl`, locale and theme resolution | `js/site-chrome.js` lines 13–15 state they are \"intentionally re-implemented here verbatim\" from `js/download/download.js` (line 752) | Single framework primitive (`SegmentedControl`, `ThemeChooser`, `LocaleChooser`) shared by all pages |\n| Per-locale `LABELS` JS dicts | `site-chrome.js`, `download.js` | Move into lino-i18n catalogs |\n| Hand-rolled Links Notation parsing | `preferences.js` (parse/format), `memory.js` (bundle reader/writer) | Official `links-notation` parser plus `lino-objects-codec` |\n| Theme token values | `01-tokens.css`, `06-dark-theme.css` (1,097 lines of overrides), `landing.css`, download CSS | One token document → generated CSS vars for every page and theme |\n| Icon mapping tables | `toolbar-icons.jsx` (three parallel tables), emoji glyphs in `glyphs.jsx` | One icon registry in Links Notation (action → per-pack glyph) |\n| Chat UI per host | Web `/app/`, Electron wrapper, VS Code webview (#353 wants parity) | Framework chat components consumed by every host |\n| JS → TS mirror | `ts/` generated from `js/` | Generate bindings from one source (meta-language) instead of mirroring |\n| Theme applied to vanilla and Chakra separately | CSS classes vs Chakra components (#541, #550 bugs) | One component set; no mixed styling paths |\n| Similar components across other link-foundation/link-assistant UIs | Settings panels, theme/locale choosers, issue reporters, chat composers | Flag for the cross-org inventory (see sibling research files) |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Problems and limitations\n\n1. **Monolith.** `application.jsx` is 1,445 lines with one `App`. Its predecessor `main.jsx` reached 9,269 lines (#951); a CI line budget and boundary lint were needed to contain it.\n2. **Mixed paradigms.** Three styles coexist: React + Chakra (partial migration), plain CSS classes, and vanilla IIFE pages using `window.*` globals (`FormalAiI18n`, `FormalAiPreferences`, `FormalAiVendor`). There is no module graph across pages.\n3. **CSS order dependence.** The 7 stylesheets must load in numeric order. Dark mode is a large override sheet rather than token swaps, which produces recurring \"element not themed\" bugs (#388, #541, #550).\n4. **Version drift.** `i18n.js` reports `lino-i18n@0.3.0` while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n5. **Limited locales.** Only en, ru, zh and hi. There is no RTL support or pluralization evidence in the UI layer.\n6. **Accessibility is partial.**\n   - No automated a11y audit.\n   - Reduced motion is handled in a single stylesheet, even though animations (minimum message time, step reveal) are central.\n   - The sidebar has a mouse-scroll bug (#447).\n   - No documented contrast checks beyond a `contrast` skin.\n7. **Mobile fragility.** Repeated mobile bugs: iOS accessory bar, focus layout, overflow and menu width (#108, #110, #112).\n8. **Committed minified bundles** make diffs and reviews noisy (#953).\n9. **No platform-guideline mapping.** Skins are named after looks (glass, material) rather than formally following Apple HIG, Material 3 or Fluent. Material and glass are approximations.\n10. **No WYSIWYG configuration.** All configuration happens through the settings panel or chat commands; there is no visual editor or inspector.\n11. **No animation recording.** Animations are CSS/JS timing only; there is no capture or replay of UI sessions, even though the event log could support it.\n12. **Charts.** No chart components; diagrams rely on Mermaid only, and Mermaid rendering breaks on GitHub (#1190).\n13. **Asset licensing.** Icon packs are third-party fonts (FontAwesome, Material Symbols, Bootstrap Icons, Ionicons, Remix, Tabler), not public domain. A public-domain-only framework needs its own set or a `names` fallback.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes (formal-ai → associative UI framework)\n\n1. **Phase 0: contracts first.**\n   - Freeze the existing external contracts as compatibility tests: `formal-ai.preferences.v1` (root `demo_preferences`), `data-theme`, the `formal-ai:i18n-ready` event, `window.FormalAi*` hooks and all `data-testid` values.\n   - The framework's config loader should read the old preference document and map each key (`uiSkin`, `chatStyle`, `composerStyle`, `toolbarIconPack`, `glassOpacity`, `uiLanguage`, …) onto framework config links.\n2. **Phase 1: tokens.**\n   - Express `01-tokens.css` plus the dark overrides as one Links Notation token document with context-relative values (light/dark/contrast).\n   - Generate the CSS vars and the Chakra semantic-token bridge from it.\n   - Delete `06-dark-theme.css` incrementally, verified by per-theme screenshot diffs (#672 F1).\n3. **Phase 2: shared chrome.** Replace `site-chrome.js` and `download.js` helpers with framework `SegmentedControl`/`ThemeChooser`/`LocaleChooser` vanilla-JS bindings, and move the `LABELS` dicts into lino-i18n catalogs.\n4. **Phase 3: skins as framework themes.**\n   - Map `ui-skin-*`, `chat-style-*`, `composer-style-*` and `toolbar-icon-pack-*` to framework theme axes.\n   - Add guideline-conformant skins (Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG/glass) to satisfy #557.\n   - Keep the class names as aliases during the transition.\n5. **Phase 4: components.**\n   - Extract framework components in this order:\n     - `CollapsibleSection`\n     - `ToolbarButton` with priority overflow\n     - Settings rows with reset\n     - Composer\n     - Message\n     - Reasoning-trace view\n     - Issue reporter\n     - Links-network view\n   - Keep each `data-testid`.\n   - This also advances #951 (split monolith) and #550 (uniform components).\n6. **Phase 5: storage.**\n   - Back the framework's state store with the same append-only event-log shape as `memory.js`, so UI edits, memory and recordings share one exportable `.lino` bundle and `doublets-web` can be dropped in later.\n   - Replace hand-rolled parsers with `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec`.\n7. **Phase 6: hosts.** Electron and VS Code webviews consume the same framework package (#353 parity). React Native, Swift and Kotlin bindings reuse the token, i18n and config documents rather than the DOM components.\n8. **Risks.**\n   - Chakra coupling: the framework should own the tokens and treat Chakra as one optional binding.\n   - The generated `ts/` mirror must be regenerated, not hand-edited.\n   - The CI gates (i18n parity, UI boundary, line budgets) must keep passing throughout the migration.\n"

Gaps and open questions\n\n1. **Typed values.** The core tree has only strings, and `\"1\"` and `1` produce\n   the same reference. The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.\n\n   Recommendation: (b) for dimensions, durations and colours, with (a) as the\n   fallback for free-form props. Prefer structured links instead:\n   `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))` and `(aspect 16 9)`.\n4. **Comments and formatting are lost on round trip.** A WYSIWYG editor that\n   writes back to `.lino` will strip the user's comments and reflow the layout.\n   Options:\n   - (a) A CST mode upstream (trivia and spans, as meta-language already does\n     for CSS).\n   - (b) Make comments first-class links, for example `(note \"...\")`.\n   - (c) Patch-in-place edits using parser positions.\n\n   This needs an issue upstream in links-notation.\n5. **Ordering.** Link values are ordered, which is good for children and\n   keyframes. Property order, however, should be insignificant. The dialect\n   must state which parts are sequences (children, keyframes, transitions) and\n   which are sets (props). It must also define the meaning of a duplicate key:\n   last wins, as in lino-store logs.\n6. **Ids and scoping.** Ids are document-global strings, and nothing prevents\n   duplicates. Questions:\n   - Do we need namespaces (`login.save`) or nested id scopes per component?\n   - How do ids map to doublet numeric addresses, and are they stable across\n     edits? The editor needs stable ids for selection, undo and collaboration.\n7. **References for styles and tokens.** There is no built-in reference sigil.\n   A convention is needed:\n   - `@token.path` for design tokens\n   - `$param` for component parameters (the linksql / transformer convention)\n   - a bare id for elements and keyframe tracks\n\n   Open questions: resolution order (component, then theme, then base),\n   cycles, and fallbacks (`(or @color.accent \"#3390ec\")`).\n8. **Schemas and validation.** lino-schema is only a stub. Patterns worth adopting\n\n### 3.1 Architecture\n\n- **Pure model, thin view.** Display shaping (`message-parts.js`,\n  `message-text.js`, `chat-model.js`) has no DOM and no React, so it can be unit\n  tested. In `link-foundation/ui` the same split should become LiNo-in, LiNo-out\n  transforms that every target (React, React Native, Vue, SwiftUI, Compose)\n  reuses.\n- **Injected `api`.** Every screen takes its data source as a prop. This is the\n  seam the WYSIWYG editor needs to render components against fake data.\n- **Links as the data model.** Messages, plans, graphs and replies are already\n  links stored as LiNo. A LiNo UI description sitting next to LiNo data is the\n  natural next step.\n- **The `el()` style without JSX** makes the component tree a plain function of\n  data. That is easy to generate from a LiNo element tree and easy to emit from\n  a code generator.\n\n### 3.2 Theming and configurability\n\nThe model: modes × skins × tokens.\n\n- `appearance.js` sets `<html data-theme-mode>` (system, light, dark, or auto,\n  where auto means light 07:00-19:00), `data-theme` (the resolved mode) and\n  `data-skin`.\n- Skins are `t3` (default), `telegram`, `whatsapp` and `signal`, defined at\n  `app.css` around lines 3310-3400.\n- Choices are stored in localStorage (`metaSovereignTheme`, `metaSovereignSkin`).\n\nThere is a semantic token layer:\n\n- General: `--bg`, `--bg-elev`, `--bg-input`, `--bg-active`, `--border`,\n  `--text`, `--text-muted`, `--text-subtle`, `--accent`, `--accent-fill`,\n  `--accent-bg`, `--danger`, `--link`, `--shadow`.\n- Sizing: `--control-h: 2.25rem`, `--control-gap`, `--control-pad`,\n  `--radius: 8px`, `--topbar-h`, `--bottom-nav-h`,\n  `--safe-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.\n- Chat: `--chat-bg`, `--chat-sidebar`, `--chat-accent`, `--bubble-in` /\n  `-text` / `-pad`, `--bubble-out` / `-text`, `--bubble-radius` (Telegram 15px,\n  WhatsApp 7.5px, Signal 18px), `--bubble-tail`.\n\nThis is effectively the issue's \"themes that reproduce classical UIs\", in its\nfirst form. These token names are the seed vocabulary for the LiNo theme\nformat (see `links-notation-ecosystem.md` section 6.3).\n\nOther patterns in the same area:\n\n- **Accessible accents.** Filled accents are darkened to keep 4.5:1 contrast,\n  and shared filled-control tokens fixed white-on-white failures across badges,\n  tabs and Mini App buttons (`docs/DELIVERY-AUDIT.md`).\n- **Runtime themes from data.** `cloud-themes.js` maps a Telegram cloud\n  theme's colours (accent, outgoing bubble, light or dark) onto the CSS tokens.\n  In other words, theme application is already \"data in, token overrides out\".\n- **Scale through rem.** `ui-scale.js` sets the `<html>` font-size to 100-200 %\n  and a separate message text size. Everything is sized in rem, so one knob\n  scales the whole UI.\n- **Adaptive effects.** `effects.js` runs a bounded frame-time probe and sets\n  `<html data-effects=\"reduced\">` on slow GPUs. It also honours\n  `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-reduced-transparency` and\n  `prefers-color-scheme`.\n- **Wallpapers as data.** `{ kind: 'none' | 'telegram' | 'file' }` is turned\n  into `--wp-*` variables by a pure function.\n\n### 3.3 Performance\n\n- The chat list uses a **measured virtual list** with binary-search offsets\n  and one screen of overscan, plus `content-visibility: auto` and\n  `contain-intrinsic-size`.\n- **Paged history**, store first and network second:\n  - pages are read from the local store before the network (Telegram)\n  - a priority prefetch queue (`PAGE_SIZE 50`, `PREFETCH_SIZE 30`,\n    `PREFETCH_QUEUE 40`, `STALL_MS 5000`, `HOLD_MS 30000`)\n  - unread chats are prefetched\n  - when jumping far back, a `ceiling` keeps newer messages from showing above\n    a gap\n- **Avatars.**\n  - Read-ahead covers one viewport, with at most two uncached loads at once.\n  - The URL cache is limited to 512 entries.\n  - Initials are the fallback, so there are no spinner storms\n    (`docs/UI-STATES.md`).\n- **Optimistic sends.** The pending bubble and directory preview update at\n  once, and an outbox with a stable `clientId` handles retries.\n- The **geometry-only layout trace** (`chat-layout-trace.js`) records\n  diagnostics without logging message text.\n\n### 3.4 Interaction rules worth codifying\n\nThese come from `docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md`:\n\n- Local and immediate interactions.\n- A context-menu target is distinct from a multi-selection.\n- Jumps load the history around the target and briefly highlight it.\n- A missing provider capability is never shown as success.\n- Keyboard parity: a skip link, visible focus, shortcuts that never steal plain\n  keys from fields, and focus traps in dialogs.\n\nThese rules belong in the framework's component contracts and tests, not only\nin one app.\n\n## 4. Duplication candidates (what `link-foundation/ui` should own)\n\n| Candidate | Today in meta-sovereign | Proposed generic component / module |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Design tokens and skins | Hard-coded in `app.css` (`:root[data-skin=...]`) plus `appearance.js` | `theme` links in LiNo, compiled to CSS variables and native themes. Skins become data files: `t3.lino`, `telegram.lino`, `whatsapp.lino`, `signal.lino` |\n| Virtual list | `chat-list-window.js`, part of `chat-window.js` | `VirtualList` (measured, bidirectional, anchor-preserving) |\n| Paged bidirectional history | `chat-window.js`, `chat-jump.js`, `chat-follow.js` | `Timeline` / `MessageStream` with `loadOlder`, `loadNewer`, `jumpTo`, ceiling, stick-to-bottom |\n| Message bubble family | `chat-message.js`, `chat-media.js` | `Bubble`, `ReplyQuote`, `ReactionBar`, `MediaTile`, `ServiceLine`, `DeliveryTicks` |\n| Composer | `chat-view.js`, `chat-composer-*.js`, `chat-attach.js`, `chat-voice.js`, `chat-emoji.js` | `Composer` with slots (attach, emoji, voice) and an auto-grow `TextArea` with a reserved-space contract |\n| Rich text | `message-text.js`, `rich-text-nodes.js` | `RichText` driven by an entity list (offsets are UTF-16 code units) |\n| Context menu and selection | `chat-selection.js`, `chat-drag.js`, `menuPlace()` | `ContextMenu` (placement maths), `SelectionModel` (range and drag) |\n| Date separators and calendar | `chat-days.js` | `DaySeparator`, `StickyDate`, `CalendarPicker` |\n| Resizable panes | `panel-resize.js` | `Split` / `ResizeHandle` with keyboard control and persistence (the `split` element in the LiNo sketch) |\n| Responsive shell | `shell/app-shell.js` | `AppShell` with Material 3 breakpoints (bottom bar, rail, drawer) |\n| Scale and effects | `ui-scale.js`, `effects.js` | Framework-level `Settings` for scale, motion and transparency |\n| Icons | `icons.js` (Lucide shapes, ISC) | Icon registry addressed by name. Use a public-domain set, as the issue asks: Lucide is ISC, not public domain |\n| i18n | `i18n.js` plus JSON locales | Replace with lino-i18n (`.lino` catalogues, React adapter) |\n| Settings persistence | localStorage keys per feature | One LiNo settings document resolved through lino-arguments (defaults, file, user) |\n\n## 5. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 5.1 From the issue tracker\n\n<https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues>: 25 issues, 1 open,\nand 30 PRs. The UI-related issues and their state:\n\n- [#25](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/25) asked for:\n  - mobile-first design\n  - full translation\n  - a dedicated connections page\n  - a tutorial based on real UI elements\n  - Apple-glass translucency\n  - **Chakra UI + React**\n\n  It was closed by PR #26 (mobile-first shell, Connections, tutorial spotlight),\n  but Chakra UI was not adopted. The UI stayed hand-written CSS.\n- [#27](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/27): \"simplify\n  the UI, and reduce repeating ourselves (DRY in code and UI/UX)\". The author\n  writes that the earlier vision was \"partially ignored\". This is direct\n  evidence of the duplication problem that a shared component framework should\n  solve.\n- [#10](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/10) (hide\n  empty sections) and [#13](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/13)\n  (tutorial progress lost after refresh, fixed in PR #14) are UI-state\n  persistence bugs.\n- [#18](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/18): i18n was\n  added later rather than designed in. Strings were retrofitted.\n- [#42](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/42) (open)\n  is about provider coverage, not UI.\n\n### 5.2 Observed in the code and docs\n\n1. **CSS monolith.** `app.css` has 13.8k lines and 200 `!important`, plus\n   overrides that depend on order. Some skin rules sit thousands of lines away\n   from their definitions, for example\n   `:root[data-theme='dark'][data-skin='t3']` at around line 13,589 versus the\n   skin block at around line 3,317. There is no scoping (no CSS modules or\n   layers), and the tokens are not machine-readable outside CSS.\n2. **Skins are code, not data.** A new classical theme requires CSS edits in\n   several places. Users cannot share or edit skins as files. Preferences live\n   in scattered localStorage keys, not in LiNo, which contradicts the project's\n   own \"everything is links\" model.\n3. **Bundle size.** `app.min.js` is 4.6 MB, committed, and served whole. There\n   is no route-level code splitting, even though KaTeX, lottie-web and the\n   emoji and sticker panels are heavy and rarely used.\n4. **Platform reach.** Mobile is a Capacitor WebView around the same bundle:\n   - no native components\n   - no React Native, Swift or Kotlin UI, all of which the issue asks for\n\n   Desktop is Electron 45. Both inherit the web bundle's size and performance.\n5. **Fragile layout areas.** These need dedicated fixes and regressions, which\n   shows how hard they are to get right:\n   - floating composer clearance and overlap at the live tail\n   - typing / header overlap (`docs/DELIVERY-2026-10-31.md`)\n   - WebKit `ResizeObserver` loops (`chat-composer-height.js`)\n   - white-on-white selection controls (`docs/DELIVERY-AUDIT.md`)\n6. **Tight coupling to Telegram semantics.** Bubble, media and selection\n   components encode Telegram concepts directly (`msg:telegram:*`, entities,\n   topics, `.tgs`). Other providers get Telegram's shape. A framework needs\n   provider-neutral component contracts, with capabilities passed as data.\n7. **Licensing.**\n   - Behaviour is \"learned, never copied\" from GPL/AGPL clients (tweb,\n     telegram-tt, tdesktop, Signal, Element).\n   - Icons are Lucide (ISC).\n   - Neither is public domain. The framework must source public-domain assets\n     separately, as the issue requires.\n8. **Server limits.** The Rust server crates are `publish = false`, with server\n   state in memory. The npm package is not published, so other projects cannot\n   reuse any component today.\n9. **No visual editor.** Appearance is changed only through settings panels.\n   There is no inspector, no live token editing and no dev/config overlay.\n   These are features the issue explicitly wants (WYSIWYG, dev/config mode).\n\n## 6. Migration notes (meta-sovereign onto `link-foundation/ui`)\n\n1. **Tokens first, with zero visual change.**\n   - Extract the 60 root custom properties and the four skin blocks from\n     `app.css` into `themes/*.lino` (token names unchanged).\n   - Generate a CSS file of `:root[data-skin=...][data-theme=...]` variables\n     from them.\n   - meta-sovereign keeps its existing selectors. Only the source of truth\n     moves.\n\n   Validate with the existing Playwright pixel and contrast checks.\n2. **Settings as LiNo.**\n   - Replace the localStorage keys (`metaSovereignTheme`, `metaSovereignSkin`,\n     scale, effects, locale) with one settings link, resolved with\n     lino-arguments and stored in the existing lino store.\n   - Keep localStorage as a cache.\n3. **Leaf components next.** Extract the pure modules first, because they have\n   no DOM coupling and already have unit tests:\n   - `message-text.js` becomes `RichText`\n   - `message-parts.js` becomes a media model\n   - `chat-model.js` provides date grouping and delivery status\n   - `wallpaper-css.js`\n\n   Then extract `panel-resize.js` (`Split`), `chat-list-window.js`\n   (`VirtualList`) and `menuPlace` (`ContextMenu`).\n4. **Bubble and composer behind a provider-neutral contract.**\n   - Define `Bubble` / `Composer` props in a LiNo schema (capabilities such as\n     `can-edit`, `can-react` and `max-attachments` as data).\n   - Adapt the Telegram specifics in meta-sovereign, not in the framework.\n5. **i18n swap.** Convert `js/src/web/locales/*` to lino-i18n catalogues with\n   its CLI. Keep the `t()` signature through the lino-i18n React adapter.\n6. **Screens declared in LiNo.**\n   - Describe the shell and chat layout (`split`, `list`, `stack`) as LiNo,\n     rendered by the framework's React target.\n   - Keep the hand-written behaviour hooks (`useChatState`, `chat-window.js`)\n     as named behaviours that the LiNo document references, for example\n     `(behavior chat-window)`.\n7. **Constraints to preserve.**\n   - no JSX requirement (the `el()` style is fine for generated code)\n   - CSP-friendly: no `eval`, which lottie-web light already respects\n   - axe-core gating\n   - Chromium and WebKit e2e\n   - reduced-motion / transparency / effects switches\n   - rem-based scaling\n   - offline-first, immediate interactions\n8. **Risks.**\n   - 13.8k lines of CSS with order-dependent overrides. Migrate per area and\n     diff screenshots.\n   - Behaviour hidden in CSS (`content-visibility`, composer reserve) must\n     become explicit component props.\n   - The 215 chat modules change often (1.2.0 was released recently), so\n     extraction should happen upstream-first with thin re-exports to avoid\n     long-lived forks.\n"

The sections cite the grammar file (`docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md`) and protocol docs.\n- **Two syntax traps for UI:**\n  - A `#` after whitespace starts a comment, so hex colours must be quoted.\n  - `:` is not allowed in a bare value, so URLs, `:hover` and `16:9` must be quoted or written as structured links.\n- **Implementations:** JS, Rust, C#, Python, Go and C++ are all at 0.27.1 and kept in step by a shared test corpus. The front\n  matter carries the key, title, issue type, labels, phase, the keys of the\n  blocking issues and the requirement IDs.\n- [`issue-footer.md`](issue-footer.md) is appended to every issue body. It holds\n  the conventions every implementer (human or AI agent) must follow.\n- [`created-issues.json`](created-issues.json) maps each key to the GitHub\n  issue number and ID.
