This is the \"blueprint\" visual language that\n75\t  konard.github.io later adopted for its network glyphs.\n76\t- **Stack.**\n77\t  - Plain HTML pages plus ES modules in `js/`.\n78\t  - **D3 v7 is loaded at runtime** through `https://esm.sh/use-m`, as `use('d3')`.\n79\t  - SVG rendering with an optional Canvas mode.\n80\t  - A Bun `serve.ts` dev server.\n81\t  - Unit tests with `node --test`; e2e tests with Playwright / browser-commander.\n82\t- **License.** Unlicense ([L:LICENSE](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/LICENSE)), so it\n83\t  can be adopted directly. The repo is about 5.5 MB.\n84\t- **Key paths.**\n85\t  - Pages:\n86\t    - [L:index.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/index.html): one draggable link\n87\t    - [L:blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/blueprint.html): a 9-point spline blueprint\n88\t    - [L:animated-blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/animated-blueprint.html): IK bending and looping\n89\t    - [L:grid.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/grid.html): 1–64 links on an infinite grid\n90\t    - [L:draw.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/draw.html): freehand strokes become links\n91\t    - `H-fractal.html`, `fabrik.html`, `fabrik-horizontal.html`, `distance-constrained-blueprint.html`, `tests.html`\n92\t  - Modules in [L:js/](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/tree/main/js):\n93\t    - `zoom-pan.mjs`, `grid.mjs`, `markers.mjs`, `blueprint-link.mjs`, `draw-link.mjs`, `ik-pure.mjs`,\n94\t      `ik.mjs`, `path.mjs`, `geometry.mjs`, `control-points.mjs`\n95\t    - `state.mjs`, `render-mode.mjs`, `canvas-render.mjs`, `hud.mjs`, `panels.mjs`, `sliders.mjs`,\n96\t      `animation.mjs`, `resize.mjs`, `svg-setup.mjs`, `constants.mjs`\n97\t  - History of earlier attempts: [L:docs/links-visuals-history.md](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/docs/links-visuals-history.md)\n98\t  - `failed-attempts/`: 76 HTML snapshots\n99\t  - Case studies: `docs/case-studies/issue-{15,21,27,28}`\n100\t  - 13 issues, all closed\n101\t\n102\t---\n103\t\n104\t## 2. Configurability model (konard.github.io)\n105\t\n106\tThis is the most mature part of the two repos and the strongest candidate for the core of link-foundation/ui.\n107\t\n108\t1. **The schema is a list of sections of flat fields.**\n109\t   - Defined in [K:src/settings/schema.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/schema.js).\n110\t   - A section is `{id, column, title:{en,ru}, lead, fields, when(settings), tabs}`.\n111\t   - A field is created by a factory in [K:src/settings/fields.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/fields.js):\n112\t     - `range(key, d, min, max, step, label, extra)`\n113\t     - `toggle(...)`\n114\t     - `select(key, d, options, label)` with `option(value, en, ru)`\n115\t     - `color(...)`\n116\t   - Keys are dotted paths such as `liquid.blur`, `skin.name`, `ui.cornerTL`. They are already link-like\n117\t     (`section.key`) and would map one-to-one onto Links Notation doublets.\n118\t   - The sections are:\n119\t     - motion, nebula, stars, grid, beams, rain, sound\n120\t     - skins: glass, liquid, futuristic, materials, palettes, corners\n121\t     - ui: control sizes, borders, per-corner radii (−1 means \"follow the skin\"), menu size, slider track\n122\t     - theory: `theory.notation` chooses L→L² or R→R²\n123\t   - Split files: `schema.ui.js`, `schema.skins.js`, `schema.background.js`, `schema.layers.js`,\n124\t     `schema.materials.js`, `schema.sound.js`.\n125\t   - There are about 114 factory call sites; loops generate hundreds of fields, many of them script-only\n126\t     (`css:false`).\n127\t2. **One rule table.**\n128\t   - `RULES` maps each key to `{d, min, max, u, o, c}`: default, limits, unit, options, colour flag.\n129\t   - `CSS_RULES` is the subset that is projected into CSS.\n130\t   - `DEFAULTS` and `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS` are exported.\n131\t   - [K:src/settings/schema.defaults.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/schema.defaults.js)\n132\t     holds `DEFAULT_LOOK`, the JSON the owner pasted in issue #45 (\"That is defaults.\").\n133\t3. **Normalization and migration.**\n134\t   - Lives in [K:src/settings/apply.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/apply.js).\n135\t   - `normalize(rules, stored)` clamps numbers, drops unknown options and validates `#rrggbb` colours.\n136\t   - It also migrates old values, for example `future.surface: 'transparent'` becomes a solid surface with\n137\t     opacity 0.\n138\t4. **Projection into the DOM, without the framework.** `applySettings(root, rules, settings)` writes:\n139\t   - numbers and colours as CSS variables on `<html>` (`liquid.blur` becomes `--liquid-blur: 18px`)\n140\t   - selects and toggles as `data-*` attributes (`skin.name` becomes `data-skin-name=\"glass\"`)\n141\t   - derived values: corner-radius fallbacks, `--ui-accent-rgb`, an SVG `feTurbulence` noise data-URI, and\n142\t     `data-surface-invisible`\n143\t\n144\t   All styling is then plain CSS that keys off these variables and attributes.\n145\t\n146\t5. **Before-paint script.**\n147\t   - `normalize` and `applySettings` are serialized with `Function.toString` into `SETTINGS_SCRIPT`.\n148\t   - The `themeBeforePaint` Vite plugin prepends it into `<head>` together with `THEME_SCRIPT`\n149\t     ([K:vite.config.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/vite.config.js)).\n150\t   - This avoids a flash of the wrong theme or skin, and it is the same code as at runtime, not a copy.\n151\t6. **Store.**\n152\t   - [K:src/settings/store.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/store.js)\n153\t     is built on `useSyncExternalStore`. It has no context provider.\n154\t   - **Only the diff from defaults** is stored, in localStorage `settings`. Users who never touched a key\n155\t     therefore get improved defaults automatically.\n156\t   - Other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.\n157\t   - API: `setSettings(patch)`, `resetSettings(keys)`, `changesOf`.\n158\t7. **Looks (presets).** Defined in [K:src/settings/presets.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/presets.js).\n159\t   - Built-in presets: Matrix universe (default), glass-universe, calm, matrix, deep-space, warp,\n160\t     neon (Tron), liquid, blueprint, and \"Light and fast\" for slow phones.\n161\t   - `before45()` rebases old presets onto `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS`.\n162\t   - `COMFORT` lists keys that presets, shared links and Random never change:\n163\t     `motion.mode`, `sound.on`, `sound.volume`, `theory.notation`, `ui.transparency`. These are\n164\t     accessibility and preference keys; the idea comes from immortality's `src/settings.ts`.\n165\t   - `randomLook()` never goes above the default cost on any heavy key (counts, fps, blur, glow).\n166\t   - Saved looks are stored as `[{name, look}]` under `settings-presets`, with add, remove, import and rename.\n167\t   - Sharing: `#settings=<urlencoded JSON>` (`shareLink`, `lookOfHash`). When a shared link is opened,\n168\t     `openSharedLook()` applies it, saves the previous look as a \"Before the link\" preset, and strips the hash.\n169\t8. **Preferences outside the schema.** [K:src/i18n/prefs.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/i18n/prefs.js)\n170\t   - Language is resolved as `?lang`, then the stored value, then `navigator`, then `en`.\n171\t   - Theme is auto/light/dark.\n172\t   - Each is a tiny external store.\n173\t   - All UI text is written inline as `{en, ru}` objects, and `plural.js` handles Russian plural forms.\n174\t9. **The network editor's local style model.** [K:src/links/style.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/style.js)\n175\t   - `STYLE_SECTIONS` reuses the same field factories.\n176\t   - `normalizeStyle` validates; `styleToParams` and `styleFromParams` put **only non-default values in the\n177\t     query string**.\n178\t   - There are six link palettes: site, neon, pastel, warm, cold, print.\n179\t   - The network uses the same configuration grammar as the site settings, but it is scoped to a document\n180\t     (the URL) instead of the user (localStorage).\n181\t10. **Settings page as live designer.** [K:src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx)\n182\t    - The page is generated from the schema. Each row is `label | control | value | ↺ reset`, and changed\n183\t      rows get an `is-changed` class.\n184\t    - Layer tabs show a dot when that layer is active.\n185\t    - There is a Reset button per section plus \"Reset everything\".\n186\t    - \"Look at the background\" is a peek mode that hides the panels.\n187\t    - The \"Your changes\" box shows the diff JSON with Copy, and has a paste area that loads either settings\n188\t      or `{presets:[...]}`.\n189\t    - Sounds have ▶ preview buttons.\n190\t    - The page itself is the preview: it includes `InterfacePreview`, `UiSamples` (small samples of every UI\n191\t      element, from #45), `MaterialPresets` and `CornerTiles`.\n192\t    - Columns are explicit because CSS multicol was buggy in Safari.\n193\t    - This is the closest existing thing to the \"VS-designer configuration mode\" the issue asks for, though\n194\t      it edits global tokens, not per-element instances.\n195\t11. **Testing every setting.** Issue #15 asked for proof that every setting is applied.\n196\t    [K:src/settings/applied.test.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/applied.test.js)\n197\t    goes through every field in `FIELDS` and fails if a setting is used in none of three ways: as a CSS\n198\t    variable or `<html>` attribute that a stylesheet reads, as an option a background script reads, or as a\n199\t    key a component reads.\n200\t12. **Skins and frames.**\n201\t    - [K:src/skins.frames.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/skins.frames.js)\n202\t      defines corner shapes and corner lines once:\n203\t      - shapes: square, cut, tall, wide, round, scoop, notch\n204\t      - lines: none, gap, line, accent, bracket\n205\t    - `npm run build:frames` generates `skins.frames.css` from it, and the same definitions draw the\n206\t      `CornerTiles` previews. A test keeps the generated CSS in sync.\n207\t    - The CSS uses `@property` typed lengths and `:where()` to keep specificity at zero.\n208\t    - `schema.skins.js` has 12 palettes (from immortality) and the skins `glass`, `liquid`, `futuristic`.\n209\t    - Owner requirements from issues:\n210\t      - #39: a single transparency setting for all backgrounds; matte, glossy and liquid glass presets; no\n211\t        rounded corners in the futuristic look by default; rounded corners following t3code practice\n212\t      - #45: one per-side border configuration shared by panels, blocks, buttons and other elements; top\n213\t        highlight width set separately from corner/side widths; the corner layer above or below content;\n214\t        colours picked from palettes\n215\t\n216\t---\n217\t\n218\t## 3. Visualizations\n219\t\n220\t### 3.1 Single link (links-visuals)\n221\t\n222\t| Page                                                                                                                         | What it shows                                                                                                     | Tech / notes                                                                                                                             |\n223\t| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n224\t| [index.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/index.html)                                                   | A diagonal line with a cross (source) and an arrow (target), draggable endpoints, fullscreen, a coordinates panel | D3 + SVG markers                                                                                                                         |\n225\t| [H-fractal.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/H-fractal.html)                                           | Recursive H subdivision with straight arrows                                                                      | Recursion demo                                                                                                                           |\n226\t| [blueprint.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/blueprint.html)                                           | A configurable link spline with 9 control points (start, p1–p3, center, p4–p6, end) on a grid                     | `path.mjs` converts Catmull-Rom to cubic. |\n231\t\n232\tMarkers ([L:js/markers.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/markers.mjs)):\n233\t\n234\t- The cross and arrow use `viewBox 0 0 100 100` and `markerUnits=\"strokeWidth\"`, so they scale with the line.\n235\t- Their proportions use the golden ratio.\n236\t- They are hardcoded black.\n237\t\n238\t### 3.2 Networks (links-visuals)\n239\t\n240\t- [grid.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/grid.html)\n241\t  - 1–64 coloured links placed on grid cells, with a link-count slider, Reset and snapping.\n242\t  - Proportions are shared with single-link mode through `blueprint-link.mjs` (fixed in #23 and #28).\n243\t- [draw.html](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/draw.html)\n244\t  - Freehand input through Pointer Events: Apple Pencil, touch and mouse, with `touch-action:none`.\n245\t  - A stroke is simplified into a link whose center is the 50% arc-length point.\n246\t  - An endpoint dropped near another link's center snaps and pins to it. Pins are re-resolved at render time\n247\t    by `applyCenterAnchors`, so links follow when their target moves.\n248\t  - Select and Draw modes; links persist in localStorage (#27).\n249\t- Infinite grid ([L:js/grid.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/grid.mjs)): SVG\n250\t  `pattern` tiles of minor and major lines over a 1e6-sized rect (#15).\n251\t- Zoom and pan ([L:js/zoom-pan.mjs](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/js/zoom-pan.mjs))\n252\t  - The wheel zooms about the pointer with factor `0.999^delta`, scale 0.1–20.\n253\t  - Listeners sit on `document`, which fixed the \"zoom does not work far from the center\" bugs (#19, #21).\n254\t  - `?debug=zoom` turns on a debug overlay.\n255\t- [L:docs/links-visuals-history.md](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/blob/main/docs/links-visuals-history.md)\n256\t  surveys earlier attempts:\n257\t  - LinksPlatform web UI prototypes; doublet and triplet circle symbols\n258\t  - Cytoscape issue #1217 (edges to edges), declined, and its compound-node workarounds\n259\t  - GoJS label nodes; dmx cytoscape-edge-connections\n260\t  - Deep.Case Cytoscape (link node plus from/to edges) and A-Frame 3D\n261\t  - DeepVisual (Python); doublets-web SVG; react-deep-tree\n262\t\n263\t  It ends with the open goal: _\"stable identity, arbitrary source/target references, self-reference and\n264\t  cycles, understandable recursive structure, and layout that stays readable as links move.\"_\n265\t\n266\t### 3.3 Networks as symbols (konard.github.io)\n267\t\n268\t- **Encoding.** [K:src/links/configurations.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/configurations.js)\n269\t  - A doublet network of N links (plus the 0 link meaning \"nothing\") is written as 2N digits in base N+1,\n270\t    for example `01 20`. With more than 9 links it is written as `s,t;s,t`.\n271\t  - Functions: `decode`, `encode`, `codeAt`, `indexOf` (BigInt), `randomCode`, `mathNotation` (subscripts),\n272\t    `linksNotation` (gives `(1: 0 1)`).\n273\t  - Classes up to relabelling are counted with Burnside's lemma (`classCount`, `representatives`), and there\n274\t    is a \"real references only\" mode.\n275\t- **Five editable notations that stay in sync.** These are in `Notations` in\n276\t  [K:src/pages/NetworkEditor.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/NetworkEditor.jsx):\n277\t  - theory notation, e.g. `λ = {1 ↦ (0, 1)}`, in L→L² or R→R² form ([K:src/links/notation.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/notation.js))\n278\t  - pairs\n279\t  - the N-ary number, e.g. `0120₃`\n280\t  - its decimal index\n281\t  - Links Notation\n282\t\n283\t  The parsers are in [K:src/links/edit.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/edit.js)\n284\t  and return bilingual errors. While the user types, the text stays as typed and the other notations follow.\n285\t\n286\t- **Glyph.** [K:src/links/glyph.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/glyph.js)\n287\t  - Each link is one cubic-Bézier curve: a bar at the source, a middle, and an arrow at the target. This is\n288\t    the links-visuals blueprint.\n289\t  - Other links refer to a link by touching its middle.\n290\t  - A reference to 0 is a free end; a self-reference is a loop, so `(1: 1 1)` renders as ∞.\n291\t  - Constants: `SIZE=100`, `STROKE=2.4`, a 9-colour palette.\n292\t  - Markers: bar, arrow, triangle, tail, dot, circle, square, diamond, none.\n293\t  - `SHAPE` options: placement, order, frame, forces, rotation, spread, padding, bendMode, and more.\n294\t- **Placement.** [K:src/links/placement.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/placement.js)\n295\t  offers circle, square grid, hex, dice, playing card, spiral, and d3-force.\n296\t- **Overlap reduction.**\n297\t  - `collisions.js`, `collision-gaps.js` and `collision-symmetry.js` add spacing automatically.\n298\t  - The work runs in a cancellable Web Worker (`collision-worker.js`, `solver-job.js`).\n299\t  - [K:src/pages/useCollisionSolver.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/useCollisionSolver.js)\n300\t    keys each result so a stale one never replaces a newer drawing.\n301\t- **Render and export.**\n302\t  - [K:src/links/render.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/render.js):\n303\t    `networkSvg` builds one standalone SVG string. It is used for the on-screen preview _and_ every export.\n304\t    XML is escaped and values are normalized. It supports solid, linear and radial backgrounds, a card, and\n305\t    captions in the chosen notation.\n306\t  - [K:src/links/export.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/export.js)\n307\t    exports:\n308\t    - SVG, plus PNG, JPEG and WebP by rasterizing on a canvas\n309\t    - a `.lino` file (Links Notation)\n310\t    - clipboard copies of text and images\n311\t    - the Web Share API and social share URLs\n312\t- **Editor page.** [K:src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/NetworkPage.jsx)\n313\t  - URL: `/network/?code=…&<non-default style params>`, with `DEFAULT_CODE='11 22 12'`.\n314\t  - Sections: Notations, Links (a table plus per-link cards for colour, turns and gaps), Style, Share.\n315\t  - `useNetworkHistory.js` keeps debounced URL history and pauses it while a slider is being dragged.\n316\t    `localStorage network.debug` enables debugging.\n317\t  - The gallery is at `/art/#symbols` (`NetworkGallery.jsx`).\n318\t- **Other data visuals.** These are hand-built SVG/React components:\n319\t  - `ContributionCalendar`, `ContributionsChart`, `LanguagesChart`, `LanguageCloud`, `StatTiles`, `Timeline`\n320\t  - `EcosystemMap` (an orbit diagram), `ProblemSolvingDiagram`, `MetaTheory`, `Cosmos`, `LiquidRefraction`\n321\t- **Animated backgrounds.** [K:src/visuals/](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/main/src/visuals)\n322\t  - Layered canvases: nebula, stars, beams, and rain (a \"digital rain\" of link glyphs).\n323\t  - [K:src/visuals/governor.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/visuals/governor.js)\n324\t    is an FPS governor. It lowers resolution first and then fps, and never raises them again\n325\t    (`SLOW_GAP` 45 ms, `MIN_SCALE` 0.4).\n326\t\n327\t---\n328\t\n329\t## 4. geometry expressed as fractions of `gridSpacing` |\n365\t\n366\t---\n367\t\n368\t## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n369\t\n370\t1. **One rule table per key**: `{default, min, max, unit, options, isColor}`. It drives normalization,\n371\t   validation, the generated UI, CSS projection and tests. It translates naturally into a Links Notation\n372\t   schema, e.g. `(liquid.blur: range 18 0 40 px)`.\n373\t2. **Store the diff from defaults, never the full state.** Defaults can then improve for everyone, and saved\n374\t   looks and share links stay small.\n375\t3. **Project settings into CSS variables and `data-*` attributes on the root.** Theming then works without\n376\t   any framework, and the same tokens can be emitted for SwiftUI and Compose as constant tables.\n377\t4. **Run the same `normalize` and `apply` before first paint**, serialized from the real functions rather\n378\t   than copied. There is no theme flash and no second implementation.\n379\t5. **Comfort keys.** Accessibility and preference keys (reduced motion, sound, volume, transparency,\n380\t   notation) are excluded from presets, shared links and randomization.\n381\t6. **Looks as data.** Built-in presets, saved presets, import/export JSON, `#settings=` share links, and an\n382\t   automatic \"Before the link\" backup when a shared look is applied.\n383\t7. **Bounded randomization.** `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on heavy keys, so Random is safe\n384\t   on slow devices. There is also an explicit \"Light and fast\" preset.\n385\t8. **The settings page is the live preview.** Each row has a per-field ↺ reset and changed rows are marked.\n386\t   There are section resets, a peek mode, a diff box with copy and paste, and sample tiles of every UI\n387\t   element. Extending this to per-element editing gives the WYSIWYG configuration mode.\n388\t9. **One source generates both CSS and preview tiles** (`skins.frames.js`), and a test fails if the\n389\t   generated CSS is out of date.\n390\t10. **One renderer for preview and export.** A single SVG string (`networkSvg`) is reused for PNG, JPEG and\n391\t    WebP export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen. The same idea fits animation recording: record\n392\t    the frames of the model, not screenshots.\n393\t11. **URL state holds only non-default parameters** (`styleToParams`), with debounced history that pauses\n394\t    while a slider is dragged.\n395\t12. **Several synchronized notations of one model**, with typed-text preservation and bilingual errors. This\n396\t    shows the framework's \"DOM-like language and Links Notation as two views of one tree\" in miniature.\n397\t13. **Expensive layout in a cancellable worker**, with keyed results that cannot overwrite newer state\n398\t    (`solver-job.js`, `useCollisionSolver.js`).\n399\t14. **Performance governors.** The FPS governor degrades resolution and then fps, and `panelVisibility.js`\n400\t    limits live `backdrop-filter` surfaces. Both belong in the framework runtime.\n401\t15. **Owned, ARIA-compliant controls.** Select follows the APG patterns, numeric keys are shared, and popups\n402\t    are portaled and clamped to the viewport. #39 says \"all UI elements must be owned by us\".\n403\t16. **Declarative sound.** A `data-sound` attribute on any element plus document-level role mapping, so\n404\t    components do not hard-code audio.\n405\t17. **Language and theme stores built on `useSyncExternalStore`, with no provider.** This ports cleanly to\n406\t    signals or observables in Vue, Swift and Kotlin.\n407\t18. **Pointer-centred zoom with document-level listeners** and an infinite pattern grid (links-visuals #15,\n408\t    #19, #21). These are designer-canvas basics.\n409\t19. **Arc-length center anchors for links that point at links.** An anchor is pinned and re-resolved at\n410\t    render time (`applyCenterAnchors`), which is the core of drawing associative links, not just node graphs.\n411\t20. **Pure geometry and IK separated from rendering** (`ik-pure.mjs`), so they can be unit-tested and ported\n412\t    to Swift and Kotlin.\n413\t21. **A test suite per issue** (`*-NN.test.js`, `experiments/issue-N-browser.mjs` on three browser engines),\n414\t    a case study per issue, and a hard 1500-line file limit.\n415\t\n416\t---\n417\t\n418\t## 6. |\n436\t\n437\t---\n438\t\n439\t## 7. Problems, bugs and limitations observed\n440\t\n441\t### konard.github.io\n442\t\n443\t1. **No license.** The code cannot legally be copied into a public-domain framework until it is relicensed\n444\t   (for example to Unlicense, like links-visuals and immortality).\n445\t2. **Links Notation is hand-parsed.** `parseLinks` in `edit.js` uses the regex\n446\t   `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g`, and `links-notation` is not imported anywhere in `src/`.\n447\t   It only accepts numeric doublets and does not handle nesting, names or multi-line input.\n448\t3. **Settings are JSON, not Links Notation.** This applies to localStorage, the `#settings=` hash, the\n449\t   diff box, and import/export. It contradicts the framework goal of representing everything in Links\n450\t   Notation.\n451\t4. **Bilingual text is hard-coded** as `{en, ru}` objects inside components, including long templated\n452\t   sentences in `NetworkEditor.jsx`. Adding a language means editing every component; there is no catalog.\n453\t5. **Configuration is global only.** The tokens style every element of a kind. There is no per-instance\n454\t   override and no element tree to select from, so it is not yet a WYSIWYG designer.\n455\t6. **React-bound.** The store, pages and controls are React components; only `apply.js` and `src/links/*`\n456\t   are framework-free.\n457\t7. **Open issue #47.** The top-left corner and the top and bottom edges are not transparent by default,\n458\t   although every other element is. These are still border/corner layering bugs from the #45 redesign.\n459\t8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n460\t   - #13: the rain sometimes scaled up too much on refresh.\n461\t   - #45: some border configurations clipped overflowing content or broke transparent backgrounds and\n462\t     selection.\n463\t   - CSS multicol was unreliable in Safari, so columns are explicit.\n464\t   - Safari needed a focus fix in `numericKeys.js`.\n465\t9. **Heavy generated CSS.** `skins.frames.css` is about 84 KB / 1067 lines, and a very large number of\n466\t   fields (hundreds) costs payload and maintenance.\n467\t10. **Repo weight.** About 372 MB, from case studies, logs and archives committed to the repo, so it is\n468\t    slow to clone. Sparse clones are needed.\n469\t11. **Migrations are ad hoc** (`before45()`, special cases in `normalize`). There is no versioned schema\n470\t    migration mechanism.\n471\t\n472\t### links-visuals\n473\t\n474\t1. **CDN at runtime.** D3 is fetched from `esm.sh/use-m` on every load. It does not work offline, it is\n475\t   unpinned and therefore a supply-chain risk, and it is not reproducible.\n476\t2. **Global mutable state** in `state.mjs` (module singletons with setters). Two views cannot share a page.\n477\t3. **Duplicated renderers.** `canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG markers and paths by hand, and the\n478\t   two can drift apart.\n479\t4. **A rAF loop runs every frame even when idle** (`animation.mjs`), which wastes battery.\n480\t5. **Inline CSS is copied into every HTML page**, with no theming. Markers are hardcoded black, and only\n481\t   grid.html and draw.html have colour.\n482\t6. **Experiments are not composable.** Each page wires modules differently, and `failed-attempts/` holds 76\n483\t   HTML snapshots instead of git history.\n484\t7. **Limits of the network model.** grid.html places links in cells without real references. Only draw.html\n485\t   has link-to-link anchors, and only to centers (no source/target-to-endpoint semantics, no layout engine).\n486\t8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n487\t   - #1/#3: start-point snapping.\n488\t   - #15: the grid was not infinite.\n489\t   - #19/#21: zoom failed away from the center because the hit area was the SVG; listeners were moved to\n490\t     `document`.\n491\t   - #23/#28: grid proportions were inconsistent with single-link mode.\n492\t\n493\t---\n494\t\n495\t## 8. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n496\t\n497\t1. **Licensing first.** links-visuals is Unlicense and can be ported now. For konard.github.io, ask the\n498\t   owner to add an Unlicense LICENSE before any code is moved. The sound engine and palettes are already\n499\t   Unlicense through immortality.\n500\t2. **Schema in Links Notation.** Express each RULES entry as links, for example:\n501\t   ```\n502\t   (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (unit px))\n503\t   (skin.name: (type select) (default glass) (options glass liquid futuristic))\n504\t   ```\n505\t   Then generate the JS and TS rule tables, and the Swift and Kotlin constants, from it. Store user diffs as\n506\t   Links Notation too: `(liquid.blur 24)`. Keep JSON import for backward compatibility with existing\n507\t   `settings` and `settings-presets` values and `#settings=` links.\n508\t3. **Keep the projection contract.** Write `--section-key` CSS variables and `data-section-key` attributes,\n509\t   and keep the before-paint injection for web targets. Native targets get the same normalized map as an\n510\t   observable store.\n511\t4. **Scopes.** Keep the user/document split (localStorage vs URL or `.lino`), and add an element scope so the\n512\t   designer mode can override tokens per node in the DOM-like tree.\n513\t5. **Controls.** Port Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip and numericKeys with their tests (`*.test.jsx`)\n514\t   as the first `controls` set. Keep WAI-ARIA APG behaviour and the Safari fixes.\n515\t6. **Links view.** Merge the K:src/links glyph, placement, collisions and render code with the L:js\n516\t   zoom-pan, grid, anchors and IK into a single renderer:\n517\t   - one marker set, with SVG and Canvas back ends generated from it\n518\t   - no global state; instance objects instead\n519\t   - D3 bundled and pinned, or dropped where `d3-force` alone is enough\n520\t   - an idle-stopping animation loop\n521\t7. **Parsing.** Replace the regex parser with the official `links-notation` package. Keep `configurations.js`\n522\t   (code and index maths, Burnside counting) as a pure utility.\n523\t8. **i18n.** Move the `{en, ru}` literals into per-language catalogs keyed by id, preferably in Links\n524\t   Notation, and keep `plural.js` rules per language.\n525\t9. **Themes.** Treat `glass`, `liquid` and `futuristic`, plus the 12 palettes and the corner/frame generator,\n526\t   as the first theme pack. Classic UIs (Windows 9x, Aqua and so on) become more theme packs on the same\n527\t   tokens. Fix #47-style corner and edge transparency in the generator, not in per-skin CSS.\n528\t10. **Animation recording.** Reuse the export pipeline: one model goes to a standalone SVG and then to a\n529\t    raster, over a timeline of settings and link diffs. The IK animation in links-visuals and the canvas\n530\t    backgrounds are the first recording targets.\n531\t11. **Process.** Adopt the per-issue test files, the three-engine Playwright runs, a case study per issue,\n532\t    and the 1500-line limit. Do not commit logs or archives, so the framework repo does not grow to hundreds\n533\t    of megabytes.\n534\t"

Optional exports\ninclude `messages`, `intl`, `server`, `react-server`, `tooling` and `compiler`.\n[Optional Vue components and SFC extraction](../docs/vue.md) provide reactive\nsource messages, SSR/hydration and template-scope diagnostics.\n[TanStack Start integration](../docs/tanstack-start.md) adds request middleware,\nserver functions, loader snapshots and localized Router navigation.\nThe native browser entry retains its dependency-free keyed runtime; source ICU\nand React browser applications use a bundler.\n\n```bash\nlino-i18n extract --in src --out locales --locale en\nlino-i18n check --dir locales --manifest locales/messages.json\n```\n\nThe complete [source-message guide](../docs/source-messages.md)\ncovers dictionaries, static derivation, provider candidates, versioned loading,\nrequest isolation and snapshot hydration. The\n[GT capability study](../docs/case-studies/issue-25/README.md)\nrecords supported workflows and remaining ecosystem integrations.\n\n## Usage\n\n```js\nimport { createI18n } from 'lino-i18n';\nimport { loadLocalesFromDirectory } from 'lino-i18n/loaders';\n\nconst catalogues = await loadLocalesFromDirectory('./locales');\nconst i18n = createI18n({\n  locales: catalogues,\n  defaultLocale: 'en',\n  fallback: ['en'],\n});\n\ni18n.t('greeting', { name: 'World' }); // → \"Hello, World!\"\ni18n.t('cart.items', { count: 0 }); // → \"Your cart is empty\"\ni18n.t('cart.items', { count: 3 }, { locale: 'ru' }); // → \"3 товара\"\ni18n.t('role', { context: 'female' }); // → \"She is a developer\"\ni18n.t('telegram.help.solve.alias.detail'); // → \"Tool aliases imply `--tool <tool>`\"\n```\n\n### Nested locale directories\n\nDirectory loading is shallow by default. Use `recursive: true` to merge UI text,\nuser prompts and system prompts into the same locale tables:\n\n```text\nlocales/\n  en.lino\n  prompts/\n    messages.lino\n    system/\n      messages.lino\n```\n\n```js\nconst catalogues = await loadLocalesFromDirectory('./locales', {\n  recursive: true,\n  compatibilityAliases: ['collapseTail', 'parentLabel'], // Optional migration aliases\n});\n```\n\nEach file can declare multiple locales; locale roots inside files determine the\ncatalogue language, regardless of filenames or directory names. Directory names\nadd no prefix to translation keys. Recursive traversal sorts entries by name in\nUTF-16 code-unit order (case-sensitive and independent of the host locale), then\nvisits them depth first: a directory's contents are processed at that directory's\nposition among its siblings. Later files and later locale blocks overwrite earlier\nvalues for duplicate keys in the same locale. For example, `en.lino` is read before\n`prompts/`, and `z.lino` after it. Other keys are preserved.\n\nOnly regular `.lino` files are loaded; symbolic links and other files are skipped.\nRead and parse errors reject the load. Compatibility aliases (including the\n`mode` shortcut) are expanded once after the entire tree is merged, preserving\nexplicit keys. The returned catalogues work with the usual `createI18n` fallback,\ninterpolation and plural handling.\n\n## Browser\n\nImport `lino-i18n/browser` for native ES modules or browser bundles. This\nentry point has no Node built-ins and uses the same translation engine and\n`t(key, params, options)` API as the main entry point:\n\n## CLI\n\nThe package ships a converter that turns popular i18n formats into\n`.lino`:\n\n```bash\n# i18next JSON → .lino\nnpx lino-i18n convert --from i18next \\\n  --in locales/en.json --out locales --locale en\n\n# i18n-js JSON → .lino\nnpx lino-i18n convert --from i18n-js \\\n  --in config/locales/en.json --out locales\n\n# react-intl bundle (AST or string) → .lino\nnpx lino-i18n convert --from react-intl \\\n  --in messages/en.json --out locales --locale en\n\n# Bundle all converted locales into one .lino file\nnpx lino-i18n convert --from i18next \\\n  --in locales-json --out locales --single-file all.lino\n```\n\nRun `npx lino-i18n --help` for every option.\n\n## Features\n\n- CLDR plural categories via `Intl.PluralRules`.\n- Nested `.lino` authoring with multiline quoted values.\n- `{{var}}` and `{var}` placeholder syntax for compatibility with i18next\n  and `react-intl`.\n- Context (gender) suffixes: `role_male`, `role_female`, `role_other`.\n- Migration aliases for deeper nested keys and parent labels.\n- Namespace prefixes via `:` (`navigation:home`) and `.` (`cart.title`).\n- Group label aliases via `label` children.\n- Configurable fallback chain.\n- Bundled multi-locale `.lino` files and per-language directories.\n- Optional missing-key handler.\n- Converter CLI for `i18next`, `i18n-js`, and `react-intl`.\n- JSON config files via `--config`.\n\n## Scripts\n\n```bash\nnpm test           # The front\n  matter carries the key, title, issue type, labels, phase, the keys of the\n  blocking issues and the requirement IDs.\n- [`issue-footer.md`](issue-footer.md) is appended to every issue body. It holds\n  the conventions every implementer (human or AI agent) must follow.\n- [`created-issues.json`](created-issues.json) maps each key to the GitHub\n  issue number and ID. It is written by the creation script.\n- [`../../../../experiments/issue-1/create-roadmap-issues.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-1/create-roadmap-issues.mjs)\n  creates the issues (bugs first, then features in key order), resolves\n  `{{KEY}}` references to `#number`, adds the \"blocked by\" relations with the\n  GitHub issue dependencies API, attaches every issue as a sub-issue of the\n  tracking issue, and generates [`../../../ROADMAP.md`](../../../ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Rules used to cut the issues\n\n1. **Bugs first.** Every defect found while studying this repository is a\n   `Bug` issue with key `Bxx`. Bugs have no feature blockers, so they can be\n   done first and in parallel.\n2. **Features next**, keyed `Fxx` in delivery order. The key order is a\n   suggested order only; the real constraint is the dependency graph.\n3. **Parallel by default.** An issue is blocked only by issues whose output it\n   directly consumes (a package API, a file format, a deployed site). Shared\n   knowledge is a reference, not a blocker.\n4. **One reviewable pull request per issue.** An issue that would need more\n   than about 1,500 changed lines of source is split.\n5. **Written for a less capable agent.** Each body says why, what is in and\n   out of scope, which files to create, step-by-step instructions, checkable\n   acceptance criteria, exact verification commands, prior art and the\n   requirement IDs it delivers.\n\n## Issue body template\n\nEvery file in `issues/` uses these sections, in this order:\n\n```markdown\n---\nkey: F06\ntitle: 'ui-core: parse Links Notation into the UI element tree'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 2\nblocked_by: [F01, F03]\nrequirements: [R2, R3, R6]\n---\n\n## Context\n\n## Goal\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n### Out of scope\n\n## Dependencies\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n## How to verify\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n## References\n```\n\n## Issue list\n\n`Blocked by` lists the issues that must be merged first. Dark values come from `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback.\n130\t- **Selector counts.** About 248 `[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and 244 `[data-theme=\"light\"]` selectors across the CSS. Most dark overrides live in `06-dark-theme.css`.\n131\t- **Chakra bridge.** `theme.js` maps tokens 1:1, e.g. `fa.surface.card → var(--fa-surface-card)`. Chakra components therefore follow the same CSS variables without a parallel theme object.\n132\t- **Root-class composition.** Skins, chat styles, composer styles and icon packs are orthogonal root classes. The CSS combines them, e.g. `.ui-skin-glass.composer-style-glass-clear`.\n133\t\n134\t### 2.5 i18n\n135\t\n136\t- **Runtime.** `js/i18n.js` is an IIFE exposing `window.FormalAiI18n`. It calls `loadCatalogs([...])` and `createI18n({locales, defaultLocale:'en', fallback:['en']})`, then dispatches `formal-ai:i18n-ready`.\n137\t- **Catalog format.** Nested Links Notation blocks (`en` / `buttons` / `key \"...\"`) with `\"\"\"` multiline strings ([#117](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/117)).\n138\t- **CI checks.**\n139\t  - Key parity across all locales (`tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`).\n140\t  - A lint against hardcoded natural language ([#659](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/659), R379).\n141\t- **Gaps.**\n142\t  - `PUBLISHED_RUNTIME_SOURCE = \"lino-i18n@0.3.0\"` in `i18n.js`, while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n143\t  - The vanilla pages use their own JS `LABELS` dicts instead of the catalogs.\n144\t\n145\t### 2.6 Preferences & memory\n146\t\n147\t- **Preferences (`preferences.js`, 123 lines).**\n148\t  - A hand-rolled Links Notation reader/writer with root `demo_preferences` and indented `key \"value\"` lines. Booleans are stored as `on`/`off`.\n149\t  - API: `[REDACTED] {load, save, format, parse, STORAGE_KEY, ROOT}`.\n150\t  - Every page shares the `formal-ai.preferences.v1` key.\n151\t  - It does not use the `links-notation` parser.\n152\t- **Memory (`memory.js`).**\n153\t  - IndexedDB database `formal-ai-demo`, store `events`, root `demo_memory`, bundle header `formal_ai_bundle`, `LINK_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION \"0.2.0\"`.\n154\t  - Events are append-only. `EXPORT_FIELDS` include `kind`, `role`, `intent`, `tool`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `content`, `attachments`, `sentAt`, `evidence`, `accessCount`, `writeCount`, `conversationId` and `conversationTitle`.\n155\t  - It exports `formal-ai-memory.lino`. Import, reset and purge sit behind confirmations ([#196](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/196)).\n156\t  - It reports a `doublets-web` backend only if that global runtime is present.\n157\t\n158\t### 2.7 Web search component\n159\t\n160\t- **Ranking.** `getDefaultProviderIds()` selects the providers, and `mergeResults` merges their results with the `rrf` strategy and `removeDuplicates`.\n161\t- **Capture adapter.** Fetches `/fetch?url=…` from a configurable base (default `http://localhost:3000`, 2,000 ms deadline). On transport failure it falls back to a direct CORS fetch.\n162\t- **Output.** Results are pushed as evidence strings into the trace. [#153](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/153) asks for a unified, deduplicated search-result template.\n163\t\n164\t### 2.8 Accessibility snapshot\n165\t\n166\t- **ARIA.** About 89 `aria-*` attributes: `aria-label` ×26, `aria-hidden` ×14, `aria-pressed` ×11. Also 9 `role=status`, plus `radiogroup`/`menu`/`menuitem`/`option` roles and 2 `aria-live` regions.\n167\t- **Focus.** `:focus-visible` styles appear in `02`, `03`, `06` and `07`.\n168\t- **Reduced motion.** `prefers-reduced-motion` appears only 3 times, all in `04-message-content.css`.\n169\t- **Keyboard.** The resizer supports keyboard steps (40 px, 16 px with Shift).\n170\t- **Audits.** No systematic audit (axe or similar) exists in CI. Open bug [#447](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/447): the left panel cannot be scrolled with the mouse.\n171\t\n172\t---\n173\t\n174\t## 3. Associative tech stack usage plan for the UI framework\n240\t\n241\t| Component | What for in the UI framework | How (based on formal-ai evidence) |\n242\t|---|---|---|\n243\t| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) parser | Canonical text form of every UI artefact: component trees, themes, tokens, skins, layouts, settings and recorded animations | Replace hand-rolled readers like `js/preferences.js` with the official JS parser. Keep a `.lino` file per artefact so it can be diffed and reviewed, as formal-ai does with catalogs, example prompts and memory exports |\n244\t| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec) | Typed (de)serialization of props, theme objects and config at strict boundaries | Use the codec's indented-format parser to validate on import, mirroring `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `associative_package.rs`. Run strict decoding on paste/import of themes or layouts, and canonical encoding on export so round-trips are byte-stable |\n245\t| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) | All user-visible strings in every binding (JS, React, Vue, RN; Swift and Kotlin through generated tables) | Reuse formal-ai's nested and multiline catalog layout, `loadCatalogs`/`createI18n` with an `en` fallback, a ready event, CI key parity and a hardcoded-language lint. Forbid per-page JS `LABELS` tables |\n246\t| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) | Layered configuration: defaults, `.lenv`, env, URL params and CLI flags, merged into a single UI config | Used today only at the Rust CLI boundary. In the framework, use it for the dev server/CLI and a small browser adapter that reads URL query and localStorage in the same precedence. Expose the result as one Links Notation config document (generalizing `formal-ai.preferences.v1`) |\n247\t| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web) / IndexedDB | Persistent store for UI state, WYSIWYG edit history and animation/interaction recordings | Copy the `memory.js` model: an append-only event log projected to doublets, IndexedDB fallback, and `doublets-web` reported only when present. Every WYSIWYG edit becomes an appended event, which gives undo/redo, replay and animation recording for free (matches #672 F4) |\n248\t| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language) | Lossless CST/AST of UI documents: component source (JSX/Vue SFC/SwiftUI/Compose) and markup | Use it as formal-ai uses it in `rust/src/coding/cst.rs` and `document_formats.rs`: parse, check a full match and reconstruct text losslessly. This enables WYSIWYG edits that write back to source in each binding's language, plus translation between bindings (as formal-ai's `js` to `ts` mirror does) |\n249\t| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli) query / substitution dialect | Selecting and rewriting UI links: theme rules, skin overrides, migrations, codemods | Theme and skin application becomes \"match link pattern, substitute values\", like `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `links_substitution_query/`. The native store (link-cli plus doublets-rs) can back a desktop or server-side design registry |\n250\t| [web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search) / [web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture) | Optional components: search box and results with RRF merge; page capture for previews or documentation | Ship as opt-in packages. Reuse the unified result template requested in #153 and the capture adapter's timeout and CORS fallback |\n251\t| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) (concept) | Context-relative values: a token resolves differently by context (theme, platform guideline, locale, density) | Model \"token X in context dark/iOS/ru\" as relative statements instead of flat override files; this addresses the 1,097-line dark override sheet |\n252\t| [transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer) (concept) | Transformations between representations: Links Notation to React/Vue/RN/SwiftUI/Compose | Vocabulary for binding generators; formal-ai's `substitution.rs` shows `.lino` rules rewriting link patterns |\n253\t| [link-calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator) | Optional: computed layout values and expression fields in WYSIWYG mode | Evaluate expression properties (e.g. `spacing * 2`) with an inspectable Links Notation trace |\n254\t\n255\t---\n256\t\n257\t## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n258\t\n259\t1. **CSS-token → component-library bridge.**\n260\t   - One set of `--fa-*` CSS variables is the source of truth.\n261\t   - Chakra semantic tokens point at `var(--…)` (`theme.js`).\n262\t   - The framework should generate both from one Links Notation token document.\n263\t2. **Orthogonal appearance axes as root classes.** Skin × chat style × composer style × icon pack × theme combine freely and are applied as root classes plus CSS vars. This maps directly to a \"theme = set of axis values\" model.\n264\t3. **Icon-pack abstraction.** Each action has a semantic name, mapped per pack (font name, short name, shape), with a `names` text-only fallback. Use this as the basis for public-domain icon handling.\n265\t4. **Priority-based responsive overflow.** `data-menu-priority` moves top-bar actions into the drawer as width shrinks. #388 asks for measured sizes; generalize this into a layout primitive.\n266\t5. **Collapsible sections with isolate.** An isolate button plus Shift+click \"expand only this\".\n267\t6. **Per-setting reset and reset-all** using a default-detection helper (`settingIsDefault`).\n268\t7. **Shared preferences contract** across separately built pages: one storage key, Links Notation format, `data-theme` on `<html>`.\n269\t8. **Natural-language interface commands.** The UI can be configured through chat (`interface-commands.jsx`), a natural fit for an associative, notation-driven config.\n270\t9. **Issue reporting with user context.**\n271\t   - A prefilled GitHub issue within the URL budget, embedding UI state (skin, theme, viewport, language, mode).\n272\t   - Use it as a framework-level \"report UI bug\" component.\n273\t10. **Append-only event log** for memory, giving export/import as `.lino` and destructive actions behind confirmation and export prompts.\n274\t11. **Quality gates in CI.**\n275\t    - i18n key parity and a hardcoded-language lint.\n276\t    - A UI-boundary lint (no business logic in view code).\n277\t    - Per-locale and per-theme screenshots.\n278\t    - A cross-org duplication scanner (`cross-org-duplication.yml`).\n279\t12. **Stable test hooks.** Systematic `data-testid` (`setting-*`, `composer-*`, `conversation-*`) and `window.FormalAi*` page APIs for E2E.\n280\t13. **Security defaults.** A strict CSP on static pages, DOMPurify on rendered markdown, Mermaid with `securityLevel: strict`, and cache-busting asset versions.\n281\t14. **Reasoning-trace presentation.** A hierarchical step view with fade gradient, last-paragraph preview and an animation budget; a candidate reusable \"process/trace\" component.\n282\t15. **Terminology rule.** Say \"links network\", not \"graph\" (#664), so the framework's visualization components use consistent vocabulary.\n283\t\n284\t---\n285\t\n286\t## 6. Duplication candidates\n287\t\n288\t| Duplicate | Where | Recommendation |\n289\t|---|---|---|\n290\t| `h()` hyperscript, `segmentedControl`, locale and theme resolution | `js/site-chrome.js` lines 13–15 state they are \"intentionally re-implemented here verbatim\" from `js/download/download.js` (line 752) | Single framework primitive (`SegmentedControl`, `ThemeChooser`, `LocaleChooser`) shared by all pages |\n291\t| Per-locale `LABELS` JS dicts | `site-chrome.js`, `download.js` | Move into lino-i18n catalogs |\n292\t| Hand-rolled Links Notation parsing | `preferences.js` (parse/format), `memory.js` (bundle reader/writer) | Official `links-notation` parser plus `lino-objects-codec` |\n293\t| Theme token values | `01-tokens.css`, `06-dark-theme.css` (1,097 lines of overrides), `landing.css`, download CSS | One token document → generated CSS vars for every page and theme |\n294\t| Icon mapping tables | `toolbar-icons.jsx` (three parallel tables), emoji glyphs in `glyphs.jsx` | One icon registry in Links Notation (action → per-pack glyph) |\n295\t| Chat UI per host | Web `/app/`, Electron wrapper, VS Code webview (#353 wants parity) | Framework chat components consumed by every host |\n296\t| JS → TS mirror | `ts/` generated from `js/` | Generate bindings from one source (meta-language) instead of mirroring |\n297\t| Theme applied to vanilla and Chakra separately | CSS classes vs Chakra components (#541, #550 bugs) | One component set; no mixed styling paths |\n298\t| Similar components across other link-foundation/link-assistant UIs | Settings panels, theme/locale choosers, issue reporters, chat composers | Flag for the cross-org inventory (see sibling research files) |\n299\t\n300\t---\n301\t\n302\t## 7. Problems and limitations\n303\t\n304\t1. **Monolith.** `application.jsx` is 1,445 lines with one `App`. Its predecessor `main.jsx` reached 9,269 lines (#951); a CI line budget and boundary lint were needed to contain it.\n305\t2. **Mixed paradigms.** Three styles coexist: React + Chakra (partial migration), plain CSS classes, and vanilla IIFE pages using `window.*` globals (`FormalAiI18n`, `FormalAiPreferences`, `FormalAiVendor`). There is no module graph across pages.\n306\t3. **CSS order dependence.** The 7 stylesheets must load in numeric order. Dark mode is a large override sheet rather than token swaps, which produces recurring \"element not themed\" bugs (#388, #541, #550).\n307\t4. **Version drift.** `i18n.js` reports `lino-i18n@0.3.0` while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n308\t5. **Limited locales.** Only en, ru, zh and hi. There is no RTL support or pluralization evidence in the UI layer.\n309\t6. **Accessibility is partial.**\n310\t   - No automated a11y audit.\n311\t   - Reduced motion is handled in a single stylesheet, even though animations (minimum message time, step reveal) are central.\n312\t   - The sidebar has a mouse-scroll bug (#447).\n313\t   - No documented contrast checks beyond a `contrast` skin.\n314\t7. **Mobile fragility.** Repeated mobile bugs: iOS accessory bar, focus layout, overflow and menu width (#108, #110, #112).\n315\t8. **Committed minified bundles** make diffs and reviews noisy (#953).\n316\t9. **No platform-guideline mapping.** Skins are named after looks (glass, material) rather than formally following Apple HIG, Material 3 or Fluent. Material and glass are approximations.\n317\t10. **No WYSIWYG configuration.** All configuration happens through the settings panel or chat commands; there is no visual editor or inspector.\n318\t11. **No animation recording.** Animations are CSS/JS timing only; there is no capture or replay of UI sessions, even though the event log could support it.\n319\t12. **Charts.** No chart components; diagrams rely on Mermaid only, and Mermaid rendering breaks on GitHub (#1190).\n320\t13. **Asset licensing.** Icon packs are third-party fonts (FontAwesome, Material Symbols, Bootstrap Icons, Ionicons, Remix, Tabler), not public domain. A public-domain-only framework needs its own set or a `names` fallback.\n321\t\n322\t---\n323\t\n324\t## 8. Migration notes (formal-ai → associative UI framework)\n325\t\n326\t1. **Phase 0: contracts first.**\n327\t   - Freeze the existing external contracts as compatibility tests: `formal-ai.preferences.v1` (root `demo_preferences`), `data-theme`, the `formal-ai:i18n-ready` event, `window.FormalAi*` hooks and all `data-testid` values.\n328\t   - The framework's config loader should read the old preference document and map each key (`uiSkin`, `chatStyle`, `composerStyle`, `toolbarIconPack`, `glassOpacity`, `uiLanguage`, …) onto framework config links.\n329\t2. **Phase 1: tokens.**\n330\t   - Express `01-tokens.css` plus the dark overrides as one Links Notation token document with context-relative values (light/dark/contrast).\n331\t   - Generate the CSS vars and the Chakra semantic-token bridge from it.\n332\t   - Delete `06-dark-theme.css` incrementally, verified by per-theme screenshot diffs (#672 F1).\n333\t3. **Phase 2: shared chrome.** Replace `site-chrome.js` and `download.js` helpers with framework `SegmentedControl`/`ThemeChooser`/`LocaleChooser` vanilla-JS bindings, and move the `LABELS` dicts into lino-i18n catalogs.\n334\t4. **Phase 3: skins as framework themes.**\n335\t   - Map `ui-skin-*`, `chat-style-*`, `composer-style-*` and `toolbar-icon-pack-*` to framework theme axes.\n336\t   - Add guideline-conformant skins (Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG/glass) to satisfy #557.\n337\t   - Keep the class names as aliases during the transition.\n338\t5. **Phase 4: components.**\n339\t   - Extract framework components in this order:\n340\t     - `CollapsibleSection`\n341\t     - `ToolbarButton` with priority overflow\n342\t     - Data was collected on 2026-11-01 from GitHub and package registries.\nSources: shallow/sparse checkouts of the repositories listed below and `gh api`.\nNo downloaded code was executed.\n\nPrimary sources:\n\n- Repository: <https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation>\n- Grammar (EBNF, v0.24.0 grammar, current packages 0.27.1):\n  [`docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/grammar/GRAMMAR.md),\n  and the same grammar written in LiNo itself:\n  [`docs/grammar/grammar.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/grammar/grammar.lino)\n- Reference literals: [`docs/protocol/reference-literals.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/protocol/reference-literals.md)\n- Binary form: [`docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md)\n- Cross-language parity corpus: [`parity/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/tree/main/parity) (`parity/text-fixtures.json`)\n\n## 1. Syntax summary\n\nA **link** is an ordered sequence of references, written `(id: v1 v2 ...)`.\nThe id is optional, and so is everything else. A **reference** is either a\nsimple token or a delimited (quoted) string. Values can themselves be links,\nso nesting goes as deep as you like.\n\n### 1.1 Links and ids\n\n```lino\npapa loves mama                 # anonymous link with three values\nfamily: papa mama son daughter  # link with id \"family\" and four values\n(papa loves mama)               # same as line 1, explicit parentheses\n(outer: (inner: v1 v2) v3)      # inline nesting\n```\n\nThe id is a **single** reference followed by `:`. `a b: c` is not a link with a\ntwo-word id.\n\n### 1.2 Indentation (hierarchy without parentheses)\n\n```lino\nfamily:\n  papa\n  mama\n```\n\nThis is `(family: papa mama)`. A value line that has indented children forms a\nnested link:\n\n```lino\nroot:\n  child1\n  child2\n    grandchild\n```\n\nThis is `(root: child1 (child2 grandchild))`. The rules:\n\n- The first content line sets the base indentation.\n- Children must be indented more than their parent, and siblings must be\n  indented equally.\n- Only spaces count; tabs do not.\n\n### 1.3 Multi-line groups (nested context, issue #282, v0.14.0+)\n\n```lino\narray (\n  a\n    b\n  c\n)\n```\n\nA `(` opens a nested context that starts again at indentation level 0, so the\nindentation inside it is structural. A body that yields a single link collapses\nto that link, so `(a b c)` is one link. `((a b))` stays distinct from `(a b)`.\n\n### 1.4 References and quoting\n\n- Simple reference: any characters except whitespace, `(`, `:` and `)`. So\n  `button.primary`, `@space.3`, `$accent`, `8px`, `100%`, `0.25` and `-1` are\n  all plain simple references.\n- Delimiters: `\"`, `'` and `` ` `` behave identically. N-quoting works as\n  follows: a run of N delimiters opens and closes, and a run of 2N delimiters\n  inside the body stands for N literal delimiters. Example: `\"\"say \"\"hi\"\" \"\"`.\n- `\"\"` is the empty reference. Formatters write it explicitly so it round-trips.\n- Lossless literal, v0.24.0+: `~1{hex UTF-8}`, for example `~1{e282ac}` for the\n  euro sign. Any string, control characters included, round-trips exactly. The\n  prefix `~[0-9]+{` is reserved.\n\n### 1.5 Comments (issue #301)\n\n```lino\n# the machines this deploys to\ndeploy: staging # only staging, for now\n```\n\n- `#` opens a comment only at the start of the document or after whitespace.\n  `issue#1047` and `\"#\"` are literal.\n- Comment characters are replaced by spaces, so error positions stay correct.\n- Comments are on by default and can be disabled (`comments: false`) for legacy\n  documents.\n- Formatters quote references that start with `#` (`'#tag'`).\n\n**Consequence for UI:** CSS hex colours (`#3390ec`) must be quoted, otherwise\nthey are read as comments. URLs and CSS pseudo-classes contain `:`, so they\nmust be quoted too (`\"https://...\"`, `\":hover\"`).\n\n### 1.6 Other forms\n\n- **Streaming parsers** exist in all 8 languages: push events (`link`, `error`,\n  `end`) plus iterators. Useful for large documents and live editing.\n- **Binary Links Notation v1** (`docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md`,\n  originating in link-cli PR #106) has golden vectors. It is a candidate wire\n  and storage format between a UI runtime and a doublets store.\n\n## 2. Implementations\n\nAll implementations are hand-written. JS is the reference, and the others are\nheld to it by the shared parity corpus (`parity/text-fixtures.json`) and golden\nround-trip tests. | - | - | **Missing.** Needed for the issue's Swift target |\n| Kotlin | none (could use Java once published) | - | - | - | **Blocked on #192** |\n\n### 2.1 JS API surface (the one the UI framework will use first)\n\n- `new Parser({ maxInputSize, maxDepth = 64, comments })`.\n  - `.parse(text)` returns `Link[]`.\n  - `.parseGroups(text)` returns a `LinksGroup` tree. `LinksGroup` exists only in\n    JS, C#, Java and C++.\n- `new Link(id, values)`, with `.format(options)` and `.toString()`.\n- `formatLinks(links, { lessParentheses, maxLineLength, indentLongLines, maxInlineRefs, groupConsecutive })`.\n- `parseIndentedDocument` / `formatIndentedDocument` (JS and C++ only).\n- `escapeReference(ref, { minimal })` / `unescapeReference(ref)`.\n- `StreamParser`: events `link`, `error` and `end`, plus `position()`, `drain()`\n  and `reset()`.\n\n### 2.2 Round-trip guarantees\n\n| Guarantee | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| `parse -> format -> parse` yields the same link tree | Yes, in every language, tested against the golden corpus |\n| Any Unicode string survives as a reference | Yes, via quoting or the `~1{}` literal |\n| Same tree across languages | Yes, via the parity fixtures |\n| Comments survive | **No.** They are dropped during parsing |\n| Original layout survives (indentation vs parentheses, quote style, blank lines) | **No.** The formatter re-chooses the layout |\n| Quoted vs bare distinction is visible in the tree | **No.** `\"1\"` and `1` are the same reference string |\n\nFor a WYSIWYG editor that edits the user's `.lino` file, the last three rows\nmatter most. See section 5.\n\n### 2.3 Open and relevant issues (links-notation)\n\n- Open: [#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)\n  (publish Java and PHP) and #350 (dependabot). The repository is otherwise\n  quiet and stable.\n- Closed but relevant to UI:\n  - #301 (comments)\n  - #282 (nested context for multi-line groups)\n  - #332 (lossless reference literal)\n  - #351 (browser bundling)\n  - #313 (formatter / empty reference)\n  - #184 (multi-reference values)\n\n## 3. What a UI dialect needs that LiNo already has\n\n| UI need | Existing LiNo feature |\n| --- | --- |\n| Tree of elements (DOM-like) | Indentation and nested groups. `parseGroups` keeps the hierarchy |\n| Element identity | Link id (`save:`). Ids are single references, globally addressable |\n| Graph, not just tree (reuse, references between elements and tokens) | A reference is just a name, so `@token` / `$name` / an element id can point anywhere in the document. This is native to the associative model |\n| Attributes / props | `(key value)` sub-links, the lino-objects-codec convention |\n| Text content with any characters | Quoting, N-quoting and `~1{}` literals |\n| Comments in hand-written files | `#` comments (read side only) |\n| Big documents, live editing | Streaming parsers, `position()` for error locations |\n| One spec for many targets | 8 implementations with a parity corpus. Rust compiles to WASM |\n| Typed config objects | lino-objects-codec (quoted = string, bare = number/bool/null) |\n| i18n strings | lino-i18n catalogues and React adapter |\n| Settings resolution | lino-arguments (pure build for browser) |\n| Import of existing HTML/CSS | meta-language HTML/CSS importers with lossless CST |\n| Storage as a links network | doublets-web (WASM), link-cli, binary LiNo |\n| Visualizing the network | link-cli workbench and doublets-web playground graph views (prior art for the issue's \"LiNo -> links network UI\" converter) |\n\n## 5. Gaps and open questions\n\n1. **Typed values.** The core tree has only strings, and `\"1\"` and `1` produce\n   the same reference. The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.\n\n   Recommendation: (b) for dimensions, durations and colours, with (a) as the\n   fallback for free-form props. Also ask upstream for a `quoted` flag on\n   parsed references, which would remove the need for a second reader.\n2. **Units and colours.**\n   - `8px`, `0.2s`, `50%` and `1.5rem` are valid bare references, but they are\n     strings until a schema parses them.\n   - Hex colours must be quoted because of `#` comments.\n   - Alternative: `rgb(...)` / `oklch(...)` as links, for example\n     `(oklch 0.62 0.19 255)`, which is better for the associative model and for\n     theme maths.\n3. **`:` in values.** URLs, CSS pseudo-classes (`:hover`), media queries and\n   ratios (`16:9`) need quoting. Prefer structured links instead:\n   `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))` and `(aspect 16 9)`.\n4. **Comments and formatting are lost on round trip.** A WYSIWYG editor that\n   writes back to `.lino` will strip the user's comments and reflow the layout.\n   Options:\n   - (a) A CST mode upstream (trivia and spans, as meta-language already does\n     for CSS).\n   - (b) Make comments first-class links, for example `(note \"...\")`.\n   - (c) Patch-in-place edits using parser positions.\n\n   This needs an issue upstream in links-notation.\n5. **Ordering.** Link values are ordered, which is good for children and\n   keyframes. Property order, however, should be insignificant. The dialect\n   must state which parts are sequences (children, keyframes, transitions) and\n   which are sets (props). It must also define the meaning of a duplicate key:\n   last wins, as in lino-store logs.\n6. **Ids and scoping.** Ids are document-global strings, and nothing prevents\n   duplicates. Questions:\n   - Do we need namespaces (`login.save`) or nested id scopes per component?\n   - How do ids map to doublet numeric addresses, and are they stable across\n     edits? The editor needs stable ids for selection, undo and collaboration.\n7. **References for styles and tokens.** There is no built-in reference sigil.\n   A convention is needed:\n   - `@token.path` for design tokens\n   - `$param` for component parameters (the linksql / transformer convention)\n   - a bare id for elements and keyframe tracks\n\n   Open questions: resolution order (component, then theme, then base),\n   cycles, and fallbacks (`(or @color.accent \"#3390ec\")`).\n8. **Schemas and validation.** lino-schema is only a stub. The dialect needs a\n   schema (which props an element accepts, their types and defaults) for:\n   - the editor's property panel\n   - validation\n   - codegen to React, Vue, React Native, SwiftUI and Compose\n9. **Expressions and bindings.** Event handlers, data bindings and conditional\n   rendering need a small expression vocabulary, for example\n   `(on press (emit save))`, `(bind value $draft.text)` and\n   `(when $sending (show spinner))`. Decide whether this reuses the linksql\n   substitution syntax.\n10. **Missing languages.**\n    - Swift: no implementation exists.\n    - Kotlin: blocked by the unpublished Java package (#192).\n\n    Options: native targets either ship a parser or consume a precompiled\n    form (JSON or binary LiNo) produced by the JS/Rust toolchain.\n11. **Security.** The parser has `maxDepth = 64` and `maxInputSize`. User-supplied\n    themes must never contain executable code. Event handlers are names, not\n    code.\n\n## 6. Proposed sketch of a UI dialect in LiNo (PROPOSAL, not an existing format)\n\n> Everything in this section is a **proposal for discussion**. It is not\n> implemented anywhere. It only uses syntax the current grammar (0.27.1)\n> accepts. The meaning of every name is defined by the proposed dialect\n> schema, not by LiNo itself.\n\nConventions used:\n\n- An indented id link (`save:`) declares an element, token set or animation.\n  Its first value is the **kind** (`button`, `stack`, `theme`, `animation`).\n- Props are `(key value...)` sub-links. Their order does not matter.\n- Children, keyframes and transitions are ordered.\n- `@a.b.c` is a design-token reference. `$name` is a component parameter. A\n  bare id is an element or animation reference.\n- Quoted text is a literal string. Bare values are interpreted by the property\n  schema (number, dimension, duration, enum).\n- Colours are quoted hex or structured `(oklch L C H)`.\n\n### 6.1 A button\n\n```lino\nsave:\n  button\n  (label (t \"composer.send\"))          # i18n key, resolved by lino-i18n\n  (variant primary)\n  (size md)\n  (icon send)                          # public-domain icon set, by name\n  (disabled $draft.empty)              # binding to a parameter\n  (on press (emit message.send))       # handlers are names, never code\n  (style\n    (background @color.accent-fill)\n    (color @color.on-accent)\n    (radius @radius.control)\n    (padding @space.2 @space.3)\n    (state hover (background @color.accent))\n    (state pressed (scale 0.97)))\n  (enter bubble-in)                    # reference to an animation below\n```\n\n### 6.2 A layout\n\n```lino\nchat-screen:\n  split\n  (direction row)\n  (resizable true)\n  (remember-size \"chat.columns\")\n  (children chat-list conversation)\n\nchat-list:\n  list\n  (virtualized true)\n  (item-height 3.5rem)\n  (min-width 16rem)\n  (items $chats)\n  (template chat-row)\n\nconversation:\n  stack\n  (direction column)\n  (max-width @size.chat-column)\n  (children\n    (header (title $chat.name))\n    (messages (items $messages) (group-by sender) (follow bottom))\n    composer)\n\ncompact-layout:\n  breakpoint\n  (when (max-width 640px))\n  (override chat-screen (direction column) (children conversation))\n```\n\n`children` holds element ids, so the same element can sit in several layouts.\nThat reuse is the graph property the associative model gives for free. Inline\nanonymous children (`(header ...)`) are also allowed.\n\n### 6.3 A theme token set\n\n```lino\nbase:\n  theme\n  (space (1 0.25rem) (2 0.5rem) (3 0.75rem) (4 1rem))\n  (radius (control 8px) (bubble 15px))\n  (size (control-h 2.25rem) (chat-column 44rem))\n  (motion (fast 120ms) (normal 200ms) (easing standard))\n\ntelegram-light:\n  theme\n  (extends base)\n  (mode light)\n  (color\n    (bg \"#ffffff\")\n    (text \"#000000\")\n    (accent \"#3390ec\")\n    (accent-fill \"#2a7bd0\")              # darkened for 4.5:1 contrast\n    (on-accent \"#ffffff\")\n    (bubble-out \"#e3fee0\")\n    (bubble-in \"#ffffff\"))\n  (radius (bubble 15px))\n\ntelegram-dark:\n  theme\n  (extends telegram-light)\n  (mode dark)\n  (color (bg \"#212121\") (text \"#ffffff\") (bubble-out \"#8774e1\") (bubble-in \"#212121\"))\n```\n\nThe token names were chosen so that meta-sovereign's existing CSS custom\nproperties (`--bg`, `--accent`, `--accent-fill`, `--bubble-out`,\n`--bubble-radius`, `--control-h`, `--chat-column`) map onto them one to one.\nA theme compiles to `:root[data-theme=...]` CSS variables on the web and to\nplatform theme objects elsewhere. The colour values above are illustrative.\n\n### 6.4 An animation keyframe track\n\n```lino\nbubble-in:\n  animation\n  (duration @motion.normal)\n  (easing \"cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)\")  # quoted because it has parens\n  (fill both)\n  (keyframes\n    (at 0 (opacity 0) (translate-y 8px) (scale 0.98))\n    (at 0.6 (opacity 1))\n    (at 1 (opacity 1) (translate-y 0) (scale 1)))\n  (reduced-motion (duration 0ms))        # honours prefers-reduced-motion\n\ntyping-dots:\n  animation\n  (duration 1.2s)\n  (iterations infinite)\n  (tracks\n    (track dot-1 (keyframes (at 0 (opacity 0.3)) (at 0.5 (opacity 1)) (at 1 (opacity 0.3))))\n    (track dot-2 (delay 0.15s) (same-as dot-1))\n    (track dot-3 (delay 0.3s) (same-as dot-1)))\n```\n\n`keyframes` is an ordered sequence of `(at offset props...)`. `tracks` lets one\nanimation drive several targets, which suits a timeline editor in the WYSIWYG\ntool. Targets: CSS `@keyframes` / the Web Animations API, React Native\n`Animated`, SwiftUI `keyframeAnimator` and Compose `keyframes`.\n\n### 6.5 Open decisions for this sketch\n\n- Should the kind be the first value (`save:\\n  button`), or should the id\n  carry it (`button.save:`)? The first keeps ids clean. The second makes\n  queries such as \"all buttons\" a prefix match.\n- Should `style` be inline, or always a reference to a named style link? The\n  latter deduplicates better, can use deduplino, and maps better to doublets.\n- Should a document be decoded through lino-objects-codec (typed) or through\n  the core parser plus a schema (strings)? Both are viable. The schema route\n  keeps one parser across all 8 languages.",

[2026-11-01T11:46:26.199Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Architecture (proposal)\n\nThis document is the target architecture of the associative UI framework\nplanned in [issue #1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1). It is a\n**proposal**: every part of it is delivered by a roadmap issue listed in\n[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), and each roadmap issue may refine it. The evidence\nbehind each decision is in the\n[issue 1 case study](case-studies/issue-1/README.md).\n\n## Principles\n\n1. **Links first.** Every UI concept (element, property, style rule, design\n   token, theme, behaviour, data binding, animation, recording, configuration\n   override, asset licence) is a link in a links network. Links Notation\n   (LiNo, [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation))\n   is its only canonical text form. JSON, CSS, JSX, XAML, SwiftUI and so on are\n   import or export formats, never the source of truth.\n2. **One dialect.** Structure, configuration, styles, tokens, animations and\n   recordings use one LiNo vocabulary (the _UI dialect_), so any other UI\n   framework can be described as a LiNo document in that dialect.\n3. **Sharable by default.** A UI, a theme, a set of overrides or a recording is\n   a plain LiNo text that can be pasted into an issue, a chat with an agent,\n   or a URL.\n4. **Runtime interpreter, thin renderers.** One platform-neutral core\n   interprets the links network. Each platform (DOM, React, Vue, React Native,\n   SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose) has a thin renderer. Code generation is used only\n   for wrappers, types and optional \"eject to code\" exports.\n5. **JavaScript first.** As required by [`javascript-first.md`](javascript-first.md),\n   the JavaScript implementation and shared conformance fixtures come first.\n   Swift and Kotlin ports must pass the same fixtures.\n6. **Everything editable at runtime.** Every rendered element keeps a stable\n   link ID that maps back to its LiNo source. This is what makes the\n   development/configuration mode and the WYSIWYG designer possible on any\n   site built with the framework.\n7. **Public domain.** Code is released under the [Unlicense](../LICENSE). Our\n   own non-code assets are dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0).\n   Third-party assets are allowed only with a machine-readable record of the\n   source, copyright holder, licence (SPDX ID) and attribution text.\n\n## Layers\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph Sources[\"LiNo sources (sharable text)\"]\n    Doc[\"documents<br/>(structure)\"]\n    Tok[\"tokens & themes\"]\n    Sty[\"styles\"]\n    Ani[\"animations & recordings\"]\n    Cfg[\"configuration overrides\"]\n    Ast[\"asset records\"]\n  end\n  Sources --> Core[\"ui-core<br/>parse · validate · project · diff/patch\"]\n  Core --> Store[\"links store<br/>(in-memory network, transactions, undo/redo,<br/>IndexedDB / doublets-web persistence)\"]\n  Store --> Config[\"configuration layers<br/>defaults < theme < site < user < session\"]\n  Config --> Engine[\"style & token resolver,<br/>behaviour state machines, animation engine\"]\n  Engine --> DOM[\"DOM renderer<br/>(custom elements)\"]\n  DOM --> React[\"React adapter\"]\n  DOM --> Vue[\"Vue adapter\"]\n  Engine --> RN[\"React Native renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Swift[\"SwiftUI renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Kotlin[\"Compose renderer\"]\n  Store --> Dev[\"dev/configuration mode<br/>(inspector overlay)\"]\n  Dev --> Designer[\"WYSIWYG designer\"]\n  Dev --> Export[\"export overrides as LiNo<br/>(agent hand-off, share URL)\"]\n```\n\n| Layer                 | Package (working name)                         | Responsibility                                                                                                                     |\n| |\n| Styles                | `@link-foundation/ui-style`                    | Style rules as links (selectors, states, responsive conditions) resolved against tokens.
