asset records with SPDX licences.                                                                   |\n\nPackage names are working names; the monorepo issue decides the final ones.\n\n## The UI dialect (sketch)\n\nThe samples below are in\n[`case-studies/issue-1/samples/`](case-studies/issue-1/samples/) and are\nchecked by [`experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs):\n`links-notation` 0.27.1 parses every sample and formats it back to an equal\nlinks network.\n\nA document (structure, configuration and behaviour in one place):\n\n```lino\n(app: document\n  (title 'Links UI demo')\n  (theme material3)\n  (body: stack\n    (direction vertical)\n    (gap (token space.medium))\n    (greeting: text 'Hello, links')\n    (ok: button\n      (label 'OK')\n      (variant filled)\n      (on press (navigate home)))))\n```\n\nTokens and themes:\n\n```lino\n(material3: theme\n  (extends base)\n  (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n  (token space.medium 16px)\n  (token motion.duration.short 150ms))\n```\n\nAnimation and a recording:\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n(recording-1: recording\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nConfiguration overrides produced by the dev mode (what a user hands to an\nagent with \"make these the defaults\"):\n\n```lino\n(user-overrides: overrides\n  (layer user)\n  (base app)\n  (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n  (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n```\n\n### Links Notation parse shapes\n\nThe experiment\n[`experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs)\nshows that `links-notation` 0.27.1 returns **different link structures** for\nthe same element depending on how it is written:\n\n- `(ok: button (label 'OK'))` on one line gives one nested link;\n- the same text split over several lines inside parentheses, and the indented\n  form `ok: button` / `  label 'OK'`, are returned by `Parser.parse()` as\n  expanded path links such as `((ok: button) (label OK))`;\n- `Parser.parseGroups()` keeps the indented form as an explicit tree.\n\n`ui-core` therefore defines one **tree projection** that accepts all three\nforms and produces the same element tree. The dialect specification issue\nfixes this projection and its conformance fixtures.\n\n## Configuration layers and agent hand-off\n\nEvery value an element uses is resolved through ordered layers:\n\n1. `defaults` — the component's own defaults (shipped in the package);\n2. `theme` — the active theme(s), which may be nested per subtree;\n3. `site` — the application's committed LiNo configuration;\n4. `user` — overrides saved in the browser (IndexedDB);\n5. `session` — temporary overrides made in dev mode and not yet saved.\n\nDev mode writes only to `user` or `session`. \"Make these the defaults\" exports\nthe difference between the top layers and `site` as an `overrides` LiNo\ndocument, a share URL, and a ready-to-paste agent instruction. The agent then\napplies the patch to the committed `site` configuration.\n\n## Development/configuration mode and designer\n\n- Enter dev mode with a keyboard shortcut, a `?ui-dev` URL parameter, or a\n  `<ui-dev-mode>` element. Sites can disable or restrict it.\n- Hovering highlights elements and clicking selects them. The inspector shows\n  the outline tree (links network), the property grid (resolved value plus the\n  layer it came from), styles, tokens, animations and the LiNo source.\n- The WYSIWYG designer reuses the inspector and adds a toolbox, canvas drag\n  and drop, alignment guides, multi-select, undo/redo, docked panels,\n  two-way source sync and a timeline. It is built with the framework itself.\n\n## Themes and other frameworks as LiNo\n\nA theme is a LiNo package of tokens, style rules and component templates\n(the XAML control-template idea). Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG-guided and\n\"classic\" themes (deepcase versions, konard.github.io styles, retro desktop\nlooks) are just alternative packages. Migration from MUI, Fluent UI, shadcn/ui\nand other frameworks is a converter plus a mapping table into the same\ndialect.\n\n## Platforms\n\n- **Web:** custom elements (plain JavaScript), React and Vue wrappers over the\n  same core.\n- **React Native:** a renderer that maps dialect elements to React Native\n  primitives (New Architecture).\n- **Swift:** a SwiftPM package with a SwiftUI renderer. It reads LiNo with a\n  Swift parser (an upstream `links-notation` port, or a port created by the\n  roadmap if none exists).\n- **Kotlin:** a Gradle/Kotlin Multiplatform package with a Jetpack Compose /\n  Compose Multiplatform renderer, with the same parser condition.\n\nAll implementations run the shared conformance fixtures from `docs/spec/`.\n\n## Associative technology stack usage\n\n| Component                                                                     | Use in this framework                                                    |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)           | Canonical text format; parser and formatter for every implementation.    |\n| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)   | Strict encoding and decoding of object-shaped configuration.             |\n| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)           | CLI, environment and `.lenv` configuration of tools (converters, build). |\n| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)                     | Localisation catalogs for every component and the designer.              |\n| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)             | Lossless CST networks for importing source code (JSX, Vue SFC, HTML).    |\n| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)                       | Query and substitution conventions for selectors and patches.            |\n| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)                 | Compatibility target for browser persistence of the links store.         |\n| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) | Context-relative values (per theme, per user, per device) as a model.    |\n\nThe full mapping, including which Architecture: links-as-UI and client handlers\n\n### 2.1 UI stored as links\n\nA UI component is a **code link** plus **binding links**:\n\n```\n(handler: Handler clientSupportsJs -> tsxCodeLink)      # \"this code runs in the browser\"\n(handleClient: HandleClient SomeType -> handler)        # \"render links of SomeType with it\"\n```\n\n- The code link (type `TSX`, `@deep-foundation/core`) holds a string value of the form\n  `({deep, require}) => { const React = require('react'); ... return Component }`.\n- `deep._findHandler({ handlerId, context })` (deeplinks `imports/client.tsx` ~L2277) queries the\n  `handlers` table filtered by the JS execution provider. Without `handlerId` it matches a\n  `@deep-foundation/deepcase` `Context` link among the context ids — i.e. handler choice is\n  context-sensitive and itself a link query.\n- `evalClientHandler` (deeplinks `imports/client-handler.tsx`) runs `eval(value)`, expects a\n  function, calls it with `{deep, gql, require, ...input}`, and renders the returned component.\n- `require` is a **whitelist map** (`r.list` in deepcase `imports/client-handler.tsx`) of\n  packages: react, chakra, framer-motion, monaco, cytoscape, recharts, d3, etc. Heavier modules\n  are resolved lazily through `DeepClient.resolveDependency`.\n- `CatchErrors` is an error boundary that renders a Chakra `Alert` with a reset button.\n  Perception replaces it with `ClientHandlerErrorComponent` (modal, src/dist toggle, FinderButton).\n- `ClientHandlerRenderer` props: `fillSize`, `onClose`, `linkId`, `handlerId`, `context`.\n\n### 2.2 Package-defined handlers (`deep.json` of deepcase)\n\n| Handler                  | Bound to types                       |\n| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |\n| `asyncFileClientHandler` | AsyncFile (image/video/file preview) |\n| `stringClientHandler`    | Join, PackageQuery, Contain          |\n| `queryClientHandler`     | Query                                |\n| `editorClientHandler`    | SyncTextFile, TSX                    |\n\nOther types declared: `Traveler` (Any -> Query, symbol 🧳), `ContextToken`, `Context`.\n\n### 2.3 HandleCyto — graph rendering as links\n\n`@deep-foundation/handle-cyto` defines `HandleCyto`: a handler that returns Cytoscape `elements`\nand `stylesheets` for links of a given type (`imports/cyto-handler.tsx`). Example:\n`HandleCytoContainInvisible` hides Contain edges. Rules can be toggled per handler\n(`useCytoHandlersRules`). So **per-type visual representation is data**, not code in the shell.\n\n### 2.4 State stores\n\n`@deep-foundation/store` provides one hook API over three backends:\n`useQueryStore` (URL query, shareable), `useLocalStore` (localStorage), `useCookiesStore`.\nExamples: `useSpaceId`, `useContainer` (query store); `layout`, `editor-tabs` (local store).\n\n### 2.5 Perception (second generation)\n\n- `perception-imports/imports/go.tsx` (927 lines): `GoI`, `GoProvider`, `useGo` — navigation as a\n  chainable cursor (`go.focus`, `go.do`, `go.parents`) with `History` / `HistoryHandler` links.\n- `perception-imports/imports/react-handler.tsx`: `ReactHandler`, `ReactHandlersProvider`,\n  `createComponent` — handlers usable as plain React components.\n- `perception-app/pages/index.tsx`: the **whole app shell is a handler** —\n  `<go.Handler handlerId={deep.idLocal('@deep-foundation/perception-links','Layout')} Auth={...} Status={...} ColorMode={...}/>`.\n  The shell supplies only slot components (auth slide-out panel, status indicator, color mode).\n- Also: Telegram web-app script, regenerable `preloaded.json` (handlers bundled offline).\n\n### 2.6 The 2025 rewrite (`deep-foundation/deep`)\n\nNext 15 app router, MUI 6 dark theme (`src/theme.tsx`) with a **per-JS-value-type palette**\n(`types.value/symbol/undefined/promise/boolean/string/number/bigint/set/weakSet...`, each with\nmain/light/dark), black canvas page rendering an echarts graph (`src/app/page.tsx`,\n`src/components/echarts.js`).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Graph visualization\n\n**Library:** Cytoscape via `react-cytoscapejs` (`imports/cyto/graph.tsx`).\nPlugins: dagre, cola, d3-force, custom `cytoscape-deep-d3-force`, custom fork of cxtmenu\n(`imports/cyto/cxtmenu.tsx`), edge-connections, edgehandles (drag to create links).\n\n**Layouts** (`imports/cyto/layouts.tsx`, chosen in top menu, stored in local store `layout`):\n\n| Layout                    | Parameters                                                                                    |\n| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `deep-d3-force` (default) | manyBodyStrength -2000, linkDistance 100, alpha 0.8, `infinite: true` (continuous simulation) |\n| `cola`                    | edgeLength = 100 + 10 \\* connectedEdges                                                       |\n| `dagre`                   | hierarchical                                                                                  |\n\n**Encoding a link** (`imports/cyto/elements.tsx`): every link is a node; `from`, `to` and `type`\nbecome separate edges from that node. Missing endpoints are auto-added as id-only nodes.\nLabel: `id\\ntype:Name\\nname:Name\\nvalue(11 chars + \"...\" + 9 chars)\\n\\n symbol`; symbol from the\ntype's `Symbol` link, default 📍.\n\n**Stylesheet** (`imports/cyto/stylesheets.tsx`):\n\n| Selector             | Style                             |\n| -------------------- | --------------------------------- |\n| `.link-node`         | 30x30, white, label below         |\n| `.link-from`         | edge, `tee` arrow                 |\n| `.link-to`           | edge, triangle arrow              |\n| `.link-type`         | dashed `[5,5]`, triangle arrow    |\n| `:hover`             | underlay #0080ff                  |\n| `.focused`           | border-width 4, blue.500          |\n| `.query-link-*-node` | small 8px / 16px dots             |\n| `:parent`            | compound nodes, gray, opacity 0.1 |\n\n**Interactions**\n\n- Radial context menu on node (`cxttapstart` / `taphold`), radius 108, activeFillColor\n  `rgba(0,128,255,0.75)`: editor, unlock, delete, delete down, insert, update, login, space,\n  container, traveler (n), readme. Core (background) menu: insert, center, query.\n- Double click opens the type's handler as a floating window; drag positions get saved as Focus.\n- Edgehandles: drag from a node to create a link (type picked afterwards).\n- Traveler (`imports/cyto/traveler.tsx`): per-node sub-menu toggling query links that pull in\n  neighbours: types, out, in, up, down, to, from, typed, all / by-type. A `Traveler` link points\n  to an active `Query` contained in the space.\n- Search (`MenuSearch`), \"clear focuses\", per-handler HandleCyto toggles.\n\n**Perception graph** (`perception-app/imports/graph.tsx`): declarative React components\n`<Graph>`, `<GraphNode>`, `<GraphEdge>`, `<GraphStyle>` over cytoscape, with\n`cytoscape-node-html-label` (HTML labels in nodes), cola and dagre.\n\n**Keyboard orientation** (`perception-app/imports/orientation.tsx`): `NavDirection` values\ncurrent, close, delete, edit-from, from, type, to, edit-to, out, typed, in, up, down, prev, next,\nparents, contains, insert, value, results. Each has a left/up/right/down mapping — a spatial\nkeyboard map over link relations.\n\n**3D**: aframe + aframe-forcegraph code exists but is fully commented out; 3D mode requested in\ndeepcase-app #159.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Windows / frames / tabs model\n\nAll window state is **links in the space**, so a layout is persistable and shareable:\n\n| Concept                      | Representation                                                        |\n| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Space (workspace)            | a link id in URL (`useSpaceId`), \"enter space\" via radial menu        |\n| Container (where inserts go) | link id in URL (`useContainer`)                                       |\n| Node position                | `Focus` link (space -> link), value `{x, y}`; \"unlock\" deletes it     |\n| Open window                  | `Opened` link (space -> link) from `@deep-foundation/deepcase-opened` |\n| Which handler in the window  | `OpenedHandler` link (Opened -> Handler)                              |\n| Visible neighbours           | `Traveler` -> `Query` links                                           |\n\n- API: `useOpenedMethods()` in `imports/cyto/opened.tsx` -> `open(id, handlerId)`, `close(id)`,\n  `isOpened(id)`.\n- Windows are React overlays anchored to graph nodes: `CytoReactLayout`\n  (`imports/cyto/react.tsx`) applies a CSS transform to a div synchronized with Cytoscape\n  `pan zoom`, `render`, `add`, `layoutstop`, `data`, `position bounds` events.\n- Window header (`imports/cyto/hooks.tsx` ~L640-710): handler picker popover\n  (`CytoReactLinksCard`), \"open in new full tab\" button, close button.\n- Full tab: `/client-handler?props={\"linkId\":..,\"handlerId\":..}` (deepcase-app\n  `pages/client-handler.tsx`) renders any handler as a standalone page.\n- Modal windows: editor (`CytoEditor`), packager (`PackagerInterface`: npm search + install /\n  uninstall tabs), connector (local docker/engine portal).\n- Top menu (`imports/cyto/menu.tsx`, framer-motion animated) — attached ButtonGroups:\n  `auth <id> x`, `space <id> x`, `container <id> x`, copy token / paste token / login token,\n  gql, editor; switches: autofocus, focus, opened, debug, types, traveler, breadcrumbs,\n  cytoHandlers, animation; layout select; search; clear focuses; Travelers popover; CytoHandlers\n  popover. Version text bottom-left; sun/moon toggle fixed top-right (`imports/switch-mode.tsx`).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Editors\n\n1. **Code editor modal** — `CytoEditor` (`imports/cyto/editor.tsx`, 656 lines):\n   - Tabs persisted in local store `editor-tabs` + active `editor-tab`; drafts in `editor-values`\n     (500 ms debounce). `EditorTab` = `{id, saved, active, loading, initialValue}` with unsaved dot.\n   - `EditorGrid` (`imports/editor/editor-grid.tsx`): two columns or VerticalSash split; left\n     Monaco, right switchable area (`editor-switcher.tsx`): **Preview** (runs handler on the link,\n     `fillSize` toggle), **Handlers** (which handlers bind this code), **Results** (handler/\n     promise results). Language list `editor-lang-list`, TS diagnostics options.\n2. **WYSIWYG** — `DeepWysiwyg` (`imports/deep-wysiwyg.tsx`): Slate with Mark buttons (bold,\n   italic, underline, code) and Block buttons (h1/h2, quote, numbered/bulleted list, align),\n   HTML (de)serialization via slate-serializers; `useStringSaver` writes the link's string value.\n3. **Forms** — rjsf JSON-schema forms and react-hook-form for structured values.\n4. **Graph editing** — insert / update / delete via radial menu and edgehandles.\n5. **Perception editor** — Monaco plus CodeMirror (`@uiw/react-codemirror`) for mobile.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Theming\n\n**deepcase theme** (`imports/theme/theme.tsx`): Chakra `extendTheme`, `cssVarPrefix: 'deepCase'`,\n`initialColorMode: 'light'`.\n\n| Token / color               | Light                                                 | Dark                |\n| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |\n| body bg                     | gray.100                                              | cyDark `#141214`    |\n| backgroundModal             | blue.50                                               | blue.900 `#19202B`  |\n| editorPreviewBackgroundGrid | `#e5eefc`                                             | `#404040`           |\n| primary                     | `#0080ff`                                             | `#0080ff`           |\n| text                        | grayText `#3a3a3a`                                    | whiteText `#ebf8ff` |\n| other                       | whiteBg `#fcfcfc`, gray.10 `#eee`, gray.900 `#111720` |                     |\n\nSemantic tokens: [REDACTED], borderColor, backgroundModal, buttonBackgroundModal, switchOn/Off,\neditorPreviewBackground, editorPreviewBackgroundGrid, whiteGray, bgColor, siteBg.\n\n**perception theme** (`perception-imports/imports/theme.tsx`): `initialColorMode: 'dark'`,\n`useSystemColorMode: true`; `deep` palette 50 `#EBF8FF`, 100 `#BEE3F8`, 400 `#4299E1`,\n600 `#2B6CB0`, 700 `#2C5282`, 800 `#1B2535`, 900 `#19202B`, 950 `#0000004d`; `danger` palette;\nactive `#00438F` (light) / cyan (dark); splash `#0D1117`; tokens deepBg, deepColor, deepBgHover,\ndeepBgActive, deepLine, deepLinkNodeBg; `ColorMode` button component.\n\n**deep (2025)** (`src/theme.tsx`): MUI dark, neutral primary `#cccccc`, per-value-type colors\n(value `#64B5F6`, symbol `#FFD54F`, undefined `#90A4AE`, promise `#4DB6AC`, boolean `#F06292`,\nstring `#81C784`, number `#7986CB`, bigint `#9575CD`, set `#4DD0E1`, ...), black canvas.\n\nGraph colors live separately in Cytoscape stylesheets (not in Chakra tokens) — a source of\nlight/dark bugs (see section 10).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Classic UI versions worth reproducing as themes\n\n1. **\"DeepCase classic light\" (0.1.0-beta, deepcase-app issue #76 screenshot)**\n   - Full-screen pale gray-blue canvas (`#edf2f7`-like, Chakra gray.100); hundreds of small\n     emoji nodes (⭐ Type, 📍 default, 🔥 Operation, 📎 Value, 🌲 Tree) with multi-line labels\n     `75 / type:Type / name:Schedule`; thin gray edges with arrowheads.\n   - Row 1: attached outlined button groups `auth 376 x | space 182 x | container 182 x |\ncopy token | paste token | gql | editor`; blue `packager` button top-right.\n   - Row 2: switches autofocus (on, blue), focus, debug, types, promises, traveler, breadcrumbs;\n     search input below; version `0.1.0-beta.2` bottom-left.\n2. **\"DeepCase dark + radial menu\" (issue #299)** — `#141214` canvas, selected node white circle\n   with blue ring and emoji avatar, large faded label `1044 type:User`, dark gray pie menu with\n   rotated wedge labels (editor, traveler (0), container, space, login, update, insert,\n   delete down, delete, unlock); blue active wedge.\n3. **\"DeepCase handler windows\"** — floating Chakra cards anchored to nodes, header with handler\n   picker / new tab / close; Monaco editor modal with tab strip and Preview/Handlers/Results.\n4. **\"Perception dark\"** — `deep` palette (`#19202B`/`#1B2535`), cyan active, HTML labels inside\n   nodes, keyboard-orientation navigation, slide-out auth panel, status dot.\n5. **\"deepcase.github.io landing\"** — `DeepFrame` (`imports/deep-case-frame/deep-frame.tsx`):\n   framer-motion spring tilt card (rotateX/rotateY +/-15 deg, perspective 450) with DeepCaseMini\n   inside, play button, toggler; flying words, typist effect.\n6. **\"Deep 2025 echarts\"** — black canvas, MUI dark, nodes colored by JS value type.\n7. **\"RTS / game mode\"** (deepcase-app #116, #112, #114) — UI \"inspired by RTS games\",\n   edge-scrolling, keyboard scroll, fullscreen; must be switchable back to \"boring\".\n8. **\"3D / VR force graph\"** (#159, commented-out aframe-forcegraph code).\n\nEach can be captured as a nested Links Notation theme: tokens (colors), graph style rules\n(selector -> properties), chrome layout (which menus/rows/switches exist), interaction profile\n(radial vs linear menu, mouse vs keyboard).\n\n---\n\n## 8. Patterns worth adopting (concrete)\n\n1. **Type-bound renderers as links**: `HandleClient(Type -> Handler)`; renderer lookup is a\n   query, so adding a renderer never touches the shell.\n2. **Context-sensitive handler selection** via `Context` links (same link, different view per\n   context: graph node, window, full tab, list row).\n3. **Separate visual-in-graph handlers** (`HandleCyto`) from content handlers — two binding kinds:\n   \"how it looks as a node\" vs \"how it looks when opened\".\n4. **Window state as links**: `Opened(space -> link)` + `OpenedHandler(opened -> handler)`.\n5. **Positions as links**: `Focus(space -> link) = {x, y}` — layout is data; unlock = delete.\n6. **Workspace = link** (space) and **insertion target = link** (container), both in the URL.\n7. **Traveler**: neighbourhood expansion as stored, toggleable queries (types/in/out/up/down/...).\n8. **Overlay sync**: HTML windows positioned by graph pan/zoom transform (`CytoReactLayout`).\n9. **Declarative graph DSL** (`<Graph><GraphNode/><GraphEdge/><GraphStyle/></Graph>`) — maps\n   1:1 to nested Links Notation.\n10. **Keyboard orientation map**: relation -> arrow-key direction table (`orientation.tsx`).\n11. **One store API, three backends** (URL / local / cookie) — shareable vs private state.\n12. **Semantic tokens with light/dark values** (Chakra semantic tokens, `cssVarPrefix`).\n13. **Require whitelist** for user code and lazy dependency resolution.\n14. **Error boundary per handler** with reset and source/dist view.\n15. **Layout picker** with layout parameters as data (force, cola, dagre).\n16. **Full-tab URL for any (link, handler) pair** — deep linking into any view.\n17. **Editor = tabs + code + Preview/Handlers/Results**; drafts autosaved with debounce.\n18. **WYSIWYG for string values** with HTML serialization.\n19. **App shell itself as a handler** (perception `Layout` link with Auth/Status/ColorMode slots).\n20. **Per-value-type color palette** (deep 2025) as a theme dimension.\n21. **Link label template** (`id / type / name / value / symbol`) and **type Symbol** (emoji\n    icon per type) as default node rendering.\n22. **Radial context menu** for link operations; linear alternative for readability (#299).\n\n---\n\n## 9. Problems, bugs, limitations\n\nIssue numbers: `#N` up to #85 without prefix = [deepcase issues](https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase/issues);\nnumbers marked \"deepcase-app\" or above #85 = [deepcase-app issues](https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase-app/issues).\n\n**Architectural**\n\n- `eval` of TSX strings: no sandbox, full DOM/network access; whitelist only limits `require`\n  (deepcase #85 proposes renaming to \"unsafe\" handlers and adding safe ones).\n- Handlers tied to React + Chakra + browser; no React Native / Swift / Kotlin path.\n- Handler dependency resolution and paths (#60, #63, #64 `import.meta`), MUI in handlers (#72/#74).\n- Graph styles live in Cytoscape stylesheets, outside theme tokens -> dark/light mismatches\n  (#22 icons disappear in dark mode; deepcase-app #234/#80/#296 light-theme readability).\n- No label LOD: tiny/overlapping text is rendered (#37, #47); no pagination (#36).\n- Performance: too many re-renders (#65), slow/crashes after 24 h (#24), freezes/white screen\n  (deepcase-app #226/#123), iPadOS nodes disappear (#235), edges disappear when moving (#320).\n\n**Layout**\n\n- d3-force with `infinite: true` is unstable and wanders (#51, #52, deepcase-app #269/#218/#191);\n  cola cannot accept positions (#27); auto-place over the whole screen requested (#56);\n  Any-Any link treated as node (#28).\n\n**Windows**\n\n- deepcase-app: z-index of handler window over modal (deepcase-app #290); handler not fully visible in preview\n  (#297), handler not reopened / freeze with duplicate handlers (#282/#281); deepcase: handler\n  link floats (#53), double click opens twice (#30); remember last opened handler (#292); draggable\n  widget header requested (#198).\n\n**Editor**\n\n- State/tab bugs (deepcase-app #243, #238, #231, #178, #171, #170, #138, #137, #240), random\n  links opened (#45), splitter not remembered (#54), code lost when switching tabs (#43),\n  links unsorted (#84), no warn-before-update (#44), cannot set empty string (#35), clicking a\n  code file runs it (#3).\n\n**UX**\n\n- deepcase-app: rotated radial menu text unreadable (#299); browser context menu conflicts (#57/#87/#95);\n  search case / trailing space bugs (#110/#99/#245); drag & drop broken (#293).\n- Requested: user-configurable themes (#300, #247) and backgrounds/animated handlers (#301),\n  multilingual UI (#274), linear.app-style keyboard (#228), graph aggregation / filters / time\n  sort / PNG-PDF export (#89, Linkurious/Ogma references), and in deepcase zoom-into-space (#82),\n  return to last space (#83), pinning (#41), graphical undo/snapshots (#8), 3D (#159), voice/sounds (#155-#158).\n- Build/OS: Vite/bun (#9/#10), many build/OS issues (deepcase-app #31-#41).\n\n---\n\n## 11. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n\n1. **Replace eval'd TSX with Links Notation component trees.** A handler becomes a LiNo tree\n   (element / props / children / bindings) interpreted by per-platform renderers (DOM, React,\n   React Native, Vue, SwiftUI, Compose). The front\n  matter carries the key, title, issue type, labels, phase, the keys of the\n  blocking issues and the requirement IDs.\n- [`issue-footer.md`](issue-footer.md) is appended to every issue body. It holds\n  the conventions every implementer (human or AI agent) must follow.\n- [`created-issues.json`](created-issues.json) maps each key to the GitHub\n  issue number and ID. It is written by the creation script.\n- [`../../../../experiments/issue-1/create-roadmap-issues.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-1/create-roadmap-issues.mjs)\n  creates the issues (bugs first, then features in key order), resolves\n  `{{KEY}}` references to `#number`, adds the \"blocked by\" relations with the\n  GitHub issue dependencies API, attaches every issue as a sub-issue of the\n  tracking issue, and generates [`../../../ROADMAP.md`](../../../ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Rules used to cut the issues\n\n1. **Bugs first.** Every defect found while studying this repository is a\n   `Bug` issue with key `Bxx`. Bugs have no feature blockers, so they can be\n   done first and in parallel.\n2. **Features next**, keyed `Fxx` in delivery order. The key order is a\n   suggested order only; the real constraint is the dependency graph.\n3. **Parallel by default.** An issue is blocked only by issues whose output it\n   directly consumes (a package API, a file format, a deployed site). Shared\n   knowledge is a reference, not a blocker.\n4. **One reviewable pull request per issue.** An issue that would need more\n   than about 1,500 changed lines of source is split.\n5. **Written for a less capable agent.** Each body says why, what is in and\n   out of scope, which files to create, step-by-step instructions, checkable\n   acceptance criteria, exact verification commands, prior art and the\n   requirement IDs it delivers.\n\n## Issue body template\n\nEvery file in `issues/` uses these sections, in this order:\n\n```markdown\n---\nkey: F06\ntitle: 'ui-core: parse Links Notation into the UI element tree'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 2\nblocked_by: [F01, F03]\nrequirements: [R2, R3, R6]\n---\n\n## Context\n\n## Goal\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n### Out of scope\n\n## Dependencies\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n## How to verify\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n## References\n```\n\n## Issue list\n\n`Blocked by` lists the issues that must be merged first. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **One rule table per key**: `{default, min, max, unit, options, isColor}`. It drives normalization,\n   validation, the generated UI, CSS projection and tests. It translates naturally into a Links Notation\n   schema, e.g. `(liquid.blur: range 18 0 40 px)`.\n2. **Store the diff from defaults, never the full state.** Defaults can then improve for everyone, and saved\n   looks and share links stay small.\n3. **Project settings into CSS variables and `data-*` attributes on the root.** Theming then works without\n   any framework, and the same tokens can be emitted for SwiftUI and Compose as constant tables.\n4. **Run the same `normalize` and `apply` before first paint**, serialized from the real functions rather\n   than copied. There is no theme flash and no second implementation.\n5. **Comfort keys.** Accessibility and preference keys (reduced motion, sound, volume, transparency,\n   notation) are excluded from presets, shared links and randomization.\n6. **Looks as data.** Built-in presets, saved presets, import/export JSON, `#settings=` share links, and an\n   automatic \"Before the link\" backup when a shared look is applied.\n7. **Bounded randomization.** `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on heavy keys, so Random is safe\n   on slow devices. There is also an explicit \"Light and fast\" preset.\n8. **The settings page is the live preview.** Each row has a per-field ↺ reset and changed rows are marked.\n   There are section resets, a peek mode, a diff box with copy and paste, and sample tiles of every UI\n   element. Extending this to per-element editing gives the WYSIWYG configuration mode.\n9. **One source generates both CSS and preview tiles** (`skins.frames.js`), and a test fails if the\n   generated CSS is out of date.\n10. **One renderer for preview and export.** A single SVG string (`networkSvg`) is reused for PNG, JPEG and\n    WebP export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen. The same idea fits animation recording: record\n    the frames of the model, not screenshots.\n11. **URL state holds only non-default parameters** (`styleToParams`), with debounced history that pauses\n    while a slider is dragged.\n12. **Several synchronized notations of one model**, with typed-text preservation and bilingual errors. This\n    shows the framework's \"DOM-like language and Links Notation as two views of one tree\" in miniature.\n13. **Expensive layout in a cancellable worker**, with keyed results that cannot overwrite newer state\n    (`solver-job.js`, `useCollisionSolver.js`).\n14. **Performance governors.** The FPS governor degrades resolution and then fps, and `panelVisibility.js`\n    limits live `backdrop-filter` surfaces. Both belong in the framework runtime.\n15. **Owned, ARIA-compliant controls.** Select follows the APG patterns, numeric keys are shared, and popups\n    are portaled and clamped to the viewport. #39 says \"all UI elements must be owned by us\".\n16. **Declarative sound.** A `data-sound` attribute on any element plus document-level role mapping, so\n    components do not hard-code audio.\n17. **Language and theme stores built on `useSyncExternalStore`, with no provider.** This ports cleanly to\n    signals or observables in Vue, Swift and Kotlin.\n18. **Pointer-centred zoom with document-level listeners** and an infinite pattern grid (links-visuals #15,\n    #19, #21). These are designer-canvas basics.\n19. **Arc-length center anchors for links that point at links.** An anchor is pinned and re-resolved at\n    render time (`applyCenterAnchors`), which is the core of drawing associative links, not just node graphs.\n20. **Pure geometry and IK separated from rendering** (`ik-pure.mjs`), so they can be unit-tested and ported\n    to Swift and Kotlin.\n21. **A test suite per issue** (`*-NN.test.js`, `experiments/issue-N-browser.mjs` on three browser engines),\n    a case study per issue, and a hard 1500-line file limit.\n\n---\n\n## 6. [2026-11-01T11:46:40.770Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Architecture (proposal)\n\nThis document is the target architecture of the associative UI framework\nplanned in [issue #1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues/1). It is a\n**proposal**: every part of it is delivered by a roadmap issue listed in\n[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), and each roadmap issue may refine it. The evidence\nbehind each decision is in the\n[issue 1 case study](case-studies/issue-1/README.md).\n\n## Principles\n\n1. **Links first.** Every UI concept (element, property, style rule, design\n   token, theme, behaviour, data binding, animation, recording, configuration\n   override, asset licence) is a link in a links network. Links Notation\n   (LiNo, [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation))\n   is its only canonical text form. JSON, CSS, JSX, XAML, SwiftUI and so on are\n   import or export formats, never the source of truth.\n2. **One dialect.** Structure, configuration, styles, tokens, animations and\n   recordings use one LiNo vocabulary (the _UI dialect_), so any other UI\n   framework can be described as a LiNo document in that dialect.\n3. **Sharable by default.** A UI, a theme, a set of overrides or a recording is\n   a plain LiNo text that can be pasted into an issue, a chat with an agent,\n   or a URL.\n4. **Runtime interpreter, thin renderers.** One platform-neutral core\n   interprets the links network. Each platform (DOM, React, Vue, React Native,\n   SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose) has a thin renderer. Code generation is used only\n   for wrappers, types and optional \"eject to code\" exports.\n5. **JavaScript first.** As required by [`javascript-first.md`](javascript-first.md),\n   the JavaScript implementation and shared conformance fixtures come first.\n   Swift and Kotlin ports must pass the same fixtures.\n6. **Everything editable at runtime.** Every rendered element keeps a stable\n   link ID that maps back to its LiNo source. This is what makes the\n   development/configuration mode and the WYSIWYG designer possible on any\n   site built with the framework.\n7. **Public domain.** Code is released under the [Unlicense](../LICENSE). Our\n   own non-code assets are dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0).\n   Third-party assets are allowed only with a machine-readable record of the\n   source, copyright holder, licence (SPDX ID) and attribution text.\n\n## Layers\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph Sources[\"LiNo sources (sharable text)\"]\n    Doc[\"documents<br/>(structure)\"]\n    Tok[\"tokens & themes\"]\n    Sty[\"styles\"]\n    Ani[\"animations & recordings\"]\n    Cfg[\"configuration overrides\"]\n    Ast[\"asset records\"]\n  end\n  Sources --> Core[\"ui-core<br/>parse · validate · project · diff/patch\"]\n  Core --> Store[\"links store<br/>(in-memory network, transactions, undo/redo,<br/>IndexedDB / doublets-web persistence)\"]\n  Store --> Config[\"configuration layers<br/>defaults < theme < site < user < session\"]\n  Config --> Engine[\"style & token resolver,<br/>behaviour state machines, animation engine\"]\n  Engine --> DOM[\"DOM renderer<br/>(custom elements)\"]\n  DOM --> React[\"React adapter\"]\n  DOM --> Vue[\"Vue adapter\"]\n  Engine --> RN[\"React Native renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Swift[\"SwiftUI renderer\"]\n  Engine --> Kotlin[\"Compose renderer\"]\n  Store --> Dev[\"dev/configuration mode<br/>(inspector overlay)\"]\n  Dev --> Designer[\"WYSIWYG designer\"]\n  Dev --> Export[\"export overrides as LiNo<br/>(agent hand-off, share URL)\"]\n```\n\n| Layer ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Dialect specification | `docs/spec/`                                   | Vocabulary, grammar of the UI dialect on top of LiNo, conformance fixtures shared by every implementation.                         |\n| Core                  | `@link-foundation/ui-core`                     | Parse LiNo (via `links-notation`), project links into an element tree, validate against the dialect, format back, diff and patch.  |\n| Store                 | `@link-foundation/ui-store`                    | Mutable links network with stable IDs, change events, transactions, undo/redo, persistence (IndexedDB; `doublets-web` compatible). |\n| Configuration         | `@link-foundation/ui-config`                   | Layered configuration and overrides; export of overrides as LiNo patches.                                                          |\n| Tokens and themes     | `@link-foundation/ui-tokens`                   | Design tokens in LiNo; export to CSS custom properties, DTCG 2025.10 JSON, Swift and Kotlin.                                       |\n| Styles                | `@link-foundation/ui-style`                    | Style rules as links (selectors, states, responsive conditions) resolved against tokens.                                           |\n| DOM renderer          | `@link-foundation/ui-dom`                      | Reference renderer with custom elements and incremental updates.                                                                   |\n| Framework adapters    | `ui-react`, `ui-vue`, `ui-react-native`        | Thin bindings over the core and DOM renderer (React Native renders natively).                                                      |\n| Native ports          | `ui-swift` (SwiftPM), `ui-kotlin` (Gradle/KMP) | SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose renderers of the same dialect.                                                                         |\n| Components            | `@link-foundation/ui-components`               | Controls, layout, chat, charts, diagrams, links-network visualisation; behaviour as state machines described in LiNo.              |\n| Animation             | `@link-foundation/ui-animation`                | Keyframe/spring/timeline model, player (Web Animations API), recorder (timestamped LiNo events).                                   |\n| Dev mode              | `@link-foundation/ui-devmode`                  | Runtime inspector overlay, property editing, persistence, \"make these the defaults\" export.                                        |\n| Designer              | `@link-foundation/ui-designer`                 | Visual Studio-like WYSIWYG designer built with the framework itself.                                                               |\n| Converters            | `@link-foundation/ui-convert`                  | Importers (HTML/DOM, JSX/MUI, Vue SFC, Mermaid, Vega-Lite, Lottie, DTCG) and exporters.                                            |\n| Assets                | `assets/` + `assets.lino`                      | Own CC0 assets and third-party asset records with SPDX licences.                                                                   |\n\nPackage names are working names; the monorepo issue decides the final ones.\n\n## The UI dialect (sketch)\n\nThe samples below are in\n[`case-studies/issue-1/samples/`](case-studies/issue-1/samples/) and are\nchecked by [`experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-ui-dialect-roundtrip.mjs):\n`links-notation` 0.27.1 parses every sample and formats it back to an equal\nlinks network.\n\nA document (structure, configuration and behaviour in one place):\n\n```lino\n(app: document\n  (title 'Links UI demo')\n  (theme material3)\n  (body: stack\n    (direction vertical)\n    (gap (token space.medium))\n    (greeting: text 'Hello, links')\n    (ok: button\n      (label 'OK')\n      (variant filled)\n      (on press (navigate home)))))\n```\n\nTokens and themes:\n\n```lino\n(material3: theme\n  (extends base)\n  (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n  (token space.medium 16px)\n  (token motion.duration.short 150ms))\n```\n\nAnimation and a recording:\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n(recording-1: recording\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nConfiguration overrides produced by the dev mode (what a user hands to an\nagent with \"make these the defaults\"):\n\n```lino\n(user-overrides: overrides\n  (layer user)\n  (base app)\n  (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n  (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n```\n\n### Links Notation parse shapes\n\nThe experiment\n[`experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs`](../experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs)\nshows that `links-notation` 0.27.1 returns **different link structures** for\nthe same element depending on how it is written:\n\n- `(ok: button (label 'OK'))` on one line gives one nested link;\n- the same text split over several lines inside parentheses, and the indented\n  form `ok: button` / `  label 'OK'`, are returned by `Parser.parse()` as\n  expanded path links such as `((ok: button) (label OK))`;\n- `Parser.parseGroups()` keeps the indented form as an explicit tree.\n\n`ui-core` therefore defines one **tree projection** that accepts all three\nforms and produces the same element tree. The dialect specification issue\nfixes this projection and its conformance fixtures.\n\n## Configuration layers and agent hand-off\n\nEvery value an element uses is resolved through ordered layers:\n\n1. `defaults` — the component's own defaults (shipped in the package);\n2. `theme` — the active theme(s), which may be nested per subtree;\n3. `site` — the application's committed LiNo configuration;\n4. `user` — overrides saved in the browser (IndexedDB);\n5. `session` — temporary overrides made in dev mode and not yet saved.\n\nDev mode writes only to `user` or `session`. \"Make these the defaults\" exports\nthe difference between the top layers and `site` as an `overrides` LiNo\ndocument, a share URL, and a ready-to-paste agent instruction. The agent then\napplies the patch to the committed `site` configuration.\n\n## Development/configuration mode and designer\n\n- Enter dev mode with a keyboard shortcut, a `?ui-dev` URL parameter, or a\n  `<ui-dev-mode>` element. Sites can disable or restrict it.\n- Hovering highlights elements and clicking selects them. The inspector shows\n  the outline tree (links network), the property grid (resolved value plus the\n  layer it came from), styles, tokens, animations and the LiNo source.\n- The WYSIWYG designer reuses the inspector and adds a toolbox, canvas drag\n  and drop, alignment guides, multi-select, undo/redo, docked panels,\n  two-way source sync and a timeline. It is built with the framework itself.\n\n## Themes and other frameworks as LiNo\n\nA theme is a LiNo package of tokens, style rules and component templates\n(the XAML control-template idea). Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG-guided and\n\"classic\" themes (deepcase versions, konard.github.io styles, retro desktop\nlooks) are just alternative packages. Migration from MUI, Fluent UI, shadcn/ui\nand other frameworks is a converter plus a mapping table into the same\ndialect.\n\n## Platforms\n\n- **Web:** custom elements (plain JavaScript), React and Vue wrappers over the\n  same core.\n- **React Native:** a renderer that maps dialect elements to React Native\n  primitives (New Architecture).\n- **Swift:** a SwiftPM package with a SwiftUI renderer. It reads LiNo with a\n  Swift parser (an upstream `links-notation` port, or a port created by the\n  roadmap if none exists).\n- **Kotlin:** a Gradle/Kotlin Multiplatform package with a Jetpack Compose /\n  Compose Multiplatform renderer, with the same parser condition.\n\nAll implementations run the shared conformance fixtures from `docs/spec/`.\n\n## Associative technology stack usage\n\n| Component                                                                     | Use in this framework                                                    |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)           | Canonical text format; parser and formatter for every implementation.    |\n| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)   | Strict encoding and decoding of object-shaped configuration.             |\n| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)           | CLI, environment and `.lenv` configuration of tools (converters, build). |\n| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)                     | Localisation catalogs for every component and the designer.              |\n| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)             | Lossless CST networks for importing source code (JSX, Vue SFC, HTML).    |\n| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)                       | Query and substitution conventions for selectors and patches.            |\n| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)                 | Compatibility target for browser persistence of the links store.         |\n| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) | Context-relative values (per theme, per user, per device) as a model.    |\n\nThe full mapping, including which Build on these (permissive, healthy, aligned)\n\n1. **Links Notation as the single source of truth**, with lossless conversion\n to the closest standard in each domain:\n - **DTCG 2025.10** for tokens (via **Style Dictionary** transforms to CSS,\n Swift, Kotlin and JS);\n - **WAAPI / Lottie** for animation;\n - **Vega-Lite** for charts;\n - **Mermaid / DOT** for diagrams;\n - **A2UI / Adaptive Cards / JSON Forms** for UI trees;\n - **Custom Elements Manifest** for component metadata.\n\n \"Every other framework is just LiNo\" then becomes concrete: each one has an\n importer and exporter.\n\n2. **Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements)** as the reference\n vanilla-JS renderer. Generate **React and Vue wrappers** with a Stencil-like\n output-target approach, so one implementation serves all web frameworks.\n3. **Zag.js-style state machines** (adopt Zag.js, or reimplement its machines\n described in LiNo) for component behaviour and accessibility. Use **React\n Aria** and WAI-ARIA APG as the acceptance criteria. **Floating UI** for\n positioning.\n4. **Three-layer tokens** (reference → semantic → component), with\n **material-color-utilities** for palette generation. **Material, Fluent and\n Apple (HIG-guided) themes** plus \"classic\" themes as alternative token sets\n and control templates. Use **Ionic's modes** and **XAML control templates**\n as the model, and **Open UI** research for canonical component and part\n names.\n5. **Visualisation:** D3 modules plus our own LiNo chart grammar\n (Vega-Lite-like). Renderers: **ECharts** (broad charts), **Cytoscape.js**,\n **Sigma.js/Graphology** and **force-graph/3d-force-graph** (links networks),\n **xyflow** (editable node graphs, React), **Dagre** (default layout).\n6. **Animation:** our own LiNo keyframe and spring and state-machine model,\n compiled to **WAAPI / View Transitions**, **Motion** (MIT) on web, and\n SwiftUI and Compose natively. **rrweb** as an optional DOM-level session\n recorder. **Playwright** for turning recordings into tests.\n7. **Designer and dev mode:** our own, over the LiNo tree. Copy the panel\n architecture from **GrapesJS / Puck / Visual Studio**, the runtime-overlay\n inspector from **React DevTools / Live Visual Tree**, the variants matrix\n from **Xcode Previews / Storybook**, and the timeline from **Theatre.js**\n (design only). Use **Puck** (MIT) or **GrapesJS** (BSD-3) only for a\n throw-away early prototype if speed matters.\n8. **Native:** **SwiftUI** (SwiftPM) and **Jetpack Compose / Compose\n Multiplatform** renderers that interpret the same LiNo. **React Native New\n Architecture** (0.82+) with **Expo** for demos, and **React Native Web** to\n show RN components on the docs site. **Tauri** for a desktop designer shell\n that can use the Rust associative stack (`doublets-rs`, `link-cli`).\n9. **Assets:** our own icon and illustration set under **CC0-1.0**. Default\n third-party sets: **Lucide** (ISC), **Material Symbols** (Apache-2.0),\n **Fluent System Icons** (MIT), **Phosphor / Tabler** (MIT), **Health Icons /\n Kenney** (CC0). Keep attribution records in LiNo modelled on **Iconify's\n per-set metadata**, with **SPDX** IDs, a **REUSE 3.3** compliant repo\n (`REUSE.toml`), and **ScanCode** license scanning in CI.\n\n### B. Only interoperate with (import, export or optional adapter; no core dependency)\n\n- **Figma** (Dev Mode, Variables, Code Connect) and **Penpot** (MPL-2.0;\n DTCG tokens). Token sync and component mapping only.\n- **MUI, Radix, shadcn/ui, Base UI, Headless UI, Fluent UI React,\n Ionic.** Migration converters (theme to tokens, component-name mapping) and\n a **shadcn-registry export** so agents can install our components.\n- **A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms, DivKit, json-render.** Importers and\n exporters, plus learning their catalog and versioning models.\n- **Lottie / dotLottie** for animation exchange. **Mermaid / Graphviz DOT /\n Vega-Lite** for diagrams and charts.\n- **ELK.js (EPL-2.0)** and **Graphviz WASM (EPL)**. Optional, separately\n licensed plugin packages only.\n- **OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0)**, **Twemoji (CC BY 4.0)**, **game-icons\n (CC BY 3.0)**. Optional packs with the required credits.\n- **Skip** (LGPL libraries), **Capacitor**, **Electron**. Optional delivery\n routes.\n- **SF Symbols and SF fonts.** Reference by name at runtime on Apple platforms\n only.\n\n### C. Avoid (license or maintenance conflicts)\n\n- **GSAP.** Its \"Standard No Charge\" license is proprietary and explicitly\n forbids use in no-code visual animation tools that compete with Webflow,\n which is our designer. Webflow can also revoke or change the terms.\n- **tldraw SDK.** Production requires a license key (since 4.0), with a\n watermark on hobby licenses. Incompatible with public-domain redistribution.\n- **Theatre.js Studio (AGPL-3.0)**, the **Plasmic `platform/` code (AGPL)**,\n **ToolJet (AGPL)**, **Qt/QML** and **Slint** (GPL/commercial) as\n dependencies. Learn from their designs only.\n- **Rive editor and `.riv` as the core format.** Closed editor and format,\n though the runtimes are MIT.\n- **Remix Icon** (custom license since January 2026) and **SF Symbols / SF Pro\n / Segoe UI** (restricted) in any bundled package.\n- **Commercial-only libraries** (GoJS, yFiles, Highcharts, amCharts, AG\n Grid/Charts Enterprise, MUI X Pro, JointJS+, Remotion) in core.\n- **Material Web (MWC)** as a dependency, because it is in maintenance mode.\n Use material-color-utilities and the M3 token specs directly.\n- **Heavy code generation as the primary architecture** (lesson from Airbnb\n Lona, and Mitosis' slow progress). Prefer a runtime LiNo interpreter plus\n thin native renderers, and use codegen only for wrappers and types.\n\n### D. Reuse the standard\npanel architecture: Toolbox/Blocks, Layers/Outline, Properties/Traits,\nStyles/Tokens, a Timeline for animations, and Variants/States. Puck or GrapesJS\ncan speed up an early React prototype, but they must not become the source of\ntruth. Dev mode is a runtime overlay, like React DevTools combined with\nVisual Studio's Live Visual Tree. It requires every rendered node to carry a\nstable link ID that maps back to its LiNo source.\n\n\n## Recommendations\n\n### A. Build on these (permissive, healthy, aligned)\n\n1. **Links Notation as the single source of truth**, with lossless conversion\n   to the closest standard in each domain:\n   - **DTCG 2025.10** for tokens (via **Style Dictionary** transforms to CSS,\n     Swift, Kotlin and JS);\n   - **WAAPI / Lottie** for animation;\n   - **Vega-Lite** for charts;\n   - **Mermaid / DOT** for diagrams;\n   - **A2UI / Adaptive Cards / JSON Forms** for UI trees;\n   - **Custom Elements Manifest** for component metadata.\n\n   \"Every other framework is just LiNo\" then becomes concrete: each one has an\n   importer and exporter.\n\n2. **Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements)** as the reference\n   vanilla-JS renderer. Generate **React and Vue wrappers** with a Stencil-like\n   output-target approach, so one implementation serves all web frameworks.\n3. **Zag.js-style state machines** (adopt Zag.js, or reimplement its machines\n   described in LiNo) for component behaviour and accessibility. Use **React\n   Aria** and WAI-ARIA APG as the acceptance criteria. **Floating UI** for\n   positioning.\n4. **Three-layer tokens** (reference → semantic → component), with\n   **material-color-utilities** for palette generation. **Material, Fluent and\n   Apple (HIG-guided) themes** plus \"classic\" themes as alternative token sets\n   and control templates. Use **Ionic's modes** and **XAML control templates**\n   as the model, and **Open UI** research for canonical component and part\n   names.\n5. **Visualisation:** D3 modules plus our own LiNo chart grammar\n   (Vega-Lite-like). Renderers: **ECharts** (broad charts), **Cytoscape.js**,\n   **Sigma.js/Graphology** and **force-graph/3d-force-graph** (links networks),\n   **xyflow** (editable node graphs, React), **Dagre** (default layout).\n6. **Animation:** our own LiNo keyframe and spring and state-machine model,\n   compiled to **WAAPI / View Transitions**, **Motion** (MIT) on web, and\n   SwiftUI and Compose natively. **rrweb** as an optional DOM-level session\n   recorder. **Playwright** for turning recordings into tests.\n7. **Designer and dev mode:** our own, over the LiNo tree. Copy the panel\n   architecture from **GrapesJS / Puck / Visual Studio**, the runtime-overlay\n   inspector from **React DevTools / Live Visual Tree**, the variants matrix\n   from **Xcode Previews / Storybook**, and the timeline from **Theatre.js**\n   (design only). Use **Puck** (MIT) or **GrapesJS** (BSD-3) only for a\n   throw-away early prototype if speed matters.\n8. **Native:** **SwiftUI** (SwiftPM) and **Jetpack Compose / Compose\n   Multiplatform** renderers that interpret the same LiNo. **React Native New\n   Architecture** (0.82+) with **Expo** for demos, and **React Native Web** to\n   show RN components on the docs site. **Tauri** for a desktop designer shell\n   that can use the Rust associative stack (`doublets-rs`, `link-cli`).\n9. **Assets:** our own icon and illustration set under **CC0-1.0**. Default\n   third-party sets: **Lucide** (ISC), **Material Symbols** (Apache-2.0),\n   **Fluent System Icons** (MIT), **Phosphor / Tabler** (MIT), **Health Icons /\n   Kenney** (CC0). Keep attribution records in LiNo modelled on **Iconify's\n   per-set metadata**, with **SPDX** IDs, a **REUSE 3.3** compliant repo\n   (`REUSE.toml`), and **ScanCode** license scanning in CI.\n\n### B. Only interoperate with (import, export or optional adapter; no core dependency)\n\n- **Figma** (Dev Mode, Variables, Code Connect) and **Penpot** (MPL-2.0;\n  DTCG tokens). Token sync and component mapping only.\n- **MUI, Radix, shadcn/ui, Base UI, Headless UI, Fluent UI React,\n  Ionic.** Migration converters (theme to tokens, component-name mapping) and\n  a **shadcn-registry export** so agents can install our components.\n- **A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms, DivKit, json-render.** Importers and\n  exporters, plus learning their catalog and versioning models.\n- **Lottie / dotLottie** for animation exchange. **Mermaid / Graphviz DOT /\n  Vega-Lite** for diagrams and charts.\n- **ELK.js (EPL-2.0)** and **Graphviz WASM (EPL)**. Optional, separately\n  licensed plugin packages only.\n- **OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0)**, **Twemoji (CC BY 4.0)**, **game-icons\n  (CC BY 3.0)**. Optional packs with the required credits.\n- **Skip** (LGPL libraries), **Capacitor**, **Electron**. Optional delivery\n  routes.\n- **SF Symbols and SF fonts.** Reference by name at runtime on Apple platforms\n  only.\n\n### C. Avoid (license or maintenance conflicts)\n\n- **GSAP.** Its \"Standard No Charge\" license is proprietary and explicitly\n  forbids use in no-code visual animation tools that compete with Webflow,\n  which is our designer. Webflow can also revoke or change the terms.\n- **tldraw SDK.** Production requires a license key (since 4.0), with a\n  watermark on hobby licenses. Incompatible with public-domain redistribution.\n- **Theatre.js Studio (AGPL-3.0)**, the **Plasmic `platform/` code (AGPL)**,\n  **ToolJet (AGPL)**, **Qt/QML** and **Slint** (GPL/commercial) as\n  dependencies. Learn from their designs only.\n- **Rive editor and `.riv` as the core format.** Closed editor and format,\n  though the runtimes are MIT.\n- **Remix Icon** (custom license since January 2026) and **SF Symbols / SF Pro\n  / Segoe UI** (restricted) in any bundled package.\n- **Commercial-only libraries** (GoJS, yFiles, Highcharts, amCharts, AG\n  Grid/Charts Enterprise, MUI X Pro, JointJS+, Remotion) in core.\n- **Material Web (MWC)** as a dependency, because it is in maintenance mode.\n  Use material-color-utilities and the M3 token specs directly.\n- **Heavy code generation as the primary architecture** (lesson from Airbnb\n  Lona, and Mitosis' slow progress). Prefer a runtime LiNo interpreter plus\n  thin native renderers, and use codegen only for wrappers and types.\n\n### D. Confirm each in the repo's\n  LICENSE file.\n- Whether link-foundation standardises on Unlicense or CC0 for code. Check\n  `links-notation` and sibling repos.\n\n---\n\n## Sources",

Build on these (permissive, healthy, aligned)\n77\t\n78\t1. **Links Notation as the single source of truth**, with lossless conversion\n79\t   to the closest standard in each domain:\n80\t   - **DTCG 2025.10** for tokens (via **Style Dictionary** transforms to CSS,\n81\t     Swift, Kotlin and JS);\n82\t   - **WAAPI / Lottie** for animation;\n83\t   - **Vega-Lite** for charts;\n84\t   - **Mermaid / DOT** for diagrams;\n85\t   - **A2UI / Adaptive Cards / JSON Forms** for UI trees;\n86\t   - **Custom Elements Manifest** for component metadata.\n87\t\n88\t   \"Every other framework is just LiNo\" then becomes concrete: each one has an\n89\t   importer and exporter.\n90\t\n91\t2. **Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements)** as the reference\n92\t   vanilla-JS renderer. Generate **React and Vue wrappers** with a Stencil-like\n93\t   output-target approach, so one implementation serves all web frameworks.\n94\t3. **Zag.js-style state machines** (adopt Zag.js, or reimplement its machines\n95\t   described in LiNo) for component behaviour and accessibility. Use **React\n96\t   Aria** and WAI-ARIA APG as the acceptance criteria. **Floating UI** for\n97\t   positioning.\n98\t4. **Three-layer tokens** (reference → semantic → component), with\n99\t   **material-color-utilities** for palette generation. **Material, Fluent and\n100\t   Apple (HIG-guided) themes** plus \"classic\" themes as alternative token sets\n101\t   and control templates. Use **Ionic's modes** and **XAML control templates**\n102\t   as the model, and **Open UI** research for canonical component and part\n103\t   names.\n104\t5. **Visualisation:** D3 modules plus our own LiNo chart grammar\n105\t   (Vega-Lite-like). Renderers: **ECharts** (broad charts), **Cytoscape.js**,\n106\t   **Sigma.js/Graphology** and **force-graph/3d-force-graph** (links networks),\n107\t   **xyflow** (editable node graphs, React), **Dagre** (default layout).\n108\t6. **Animation:** our own LiNo keyframe and spring and state-machine model,\n109\t   compiled to **WAAPI / View Transitions**, **Motion** (MIT) on web, and\n110\t   SwiftUI and Compose natively. **rrweb** as an optional DOM-level session\n111\t   recorder. **Playwright** for turning recordings into tests.\n112\t7. **Designer and dev mode:** our own, over the LiNo tree. Copy the panel\n113\t   architecture from **GrapesJS / Puck / Visual Studio**, the runtime-overlay\n114\t   inspector from **React DevTools / Live Visual Tree**, the variants matrix\n115\t   from **Xcode Previews / Storybook**, and the timeline from **Theatre.js**\n116\t   (design only). Only interoperate with (import, export or optional adapter; no core dependency)\n131\t\n132\t- **Figma** (Dev Mode, Variables, Code Connect) and **Penpot** (MPL-2.0;\n133\t  DTCG tokens). Token sync and component mapping only.\n134\t- **MUI, Radix, shadcn/ui, Base UI, Headless UI, Fluent UI React,\n135\t  Ionic.** Migration converters (theme to tokens, component-name mapping) and\n136\t  a **shadcn-registry export** so agents can install our components.\n137\t- **A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms, DivKit, json-render.** Importers and\n138\t  exporters, plus learning their catalog and versioning models.\n139\t- **Lottie / dotLottie** for animation exchange. **Mermaid / Graphviz DOT /\n140\t  Vega-Lite** for diagrams and charts.\n141\t- **ELK.js (EPL-2.0)** and **Graphviz WASM (EPL)**. Optional delivery\n146\t  routes.\n147\t- **SF Symbols and SF fonts.** Reference by name at runtime on Apple platforms\n148\t  only.\n149\t\n150\t### C. Avoid (license or maintenance conflicts)\n151\t\n152\t- **GSAP.** Its \"Standard No Charge\" license is proprietary and explicitly\n153\t  forbids use in no-code visual animation tools that compete with Webflow,\n154\t  which is our designer. Webflow can also revoke or change the terms.\n155\t- **tldraw SDK.** Production requires a license key (since 4.0), with a\n156\t  watermark on hobby licenses. Incompatible with public-domain redistribution.\n157\t- **Theatre.js Studio (AGPL-3.0)**, the **Plasmic `platform/` code (AGPL)**,\n158\t  **ToolJet (AGPL)**, **Qt/QML** and **Slint** (GPL/commercial) as\n159\t  dependencies. Learn from their designs only.\n160\t- **Rive editor and `.riv` as the core format.** Closed editor and format,\n161\t  though the runtimes are MIT.\n162\t- **Remix Icon** (custom license since January 2026) and **SF Symbols / SF Pro\n163\t  / Segoe UI** (restricted) in any bundled package.\n164\t- **Commercial-only libraries** (GoJS, yFiles, Highcharts, amCharts, AG\n165\t  Grid/Charts Enterprise, MUI X Pro, JointJS+, Remotion) in core.\n166\t- **Material Web (MWC)** as a dependency, because it is in maintenance mode.\n167\t  Use material-color-utilities and the M3 token specs directly.\n168\t- **Heavy code generation as the primary architecture** (lesson from Airbnb\n169\t  Lona, and Mitosis' slow progress). Prefer a runtime LiNo interpreter plus\n170\t  thin native renderers, and use codegen only for wrappers and types.\n171\t\n172\t### D. Configurability model\n\n### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n\n`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n\n- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n  - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n  - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Unread line |\n| Misc. chat | `chat-pinned.js`, `chat-schedule.js`, `chat-poll.js`, `chat-wallpaper.js` + `wallpaper-css.js` (158), `chat-layout-trace.js` (86) | Pinned bar, scheduled messages, polls, wallpapers through `--wp-*` CSS variables, geometry-only diagnostics |\n| App chrome | `shell/app-shell.js` (270), `panel-resize.js` (97), `shortcuts.js` (237), `icons.js` (587), `dialog-focus.js`, `tutorial.js` | Responsive navigation, draggable dividers with keyboard control and saved widths, Ctrl/Cmd/Alt chords, Lucide-shaped line icons (ISC) in `currentColor`, focus traps, spotlight tutorial |\n| Appearance | `appearance.js`, `cloud-themes.js` (425), `ui-scale.js` (167), `effects.js` (265) | See section 3.2 |\n\n## 3. Patterns worth adopting\n\n### 3.1 Architecture\n\n- **Pure model, thin view.** Display shaping (`message-parts.js`,\n  `message-text.js`, `chat-model.js`) has no DOM and no React, so it can be unit\n  tested. In `link-foundation/ui` the same split should become LiNo-in, LiNo-out\n  transforms that every target (React, React Native, Vue, SwiftUI, Compose)\n  reuses.\n- **Injected `api`.** Every screen takes its data source as a prop. This is the\n  seam the WYSIWYG editor needs to render components against fake data.\n- **Links as the data model.** Messages, plans, graphs and replies are already\n  links stored as LiNo. A LiNo UI description sitting next to LiNo data is the\n  natural next step.\n- **The `el()` style without JSX** makes the component tree a plain function of\n  data. That is easy to generate from a LiNo element tree and easy to emit from\n  a code generator.\n\n### 3.2 Theming and configurability\n\nThe model: modes × skins × tokens.\n\n- `appearance.js` sets `<html data-theme-mode>` (system, light, dark, or auto,\n  where auto means light 07:00-19:00), `data-theme` (the resolved mode) and\n  `data-skin`.\n- Skins are `t3` (default), `telegram`, `whatsapp` and `signal`, defined at\n  `app.css` around lines 3310-3400.\n- Choices are stored in localStorage (`metaSovereignTheme`, `metaSovereignSkin`).\n\nThere is a semantic token layer:\n\n- General: `--bg`, `--bg-elev`, `--bg-input`, `--bg-active`, `--border`,\n  `--text`, `--text-muted`, `--text-subtle`, `--accent`, `--accent-fill`,\n  `--accent-bg`, `--danger`, `--link`, `--shadow`.\n- Sizing: `--control-h: 2.25rem`, `--control-gap`, `--control-pad`,\n  `--radius: 8px`, `--topbar-h`, `--bottom-nav-h`,\n  `--safe-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.\n- Chat: `--chat-bg`, `--chat-sidebar`, `--chat-accent`, `--bubble-in` /\n  `-text` / `-pad`, `--bubble-out` / `-text`, `--bubble-radius` (Telegram 15px,\n  WhatsApp 7.5px, Signal 18px), `--bubble-tail`.\n\nThis is effectively the issue's \"themes that reproduce classical UIs\", in its\nfirst form. These token names are the seed vocabulary for the LiNo theme\nformat (see `links-notation-ecosystem.md` section 6.3).\n\nOther patterns in the same area:\n\n- **Accessible accents.** Filled accents are darkened to keep 4.5:1 contrast,\n  and shared filled-control tokens fixed white-on-white failures across badges,\n  tabs and Mini App buttons (`docs/DELIVERY-AUDIT.md`).\n- **Runtime themes from data.** `cloud-themes.js` maps a Telegram cloud\n  theme's colours (accent, outgoing bubble, light or dark) onto the CSS tokens.\n  In other words, theme application is already \"data in, token overrides out\".\n- **Scale through rem.** `ui-scale.js` sets the `<html>` font-size to 100-200 %\n  and a separate message text size. Everything is sized in rem, so one knob\n  scales the whole UI.\n- **Adaptive effects.** `effects.js` runs a bounded frame-time probe and sets\n  `<html data-effects=\"reduced\">` on slow GPUs. It also honours\n  `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-reduced-transparency` and\n  `prefers-color-scheme`.\n- **Wallpapers as data.** `{ kind: 'none' | 'telegram' | 'file' }` is turned\n  into `--wp-*` variables by a pure function.\n\n### 3.3 Performance\n\n- The chat list uses a **measured virtual list** with binary-search offsets\n  and one screen of overscan, plus `content-visibility: auto` and\n  `contain-intrinsic-size`.\n- **Paged history**, store first and network second:\n  - pages are read from the local store before the network (Telegram)\n  - a priority prefetch queue (`PAGE_SIZE 50`, `PREFETCH_SIZE 30`,\n    `PREFETCH_QUEUE 40`, `STALL_MS 5000`, `HOLD_MS 30000`)\n  - unread chats are prefetched\n  - when jumping far back, a `ceiling` keeps newer messages from showing above\n    a gap\n- **Avatars.**\n  - Read-ahead covers one viewport, with at most two uncached loads at once.\n  - The URL cache is limited to 512 entries.\n  - Initials are the fallback, so there are no spinner storms\n    (`docs/UI-STATES.md`).\n- **Optimistic sends.** The pending bubble and directory preview update at\n  once, and an outbox with a stable `clientId` handles retries.\n- The **geometry-only layout trace** (`chat-layout-trace.js`) records\n  diagnostics without logging message text.\n\n### 3.4 Interaction rules worth codifying\n\nThese come from `docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md`:\n\n- Local and immediate interactions.\n- A context-menu target is distinct from a multi-selection.\n- Jumps load the history around the target and briefly highlight it.\n- A missing provider capability is never shown as success.\n- Keyboard parity: a skip link, visible focus, shortcuts that never steal plain\n  keys from fields, and focus traps in dialogs.\n\nThese rules belong in the framework's component contracts and tests, not only\nin one app.\n\n## 4. Duplication candidates (what `link-foundation/ui` should own)\n\n| Candidate | Today in meta-sovereign | Proposed generic component / module |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Design tokens and skins | Hard-coded in `app.css` (`:root[data-skin=...]`) plus `appearance.js` | `theme` links in LiNo, compiled to CSS variables and native themes. Skins become data files: `t3.lino`, `telegram.lino`, `whatsapp.lino`, `signal.lino` |\n| Virtual list | `chat-list-window.js`, part of `chat-window.js` | `VirtualList` (measured, bidirectional, anchor-preserving) |\n| Paged bidirectional history | `chat-window.js`, `chat-jump.js`, `chat-follow.js` | `Timeline` / `MessageStream` with `loadOlder`, `loadNewer`, `jumpTo`, ceiling, stick-to-bottom |\n| Message bubble family | `chat-message.js`, `chat-media.js` | `Bubble`, `ReplyQuote`, `ReactionBar`, `MediaTile`, `ServiceLine`, `DeliveryTicks` |\n| Composer | `chat-view.js`, `chat-composer-*.js`, `chat-attach.js`, `chat-voice.js`, `chat-emoji.js` | `Composer` with slots (attach, emoji, voice) and an auto-grow `TextArea` with a reserved-space contract |\n| Rich text | `message-text.js`, `rich-text-nodes.js` | `RichText` driven by an entity list (offsets are UTF-16 code units) |\n| Context menu and selection | `chat-selection.js`, `chat-drag.js`, `menuPlace()` | `ContextMenu` (placement maths), `SelectionModel` (range and drag) |\n| Date separators and calendar | `chat-days.js` | `DaySeparator`, `StickyDate`, `CalendarPicker` |\n| Resizable panes | `panel-resize.js` | `Split` / `ResizeHandle` with keyboard control and persistence (the `split` element in the LiNo sketch) |\n| Responsive shell | `shell/app-shell.js` | `AppShell` with Material 3 breakpoints (bottom bar, rail, drawer) |\n| Scale and effects | `ui-scale.js`, `effects.js` | Framework-level `Settings` for scale, motion and transparency |\n| Icons | `icons.js` (Lucide shapes, ISC) | Icon registry addressed by name. Use a public-domain set, as the issue asks: Lucide is ISC, not public domain |\n| i18n | `i18n.js` plus JSON locales | Replace with lino-i18n (`.lino` catalogues, React adapter) |\n| Settings persistence | localStorage keys per feature | One LiNo settings document resolved through lino-arguments (defaults, file, user) |\n\n## 5. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 5.1 From the issue tracker\n\n<https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues>: 25 issues, 1 open,\nand 30 PRs. The UI-related issues and their state:\n\n- [#25](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/25) asked for:\n  - mobile-first design\n  - full translation\n  - a dedicated connections page\n  - a tutorial based on real UI elements\n  - Apple-glass translucency\n  - **Chakra UI + React**\n\n  It was closed by PR #26 (mobile-first shell, Connections, tutorial spotlight),\n  but Chakra UI was not adopted. The UI stayed hand-written CSS.\n- [#27](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/27): \"simplify\n  the UI, and reduce repeating ourselves (DRY in code and UI/UX)\". The author\n  writes that the earlier vision was \"partially ignored\". This is direct\n  evidence of the duplication problem that a shared component framework should\n  solve.\n- [#10](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/10) (hide\n  empty sections) and [#13](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/13)\n  (tutorial progress lost after refresh, fixed in PR #14) are UI-state\n  persistence bugs.\n- [#18](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/18): i18n was\n  added later rather than designed in. Strings were retrofitted.\n- [#42](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/issues/42) (open)\n  is about provider coverage, not UI.\n\n### 5.2 Observed in the code and docs\n\n1. **CSS monolith.** `app.css` has 13.8k lines and about 200 `!important` lines, plus\n   overrides that depend on order. Some skin rules sit thousands of lines away\n   from their definitions, for example\n   `:root[data-theme='dark'][data-skin='t3']` at around line 13,589 versus the\n   skin block at around line 3,317. There is no scoping (no CSS modules or\n   layers), and the tokens are not machine-readable outside CSS.\n2. **Skins are code, not data.** A new classical theme requires CSS edits in\n   several places. Users cannot share or edit skins as files. Preferences live\n   in scattered localStorage keys, not in LiNo, which contradicts the project's\n   own \"everything is links\" model.\n3. **Bundle size.** `app.min.js` is 4.6 MB, committed, and served whole. There\n   is no route-level code splitting, even though KaTeX, lottie-web and the\n   emoji and sticker panels are heavy and rarely used.\n4. **Platform reach.** Mobile is a Capacitor WebView around the same bundle:\n   - no native components\n   - no React Native, Swift or Kotlin UI, all of which the issue asks for\n\n   Desktop is Electron 45. Both inherit the web bundle's size and performance.\n5. **Fragile layout areas.** These need dedicated fixes and regressions, which\n   shows how hard they are to get right:\n   - floating composer clearance and overlap at the live tail\n   - typing / header overlap (`docs/DELIVERY-2026-10-31.md`)\n   - WebKit `ResizeObserver` loops (`chat-composer-height.js`)\n   - white-on-white selection controls (`docs/DELIVERY-AUDIT.md`)\n6. **Tight coupling to Telegram semantics.** Bubble, media and selection\n   components encode Telegram concepts directly (`msg:telegram:*`, entities,\n   topics, `.tgs`). Other providers get Telegram's shape. A framework needs\n   provider-neutral component contracts, with capabilities passed as data.\n7. **Licensing.**\n   - Behaviour is \"learned, never copied\" from GPL/AGPL clients (tweb,\n     telegram-tt, tdesktop, Signal, Element).\n   - Icons are Lucide (ISC).\n   - Neither is public domain. The framework must source public-domain assets\n     separately, as the issue requires.\n8. **Server limits.** The Rust server crates are `publish = false`, with server\n   state in memory. The npm package is not published, so other projects cannot\n   reuse any component today.\n9. **No visual editor.** Appearance is changed only through settings panels.\n   There is no inspector, no live token editing and no dev/config overlay.\n   These are features the issue explicitly wants (WYSIWYG, dev/config mode).\n\n## 6. Migration notes (meta-sovereign onto `link-foundation/ui`)\n\n1. **Tokens first, with zero visual change.**\n   - Extract the ~60 custom properties and the four skin blocks from\n     `app.css` into `themes/*.lino` (token names unchanged).\n   - Generate a CSS file of `:root[data-skin=...][data-theme=...]` variables\n     from them.\n   - meta-sovereign keeps its existing selectors. Only the source of truth\n     moves.\n\n   Validate with the existing Playwright pixel and contrast checks.\n2. **Settings as LiNo.**\n   - Replace the localStorage keys (`metaSovereignTheme`, `metaSovereignSkin`,\n     scale, effects, locale) with one settings link, resolved with\n     lino-arguments and stored in the existing lino store.\n   - Keep localStorage as a cache.\n3. **Leaf components next.** Extract the pure modules first, because they have\n   no DOM coupling and already have unit tests:\n   - `message-text.js` becomes `RichText`\n   - `message-parts.js` becomes a media model\n   - `chat-model.js` provides date grouping and delivery status\n   - `wallpaper-css.js`\n\n   Then extract `panel-resize.js` (`Split`), `chat-list-window.js`\n   (`VirtualList`) and `menuPlace` (`ContextMenu`).\n4. **Bubble and composer behind a provider-neutral contract.**\n   - Define `Bubble` / `Composer` props in a LiNo schema (capabilities such as\n     `can-edit`, `can-react` and `max-attachments` as data).\n   - Adapt the Telegram specifics in meta-sovereign, not in the framework.\n5. **i18n swap.** Convert `js/src/web/locales/*` to lino-i18n catalogues with\n   its CLI. Keep the `t()` signature through the lino-i18n React adapter.\n6. **Screens declared in LiNo.**\n   - Describe the shell and chat layout (`split`, `list`, `stack`) as LiNo,\n     rendered by the framework's React target.\n   - Keep the hand-written behaviour hooks (`useChatState`, `chat-window.js`)\n     as named behaviours that the LiNo document references, for example\n     `(behavior chat-window)`.\n7. **Constraints to preserve.**\n   - no JSX requirement (the `el()` style is fine for generated code)\n   - CSP-friendly: no `eval`, which lottie-web light already respects\n   - axe-core gating\n   - Chromium and WebKit e2e\n   - reduced-motion / transparency / effects switches\n   - rem-based scaling\n   - offline-first, immediate interactions\n8. **Risks.**\n   - 13.8k lines of CSS with order-dependent overrides. Migrate per area and\n     diff screenshots.\n   - Behaviour hidden in CSS (`content-visibility`, composer reserve) must\n     become explicit component props.\n   - The 215 chat modules change often, so\n     extraction should happen upstream-first with thin re-exports to avoid\n     long-lived forks.",
