Patterns worth adopting\n369\t\n370\t1. **One rule table per key**: `{default, min, max, unit, options, isColor}`. It drives normalization,\n371\t   validation, the generated UI, CSS projection and tests. It translates naturally into a Links Notation\n372\t   schema, e.g. `(liquid.blur: range 18 0 40 px)`.\n373\t2. **Store the diff from defaults, never the full state.** Defaults can then improve for everyone, and saved\n374\t   looks and share links stay small.\n375\t3. **Project settings into CSS variables and `data-*` attributes on the root.** Theming then works without\n376\t   any framework, and the same tokens can be emitted for SwiftUI and Compose as constant tables.\n377\t4. **Run the same `normalize` and `apply` before first paint**, serialized from the real functions rather\n378\t   than copied. There is no theme flash and no second implementation.\n379\t5. **Comfort keys.** Accessibility and preference keys (reduced motion, sound, volume, transparency,\n380\t   notation) are excluded from presets, shared links and randomization.\n381\t6. **Looks as data.** Built-in presets, saved presets, import/export JSON, `#settings=` share links, and an\n382\t   automatic \"Before the link\" backup when a shared look is applied.\n383\t7. **Bounded randomization.** `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on heavy keys, so Random is safe\n384\t   on slow devices. There is also an explicit \"Light and fast\" preset.\n385\t8. **The settings page is the live preview.** Each row has a per-field ↺ reset and changed rows are marked.\n386\t   There are section resets, a peek mode, a diff box with copy and paste, and sample tiles of every UI\n387\t   element. Extending this to per-element editing gives the WYSIWYG configuration mode.\n388\t9. **One source generates both CSS and preview tiles** (`skins.frames.js`), and a test fails if the\n389\t   generated CSS is out of date.\n390\t10. **One renderer for preview and export.** A single SVG string (`networkSvg`) is reused for PNG, JPEG and\n391\t    WebP export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen. The same idea fits animation recording: record\n392\t    the frames of the model, not screenshots.\n393\t11. **URL state holds only non-default parameters** (`styleToParams`), with debounced history that pauses\n394\t    while a slider is dragged.\n395\t12. **Several synchronized notations of one model**, with typed-text preservation and bilingual errors. This\n396\t    shows the framework's \"DOM-like language and Links Notation as two views of one tree\" in miniature.\n397\t13. **Expensive layout in a cancellable worker**, with keyed results that cannot overwrite newer state\n398\t    (`solver-job.js`, `useCollisionSolver.js`).\n399\t14. **Performance governors.** The FPS governor degrades resolution and then fps, and `panelVisibility.js`\n400\t    limits live `backdrop-filter` surfaces. Both belong in the framework runtime.\n401\t15. **Owned, ARIA-compliant controls.** Select follows the APG patterns, numeric keys are shared, and popups\n402\t    are portaled and clamped to the viewport. #39 says \"all UI elements must be owned by us\".\n403\t16. **Declarative sound.** A `data-sound` attribute on any element plus document-level role mapping, so\n404\t    components do not hard-code audio.\n405\t17. **Language and theme stores built on `useSyncExternalStore`, with no provider.** This ports cleanly to\n406\t    signals or observables in Vue, Swift and Kotlin.\n407\t18. **Pointer-centred zoom with document-level listeners** and an infinite pattern grid (links-visuals #15,\n408\t    #19, #21). These are designer-canvas basics.\n409\t19. **Arc-length center anchors for links that point at links.** An anchor is pinned and re-resolved at\n410\t    render time (`applyCenterAnchors`), which is the core of drawing associative links, not just node graphs.\n411\t20. **Pure geometry and IK separated from rendering** (`ik-pure.mjs`), so they can be unit-tested and ported\n412\t    to Swift and Kotlin.\n413\t21. **A test suite per issue** (`*-NN.test.js`, `experiments/issue-N-browser.mjs` on three browser engines),\n414\t    a case study per issue, and a hard 1500-line file limit.\n415\t\n416\t---\n417\t\n418\t## 6. |\n436\t\n437\t---\n438\t\n439\t## 7. Problems, bugs and limitations observed\n440\t\n441\t### konard.github.io\n442\t\n443\t1. **No license.** The code cannot legally be copied into a public-domain framework until it is relicensed\n444\t   (for example to Unlicense, like links-visuals and immortality).\n445\t2. **Links Notation is hand-parsed.** `parseLinks` in `edit.js` uses the regex\n446\t   `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g`, and `links-notation` is not imported anywhere in `src/`.\n447\t   It only accepts numeric doublets and does not handle nesting, names or multi-line input.\n448\t3. **Settings are JSON, not Links Notation.** This applies to localStorage, the `#settings=` hash, the\n449\t   diff box, and import/export. It contradicts the framework goal of representing everything in Links\n450\t   Notation.\n451\t4. **Bilingual text is hard-coded** as `{en, ru}` objects inside components, including long templated\n452\t   sentences in `NetworkEditor.jsx`. Adding a language means editing every component; there is no catalog.\n453\t5. **Configuration is global only.** The tokens style every element of a kind. There is no per-instance\n454\t   override and no element tree to select from, so it is not yet a WYSIWYG designer.\n455\t6. **React-bound.** The store, pages and controls are React components; only `apply.js` and `src/links/*`\n456\t   are framework-free.\n457\t7. **Open issue #47.** The top-left corner and the top and bottom edges are not transparent by default,\n458\t   although every other element is. These are still border/corner layering bugs from the #45 redesign.\n459\t8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n460\t   - #13: the rain sometimes scaled up too much on refresh.\n461\t   - #45: some border configurations clipped overflowing content or broke transparent backgrounds and\n462\t     selection.\n463\t   - CSS multicol was unreliable in Safari, so columns are explicit.\n464\t   - Safari needed a focus fix in `numericKeys.js`.\n465\t9. **Heavy generated CSS.** `skins.frames.css` is about 84 KB / 1067 lines, and a very large number of\n466\t   fields (hundreds) costs payload and maintenance.\n467\t10. **Repo weight.** About 372 MB, from case studies, logs and archives committed to the repo, so it is\n468\t    slow to clone. Sparse clones are needed.\n469\t11. **Migrations are ad hoc** (`before45()`, special cases in `normalize`). There is no versioned schema\n470\t    migration mechanism.\n471\t\n472\t### links-visuals\n473\t\n474\t1. **CDN at runtime.** D3 is fetched from `esm.sh/use-m` on every load. It does not work offline, it is\n475\t   unpinned and therefore a supply-chain risk, and it is not reproducible.\n476\t2. **Global mutable state** in `state.mjs` (module singletons with setters). Two views cannot share a page.\n477\t3. **Duplicated renderers.** `canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG markers and paths by hand, and the\n478\t   two can drift apart.\n479\t4. **A rAF loop runs every frame even when idle** (`animation.mjs`), which wastes battery.\n480\t5. **Inline CSS is copied into every HTML page**, with no theming. Markers are hardcoded black, and only\n481\t   grid.html and draw.html have colour.\n482\t6. **Experiments are not composable.** Each page wires modules differently, and `failed-attempts/` holds 76\n483\t   HTML snapshots instead of git history.\n484\t7. **Limits of the network model.** grid.html places links in cells without real references. Only draw.html\n485\t   has link-to-link anchors, and only to centers (no source/target-to-endpoint semantics, no layout engine).\n486\t8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n487\t   - #1/#3: start-point snapping.\n488\t   - #15: the grid was not infinite.\n489\t   - #19/#21: zoom failed away from the center because the hit area was the SVG; listeners were moved to\n490\t     `document`.\n491\t   - #23/#28: grid proportions were inconsistent with single-link mode.\n492\t\n493\t---\n494\t\n495\t## 8. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n496\t\n497\t1. **Licensing first.** links-visuals is Unlicense and can be ported now. For konard.github.io, ask the\n498\t   owner to add an Unlicense LICENSE before any code is moved. The sound engine and palettes are already\n499\t   Unlicense through immortality.\n500\t2. **Schema in Links Notation.** Express each RULES entry as links, for example:\n501\t   ```\n502\t   (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (unit px))\n503\t   (skin.name: (type select) (default glass) (options glass liquid futuristic))\n504\t   ```\n505\t   Then generate the JS and TS rule tables, and the Swift and Kotlin constants, from it. Store user diffs as\n506\t   Links Notation too: `(liquid.blur 24)`. Keep JSON import for backward compatibility with existing\n507\t   `settings` and `settings-presets` values and `#settings=` links.\n508\t3. **Keep the projection contract.** Write `--section-key` CSS variables and `data-section-key` attributes,\n509\t   and keep the before-paint injection for web targets. Native targets get the same normalized map as an\n510\t   observable store.\n511\t4. **Scopes.** Keep the user/document split (localStorage vs URL or `.lino`), and add an element scope so the\n512\t   designer mode can override tokens per node in the DOM-like tree.\n513\t5. **Controls.** Port Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip and numericKeys with their tests (`*.test.jsx`)\n514\t   as the first `controls` set. Keep WAI-ARIA APG behaviour and the Safari fixes.\n515\t6. **Links view.** Merge the K:src/links glyph, placement, collisions and render code with the L:js\n516\t   zoom-pan, grid, anchors and IK into a single renderer:\n517\t   - one marker set, with SVG and Canvas back ends generated from it\n518\t   - no global state; instance objects instead\n519\t   - D3 bundled and pinned, or dropped where `d3-force` alone is enough\n520\t   - an idle-stopping animation loop\n521\t7. **Parsing.** Replace the regex parser with the official `links-notation` package. Keep `configurations.js`\n522\t   (code and index maths, Burnside counting) as a pure utility.\n523\t8. **i18n.** Move the `{en, ru}` literals into per-language catalogs keyed by id, preferably in Links\n524\t   Notation, and keep `plural.js` rules per language.\n525\t9. **Themes.** Treat `glass`, `liquid` and `futuristic`, plus the 12 palettes and the corner/frame generator,\n526\t   as the first theme pack. Classic UIs (Windows 9x, Aqua and so on) become more theme packs on the same\n527\t   tokens. Fix #47-style corner and edge transparency in the generator, not in per-skin CSS.\n528\t10. **Animation recording.** Reuse the export pipeline: one model goes to a standalone SVG and then to a\n529\t    raster, over a timeline of settings and link diffs. The IK animation in links-visuals and the canvas\n530\t    backgrounds are the first recording targets.\n531\t11. **Process.** Adopt the per-issue test files, the three-engine Playwright runs, a case study per issue,\n532\t    and the 1500-line limit. Do not commit logs or archives, so the framework repo does not grow to hundreds\n533\t    of megabytes.\n534\t"

plus a preferred language |\n121\t| Mode | `chat`, `agent`, `fullAuto` |\n122\t| Thinking detail | `brief`, `standard`, `detailed` |\n123\t| Min message animation | Default 2 s; motion should honour reduced-motion ([#672](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/672) F3) |\n124\t| Reasoning knobs | temperature, guess probability, follow-up probability, definition fusion, blueprint composition |\n125\t| Misc | experimental OCR, location, assistant name, demo mode, diagnostics |\n126\t\n127\t### 2.4 Theming\n128\t\n129\t- **Tokens.** `--fa-*` custom properties are defined in `01-tokens.css`. Dark values come from `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback.\n130\t- **Selector counts.** About 248 `[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and 244 `[data-theme=\"light\"]` selectors across the CSS. Most dark overrides live in `06-dark-theme.css`.\n131\t- **Chakra bridge.** `theme.js` maps tokens 1:1, e.g. `fa.surface.card → var(--fa-surface-card)`. Chakra components therefore follow the same CSS variables without a parallel theme object.\n132\t- **Root-class composition.** Skins, chat styles, composer styles and icon packs are orthogonal root classes. The CSS combines them, e.g. `.ui-skin-glass.composer-style-glass-clear`.\n133\t\n134\t### 2.5 i18n\n135\t\n136\t- **Runtime.** `js/i18n.js` is an IIFE exposing `window.FormalAiI18n`. It calls `loadCatalogs([...])` and `createI18n({locales, defaultLocale:'en', fallback:['en']})`, then dispatches `formal-ai:i18n-ready`.\n137\t- **Catalog format.** Nested Links Notation blocks (`en` / `buttons` / `key \"...\"`) with `\"\"\"` multiline strings ([#117](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/117)).\n138\t- **CI checks.**\n139\t  - Key parity across all locales (`tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`).\n140\t  - A lint against hardcoded natural language ([#659](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/659), R379).\n141\t- **Gaps.**\n142\t  - `PUBLISHED_RUNTIME_SOURCE = \"lino-i18n@0.3.0\"` in `i18n.js`, while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n143\t  - The vanilla pages use their own JS `LABELS` dicts instead of the catalogs.\n144\t\n145\t### 2.6 Preferences & memory\n146\t\n147\t- **Preferences (`preferences.js`, 123 lines).**\n148\t  - A hand-rolled Links Notation reader/writer with root `demo_preferences` and indented `key \"value\"` lines. Booleans are stored as `on`/`off`.\n149\t  - API: `[REDACTED] {load, save, format, parse, STORAGE_KEY, ROOT}`.\n150\t  - Every page shares the `formal-ai.preferences.v1` key.\n151\t  - It does not use the `links-notation` parser.\n152\t- **Memory (`memory.js`).**\n153\t  - IndexedDB database `formal-ai-demo`, store `events`, root `demo_memory`, bundle header `formal_ai_bundle`, `LINK_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION \"0.2.0\"`.\n154\t  - Events are append-only. `EXPORT_FIELDS` include `kind`, `role`, `intent`, `tool`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `content`, `attachments`, `sentAt`, `evidence`, `accessCount`, `writeCount`, `conversationId` and `conversationTitle`.\n155\t  - It exports `formal-ai-memory.lino`. Import, reset and purge sit behind confirmations ([#196](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/196)).\n156\t  - It reports a `doublets-web` backend only if that global runtime is present.\n157\t\n158\t### 2.7 Web search component\n159\t\n160\t- **Ranking.** `getDefaultProviderIds()` selects the providers, and `mergeResults` merges their results with the `rrf` strategy and `removeDuplicates`.\n161\t- **Capture adapter.** Fetches `/fetch?url=…` from a configurable base (default `http://localhost:3000`, 2,000 ms deadline). On transport failure it falls back to a direct CORS fetch.\n162\t- **Output.** Results are pushed as evidence strings into the trace. [#153](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/153) asks for a unified, deduplicated search-result template.\n163\t\n164\t### 2.8 Accessibility snapshot\n165\t\n166\t- **ARIA.** About 89 `aria-*` attributes: `aria-label` ×26, `aria-hidden` ×14, `aria-pressed` ×11. Also 9 `role=status`, plus `radiogroup`/`menu`/`menuitem`/`option` roles and 2 `aria-live` regions.\n167\t- **Focus.** `:focus-visible` styles appear in `02`, `03`, `06` and `07`.\n168\t- **Reduced motion.** `prefers-reduced-motion` appears only 3 times, all in `04-message-content.css`.\n169\t- **Keyboard.** The resizer supports keyboard steps (40 px, 16 px with Shift).\n170\t- **Audits.** No systematic audit (axe or similar) exists in CI. Open bug [#447](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/447): the left panel cannot be scrolled with the mouse.\n171\t\n172\t---\n173\t\n174\t## 3. Associative tech stack usage plan for the UI framework\n240\t\n241\t| Component | What for in the UI framework | How (based on formal-ai evidence) |\n242\t|---|---|---|\n243\t| [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) parser | Canonical text form of every UI artefact: component trees, themes, tokens, skins, layouts, settings and recorded animations | Replace hand-rolled readers like `js/preferences.js` with the official JS parser. Keep a `.lino` file per artefact so it can be diffed and reviewed, as formal-ai does with catalogs, example prompts and memory exports |\n244\t| [lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec) | Typed (de)serialization of props, theme objects and config at strict boundaries | Use the codec's indented-format parser to validate on import, mirroring `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `associative_package.rs`. Run strict decoding on paste/import of themes or layouts, and canonical encoding on export so round-trips are byte-stable |\n245\t| [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) | All user-visible strings in every binding (JS, React, Vue, RN; Swift and Kotlin through generated tables) | Reuse formal-ai's nested and multiline catalog layout, `loadCatalogs`/`createI18n` with an `en` fallback, a ready event, CI key parity and a hardcoded-language lint. Forbid per-page JS `LABELS` tables |\n246\t| [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) | Layered configuration: defaults, `.lenv`, env, URL params and CLI flags, merged into a single UI config | Used today only at the Rust CLI boundary. In the framework, use it for the dev server/CLI and a small browser adapter that reads URL query and localStorage in the same precedence. Expose the result as one Links Notation config document (generalizing `formal-ai.preferences.v1`) |\n247\t| [doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web) / IndexedDB | Persistent store for UI state, WYSIWYG edit history and animation/interaction recordings | Copy the `memory.js` model: an append-only event log projected to doublets, IndexedDB fallback, and `doublets-web` reported only when present. Every WYSIWYG edit becomes an appended event, which gives undo/redo, replay and animation recording for free (matches #672 F4) |\n248\t| [meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language) | Lossless CST/AST of UI documents: component source (JSX/Vue SFC/SwiftUI/Compose) and markup | Use it as formal-ai uses it in `rust/src/coding/cst.rs` and `document_formats.rs`: parse, check a full match and reconstruct text losslessly. This enables WYSIWYG edits that write back to source in each binding's language, plus translation between bindings (as formal-ai's `js` to `ts` mirror does) |\n249\t| [link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli) query / substitution dialect | Selecting and rewriting UI links: theme rules, skin overrides, migrations, codemods | Theme and skin application becomes \"match link pattern, substitute values\", like `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `links_substitution_query/`. The native store (link-cli plus doublets-rs) can back a desktop or server-side design registry |\n250\t| [web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search) / [web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture) | Optional components: search box and results with RRF merge; page capture for previews or documentation | Ship as opt-in packages. Reuse the unified result template requested in #153 and the capture adapter's timeout and CORS fallback |\n251\t| [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic) (concept) | Context-relative values: a token resolves differently by context (theme, platform guideline, locale, density) | Model \"token X in context dark/iOS/ru\" as relative statements instead of flat override files; this addresses the 1,097-line dark override sheet |\n252\t| [transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer) (concept) | Transformations between representations: Links Notation to React/Vue/RN/SwiftUI/Compose | Vocabulary for binding generators; formal-ai's `substitution.rs` shows `.lino` rules rewriting link patterns |\n253\t| [link-calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator) | Optional: computed layout values and expression fields in WYSIWYG mode | Evaluate expression properties (e.g. `spacing * 2`) with an inspectable Links Notation trace |\n254\t\n255\t---\n256\t\n257\t## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n258\t\n259\t1. **CSS-token → component-library bridge.**\n260\t   - One set of `--fa-*` CSS variables is the source of truth.\n261\t   - Chakra semantic tokens point at `var(--…)` (`theme.js`).\n262\t   - The framework should generate both from one Links Notation token document.\n263\t2. **Orthogonal appearance axes as root classes.** Skin × chat style × composer style × icon pack × theme combine freely and are applied as root classes plus CSS vars. This maps directly to a \"theme = set of axis values\" model.\n264\t3. **Icon-pack abstraction.** Each action has a semantic name, mapped per pack (font name, short name, shape), with a `names` text-only fallback. Use this as the basis for public-domain icon handling.\n265\t4. **Priority-based responsive overflow.** `data-menu-priority` moves top-bar actions into the drawer as width shrinks. #388 asks for measured sizes; generalize this into a layout primitive.\n266\t5. **Collapsible sections with isolate.** An isolate button plus Shift+click \"expand only this\".\n267\t6. **Per-setting reset and reset-all** using a default-detection helper (`settingIsDefault`).\n268\t7. **Shared preferences contract** across separately built pages: one storage key, Links Notation format, `data-theme` on `<html>`.\n269\t8. **Natural-language interface commands.** The UI can be configured through chat (`interface-commands.jsx`), a natural fit for an associative, notation-driven config.\n270\t9. **Issue reporting with user context.**\n271\t   - A prefilled GitHub issue within the URL budget, embedding UI state (skin, theme, viewport, language, mode).\n272\t   - Use it as a framework-level \"report UI bug\" component.\n273\t10. **Append-only event log** for memory, giving export/import as `.lino` and destructive actions behind confirmation and export prompts.\n274\t11. **Quality gates in CI.**\n275\t    - i18n key parity and a hardcoded-language lint.\n276\t    - A UI-boundary lint (no business logic in view code).\n277\t    - Per-locale and per-theme screenshots.\n278\t    - A cross-org duplication scanner (`cross-org-duplication.yml`).\n279\t12. **Stable test hooks.** Systematic `data-testid` (`setting-*`, `composer-*`, `conversation-*`) and `window.FormalAi*` page APIs for E2E.\n280\t13. **Security defaults.** A strict CSP on static pages, DOMPurify on rendered markdown, Mermaid with `securityLevel: strict`, and cache-busting asset versions.\n281\t14. **Reasoning-trace presentation.** A hierarchical step view with fade gradient, last-paragraph preview and an animation budget; a candidate reusable \"process/trace\" component.\n282\t15. **Terminology rule.** Say \"links network\", not \"graph\" (#664), so the framework's visualization components use consistent vocabulary.\n283\t\n284\t---\n285\t\n286\t## 6. Duplication candidates\n287\t\n288\t| Duplicate | Where | Recommendation |\n289\t|---|---|---|\n290\t| `h()` hyperscript, `segmentedControl`, locale and theme resolution | `js/site-chrome.js` lines 13–15 state they are \"intentionally re-implemented here verbatim\" from `js/download/download.js` (line 752) | Single framework primitive (`SegmentedControl`, `ThemeChooser`, `LocaleChooser`) shared by all pages |\n291\t| Per-locale `LABELS` JS dicts | `site-chrome.js`, `download.js` | Move into lino-i18n catalogs |\n292\t| Hand-rolled Links Notation parsing | `preferences.js` (parse/format), `memory.js` (bundle reader/writer) | Official `links-notation` parser plus `lino-objects-codec` |\n293\t| Theme token values | `01-tokens.css`, `06-dark-theme.css` (1,097 lines of overrides), `landing.css`, download CSS | One token document → generated CSS vars for every page and theme |\n294\t| Icon mapping tables | `toolbar-icons.jsx` (three parallel tables), emoji glyphs in `glyphs.jsx` | One icon registry in Links Notation (action → per-pack glyph) |\n295\t| Chat UI per host | Web `/app/`, Electron wrapper, VS Code webview (#353 wants parity) | Framework chat components consumed by every host |\n296\t| JS → TS mirror | `ts/` generated from `js/` | Generate bindings from one source (meta-language) instead of mirroring |\n297\t| Theme applied to vanilla and Chakra separately | CSS classes vs Chakra components (#541, #550 bugs) | One component set; no mixed styling paths |\n298\t| Similar components across other link-foundation/link-assistant UIs | Settings panels, theme/locale choosers, issue reporters, chat composers | Flag for the cross-org inventory (see sibling research files) |\n299\t\n300\t---\n301\t\n302\t## 7. Problems and limitations\n303\t\n304\t1. **Monolith.** `application.jsx` is 1,445 lines with one `App`. Its predecessor `main.jsx` reached 9,269 lines (#951); a CI line budget and boundary lint were needed to contain it.\n305\t2. **Mixed paradigms.** Three styles coexist: React + Chakra (partial migration), plain CSS classes, and vanilla IIFE pages using `window.*` globals (`FormalAiI18n`, `FormalAiPreferences`, `FormalAiVendor`). There is no module graph across pages.\n306\t3. **CSS order dependence.** The 7 stylesheets must load in numeric order. Dark mode is a large override sheet rather than token swaps, which produces recurring \"element not themed\" bugs (#388, #541, #550).\n307\t4. **Version drift.** `i18n.js` reports `lino-i18n@0.3.0` while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n308\t5. **Limited locales.** Only en, ru, zh and hi. There is no RTL support or pluralization evidence in the UI layer.\n309\t6. **Accessibility is partial.**\n310\t   - No automated a11y audit.\n311\t   - Reduced motion is handled in a single stylesheet, even though animations (minimum message time, step reveal) are central.\n312\t   - The sidebar has a mouse-scroll bug (#447).\n313\t   - No documented contrast checks beyond a `contrast` skin.\n314\t7. **Mobile fragility.** Repeated mobile bugs: iOS accessory bar, focus layout, overflow and menu width (#108, #110, #112).\n315\t8. **Committed minified bundles** make diffs and reviews noisy (#953).\n316\t9. **No platform-guideline mapping.** Skins are named after looks (glass, material) rather than formally following Apple HIG, Material 3 or Fluent. Material and glass are approximations.\n317\t10. **No WYSIWYG configuration.** All configuration happens through the settings panel or chat commands; there is no visual editor or inspector.\n318\t11. **No animation recording.** Animations are CSS/JS timing only; there is no capture or replay of UI sessions, even though the event log could support it.\n319\t12. **Charts.** No chart components; diagrams rely on Mermaid only, and Mermaid rendering breaks on GitHub (#1190).\n320\t13. **Asset licensing.** Icon packs are third-party fonts (FontAwesome, Material Symbols, Bootstrap Icons, Ionicons, Remix, Tabler), not public domain. A public-domain-only framework needs its own set or a `names` fallback.\n321\t\n322\t---\n323\t\n324\t## 8. Migration notes (formal-ai → associative UI framework)\n325\t\n326\t1. **Phase 0: contracts first.**\n327\t   - Freeze the existing external contracts as compatibility tests: `formal-ai.preferences.v1` (root `demo_preferences`), `data-theme`, the `formal-ai:i18n-ready` event, `window.FormalAi*` hooks and all `data-testid` values.\n328\t   - The framework's config loader should read the old preference document and map each key (`uiSkin`, `chatStyle`, `composerStyle`, `toolbarIconPack`, `glassOpacity`, `uiLanguage`, …) onto framework config links.\n329\t2. **Phase 1: tokens.**\n330\t   - Express `01-tokens.css` plus the dark overrides as one Links Notation token document with context-relative values (light/dark/contrast).\n331\t   - Generate the CSS vars and the Chakra semantic-token bridge from it.\n332\t   - Delete `06-dark-theme.css` incrementally, verified by per-theme screenshot diffs (#672 F1).\n333\t3. **Phase 2: shared chrome.** Replace `site-chrome.js` and `download.js` helpers with framework `SegmentedControl`/`ThemeChooser`/`LocaleChooser` vanilla-JS bindings, and move the `LABELS` dicts into lino-i18n catalogs.\n334\t4. **Phase 3: skins as framework themes.**\n335\t   - Map `ui-skin-*`, `chat-style-*`, `composer-style-*` and `toolbar-icon-pack-*` to framework theme axes.\n336\t   - Add guideline-conformant skins (Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG/glass) to satisfy #557.\n337\t   - Keep the class names as aliases during the transition.\n338\t5. **Phase 4: components.**\n339\t   - Extract framework components in this order:\n340\t     - `CollapsibleSection`\n341\t     - `ToolbarButton` with priority overflow\n342\t     - Settings rows with reset\n343\t     - Composer\n344\t     - Message\n345\t     - Reasoning-trace view\n346\t     - Issue reporter\n347\t     - Links-network view\n348\t   - Keep each `data-testid`.\n349\t   - This also advances #951 (split monolith) and #550 (uniform components).\n350\t6. **Phase 5: storage.**\n351\t   - Back the framework's state store with the same append-only event-log shape as `memory.js`, so UI edits, memory and recordings share one exportable `.lino` bundle and `doublets-web` can be dropped in later.\n352\t   - Replace hand-rolled parsers with `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec`.\n353\t7. **Phase 6: hosts.** Electron and VS Code webviews consume the same framework package (#353 parity). React Native, Swift and Kotlin bindings reuse the token, i18n and config documents rather than the DOM components.\n354\t8. **Risks.**\n355\t   - Chakra coupling: the framework should own the tokens and treat Chakra as one optional binding.\n356\t   - The generated `ts/` mirror must be regenerated, not hand-edited.\n357\t   - The CI gates (i18n parity, UI boundary, line budgets) must keep passing throughout the migration.\n358\t"

19, 25, 26, 28, 31, 36, 39, 41).\n62\t\n63\t### 1.3 Links Notation usage\n64\t\n65\tNeither repo uses Links Notation. There are no `.lino` files and no `links-notation` dependency or reference in either repo. All configuration is TypeScript/JS objects, serialized as JSON to localStorage, to a URL hash (immortality) or to a downloaded `acs-config.json` (anime-avatar). Both formats are flat or two-level key/value maps, so they map directly to links (see section 9).\n66\t\n67\t## 2. Configurability model\n68\t\n69\t### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n70\t\n71\t`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n72\t\n73\t- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Examples: `PALETTES` (12), `SURFACES` (13 panel materials), `FRAME_STYLES` (9), `BACKGROUNDS` (21), `BACKDROP_GRADIENTS` (7), `FONTS`, `TITLE_STYLES`, `TEXT_EFFECTS`, `INTROS`, `CHART_STYLES`, `CURSORS`, `TABLE_STYLES`, `SCROLLBAR_STYLES`, `ENTRANCES`, `SOUNDS` (26). Id union types are derived with `(typeof X)[number]['id']`, so adding an option updates the types.\n74\t- **Reference registry.** `REFERENCES: Record<ReferenceId, {label, url}>` cites the design source of each option (Arwes, thegridcn, Soul Extract, glitchy.website and others). The panel renders these as links next to each axis.\n75\t- **Axes.** `AXES` has 49 entries:\n76\t  `Axis = ChoiceAxis {kind:'choice', options, display?:'buttons'|'select'} | ToggleAxis {kind:'toggle'} | RangeAxis {kind:'range', min, max, step, unit}`.\n77\t  The shared base is `{key, label, group, description?, sources?}`. `SETTING_GROUPS` defines 8 groups: Color, Panels, Type & text, Scene, HUD & charts, Controls & data, Motion, Audio.\n78\t- **Pure functions over the schema:**\n79\t  - `coerceAxisValue` and `coerceSoundList` validate one value.\n80\t  - `mergeSettings(base, raw)` accepts untrusted input and drops invalid keys.\n81\t  - `diffSettings` and `diffFromDefaults` compute what changed.\n82\t  - `parseStoredSettings` and `migrateLegacySettings` handle storage. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n83\t  - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n84\t  - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n85\t  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n86\t  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n87\t  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n88\t- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n89\t- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n90\t- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`--corner`, `--border-width`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`, `--font-scale`, `--chart-line`, `--bg-speed`, `--motion-scale`, `--bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n91\t- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n92\t  - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n93\t  - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `--fill` variable.\n94\t  - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n95\t  - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n96\t  - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n97\t- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n98\t\n99\t### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n100\t\n101\t- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n102\t  - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n103\t  - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n104\t  - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n105\t  - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.\n106\t  - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color and intensity.\n107\t  - Scene and cameras: `bg`, ground, `floorGrid`, `camera*`, a separate `svgCam*` set.\n108\t  - Toggles: `autoRotate`, `mirrorArms`, `showFPS`, and an experimental joint gizmo.\n109\t- `App.jsx` keeps cfg in React state, persists it to localStorage key `acs_B` merged over defaults, and keeps the view (`editor|tests|split|none`) in `?view=` and `acs_view`. It exposes `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}` so in-app tests can drive the UI.\n110\t- There is no schema. Each control is hand-wired in `Editor.jsx` using `Studio.Section/Row/Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle` from `ui.jsx`. Ranges, steps and labels live inline in JSX.\n111\t- Every `Section` has a randomize button and a reset button. `randomizers.js` implements per-group randomize and reset, and respects `ACS_BONE_LIMITS`.\n112\t- Config I/O: Export downloads `acs-config.json`. Import does `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(text)}` and reports errors with `alert`.\n113\t- Engine binding: `apply.js` `ACS_applyAll` runs every frame and pushes cfg into three.js state (pose merge, idle, gestures, look-at, expressions, blink, materials, grid, debug helpers). This is a declarative-state to imperative-scene reconciler.\n114\t\n115\t### 2.3 anime-avatar archive\n116\t\n117\t- `ConfigPanel.jsx` holds about 17 props: skin, hair, eye and clothes colors, blink interval, animation speed, idle and blink toggles, background, `detailLevel` 1 to 10, legs, 3D, shadows, LOD, scale, `modelUrl`.\n118\t- `useAnimationCycle({minInterval, maxInterval, animationDuration, excludeFromCycle})` picks a random named animation (idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised) on a timer.\n119\t\n120\t## 3. Animation and 3D\n121\t\n122\t### 3.1 immortality (2D UI motion)\n123\t\n124\t- **Text effects** (`textEffects.ts`): `revealOrder`, `decipherFrame` and `sequenceFrame` are pure functions of `(text, t, seed)`. A component only supplies the clock. This makes them deterministic, testable and easy to record. Ported from Arwes (MIT) and re-implemented from Soul Extract ideas (GPL, ideas only).\n125\t- **Entrances and staggering** are CSS animations scaled by `--motion-scale`. A fixed bug is documented in [case study issue-7](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7): `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels after the animation and made borders look glitchy. It is now `backwards`.\n126\t- **Backgrounds** (`Starfield.tsx`): 21 canvas renderers with `seededRandom`, `parseColor` and `useReducedMotion`. One background (\"resonance\") reacts to sound cues via `onSoundCue`, an event bus from `sound.ts`.\n127\t- **Pointer-reactive glow** in `Frame.tsx` writes `--mx/--my` directly on the element, with no React state.\n128\t- **Overlays** (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) use `pointer-events:none`. The old `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was replaced with a smooth breathing glow, a photosensitivity fix.\n129\t- **Sound as part of motion**: `sound.ts` has 10 UI events (hover, click, toggle, select, scan, open, close, type, intro, notify), up to 6 sounds per event, and random, cycle or layer modes. The bus is tone shelf, then compressor/limiter, then convolution reverb send, with pointer-positioned stereo. The AudioContext is created lazily because of autoplay rules. `throttledScan` limits repeated scan sounds.\n130\t- No recording or timeline. All motion is either CSS or a clock-driven pure function.\n131\t\n132\t### 3.2 anime-avatar (3D character motion)\n133\t\n134\t- **Clip playback**: three.js `AnimationMixer`. `retargetMixamoToVRM(asset, vrm)` in `animations.js` maps Mixamo bone names through `ACS_MIXAMO_RIG_MAP`, rebuilds `QuaternionKeyframeTrack` and `VectorKeyframeTrack` data, scales hips by rig height, and flips axes for VRM0.\n135\t- **Procedural gestures**: `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` in `gestures.js` is stateless and returns `{rot, exprs}` deltas.\n136\t  - Gestures are `ACS_GESTURE_PRESETS` (wave, nod, shake, bow, each with duration, expression and peak).\n137\t  - Moods are `ACS_MOOD_PRESETS` (`ampScale`, `speedScale`, expression, weight).\n138\t  - Easings are `ACS_EASINGS` (linear, sine, quad, cubic, easeOut, easeInOut, backOut).\n139\t  - Bell and sustained envelopes shape each gesture.\n140\t- **Additive layering**: [case study issue-28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28) established that all motion sources (pose, idle, gestures, look-at, text-motion, mouse force) add relative deltas each frame instead of replacing each other, which removes snaps at gesture start and end. `ACS_mergePose` sums pose and manual rotations, and `mergeExpressionDeltas` sums expressions.\n141\t- **Anatomical constraints**: `ACS_BONE_LIMITS` gives per-bone, per-axis ranges in degrees, citing range-of-motion references. `ACS_clampBoneRad` applies them, and sliders show degrees.\n142\t- **Gaze**: smoothed look-at follows the camera, the mouse or random targets, with a cone, saccades and separate eye and head shares.\n143\t- **Text to motion** (`textMotion.js`): a regex command table (slowWalk, run, happyWalk, stealth and others) maps to GR00T modes and procedural bone deltas, and declares resource requirements. `gearSonic.js` fetches real GEAR-SONIC reference motions (joint_pos, root_pos, root_quat at 50 fps) and a Unitree G1 MJCF/STL robot, and can call a backend.\n144\t- **Speech** (`ipaSpeech.js`): an English-to-IPA lexicon produces a phoneme timeline, which drives VRM mouth expressions and the jaw.\n145\t- **Text to model** (`textToModel.js`): a TRELLIS backend client. With no URL configured it returns `{status:'no-backend'}`, so the feature degrades cleanly.\n146\t- **Editing**: an experimental TransformControls joint gizmo (one joint at a time, hover or tap to switch, off by default).\n147\t- **Export**: GLB (`-edited.glb` via GLTFExporter) and SVG (`ACS_vrmToSVG` projects triangles with back-face culling and depth sort). The SVG export has its own camera settings.\n148\t- **Loading**: `modelLoader.js` handles glTF/VRM, FBX, OBJ, STL, PLY and MMD (PMX/VMD), including zip, rar and 7z archives (fflate and libarchive WASM). `ACS_normalizeModelURL` rewrites GitHub `blob/` and `raw/refs/heads/` URLs to raw download URLs, and `ACS_detectModelFormat` infers the format.\n149\t- **Archive demo**: CSS `@keyframes` (talk, breathe, headSway) on SVG parts, plus a parallel three.js part tree.\n150\t- **Recording**: absent. Screenshot or video export, custom pose saving and a scene editor are only listed in `ROADMAP.md`. There is no MediaRecorder use and no user-editable keyframe timeline.\n151\t\n152\t## 4. Assets and licensing\n153\t\n154\t### 4.1 immortality: zero-asset, cite-everything\n155\t\n156\t- It ships no images or audio. Everything is generated: canvas, SVG, CSS gradients, `feTurbulence` noise and Web Audio. Fonts are OFL `@fontsource` packages.\n157\t- Each option and each sound carries provenance. `OptionDef.source` points into `REFERENCES {label,url}`, and `SOUNDS` entries have `{character, sourceLabel, sourceUrl}`. Sounds have neutral names; the source names say what inspired them.\n158\t- License decisions are recorded per source in [`docs/case-studies/issue-7`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7):\n159\t  - Arwes is MIT, so code was ported with attribution in comments (`frameShapes.ts`, `textEffects.ts`).\n160\t  - Soul Extract is GPL-3.0, so only ideas were re-implemented and no code was copied.\n161\t  - thegridcn has no license, so it was used as a visual reference only.\n162\t- Library choices were weighed by size. Tone.js (about 77 KB) was rejected for plain Web Audio, and the Select was hand-rolled with downshift as the fallback. The framework should keep this habit of recording rejected alternatives.\n163\t\n164\t### 4.2 anime-avatar: per-asset metadata and conditional attribution\n165\t\n166\t- `ACS_MODEL_PRESETS` entries have the shape `{id, label, url, format, kind, credit, license, flipped?, attributionRequired?}`. Examples:\n167\t  - pixiv VRM1 sample and Seed-san: VRM Public License 1.0.\n168\t  - Alicia Solid: Niconi Commons, attribution required, `flipped`.\n169\t  - V-Sekai girl: \"See repository\".\n170\t  - Khronos Duck: CC-BY 4.0.\n171\t  - DamagedHelmet: CC-BY-NC 4.0.\n172\t  - Unitree G1: NVIDIA.\n173\t- `ACS_ANIMATION_PRESETS` (Samba and Mixamo idle from the three.js examples, Gangnam Style from V-Sekai) carry `credit` and `license: 'Mixamo terms (free use with your avatar)'`.\n174\t- `attributionRequired(vrmMeta, preset, animMeta)` in `Editor.jsx` decides attribution in this order:\n175\t  1. VRM `creditNotation`.\n176\t  2. The preset flag.\n177\t  3. The animation flag.\n178\t  4. A license-string heuristic (CC-BY, Niconi, \"attribution\").\n179\t     `AttributionOverlay` shows a credit on the stage only when attribution is required ([issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)). The Metadata section shows the loaded VRM meta.\n180\t- **Risks.**\n181\t  - `ACS_GF2_MMD_MODEL_ARCHIVES` hot-links about 70 proprietary SUNBORN Girls' Frontline 2 MMD archives from the publisher CDN, with license text \"Official GF2 Exilium art page download\".\n182\t  - DamagedHelmet is non-commercial.\n183\t  - The label \"pixiv VRM1 sample (CC-ish / VRM license)\" and the license \"See repository\" (V-Sekai girl) are not license identifiers.\n184\t  - Assets are loaded at runtime from third-party URLs (unpkg, three.js examples, GitHub raw). Availability and integrity are not pinned; there is no SRI.\n185\t  - None of these assets may enter a public-domain framework asset set.\n186\t\n187\t## 5. Patterns worth adopting\n214\t\n215\t1. **One declarative schema per configurable surface.** Declare every setting once as `{key, label, group, kind, options|min/max/step/unit, description, sources}`. Validation, defaults, the panel, presets, randomizer, diff, sharing, migration and tests all derive from it (immortality `AXES`). In the framework this schema should itself be a Links Notation document.\n216\t2. **Option catalogs with ids, labels, descriptions and provenance.** Derive types from the catalog (`(typeof X)[number]['id']`), so adding an option to a theme is a one-line data change.\n217\t3. **Store and share only the diff from defaults.** `diffFromDefaults`, plus a version tag (`v:2`), makes share links short, survives default changes and supports \"N customized\" counters.\n218\t4. **Treat all external config as untrusted.** `mergeSettings(base, raw)` coerces each value and drops unknown keys. Apply this to imports, URL hashes and storage (anime-avatar currently does not).\n219\t5. **Versioned persistence with intent-preserving migration.** Keep only what the user changed from the old defaults, so the new defaults still take effect.\n220\t6. **Comfort settings stay local.** When applying a shared look or preset, keep the viewer's accessibility and comfort keys (motion, sound, volume). Lock the same keys from randomization.\n221\t7. **Presets are partial overrides over a base**, with `isPresetActive` detection and source citations.\n222\t8. **Randomize and reset per group and globally, with an injected RNG**, respecting constraints (bone limits) and locked keys. This makes visual exploration safe and reproducible.\n223\t9. **Project theme state to `data-*` attributes and CSS variables** instead of re-rendering. This is cheap, framework-agnostic and works the same for plain JS, React and Vue. A test then checks that every option has a CSS rule (`styling.test.ts`).\n224\t10. **High-frequency visuals bypass the component tree.** Pointer glow (`--mx/--my`), canvas backgrounds and the per-frame `apply.js` loop write directly to the DOM or scene.\n225\t11. **Animations as pure functions of time** (`decipherFrame(text,t,seed)`, `ACS_gestureDelta(name,t,mood,easing)`). They are deterministic, so they can be recorded, replayed, scrubbed and tested. This is the natural basis for the framework's animation recording: record the clock and inputs, not the pixels.\n226\t12. **Additive animation layers.** Each source contributes deltas that are summed each frame, with envelopes for start and end, so nothing snaps (anime-avatar issue-28).\n227\t13. **Named easing and envelope catalog** (`ACS_EASINGS`, bell and sustained) shared by every animation.\n228\t14. **Domain constraints as data** (`ACS_BONE_LIMITS` in degrees, with references), used for clamping sliders, randomizers and gizmos alike.\n229\t15. **Reduced motion and photosensitivity by default.** Use `motionAllowed()` (the setting combined with `prefers-reduced-motion`), and avoid hard flashes, which is the reason the flicker was replaced.\n230\t16. **Accessible panel conventions**: a non-modal docked drawer, Escape to close, focus return, arrow-key tabs, `aria-pressed` toggles, `<output>` for ranges, an `aria-live` change counter, and a clipboard fallback.\n231\t17. **Accessible data twins**: every chart has a table equivalent, `role=img` and a text summary.\n232\t18. **UI sound theme** as a separate configurable layer: an event-to-sounds map, modes (random, cycle, layer), master bus, lazy AudioContext, throttling, and a cue event bus that visuals can subscribe to.\n233\t19. **Zero-binary assets.** Generate visuals and sounds procedurally so the framework's own assets are trivially public domain.\n234\t20. **Provenance on every borrowed item** (`source`, `sourceUrl`, `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired`), with license decisions recorded per source (MIT port, GPL ideas only, no license means reference only).\n235\t21. **Conditional attribution UI**: show credits only when the asset's metadata or license requires it, and always expose a Metadata/Credits view.\n236\t22. **Dev mode exposes a state handle** (`window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`) plus an in-app test runner that does not autostart, can be stopped and keeps its scroll position (issue #19). This fits a \"configuration mode\" well.\n237\t23. **View state in the URL** (`?view=`, `#ui=`), consumed and then cleaned with `replaceState`, and listening to `hashchange`.\n238\t24. **Graceful optional backends**: AI features return a typed `{status:'no-backend'}` instead of failing.\n239\t25. **URL normalization for user-supplied resources** (GitHub `blob/` to raw) and per-asset fix-up flags such as `flipped`.\n240\t26. **Case-study per issue** (requirements table, root causes, rejected libraries). Both repos already do this, and link-foundation/ui should continue it.\n241\t\n242\t## 7. Duplication candidates\n243\t\n244\tBoth repos independently built the same subsystems. They should become single framework modules:\n245\t\n246\t| Concern                   | immortality                                                    | anime-avatar                             | scene background and grid, archive petals                                | Background plugin interface                                              |\n260\t\n261\t## 8. Problems, bugs and limitations\n262\t\n263\t### 8.1 immortality\n264\t\n265\t1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n266\t2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n267\t3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n268\t4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n269\t5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n270\t6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n271\t7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n272\t8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n273\t\n274\t### 8.2 anime-avatar\n275\t\n276\t1. **No build step in production**: Babel standalone transpiles JSX in the browser on every load, React runs in its development UMD build, and dependencies come from unpkg without SRI. This is slow, fragile and unsafe for a framework.\n277\t2. **Global namespace modules** (`window.ACS_*`, `window.Studio`, `window.__acs`) with implicit load order in `index.html`.\n278\t3. **Monoliths**: `Editor.jsx` is 2381 lines in one component, and `apply.js` is 1316 lines. All styling is inline style objects, so there is no theming.\n279\t4. **Two divergent apps** in one repo (studio in `public/` and the archived Vite app in `src/`). The README mostly documents the archive, and the archive's 2D and 3D part trees (`components/svg/*`, `components/three/*`) duplicate each other.\n280\t5. **Weak config validation**: import does a shallow `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse}`. Nested `rot/scale/expr` are not validated, unknown keys persist, errors use `alert`. There is no storage version or migration, and the key `acs_B` is opaque.\n281\t6. **No schema**: ranges and labels are duplicated between `Editor.jsx` and `randomizers.js`.\n282\t7. **Licensing**: the proprietary GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, and vague license strings (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\"). The license-string heuristic in `attributionRequired` can miss cases.\n283\t8. **Bugs called out in [issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)** (since addressed): the Alicia model loaded back-to-front, GitHub `blob/` URLs failed, loading errors never auto-hid, tests autostarted and could not be stopped, the test log forced scroll to the bottom, split view was shown on mobile, and copyright was shown unconditionally.\n284\t9. **Bugs called out in [issue #28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/28)**: an unnatural wave, non-anatomical slider ranges shown in radians, and gestures replacing look-at instead of adding to it, which caused snaps.\n285\t10. **No animation recording** and no keyframe editing. The Mixamo retarget only plays existing clips. Pose, scene editor and video export are only on the roadmap.\n286\t11. **Open requests** show demand for more model sources and mocap: [#18](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/18) (VRoid Hub, CharacterStudio), [#21](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/21) (kalidokit), [#22](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/22) (webaverse), [#23](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/23) (airi), [#24](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/24) (GitHub miner), [#38](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/38) (feature parity with TheSashaDev/girl-agent). [PR #17](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/pull/17) (image-comparison e2e) is still open.\n287\t\n288\t## 9. Migration notes\n289\t\n290\t### 9.1 Representing both configs in Links Notation\n291\t\n292\tAn immortality axis declaration could become:\n293\t\n294\t```lino\n295\t(axis surface\n296\t  (label \"Panel material\")\n297\t  (group panels)\n298\t  (kind choice)\n299\t  (display buttons)\n300\t  (options gradient glass frosted solid transparent steel brass copper wood carbon holographic ...)\n301\t  (sources arwes gridcn))\n302\t(option glass (of surface) (label \"Glass\") (source arwes))\n303\t(reference arwes (label \"Arwes\") (url \"https://github.com/arwes/arwes\"))\n304\t```\n305\t\n306\tA user's settings would be the diff from defaults:\n307\t\n308\t```lino\n309\t(settings (version 2)\n310\t  (palette ares)\n311\t  (frame octagon)\n312\t  (glow medium)\n313\t  (surfaceOpacity 0.6)\n314\t  (sounds (click soft-tick glass-tap)))\n315\t```\n316\t\n317\tThe anime-avatar cfg, including nested bone rotations:\n318\t\n319\t```lino\n320\t(cfg (version 1)\n321\t  (model (preset seed-san))\n322\t  (rot (rightUpperArm (z -80)) (rightLowerArm (x -90)))\n323\t  (expr (happy 0.4))\n324\t  (light (key (color \"#ffffff\") (intensity 1.2))))\n325\t```\n326\t\n327\tThe asset provenance record:\n328\t\n329\t```lino\n330\t(asset alicia-solid\n331\t  (url \"...\")\n332\t  (format vrm)\n333\t  (credit \"DWANGO Co., Ltd.\")\n334\t  (license (spdx LicenseRef-Niconi-Commons))\n335\t  (attribution required)\n336\t  (fixup flipped))\n337\t```\n338\t\n339\t### 9.2 Steps\n340\t\n341\t1. **Port the `settings.ts` engine first.** Keep `coerce`, `merge`, `diff`, `migrate`, `encode/decode`, `applySharedLook` and `randomize` as framework-neutral pure functions, but read and write the schema and values as Links Notation. Swap the JSON share hash for a Links Notation hash and keep a JSON v2 reader for old links.\n342\t2. **Extend the axis kinds** to cover anime-avatar: `color`, `vector3` (bone rotation with per-axis limits and units), `map` (per-bone, per-mesh, per-expression), `list` (sounds per event), `asset` (URL plus format plus provenance), and `action` (buttons such as gestures and export).\n343\t3. **Add rendering hints to the schema** (`render data-attr|css-var|engine`), so `Shell`, the test assertions and engine bridges (`apply.js`-style reconcilers) are all generated.\n344\t4. **Generate the configuration-mode inspector** from the schema. It should merge `AxisControl` (a11y, sources, display hints) with the `Studio` kit (per-section randomize/reset, color pickers, chips, mobile full-screen drawer). Export `Editor.jsx`'s 22 sections as a large conformance test for that generator.\n345\t5. **Split `styles.css` into per-axis theme modules** keyed by `[data-axis='id']`, so each theme (Arwes HUD, glass, and later the classic-UI themes) is a separately loadable package.\n346\t6. **Animation recording**: build on the pure time-function pattern. A recording is a Links Notation timeline of `(at t (set key value))` and `(at t (play gesture wave (mood happy)))` entries, plus the seed. Playback re-evaluates the pure functions, so recordings are tiny, diffable and reproducible. Combine with additive layers and the shared easing catalog.\n347\t7. **Asset policy**: the framework's own assets follow immortality (procedural, Unlicense). Third-party assets need a mandatory provenance record (SPDX id or `LicenseRef-*`, source URL, credit, attribution flag, commercial-use flag) and a CI check that rejects missing or non-free licenses from the default catalog. Exclude GF2-style proprietary and NC assets from defaults, or gate them behind an explicit opt-in that displays the terms.\n348\t8. **Bindings**: the pure core (schema, store, codecs, easing, time functions, sound specs) should be a plain-JS package. React and Vue adapters wrap `useSettings`, the inspector and `Frame`. Swift and Kotlin bindings consume the same Links Notation schema and theme tokens, and implement native controls.\n349\t9. **Testing**: keep both repos' ideas. Add schema-to-CSS coverage tests (fixing the duplicated `CSS_AXES` list), a preset screenshot gallery, canvas fingerprinting and the in-app runner (no autostart, stoppable) as part of configuration mode.\n350\t10. **Do not carry over**: in-browser Babel, development React builds, unpinned CDN imports without SRI, `window.*` globals, inline-style-only theming, `alert`-based errors, and opaque storage keys.\n351\t"

This maps directly to a \"theme = set of axis values\" model.\n3. **Icon-pack abstraction.** Each action has a semantic name, mapped per pack (font name, short name, shape), with a `names` text-only fallback. Use this as the basis for public-domain icon handling.\n4. **Priority-based responsive overflow.** `data-menu-priority` moves top-bar actions into the drawer as width shrinks. #388 asks for measured sizes; generalize this into a layout primitive.\n5. **Collapsible sections with isolate.** An isolate button plus Shift+click \"expand only this\".\n6. **Per-setting reset and reset-all** using a default-detection helper (`settingIsDefault`).\n7. **Shared preferences contract** across separately built pages: one storage key, Links Notation format, `data-theme` on `<html>`.\n8. **Natural-language interface commands.** The UI can be configured through chat (`interface-commands.jsx`), a natural fit for an associative, notation-driven config.\n9. **Issue reporting with user context.**\n   - A prefilled GitHub issue within the URL budget, embedding UI state (skin, theme, viewport, language, mode).\n   - Use it as a framework-level \"report UI bug\" component.\n10. **Append-only event log** for memory, giving export/import as `.lino` and destructive actions behind confirmation and export prompts.\n11. **Quality gates in CI.**\n    - i18n key parity and a hardcoded-language lint.\n    - A UI-boundary lint (no business logic in view code).\n    - Per-locale and per-theme screenshots.\n    - A cross-org duplication scanner (`cross-org-duplication.yml`).\n12. **Stable test hooks.** Systematic `data-testid` (`setting-*`, `composer-*`, `conversation-*`) and `window.FormalAi*` page APIs for E2E.\n13. **Security defaults.** A strict CSP on static pages, DOMPurify on rendered markdown, Mermaid with `securityLevel: strict`, and cache-busting asset versions.\n14. **Reasoning-trace presentation.** A hierarchical step view with fade gradient, last-paragraph preview and an animation budget; a candidate reusable \"process/trace\" component.\n15. **Terminology rule.** Say \"links network\", not \"graph\" (#664), so the framework's visualization components use consistent vocabulary.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Duplication candidates\n\n| Duplicate | Where | Recommendation |\n|---|---|---|\n| `h()` hyperscript, `segmentedControl`, locale and theme resolution | `js/site-chrome.js` lines 13–15 state they are \"intentionally re-implemented here verbatim\" from `js/download/download.js` (line 752) | Single framework primitive (`SegmentedControl`, `ThemeChooser`, `LocaleChooser`) shared by all pages |\n| Per-locale `LABELS` JS dicts | `site-chrome.js`, `download.js` | Move into lino-i18n catalogs |\n| Hand-rolled Links Notation parsing | `preferences.js` (parse/format), `memory.js` (bundle reader/writer) | Official `links-notation` parser plus `lino-objects-codec` |\n| Theme token values | `01-tokens.css`, `06-dark-theme.css` (1,097 lines of overrides), `landing.css`, download CSS | One token document → generated CSS vars for every page and theme |\n| Icon mapping tables | `toolbar-icons.jsx` (three parallel tables), emoji glyphs in `glyphs.jsx` | One icon registry in Links Notation (action → per-pack glyph) |\n| Chat UI per host | Web `/app/`, Electron wrapper, VS Code webview (#353 wants parity) | Framework chat components consumed by every host |\n| JS → TS mirror | `ts/` generated from `js/` | Generate bindings from one source (meta-language) instead of mirroring |\n| Theme applied to vanilla and Chakra separately | CSS classes vs Chakra components (#541, #550 bugs) | One component set; no mixed styling paths |\n| Similar components across other link-foundation/link-assistant UIs | Settings panels, theme/locale choosers, issue reporters, chat composers | Flag for the cross-org inventory (see sibling research files) |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Problems and limitations\n\n1. **Monolith.** `application.jsx` is 1,445 lines with one `App`. Its predecessor `main.jsx` reached 9,269 lines (#951); a CI line budget and boundary lint were needed to contain it.\n2. **Mixed paradigms.** Three styles coexist: React + Chakra (partial migration), plain CSS classes, and vanilla IIFE pages using `window.*` globals (`FormalAiI18n`, `FormalAiPreferences`, `FormalAiVendor`). There is no module graph across pages.\n3. **CSS order dependence.** The 7 stylesheets must load in numeric order. Dark mode is a large override sheet rather than token swaps, which produces recurring \"element not themed\" bugs (#388, #541, #550).\n4. **Version drift.** `i18n.js` reports `lino-i18n@0.3.0` while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n5. **Limited locales.** Only en, ru, zh and hi. There is no RTL support or pluralization evidence in the UI layer.\n6. **Accessibility is partial.**\n   - No automated a11y audit.\n   - Reduced motion is handled in a single stylesheet, even though animations (minimum message time, step reveal) are central.\n   - The sidebar has a mouse-scroll bug (#447).\n   - No documented contrast checks beyond a `contrast` skin.\n7. **Mobile fragility.** Repeated mobile bugs: iOS accessory bar, focus layout, overflow and menu width (#108, #110, #112).\n8. **Committed minified bundles** make diffs and reviews noisy (#953).\n9. **No platform-guideline mapping.** Skins are named after looks (glass, material) rather than formally following Apple HIG, Material 3 or Fluent. Material and glass are approximations.\n10. **No WYSIWYG configuration.** All configuration happens through the settings panel or chat commands; there is no visual editor or inspector.\n11. **No animation recording.** Animations are CSS/JS timing only; there is no capture or replay of UI sessions, even though the event log could support it.\n12. **Charts.** No chart components; diagrams rely on Mermaid only, and Mermaid rendering breaks on GitHub (#1190).\n13. **Asset licensing.** Icon packs are third-party fonts (FontAwesome, Material Symbols, Bootstrap Icons, Ionicons, Remix, Tabler), not public domain. A public-domain-only framework needs its own set or a `names` fallback.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes (formal-ai → associative UI framework)\n\n1. **Phase 0: contracts first.**\n   - Freeze the existing external contracts as compatibility tests: `formal-ai.preferences.v1` (root `demo_preferences`), `data-theme`, the `formal-ai:i18n-ready` event, `window.FormalAi*` hooks and all `data-testid` values.\n   - The framework's config loader should read the old preference document and map each key (`uiSkin`, `chatStyle`, `composerStyle`, `toolbarIconPack`, `glassOpacity`, `uiLanguage`, …) onto framework config links.\n2. **Phase 1: tokens.**\n   - Express `01-tokens.css` plus the dark overrides as one Links Notation token document with context-relative values (light/dark/contrast).\n   - Generate the CSS vars and the Chakra semantic-token bridge from it.\n   - Delete `06-dark-theme.css` incrementally, verified by per-theme screenshot diffs (#672 F1).\n3. **Phase 2: shared chrome.** Replace `site-chrome.js` and `download.js` helpers with framework `SegmentedControl`/`ThemeChooser`/`LocaleChooser` vanilla-JS bindings, and move the `LABELS` dicts into lino-i18n catalogs.\n4. **Phase 3: skins as framework themes.**\n   - Map `ui-skin-*`, `chat-style-*`, `composer-style-*` and `toolbar-icon-pack-*` to framework theme axes.\n   - Add guideline-conformant skins (Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG/glass) to satisfy #557.\n   - Keep the class names as aliases during the transition.\n5. **Phase 4: components.**\n   - Extract framework components in this order:\n     - `CollapsibleSection`\n     - `ToolbarButton` with priority overflow\n     - Settings rows with reset\n     - Composer\n     - Message\n     - Reasoning-trace view\n     - Issue reporter\n     - Links-network view\n   - Keep each `data-testid`.\n   - This also advances #951 (split monolith) and #550 (uniform components).\n6. **Phase 5: storage.**\n   - Back the framework's state store with the same append-only event-log shape as `memory.js`, so UI edits, memory and recordings share one exportable `.lino` bundle and `doublets-web` can be dropped in later.\n   - Replace hand-rolled parsers with `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec`.\n7. **Phase 6: hosts.** Electron and VS Code webviews consume the same framework package (#353 parity). React Native, Swift and Kotlin bindings reuse the token, i18n and config documents rather than the DOM components.\n8. **Risks.**\n   - Chakra coupling: the framework should own the tokens and treat Chakra as one optional binding.\n   - The generated `ts/` mirror must be regenerated, not hand-edited.\n   - The CI gates (i18n parity, UI boundary, line budgets) must keep passing throughout the migration.",
