19, 25, 26, 28, 31, 36, 39, 41).\n48\t\n49\t### 1.3 Links Notation usage\n50\t\n51\tNeither repo uses Links Notation. There are no `.lino` files and no `links-notation` dependency or reference in either repo. All configuration is TypeScript/JS objects, serialized as JSON to localStorage, to a URL hash (immortality) or to a downloaded `acs-config.json` (anime-avatar). Both formats are flat or two-level key/value maps, so they map directly to links (see section 9).\n52\t\n53\t## 2. Configurability model\n54\t\n55\t### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n56\t\n57\t`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n58\t\n59\t- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Examples: `PALETTES` (12), `SURFACES` (13 panel materials), `FRAME_STYLES` (9), `BACKGROUNDS` (21), `BACKDROP_GRADIENTS` (7), `FONTS`, `TITLE_STYLES`, `TEXT_EFFECTS`, `INTROS`, `CHART_STYLES`, `CURSORS`, `TABLE_STYLES`, `SCROLLBAR_STYLES`, `ENTRANCES`, `SOUNDS` (26). Id union types are derived with `(typeof X)[number]['id']`, so adding an option updates the types.\n60\t- **Reference registry.** `REFERENCES: Record<ReferenceId, {label, url}>` cites the design source of each option (Arwes, thegridcn, Soul Extract, glitchy.website and others). The panel renders these as links next to each axis.\n61\t- **Axes.** `AXES` has 49 entries:\n62\t `Axis = ChoiceAxis {kind:'choice', options, display?:'buttons'|'select'} | ToggleAxis {kind:'toggle'} | RangeAxis {kind:'range', min, max, step, unit}`.\n63\t The shared base is `{key, label, group, description?, sources?}`. `SETTING_GROUPS` defines 8 groups: Color, Panels, Type & text, Scene, HUD & charts, Controls & data, Motion, Audio.\n64\t- **Pure functions over the schema:**\n65\t - `coerceAxisValue` and `coerceSoundList` validate one value.\n66\t - `mergeSettings(base, raw)` accepts untrusted input and drops invalid keys.\n67\t - `diffSettings` and `diffFromDefaults` compute what changed.\n68\t - `parseStoredSettings` and `migrateLegacySettings` handle storage. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n69\t - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n70\t - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n71\t - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n72\t - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n73\t - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n74\t- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n75\t- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n76\t- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`-corner`, `-border-width`, `-surface-opacity`, `-surface-blur`, `-font-scale`, `-chart-line`, `-bg-speed`, `-motion-scale`, `-bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n77\t- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n78\t - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n79\t - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `-fill` variable.\n80\t - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n81\t - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n82\t - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n83\t- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n84\t\n85\t### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n86\t\n87\t- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n88\t - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n89\t - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n90\t - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n91\t - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.\n92\t - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color and intensity.\n93\t - Scene and cameras: `bg`, ground, `floorGrid`, `camera*`, a separate `svgCam*` set.\n94\t - Toggles: `autoRotate`, `mirrorArms`, `showFPS`, and an experimental joint gizmo.\n95\t- `App.jsx` keeps cfg in React state, persists it to localStorage key `acs_B` merged over defaults, and keeps the view (`editor|tests|split|none`) in `?view=` and `acs_view`. It exposes `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}` so in-app tests can drive the UI.\n96\t- There is no schema. Each control is hand-wired in `Editor.jsx` using `Studio.Section/Row/Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle` from `ui.jsx`. Ranges, steps and labels live inline in JSX.\n97\t- Every `Section` has a randomize button and a reset button. `randomizers.js` implements per-group randomize and reset, and respects `ACS_BONE_LIMITS`.\n98\t- Config I/O: Export downloads `acs-config.json`. Import does `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(text)}` and reports errors with `alert`.\n99\t- Engine binding: `apply.js` `ACS_applyAll` runs every frame and pushes cfg into three.js state (pose merge, idle, gestures, look-at, expressions, blink, materials, grid, debug helpers). This is a declarative-state to imperative-scene reconciler.\n100\t\n101\t### 2.3 anime-avatar archive\n102\t\n103\t- `ConfigPanel.jsx` holds about 17 props: skin, hair, eye and clothes colors, blink interval, animation speed, idle and blink toggles, background, `detailLevel` 1 to 10, legs, 3D, shadows, LOD, scale, `modelUrl`.\n104\t- `useAnimationCycle({minInterval, maxInterval, animationDuration, excludeFromCycle})` picks a random named animation (idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised) on a timer.\n105\t\n106\t## 3. Animation and 3D\n107\t\n108\t### 3.1 immortality (2D UI motion)\n109\t\n110\t- **Text effects** (`textEffects.ts`): `revealOrder`, `decipherFrame` and `sequenceFrame` are pure functions of `(text, t, seed)`. A component only supplies the clock. This makes them deterministic, testable and easy to record. Ported from Arwes (MIT) and re-implemented from Soul Extract ideas (GPL, ideas only).\n111\t- **Entrances and staggering** are CSS animations scaled by `-motion-scale`. A fixed bug is documented in [case study issue-7](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7): `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels after the animation and made borders look glitchy. It is now `backwards`.\n112\t- **Backgrounds** (`Starfield.tsx`): 21 canvas renderers with `seededRandom`, `parseColor` and `useReducedMotion`. One background (\"resonance\") reacts to sound cues via `onSoundCue`, an event bus from `sound.ts`.\n113\t- **Pointer-reactive glow** in `Frame.tsx` writes `-mx/-my` directly on the element, with no React state.\n114\t- **Overlays** (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) use `pointer-events:none`. The old `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was replaced with a smooth breathing glow, a photosensitivity fix.\n115\t- **Sound as part of motion**: `sound.ts` has 10 UI events (hover, click, toggle, select, scan, open, close, type, intro, notify), up to 6 sounds per event, and random, cycle or layer modes. The bus is tone shelf, then compressor/limiter, then convolution reverb send, with pointer-positioned stereo. The AudioContext is created lazily because of autoplay rules. `throttledScan` limits repeated scan sounds.\n116\t- No recording or timeline. All motion is either CSS or a clock-driven pure function.\n117\t\n118\t### 3.2 anime-avatar (3D character motion)\n119\t\n120\t- **Clip playback**: three.js `AnimationMixer`. `retargetMixamoToVRM(asset, vrm)` in `animations.js` maps Mixamo bone names through `ACS_MIXAMO_RIG_MAP`, rebuilds `QuaternionKeyframeTrack` and `VectorKeyframeTrack` data, scales hips by rig height, and flips axes for VRM0.\n121\t- **Procedural gestures**: `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` in `gestures.js` is stateless and returns `{rot, exprs}` deltas.\n122\t - Gestures are `ACS_GESTURE_PRESETS` (wave, nod, shake, bow, each with duration, expression and peak).\n123\t - Moods are `ACS_MOOD_PRESETS` (`ampScale`, `speedScale`, expression, weight).\n124\t - Easings are `ACS_EASINGS` (linear, sine, quad, cubic, easeOut, easeInOut, backOut).\n125\t - Bell and sustained envelopes shape each gesture.\n126\t- **Additive layering**: [case study issue-28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28) established that all motion sources (pose, idle, gestures, look-at, text-motion, mouse force) add relative deltas each frame instead of replacing each other, which removes snaps at gesture start and end. `ACS_mergePose` sums pose and manual rotations, and `mergeExpressionDeltas` sums expressions.\n127\t- **Anatomical constraints**: `ACS_BONE_LIMITS` gives per-bone, per-axis ranges in degrees, citing range-of-motion references. `ACS_clampBoneRad` applies them, and sliders show degrees.\n128\t- **Gaze**: smoothed look-at follows the camera, the mouse or random targets, with a cone, saccades and separate eye and head shares.\n129\t- **Text to motion** (`textMotion.js`): a regex command table (slowWalk, run, happyWalk, stealth and others) maps to GR00T modes and procedural bone deltas, and declares resource requirements. `gearSonic.js` fetches real GEAR-SONIC reference motions (joint_pos, root_pos, root_quat at 50 fps) and a Unitree G1 MJCF/STL robot, and can call a backend.\n130\t- **Speech** (`ipaSpeech.js`): an English-to-IPA lexicon produces a phoneme timeline, which drives VRM mouth expressions and the jaw.\n131\t- **Text to model** (`textToModel.js`): a TRELLIS backend client. With no URL configured it returns `{status:'no-backend'}`, so the feature degrades cleanly.\n132\t- **Editing**: an experimental TransformControls joint gizmo (one joint at a time, hover or tap to switch, off by default).\n133\t- **Export**: GLB (`-edited.glb` via GLTFExporter) and SVG (`ACS_vrmToSVG` projects triangles with back-face culling and depth sort). The SVG export has its own camera settings.\n134\t- **Loading**: `modelLoader.js` handles glTF/VRM, FBX, OBJ, STL, PLY and MMD (PMX/VMD), including zip, rar and 7z archives (fflate and libarchive WASM). `ACS_normalizeModelURL` rewrites GitHub `blob/` and `raw/refs/heads/` URLs to raw download URLs, and `ACS_detectModelFormat` infers the format.\n135\t- **Archive demo**: CSS `@keyframes` (talk, breathe, headSway) on SVG parts, plus a parallel three.js part tree.\n136\t- **Recording**: absent. Screenshot or video export, custom pose saving and a scene editor are only listed in `ROADMAP.md`. There is no MediaRecorder use and no user-editable keyframe timeline.\n137\t\n138\t## 4. Assets and licensing\n139\t\n140\t### 4.1 immortality: zero-asset, cite-everything\n141\t\n142\t- It ships no images or audio. Everything is generated: canvas, SVG, CSS gradients, `feTurbulence` noise and Web Audio. Fonts are OFL `@fontsource` packages.\n143\t- Each option and each sound carries provenance. `OptionDef.source` points into `REFERENCES {label,url}`, and `SOUNDS` entries have `{character, sourceLabel, sourceUrl}`. Sounds have neutral names; the source names say what inspired them.\n144\t- License decisions are recorded per source in [`docs/case-studies/issue-7`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7):\n145\t - Arwes is MIT, so code was ported with attribution in comments (`frameShapes.ts`, `textEffects.ts`).\n146\t - Soul Extract is GPL-3.0, so only ideas were re-implemented and no code was copied.\n147\t - thegridcn has no license, so it was used as a visual reference only.\n148\t- Library choices were weighed by size. Tone.js (about 77 KB) was rejected for plain Web Audio, and the Select was hand-rolled with downshift as the fallback. The framework should keep this habit of recording rejected alternatives.\n149\t\n150\t### 4.2 anime-avatar: per-asset metadata and conditional attribution\n151\t\n152\t- `ACS_MODEL_PRESETS` entries have the shape `{id, label, url, format, kind, credit, license, flipped?, attributionRequired?}`. Examples:\n153\t - pixiv VRM1 sample and Seed-san: VRM Public License 1.0.\n154\t - Alicia Solid: Niconi Commons, attribution required, `flipped`.\n155\t - V-Sekai girl: \"See repository\".\n156\t - Khronos Duck: CC-BY 4.0.\n157\t - DamagedHelmet: CC-BY-NC 4.0.\n158\t - Unitree G1: NVIDIA.\n159\t- `ACS_ANIMATION_PRESETS` (Samba and Mixamo idle from the three.js examples, Gangnam Style from V-Sekai) carry `credit` and `license: 'Mixamo terms (free use with your avatar)'`.\n160\t- `attributionRequired(vrmMeta, preset, animMeta)` in `Editor.jsx` decides attribution in this order:\n161\t 1. VRM `creditNotation`.\n162\t 2. The preset flag.\n163\t 3. The animation flag.\n164\t 4. A license-string heuristic (CC-BY, Niconi, \"attribution\").\n165\t `AttributionOverlay` shows a credit on the stage only when attribution is required ([issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)). The Metadata section shows the loaded VRM meta.\n166\t- **Risks.**\n167\t - `ACS_GF2_MMD_MODEL_ARCHIVES` hot-links about 70 proprietary SUNBORN Girls' Frontline 2 MMD archives from the publisher CDN, with license text \"Official GF2 Exilium art page download\".\n168\t - DamagedHelmet is non-commercial.\n169\t - The label \"pixiv VRM1 sample (CC-ish / VRM license)\" and the license \"See repository\" (V-Sekai girl) are not license identifiers.\n170\t - Assets are loaded at runtime from third-party URLs (unpkg, three.js examples, GitHub raw). Availability and integrity are not pinned; there is no SRI.\n171\t - None of these assets may enter a public-domain framework asset set.\n172\t\n173\t## 5. Components inventory\n174\t\n175\t| Component / module | Repo | Kind | Reusable for the framework as |\n176\t| - | - | - | - |\n177\t| `settings.ts` axis schema, presets, migration, diff, share | immortality | data and logic | **Core config model** (to re-express in Links Notation) |\n178\t| `SettingsPanel` + `AxisControl` | immortality | generic panel | Auto-generated \"configuration mode\" inspector |\n179\t| `Select` (WAI-ARIA select-only combobox, type-ahead, edge flip) | immortality | control | Base dropdown |\n180\t| `Frame` + `frameShapes.ts` (9 frames, chamfer, glow, material layer) | immortality | container | Themed panel/\"window chrome\" primitive |\n181\t| `FxText` + `textEffects.ts` | immortality | text | Animated text primitive |\n182\t| `Starfield` (21 canvas backgrounds) | immortality | background | Theme backdrop plugins |\n183\t| `Overlays` (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) | immortality | overlay | Theme post-effects |\n184\t| `sound.ts` (26 voices, 10 events) | immortality | audio | UI sound theme layer |\n185\t| `LineChart`, `DataTable` (accessible twins), `Gauge`, `StatTile`, sparkline | immortality | data viz | Chart widgets with an a11y table fallback |\n186\t| `HudBar` (UTC clock), `Intro` (boot sequence) | immortality | chrome | Theme chrome |\n187\t| `useElementWidth` (ResizeObserver), `useReducedMotion`, `motionAllowed` | immortality | hooks | Platform utilities |\n188\t| `Studio.GlassPanel`, `ConfigDrawer`, `Section` (randomize/reset), `Row`, `Slider`, `ColorPick`, `Select`, `Chips`, `Toggle`, `Stage`, `useIsMobile` | anime-avatar | panel kit | Second panel kit; plugin candidates |\n195\t| `modelLoader.js`, `svg.js` | anime-avatar | IO | 3D asset plugin; vector export idea |\n196\t| `AttributionOverlay` + `attributionRequired` | anime-avatar | licensing UI | **Core attribution component** |\n197\t| Archive `AvatarSVG`, `Avatar3D`, `ConfigPanel`, `useAnimationCycle` | anime-avatar | demo | Reference only |\n198\t\n199\t## 6. Patterns worth adopting\n200\t\n201\t1. **One declarative schema per configurable surface.** Declare every setting once as `{key, label, group, kind, options|min/max/step/unit, description, sources}`. Validation, defaults, the panel, presets, randomizer, diff, sharing, migration and tests all derive from it (immortality `AXES`). In the framework this schema should itself be a Links Notation document.\n202\t2. **Option catalogs with ids, labels, descriptions and provenance.** Derive types from the catalog (`(typeof X)[number]['id']`), so adding an option to a theme is a one-line data change.\n203\t3. **Store and share only the diff from defaults.** `diffFromDefaults`, plus a version tag (`v:2`), makes share links short, survives default changes and supports \"N customized\" counters.\n204\t4. **Treat all external config as untrusted.** `mergeSettings(base, raw)` coerces each value and drops unknown keys. Apply this to imports, URL hashes and storage (anime-avatar currently does not).\n205\t5. **Versioned persistence with intent-preserving migration.** Keep only what the user changed from the old defaults, so the new defaults still take effect.\n206\t6. **Comfort settings stay local.** When applying a shared look or preset, keep the viewer's accessibility and comfort keys (motion, sound, volume). Lock the same keys from randomization.\n207\t7. **Presets are partial overrides over a base**, with `isPresetActive` detection and source citations.\n208\t8. **Randomize and reset per group and globally, with an injected RNG**, respecting constraints (bone limits) and locked keys. This makes visual exploration safe and reproducible.\n209\t9. **Project theme state to `data-*` attributes and CSS variables** instead of re-rendering. This is cheap, framework-agnostic and works the same for plain JS, React and Vue. A test then checks that every option has a CSS rule (`styling.test.ts`).\n210\t10. **High-frequency visuals bypass the component tree.** Pointer glow (`-mx/-my`), canvas backgrounds and the per-frame `apply.js` loop write directly to the DOM or scene.\n211\t11. **Animations as pure functions of time** (`decipherFrame(text,t,seed)`, `ACS_gestureDelta(name,t,mood,easing)`). They are deterministic, so they can be recorded, replayed, scrubbed and tested. This is the natural basis for the framework's animation recording: record the clock and inputs, not the pixels.\n212\t12. **Additive animation layers.** Each source contributes deltas that are summed each frame, with envelopes for start and end, so nothing snaps (anime-avatar issue-28).\n213\t13. **Named easing and envelope catalog** (`ACS_EASINGS`, bell and sustained) shared by every animation.\n214\t14. **Domain constraints as data** (`ACS_BONE_LIMITS` in degrees, with references), used for clamping sliders, randomizers and gizmos alike.\n215\t15. **Reduced motion and photosensitivity by default.** Use `motionAllowed()` (the setting combined with `prefers-reduced-motion`), and avoid hard flashes, which is the reason the flicker was replaced.\n216\t16. **Accessible panel conventions**: a non-modal docked drawer, Escape to close, focus return, arrow-key tabs, `aria-pressed` toggles, `<output>` for ranges, an `aria-live` change counter, and a clipboard fallback.\n217\t17. **Accessible data twins**: every chart has a table equivalent, `role=img` and a text summary.\n218\t18. **UI sound theme** as a separate configurable layer: an event-to-sounds map, modes (random, cycle, layer), master bus, lazy AudioContext, throttling, and a cue event bus that visuals can subscribe to.\n219\t19. **Zero-binary assets.** Generate visuals and sounds procedurally so the framework's own assets are trivially public domain.\n220\t20. **Provenance on every borrowed item** (`source`, `sourceUrl`, `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired`), with license decisions recorded per source (MIT port, GPL ideas only, no license means reference only).\n221\t21. **Conditional attribution UI**: show credits only when the asset's metadata or license requires it, and always expose a Metadata/Credits view.\n222\t22. **Dev mode exposes a state handle** (`window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`) plus an in-app test runner that does not autostart, can be stopped and keeps its scroll position (issue #19). This fits a \"configuration mode\" well.\n223\t23. **View state in the URL** (`?view=`, `#ui=`), consumed and then cleaned with `replaceState`, and listening to `hashchange`.\n224\t24. **Graceful optional backends**: AI features return a typed `{status:'no-backend'}` instead of failing.\n225\t25. **URL normalization for user-supplied resources** (GitHub `blob/` to raw) and per-asset fix-up flags such as `flipped`.\n226\t26. **Case-study per issue** (requirements table, root causes, rejected libraries). Both repos already do this, and link-foundation/ui should continue it.\n227\t\n228\t## 7. Duplication candidates\n229\t\n230\tBoth repos independently built the same subsystems. They should become single framework modules:\n231\t\n232\t| Concern | immortality | anime-avatar | Unified module |\n233\t| - | - | - | - |\n234\t| Settings schema | `AXES`, typed | implicit in `defaults.js` and `Editor.jsx` JSX | Links Notation schema with `choice/toggle/range/color/vector/list` kinds |\n235\t| Panel controls | `AxisControl`, `Select`, range with `<output>` | `Studio.Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle/Row` | One control set rendered from the schema |\n236\t| Drawer and panel chrome | `SettingsPanel` drawer, `Frame` | `ConfigDrawer`, `GlassPanel` (inline styles) | Themeable panel primitive |\n237\t| Group randomize and reset | `randomizeSettings`, Restore defaults | `randomizers.js`, per-`Section` buttons | Schema-driven randomize/reset with locks and constraints |\n238\t| Persistence | `loadSettings/saveSettings`, versioned key, migration | `localStorage` `acs_B` shallow merge | One store with versioning, migration, and a diff codec |\n239\t| Share and export | `#ui=` hash of the diff | `acs-config.json` download and import | Links Notation text for both URL and file |\n240\t| Easing and timing | CSS timing functions, text-effect clocks | `ACS_EASINGS`, envelopes | Shared easing catalog usable in CSS and JS |\n241\t| Motion preference | `motionAllowed`, `useReducedMotion` | none in the studio (idle, auto-rotate and gaze always on unless toggled) | Platform motion policy |\n242\t| Responsive helpers | `useElementWidth` | `useIsMobile` (720 px) | Shared breakpoint and size utilities |\n243\t| Provenance metadata | `REFERENCES`, `source`, `sourceUrl` | `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired` | One attribution record, using SPDX ids where possible |\n244\t| Visual regression | `experiments/preset-gallery.js` screenshots, `styling.test.ts` | canvas fingerprint, `probeDiff`, PR #17 image compare | Shared screenshot and fingerprint test harness |\n245\t| Canvas backgrounds | `Starfield` (21) | scene background and grid, archive petals | Background plugin interface |\n246\t\n247\t## 8. Problems, bugs and limitations\n248\t\n249\t### 8.1 immortality\n250\t\n251\t1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n252\t2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n253\t3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n254\t4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n255\t5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n256\t6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n257\t7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n258\t8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n259\t\n260\t### 8.2 anime-avatar\n261\t\n262\t1. **No build step in production**: Babel standalone transpiles JSX in the browser on every load, React runs in its development UMD build, and dependencies come from unpkg without SRI. This is slow, fragile and unsafe for a framework.\n263\t2. **Global namespace modules** (`window.ACS_*`, `window.Studio`, `window.__acs`) with implicit load order in `index.html`.\n264\t3. **Monoliths**: `Editor.jsx` is 2381 lines in one component, and `apply.js` is 1316 lines. All styling is inline style objects, so there is no theming.\n265\t4. **Two divergent apps** in one repo (studio in `public/` and the archived Vite app in `src/`). The README mostly documents the archive, and the archive's 2D and 3D part trees (`components/svg/*`, `components/three/*`) duplicate each other.\n266\t5. **Weak config validation**: import does a shallow `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse}`. Nested `rot/scale/expr` are not validated, unknown keys persist, errors use `alert`. There is no storage version or migration, and the key `acs_B` is opaque.\n267\t6. **No schema**: ranges and labels are duplicated between `Editor.jsx` and `randomizers.js`.\n268\t7. **Licensing**: the proprietary GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, and vague license strings (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\"). The license-string heuristic in `attributionRequired` can miss cases.\n269\t8. **Bugs called out in [issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)** (since addressed): the Alicia model loaded back-to-front, GitHub `blob/` URLs failed, loading errors never auto-hid, tests autostarted and could not be stopped, the test log forced scroll to the bottom, split view was shown on mobile, and copyright was shown unconditionally.\n270\t9. **Bugs called out in [issue #28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/28)**: an unnatural wave, non-anatomical slider ranges shown in radians, and gestures replacing look-at instead of adding to it, which caused snaps.\n271\t10. **No animation recording** and no keyframe editing. The Mixamo retarget only plays existing clips. Pose, scene editor and video export are only on the roadmap.\n272\t11. **Open requests** show demand for more model sources and mocap: [#18](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/18) (VRoid Hub, CharacterStudio), [#21](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/21) (kalidokit), [#22](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/22) (webaverse), [#23](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/23) (airi), [#24](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/24) (GitHub miner), [#38](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/38) (feature parity with TheSashaDev/girl-agent). [PR #17](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/pull/17) (image-comparison e2e) is still open.\n273\t\n274\t## 9. Migration notes\n275\t\n276\t### 9.1 Representing both configs in Links Notation\n277\t\n278\tAn immortality axis declaration could become:\n279\t\n280\t```lino\n281\t(axis surface\n282\t (label \"Panel material\")\n283\t (group panels)\n284\t (kind choice)\n285\t (display buttons)\n286\t (options gradient glass frosted solid transparent steel brass copper wood carbon holographic ...)\n287\t (sources arwes gridcn))\n288\t(option glass (of surface) (label \"Glass\") (source arwes))\n289\t(reference arwes (label \"Arwes\") (url \"https://github.com/arwes/arwes\"))\n290\t```\n291\t\n292\tA user's settings would be the diff from defaults:\n293\t\n294\t```lino\n295\t(settings (version 2)\n296\t (palette ares)\n297\t (frame octagon)\n298\t (glow medium)\n299\t (surfaceOpacity 0.6)\n300\t (sounds (click soft-tick glass-tap)))\n301\t```\n302\t\n303\tThe anime-avatar cfg, including nested bone rotations:\n304\t\n305\t```lino\n306\t(cfg (version 1)\n307\t (model (preset seed-san))\n308\t (rot (rightUpperArm (z -80)) (rightLowerArm (x -90)))\n309\t (expr (happy 0.4))\n310\t (light (key (color \"#ffffff\") (intensity 1.2))))\n311\t```\n312\t\n313\tThe asset provenance record:\n314\t\n315\t```lino\n316\t(asset alicia-solid\n317\t (url \"...\")\n318\t (format vrm)\n319\t (credit \"DWANGO Co., Ltd.\")\n320\t (license (spdx LicenseRef-Niconi-Commons))\n321\t (attribution required)\n322\t (fixup flipped))\n323\t```\n324\t\n325\t### 9.2 Steps\n326\t\n327\t1. **Port the `settings.ts` engine first.** Keep `coerce`, `merge`, `diff`, `migrate`, `encode/decode`, `applySharedLook` and `randomize` as framework-neutral pure functions, but read and write the schema and values as Links Notation. Swap the JSON share hash for a Links Notation hash and keep a JSON v2 reader for old links.\n328\t2. **Extend the axis kinds** to cover anime-avatar: `color`, `vector3` (bone rotation with per-axis limits and units), `map` (per-bone, per-mesh, per-expression), `list` (sounds per event), `asset` (URL plus format plus provenance), and `action` (buttons such as gestures and export).\n329\t3. **Add rendering hints to the schema** (`render data-attr|css-var|engine`), so `Shell`, the test assertions and engine bridges (`apply.js`-style reconcilers) are all generated.\n330\t4. **Generate the configuration-mode inspector** from the schema. It should merge `AxisControl` (a11y, sources, display hints) with the `Studio` kit (per-section randomize/reset, color pickers, chips, mobile full-screen drawer). Export `Editor.jsx`'s 22 sections as a large conformance test for that generator.\n331\t5. **Split `styles.css` into per-axis theme modules** keyed by `[data-axis='id']`, so each theme (Arwes HUD, glass, and later the classic-UI themes) is a separately loadable package.\n332\t6. **Animation recording**: build on the pure time-function pattern. A recording is a Links Notation timeline of `(at t (set key value))` and `(at t (play gesture wave (mood happy)))` entries, plus the seed. Playback re-evaluates the pure functions, so recordings are tiny, diffable and reproducible. Combine with additive layers and the shared easing catalog.\n333\t7. **Asset policy**: the framework's own assets follow immortality (procedural, Unlicense). Third-party assets need a mandatory provenance record (SPDX id or `LicenseRef-*`, source URL, credit, attribution flag, commercial-use flag) and a CI check that rejects missing or non-free licenses from the default catalog. Exclude GF2-style proprietary and NC assets from defaults, or gate them behind an explicit opt-in that displays the terms.\n334\t8. **Bindings**: the pure core (schema, store, codecs, easing, time functions, sound specs) should be a plain-JS package. React and Vue adapters wrap `useSettings`, the inspector and `Frame`. Swift and Kotlin bindings consume the same Links Notation schema and theme tokens, and implement native controls.\n335\t9. **Testing**: keep both repos' ideas. Add schema-to-CSS coverage tests (fixing the duplicated `CSS_AXES` list), a preset screenshot gallery, canvas fingerprinting and the in-app runner (no autostart, stoppable) as part of configuration mode.\n336\t10. **Do not carry over**: in-browser Babel, development React builds, unpinned CDN imports without SRI, `window.*` globals, inline-style-only theming, `alert`-based errors, and opaque storage keys.\n337\t"

Values can themselves be links,\nso nesting goes as deep as you like.\n\n### 1.1 Links and ids\n\n```lino\n| Go | `github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/go` (`lino.Parse`) | v0.27.1 | hand-written | 139 | Stable, smaller API |\n| Java | `io.github.link-foundation:links-notation` | not on Maven Central ([#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)) | hand-written | 185 | Source only |\n| PHP | `link-foundation/links-notation` | not on Packagist (#192) | hand-written | 235 | Source only |\n| C++ | CMake, release archives | 0.27.1 | hand-written | 346 | Stable |\n| Swift | none | - `.parse(text)` returns `Link[]`.\n  - `.parseGroups(text)` returns a `LinksGroup` tree. `LinksGroup` exists only in\n    JS, C#, Java and C++.\n- `new Link(id, values)`, with `.format(options)` and `.toString()`.\n- `formatLinks(links, { lessParentheses, maxLineLength, indentLongLines, maxInlineRefs, groupConsecutive })`.\n- `parseIndentedDocument` / `formatIndentedDocument` (JS and C++ only).\n- `escapeReference(ref, { minimal })` / `unescapeReference(ref)`.\n- `StreamParser`: events `link`, `error` and `end`, plus `position()`, `drain()`\n  and `reset()`.\n\n### 2.2 Round-trip guarantees\n\n| Guarantee | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| `parse -> format -> parse` yields the same link tree | Yes, in every language, tested against the golden corpus |\n| Any Unicode string survives as a reference | Yes, via quoting or the `~1{}` literal |\n| Same tree across languages | Yes, via the parity fixtures |\n| Comments survive | **No.** They are dropped during parsing |\n| Original layout survives (indentation vs parentheses, quote style, blank lines) | **No.** The formatter re-chooses the layout |\n| Quoted vs bare distinction is visible in the tree | **No.** `\"1\"` and `1` are the same reference string |\n\nFor a WYSIWYG editor that edits the user's `.lino` file, the last three rows\nmatter most. See section 5.\n\n### 2.3 Open and relevant issues (links-notation)\n\n- Open: [#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)\n  (publish Java and PHP) and #350 (dependabot). The repository is otherwise\n  quiet and stable.\n- Closed but relevant to UI:\n  - #301 (comments)\n  - #282 (nested context for multi-line groups)\n  - #332 (lossless reference literal)\n  - #351 (browser bundling)\n  - #313 (formatter / empty reference)\n  - #184 (multi-reference values)\n\n## 3. What a UI dialect needs that LiNo already has\n\n| UI need | Existing LiNo feature |\n| --- | --- |\n| Tree of elements (DOM-like) | Indentation and nested groups. `parseGroups` keeps the hierarchy |\n| Element identity | Link id (`save:`). Ids are single references, globally addressable |\n| Graph, not just tree (reuse, references between elements and tokens) | A reference is just a name, so `@token` / `$name` / an element id can point anywhere in the document. This is native to the associative model |\n| Attributes / props | `(key value)` sub-links, the lino-objects-codec convention |\n| Text content with any characters | Quoting, N-quoting and `~1{}` literals |\n| Comments in hand-written files | `#` comments (read side only) |\n| Big documents, live editing | Streaming parsers, `position()` for error locations |\n| One spec for many targets | 8 implementations with a parity corpus. Rust compiles to WASM |\n| Typed config objects | lino-objects-codec (quoted = string, bare = number/bool/null) |\n| i18n strings | lino-i18n catalogues and React adapter |\n| Settings resolution | lino-arguments (pure build for browser) |\n| Import of existing HTML/CSS | meta-language HTML/CSS importers with lossless CST |\n| Storage as a links network | doublets-web (WASM), link-cli, binary LiNo |\n| Visualizing the network | link-cli workbench and doublets-web playground graph views (prior art for the issue's \"LiNo -> links network UI\" converter) |\n\n## 5. Gaps and open questions\n\n1. **Typed values.** The core tree has only strings, and `\"1\"` and `1` produce\n   the same reference. The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.",

Build on these (permissive, healthy, aligned)\n\n1. **Links Notation as the single source of truth**, with lossless conversion\n   to the closest standard in each domain:\n   - **DTCG 2025.10** for tokens (via **Style Dictionary** transforms to CSS,\n     Swift, Kotlin and JS);\n   - **WAAPI / Lottie** for animation;\n   - **Vega-Lite** for charts;\n   - **Mermaid / DOT** for diagrams;\n   - **A2UI / Adaptive Cards / JSON Forms** for UI trees;\n   - **Custom Elements Manifest** for component metadata.\n\n   \"Every other framework is just LiNo\" then becomes concrete: each one has an\n   importer and exporter.\n\n2. **Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements)** as the reference\n   vanilla-JS renderer. Generate **React and Vue wrappers** with a Stencil-like\n   output-target approach, so one implementation serves all web frameworks.\n3. **Zag.js-style state machines** (adopt Zag.js, or reimplement its machines\n   described in LiNo) for component behaviour and accessibility. Use **React\n   Aria** and WAI-ARIA APG as the acceptance criteria. **Floating UI** for\n   positioning.\n4. **Three-layer tokens** (reference → semantic → component), with\n   **material-color-utilities** for palette generation. **Material, Fluent and\n   Apple (HIG-guided) themes** plus \"classic\" themes as alternative token sets\n   and control templates. Use **Ionic's modes** and **XAML control templates**\n   as the model, and **Open UI** research for canonical component and part\n   names.\n5. **Visualisation:** D3 modules plus our own LiNo chart grammar\n   (Vega-Lite-like). Renderers: **ECharts** (broad charts), **Cytoscape.js**,\n   **Sigma.js/Graphology** and **force-graph/3d-force-graph** (links networks),\n   **xyflow** (editable node graphs, React), **Dagre** (default layout).\n6. **Animation:** our own LiNo keyframe and spring and state-machine model,\n   compiled to **WAAPI / View Transitions**, **Motion** (MIT) on web, and\n   SwiftUI and Compose natively. **rrweb** as an optional DOM-level session\n   recorder. **Playwright** for turning recordings into tests.\n7. **Designer and dev mode:** our own, over the LiNo tree. Copy the panel\n   architecture from **GrapesJS / Puck / Visual Studio**, the runtime-overlay\n   inspector from **React DevTools / Live Visual Tree**, the variants matrix\n   from **Xcode Previews / Storybook**, and the timeline from **Theatre.js**\n   (design only). Use **Puck** (MIT) or **GrapesJS** (BSD-3) only for a\n   throw-away early prototype if speed matters.\n8. **Native:** **SwiftUI** (SwiftPM) and **Jetpack Compose / Compose\n   Multiplatform** renderers that interpret the same LiNo. **React Native New\n   Architecture** (0.82+) with **Expo** for demos, and **React Native Web** to\n   show RN components on the docs site. **Tauri** for a desktop designer shell\n   that can use the Rust associative stack (`doublets-rs`, `link-cli`).\n9. **Assets:** our own icon and illustration set under **CC0-1.0**. Default\n   third-party sets: **Lucide** (ISC), **Material Symbols** (Apache-2.0),\n   **Fluent System Icons** (MIT), **Phosphor / Tabler** (MIT), **Health Icons /\n   Kenney** (CC0). Keep attribution records in LiNo modelled on **Iconify's\n   per-set metadata**, with **SPDX** IDs, a **REUSE 3.3** compliant repo\n   (`REUSE.toml`), and **ScanCode** license scanning in CI.\n\n### B. Only interoperate with (import, export or optional adapter; no core dependency)\n\n- **Figma** (Dev Mode, Variables, Code Connect) and **Penpot** (MPL-2.0;\n  DTCG tokens). What a UI dialect needs that LiNo already has\n\n| UI need | Existing LiNo feature |\n| --- | --- |\n| Tree of elements (DOM-like) | Indentation and nested groups. `parseGroups` keeps the hierarchy |\n| Element identity | Link id (`save:`). Ids are single references, globally addressable |\n| Graph, not just tree (reuse, references between elements and tokens) | A reference is just a name, so `@token` / `$name` / an element id can point anywhere in the document. This is native to the associative model |\n| Attributes / props | `(key value)` sub-links, the lino-objects-codec convention |\n| Text content with any characters | Quoting, N-quoting and `~1{}` literals |\n| Comments in hand-written files | `#` comments (read side only) |\n| Big documents, live editing | Streaming parsers, `position()` for error locations |\n| One spec for many targets | 8 implementations with a parity corpus. Rust compiles to WASM |\n| Typed config objects | lino-objects-codec (quoted = string, bare = number/bool/null) |\n| i18n strings | lino-i18n catalogues and React adapter |\n| Settings resolution | lino-arguments (pure build for browser) |\n| Import of existing HTML/CSS | meta-language HTML/CSS importers with lossless CST |\n| Storage as a links network | doublets-web (WASM), link-cli, binary LiNo |\n| Visualizing the network | link-cli workbench and doublets-web playground graph views (prior art for the issue's \"LiNo -> links network UI\" converter) |\n\n## 5. Gaps and open questions\n\n1. **Typed values.** The core tree has only strings, and `\"1\"` and `1` produce\n   the same reference. The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.\n\n   Recommendation: (b) for dimensions, durations and colours, with (a) as the\n   fallback for free-form props. Also ask upstream for a `quoted` flag on\n   parsed references, which would remove the need for a second reader.\n2. **Units and colours.**\n   - `8px`, `0.2s`, `50%` and `1.5rem` are valid bare references, but they are\n     strings until a schema parses them.\n   - Hex colours must be quoted because of `#` comments.\n   - Alternative: `rgb(...)` / `oklch(...)` as links, for example\n     `(oklch 0.62 0.19 255)`, which is better for the associative model and for\n     theme maths.\n3. **`:` in values.** URLs, CSS pseudo-classes (`:hover`), media queries and\n   ratios (`16:9`) need quoting. Prefer structured links instead:\n   `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))` and `(aspect 16 9)`.\n4. **Comments and formatting are lost on round trip.** A WYSIWYG editor that\n   writes back to `.lino` will strip the user's comments and reflow the layout.\n   Options:\n   - (a) A CST mode upstream (trivia and spans, as meta-language already does\n     for CSS).\n   - (b) Make comments first-class links, for example `(note \"...\")`.\n   - (c) Patch-in-place edits using parser positions.\n\n   This needs an issue upstream in links-notation.\n5. **Ordering.** Link values are ordered, which is good for children and\n   keyframes. Property order, however, should be insignificant. The dialect\n   must state which parts are sequences (children, keyframes, transitions) and\n   which are sets (props). It must also define the meaning of a duplicate key:\n   last wins, as in lino-store logs.\n6. **Ids and scoping.** Ids are document-global strings, and nothing prevents\n   duplicates. Questions:\n   - Do we need namespaces (`login.save`) or nested id scopes per component?\n   - How do ids map to doublet numeric addresses, and are they stable across\n     edits? The editor needs stable ids for selection, undo and collaboration.\n7. **References for styles and tokens.** There is no built-in reference sigil.\n   A convention is needed:\n   - `@token.path` for design tokens\n   - `$param` for component parameters (the linksql / transformer convention)\n   - a bare id for elements and keyframe tracks\n\n   Open questions: resolution order (component, then theme, then base),\n   cycles, and fallbacks (`(or @color.accent \"#3390ec\")`).\n8. **Schemas and validation.** lino-schema is only a stub. The dialect needs a\n   schema (which props an element accepts, their types and defaults) for:\n   - the editor's property panel\n   - validation\n   - codegen to React, Vue, React Native, SwiftUI and Compose\n9. **Expressions and bindings.** Event handlers, data bindings and conditional\n   rendering need a small expression vocabulary, for example\n   `(on press (emit save))`, `(bind value $draft.text)` and\n   `(when $sending (show spinner))`. Decide whether this reuses the linksql\n   substitution syntax.\n10. **Missing languages.**\n    - Swift: no implementation exists.\n    - Kotlin: blocked by the unpublished Java package (#192).\n\n    Options: native targets either ship a parser or consume a precompiled\n    form (JSON or binary LiNo) produced by the JS/Rust toolchain.\n11. **Security.** The parser has `maxDepth = 64` and `maxInputSize`. User-supplied\n    themes must never contain executable code. Event handlers are names, not\n    code.\n\n## 6. Proposed sketch of a UI dialect in LiNo (PROPOSAL, not an existing format)\n\n> Everything in this section is a **proposal for discussion**. It is not\n> implemented anywhere. It only uses syntax the current grammar (0.27.1)\n> accepts. The meaning of every name is defined by the proposed dialect\n> schema, not by LiNo itself.\n\nConventions used:\n\n- An indented id link (`save:`) declares an element, token set or animation.\n  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`--corner`, `--border-width`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`, `--font-scale`, `--chart-line`, `--bg-speed`, `--motion-scale`, `--bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n  - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n  - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `--fill` variable.\n  - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n  - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n  - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\n### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n\n- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n  - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n  - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n  - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n  - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.\n  - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color and intensity.\n  - Scene and cameras: `bg`, ground, `floorGrid`, `camera*`, a separate `svgCam*` set.\n  - Toggles: `autoRotate`, `mirrorArms`, `showFPS`, and an experimental joint gizmo.\n- `App.jsx` keeps cfg in React state, persists it to localStorage key `acs_B` merged over defaults, and keeps the view (`editor|tests|split|none`) in `?view=` and `acs_view`. It exposes `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}` so in-app tests can drive the UI.\n- There is no schema. Each control is hand-wired in `Editor.jsx` using `Studio.Section/Row/Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle` from `ui.jsx`. Ranges, steps and labels live inline in JSX.\n| `AttributionOverlay` + `attributionRequired`                                                                                                        | anime-avatar | licensing UI   | **Core attribution component**                          |\n| Archive `AvatarSVG`, `Avatar3D`, `ConfigPanel`, `useAnimationCycle`                                                                                 | anime-avatar | demo           | Reference only                                          |\n\n## 6. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **One declarative schema per configurable surface.** Declare every setting once as `{key, label, group, kind, options|min/max/step/unit, description, sources}`. Validation, defaults, the panel, presets, randomizer, diff, sharing, migration and tests all derive from it (immortality `AXES`). In the framework this schema should itself be a Links Notation document.\n2. **Option catalogs with ids, labels, descriptions and provenance.** Derive types from the catalog (`(typeof X)[number]['id']`), so adding an option to a theme is a one-line data change.\n3. **Store and share only the diff from defaults.** `diffFromDefaults`, plus a version tag (`v:2`), makes share links short, survives default changes and supports \"N customized\" counters.\n4. **Treat all external config as untrusted.** `mergeSettings(base, raw)` coerces each value and drops unknown keys. Apply this to imports, URL hashes and storage (anime-avatar currently does not).\n5. **Versioned persistence with intent-preserving migration.** Keep only what the user changed from the old defaults, so the new defaults still take effect.\n6. **Comfort settings stay local.** When applying a shared look or preset, keep the viewer's accessibility and comfort keys (motion, sound, volume). Lock the same keys from randomization.\n7. **Presets are partial overrides over a base**, with `isPresetActive` detection and source citations.\n8. **Randomize and reset per group and globally, with an injected RNG**, respecting constraints (bone limits) and locked keys. This makes visual exploration safe and reproducible.\n9. **Project theme state to `data-*` attributes and CSS variables** instead of re-rendering. This is cheap, framework-agnostic and works the same for plain JS, React and Vue. A test then checks that every option has a CSS rule (`styling.test.ts`).\n10. **High-frequency visuals bypass the component tree.** Pointer glow (`--mx/--my`), canvas backgrounds and the per-frame `apply.js` loop write directly to the DOM or scene.\n11. **Animations as pure functions of time** (`decipherFrame(text,t,seed)`, `ACS_gestureDelta(name,t,mood,easing)`). They are deterministic, so they can be recorded, replayed, scrubbed and tested. This is the natural basis for the framework's animation recording: record the clock and inputs, not the pixels.\n12. **Additive animation layers.** Each source contributes deltas that are summed each frame, with envelopes for start and end, so nothing snaps (anime-avatar issue-28).\n13. **Named easing and envelope catalog** (`ACS_EASINGS`, bell and sustained) shared by every animation.\n14. **Domain constraints as data** (`ACS_BONE_LIMITS` in degrees, with references), used for clamping sliders, randomizers and gizmos alike.\n15. **Reduced motion and photosensitivity by default.** Use `motionAllowed()` (the setting combined with `prefers-reduced-motion`), and avoid hard flashes, which is the reason the flicker was replaced.\n16. **Accessible panel conventions**: a non-modal docked drawer, Escape to close, focus return, arrow-key tabs, `aria-pressed` toggles, `<output>` for ranges, an `aria-live` change counter, and a clipboard fallback.\n17. **Accessible data twins**: every chart has a table equivalent, `role=img` and a text summary.\n18. **UI sound theme** as a separate configurable layer: an event-to-sounds map, modes (random, cycle, layer), master bus, lazy AudioContext, throttling, and a cue event bus that visuals can subscribe to.\n19. **Zero-binary assets.** Generate visuals and sounds procedurally so the framework's own assets are trivially public domain.\n20. **Provenance on every borrowed item** (`source`, `sourceUrl`, `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired`), with license decisions recorded per source (MIT port, GPL ideas only, no license means reference only).\n21. **Conditional attribution UI**: show credits only when the asset's metadata or license requires it, and always expose a Metadata/Credits view.\n22. **Dev mode exposes a state handle** (`window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`) plus an in-app test runner that does not autostart, can be stopped and keeps its scroll position (issue #19). This fits a \"configuration mode\" well.\n23. **View state in the URL** (`?view=`, `#ui=`), consumed and then cleaned with `replaceState`, and listening to `hashchange`.\n24. **Graceful optional backends**: AI features return a typed `{status:'no-backend'}` instead of failing.\n25. **URL normalization for user-supplied resources** (GitHub `blob/` to raw) and per-asset fix-up flags such as `flipped`.\n26. **Case-study per issue** (requirements table, root causes, rejected libraries). Both repos already do this, and link-foundation/ui should continue it.\n\n## 7. Duplication candidates\n\nBoth repos independently built the same subsystems. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 8.1 immortality\n\n1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n\n### 8.2 anime-avatar",

It also migrates old values, for example `future.surface: 'transparent'` becomes a solid surface with\n     opacity 0.\n4. **Projection into the DOM, without the framework.** `applySettings(root, rules, settings)` writes:\n   - numbers and colours as CSS variables on `<html>` (`liquid.blur` becomes `--liquid-blur: 18px`)\n   - selects and toggles as `data-*` attributes (`skin.name` becomes `data-skin-name=\"glass\"`)\n   - derived values: corner-radius fallbacks, `--ui-accent-rgb`, an SVG `feTurbulence` noise data-URI, and\n     `data-surface-invisible`\n\n   All styling is then plain CSS that keys off these variables and attributes.\n\n5. **Before-paint script.**\n   - `normalize` and `applySettings` are serialized with `Function.toString` into `SETTINGS_SCRIPT`.\n   - The `themeBeforePaint` Vite plugin prepends it into `<head>` together with `THEME_SCRIPT`\n     ([K:vite.config.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/vite.config.js)).\n   - This avoids a flash of the wrong theme or skin, and it is the same code as at runtime, not a copy.\n6. **Store.**\n   - [K:src/settings/store.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/store.js)\n     is built on `useSyncExternalStore`. It has no context provider.\n   - **Only the diff from defaults** is stored, in localStorage `settings`. Users who never touched a key\n     therefore get improved defaults automatically.\n   - Other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.\n   - API: `setSettings(patch)`, `resetSettings(keys)`, `changesOf`.\n7. **Looks (presets).** Defined in [K:src/settings/presets.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/presets.js).\n   - Built-in presets: Matrix universe (default), glass-universe, calm, matrix, deep-space, warp,\n     neon (Tron), liquid, blueprint, and \"Light and fast\" for slow phones.\n   - `before45()` rebases old presets onto `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS`.\n   - `COMFORT` lists keys that presets, shared links and Random never change:\n     `motion.mode`, `sound.on`, `sound.volume`, `theory.notation`, `ui.transparency`. These are\n     accessibility and preference keys; the idea comes from immortality's `src/settings.ts`.\n   - `randomLook()` never goes above the default cost on any heavy key (counts, fps, blur, glow).\n   - Saved looks are stored as `[{name, look}]` under `settings-presets`, with add, remove, import and rename.\n   - Sharing: `#settings=<urlencoded JSON>` (`shareLink`, `lookOfHash`). When a shared link is opened,\n     `openSharedLook()` applies it, saves the previous look as a \"Before the link\" preset, and strips the hash.\n8. **Preferences outside the schema.** [K:src/i18n/prefs.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/i18n/prefs.js)\n   - Language is resolved as `?lang`, then the stored value, then `navigator`, then `en`.\n   - Theme is auto/light/dark.\n   - Each is a tiny external store.\n   - All UI text is written inline as `{en, ru}` objects, and `plural.js` handles Russian plural forms.\n9. **The network editor's local style model.** [K:src/links/style.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/links/style.js)\n   - `STYLE_SECTIONS` reuses the same field factories.\n   - `normalizeStyle` validates; `styleToParams` and `styleFromParams` put **only non-default values in the\n     query string**.\n   - There are six link palettes: site, neon, pastel, warm, cold, print.\n   - The network uses the same configuration grammar as the site settings, but it is scoped to a document\n     (the URL) instead of the user (localStorage).\n10. **Settings page as live designer.** [K:src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx)\n    - The page is generated from the schema. Each row is `label | control | value | ↺ reset`, and changed\n      rows get an `is-changed` class.\n    - Layer tabs show a dot when that layer is active.\n    - There is a Reset button per section plus \"Reset everything\".\n    - \"Look at the background\" is a peek mode that hides the panels.\n    - The \"Your changes\" box shows the diff JSON with Copy, and has a paste area that loads either settings\n      or `{presets:[...]}`.\n    - Sounds have ▶ preview buttons.\n    - The page itself is the preview: it includes `InterfacePreview`, `UiSamples` (small samples of every UI\n      element, from #45), `MaterialPresets` and `CornerTiles`.\n    - Columns are explicit because CSS multicol was buggy in Safari.\n    - This is the closest existing thing to the \"VS-designer configuration mode\" the issue asks for, though\n      it edits global tokens, not per-element instances.\n11. **Testing every setting.** Issue #15 asked for proof that every setting is applied.\n    [K:src/settings/applied.test.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/settings/applied.test.js)\n    goes through every field in `FIELDS` and fails if a setting is used in none of three ways: as a CSS\n    variable or `<html>` attribute that a stylesheet reads, as an option a background script reads, or as a\n    key a component reads.\n12. **Skins and frames.**\n    - [K:src/skins.frames.js](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/main/src/skins.frames.js)\n      defines corner shapes and corner lines once:\n      - shapes: square, cut, tall, wide, round, scoop, notch\n      - lines: none, gap, line, accent, bracket\n    - `npm run build:frames` generates `skins.frames.css` from it, and the same definitions draw the\n      `CornerTiles` previews. A test keeps the generated CSS in sync.\n    - The CSS uses `@property` typed lengths and `:where()` to keep specificity at zero.\n    - `schema.skins.js` has 12 palettes (from immortality) and the skins `glass`, `liquid`, `futuristic`.\n    - Owner requirements from issues:\n      - #39: a single transparency setting for all backgrounds; matte, glossy and liquid glass presets; no\n        rounded corners in the futuristic look by default; rounded corners following t3code practice\n      - #45: one per-side border configuration shared by panels, blocks, buttons and other elements; top\n        highlight width set separately from corner/side widths; the corner layer above or below content;\n        colours picked from palettes\n\n1. **One rule table per key**: `{default, min, max, unit, options, isColor}`. It drives normalization,\n   validation, the generated UI, CSS projection and tests. It translates naturally into a Links Notation\n   schema, e.g. `(liquid.blur: range 18 0 40 px)`.\n2. **Store the diff from defaults, never the full state.** Defaults can then improve for everyone, and saved\n   looks and share links stay small.\n3. **Project settings into CSS variables and `data-*` attributes on the root.** Theming then works without\n   any framework, and the same tokens can be emitted for SwiftUI and Compose as constant tables.\n4. **Run the same `normalize` and `apply` before first paint**, serialized from the real functions rather\n   than copied. There is no theme flash and no second implementation.\n5. **Comfort keys.** Accessibility and preference keys (reduced motion, sound, volume, transparency,\n   notation) are excluded from presets, shared links and randomization.\n6. **Looks as data.** Built-in presets, saved presets, import/export JSON, `#settings=` share links, and an\n   automatic \"Before the link\" backup when a shared look is applied.\n7. **Bounded randomization.** `randomLook()` never exceeds the default cost on heavy keys, so Random is safe\n   on slow devices. There is also an explicit \"Light and fast\" preset.\n8. **The settings page is the live preview.** Each row has a per-field ↺ reset and changed rows are marked.\n   There are section resets, a peek mode, a diff box with copy and paste, and sample tiles of every UI\n   element. Extending this to per-element editing gives the WYSIWYG configuration mode.\n9. **One source generates both CSS and preview tiles** (`skins.frames.js`), and a test fails if the\n   generated CSS is out of date.\n10. **One renderer for preview and export.** A single SVG string (`networkSvg`) is reused for PNG, JPEG and\n    WebP export, so what is shared is exactly what is seen. The same idea fits animation recording: record\n    the frames of the model, not screenshots.\n11. **URL state holds only non-default parameters** (`styleToParams`), with debounced history that pauses\n    while a slider is dragged.\n12. **Several synchronized notations of one model**, with typed-text preservation and bilingual errors. This\n    shows the framework's \"DOM-like language and Links Notation as two views of one tree\" in miniature.\n13. **Expensive layout in a cancellable worker**, with keyed results that cannot overwrite newer state\n    (`solver-job.js`, `useCollisionSolver.js`).\n14. **Performance governors.** The FPS governor degrades resolution and then fps, and `panelVisibility.js`\n    limits live `backdrop-filter` surfaces. Both belong in the framework runtime.\n15. **Owned, ARIA-compliant controls.** Select follows the APG patterns, numeric keys are shared, and popups\n    are portaled and clamped to the viewport. #39 says \"all UI elements must be owned by us\".\n16. **Declarative sound.** A `data-sound` attribute on any element plus document-level role mapping, so\n    components do not hard-code audio.\n17. **Language and theme stores built on `useSyncExternalStore`, with no provider.** This ports cleanly to\n    signals or observables in Vue, Swift and Kotlin.\n18. **Pointer-centred zoom with document-level listeners** and an infinite pattern grid (links-visuals #15,\n    #19, #21). These are designer-canvas basics.\n19. **Arc-length center anchors for links that point at links.** An anchor is pinned and re-resolved at\n    render time (`applyCenterAnchors`), which is the core of drawing associative links, not just node graphs.\n2. **Links Notation is hand-parsed.** `parseLinks` in `edit.js` uses the regex\n   `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g`, and `links-notation` is not imported anywhere in `src/`.\n   It only accepts numeric doublets and does not handle nesting, names or multi-line input.\n3. **Settings are JSON, not Links Notation.** This applies to localStorage, the `#settings=` hash, the\n   diff box, and import/export. It contradicts the framework goal of representing everything in Links\n   Notation.\n4. **Bilingual text is hard-coded** as `{en, ru}` objects inside components, including long templated\n   sentences in `NetworkEditor.jsx`. Adding a language means editing every component; there is no catalog.\n5. **Configuration is global only.** The tokens style every element of a kind. There is no per-instance\n   override and no element tree to select from, so it is not yet a WYSIWYG designer.\n6. **React-bound.** The store, pages and controls are React components; only `apply.js` and `src/links/*`\n   are framework-free.\n7. **Open issue #47.** The top-left corner and the top and bottom edges are not transparent by default,\n   although every other element is. These are still border/corner layering bugs from the #45 redesign.\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #13: the rain sometimes scaled up too much on refresh.\n   - #45: some border configurations clipped overflowing content or broke transparent backgrounds and\n     selection.\n   - CSS multicol was unreliable in Safari, so columns are explicit.\n   - Safari needed a focus fix in `numericKeys.js`.\n9. **Heavy generated CSS.** `skins.frames.css` is about 84 KB / 1067 lines, and a very large number of\n   fields (hundreds) costs payload and maintenance.\n10. **Repo weight.** About 372 MB, from case studies, logs and archives committed to the repo, so it is\n    slow to clone. Sparse clones are needed.\n11. **Migrations are ad hoc** (`before45()`, special cases in `normalize`). There is no versioned schema\n    migration mechanism.\n\n### links-visuals\n\n1. **CDN at runtime.** D3 is fetched from `esm.sh/use-m` on every load. It does not work offline, it is\n   unpinned and therefore a supply-chain risk, and it is not reproducible.\n2. **Global mutable state** in `state.mjs` (module singletons with setters). Two views cannot share a page.\n3. **Duplicated renderers.** `canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG markers and paths by hand, and the\n   two can drift apart.\n4. **A rAF loop runs every frame even when idle** (`animation.mjs`), which wastes battery.\n5. **Inline CSS is copied into every HTML page**, with no theming. Markers are hardcoded black, and only\n   grid.html and draw.html have colour.\n6. **Experiments are not composable.** Each page wires modules differently, and `failed-attempts/` holds 76\n   HTML snapshots instead of git history.\n7. **Limits of the network model.** grid.html places links in cells without real references. Only draw.html\n   has link-to-link anchors, and only to centers (no source/target-to-endpoint semantics, no layout engine).\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #1/#3: start-point snapping.\n   - #15: the grid was not infinite.\n   - #19/#21: zoom failed away from the center because the hit area was the SVG; listeners were moved to\n     `document`.\n   - #23/#28: grid proportions were inconsistent with single-link mode.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n\n1. **Licensing first.** links-visuals is Unlicense and can be ported now. For konard.github.io, ask the\n   owner to add an Unlicense LICENSE before any code is moved. The sound engine and palettes are already\n   Unlicense through immortality.\n2. **Schema in Links Notation.** Express each RULES entry as links, for example:\n   ```\n   (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (unit px))\n   (skin.name: (type select) (default glass) (options glass liquid futuristic))\n   ```\n   Then generate the JS and TS rule tables, and the Swift and Kotlin constants, from it. Store user diffs as\n   Links Notation too: `(liquid.blur 24)`. Keep JSON import for backward compatibility with existing\n   `settings` and `settings-presets` values and `#settings=` links.\n3. **Keep the projection contract.** Write `--section-key` CSS variables and `data-section-key` attributes,\n   and keep the before-paint injection for web targets. Native targets get the same normalized map as an\n   observable store.\n4. **Scopes.** Keep the user/document split (localStorage vs URL or `.lino`), and add an element scope so the\n   designer mode can override tokens per node in the DOM-like tree.\n5. **Controls.** Port Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip and numericKeys with their tests (`*.test.jsx`)\n   as the first `controls` set. Keep WAI-ARIA APG behaviour and the Safari fixes.\n6. **Links view.** Merge the K:src/links glyph, placement, collisions and render code with the L:js\n   zoom-pan, grid, anchors and IK into a single renderer:\n   - one marker set, with SVG and Canvas back ends generated from it\n   - no global state; instance objects instead\n   - D3 bundled and pinned, or dropped where `d3-force` alone is enough\n   - an idle-stopping animation loop\n7. **Parsing.** Replace the regex parser with the official `links-notation` package. Keep `configurations.js`\n   (code and index maths, Burnside counting) as a pure utility.\n8. **i18n.** Move the `{en, ru}` literals into per-language catalogs keyed by id, preferably in Links\n   Notation, and keep `plural.js` rules per language.\n9. **Themes.** Treat `glass`, `liquid` and `futuristic`, plus the 12 palettes and the corner/frame generator,\n   as the first theme pack. Classic UIs (Windows 9x, Aqua and so on) become more theme packs on the same\n   tokens. Fix #47-style corner and edge transparency in the generator, not in per-skin CSS.\n10. **Animation recording.** Reuse the export pipeline: one model goes to a standalone SVG and then to a\n    raster, over a timeline of settings and link diffs. The IK animation in links-visuals and the canvas\n    backgrounds are the first recording targets.",

The dialect needs a rule. Options:\n   - (a) Adopt the lino-objects-codec rule: bare means number, boolean or null,\n     and quoted means string. This requires the codec's own reader, because the\n     core parser loses quoting.\n   - (b) Use schema-driven typing: the property's declared type decides how\n     `8px`, `0.2s` or `100%` are read.\n\n   Recommendation: (b) for dimensions, durations and colours, with (a) as the\n   fallback for free-form props. Also ask upstream for a `quoted` flag on\n   parsed references, which would remove the need for a second reader.\n2. **Units and colours.**\n   - `8px`, `0.2s`, `50%` and `1.5rem` are valid bare references, but they are\n     strings until a schema parses them.\n   - Hex colours must be quoted because of `#` comments.\n   - Alternative: `rgb(...)` / `oklch(...)` as links, for example\n     `(oklch 0.62 0.19 255)`, which is better for the associative model and for\n     theme maths.\n3. **`:` in values.** URLs, CSS pseudo-classes (`:hover`), media queries and\n   ratios (`16:9`) need quoting. Prefer structured links instead:\n   `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))` and `(aspect 16 9)`.\n4. **Comments and formatting are lost on round trip.** A WYSIWYG editor that\n   writes back to `.lino` will strip the user's comments and reflow the layout.\n   Options:\n   - (a) A CST mode upstream (trivia and spans, as meta-language already does\n     for CSS).\n   - (b) Make comments first-class links, for example `(note \"...\")`.\n   - (c) Patch-in-place edits using parser positions.\n\n   This needs an issue upstream in links-notation.\n5. **Ordering.** Link values are ordered, which is good for children and\n   keyframes. Property order, however, should be insignificant. The dialect\n   must state which parts are sequences (children, keyframes, transitions) and\n   which are sets (props). It must also define the meaning of a duplicate key:\n   last wins, as in lino-store logs.\n6. **Ids and scoping.** Ids are document-global strings, and nothing prevents\n   duplicates. Questions:\n   - Do we need namespaces (`login.save`) or nested id scopes per component?\n   - How do ids map to doublet numeric addresses, and are they stable across\n     edits? The editor needs stable ids for selection, undo and collaboration.\n7. **References for styles and tokens.** There is no built-in reference sigil.\n   A convention is needed:\n   - `@token.path` for design tokens\n   - `$param` for component parameters (the linksql / transformer convention)\n   - a bare id for elements and keyframe tracks\n\n   Open questions: resolution order (component, then theme, then base),\n   cycles, and fallbacks (`(or @color.accent \"#3390ec\")`).\n8. **Schemas and validation.** lino-schema is only a stub. [2026-11-01T11:47:26.035Z] [INFO]           "content": "# UI/UX projects inventory and migration plan (issue #1)\n\n> Scope: every repository with a user interface owned by `konard`,\n> `deep-foundation`, `link-foundation` and `link-assistant`, collected to\n> plan how each one moves to the associative UI framework (`link-foundation/ui`).\n> Snapshot date: 2026-11-01.\n\n## 1. Methodology\n\n1. **Raw listings.** Each owner was listed and saved (compact JSON, fields\n   `name, description, primaryLanguage, pushedAt, homepageUrl, isFork, stargazerCount`) to\n   [`../data/repos-<owner>.json`](../data/):\n   - `gh repo list OWNER --limit 1000 --no-archived --json ...` for `deep-foundation`,\n     `link-foundation`, `link-assistant`.\n   - `konard` has 1,463 public repositories, so `gh repo list` stopped at 1,000. Its listing\n     was rebuilt with the paginated REST API (`gh api users/konard/repos --paginate`),\n     using the same field names, with archived repos removed (5 archived, none of them UI).\n2. **Totals.**\n\n   | Owner | Not archived | Not forks | Notes |\n   | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |\n   | konard | 1,458 | 885 | 584 are `log-tmp-solution-draft-log-pr-*` (AI-solver logs), 22 are `test-*`, about 70 are copies of contributors' or clients' repos (`VisageDvachevsky-*`, `uselessgoddess-*`, `MixaByk1996-*`, `ideav-*`, ...). About 100 are konard's own projects. |\n   | deep-foundation | 107 | 102 | 2 archived (`boilerplate`, `payments-tinkoff-c2b-test-integration`), neither has a UI |\n   | link-foundation | 177 | 177 | 97 are copies of `deep-foundation` repos (pushed 2024-09 or 2025-02), so about 80 are its own projects |\n   | link-assistant | 30 | 30 | 1 archived (`scalper-trader-bot`), no UI |\n\n3. **Finding UI candidates.** A repo was a candidate if any of these held:\n   - its primary language is HTML, CSS, JS/TS, Vue, Svelte, Swift, Kotlin or Dart, and it has a UI;\n   - its description mentions an app, site, UI, visual, bot, widget or Mini App;\n   - it publishes a GitHub Pages `homepageUrl`.\n4. **Deep checks (120 repos).** For each candidate, a script read the recursive git tree\n   with `node_modules`, `dist` and `dev/log` skipped. It recorded:\n   - the number of files per extension (`tsx/jsx/vue/svelte/swift/kt/dart/html/css`);\n   - marker files (`vite.config`, `next.config`, `capacitor.config`, `electron/`,\n     `tailwind.config`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `Package.swift`, `index.html`);\n   - the dependency names in up to 4 `package.json` files.\n\n   The key repos also had their READMEs, `index.html` script tags and `src/` component\n   listings read.\n5. **Pattern search.** GitHub code search was run over all four owners for `i18next`,\n   `lino-i18n`, `d3-force`, `cytoscape`, `three`, `@telegram-apps/sdk`, `Telegram.WebApp`,\n   `@chakra-ui/react`, `@mui/material`, `tailwindcss`, `katex`, `mermaid`,\n   `electron-builder`, `@capacitor/core`, `doublets-web`, `links-notation`, `SettingsPanel`,\n   `chat-ui-kit` and `prefers-color-scheme`. The search API rate limit cut a few queries\n   short. Hits from code search can include docs or case-study folders, so the stack\n   columns below rely on `package.json` and the file tree first.\n6. **Priority rule.**\n   - **High:** the issue names the repo as a reference, it is actively developed\n     (pushed 2026), or it holds a UI pattern many other repos copy.\n   - **Medium:** an active app with a real UI that would get simpler after migration.\n   - **Low:** a single-page demo, a stale repo (2023-2024), a placeholder, a bot without\n     a web UI, or a third-party copy.\n\nLegend for the platform column: **W** web (usually GitHub Pages), **D** desktop (Electron),\n**M** mobile (Capacitor iOS/Android or native), **TMA** Telegram Mini App, **Bot** chat-bot UI\n(messages and keyboards), **Ext** browser or VS Code extension, **Lib** UI component library.\n\n\"**universal-app template**\" means the `examples/universal-app` folder copied from\n[`link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template):\nReact 19 without JSX (`createElement as h`), Vite, Capacitor (`@capacitor/android` and\n`@capacitor/ios`), and Electron (electron-builder or Electron Forge). It has no theme\nand no i18n, so each derived repo adds its own.\n\n## 2.
