Run them in parallel issues.\n\n### Wave 3: issue-named flagship apps\n- konard.github.io and immortality: migrate the settings, theme and network editor onto\n  the modules built from them in wave 0.\n- formal-ai: replace Chakra v3 with `ui` and keep its Electron and VS Code hosts.\n- meta-sovereign: move the chat modules into `ui`, then consume them.\n- link-cli web, links-notation website, lfs visualizer, meta-expression: switch to the\n  shared `LinksView`.\n- model-in-browser and react-chat-ui: replace the 6 third-party chat kits with the `ui`\n  chat (keep one kit as a comparison baseline).\n\n### Wave 4: vanilla and static pages\n- links-visuals, meta-language site, relative-meta-logic playground, meta-theory,\n  operator, money-making-machines, human-language (no-build entry)\n- konard demos: tron-demo, rotating-yin-yang, sonar, twittermatrix, single-page tools\n\nThese use the no-build ESM/UMD bundle and LiNo page descriptions.\n\n### Wave 5: Deep legacy (Next.js + Chakra/MUI + Capacitor + Electron)\n- deepcase, deepcase-app and deep: ship Chakra-v2 and MUI theme packs so the old\n  look stays reproducible, as the issue asks.\n- Then perception-app, deepmemo-app and sdk.\n- Then deepcase.github.io.\n- Archive or freeze deep-memo-app, nextjs-chatgpt-assistant-template and browser-extension.\n\n### Wave 6: native and other renderers\n- Swift (SwiftUI) and Kotlin (Jetpack Compose) bindings, piloted on air-navigator\n  (sensors/map), sleep-count-down or time-left (WidgetKit widget) and resonance.\n- Vue binding, piloted with the `lino-i18n` Vue example.\n- Bot renderer (Telegram/VK keyboards) for hive-mind, anygram, vietnam/lazada bots.\n- Terminal renderer for agent and start.\n\n## 6. Today each of our projects writes them again:\n\n- meta-sovereign has `shell/app-shell.js` (bottom bar up to 640 px, navigation\n  rail from 641 to 1023 px, drawer from 1024 px, Material 3) and\n  `panel-resize.js` (97 lines: draggable dividers with keyboard control and\n  saved widths) under `js/src/web/` of\n  https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign\n  ([research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n- deepcase opens handler and editor windows that float above the links\n  network (`imports/cyto/react.tsx` `CytoReactLayout`, `opened.tsx`\n  `useOpenedMethods()`), and its editor has a `VerticalSash` split\n  (`editor/editor-grid.tsx`). Known bugs: a handler window is drawn above a\n  modal (https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase-app/issues/290), a\n  handler is not fully visible\n  (https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase-app/issues/297), a window header\n  cannot be dragged (https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase-app/issues/198)\n  and the splitter position is not remembered\n  (https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase/issues/54)\n  ([research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)).\n- The WYSIWYG designer ({{F48}}) needs Visual Studio-like docked panels:\n  Toolbox, Properties, Document Outline and the canvas as the document area\n  ([existing solutions](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n  The classic themes ({{F43}}) need the same docking to reproduce older UIs\n  (R14).\n\n## Goal\n\n`@link-foundation/ui-components` provides the layout elements `stack`, `grid`,\n`split`, `tab-group`, `dock`, `window` and `app-shell`, described in Links\nNotation, rendered by `@link-foundation/ui-dom`, keyboard accessible, with one\nlayer manager that decides the stacking order of every floating surface and a\ndock layout that is saved and restored as Links Notation.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `stack` (direction, gap, align, justify, wrap) and `grid` (columns, rows,\n  areas, gap) as thin wrappers over CSS flexbox and grid.\n- `split` with two or more panes, draggable dividers, keyboard resizing\n  (WAI-ARIA window splitter pattern), min and max sizes, collapse, and\n  `remember-size` persistence through an injected storage object.\n- `tab-group` used inside docks (tab strip, close, reorder by drag and by\n  keyboard, overflow menu).\n- `dock`: regions left, right, top, bottom and centre; panels can be moved\n  between regions, stacked as tabs, floated, closed and restored.\n- `window`: a floating, movable, resizable surface with a draggable header,\n  kept inside the viewport.\n- `app-shell`: bottom bar, rail or drawer selected by breakpoints.\n- The layer manager (`createLayerManager`) used by windows, docks and later by\n  overlays ({{F27}}).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Dialogs, popovers, menus and toasts (they are {{F27}}; they only register\n  with the layer manager from this issue).\n- Lists, trees and tables ({{F29}}).\n- Theme visuals of classic UIs ({{F43}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **Blocked by {{F16}}** (ui-dom): we consume the element registry, the\n  custom-element base class and incremental updates to render the layout\n  elements. Before {{F16}} lands, the pure model files (`layer-manager.js`,\n  `dock-model.js`, `split-model.js`) can be written and tested without a DOM.\n- **Related:** {{F25}} (behaviour state machines; move the keyboard logic there\n  when it exists), {{F27}} (overlays register with the layer manager), {{F10}}\n  (the configuration layers that will store remembered sizes), {{F43}},\n  {{F48}}, {{F30}} (chat uses `split` and `app-shell`), {{F60}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-components/src/layout/` and export it from\n   `packages/ui-components/src/index.js`.\n2. Write `layer-manager.js`:\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @param {{ base?: number, step?: number }} [options]\n    * @returns {{\n    *   register(id: string, layer: 'base'|'dock'|'window'|'popover'|'modal'|'toast'): void,\n    *   raise(id: string): void,\n    *   zIndexOf(id: string): number,\n    *   unregister(id: string): void,\n    *   subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void\n    * }}\n    */\n   export function createLayerManager(options) {}\n   ```\n   Layers have a fixed order, so a raised `window` can never be above a\n   `modal`. Test `layer-manager.test.js` reproduces deepcase-app #290.\n3. Write `split-model.js`: `resizeSplit(sizes, index, delta, limits)` returns\n   new sizes that respect min, max and the total; `collapsePane`,\n   `restorePane`. Test `split-model.test.js`.\n4. Write `dock-model.js`, a pure model of the dock tree with\n   `movePanel(layout, panelId, target)`, `floatPanel`, `closePanel`,\n   `restorePanel`, `dockLayoutFromLinks(links)` and\n   `dockLayoutToLino(layout)`. Use the `links-notation` package for parsing;\n   never a regular expression. Test `dock-model.test.js` with a round trip.\n5. Register the custom elements with {{F16}}: `stack.js`, `grid.js`,\n   `split.js`, `tab-group.js`, `dock.js`, `window.js`, `app-shell.js`.\n6. Keyboard: split dividers use `role=\"separator\"` with `aria-valuenow`,\n   arrow keys move by 1 %, Home and End collapse and expand; tab strips follow\n   the APG tabs pattern; `Ctrl+F6`/`Ctrl+Shift+F6` cycle dock panels; a window\n   can be moved with Alt+arrow keys.\n7. Windows: header is the drag handle (pointer events with\n   `setPointerCapture`), clamp the window to the viewport on drag and on\n   `resize`, focus returns to the opener when it closes.\n8. `app-shell`: breakpoints are data, default `640px` and `1024px` as in\n   meta-sovereign; content uses `bottom-bar`, `rail` and `drawer` slots.\n9. Add the gallery page `packages/ui-components/examples/layout.html` with the\n   designer-like layout below, and Playwright tests.\n\nInput example (working names; the dialect is fixed in {{F03}}):\n\n```lino\n(designer-shell: [REDACTED]\n  (persist 'designer.layout')\n  (left: region (size 16rem) (panels toolbox outline))\n  (right: region (size 20rem) (panels properties))\n  (center: region (panels canvas))\n  (bottom: region (size 12rem) (collapsed true) (panels problems)))\n(chat-screen: split\n  (direction row)\n  (resizable true)\n  (remember-size 'chat.columns')\n  (children chat-list conversation))\n```\n\n`dockLayoutToLino` must give back the same structure after a panel moves, for\nexample `(right: region (size 20rem) (panels properties outline))`.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-components/src/layout/{layer-manager,split-model,dock-model}.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/src/layout/{stack,grid,split,tab-group,dock,window,app-shell}.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/src/layout/layout.css` (only CSS variables from\n  tokens, no hard-coded colours)\n- `packages/ui-components/tests/layout/*.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/tests/e2e/layout.spec.js` (Playwright)\n- `packages/ui-components/examples/layout.html`\n- `.changeset/*.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `createLayerManager` keeps every `modal` above every `window`, even after\n      `raise()` of the window (test `layer-manager.test.js`).\n- [ ] `resizeSplit` never returns a size below `min` or above `max`, and the\n      sum of sizes stays constant (test `split-model.test.js`).\n- [ ] A dock layout parsed from LiNo, changed by `movePanel`, and written with\n      `dockLayoutToLino` parses back to an equal model (test\n      `dock-model.test.js`).\n- [ ] A split remembers its sizes through the injected storage after reload\n      (Playwright).\n- [ ] Every divider, tab strip and window can be operated with the keyboard\n      only (Playwright test without mouse events).\n- [ ] A floating window cannot be dragged outside the viewport (Playwright).\n- [ ] `app-shell` shows a bottom bar at 600 px, a rail at 800 px and a drawer\n      at 1280 px width (three screenshots).\n- [ ] axe reports no violations on `examples/layout.html`.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnode --test packages/ui-components/tests/layout/*.test.js\nnpx playwright test packages/ui-components/tests/e2e/layout.spec.js\nnpm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run check:duplication\n```\n\nExpected screenshots: the designer-like dock with toolbox and outline on the\nleft, properties on the right, a canvas in the centre; then the same page\nafter moving `outline` to the right region; then the app shell at the three\nwidths.\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- meta-sovereign `shell/app-shell.js`, `panel-resize.js` (Unlicense, can be\n  ported).\n- deepcase floating windows and their bugs (learn only).\n- WAI-ARIA APG \"Window Splitter\" and \"Tabs\" patterns.\n- dockview and golden-layout are well-known docking libraries; they are not in\n  our research, so check their licence and current version before even\n  learning from them. Prefer our own small model, because the layout must be\n  stored as LiNo.\n- Floating UI (MIT) can position windows relative to anchors if needed.\n\n## References\n\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md\n- https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/\n- https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/\n"

[2026-11-01T11:50:07.657Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F16\ntitle: 'ui-dom: reference DOM renderer with custom elements'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 3\nblocked_by: [F08, F12]\nrequirements: [R3, R18]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nThe framework is a runtime interpreter of a links network with thin renderers\nper platform (principle 4 of\n[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).\nThe web reference renderer is `@link-foundation/ui-dom`: plain JavaScript,\ncustom elements (Web Components), no framework. React ({{F18}}) and Vue\n({{F19}}) adapters wrap it, components ({{F25}}, {{F26}}, {{F27}}) plug into it,\nand dev mode ({{F46}}) depends on one property of it: every rendered node\ncarries the stable link ID of the element it came from (principle 6).\n\nThe research recommends \"Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements) as the\nreference vanilla-JS renderer\" and warns against heavy code generation\n(section \"Recommendations\" A.2 and C in\n[existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\nkonard.github.io and immortality show that projecting state to `data-*`\nattributes and CSS variables works the same for plain JS, React and Vue\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)\npattern 3,\n[immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)\npattern 9).\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-dom/` that renders a `ui-store` links network into the DOM\nas custom elements, keeps it in sync incrementally from store change events,\napplies resolved styles from `ui-style`, dispatches declared actions as data,\nand marks every node with `data-link-id`.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `render(container, store, options)` and the convenience\n  `mountDocument(container, linoText, options)` (parse with `ui-core`, create a\n  store, render).\n- Custom elements with the `ui-` prefix for the basic kinds needed by the\n  dialect samples: `document`, `stack`, `text`, `button`, `image`, plus a\n  `ui-unknown` fallback for kinds without a registered renderer.\n- A kind registry (`defineKind`) so components and adapters add kinds without\n  touching the renderer.\n- Incremental updates: insert, update, remove and move of elements, batched in\n  one microtask per store transaction.\n- `data-link-id` on every element node; `handle.nodeFor(id)` and\n  `handle.idFor(node)` lookups.\n- Styles: inject the stylesheet produced by `ui-style` ({{F12}}) and token CSS\n  custom properties ({{F11}} output) with `adoptedStyleSheets` (fallback:\n  one `<style>` element).\n- Events: `(on press (navigate home))` dispatches a `ui-action` `CustomEvent`\n  and calls `options.onAction`. Handlers are data, never code.\n- `renderToHTML(store | tree, options)`: static HTML string export with the same\n  tags and `data-link-id` attributes (no hydration).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Full controls, state machines and accessibility behaviour ({{F25}}, {{F26}},\n  {{F27}}). The basic `button` here is a native `<button>` inside `ui-button`.\n- Layout primitives beyond `stack` ({{F28}}), animation ({{F44}}), dev mode\n  overlay ({{F46}}).\n- Hydration of server-rendered HTML; Shadow DOM per kind (may be added later\n  per kind).\n- Lit or any other runtime library: use plain custom elements (zero runtime\n  dependencies besides workspace packages and `links-notation`).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F08}} (blocker): the store API — read the tree, `subscribe(listener)` to\n  change events, transactions, stable IDs for every element including\n  anonymous ones. This issue assumes events shaped like\n  `{ type: 'insert' | 'update' | 'remove' | 'move', id, parentId, index, props }`;\n  adapt to the event shape actually merged in F08.\n- {{F12}} (blocker): the style resolver — a compiled stylesheet (or resolved\n  declarations per element and state) from LiNo `style` links such as\n  `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/styles.lino`.\n- Indirect: {{F06}} (`parse` to the element tree, used by `mountDocument`),\n  {{F11}} (token CSS custom properties).\n- Related: {{F05}} (Playwright and axe harness), {{F17}} (HTML import, the\n  reverse direction), {{F18}}, {{F19}}, {{F25}}, {{F46}}, {{F54}}.\n- To start before F12 merges, inject styles through `options.styles` (a CSS\n  string) and add the F12 call in the last step.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-dom/package.json` (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-dom\"`,\n   `\"type\": \"module\"`, `exports` for `.` and `./html`), `README.md` and\n   `src/index.d.ts`. Dependencies: `@link-foundation/ui-core`,\n   `@link-foundation/ui-store`, `@link-foundation/ui-style` (workspace).\n   Dev dependency for tests: `jsdom` (MIT).\n2. `src/kinds.js`: a registry.\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @typedef {object} KindSpec\n    * @property {string} tag  custom element name, e.g. 'ui-button'\n    * @property {(el: UiElement, ctx: RenderContext) => Element} create\n    * @property {(node: Element, el: UiElement, changed: string[], ctx: RenderContext) => void} update\n    * @property {(node: Element) => Element | null} [childrenSlot] where children go; null = no children\n    * @property {(node: Element) => void} [destroy]\n    */\n   /** @param {string} kind @param {KindSpec} spec */\n   export function defineKind(kind, spec) {}\n   ```\n   Registering a tag calls `customElements.define` only if\n   `customElements.get(tag)` is undefined, so importing twice is safe.\n3. `src/kinds/basic.js`: `document` (`ui-document`, sets `document.title` only\n   when `options.setTitle` is true), `stack` (`direction`, `gap` as CSS\n   `flex-direction` and `gap`), `text` (text content), `button` (native\n   `<button type=\"button\">` child, `label`, `variant` mirrored to an attribute\n   for style selectors, `disabled`), `image` (`<img>` with `src` and `alt`;\n   an `image` without `alt` gets `alt=\"\"` and a diagnostic), `unknown`.\n4. `src/render.js`: walk the store tree, create nodes, set\n   `data-link-id=\"<id>\"` on every element, keep `Map<id, Element>` and a\n   `WeakMap<Element, id>`. Return\n   `{ nodeFor(id), idFor(node), flush(), destroy() }`.\n5. `src/patch.js` and `src/scheduler.js`: on each store change event, queue a\n   patch; apply all queued patches in one microtask (`queueMicrotask`).\n   `update` re-uses the existing node and calls `spec.update` with the changed\n   prop names only; `move` uses `insertBefore`; `remove` calls `spec.destroy`\n   and drops map entries. `flush()` applies the queue synchronously (tests).\n6. `src/events.js`: for each `(on <event> <action...>)` prop, attach a listener\n   for the mapped DOM event (`press` = `click` on the native button, plus\n   Enter/Space through the native button). Dispatch\n   `new CustomEvent('ui-action', { bubbles: true, composed: true, detail })`\n   with `detail = { source: 'ok', event: 'press', action: ['navigate', 'home'] }`\n   and call `options.onAction?.(detail)`. Never call `eval`, `new Function`\n   or set `on*` attributes from document text.\n7. `src/styles.js`: build one `CSSStyleSheet` from the F12 output and token\n   variables; adopt it on the container's root node; selectors use the custom\n   element tag plus attributes, e.g. `ui-button[variant=\"filled\"]`. Light DOM\n   is used so that page CSS, dev mode and native form participation work.\n8. `src/html.js`: `renderToHTML(source, { kinds })` returns a string such as\n   `<ui-document data-link-id=\"app\"><ui-stack data-link-id=\"body\" ...>`. Escape\n   text and attribute values; never emit `on*` attributes or `<script>`.\n9. `mountDocument(container, text, options)` in `src/index.js`: parse with\n   `ui-core`, build a store with `ui-store`, call `render`, return\n   `{ store, handle }`.\n10. Example page `examples/ui-dom/index.html` + `main.js` that mounts\n    `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/document.lino` with the sample styles\n    and tokens, and a button that changes `greeting` through the store.\n11. Write the tests listed below, the README (API, kind registry, decision\n    \"plain custom elements, light DOM\" with the reasons above) and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-dom/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`, `src/index.d.ts`\n- `packages/ui-dom/src/{kinds.js,render.js,patch.js,scheduler.js,events.js,styles.js,html.js}`\n- `packages/ui-dom/src/kinds/basic.js`\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/setup-dom.js` (jsdom globals)\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/{render,incremental,events,styles,html,kinds}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/__snapshots__/document.html`\n- `examples/ui-dom/index.html`, `examples/ui-dom/main.js`\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `render.test.js`: `samples/document.lino` renders\n      `ui-document > ui-stack > (ui-text, ui-button)` and matches\n      `tests/__snapshots__/document.html`.\n- [ ] Every rendered element node has `data-link-id`; [2026-11-01T11:50:18.941Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F46\ntitle: 'Development/configuration mode inspector overlay'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 7\nblocked_by: [F10, F16]\nrequirements: [R9, R11]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nIssue #1 asks that \"the framework can enter a development and/or configuration\nmode in which every UI/UX element can be fully configured visually\" (R11) and\nthat we can \"modify the UI/UX on the fly on any of our websites\" (R9).\n[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)\n(\"Development/configuration mode and designer\") fixes the shape: a runtime\ninspector overlay, like React DevTools combined with Visual Studio's Live\nVisual Tree, over the links network that every page built with the framework\nalready has. Every rendered element keeps a stable link ID that maps back to\nits LiNo source, so selecting an element on screen selects a link.\n\nPrior art in our own projects:\n\n- konard.github.io already modifies its UI on the fly. Its\n  `src/pages/SettingsPage.jsx` renders rows `label | control | value | ↺ reset`,\n  marks changed rows with `is-changed`, has per-section and global resets and\n  a \"Your changes\" diff box. It edits global tokens only: there is no element\n  tree to select from\n  ([research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md),\n  sections 2.10 and 7.5).\n- formal-ai changes its UI through chat commands (`js/app/interface-commands.jsx`)\n  and has a debugger view (`js/app/debugger-view.jsx`), but \"there is no visual\n  editor or inspector\"\n  ([research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md),\n  sections 2.2 and 7.10).\n- anime-avatar exposes a dev state handle `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`\n  for in-app tests\n  ([research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md),\n  pattern 22).\n\n## Goal\n\nA new package `@link-foundation/ui-devmode` (`packages/ui-devmode/`) that any\npage rendered by `ui-dom` can enter at runtime. In dev mode the user hovers to\nhighlight, clicks to select, and inspects and edits the selected element in a\ndocked inspector. Every edit is written only to the `session` or `user`\nconfiguration layer, never to the committed `site` layer.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Three entry points: a keyboard shortcut (default `Alt+Shift+D`, ignored while\n  focus is in an editable field), the `?ui-dev` URL parameter, and a\n  `<ui-dev-mode>` custom element placed in the page.\n- A site policy, read from the site configuration, that can disable dev mode or\n  restrict entry points, writable layers and editable elements:\n\n  ```lino\n  (site-dev-mode: dev-mode\n    (enabled true)\n    (entry shortcut url-parameter element)\n    (shortcut 'Alt+Shift+D')\n    (write-layers session user)\n    (locked-elements payment-form))\n  ```\n\n  With `(enabled false)` the heavy inspector code is never loaded (dynamic\n  `import()` happens only after activation).\n- Overlay: hover highlight box with a label (`id: type`), click to select (the\n  click is captured and not delivered to the app while in pick mode), `Escape`\n  leaves pick mode, a second `Escape` closes dev mode.\n- Inspector, docked to the right and resizable, rendered in a shadow root so\n  site styles do not leak in. Tabs:\n  1. **Outline**: the element tree of the links network (tree view, keyboard\n     navigable per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern), synchronised with the selection.\n  2. **Properties**: property grid. Each row is\n     `name | editor | resolved value | source layer | reset`. The source layer\n     is one of `defaults`, `theme`, `site`, `user`, `session`. Changed rows are\n     marked (the konard.github.io `is-changed` idea).\n  3. **Styles**: style rules that match the element and the state they apply in.\n  4. **Tokens**: tokens used by the element, with resolved value and layer.\n  5. **Animations**: animations whose `target` is the element (read-only list).\n  6. **Source**: the LiNo text of the selected element (read-only here).\n- Typed editors chosen from the property type: number with unit, colour,\n  enum (select), boolean (switch), string, token reference. Plain native inputs\n  are acceptable; the controls from {{F26}} can replace them later.\n- Session edits are applied live. \"Save\" moves the session layer into the user\n  layer (persisted by ui-config). \"Discard\" clears the session layer. \"Reset\"\n  on a row removes that property from the top writable layer.\n- A test and agent handle: `globalThis.linkUiDevMode` with\n  `{ select(id), getSelection(), setProperty(id, name, value), close() }`,\n  present only while dev mode is open.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Exporting overrides, share links, agent instruction: {{F47}}.\n- Moving or inserting elements, toolbox, source editing: {{F48}}.\n- Editing animations and recordings: {{F49}}.\n- Pages not built with the framework: {{F50}}.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F10}} (blocker): the layered configuration. Consumed: resolving a property\n  to `{ value, layer }`, writing an override into `session` or `user`, removing\n  an override, moving `session` into `user`, change events. Use the names\n  merged in F10; the ones below are placeholders.\n- {{F16}} (blocker): the DOM renderer. Consumed: the element-to-link-ID mapping\n  (for example a `data-link-id` attribute or a `WeakMap`), the element tree, and\n  incremental re-render when the configuration changes.\n- Related: {{F14}} (source-preserving formatting for the Source tab), {{F12}}\n  and {{F11}} (style and token resolution for the Styles and Tokens tabs),\n  {{F44}} (animation list), {{F37}} (settings panel shares the editors),\n  {{F05}} (Playwright and axe infrastructure).\n- Work can start on the pure modules (policy, activation, outline, rows) with\n  a stub config object that has the API listed in step 4.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-devmode/` with `package.json`\n   (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-devmode\"`, ES module, JSDoc types), `src/`,\n   `tests/` and a `README.md`, following the workspace layout from {{F01}}.\n2. `src/policy.js`: `parseDevModePolicy(links)` returns\n   `{ enabled, entry: Set<string>, shortcut, writeLayers, lockedElements }`\n   from the `dev-mode` link of the site configuration. Defaults:\n   `enabled: true`, all three entries, `write-layers session user`. Unknown\n   keys produce a warning, not an error.\n3. `src/activation.js`:\n   `shouldActivate({ url, policy, hasElement })` (pure) and\n   `installActivation({ window, policy, onActivate })` (adds the key listener,\n   reads `URLSearchParams`, defines the `ui-dev-mode` custom element). The key\n   listener ignores events whose target is `input`, `textarea`, `select` or\n   `[contenteditable]`.\n4. `src/model.js` (pure, no DOM):\n   - `buildOutline(tree)` returns `{ id, type, children }[]`;\n   - `propertyRows(element, config)` returns\n     `{ name, type, value, layer, changed, locked }[]`, where `config` is the\n     F10 object with `resolve(id, name) -> { value, layer }`;\n   - `applyEdit(config, { id, name, value, layer })` validates the layer\n     against the policy and the value against the property type, then calls the\n     F10 write function. Writing to `site`, `theme` or `defaults` throws.\n5. `src/overlay.js`: highlight and selection boxes positioned with\n   `getBoundingClientRect()`, updated on scroll, resize and re-render,\n   `pointer-events: none`, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` (no transitions).\n6. `src/inspector.js` and `src/inspector.lino`: the inspector layout described\n   in LiNo and rendered with `ui-dom` inside a shadow root. Tabs as in scope.\n   Every visible string goes through a small message table so {{F13}} can\n   localise it later.\n7. `src/index.js`: `mountDevMode({ root, config, policy })` returns\n   `{ open(), close(), select(id), destroy() }`; it wires activation, overlay,\n   inspector and the `globalThis.linkUiDevMode` handle.\n8. `examples/index.html`: a page that renders the sample document\n   ([`samples/document.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/document.lino))\n   and mounts dev mode.\n9. Unit tests (`node --test`) for steps 2–4; a Playwright test for steps 5–8.\n10. Add a changeset for the new package.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-devmode/package.json`, `README.md`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/src/{index,policy,activation,model,overlay,inspector}.js`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/src/inspector.lino`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/examples/index.html`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/tests/{policy,activation,model}.test.js`\n- Browser test in the location set up by {{F05}}, e.g. `devmode.e2e.test.js`\n- `.changeset/*.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `parseDevModePolicy` handles the example policy above and the defaults;\n      `(enabled false)` makes `shouldActivate` return `false` for every entry.\n- [ ] Opening `examples/index.html?ui-dev` opens dev mode; `Alt+Shift+D` toggles\n      it; the shortcut does nothing while typing in a text input.\n- [ ] With `(enabled false)` no inspector module is requested over the network\n      (checked in the Playwright test).\n- [ ] Hovering `ok` shows a highlight labelled `ok: button`; clicking selects it\n      and does not trigger its `on press` action.\n- [ ] The Outline tab shows `app > body > greeting, ok` and selecting a row\n      selects the element on the page.\n- [ ] Changing the `ok` label in the property grid updates the page at once and\n      the row shows source layer `session`; React ({{F18}}) and Vue\n({{F19}}) adapters wrap it, components ({{F25}}, {{F26}}, {{F27}}) plug into it,\nand dev mode ({{F46}}) depends on one property of it: every rendered node\ncarries the stable link ID of the element it came from (principle 6).\n\nThe research recommends \"Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements) as the\nreference vanilla-JS renderer\" and warns against heavy code generation\n(section \"Recommendations\" A.2 and C in\n[existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\nkonard.github.io and immortality show that projecting state to `data-*`\nattributes and CSS variables works the same for plain JS, React and Vue\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)\npattern 3,\n[immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)\npattern 9).\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-dom/` that renders a `ui-store` links network into the DOM\nas custom elements, keeps it in sync incrementally from store change events,\napplies resolved styles from `ui-style`, dispatches declared actions as data,\nand marks every node with `data-link-id`.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `render(container, store, options)` and the convenience\n  `mountDocument(container, linoText, options)` (parse with `ui-core`, create a\n  store, render).\n- Custom elements with the `ui-` prefix for the basic kinds needed by the\n  dialect samples: `document`, `stack`, `text`, `button`, `image`, plus a\n  `ui-unknown` fallback for kinds without a registered renderer.\n- A kind registry (`defineKind`) so components and adapters add kinds without\n  touching the renderer.\n- Incremental updates: insert, update, remove and move of elements, batched in\n  one microtask per store transaction.\n- `data-link-id` on every element node; `handle.nodeFor(id)` and\n  `handle.idFor(node)` lookups.\n- Styles: inject the stylesheet produced by `ui-style` ({{F12}}) and token CSS\n  custom properties ({{F11}} output) with `adoptedStyleSheets` (fallback:\n  one `<style>` element).\n- Events: `(on press (navigate home))` dispatches a `ui-action` `CustomEvent`\n  and calls `options.onAction`. Handlers are data, never code.\n- `renderToHTML(store | tree, options)`: static HTML string export with the same\n  tags and `data-link-id` attributes (no hydration).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Full controls, state machines and accessibility behaviour ({{F25}}, {{F26}},\n  {{F27}}). The basic `button` here is a native `<button>` inside `ui-button`.\n- Layout primitives beyond `stack` ({{F28}}), animation ({{F44}}), dev mode\n  overlay ({{F46}}).\n- Hydration of server-rendered HTML; Shadow DOM per kind (may be added later\n  per kind).\n- Lit or any other runtime library: use plain custom elements (zero runtime\n  dependencies besides workspace packages and `links-notation`).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F08}} (blocker): the store API — read the tree, `subscribe(listener)` to\n  change events, transactions, stable IDs for every element including\n  anonymous ones. Create `packages/ui-dom/package.json` (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-dom\"`,\n   `\"type\": \"module\"`, `exports` for `.` and `./html`), `README.md` and\n   `src/index.d.ts`. Dependencies: `@link-foundation/ui-core`,\n   `@link-foundation/ui-store`, `@link-foundation/ui-style` (workspace).\n   Dev dependency for tests: `jsdom` (MIT).\n2. `src/kinds.js`: a registry.\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @typedef {object} KindSpec\n    * @property {string} tag  custom element name, e.g. 'ui-button'\n    * @property {(el: UiElement, ctx: RenderContext) => Element} create\n    * @property {(node: Element, el: UiElement, changed: string[], ctx: RenderContext) => void} update\n    * @property {(node: Element) => Element | null} [childrenSlot] where children go; null = no children\n    * @property {(node: Element) => void} [destroy]\n    */\n   /** @param {string} kind @param {KindSpec} spec */\n   export function defineKind(kind, spec) {}\n   ```\n   Registering a tag calls `customElements.define` only if\n   `customElements.get(tag)` is undefined, so importing twice is safe.\n3. `src/kinds/basic.js`: `document` (`ui-document`, sets `document.title` only\n   when `options.setTitle` is true), `stack` (`direction`, `gap` as CSS\n   `flex-direction` and `gap`), `text` (text content), `button` (native\n   `<button type=\"button\">` child, `label`, `variant` mirrored to an attribute\n   for style selectors, `disabled`), `image` (`<img>` with `src` and `alt`;\n   an `image` without `alt` gets `alt=\"\"` and a diagnostic), `unknown`.\n4. `src/render.js`: walk the store tree, create nodes, set\n   `data-link-id=\"<id>\"` on every element, keep `Map<id, Element>` and a\n   `WeakMap<Element, id>`. Return\n   `{ nodeFor(id), idFor(node), flush(), destroy() }`.\n5. `src/patch.js` and `src/scheduler.js`: on each store change event, queue a\n   patch; apply all queued patches in one microtask (`queueMicrotask`).\n   `update` re-uses the existing node and calls `spec.update` with the changed\n   prop names only; `move` uses `insertBefore`; `remove` calls `spec.destroy`\n   and drops map entries. `flush()` applies the queue synchronously (tests).\n6. `src/events.js`: for each `(on <event> <action...>)` prop, attach a listener\n   for the mapped DOM event (`press` = `click` on the native button, plus\n   Enter/Space through the native button). Dispatch\n   `new CustomEvent('ui-action', { bubbles: true, composed: true, detail })`\n   with `detail = { source: 'ok', event: 'press', action: ['navigate', 'home'] }`\n   and call `options.onAction?.(detail)`. Never call `eval`, `new Function`\n   or set `on*` attributes from document text.\n7. `src/styles.js`: build one `CSSStyleSheet` from the F12 output and token\n   variables; adopt it on the container's root node; selectors use the custom\n   element tag plus attributes, e.g. `ui-button[variant=\"filled\"]`. Light DOM\n   is used so that page CSS, dev mode and native form participation work.\n8. `src/html.js`: `renderToHTML(source, { kinds })` returns a string such as\n   `<ui-document data-link-id=\"app\"><ui-stack data-link-id=\"body\" ...>`. Escape\n   text and attribute values; never emit `on*` attributes or `<script>`.\n9. `mountDocument(container, text, options)` in `src/index.js`: parse with\n   `ui-core`, build a store with `ui-store`, call `render`, return\n   `{ store, handle }`.\n10. Example page `examples/ui-dom/index.html` + `main.js` that mounts\n    `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/document.lino` with the sample styles\n    and tokens, and a button that changes `greeting` through the store.\n11. experimental OCR, location, assistant name, demo mode, diagnostics |\n\n### 2.4 Theming\n\n- **Tokens.** `--fa-*` custom properties are defined in `01-tokens.css`. Dark values come from `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback.\n- **Selector counts.** About 248 `[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and 244 `[data-theme=\"light\"]` selectors across the CSS. Most dark overrides live in `06-dark-theme.css`.\n- **Chakra bridge.** `theme.js` maps tokens 1:1, e.g. `fa.surface.card → var(--fa-surface-card)`. Chakra components therefore follow the same CSS variables without a parallel theme object.\n- **Root-class composition.** Skins, chat styles, composer styles and icon packs are orthogonal root classes. The CSS combines them, e.g. `.ui-skin-glass.composer-style-glass-clear`.\n\n### 2.5 i18n\n\n- **Runtime.** `js/i18n.js` is an IIFE exposing `window.FormalAiI18n`. It calls `loadCatalogs([...])` and `createI18n({locales, defaultLocale:'en', fallback:['en']})`, then dispatches `formal-ai:i18n-ready`.\n- **Catalog format.** Nested Links Notation blocks (`en` / `buttons` / `key \"...\"`) with `\"\"\"` multiline strings ([#117](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/117)).\n- **CI checks.**\n  - Key parity across all locales (`tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`).\n  - A lint against hardcoded natural language ([#659](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/659), R379).\n- **Gaps.**\n  - `PUBLISHED_RUNTIME_SOURCE = \"lino-i18n@0.3.0\"` in `i18n.js`, while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n  - The vanilla pages use their own JS `LABELS` dicts instead of the catalogs.\n\n### 2.6 Preferences & memory\n\n- **Preferences (`preferences.js`, 123 lines).**\n  - A hand-rolled Links Notation reader/writer with root `demo_preferences` and indented `key \"value\"` lines. Booleans are stored as `on`/`off`.\n  - API: `[REDACTED] {load, save, format, parse, STORAGE_KEY, ROOT}`.\n  - Every page shares the `formal-ai.preferences.v1` key.\n  - It does not use the `links-notation` parser.\n- **Memory (`memory.js`).**\n  - IndexedDB database `formal-ai-demo`, store `events`, root `demo_memory`, bundle header `formal_ai_bundle`, `LINK_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION \"0.2.0\"`.\n  - Events are append-only. `EXPORT_FIELDS` include `kind`, `role`, `intent`, `tool`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `content`, `attachments`, `sentAt`, `evidence`, `accessCount`, `writeCount`, `conversationId` and `conversationTitle`.\n  - It exports `formal-ai-memory.lino`. Import, reset and purge sit behind confirmations ([#196](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/196)).\n  - It reports a `doublets-web` backend only if that global runtime is present.\n\n### 2.7 Web search component\n\n- **Ranking.** `getDefaultProviderIds()` selects the providers, and `mergeResults` merges their results with the `rrf` strategy and `removeDuplicates`.\n## 6. Duplication candidates\n\n| Duplicate | Where | Recommendation |\n|---|---|---|\n| `h()` hyperscript, `segmentedControl`, locale and theme resolution | `js/site-chrome.js` lines 13–15 state they are \"intentionally re-implemented here verbatim\" from `js/download/download.js` (line 752) | Single framework primitive (`SegmentedControl`, `ThemeChooser`, `LocaleChooser`) shared by all pages |\n| Per-locale `LABELS` JS dicts | `site-chrome.js`, `download.js` | Move into lino-i18n catalogs |\n| Hand-rolled Links Notation parsing | `preferences.js` (parse/format), `memory.js` (bundle reader/writer) | Official `links-notation` parser plus `lino-objects-codec` |\n| Theme token values | `01-tokens.css`, `06-dark-theme.css` (1,097 lines of overrides), `landing.css`, download CSS | One token document → generated CSS vars for every page and theme |\n| Icon mapping tables | `toolbar-icons.jsx` (three parallel tables), emoji glyphs in `glyphs.jsx` | One icon registry in Links Notation (action → per-pack glyph) |\n| Chat UI per host | Web `/app/`, Electron wrapper, VS Code webview (#353 wants parity) | Framework chat components consumed by every host |\n| JS → TS mirror | `ts/` generated from `js/` | Generate bindings from one source (meta-language) instead of mirroring |\n| Theme applied to vanilla and Chakra separately | CSS classes vs Chakra components (#541, #550 bugs) | One component set; no mixed styling paths |\n| Similar components across other link-foundation/link-assistant UIs | Settings panels, theme/locale choosers, issue reporters, chat composers | Flag for the cross-org inventory (see sibling research files) |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Problems and limitations\n\n1. **Monolith.** `application.jsx` is 1,445 lines with one `App`. Its predecessor `main.jsx` reached 9,269 lines (#951); a CI line budget and boundary lint were needed to contain it.\n2. **Mixed paradigms.** Three styles coexist: React + Chakra (partial migration), plain CSS classes, and vanilla IIFE pages using `window.*` globals (`FormalAiI18n`, `FormalAiPreferences`, `FormalAiVendor`). There is no module graph across pages.\n3. **CSS order dependence.** The 7 stylesheets must load in numeric order. Dark mode is a large override sheet rather than token swaps, which produces recurring \"element not themed\" bugs (#388, #541, #550).\n4. **Version drift.** `i18n.js` reports `lino-i18n@0.3.0` while `package.json` pins `0.4.0`.\n5. **Limited locales.** Only en, ru, zh and hi. There is no RTL support or pluralization evidence in the UI layer.\n6. **Accessibility is partial.**\n   - No automated a11y audit.\n   - Reduced motion is handled in a single stylesheet, even though animations (minimum message time, step reveal) are central.\n   - The sidebar has a mouse-scroll bug (#447).\n   - No documented contrast checks beyond a `contrast` skin.\n7. **Mobile fragility.** Repeated mobile bugs: iOS accessory bar, focus layout, overflow and menu width (#108, #110, #112).\n8. **Committed minified bundles** make diffs and reviews noisy (#953).\n9. **No platform-guideline mapping.** Skins are named after looks (glass, material) rather than formally following Apple HIG, Material 3 or Fluent. Material and glass are approximations.\n10. **No WYSIWYG configuration.** All configuration happens through the settings panel or chat commands; there is no visual editor or inspector.\n11. **No animation recording.** Animations are CSS/JS timing only; there is no capture or replay of UI sessions, even though the event log could support it.\n12. **Charts.** No chart components; diagrams rely on Mermaid only, and Mermaid rendering breaks on GitHub (#1190).\n13. **Asset licensing.** Icon packs are third-party fonts (FontAwesome, Material Symbols, Bootstrap Icons, Ionicons, Remix, Tabler), not public domain. A public-domain-only framework needs its own set or a `names` fallback.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes (formal-ai → associative UI framework)\n\n1. **Phase 0: contracts first.**\n   - Freeze the existing external contracts as compatibility tests: `formal-ai.preferences.v1` (root `demo_preferences`), `data-theme`, the `formal-ai:i18n-ready` event, `window.FormalAi*` hooks and all `data-testid` values.\n   - The framework's config loader should read the old preference document and map each key (`uiSkin`, `chatStyle`, `composerStyle`, `toolbarIconPack`, `glassOpacity`, `uiLanguage`, …) onto framework config links.\n2. **Phase 1: tokens.**\n   - Express `01-tokens.css` plus the dark overrides as one Links Notation token document with context-relative values (light/dark/contrast).\n   - Generate the CSS vars and the Chakra semantic-token bridge from it.\n   - Delete `06-dark-theme.css` incrementally, verified by per-theme screenshot diffs (#672 F1).\n3. **Phase 2: shared chrome.** Replace `site-chrome.js` and `download.js` helpers with framework `SegmentedControl`/`ThemeChooser`/`LocaleChooser` vanilla-JS bindings, and move the `LABELS` dicts into lino-i18n catalogs.\n4. **Phase 3: skins as framework themes.**\n   - Map `ui-skin-*`, `chat-style-*`, `composer-style-*` and `toolbar-icon-pack-*` to framework theme axes.\n   - Add guideline-conformant skins (Material 3, Fluent 2, Apple HIG/glass) to satisfy #557.\n   - Keep the class names as aliases during the transition.\n5. **Phase 4: components.**\n   - Extract framework components in this order:\n     - `CollapsibleSection`\n     - `ToolbarButton` with priority overflow\n     - Settings rows with reset\n     - Composer\n     - Message\n     - Reasoning-trace view\n     - Issue reporter\n     - Links-network view\n   - Keep each `data-testid`.\n   - This also advances #951 (split monolith) and #550 (uniform components).\n6. **Phase 5: storage.**\n   - Back the framework's state store with the same append-only event-log shape as `memory.js`, so UI edits, memory and recordings share one exportable `.lino` bundle and `doublets-web` can be dropped in later.\n   - Replace hand-rolled parsers with `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec`.\n7. **Phase 6: hosts.** Electron and VS Code webviews consume the same framework package (#353 parity). React Native, Swift and Kotlin bindings reuse the token, i18n and config documents rather than the DOM components.\n8. **Risks.**\n   - Chakra coupling: the framework should own the tokens and treat Chakra as one optional binding.\n   - The generated `ts/` mirror must be regenerated, not hand-edited.\n   - The CI gates (i18n parity, UI boundary, line budgets) must keep passing throughout the migration.",

[2026-11-01T11:50:41.648Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F17\ntitle: 'HTML/DOM to LiNo importer'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 3\nblocked_by: [F06]\nrequirements: [R6, R9, R23]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nIssue #1 asks that \"any other UI/UX framework is just a Links Notation\ndocument\" (R6), that every website can be modified on the fly (R9) and that\nexisting projects are easy to migrate (R23). Two later features need to turn\nexisting HTML into the UI dialect:\n\n- dev mode on pages that were not built with the framework ({{F50}}) must\n  import the live DOM, keep a map from link IDs to DOM nodes and show it in the\n  inspector;\n- migration of our projects ({{F57}}–{{F65}}) and the JSX/Vue importers\n  ({{F51}}) start from HTML.\n\n`meta-language` (npm 0.46.0) already has a native HTML import (tag stack, raw\n`script`/`style` text) and a CSS import with a lossless CST (trivia and spans)\n([links-notation-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)\nsection 3). The ARCHITECTURE puts importers in `@link-foundation/ui-convert`.\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-convert/` with an HTML/DOM importer that turns an HTML\nstring or a live DOM subtree into a UI dialect LiNo document, plus a map from\ngenerated link IDs back to source nodes and source spans.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `importHtml(text, options)` for HTML strings (Node and browser), using the\n  `meta-language` HTML import for source spans.\n- `importDom(root, options)` for a live DOM subtree (browser and jsdom), which\n  returns `nodeMap: Map<string, Node>` for dev mode.\n- One shared intermediate form `{ tag, attrs, children, text, span }` and one\n  mapping step from it to dialect elements.\n- A mapping table from semantic HTML to dialect kinds, with a lossless\n  fallback element for everything else.\n- Inline `style` attributes to `(style ...)` links; classes and other\n  attributes preserved.\n- Deterministic link IDs.\n- Security: scripts and `on*` attributes are dropped with a diagnostic.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Importing stylesheets and `<style>` rules into `ui-style` rules (follow-up\n  through the `meta-language` CSS import; keep `<style>` text as a raw link).\n- Computed styles, JSX, MUI and Vue SFC ({{F51}}).\n- The dev mode UI for foreign pages ({{F50}}).\n- Exporting LiNo back to HTML (that is `renderToHTML` in {{F16}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F06}} (blocker): the element tree types and `parse`, used to check that\n  every import result is a valid dialect document (round trip:\n  import, format, parse, compare trees).\n- Related: {{F03}} (dialect vocabulary: use its kind and prop names in the\n  mapping table), {{F07}} (typed values: units and colours in inline styles),\n  {{F16}} (reverse direction), {{F50}}, {{F51}}, {{F57}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-convert/` (`@link-foundation/ui-convert`, ES module)\n   with `src/html/` and `tests/html/`. If {{F51}} or another issue already\n   created the package, add the `html` folder to it. Dependencies:\n   `links-notation`, `meta-language` (check the current version and licence\n   in its `package.json`; it is a link-foundation package), and\n   `@link-foundation/ui-core`. Dev dependency: `jsdom` (MIT).\n2. Read the `meta-language` README and exports and find its HTML import entry\n   point and the node shape it returns (tags, attributes, text, spans). Write\n   `src/html/from-meta-language.js` that converts that result into the\n   intermediate form:\n   ```js\n   /** @typedef {{ tag: string, attrs: [string, string][], children: HtmlNode[],\n    *   text?: string, span?: { start: number, end: number } }} HtmlNode */\n   ```\n   If the HTML import is not usable from the npm package, stop and open an\n   issue in https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language instead of writing\n   a regex HTML parser.\n3. `src/html/from-dom.js`: walk a DOM `Node` into the same intermediate form,\n   skipping comment nodes unless `options.comments` is true and recording\n   `Node` references for `nodeMap`.\n4. `src/html/mapping.js`: a table, kept as data, for example:\n\n   | HTML                                  | Dialect kind                    |\n   | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |\n   | `button`, `input[type=button]`        | `button` (`label` from text)    |\n   | `a[href]`                             | `link` (`href` quoted)          |\n   | `p`, `span`, `h1`–`h6`, `label`       | `text` (`level` for headings)   |\n   | `img`                                 | `image` (`src`, `alt`)          |\n   | `input[type=checkbox]`                | `checkbox`                      |\n   | `input[type=text]`, `textarea`        | `text-field`, `text-area`       |\n   | `ul`, `ol`                            | `list`                          |\n   | `div`, `section`, `main`, `nav`, etc. | `html` fallback with `(tag ...)` |\n\n   Use the kind names fixed by {{F03}}; when a name is missing there, use the\n   `html` fallback, which keeps every attribute:\n   `(card-1: html (tag div) (attr class 'card') ...)`.\n\n5. `src/html/ids.js`: ID rules. Use the element's `id` attribute when it is a\n   valid LiNo reference and unique; otherwise a path ID from the tag and\n   sibling index (`div-0-2-1`). The same input must always give the same IDs.\n6. `src/html/style.js`: split inline `style` into declarations and emit\n   `(style (padding 8px) (color '#3390ec'))`. Quote any value that contains\n   `#`, `:`, `(`, `)`, whitespace or a quote; use `escapeReference` from\n   `links-notation`, never hand-made quoting.\n7. `src/html/import.js`: build `Link` objects from `links-notation` and format\n   them with `formatLinks` (never string concatenation). Return\n   `{ text, tree, nodeMap?, spans, diagnostics }` where `spans` maps link ID\n   to `{ start, end }` in the source HTML.\n8. Security rules: drop `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, every `on*`\n   attribute and `javascript:` URLs, each with a diagnostic\n   `{ code: 'dropped-script', id, message }`. Keep `<style>` text as\n   `(raw-css '...')` on the parent.\n9. Add fixtures and tests (below), a README section and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-convert/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`\n- `packages/ui-convert/src/html/{import.js,from-meta-language.js,from-dom.js,mapping.js,ids.js,style.js}`\n- `packages/ui-convert/tests/html/fixtures/*.html` and the expected\n  `*.lino` next to each one (at least: `button-form.html`, `landing.html`\n  with nav and cards, `inline-styles.html`, `unsafe.html` with scripts and\n  `onclick`, `unicode.html`)\n- `packages/ui-convert/tests/html/{import-html,import-dom,mapping,ids,style,security,roundtrip}.test.js`\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\nExample: input `<button id=\"ok\" class=\"primary\">OK</button>` gives\n\n```lino\n(ok: button\n  (label 'OK')\n  (attr class primary))\n```\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `importHtml` and `importDom` (jsdom) give the same `text` for every\n      fixture (`import-dom.test.js`).\n- [ ] Every fixture's output equals its expected `.lino` file.\n- [ ] `roundtrip.test.js`: for every fixture, `parse(text)` with `ui-core`\n      succeeds without diagnostics and formatting it again gives the same\n      links.\n- [ ] IDs are deterministic (importing twice gives identical text) and unique\n      (duplicate `id` attributes get suffixes, tested).\n- [ ] `spans` points at the original source of each element (a test slices the\n      HTML with each span and finds the tag name).\n- [ ] `importDom` returns a `nodeMap` whose entries are the original DOM nodes.\n- [ ] `security.test.js`: `unsafe.html` output contains no `script`,\n      `onclick` or `javascript:` text and reports one diagnostic per dropped\n      item.\n- [ ] Hex colours, URLs and `:`-containing values are quoted; Some skin rules sit thousands of lines away\n   from their definitions, for example\n   `:root[data-theme='dark'][data-skin='t3']` at around line 13,589 versus the\n   skin block at around line 3,317. Users cannot share or edit skins as files. Preferences live\n   in scattered localStorage keys, not in LiNo, which contradicts the project's\n   own \"everything is links\" model.\n3. **Bundle size.** `app.min.js` is 4.6 MB, committed, and served whole. Other providers get Telegram's shape. A framework needs\n   provider-neutral component contracts, with capabilities passed as data.\n7. **Licensing.**\n   - Behaviour is \"learned, never copied\" from GPL/AGPL clients (tweb,\n     telegram-tt, tdesktop, Signal, Element).\n   - Icons are Lucide (ISC).\n   - Neither is public domain. 19, 25, 26, 28, 31, 36, 39, 41).\n\n### 1.3 Links Notation usage\n\nNeither repo uses Links Notation. There are no `.lino` files and no `links-notation` dependency or reference in either repo. All configuration is TypeScript/JS objects, serialized as JSON to localStorage, to a URL hash (immortality) or to a downloaded `acs-config.json` (anime-avatar). Both formats are flat or two-level key/value maps, so they map directly to links (see section 9).\n\n## 2. Configurability model\n\n### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n\n`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n\n- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Examples: `PALETTES` (12), `SURFACES` (13 panel materials), `FRAME_STYLES` (9), `BACKGROUNDS` (21), `BACKDROP_GRADIENTS` (7), `FONTS`, `TITLE_STYLES`, `TEXT_EFFECTS`, `INTROS`, `CHART_STYLES`, `CURSORS`, `TABLE_STYLES`, `SCROLLBAR_STYLES`, `ENTRANCES`, `SOUNDS` (26). Id union types are derived with `(typeof X)[number]['id']`, so adding an option updates the types.\n- **Reference registry.** `REFERENCES: Record<ReferenceId, {label, url}>` cites the design source of each option (Arwes, thegridcn, Soul Extract, glitchy.website and others). The panel renders these as links next to each axis.\n- **Axes.** `AXES` has 49 entries:\n  `Axis = ChoiceAxis {kind:'choice', options, display?:'buttons'|'select'} | ToggleAxis {kind:'toggle'} | RangeAxis {kind:'range', min, max, step, unit}`.\n  The shared base is `{key, label, group, description?, sources?}`. `SETTING_GROUPS` defines 8 groups: Color, Panels, Type & text, Scene, HUD & charts, Controls & data, Motion, Audio.\n- **Pure functions over the schema:**\n  - `coerceAxisValue` and `coerceSoundList` validate one value.\n  - `mergeSettings(base, raw)` accepts untrusted input and drops invalid keys.\n  - `diffSettings` and `diffFromDefaults` compute what changed.\n  - `parseStoredSettings` and `migrateLegacySettings` handle storage. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n  - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n  - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`--corner`, `--border-width`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`, `--font-scale`, `--chart-line`, `--bg-speed`, `--motion-scale`, `--bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n  - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n  - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `--fill` variable.\n  - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n  - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n  - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\n### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n\n- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n  - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n  - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n  - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n  - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.\n  - Lights: key, fill, rim and ambient color and intensity.\n  - Scene and cameras: `bg`, ground, `floorGrid`, `camera*`, a separate `svgCam*` set.\n  - Toggles: `autoRotate`, `mirrorArms`, `showFPS`, and an experimental joint gizmo.\n- `App.jsx` keeps cfg in React state, persists it to localStorage key `acs_B` merged over defaults, and keeps the view (`editor|tests|split|none`) in `?view=` and `acs_view`. It exposes `window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}` so in-app tests can drive the UI.\n- There is no schema. Each control is hand-wired in `Editor.jsx` using `Studio.Section/Row/Slider/ColorPick/Select/Chips/Toggle` from `ui.jsx`. Ranges, steps and labels live inline in JSX.\n- Every `Section` has a randomize button and a reset button. `randomizers.js` implements per-group randomize and reset, and respects `ACS_BONE_LIMITS`.\n- Config I/O: Export downloads `acs-config.json`. Import does `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(text)}` and reports errors with `alert`.\n- Engine binding: `apply.js` `ACS_applyAll` runs every frame and pushes cfg into three.js state (pose merge, idle, gestures, look-at, expressions, blink, materials, grid, debug helpers). This is a declarative-state to imperative-scene reconciler.\n\n### 2.3 anime-avatar archive\n\n- `ConfigPanel.jsx` holds about 17 props: skin, hair, eye and clothes colors, blink interval, animation speed, idle and blink toggles, background, `detailLevel` 1 to 10, legs, 3D, shadows, LOD, scale, `modelUrl`.\n- `useAnimationCycle({minInterval, maxInterval, animationDuration, excludeFromCycle})` picks a random named animation (idle, happy, wave, nod, thinking, surprised) on a timer.",

    |\n\n## 6. Patterns worth adopting\n\n1. **One declarative schema per configurable surface.** Declare every setting once as `{key, label, group, kind, options|min/max/step/unit, description, sources}`. Validation, defaults, the panel, presets, randomizer, diff, sharing, migration and tests all derive from it (immortality `AXES`). In the framework this schema should itself be a Links Notation document.\n2. **Option catalogs with ids, labels, descriptions and provenance.** Derive types from the catalog (`(typeof X)[number]['id']`), so adding an option to a theme is a one-line data change.\n3. **Store and share only the diff from defaults.** `diffFromDefaults`, plus a version tag (`v:2`), makes share links short, survives default changes and supports \"N customized\" counters.\n4. **Treat all external config as untrusted.** `mergeSettings(base, raw)` coerces each value and drops unknown keys. Apply this to imports, URL hashes and storage (anime-avatar currently does not).\n5. **Versioned persistence with intent-preserving migration.** Keep only what the user changed from the old defaults, so the new defaults still take effect.\n6. **Comfort settings stay local.** When applying a shared look or preset, keep the viewer's accessibility and comfort keys (motion, sound, volume). Lock the same keys from randomization.\n7. **Presets are partial overrides over a base**, with `isPresetActive` detection and source citations.\n8. **Randomize and reset per group and globally, with an injected RNG**, respecting constraints (bone limits) and locked keys. This makes visual exploration safe and reproducible.\n9. **Project theme state to `data-*` attributes and CSS variables** instead of re-rendering. This is cheap, framework-agnostic and works the same for plain JS, React and Vue. A test then checks that every option has a CSS rule (`styling.test.ts`).\n10. **High-frequency visuals bypass the component tree.** Pointer glow (`--mx/--my`), canvas backgrounds and the per-frame `apply.js` loop write directly to the DOM or scene.\n11. **Animations as pure functions of time** (`decipherFrame(text,t,seed)`, `ACS_gestureDelta(name,t,mood,easing)`). They are deterministic, so they can be recorded, replayed, scrubbed and tested. This is the natural basis for the framework's animation recording: record the clock and inputs, not the pixels.\n12. **Additive animation layers.** Each source contributes deltas that are summed each frame, with envelopes for start and end, so nothing snaps (anime-avatar issue-28).\n13. **Named easing and envelope catalog** (`ACS_EASINGS`, bell and sustained) shared by every animation.\n14. **Domain constraints as data** (`ACS_BONE_LIMITS` in degrees, with references), used for clamping sliders, randomizers and gizmos alike.\n15. **Reduced motion and photosensitivity by default.** Use `motionAllowed()` (the setting combined with `prefers-reduced-motion`), and avoid hard flashes, which is the reason the flicker was replaced.\n16. **Accessible panel conventions**: a non-modal docked drawer, Escape to close, focus return, arrow-key tabs, `aria-pressed` toggles, `<output>` for ranges, an `aria-live` change counter, and a clipboard fallback.\n17. **Accessible data twins**: every chart has a table equivalent, `role=img` and a text summary.\n18. **UI sound theme** as a separate configurable layer: an event-to-sounds map, modes (random, cycle, layer), master bus, lazy AudioContext, throttling, and a cue event bus that visuals can subscribe to.\n19. **Zero-binary assets.** Generate visuals and sounds procedurally so the framework's own assets are trivially public domain.\n20. **Provenance on every borrowed item** (`source`, `sourceUrl`, `credit`, `license`, `attributionRequired`), with license decisions recorded per source (MIT port, GPL ideas only, no license means reference only).\n21. **Conditional attribution UI**: show credits only when the asset's metadata or license requires it, and always expose a Metadata/Credits view.\n22. **Dev mode exposes a state handle** (`window.__acs = {cfg, setCfg, probe}`) plus an in-app test runner that does not autostart, can be stopped and keeps its scroll position (issue #19). This fits a \"configuration mode\" well.\n23. **View state in the URL** (`?view=`, `#ui=`), consumed and then cleaned with `replaceState`, and listening to `hashchange`.\n24. **Graceful optional backends**: AI features return a typed `{status:'no-backend'}` instead of failing.\n25. **URL normalization for user-supplied resources** (GitHub `blob/` to raw) and per-asset fix-up flags such as `flipped`.\n26. **Case-study per issue** (requirements table, root causes, rejected libraries). Both repos already do this, and link-foundation/ui should continue it.\n\n## 7. Duplication candidates\n\nBoth repos independently built the same subsystems. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 8.1 immortality\n\n1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n\n### 8.2 anime-avatar\n\n1. **No build step in production**: Babel standalone transpiles JSX in the browser on every load, React runs in its development UMD build, and dependencies come from unpkg without SRI. This is slow, fragile and unsafe for a framework.\n2. **Global namespace modules** (`window.ACS_*`, `window.Studio`, `window.__acs`) with implicit load order in `index.html`.\n3. **Monoliths**: `Editor.jsx` is 2381 lines in one component, and `apply.js` is 1316 lines. All styling is inline style objects, so there is no theming.\n4. **Two divergent apps** in one repo (studio in `public/` and the archived Vite app in `src/`). The README mostly documents the archive, and the archive's 2D and 3D part trees (`components/svg/*`, `components/three/*`) duplicate each other.\n5. **Weak config validation**: import does a shallow `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse}`. Nested `rot/scale/expr` are not validated, unknown keys persist, errors use `alert`. There is no storage version or migration, and the key `acs_B` is opaque.\n6. **No schema**: ranges and labels are duplicated between `Editor.jsx` and `randomizers.js`.\n7. **Licensing**: the proprietary GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, and vague license strings (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\"). The license-string heuristic in `attributionRequired` can miss cases.\n8. **Bugs called out in [issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)** (since addressed): the Alicia model loaded back-to-front, GitHub `blob/` URLs failed, loading errors never auto-hid, tests autostarted and could not be stopped, the test log forced scroll to the bottom, split view was shown on mobile, and copyright was shown unconditionally.\n9. **Bugs called out in [issue #28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/28)**: an unnatural wave, non-anatomical slider ranges shown in radians, and gestures replacing look-at instead of adding to it, which caused snaps.\n10. **No animation recording** and no keyframe editing. The Mixamo retarget only plays existing clips. Pose, scene editor and video export are only on the roadmap.\n11. **Open requests** show demand for more model sources and mocap: [#18](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/18) (VRoid Hub, CharacterStudio), [#21](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/21) (kalidokit), [#22](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/22) (webaverse), [#23](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/23) (airi), [#24](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/24) (GitHub miner), [#38](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/38) (feature parity with TheSashaDev/girl-agent). [PR #17](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/pull/17) (image-comparison e2e) is still open.\n\n## 9. Migration notes\n\n### 9.1 Representing both configs in Links Notation\n\nAn immortality axis declaration could become:\n\n```lino\n(axis surface\n  (label \"Panel material\")\n  (group panels)\n  (kind choice)\n  (display buttons)\n  (options gradient glass frosted solid transparent steel brass copper wood carbon holographic ...)\n  (sources arwes gridcn))\n(option glass (of surface) (label \"Glass\") (source arwes))\n(reference arwes (label \"Arwes\") (url \"https://github.com/arwes/arwes\"))\n```\n\nA user's settings would be the diff from defaults:\n\n```lino\n(settings (version 2)\n  (palette ares)\n  (frame octagon)\n  (glow medium)\n  (surfaceOpacity 0.6)\n  (sounds (click soft-tick glass-tap)))\n```\n\nThe anime-avatar cfg, including nested bone rotations:\n\n```lino\n(cfg (version 1)\n  (model (preset seed-san))\n  (rot (rightUpperArm (z -80)) (rightLowerArm (x -90)))\n  (expr (happy 0.4))\n  (light (key (color \"#ffffff\") (intensity 1.2))))\n```\n\nThe asset provenance record:\n\n```lino\n(asset alicia-solid\n  (url \"...\")\n  (format vrm)\n  (credit \"DWANGO Co., Ltd.\")\n  (license (spdx LicenseRef-Niconi-Commons))\n  (attribution required)\n  (fixup flipped))\n```\n\n### 9.2 Steps\n\n1. **Port the `settings.ts` engine first.** Keep `coerce`, `merge`, `diff`, `migrate`, `encode/decode`, `applySharedLook` and `randomize` as framework-neutral pure functions, but read and write the schema and values as Links Notation. Swap the JSON share hash for a Links Notation hash and keep a JSON v2 reader for old links.\n2. **Extend the axis kinds** to cover anime-avatar: `color`, `vector3` (bone rotation with per-axis limits and units), `map` (per-bone, per-mesh, per-expression), `list` (sounds per event), `asset` (URL plus format plus provenance), and `action` (buttons such as gestures and export).\n3. **Add rendering hints to the schema** (`render data-attr|css-var|engine`), so `Shell`, the test assertions and engine bridges (`apply.js`-style reconcilers) are all generated.\n4. **Generate the configuration-mode inspector** from the schema. It should merge `AxisControl` (a11y, sources, display hints) with the `Studio` kit (per-section randomize/reset, color pickers, chips, mobile full-screen drawer). Export `Editor.jsx`'s 22 sections as a large conformance test for that generator.\n5. **Split `styles.css` into per-axis theme modules** keyed by `[data-axis='id']`, so each theme (Arwes HUD, glass, and later the classic-UI themes) is a separately loadable package.\n6. **Animation recording**: build on the pure time-function pattern. A recording is a Links Notation timeline of `(at t (set key value))` and `(at t (play gesture wave (mood happy)))` entries, plus the seed. Playback re-evaluates the pure functions, so recordings are tiny, diffable and reproducible. Combine with additive layers and the shared easing catalog.\n7. **Asset policy**: the framework's own assets follow immortality (procedural, Unlicense). Third-party assets need a mandatory provenance record (SPDX id or `LicenseRef-*`, source URL, credit, attribution flag, commercial-use flag) and a CI check that rejects missing or non-free licenses from the default catalog. Exclude GF2-style proprietary and NC assets from defaults, or gate them behind an explicit opt-in that displays the terms.\n8. **Bindings**: the pure core (schema, store, codecs, easing, time functions, sound specs) should be a plain-JS package. React and Vue adapters wrap `useSettings`, the inspector and `Frame`. Swift and Kotlin bindings consume the same Links Notation schema and theme tokens, and implement native controls.\n9. **Testing**: keep both repos' ideas. Add schema-to-CSS coverage tests (fixing the duplicated `CSS_AXES` list), a preset screenshot gallery, canvas fingerprinting and the in-app runner (no autostart, stoppable) as part of configuration mode.\n10. **Do not carry over**: in-browser Babel, development React builds, unpinned CDN imports without SRI, `window.*` globals, inline-style-only theming, `alert`-based errors, and opaque storage keys.",
