Dev mode ({{F46}}) writes every\nchange to the `user` or `session` configuration layer. This issue turns those\nchanges into three hand-off artefacts, as planned in\n[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)\n(\"Configuration layers and agent hand-off\"):\n\n1. an `overrides` LiNo document (the shape of\n   [`samples/overrides.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/overrides.lino)):\n\n   ```lino\n   (user-overrides: overrides\n     (layer user)\n     (base app)\n     (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n     (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n   ```\n\n2. a share URL that carries only that diff;\n3. a ready-to-paste instruction that tells an AI agent to apply the patch to\n   the committed `site` configuration and open a pull request.\n\nPrior art we already have\n([konard.github.io research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)\nsection 2,\n[immortality research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)\nsections 6 and 8.1,\n[formal-ai research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md)\nsection 5):\n\n- konard.github.io shares looks as `#settings=<urlencoded JSON>`; opening a\n  link applies it, saves the previous look as a \"Before the link\" preset and\n  strips the hash. Only non-default values are stored.\n- immortality shares only the diff from defaults (`diffFromDefaults`, version\n  tag `v:2`), treats all external configuration as untrusted\n  (`mergeSettings` coerces values and drops unknown keys) and keeps the\n  viewer's comfort keys (motion, sound, volume) when applying a shared look.\n  Its share links are percent-encoded JSON, \"long and unreadable\".\n- formal-ai builds prefilled GitHub issue URLs capped at an 8,192-character\n  URL budget.\n\n## Goal\n\nFrom dev mode a user presses **Make these the defaults** and gets: the\noverrides as LiNo text, a share link, and an agent instruction, each with a\nCopy button. Opening a share link previews the overrides in the `session`\nlayer after strict validation.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `exportOverrides(config, options)` that produces the `overrides` document\n  from the difference between the writable layers (`user`, `session`) and the\n  `site` layer, using the patch export of {{F10}}. Deterministic order (by\n  element id, then property).\n- Share link encode and decode: `#ui-overrides=<percent-encoded LiNo>`.\n  If the URL would exceed 8,192 characters the share button is disabled with a\n  message to copy the LiNo text instead.\n- Untrusted input validation for share links and pasted text (see step 4).\n- Applying a share link: decode, validate, show a banner\n  \"Shared UI changes are previewed. Keep / Discard\", write to `session`,\n  save the previous `session` and `user` overrides as a \"Before the link\"\n  backup, remove the hash with `history.replaceState`.\n- Comfort keys: a site-declared list (for example\n  `(comfort-keys motion.mode sound.on sound.volume)`) that shared links never\n  change.\n- Agent instruction generator from a template file with `{name}` placeholders.\n- A \"Make these the defaults\" dialog in the dev mode inspector with three\n  read-only text areas, Copy buttons and an optional \"Open as GitHub issue\"\n  link when the site policy declares a repository.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- A CLI or bot that applies the patch automatically (a follow-up on top of\n  {{F14}}).\n- Sharing whole documents or designer output: {{F55}} and {{F48}}.\n- Presets, randomisation and the settings schema: {{F15}} and {{F37}}.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F46}} (blocker): the inspector, the dev mode policy and the place for the\n  dialog. Through it, the {{F10}} configuration API (layers, patch export,\n  writes to `session`).\n- Related: {{F15}} (diff-only sharing of schema settings; reuse its codec if it\n  is merged first), {{F14}} (what the agent uses to keep comments when it\n  edits the site file), {{F13}} (localised dialog text).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. In `packages/ui-devmode/src/export.js` implement\n   `exportOverrides(config, { id = 'user-overrides', base, layers = ['user', 'session'] })`\n   returning `{ text, links, count }`. `text` is formatted with the official\n   `links-notation` formatter and parses back to the same links.\n2. Extend the dev mode policy ({{F46}}) with optional keys:\n\n   ```lino\n   (site-dev-mode: dev-mode\n     (repository link-foundation/ui)\n     (site-config site/config/site.lino)\n     (comfort-keys motion.mode sound.on sound.volume))\n   ```\n\n3. `src/share.js`: `encodeShareHash(text)` returns `'#ui-overrides=' + encodeURIComponent(text)`;\n   `decodeShareHash(hash)` returns the text or `null`. `shareUrl(location, text)`\n   returns `{ url, tooLong }` with the 8,192-character budget.\n4. `src/validate.js`: `validateOverrides(text, { schema, policy })` returns\n   `{ links, rejected: [{ link, reason }] }`:\n   - parse with `new Parser({ maxInputSize: 65536, maxDepth: 16 })`;\n   - exactly one top-level link of type `overrides`;\n   - only `layer`, `base` and `set` children; `set` targets an existing element\n     or token and a property that the dialect schema allows for its type;\n   - values are checked against the property type (length, colour, enum, text);\n   - `on` (actions), locked elements and comfort keys are rejected;\n   - nothing is ever evaluated; rejected links are reported in the banner.\n5. `src/apply-shared.js`: `applySharedOverrides({ config, location, history, storage })`\n   implements the flow in scope and returns the report.\n6. `src/agent-instruction.txt`: the template. Suggested text:\n\n   ```text\n   Make these UI overrides the defaults of {repository}.\n   1. Open {siteConfig}. Apply every `set` link below to the matching element\n      or token. Keep comments and layout (do not reformat the file).\n   2. Do not change anything else. Run: npm test\n   3. Open a pull request titled \"Make UI overrides the defaults\"\n      and paste the overrides block into its description.\n\n   {overrides}\n   ```\n\n   `renderAgentInstruction({ repository, siteConfig, overrides })` replaces\n   the placeholders; a missing value is replaced by a clear `<unknown ...>`\n   marker, never by an empty string.\n7. `src/defaults-dialog.js`: the dialog (accessible modal dialog with focus\n   trap, `Escape` closes, focus returns to the button), three text areas, Copy\n   buttons with a fallback to selecting the text when the clipboard API is\n   blocked (immortality pattern), an `aria-live` count \"N changes\".\n8. The\n  pure `chart-model.js` and the SVG string renderer can be written before it.\n- **Related:** {{F11}} (chart colours come from tokens such as\n  `color.chart.1`), {{F29}} (the table twin uses `table`), {{F53}} (Vega-Lite\n  import), {{F55}} (gallery).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Write `scales.js` that maps encodings to `d3-scale` scales (bundle and pin\n   the version in `package.json`; never load D3 from a CDN at run time).\n4. Problems, bugs and limitations observed\n\n### konard.github.io\n\n1. **No license.** The code cannot legally be copied into a public-domain framework until it is relicensed\n   (for example to Unlicense, like links-visuals and immortality).\n2. **Links Notation is hand-parsed.** `parseLinks` in `edit.js` uses the regex\n   `/\\(\\s*(?:(\\d+)\\s*:)?\\s*(\\d+)[\\s,]+(\\d+)\\s*\\)/g`, and `links-notation` is not imported anywhere in `src/`.\n   It only accepts numeric doublets and does not handle nesting, names or multi-line input.\n3. **Settings are JSON, not Links Notation.** This applies to localStorage, the `#settings=` hash, the\n   diff box, and import/export. It contradicts the framework goal of representing everything in Links\n   Notation.\n4. **Bilingual text is hard-coded** as `{en, ru}` objects inside components, including long templated\n   sentences in `NetworkEditor.jsx`. Adding a language means editing every component; there is no catalog.\n5. **Configuration is global only.** The tokens style every element of a kind. There is no per-instance\n   override and no element tree to select from, so it is not yet a WYSIWYG designer.\n6. **React-bound.** The store, pages and controls are React components; only `apply.js` and `src/links/*`\n   are framework-free.\n7. **Open issue #47.** The top-left corner and the top and bottom edges are not transparent by default,\n   although every other element is. These are still border/corner layering bugs from the #45 redesign.\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #13: the rain sometimes scaled up too much on refresh.\n   - #45: some border configurations clipped overflowing content or broke transparent backgrounds and\n     selection.\n   - CSS multicol was unreliable in Safari, so columns are explicit.\n   - Safari needed a focus fix in `numericKeys.js`.\n9. **Heavy generated CSS.** `skins.frames.css` is about 84 KB / 1067 lines, and a very large number of\n   fields (hundreds) costs payload and maintenance.\n10. **Repo weight.** About 372 MB, from case studies, logs and archives committed to the repo, so it is\n    slow to clone. Sparse clones are needed.\n11. **Migrations are ad hoc** (`before45()`, special cases in `normalize`). There is no versioned schema\n    migration mechanism.\n\n### links-visuals\n\n1. **CDN at runtime.** D3 is fetched from `esm.sh/use-m` on every load. It does not work offline, it is\n   unpinned and therefore a supply-chain risk, and it is not reproducible.\n2. **Global mutable state** in `state.mjs` (module singletons with setters). Two views cannot share a page.\n3. **Duplicated renderers.** `canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG markers and paths by hand, and the\n   two can drift apart.\n4. **A rAF loop runs every frame even when idle** (`animation.mjs`), which wastes battery.\n5. **Inline CSS is copied into every HTML page**, with no theming. Markers are hardcoded black, and only\n   grid.html and draw.html have colour.\n6. **Experiments are not composable.** Each page wires modules differently, and `failed-attempts/` holds 76\n   HTML snapshots instead of git history.\n7. **Limits of the network model.** grid.html places links in cells without real references. Only draw.html\n   has link-to-link anchors, and only to centers (no source/target-to-endpoint semantics, no layout engine).\n8. **Fixed bugs worth remembering.**\n   - #1/#3: start-point snapping.\n   - #15: the grid was not infinite.\n   - #19/#21: zoom failed away from the center because the hit area was the SVG; listeners were moved to\n     `document`.\n   - #23/#28: grid proportions were inconsistent with single-link mode.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Migration notes for link-foundation/ui\n\n1. **Licensing first.** links-visuals is Unlicense and can be ported now. For konard.github.io, ask the\n   owner to add an Unlicense LICENSE before any code is moved. The sound engine and palettes are already\n   Unlicense through immortality.\n2. **Schema in Links Notation.** Express each RULES entry as links, for example:\n   ```\n   (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (unit px))\n   (skin.name: (type select) (default glass) (options glass liquid futuristic))\n   ```\n   Then generate the JS and TS rule tables, and the Swift and Kotlin constants, from it. Store user diffs as\n   Links Notation too: `(liquid.blur 24)`. Keep JSON import for backward compatibility with existing\n   `settings` and `settings-presets` values and `#settings=` links.\n3. **Keep the projection contract.** Write `--section-key` CSS variables and `data-section-key` attributes,\n   and keep the before-paint injection for web targets. Native targets get the same normalized map as an\n   observable store.\n4. **Scopes.** Keep the user/document split (localStorage vs URL or `.lino`), and add an element scope so the\n   designer mode can override tokens per node in the DOM-like tree.\n5. **Controls.** Port Select, ColorInput, NumberInput, Tooltip and numericKeys with their tests (`*.test.jsx`)\n   as the first `controls` set. Keep WAI-ARIA APG behaviour and the Safari fixes.\n6. **Links view.** Merge the K:src/links glyph, placement, collisions and render code with the L:js\n   zoom-pan, grid, anchors and IK into a single renderer:\n   - one marker set, with SVG and Canvas back ends generated from it\n   - no global state; instance objects instead\n   - D3 bundled and pinned, or dropped where `d3-force` alone is enough\n   - an idle-stopping animation loop\n7. **Parsing.** Replace the regex parser with the official `links-notation` package. Keep `configurations.js`\n   (code and index maths, Burnside counting) as a pure utility.\n8. **i18n.** Move the `{en, ru}` literals into per-language catalogs keyed by id, preferably in Links\n   Notation, and keep `plural.js` rules per language.\n9. **Themes.** Treat `glass`, `liquid` and `futuristic`, plus the 12 palettes and the corner/frame generator,\n   as the first theme pack. Classic UIs (Windows 9x, Aqua and so on) become more theme packs on the same\n   tokens. Fix #47-style corner and edge transparency in the generator, not in per-skin CSS.\n10. **Animation recording.** Reuse the export pipeline: one model goes to a standalone SVG and then to a\n    raster, over a timeline of settings and link diffs. The IK animation in links-visuals and the canvas\n    backgrounds are the first recording targets.\n11. **Process.** Adopt the per-issue test files, the three-engine Playwright runs, a case study per issue,\n    and the 1500-line limit. Do not commit logs or archives, so the framework repo does not grow to hundreds\n    of megabytes.",

Create `packages/ui-dom/package.json` (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-dom\"`,\n   `\"type\": \"module\"`, `exports` for `.` and `./html`), `README.md` and\n   `src/index.d.ts`. Dependencies: `@link-foundation/ui-core`,\n   `@link-foundation/ui-store`, `@link-foundation/ui-style` (workspace).\n   Dev dependency for tests: `jsdom` (MIT).\n2. `src/kinds.js`: a registry.\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @typedef {object} KindSpec\n    * @property {string} tag  custom element name, e.g. 'ui-button'\n    * @property {(el: UiElement, ctx: RenderContext) => Element} create\n    * @property {(node: Element, el: UiElement, changed: string[], ctx: RenderContext) => void} update\n    * @property {(node: Element) => Element | null} [childrenSlot] where children go; null = no children\n    * @property {(node: Element) => void} [destroy]\n    */\n   /** @param {string} kind @param {KindSpec} spec */\n   export function defineKind(kind, spec) {}\n   ```\n   Registering a tag calls `customElements.define` only if\n   `customElements.get(tag)` is undefined, so importing twice is safe.\n3. `src/kinds/basic.js`: `document` (`ui-document`, sets `document.title` only\n   when `options.setTitle` is true), `stack` (`direction`, `gap` as CSS\n   `flex-direction` and `gap`), `text` (text content), `button` (native\n   `<button type=\"button\">` child, `label`, `variant` mirrored to an attribute\n   for style selectors, `disabled`), `image` (`<img>` with `src` and `alt`;\n   an `image` without `alt` gets `alt=\"\"` and a diagnostic), `unknown`.\n4. `src/render.js`: walk the store tree, create nodes, set\n   `data-link-id=\"<id>\"` on every element, keep `Map<id, Element>` and a\n   `WeakMap<Element, id>`. Return\n   `{ nodeFor(id), idFor(node), flush(), destroy() }`.\n5. `src/patch.js` and `src/scheduler.js`: on each store change event, queue a\n   patch; apply all queued patches in one microtask (`queueMicrotask`).\n   `update` re-uses the existing node and calls `spec.update` with the changed\n   prop names only; `move` uses `insertBefore`; `remove` calls `spec.destroy`\n   and drops map entries. `flush()` applies the queue synchronously (tests).\n6. `src/events.js`: for each `(on <event> <action...>)` prop, attach a listener\n   for the mapped DOM event (`press` = `click` on the native button, plus\n   Enter/Space through the native button). Dispatch\n   `new CustomEvent('ui-action', { bubbles: true, composed: true, detail })`\n   with `detail = { source: 'ok', event: 'press', action: ['navigate', 'home'] }`\n   and call `options.onAction?.(detail)`. Never call `eval`, `new Function`\n   or set `on*` attributes from document text.\n7. `src/styles.js`: build one `CSSStyleSheet` from the F12 output and token\n   variables; adopt it on the container's root node; selectors use the custom\n   element tag plus attributes, e.g. `ui-button[variant=\"filled\"]`. Light DOM\n   is used so that page CSS, dev mode and native form participation work.\n8. `src/html.js`: `renderToHTML(source, { kinds })` returns a string such as\n   `<ui-document data-link-id=\"app\"><ui-stack data-link-id=\"body\" ...>`. Escape\n   text and attribute values; never emit `on*` attributes or `<script>`.\n9. `mountDocument(container, text, options)` in `src/index.js`: parse with\n   `ui-core`, build a store with `ui-store`, call `render`, return\n   `{ store, handle }`.\n10. Example page `examples/ui-dom/index.html` + `main.js` that mounts\n    `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/document.lino` with the sample styles\n    and tokens, and a button that changes `greeting` through the store.\n11. Write the tests listed below, the README (API, kind registry, decision\n    \"plain custom elements, light DOM\" with the reasons above) and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-dom/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`, `src/index.d.ts`\n- `packages/ui-dom/src/{kinds.js,render.js,patch.js,scheduler.js,events.js,styles.js,html.js}`\n- `packages/ui-dom/src/kinds/basic.js`\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/setup-dom.js` (jsdom globals)\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/{render,incremental,events,styles,html,kinds}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-dom/tests/__snapshots__/document.html`\n- `examples/ui-dom/index.html`, `examples/ui-dom/main.js`\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `render.test.js`: `samples/document.lino` renders\n      `ui-document > ui-stack > (ui-text, ui-button)` and matches\n      `tests/__snapshots__/document.html`.\n- [ ] Every rendered element node has `data-link-id`; Most of our UI\nprojects are React today: formal-ai (React 19 + Chakra), meta-sovereign,\nimmortality, anime-avatar, konard.github.io and deepcase (see the research\nfiles). The architecture keeps React thin: the DOM renderer `ui-dom`\n({{F16}}) does the rendering, and React only mounts it, subscribes to the store\nand lets React components render custom kinds\n([ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md),\n\"Framework adapters\"). React 19 supports custom elements natively, so the\n`ui-*` tags can also be written in JSX\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)\nsection 1, \"Web Components\").\n\nThe hooks must not depend on the DOM, because the React Native renderer\n({{F20}}) reuses them.\n\n## Goal\n\nPublish `@link-foundation/ui-react` with a `<UiDocument>` component, a\nprovider, DOM-free store hooks and a way to render React components for\ncustom dialect kinds.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `<UiDocument source | store, actions, onAction, components, className />`\n  that mounts `ui-dom` into a container `<div>` and cleans up on unmount.\n- `<UiProvider store actions>` and `useUiContext()`.\n- Hooks (entry `@link-foundation/ui-react/hooks`, no `react-dom`, no\n  `ui-dom` import): `useUiStore(store, selector)`, `useUiElement(id)`,\n  `useUiProp(id, name)`, `useUiAction(name, handler)`.\n- `components` prop: `{ chart: MyChart }` registers a `ui-dom` kind whose\n  node is a host element, and React renders `MyChart` into it with\n  `createPortal`, receiving `{ id, props, children }`.\n- Server rendering safety: `renderToString(<UiDocument source=... />)` does\n  not touch `window`; with `ssr` it inlines `renderToHTML` output from\n  {{F16}}, which is replaced on mount.\n- Type declarations (`src/index.d.ts`) and an example Vite app.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Re-implementing rendering in React (no per-element React components for\n  built-in kinds).\n- React Native ({{F20}}), code export to React source ({{F52}}), MUI theme\n  mapping ({{F40}}), JSX import ({{F51}}).\n- Hydration that reuses server nodes.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F16}} (blocker): `render(container, store, options)`, `RenderHandle`,\n  `defineKind`, `renderToHTML`, the `ui-action` event and `onAction`\n  callback.\n- Indirect: {{F08}} store (`subscribe`, `getSnapshot`-like read, `transaction`),\n  {{F06}} `parse` for `source` strings.\n- Related: {{F19}} (same shape for Vue; Must\n   be safe under `<StrictMode>` (mount, unmount, mount).\n5. `src/components.js`: for each entry of `components`, call `defineKind` with a\n   spec whose `create` returns a `<ui-react-host data-kind=...>` element and\n   records it in a state list; `UiDocument` renders\n   `createPortal(<Comp id props />, host)` for each recorded host. Multi-line parens `(ok: button\\n  (label 'OK'))` → `((ok: button) ((ok: button) (label OK)))`.\n     - Nested multi-line `(a: b\\n  (c d)\\n  (e: f\\n    (g h)))` → `((a: b) ((a: b) (c d)) ((a: b) ((e: f) ((e: f) (g h)))))`. `parseGroups` returns the same as one element with no children.\n     - Indented `ok: button\\n  label 'OK'\\n  on press\\n    navigate home`: `parse()` → `['(ok: button)','((ok: button) (label OK))','((ok: button) (on press))','(((ok: button) (on press)) (navigate home))']`. `parseGroups()` → a tree `{element:\"(ok: button)\", children:[{(label OK)}, {(on press), children:[(navigate home)]}]}`.\n     - `root:\\n  child1\\n  child2\\n    grandchild` → `(root: child1 (child2 grandchild))`.\n     - `(x #6750A4)` throws ParseError \"Syntax error at line 1, column 12\" (the comment eats `)`), so unquoted hex is invalid input. `(x '#6750A4' 16px)` is fine.\n     - `(t a:b)` is a syntax error; `(t 'a:b')` is OK.\n     - `(t 1 '1')` → both values have id \"1\", so the quoted/bare distinction is lost.\n     - `(button.save: button)` gives id \"button.save\". `@color.primary` and `$draft.text` are plain references.\n     - Duplicate ids `(a: b)\\n(a: c)` parse silently as two links.\n   - **Research gaps (section 5) to decide in F03:**\n     1. typed values (codec rule vs schema-driven; recommendation: schema-driven for dimensions/durations/colours, codec fallback; ask upstream for a `quoted` flag);\n     2. units/colours (quoted hex or `(oklch L C H)`);\n     3. `:` in values: use structured `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))`, `(aspect 16 9)`;\n     4. comments/layout lost on round trip (CST upstream / first-class notes / patch-in-place; relates to F14);\n     5. ordering (children/keyframes are sequences; props are sets; duplicate key: last wins);\n     6. ids/scoping (global ids, duplicates, namespaces, stable ids, doublet mapping);\n     7. reference sigils: [REDACTED]\n     8. schemas (lino-schema is a stub);\n     9. expressions/bindings `(on press (emit save))`, `(bind value $draft.text)`, `(when $sending (show spinner))`; linksql reuse?;\n     10. missing languages;\n     11. security (maxDepth 64, maxInputSize, handlers are names, never code).\n     - Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 3\nblocked_by: [F08, F12]\nrequirements: [R3, R18]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nThe framework is a runtime interpreter of a links network with thin renderers\nper platform (principle 4 of\n[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).\nThe web reference renderer is `@link-foundation/ui-dom`: plain JavaScript,\ncustom elements (Web Components), no framework. React ({{F18}}) and Vue\n({{F19}}) adapters wrap it, components ({{F25}}, {{F26}}, {{F27}}) plug into it,\nand dev mode ({{F46}}) depends on one property of it: every rendered node\ncarries the stable link ID of the element it came from (principle 6).\n\nThe research recommends \"Web Components (Lit or plain custom elements) as the\nreference vanilla-JS renderer\" and warns against heavy code generation\n(section \"Recommendations\" A.2 and C in\n[existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\nkonard.github.io and immortality show that projecting state to `data-*`\nattributes and CSS variables works the same for plain JS, React and Vue\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)\npattern 3,\n[immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)\npattern 9).\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-dom/` that renders a `ui-store` links network into the DOM\nas custom elements, keeps it in sync incrementally from store change events,\napplies resolved styles from `ui-style`, dispatches declared actions as data,\nand marks every node with `data-link-id`.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `render(container, store, options)` and the convenience\n  `mountDocument(container, linoText, options)` (parse with `ui-core`, create a\n  store, render).\n- Custom elements with the `ui-` prefix for the basic kinds needed by the\n  dialect samples: `document`, `stack`, `text`, `button`, `image`, plus a\n  `ui-unknown` fallback for kinds without a registered renderer.\n- A kind registry (`defineKind`) so components and adapters add kinds without\n  touching the renderer.\n- Incremental updates: insert, update, remove and move of elements, batched in\n  one microtask per store transaction.\n- `data-link-id` on every element node; `handle.nodeFor(id)` and\n If the pull request would exceed about 1,500\nchanged lines, open one pull request per milestone (`Part of` this issue; the\nlast one says `Fixes`).\n\n- **M1 Shell.** Designer layout described in LiNo (`src/designer.lino`) and\n  rendered with the framework: docked panels from {{F28}} (left: Toolbox and\n  Outline; centre: Canvas; right: Properties from {{F46}}; bottom: Source),\n  resizable, collapsible, layout persisted in the `user` layer. Design mode and\n  Run mode toggle (in Design mode clicks select, in Run mode the UI works).\n- **M2 Editing.** Toolbox generated from the component catalog of {{F26}}\n  (one item per component, with icon and name), drag from toolbox to canvas or\n  Outline to insert, drag on canvas or Outline to move, delete, duplicate,\n  cut/copy/paste of LiNo fragments, multi-select (Shift+click, Ctrl/Cmd+click,\n  marquee), undo/redo (`Ctrl/Cmd+Z`, `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z`) using the ui-store\n  transactions from {{F08}}. One user gesture is one transaction.\n- **M3 Layout aids.** Alignment guides and snapping to sibling edges and\n  centres (threshold 6 CSS pixels, configurable), drop indicators for flow\n  layouts (stack/grid insert position), resize handles for elements with\n  explicit size, keyboard nudging (arrows 1 px, Shift+arrows 10 px).\n- **M4 Two-way sync.** Canvas edits are written to the LiNo text via {{F14}};\n  text edits in the Source panel are parsed, diffed against the store and\n  applied as one transaction that keeps stable ids. Parse errors are shown with\n  line and column and do not destroy the canvas state.\n- Accessibility: every canvas action has a keyboard path (select in Outline,\n  `Alt+Up/Down` to reorder among siblings, `Enter` on a toolbox item inserts\n  into the selected container).\n- Save and open: open a `.lino` file (file input), save by download and copy;\n  the draft is kept in the store so reload restores it.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Animation timeline: {{F49}}.\n- Pages not built with the framework: {{F50}}.\n- Code export: {{F52}}. Imports: {{F51}}.\n- Real-time collaboration, design-time data and variant matrices (follow-ups).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F46}} (blocker): hover/selection overlay, property grid, outline model,\n  dev mode policy.\n- {{F28}} (blocker): split panes and docking used for the designer shell.\n- {{F26}} (blocker): controls (buttons, inputs, tree, tabs) and the component\n  catalog metadata (type, allowed children, properties with types and\n  defaults) that drives the toolbox and the drop rules.\n- {{F14}} (blocker): source-preserving edits (insert, move, remove, set\n  property) on LiNo text.\n- Related: {{F08}} (transactions, undo/redo), {{F38}} (code editor for the\n  Source panel; use a plain `textarea` until it is merged), {{F36}} (toolbox\n  icons), {{F13}} (localised designer UI).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-designer/` (`package.json` named\n   `@link-foundation/ui-designer`, `src/`, `tests/`, `examples/`).\n2. `src/commands.js` (pure): `insertElement(store, { parentId, index, type, props })`,\n   `moveElements(store, { ids, parentId, index })`, `removeElements(store, ids)`,\n   `duplicateElements(store, ids)`, `setProperty(store, id, name, value)`.\n   Each runs in one store transaction and returns the new ids. Drop rules come\n   from the catalog: `canContain(catalog, parentType, childType)`.\n3. `src/selection.js` (pure): selection set, anchor, `toggle`, `range`,\n   `marquee(rects, box)`.\n4. `src/snap.js` (pure):\n   `computeSnap(moving, others, { threshold = 6 })` returns\n   `{ dx, dy, guides: [{ axis, position, from, to }] }`; edges and centres.\n5. `src/sync.js`: `canvasToSource(sourceText, change)` uses {{F14}};\n   `sourceToStore(store, text)` parses, maps ids, applies a diff in one\n   transaction; on error returns `{ error: { line, column, message } }`.\n6. `src/designer.lino` and `src/designer.js`: the shell (M1), wiring panels,\n   overlay and commands. `mountDesigner({ root, documentText })` returns\n   `{ getText(), undo(), redo(), destroy() }`.\n7. `src/canvas.js`: pointer-based drag and drop (Pointer Events, pointer\n   capture), drop indicator, guides rendering, design/run mode.\n8. `examples/index.html`: designer opened on the sample document.\n9. Tests per module; Playwright scenarios for each milestone.\n\nExample: dragging a `text` from the toolbox between `greeting` and `ok` and\nsetting its text produces, with the original comment kept:\n\n```lino\n(app: document\n  (title 'Links UI demo')\n  (theme material3)\n  (body: stack\n    (direction vertical)\n    (gap (token space.medium))\n    (greeting: text 'Hello, links')\n    (text-1: text 'New text')\n    (ok: button\n      (label 'OK')\n      (variant filled)\n      (on press (navigate home)))))\n```\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-designer/package.json`, `README.md`\n- `packages/ui-designer/src/{commands,selection,snap,sync,canvas,designer}.js`\n- `packages/ui-designer/src/designer.lino`\n- `packages/ui-designer/examples/index.html`\n- `packages/ui-designer/tests/{commands,selection,snap,sync}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-designer/tests/fixtures/*.lino` (inputs with comments and\n  expected outputs)\n- Browser tests in the {{F05}} location; `.changeset/*.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] M1: the shell renders with four docked panels, panels resize and\n      collapse, layout survives reload; screenshot attached.\n- [ ] M2: insert, move, delete, duplicate, copy/paste and multi-select work on\n      canvas and in Outline; [2026-11-01T11:51:41.526Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F06\ntitle: 'ui-core: parse Links Notation into the UI element tree'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 2\nblocked_by: [F01, F03]\nrequirements: [R2, R3, R6, R8]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nEvery package of the framework reads UI documents written in Links Notation\n(LiNo). The official parser\n[`links-notation`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/links-notation) (npm 0.27.1,\nUnlicense) returns generic `Link` objects (`{ id, values }`), not a UI tree.\nThe same document has three different parse shapes depending on how it is\nwritten (see \"Links Notation parse shapes\" in\n[ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)\nand the script\n[experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs)):\n\n| Form                       | `new Parser().parse(text)` result                                                    |\n| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| One line                   | one link `(ok: button (label OK) (on press (navigate home)))`                        |\n| Multi-line parentheses     | head repeated: `((ok: button) ((ok: button) (label OK)) ...)`                        |\n| Indented (no parentheses)  | a flat list of path links: `(app: document)`, `((app: document) (title '...'))`, ... |\n\n`parser.parseGroups(text)` keeps the indented structure as\n`{ element: Link, children: IndentedGroup[] }`. {{F03}} defines the single tree\nprojection (the UI dialect) and ships conformance fixtures. This issue\nimplements that projection in the first package, `@link-foundation/ui-core`.\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-core` exports `parse(text)` that turns any of the three forms of\nthe same document into the same `UiDocument` tree, `format(doc)` that prints it\nback to canonical LiNo, and passes every {{F03}} conformance fixture.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `parse(text, options)` → `UiDocument` (roots, `byId` map, diagnostics).\n- Projection rules from {{F03}}: a value link with an id (`greeting: text ...`)\n  is a child element; an anonymous link (`(label 'OK')`) is a property whose\n  name is its first reference; positional references after the kind are\n  `args` (for example `text 'Hello, links'`).\n- Unfolding of the multi-line head-repeated shape and of indented path links\n  (prefer `parseGroups` for indented input).\n- `format(doc, { style: 'inline' | 'multiline' | 'indented' })`.\n- Diagnostics: duplicate ids, unknown shape, parse errors with line and column\n  taken from `ParseError` (`line`, `column`, `offset`).\n- Safety limits passed to the parser: `maxDepth` (default\n  `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH` = 64) and `maxInputSize`.\n- A conformance runner over the {{F03}} fixtures.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Typed values (numbers, units, colours, token references) — {{F07}}. Here all\n  leaf values stay strings.\n- Schema validation of kinds and properties (per-kind schemas come with\n  {{F26}}); a mutable store — {{F08}}; keeping comments and layout — {{F14}}.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F01}} (blocker): the monorepo workspace, `packages/` layout and the shared\n  test/lint scripts. Consumed: `packages/<name>/` conventions and root\n  `npm test` picking up `packages/*/tests/*.test.js`.\n- {{F03}} (blocker): the dialect specification (`docs/spec/`) and the\n  fixtures. Consumed: projection rules and fixture files. The fixture layout is\n  decided in F03; this issue assumes pairs like\n  `docs/spec/fixtures/<name>.lino` + `docs/spec/fixtures/<name>.tree.json`\n  — adapt the runner to the real layout.\n- Related: {{F07}}, {{F08}}, {{F14}}, {{F16}}, {{F17}} (all consume `parse`).\n- Starting before F03 merges: implement the provisional rule above, write the\n  three sample-based tests, and add the fixture runner last.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-core/package.json` (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-core\"`,\n   `\"type\": \"module\"`, `\"exports\": { \".\": \"./src/index.js\" }`), dependency\n   `links-notation` (check the current version; 0.27.1 at planning time).\n2. `src/types.js` — JSDoc types only:\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @typedef {object} UiProp\n    * @property {string} name          e.g. 'label'\n    * @property {Array<string|UiValue>} values  raw values, e.g. ['OK']\n    * @typedef {{ ref?: string, values?: UiValue[] }} UiValue  nested anonymous link\n    * @typedef {object} UiNode\n    * @property {string|null} id       'ok', or null for anonymous elements\n    * @property {string} kind          'button'\n    * @property {string[]} args        positional values after the kind\n    * @property {UiProp[]} props       in source order (duplicates kept)\n    * @property {UiNode[]} children    in source order\n    * @typedef {{ roots: UiNode[], byId: Map<string, UiNode>, diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }} UiDocument\n    * @typedef {{ code: string, message: string, line?: number, column?: number, id?: string }} Diagnostic\n    */\n   ```\n3. `src/unfold.js`: `unfoldHeads(link)` — detects `(H (H a) (H b))` where the\n   first value equals the outer head (use `Link.equals`) and returns\n   `{ head: H, values: [a, b] }` recursively. Never inspect the text with\n   regular expressions; only walk `Link` objects.\n4. `src/project.js`: `projectLink(link) → UiNode | UiProp` applying the\n   F03 rules; `projectGroups(groups) → UiNode[]` for `parseGroups` output.\n5. `src/parse.js`: `parse(text, { maxDepth, maxInputSize } = {})`. Detect the\n   indented form (top-level links that are not parenthesised, i.e.\n   `parseGroups` yields groups with children) and choose the path. Catch\n   `ParseError` and return `{ roots: [], diagnostics: [{ code: 'parse-error', line, column, message }] }`\n   instead of throwing; export `parseOrThrow` for callers that want to throw.\n6. Build `byId`; on a duplicate id add `{ code: 'duplicate-id', id }` and keep\n   the first node in `byId` (F03 may decide otherwise — follow the spec).\n7. `src/format.js`: `format(doc, { style })`. Build `Link` objects and call\n   `link.format()` / `formatIndentedDocument` from `links-notation`; quote\n   values that need it with `escapeReference`. Default style `multiline`\n   (one child or prop per line, two spaces).\n8. `src/index.js` re-exports `parse`, `parseOrThrow`, `format`, `projectLink`,\n   `walk(doc, visitor)` and the type definitions; add `src/index.d.ts`.\n9. [2026-11-01T11:52:01.006Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F39\ntitle: 'Theme engine: nested themes, colour schemes, contrast, motion'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 5\nblocked_by: [F11, F12, F26]\nrequirements: [R14, R15]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nIn the UI dialect a theme is a LiNo package of tokens, style rules and\ncomponent templates. The idea comes from XAML control templates and Ionic\n\"modes\": one document, many looks\n([`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md),\nsection \"Themes and other frameworks as LiNo\"). Material 3 ({{F40}}), Fluent 2\n({{F41}}), the Apple HIG-guided theme ({{F42}}) and the classic themes ({{F43}})\nare all theme packages built on the engine from this issue.\n\nOur projects show what works and what breaks:\n\n- **What works.** immortality and konard.github.io switch looks without a\n  re-render. They write every choice to `data-*` attributes and CSS custom\n  properties. konard.github.io also runs a before-paint script so the page\n  never flashes the wrong theme\n  ([immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md),\n  [konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)).\n- **What breaks.** formal-ai implements dark mode as an override file,\n  `06-dark-theme.css`, which is 1,097 lines and holds about 248 dark selectors.\n  The same \"theme not applied everywhere\" bugs keep coming back: formal-ai\n  issues [388](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/388),\n  [541](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/541) and\n  [550](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/550)\n  ([formal-ai.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md)).\n  deepcase has the same class of bug because its graph styles live outside the\n  tokens\n  ([deepcase.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)\n  section 10).\n- **What to copy.** meta-sovereign darkens filled accents until they keep a\n  4.5:1 contrast ratio, and honours `prefers-reduced-motion`,\n  `prefers-reduced-transparency` and `prefers-color-scheme`\n  ([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nBuild a theme engine. It loads theme packages written in LiNo, resolves\ninheritance and modes (light, dark, high contrast, reduced motion), and\ncompiles each theme to scoped CSS custom properties. The renderer applies a\ntheme to any subtree by setting `data-*` attributes, so a subtree can carry a\nnested theme and switching a theme never re-renders. A colour scheme is a set\nof token values, never a separate override stylesheet.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- The theme model in `@link-foundation/ui-tokens`, in `packages/ui-tokens/src/themes/`:\n  - `theme` links with `extends`, `token`, `style`, `template`, and the\n    `mode dark`, `mode high-contrast` and `motion reduced` blocks.\n- The new package `packages/ui-themes/` (`@link-foundation/ui-themes`). It\n  holds theme packages as data and starts with the `base` theme only.\n- Nested themes. `(theme x)` and `(scheme dark)` on any element apply to its\n  subtree, and an inner subtree can switch back to `light`.\n- Modes:\n  - Colour scheme: `light`, `dark` and `system`, where `system` follows\n    `prefers-color-scheme`.\n  - Contrast: `normal` and `more`. `more` follows `prefers-contrast: more`,\n    and `forced-colors: active` maps to system colours.\n  - Motion: `full` and `reduced`. `reduced` follows `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n- Contrast-safe accents. Declared colour pairs are checked against WCAG 2.2\n  ratios, and any filled accent that fails is adjusted automatically.\n- Component templates, following the XAML control-template idea. A theme can\n  replace the part tree of a {{F26}} control. Part names follow Open UI\n  anatomy (`root`, `label`, `icon`, `indicator`).\n- Theme switching without re-rendering, plus a before-paint script that stops\n  the wrong theme from flashing on load.\n- Comfort keys. A theme must never override the user's motion, sound, volume\n  or transparency choices (the konard.github.io COMFORT keys).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The concrete design-system themes: {{F40}}, {{F41}}, {{F42}} and {{F43}}.\n- The settings panel UI for choosing themes ({{F37}}).\n- Animation runtime. This issue only defines motion tokens and the reduced\n  mode; {{F44}} covers animation.\n- Native exporters for themes (Swift and Kotlin). {{F11}} exports tokens, and\n  native theme switching belongs to {{F21}} and {{F23}}.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F11}} (blocker). Supplies the token model, reference/semantic/component\n  layers, the CSS custom property naming (for example `--color-primary`) and\n  the DTCG 2025.10 export. Themes are token sets, so reuse its resolver and do\n  not write a second one.\n- {{F12}} (blocker). Supplies style rules with `(state ...)` and\n  `(media ...)`. The engine compiles `style` links inside a theme with this\n  resolver, scoped to `[data-theme=\"<id>\"]`.\n- {{F26}} (blocker). Supplies the basic controls and their default part trees.\n  The `button` control is the first consumer of `resolveTemplate`.\n- Indirect: {{F06}} (parser), {{F07}} (colour values, OKLCH conversion) and\n  {{F16}} (ui-dom, which writes the attributes).\n- Related: {{F10}} (configuration layers, where the user's `theme` and\n  `scheme` choices live), {{F37}}, {{F40}}–{{F43}}, {{F54}}, {{F57}}.\n- To start before {{F26}} merges, test templates against a stub `button` kind\n  registered in the test file.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Write a theme package format. Save this example as\n   `packages/ui-themes/themes/base/theme.lino`; the final syntax is fixed by {{F03}}:\n   ```lino\n   (base: theme\n     (token color.primary '#3A5BA0')\n     (token color.on-primary '#FFFFFF')\n     (token color.surface '#FFFFFF')\n     (token color.on-surface '#1B1B1F')\n     (token motion.duration.short 150ms)\n     (pair color.on-primary color.primary)\n     (pair color.on-surface color.surface)\n     (mode dark\n       (token color.primary '#AFC6FF')\n       (token color.on-primary '#0A2F6B')\n       (token color.surface '#121316')\n       (token color.on-surface '#E3E2E6'))\n     (mode high-contrast\n       (token color.primary '#0B2A66'))\n     (motion reduced\n       (token motion.duration.short 0ms)))\n   ```\n2. In `packages/ui-tokens/src/themes/model.js`, implement:\n   ```js\n   /** @typedef {{ id: string, extends: string[], tokens: [REDACTED], TokenValue>,\n    *   modes: Record<string, Map<string, TokenValue>>, styles: StyleRule[],\n    *   templates: Map<string, TemplateNode>, pairs: [string, string][] }} Theme */\n   /** @param {string} linoText @returns {{ themes: Theme[], diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }} */\n   export function loadThemes(linoText) {}\n   /** Merges the `extends` chain; the child wins and order is deterministic.\n    * @param {Map<string, Theme>} registry @param {string} id @returns {Theme} */\n   export function resolveTheme(registry, id) {}\n   ```\n   Reject executable content: any value containing `javascript:` or\n   `expression(` and any `script` link. Each rejection produces a diagnostic.\n   Inheritance cycles produce a diagnostic, not a crash.\n3. In `src/themes/contrast.js`, implement:\n   ```js\n   /** WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance contrast ratio. @returns {number} */\n   export function contrastRatio(fg, bg) {}\n   /** Moves `fill` in OKLCH lightness until contrastRatio(on, fill) >= min.\n    * @returns {{ color: string, adjusted: boolean, ratio: number }} */\n   export function ensureContrast(on, fill, min = 4.5) {}\n   ```\n   Every `pair` in every mode is checked. When a pair fails, the engine writes\n   the adjusted colour into the compiled output and emits a warning\n   diagnostic. `{ strict: true }` turns that warning into an error.\n4. In `src/themes/compile-css.js`, write\n   `compileThemeCss(theme, options) -> string`. It emits:\n   - `[data-theme=\"base\"]` with the light values;\n   - `[data-theme=\"base\"][data-scheme=\"dark\"]`;\n   - `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { [data-theme=\"base\"][data-scheme=\"system\"] {...} }`;\n   - `[data-contrast=\"more\"]` and `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` for\n     `data-contrast=\"system\"`;\n   - `@media (forced-colors: active)`, which maps semantic tokens to system\n     colours (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `ButtonText`, `Highlight`);\n   - `[data-motion=\"reduced\"]` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.\n\n   Style rules from the theme are compiled with {{F12}} and prefixed with\n   `:where([data-theme=\"base\"])` so that their specificity stays low.\n5. Nesting. In ui-dom ({{F16}}), add `src/themes.js`, which handles every\n   element that carries `theme`, `scheme`, `contrast` or `motion`. On that\n   element it writes all four effective values as `data-theme`,\n   `data-scheme`, `data-contrast` and `data-motion`, copying any value it\n   does not set from the nearest themed ancestor. Custom properties inherit,\n   so the innermost theme wins. Setting a new value is a store `set`, and the\n   change handler only rewrites attributes on the theme boundaries; it never\n   rebuilds nodes.\n6. Comfort keys. `motion`, `sound`, `volume` and `transparency` are read from\n   configuration ({{F10}}), and a theme may only supply defaults for them. The\n   user layer always wins. Add a test that applies a theme with\n   `(motion reduced)` defaults to a user who chose `full`.\n7. Templates. Write\n   `resolveTemplate(themeChain, kind) -> TemplateNode | null` in\n   `src/themes/templates.js` and call it from the {{F26}} `button` kind. An\n   example template:\n   `(template button (part root (kind box)) (part icon (kind icon)) (part label (kind text)))`.\n   An unknown part name produces a diagnostic.\n8. Before-paint script. Write\n   `themeBootScript({ storageKey }) -> string`, an inline script of at most\n   1 KB. It reads the saved theme and scheme from `localStorage` and sets the\n   attributes on `<html>` before first paint, following the konard.github.io\n   `themeBeforePaint` pattern.\n9. DTCG. Write `exportThemeResolver(theme) -> object`, which maps the modes\n   to a DTCG 2025.10 Resolver Module document. Check the current Resolver\n   Module schema and validate against it in a test.\n10. In `examples/themes/`, build a page that shows the same {{F26}} controls\n    four times: base light, base dark, nested dark-inside-light, and high\n    contrast. Add the README, the changesets for ui-tokens, ui-dom and\n    ui-themes, and the tests listed below.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-tokens/src/themes/{model,contrast,compile-css,templates,boot,dtcg-resolver}.js`\n- `packages/ui-tokens/tests/{themes-model,themes-contrast,themes-css,themes-templates,themes-dtcg}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-dom/src/themes.js`, `packages/ui-dom/tests/themes.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-themes/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`\n  (`listThemes()`, `loadTheme(id)`), `themes/base/theme.lino`\n- `examples/themes/index.html`, `examples/themes/main.js`\n- `tests/e2e/themes.spec.js` (Playwright, uses the {{F05}} harness)\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `themes-model.test.js`: `extends` chains of depth 3 resolve\n      deterministically, a cycle gives a diagnostic, and a `script` link or a\n      `javascript:` value is rejected.\n- [ ] `themes-contrast.test.js`: `contrastRatio('#FFFFFF', '#000000')` is 21,\n      and `ensureContrast` raises a failing pair to at least 4.5:1.\n- [ ] Every `pair` in `base` passes 4.5:1 in the light, dark and high-contrast\n      modes. If the target has no\n      licence (as konard.github.io today), the owner must add one first.\n   2. **Inventory.** List pages, components, stylesheets (with line counts),\n      settings keys, storage keys, i18n sources and test suites. Record each\n      with its file path.\n   3. **Freeze contracts.** Write compatibility tests for every external\n      contract before changing code: storage keys and formats, URL hashes,\n      `data-*` attributes, CSS variable names, `data-testid` values, global\n      hooks and events.\n   4. **Baseline screenshots.** Use the target's own Playwright setup, or the\n      {{F05}} harness: every page × theme × viewport.\n   5. **Tokens first, zero visual change.** Move the CSS custom properties\n      into a LiNo theme ({{F39}}) and generate the same variable names.\n   6. **Settings as LiNo.** Use the {{F15}} schema with a reader for the old\n      JSON format, kept for at least one release.\n   7. **i18n.** Use {{F13}} catalogs, keeping the old `t()` signature.\n   8. **Leaf components, then screens.** Use the strangler pattern: one\n      component per pull request behind a thin re-export.\n   9. **Delete.** Remove the old code, CSS and parsers, and record the\n      line-count reduction.\n3. Colours come from tokens,\n   not from the code.\n4. Write `render-svg.js`: `renderLinkSvg(geometry, style) → string`, and\n   `render-canvas.js`: `drawLinkCanvas(ctx, geometry, style)`. Both read\n   `markers.js`; a test checks that both use the same marker ids.\n5. Write `zoom-pan.js`:\n   `createZoomPan(element, { min = 0.1, max = 20, onChange }) → { get(), set(view), destroy() }`.\n   Listeners are attached to `element` (pointer capture while dragging), not to\n   `document`, and `destroy()` removes them (test with a fake element).\n6. Write `animator.js`: `createAnimator({ now, raf })` with `start(id, fn)`\n   and `stop(id)`; the frame loop stops when no animation is active. Inject\n   `now` and `raf` for tests.\n7. Write the `link-view` element: draws one link from LiNo, optional\n   `blueprint` points and `grid`, keyboard zoom (`+`, `-`, `0` to reset) and an\n   accessible name such as \"Link 1 from 1 to 2\".\n8. Pin D3 modules if used (`d3-zoom` is optional; plain pointer code is\n   enough). Never load scripts from a CDN at run time.\n9. Gallery page `packages/ui-components/examples/link-view.html` with: a\n   simple link, a self-loop, a link with a free end, and the blueprint mode.\n\nInput example (working names; the dialect is fixed in {{F03}}):\n\n```lino\n(simple: link-view\n  (link (id 1) (source 1) (target 2))\n  (markers (source bar) (target arrow))\n  (blueprint true)\n  (grid true))\n```\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-components/src/links-view/{geometry,markers,render-svg,render-canvas,zoom-pan,animator}.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/src/links-view/link-view.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/tests/links-view/*.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/tests/e2e/link-view.spec.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/examples/link-view.html`, `.changeset/*.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `geometry.test.js` checks the centre of a straight link and of a curved\n      link against fixed numbers (tolerance 1e-6).\n- [ ] SVG and Canvas renderers import marker shapes only from `markers.js`\n      (test scans imports) and produce matching pixels within 2 % in a\n      Playwright pixel comparison.\n- [ ] No module in `src/links-view/` has module-level mutable state (lint rule\n      or test).\n- [ ] With nothing moving, no `requestAnimationFrame` callback runs for 1\n      second (test with the injected `raf`).\n- [ ] Two `link-view` elements on one page zoom independently (Playwright).\n- [ ] `renderLinkSvg` gives identical output on two runs (snapshot).\n- [ ] No network request goes to esm.sh or any CDN (Playwright).\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnode --test packages/ui-components/tests/links-view/*.test.js\nnpx playwright test packages/ui-components/tests/e2e/link-view.spec.js\nnpm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run check:duplication\n```\n\nExpected screenshots: the four gallery cases in light and dark themes; the\nblueprint case shows the start point green, the end point red, the centre\nblack (or the token colour in dark mode) and the other points blue with a\ndashed `4 2` guide.\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- links-visuals (Unlicense): port geometry, markers, zoom-pan and grid.\n- konard.github.io `src/links/glyph.js`: learn the glyph rules only (no\n  licence).\n- `d3-zoom` (ISC) is optional; stale results are dropped.\n- SVG back end for up to 2 000 links and Canvas back end above that, sharing\n  `markers.js`.\n- Export to SVG and PNG.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Converting arbitrary LiNo text to a network ({{F35}}).\n- 3D views (https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase-app/issues/159) and\n  WebGL rendering for more than 10⁴ links (follow-up; see Sigma.js below).\n- Editing link values (the app handles actions).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **Blocked by {{F33}}**: `linkGeometry`, `markers.js`, both renderers,\n  `createZoomPan` and `createAnimator`.\n- **Blocked by {{F08}}**: the store subscription API; the view listens to\n  link additions, removals and changes and updates only the changed links.\n  Until {{F08}} exists, use an in-memory stub with the same `subscribe`\n  signature.\n- **Related:** {{F32}} (Dagre layout), {{F27}} (context menu), {{F35}},\n  {{F58}} (konard.github.io migration), {{F62}} (deepcase migration).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. [2026-11-01T11:53:03.296Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F40\ntitle: 'Material 3 theme and MUI mapping'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 5\nblocked_by: [F39, F04]\nrequirements: [R14, R15]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nRequirement R15 asks us to follow the Google, Microsoft and Apple guidelines\nso that moving off Material UI (MUI) and similar frameworks is easy. Many of\nour projects, and many outside ones, use MUI. The Deep 2025 rewrite is one of\nthem: it runs MUI 6 in dark mode\n([deepcase.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)).\n\nThe research recommends this route\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)):\n\n1. Implement Material 3 as a theme package. M3 tokens are `md.ref.*`\n   (reference) and `md.sys.*` (system), and palettes are generated from a\n   seed colour with material-color-utilities (Apache-2.0).\n2. Add a converter from an MUI theme object to LiNo tokens.\n3. Add a mapping table from MUI component and prop names to ours.\n\nMaterial Web (MWC) is in maintenance mode\n(https://github.com/material-components/material-web/discussions/5642), so\n**do not depend on it**. MUI Core is MIT, but MUI X Pro and Premium are\ncommercial, so never import them.\n\n## Goal\n\nShip `material3`, a theme package with light, dark and high-contrast schemes,\nbuilt on the {{F39}} engine and following the Material 3 digest from {{F04}}.\nAlongside it, ship `muiThemeToLino()` and a machine-readable MUI-to-UI mapping\ntable. The JSX importer ({{F51}}) and the migration guide ({{F57}}) both\nconsume that table.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/material3/`:\n  - colour roles (`primary`, `on-primary`, `primary-container`, `secondary`,\n    `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `surface-container-*`, `outline` and so\n    on) for light, dark and high contrast;\n  - the type scale (display, headline, title, body and label, each in large,\n    medium and small);\n  - the shape scale, elevation levels, the motion easing and duration tokens,\n    and the state-layer opacities.\n- Style rules and component templates for the {{F26}} controls: filled,\n  tonal, outlined, text and elevated buttons, text field (filled and\n  outlined), checkbox, radio, switch and slider.\n- `materialThemeFromSeed(seed, options)`, which builds a full LiNo theme from\n  one seed colour with `@material/material-color-utilities`.\n- `muiThemeToLino(themeOptions)`, which converts a plain MUI `createTheme`\n  options object into a LiNo theme that extends `material3`. It must not\n  depend on MUI.\n- `mui-mapping.lino`, which maps MUI component names, props and prop values\n  to our kinds and props, and marks each row's status.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Parsing JSX or `sx` props, which belongs to {{F51}}. Writing the migration\n  guide prose, which belongs to {{F57}}.\n- Material 3 Expressive (2025) variants. A follow-up issue can add them as a\n  second package.\n- Bundling Roboto or Material Symbols. Roboto is only named in the\n  `font-family` stack, and icons come from {{F36}}.\n- MUI X (data grid, date pickers). Only rows for components we own are mapped.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F39}} (blocker). Supplies the theme package format, the modes, the\n  contrast check, the templates and `compileThemeCss`.\n- {{F04}} (blocker). Supplies the Material 3 section of the design guidelines\n  digest: token names, roles, values and component rules, with source links.\n  To start before {{F04}} merges, take the values from https://m3.material.io,\n  record each source URL in the theme file comments, and reconcile once\n  {{F04}} lands.\n- Related: {{F26}}, {{F27}}, {{F29}} (component names in the mapping table),\n  {{F41}}, {{F42}}, {{F51}}, {{F54}}, {{F55}}, {{F57}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Add `@material/material-color-utilities` as a dependency of\n   `packages/ui-themes` (Apache-2.0; check the current version). Record its\n   licence in the package README.\n2. Write `scripts/generate-material3.mjs`. It calls\n   `materialThemeFromSeed('#6750A4')`, the M3 baseline seed, and writes\n   `themes/material3/colors.lino`. Generated values are committed, so the\n   build does not need the generator. The generated file must look like this:\n   ```lino\n   (material3-colors: theme\n     (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n     (token color.on-primary '#FFFFFF')\n     (pair color.on-primary color.primary)\n     (mode dark\n       (token color.primary '#D0BCFF')\n       (token color.on-primary '#381E72')))\n   ```\n   Do not copy these numbers. Take the real values from the generator output.\n3. In `src/material3/seed.js`, implement:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {string} seed hex colour\n    * @param {{ id?: string, contrast?: number, variant?: 'tonal-spot' | 'vibrant' | 'neutral' }} [options]\n    * @returns {string} LiNo theme text with light, dark and high-contrast modes */\n   export function materialThemeFromSeed(seed, options) {}\n   ```\n4. Write `themes/material3/theme.lino`. It does `(extends base)` and pulls in\n   `colors.lino`, `type.lino`, `shape.lino`, `elevation.lino` and\n   `motion.lino`.\n   - Names map from M3 to ours, for example `md.sys.color.primary` becomes\n     `color.primary` and `md.sys.shape.corner.medium` becomes\n     `shape.corner.medium`.\n   - Each file records the original M3 token name next to our name as\n     `(m3 md.sys.color.primary)`, so a reverse export is possible.\n   - Take the type-scale, shape, elevation and motion values from the {{F04}}\n     digest, and check every value against m3.material.io.\n5. Write `themes/material3/styles.lino` and `templates.lino` for the\n   in-scope controls. Use the state layers with `(state hover ...)`,\n   `(state focus ...)` and `(state pressed ...)` from {{F12}}. The focus ring\n   must remain visible in high-contrast and forced-colours modes.\n6. In `src/material3/mui.js`, implement:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {object} themeOptions plain object passed to MUI createTheme()\n    * @param {{ id?: string }} [options]\n    * @returns {{ lino: string, unmapped: string[] }} */\n   export function muiThemeToLino(themeOptions, options) {}\n   ```\n   Map these fields, and list every other path in `unmapped`:\n   - `palette.mode`;\n   - `palette.{primary,secondary,error,warning,info,success}.{main,contrastText}`;\n   - `palette.background.{default,paper}` and `palette.text.{primary,secondary}`;\n   - `shape.borderRadius`, `spacing` (when it is a number), `typography.fontFamily`;\n   - `breakpoints.values` and `transitions.duration`.\n\n   An example output:\n   ```lino\n   (mui-import: theme\n     (extends material3)\n     (token color.primary '#1976D2')\n     (token color.on-primary '#FFFFFF')\n     (token shape.corner.small 4px)\n     (token space.unit 8px))\n   ```\n7. Write `themes/material3/mui-mapping.lino`, with one link per row:\n   ```lino\n   (map Button (kind button)\n     (prop variant contained (variant filled))\n     (prop variant outlined (variant outlined))\n     (prop variant text (variant text))\n     (status mapped))\n   (map TextField (kind text-field) (status partial))\n   ```\n   - Cover at least these MUI components: Button, IconButton, TextField,\n     Checkbox, Radio, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider, Select, Dialog, Menu,\n     Tooltip, Snackbar, Drawer, AppBar, Tabs, Card, List, Table, Chip, Avatar,\n     Badge, Box, Stack, Grid, Typography and CircularProgress.\n   - Use the kind names actually merged in {{F26}}–{{F29}}, and mark a row\n     `(status none)` when we have no equivalent yet.\n   - Export `getMuiMapping()`, which returns the parsed table as plain\n     objects.\n8. Write `docs/themes/material3.md`. It holds a generated Markdown version of\n   the mapping table, produced by `scripts/mapping-to-md.mjs`; do not edit it\n   by hand.\n9. In `examples/themes/material3.html`, build a gallery page that shows all\n   in-scope controls in light, dark and high contrast. Add Playwright\n   screenshots, tests and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/material3/{theme,colors,type,shape,elevation,motion,styles,templates,mui-mapping}.lino`\n- `packages/ui-themes/src/material3/{seed,mui,mapping}.js`, exported from `src/index.js`\n- `packages/ui-themes/scripts/{generate-material3,mapping-to-md}.mjs`\n- `packages/ui-themes/tests/{material3-theme,material3-seed,mui-theme,mui-mapping}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-themes/tests/fixtures/mui-theme-*.json`, three MUI theme option objects\n- `docs/themes/material3.md`, `examples/themes/material3.html`\n- `tests/e2e/theme-material3.spec.js`, `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `material3-theme.test.js`: the package loads with zero error\n      diagnostics, and every `pair` passes 4.5:1 in light, dark and high\n      contrast.\n- [ ] Running `generate-material3.mjs` twice produces byte-identical\n      `colors.lino` (determinism test).\n- [ ] `material3-seed.test.js`: for the baseline seed `'#6750A4'`, `primary`\n      equals the material-color-utilities output for the same seed.\n- [ ] `mui-theme.test.js`: each fixture converts to LiNo that parses with\n      `links-notation` and loads in {{F39}}. `unmapped` lists unknown paths.\n      `palette.primary.main` becomes `color.primary`.\n- [ ] `mui-mapping.test.js`: every listed MUI component has a row, every\n      `kind` in a `mapped` or `partial` row is a registered kind, and the\n      generated `docs/themes/material3.md` is up to date. The test regenerates\n      it and compares.\n- [ ] No dependency on `@material/web`, `@mui/*` or any Roboto or Material\n      Symbols font package (`npm ls` checks are in the test).\n- [ ] Playwright screenshots of the gallery in light, dark and high contrast\n      are attached to the pull request, and axe reports no violations.\n- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication` and\n      `npm test` pass.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnode packages/ui-themes/scripts/generate-material3.mjs && git diff --exit-code packages/ui-themes/themes/material3\nnode --test packages/ui-themes/tests/material3-*.test.js packages/ui-themes/tests/mui-*.test.js\nnpx playwright test tests/e2e/theme-material3.spec.js\nnpm test\n```\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- Material 3 guidelines: https://m3.material.io. [2026-11-01T11:53:08.947Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F03\ntitle: 'UI dialect specification v0 with conformance fixtures'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 1\nblocked_by: []\nrequirements: [R2, R3, R6, R7, R8]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nEvery UI concept in this framework (element, property, style rule, token, theme, behaviour, animation, recording, override, asset record) is a link, and Links Notation (LiNo) is its only canonical text form (principles 1–3 of [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). The samples in [`docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/) show the intended _UI dialect_, but nothing defines it yet. The JavaScript core ({{F06}}, {{F07}}), the Swift ({{F21}}) and Kotlin ({{F23}}) parsers and every renderer need one written contract and one shared set of fixtures.\n\nThe research found concrete gaps that must be closed here (sections 4–6 of [links-notation-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)): typed values, units and colours, `:` and `#` in values, ordering, ids and scoping, reference sigils, schemas, expressions and bindings, and security limits. Facts measured with `links-notation` 0.27.1 (re-run them; check the current version):\n\n- Parse shapes differ ([`experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/experiments/issue-1/lino-parse-shapes.mjs), section \"Links Notation parse shapes\" of ARCHITECTURE.md). `(ok: button (label 'OK'))` on one line is one nested link. The same text split over lines inside parentheses gives path links `(ok: button)`, `((ok: button) (label OK))`. The indented form gives the same path links from `parse()`, and a real tree only from `parseGroups()`.\n- `(x #6750A4)` is a syntax error (the comment swallows `)`); `(x '#6750A4')` works.\n- `(t a:b)` is a syntax error; `(t 'a:b')` works.\n- `(t 1 '1')` gives two equal references `1`: the quoted/bare distinction is lost.\n- `(a: b)` followed by `(a: c)` parses without error (duplicate ids are not detected).\n- `@color.primary`, `$draft.text` and `button.save` are plain references; no sigil has a meaning.\n\n## Goal\n\nPublish `docs/spec/` as version `ui-dialect/0`: a normative description of how LiNo links map to a UI element tree, plus language-neutral conformance fixtures (`.lino` input and expected element tree JSON) that the JS, Swift and Kotlin implementations must all pass. Every open question in research section 5 is either decided or listed in `docs/spec/open-questions.md` with an owner issue.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Element model: `(id: kind positional-values... (property ...)... child-elements...)`.\n- The **tree projection** that turns all three parse shapes into the same tree.\n- The rule that classifies a sublink as property, child element, or unknown.\n- The value grammar and its JSON form: references, numbers, dimensions, durations, colours, token references, actions.\n- A machine-readable vocabulary (`docs/spec/vocabulary.lino`) listing the v0 kinds, their properties and the multi-valued properties. It covers the samples: `document`, `stack`, `text`, `button`, `image`, `theme`, `style`, `animation`, `recording`, `overrides` and `asset`.\n- Diagnostics: codes, severities, and where they point.\n- Limits: maximum depth, maximum input size, and \"handlers are names, never code\".\n- At least 30 fixtures and a checker script with a test.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The `ui-core` implementation of the projection ({{F06}}) and typed value parsing ({{F07}}).\n- Source-preserving edits and comment round trips ({{F14}}).\n- The full settings schema engine ({{F15}}).\n- The style cascade ({{F12}}) and token export ({{F11}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\nNo blockers; start immediately. `links-notation` is already in `node_modules` as a transitive dependency. Add it as a root `devDependency` (check the current version; the research used 0.27.1).\n\nRelated:\n\n- {{F06}} implements the projection and runs the fixtures.\n- {{F07}} implements `values.md`.\n- {{F21}} and {{F23}} run the fixtures in Swift and Kotlin.\n- {{F14}} owns comment preservation.\n- {{F15}} grows `vocabulary.lino` into a schema language.\n- {{F02}} owns the `asset` record fields.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `docs/spec/README.md`. Cover the version string `ui-dialect/0`, the RFC 2119 keywords, the list of documents, and how fixtures are named.\n2. Write `docs/spec/elements.md`. An element is a link whose id is the element id and whose first value is its kind. Then define how the remaining values are read:\n   - atoms after the kind are positional values (`(greeting: text 'Hello, links')`);\n   - a sublink with an id (`(body: stack ...)`) is a child element;\n   - a sublink without an id is a **property** when its head is declared for the parent kind in `vocabulary.lino`;\n   - otherwise it is an **anonymous child** when its head is a registered kind;\n   - otherwise it is kept verbatim with the diagnostic `unknown-sublink` (warning).\n\n   Decide, and write down, that the kind is the first value, never an id prefix (`button.save:` is just an id with a dot).\n3. Write `docs/spec/projection.md`. It must say:\n   - Implementations MUST project `parse()` output by **path folding**: a link without an id whose first value is a link structurally equal to an already-seen element head (or to a path made of them) appends its other values to that element or sublink.\n   - `parseGroups()` MAY be used where available; the result MUST be identical.\n   - Give the algorithm in pseudocode, plus the worked example of the four links `(ok: button)`, `((ok: button) (label OK))`, `((ok: button) (on press))` and `(((ok: button) (on press)) (navigate home))`.\n4. Write `docs/spec/values.md`:\n   - **Typing is schema-driven:** the vocabulary declares each property type. Quoting never changes a type, because the parser loses it.\n   - **Types:** `string`, `number` (`-1`, `1.5e3`), `dimension` (`16px`, `1.5rem`, `50%`; units px, rem, em, %, vw, vh), `duration` (`150ms`, `0.2s`), `color`, `enum`, `token-ref`, `element-ref` and `action`.\n   - **Colours** are quoted hex (`'#6750A4'`, `'#6750A4CC'`) or `(oklch 0.6 0.2 300)` / `(rgb 103 80 164)`. A bare `#` is invalid.\n   - **No `:` in bare values.** Use structured links instead: `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))`, `(aspect 16 9)`. Quote URLs.\n5. Decide the **reference form** in `values.md`. Canonical v0 is the structured form used by the samples: `(token color.primary)`, `(param draft.text)` and an element id as a bare reference. The prefixes `@` and `$` are reserved: a value starting with them gives the diagnostic `reserved-sigil` until a later version defines them as shorthand. Also document:\n   - resolution order: theme chain, then base;\n   - a cycle gives the error `reference-cycle`;\n   - fallbacks use `(or (token a) (token b) 8px)`.\n6. Write `docs/spec/ordering-and-ids.md`:\n   - Children and multi-valued properties (`on`, `token`, `track`, `key`, `event`, `set`) are ordered sequences.\n   - Single-valued properties are a set: a repeated property means the last one wins, with a `duplicate-property` warning.\n   - Element ids are unique per document; a duplicate gives the error `duplicate-id`.\n   - A dot in a token name is a path separator. A dot in an element id has no meaning.\n   - Cross-document references are deferred to `open-questions.md`.\n7. Write `docs/spec/behaviour.md`:\n   - Shape: `(on <event> <action>...)`, where an action is a link whose head is a vocabulary action (`navigate`, `emit`, `set`, `toggle`, `focus`).\n   - Bindings are reserved as `(bind <property> (param path))`.\n   - Conditions (`when`) and expressions are deferred and recorded.\n   - Handlers are data and are never evaluated as code. `navigate` targets are ids or quoted URLs; renderers MUST reject the `javascript:` scheme.\n8. Write `docs/spec/limits.md`:\n   - depth at most 64 (the `links-notation` default `maxDepth`);\n   - a `maxInputSize` value that you choose and record (for example 1 MiB; check the parser option name in the current version);\n   - unknown kinds render as an inert placeholder and are never executed.\n9. Write `docs/spec/vocabulary.lino`, one link per kind. A sketch:\n\n   ```lino\n   (button: kind\n     (positional label)\n     (property label string)\n     (property variant (enum filled outlined text))\n     (property on action multi)\n     (children none))\n   ```\n\n10. Write `docs/spec/element-tree.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12) for the expected trees. Use this shape:\n\n    ```json\n    {\n      \"spec\": \"ui-dialect/0\",\n      \"elements\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"ok\",\n          \"kind\": \"button\",\n          \"positional\": [],\n          \"properties\": [\n            { \"name\": \"label\", \"values\": [\"OK\"] },\n            { \"name\": \"on\", \"values\": [\"press\", [\"navigate\", \"home\"]] }\n          ],\n          \"children\": []\n        }\n      ],\n      \"diagnostics\": []\n    }\n    ```\n\n    In this shape:\n    - a reference atom is a JSON string;\n    - a nested non-element link is a JSON array;\n    - an anonymous element has `\"id\": null`;\n    - properties keep source order.\n11. Add fixtures under `docs/spec/fixtures/<area>/<name>.lino`, each with a sibling `<name>.tree.json`, or `<name>.diagnostics.json` for invalid input. Areas and minimum counts:\n    - `shapes/`: one-line, multi-line and indented forms of the same document, all with one identical tree (at least 3);\n    - `elements/` (5);\n    - `properties/` (5), including duplicates;\n    - `values/` (6): colours, dimensions, durations, URLs and `(or ...)`;\n    - `references/` (3), including `reserved-sigil`;\n    - `behaviour/` (3);\n    - `errors/` (5): `duplicate-id`, `unknown-sublink`, `reference-cycle`, depth over the limit, and unquoted hex as a syntax error;\n    - a copy of each sample in `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/`.\n12. Write `docs/spec/open-questions.md`. List each undecided point with the alternatives and an owner issue:\n    - comments on round trip ({{F14}});\n    - asking upstream for a `quoted` flag on references;\n    - whether the multi-line path expansion is intended upstream (open an issue at https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues if none exists, and link it);\n    - cross-document ids;\n    - expressions and `when`;\n    - links-theory doublet mapping of the element tree.\n13. Add `scripts/check-spec-fixtures.mjs` and `tests/spec-fixtures.test.js`. The script:\n    - parses every `.lino` with `links-notation`; files in `errors/` named `syntax-*` must throw, all others must parse;\n    - checks that every `.lino` has exactly one sibling JSON;\n    - validates each JSON against the schema (with `ajv`, MIT, as a devDependency, or a hand-written check);\n    - checks that all `shapes/*.tree.json` files in a group are byte-equal.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `docs/spec/README.md`, `elements.md`, `projection.md`, `values.md`, `ordering-and-ids.md`, `behaviour.md`, `limits.md`, `open-questions.md`\n- `docs/spec/vocabulary.lino`, `docs/spec/element-tree.schema.json`\n- `docs/spec/fixtures/**` (30 or more `.lino` files with their JSON)\n- `scripts/check-spec-fixtures.mjs`, `tests/spec-fixtures.test.js`\n- `package.json`: add the devDependencies, plus the script `\"check:spec\": \"node scripts/check-spec-fixtures.mjs\"`\n- `.changeset/*.md`, if the changeset check requires one for the new script and test\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] All eight documents listed above exist under `docs/spec/`, and each uses MUST/SHOULD/MAY wording.\n- [ ] Each research gap is either decided in a spec document or listed in `open-questions.md` with an owner issue: typed values, units, colours, `:`/`#`, ordering, ids/scoping, sigils, schemas, expressions/bindings, security, and the three section 6.5 decisions.\n- [ ] `docs/spec/fixtures/` contains at least 30 `.lino` files, each with exactly one `.tree.json` or `.diagnostics.json`.\n- [ ] `shapes/` proves that one-line, multi-line and indented input give byte-identical trees.\n- [ ] Every sample from `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/` has a fixture.\n- [ ] `npm run check:spec` exits 0, and `node --test tests/spec-fixtures.test.js` passes.\n- [ ] Every LiNo snippet in `docs/spec/*.md` parses with `links-notation`; None of our\napps use Vue today; the only Vue code is the `vue-usage` example of\nlino-i18n, which the inventory names as the pilot for this binding\n([ui-projects-inventory.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/ui-projects-inventory.md)\nsections 4 and 5, \"Wave 6\").\n\nThe architecture keeps Vue thin: `ui-dom` ({{F16}}) renders custom elements,\nand the Vue package only mounts it, exposes the store as reactive state and\nlets Vue components render custom kinds. Vue supports custom elements when the\ncompiler is told which tags are custom\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)\nsection 1, \"Web Components\" and \"Stencil\"). Dependencies:\n   `@link-foundation/ui-dom`, `@link-foundation/ui-store`,\n   `@link-foundation/ui-core`.
