Other links\ncan point at the middle of a link. The facts below come from the\n[research](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md).\n\nThe project uses plain HTML pages with ES modules in `js/`, SVG rendering\nwith an optional Canvas mode, a Bun `serve.ts` dev server, `node --test`\nunit tests and Playwright/browser-commander e2e tests. It is Unlicense, so\ncode can move into the framework directly.\n\nProblems found:\n\n- **Unpinned CDN.** D3 v7 is loaded at runtime from `https://esm.sh/use-m`\n  as `use('d3')`. It does not work offline, is not pinned, and is a\n  supply-chain risk.\n- **Global state.** `js/state.mjs` holds global singletons, so two views\n  cannot share a page.\n- **Duplicate renderer.** `js/canvas-render.mjs` re-implements the SVG\n  markers and paths by hand.\n- **Busy loop.** `js/animation.mjs` runs `requestAnimationFrame` every frame,\n  even when idle.\n- **Copied CSS.** Inline CSS is copied into every page. Markers are\n  hard-coded black.\n- **Old experiments.** `failed-attempts/` holds 76 HTML snapshots.\n\n{{F33}} ports the single-link geometry into the framework. This issue\nswitches links-visuals itself to that package, so the lab page and the\nframework stop diverging.\n\n## Goal\n\nEvery links-visuals page renders through `@link-foundation/ui-*` packages,\nwith no runtime CDN. Renderers ({{F16}}), dev mode\n({{F46}}), the WYSIWYG designer ({{F48}}) and the recorder ({{F45}}) need a\n**mutable** network that changes on the fly (R9), keeps the identity of every\nelement across edits (so a DOM node, a selection or an animation target stays\nattached), notifies subscribers, groups edits into transactions and supports\nundo/redo (R5).\n\nPrior art in our repositories:\n\n- formal-ai keeps an append-only LiNo event log (`js/memory.js`) and the\n  research recommends that \"every WYSIWYG edit is an appended event\", which\n  gives undo/redo and replay for free\n  ([formal-ai.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md)).\n- meta-sovereign-chat stores one `lino-objects-codec` record per line in an\n  append-only log with tombstones and compaction\n  (`js/src/storage/lino-store.js`,\n  [meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-store` (`@link-foundation/ui-store`) holds a UI document as a\nmutable links network with stable IDs, emits change events, supports nested\ntransactions and undo/redo, and exports back to LiNo. Persistence is {{F09}}.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `createStore({ document, text, historyLimit })` from a `UiDocument` or LiNo.\n- Stable IDs: named elements keep their name (`ok`); anonymous elements get a\n  generated ID that never changes while the store lives.\n- Operations: `insert`, `remove`, `move`, `setProp`, `removeProp`, `rename`.\n- Change events and `subscribe`; transactions; undo/redo; an ordered\n  operation log that {{F09}} persists and {{F45}} replays.\n- `toDocument()` and `toLino()` (via {{F06}} `format`).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- IndexedDB or any storage ({{F09}}); configuration layers ({{F10}}).\n- Collaboration or CRDT merging (a later issue may add it).\n- Keeping comments and layout of the source text ({{F14}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F06}} (blocker): `parse`, `format`, `UiNode`. Consumed: the initial tree\n  and the formatter. Until it merges, build stores from hand-written `UiNode`\n  objects in tests.\n- Related: {{F09}}, {{F10}}, {{F16}} (assumes events shaped\n  `{ type, id, parentId, index, props }`), {{F45}}, {{F46}}, {{F48}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-store/package.json`\n   (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-store\"`, `\"type\": \"module\"`), dependency\n   `@link-foundation/ui-core` (workspace). Reads return frozen snapshots; nobody gets a\n   mutable reference.\n4. `src/ops.js`: each operation is plain data with its inverse:\n   ```js\n   /** @typedef {{ op: 'insert', parentId: string, index: number, node: UiNode }\n    *   | { op: 'remove', id: string }\n    *   | { op: 'move', id: string, parentId: string, index: number }\n    *   | { op: 'setProp', id: string, name: string, values: unknown[] }\n    *   | { op: 'removeProp', id: string, name: string }\n    *   | { op: 'rename', id: string, to: string }} Op */\n   /** @returns {{ event: ChangeEvent, inverse: Op }} */\n   export function applyOp(model, op) {}\n   ```\n   `setProp` replaces the **last** prop with that name (duplicate key: last\n   wins, as recommended in the ecosystem research, section 5) or appends one.\n5. `src/store.js`: public API\n   ```js\n   /** @param {{ document?: UiDocument, text?: string, historyLimit?: number }} options */\n   export function createStore(options) {}\n   // store.get(id), store.roots(), store.children(id), store.parentOf(id)\n   // store.insert(parentId, index, node), store.remove(id), store.move(id, parentId, index)\n   // store.setProp(id, name, values), store.removeProp(id, name), store.rename(id, to)\n   // store.transaction(label, fn, { origin }) -> result of fn\n   // store.undo(), store.redo(), store.canUndo(), store.canRedo()\n   // store.subscribe(listener) -> unsubscribe\n   // store.log() -> LogEntry[]; store.toDocument(); store.toLino(options)\n   ```\n   An operation outside `transaction` is its own transaction.\n6. Events: `{ seq, tx, origin, type: 'insert'|'update'|'remove'|'move'|'rename', id, parentId, index, props, before, after }`.\n   Listeners are called once per committed transaction with the array of\n   events (so {{F16}} can batch). A listener that throws does not break the\n   store or other listeners; the error is reported via\n   `options.onListenerError`.\n7. Transactions: nested calls join the outer one; if `fn` throws, apply the\n   collected inverses in reverse order, emit nothing, and rethrow.\n8. Undo/redo (`src/history.js`): undo applies the inverses of the last\n   transaction as a **new** transaction with `origin: 'undo'` (append-only,\n   like formal-ai); redo re-applies. A new user transaction clears the redo\n   stack. Keep at most `historyLimit` (default 500) transactions.\n9. [2026-11-01T11:53:21.329Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F49\ntitle: 'Animation timeline editor'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 7\nblocked_by: [F48, F45]\nrequirements: [R4, R5, R10]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nIssue #1 asks to \"record and replay any animations and interactions in the\nLinks Notation format\" (R4) and for a WYSIWYG editor like Visual Studio (R5,\nR10). Animations and recordings are links\n([`samples/animation.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/animation.lino)):\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (easing standard)\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n(recording-1: recording\n  (started '2026-11-01T12:00:00Z')\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nA `track` has a property name and `(key <offset> <value>)` links, where the\noffset is a fraction from 0 to 1 of the duration. A `recording` has\n`(event <time>ms <action>)` links. {{F44}} plays animations, {{F45}} records\nand replays interactions. This issue adds the visual editor for both, as a\npanel of the designer from {{F48}}, as planned in\n[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).\n\nResearch\n([existing-solutions.md section 4](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)):\nTheatre.js core is Apache-2.0 but **Theatre.js Studio (the timeline UI) is\nAGPL-3.0**: use it for ideas only, copy no code and add no dependency. GSAP is\nnot allowed. Motion Canvas (MIT) and Anime.js (MIT) are good references for\ntimeline UX and keyframe models.\n\n## Goal\n\nA **Timeline** panel in `@link-foundation/ui-designer` that shows the\nanimations and recordings of the open document as tracks with keyframes and\nevents, lets the user scrub, play, add, move and delete keyframes and events,\nand writes every change back to the LiNo source through the designer's\nsource-preserving sync, with undo/redo.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Timeline panel docked at the bottom of the designer (next to Source),\n  listing: one row per `animation` (expandable to one lane per `track`) and\n  one row per `recording` (one lane of events).\n- Time ruler in milliseconds, zoom (Ctrl/Cmd+wheel and buttons), horizontal\n  scroll, playhead scrubbing that seeks the {{F44}} player (or the {{F45}}\n  replayer for recordings) so the canvas shows that moment.\n- Play, pause, stop, loop toggle; playback respects `prefers-reduced-motion`\n  only for the preview of the designer chrome, not for the edited animation.\n- Keyframes: select (click, Shift+click), move by drag with snapping to the\n  playhead, other keyframes and a frame grid (default 60 fps), add at the\n  playhead (`K` key or button), delete (`Delete`), edit value and easing in the\n  Properties panel of {{F46}}/{{F48}}.\n- Recording events: move in time, delete, edit the action in Properties.\n- Duration: drag the end handle of an animation; when the duration is a token\n  (as in the sample), dragging asks to replace it with a literal value.\n- Keyboard: arrow keys move the selected keyframe by one frame, Shift+arrows\n  by 10 frames; `Home`/`End` move the playhead; space toggles play.\n- Every edit is one store transaction ({{F08}}) and is written to the source\n  through the designer sync ({{F48}} M4, {{F14}}).\n- Timeline layout described in LiNo (`src/timeline/timeline.lino`) and\n  rendered with the framework.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Curve (graph) editor for easing; easing is chosen from a list. Follow-up.\n- Recording itself (capturing input) is {{F45}}.\n- Exporting animations to Lottie: {{F53}}.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F48}} (blocker): designer shell, docked panels, selection, Properties\n  panel, the transaction commands and the two-way source sync.\n- {{F45}} (blocker): recording model, `recording` parsing and the replayer\n  with seek; through it the {{F44}} player (`seek(ms)`, `play()`, `pause()`).\n  Use the names merged in those issues; this issue only names the needs.\n- Related: {{F11}} (duration tokens), {{F26}} (buttons, slider, select),\n  {{F05}} (Playwright tests).\n- The pure modules (steps 2–4) can be built and tested before {{F48}} merges.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-designer/src/timeline/`.\n2. `model.js` (pure):\n   - `readTimeline(tree)` returns\n     `{ animations: [{ id, target, durationMs, tracks: [{ property, keys: [{ offset, value }] }] }], recordings: [{ id, events: [{ timeMs, action }] }] }`;\n     a token duration is resolved through the token resolver passed in.\n   - `moveKeyframe(track, index, offset)` clamps to `0..1`, keeps the keys\n     sorted and never puts two keys at the same offset (returns a new track).\n   - `insertKeyframe(track, offset, value)`, `deleteKeyframe(track, index)`;\n     the first and last keys may be deleted only if two or more remain.\n   - `moveEvent(recording, index, timeMs)` (clamped to `>= 0`, sorted).\n3. `scale.js` (pure): `timeToX(ms, { zoom, scroll })`,\n   `xToTime(x, { zoom, scroll })`, `snapTime(ms, { fps, candidates, threshold })`.\n4. `commands.js`: wrap the model operations into designer commands that emit\n   the matching LiNo edits, e.g. moving the middle key of the sample to 0.4\n   changes only that link to `(key 0.4 0.96)`.\n5. `timeline.lino`, `timeline.js`: the panel (ruler, rows, lanes, keyframe\n   diamonds as focusable buttons with `aria-label` such as\n   `scale key at 40%, value 0.96`), playhead, toolbar.\n6. Wire the playhead to the player/replayer seek and the canvas.\n7. Add the panel to the designer layout and a timeline example to\n   `packages/ui-designer/examples/`.\n8. Tests: unit tests for steps 2–4; Playwright test for scrubbing and dragging.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-designer/src/timeline/{model,scale,commands,timeline}.js`\n- `packages/ui-designer/src/timeline/timeline.lino`\n- `packages/ui-designer/src/designer.lino` (add the panel)\n- `packages/ui-designer/examples/timeline.html`\n- `packages/ui-designer/tests/timeline-{model,scale,commands}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-designer/tests/fixtures/animation.lino` (copy of the sample)\n- Browser test in the {{F05}} location; Links Notation can carry the whole UI dialect, with three caveats\n\nAll seven samples in [`samples/`](samples/) parse with `links-notation` 0.27.1\nand format back to an equal links network. The experiments found three\nthings the framework has to design around:\n\n1. **One element, several link shapes.** The same element gives different\n   link structures depending on how it is written\n   ([`data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt`](data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt)):\n\n   ```text\n   single line       -> (ok: button (label OK) (on press (navigate home)))\n   multi-line parens -> ((ok: button) ((ok: button) (label OK)) ((ok: button) (on press (navigate home))))\n   indented parse()  -> (ok: button), ((ok: button) (label OK)), ...\n   parseGroups()     -> a tree: (ok: button) with children (label OK), (on press) -> (navigate home)\n   ```\n\n   So `ui-core` needs one **tree projection** that maps all forms to the same\n   element tree. The dialect specification (roadmap issue F03) fixes it with\n   conformance fixtures that every implementation must pass.\n\n2. **Round trip loses source details.** `Link.format()` does not keep\n   comments, layout or the original quoting. The designer must edit files\n   without destroying them, so source-preserving edits are a separate issue\n   (F14).\n\n3. **Syntax traps.** `#` after whitespace starts a comment, so colours like\n   `'#6750A4'` must be quoted, and `:` cannot appear in bare values (URLs and\n   times must be quoted). The specification and the error messages of\n   `ui-core` must say so.\n\n### 2. Swift and Kotlin need parsers first\n\nThere is no Swift port of `links-notation`, and the Java port is not published\n([links-notation#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)).\nThe roadmap therefore has a parser issue before each native renderer (F21 and\nF23). Both are driven by the shared fixtures.\n\n### 3. The same UI pieces are rebuilt again and again\n\nThe inventory found the same patterns in many repositories:\n\n- theme toggles in about 16 repositories;\n- settings panels in 7;\n- four different i18n implementations;\n- links or graph views in 10 (d3-force, Cytoscape, canvas/SVG, doublets-web);\n- chat UIs in 9.\n\nEach of these is a framework package in the roadmap. That is what makes\n\"project code gets simpler for humans and agents\" (R23) measurable: a migrated\nrepository deletes its local copy.\n\n### 4. The architecture follows from the requirements\n\nThe requirements are: runtime editing on any site (R9, R11), \"every other\nframework is just LiNo\" (R6), and five platforms (R18–R22). Together they rule\nout a code-generation-first design (the lesson of Airbnb Lona and Mitosis).\nThe proposal in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) is:\n\n- a LiNo **runtime interpreter** with stable link IDs, and thin renderers per\n  platform;\n- **Web Components** as the reference renderer;\n- **configuration layers** (defaults < theme < site < user < session), so dev\n  mode edits only the top layers, and \"make these the defaults\" (R12) is a\n  diff exported as a LiNo patch for an agent;\n- **themes** as LiNo packages of tokens, style rules and control templates.\n  This is the XAML idea, and it covers both \"classic UIs as themes\" (R14) and\n  Material, Fluent and Apple alignment (R15).\n\n### 5. Licensing narrows the library choice\n\nThe public-domain goal (R25–R27) excludes several popular options:\n\n- GSAP (proprietary terms that forbid visual animation builders);\n- the tldraw SDK (licence key);\n- Theatre.js Studio (AGPL);\n- Remix Icon (custom licence since 2026);\n- SF Symbols (restricted).\n\nELK and Graphviz (EPL) are allowed only as optional plugins. Every asset needs\na record with its SPDX licence, which the licensing issue (F02) implements with\nREUSE 3.3.\n\n## Defects found in the repository\n\nThe repository was created from a template, and several things on `main` are\nbroken or still describe the template. It has no comments, and the\n   pull request had no review comments while this work was done.\n2. **Source repositories.** Every repository named in the issue was read from\n   shallow, blob-filtered clones and `gh api`. Downloaded code was treated as\n   data and never executed. Each repository has a report that covers:\n   - purpose and stack;\n   - UI inventory;\n   - configuration and settings model;\n   - theming, i18n and animation;\n   - assets and licences;\n   - open UI issues;\n   - patterns worth adopting;\n   - duplication candidates;\n   - limitations;\n   - migration notes.\n3. **All other repositories.** The four owners were listed in full (konard\n   needed the paginated REST API, because it has more than 1,000\n   repositories). About 120 UI candidates were checked by file tree and\n   `package.json`. The result is an inventory of about 95 first-party UI\n   repositories.\n4. **Online research.** Prior art and libraries were researched for each\n   requirement area: declarative UI formats, design tokens, designers,\n   headless components, visualisation, animation, assets and licences, native\n   runtimes and documentation tooling. Licences were checked against the\n   public-domain goal.\n5. **Experiments.** The `links-notation` 0.27.1 JavaScript package was\n   installed and run against UI-shaped LiNo, to check that the proposed\n   dialect can be parsed and formatted back without loss.\n6. **Repository audit.** The failing `main` CI runs were downloaded and their\n   root causes traced. The template leftovers were listed.\n\n## Research reports\n\n| Report                                                                                       | Sources                                                                                                                   | Main takeaways                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [konard.github.io and links-visuals](research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)         | `konard/konard.github.io`, `konard/links-visuals`                                                                         | The most configurable UI so far: a settings schema with presets, diff-only share links, IndexedDB persistence, theme and i18n preferences, and a links network editor. links-visuals gives the reference drawings of a single link. Both become framework packages (settings engine, settings panel, link and network visualisation).                              |\n| [immortality and anime-avatar](research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)                     | `konard/immortality`, `konard/anime-avatar`                                                                               | Fully configurable sci-fi/HUD look built from code (canvas, SVG, Web Audio; no binary assets), many settings axes, charts, and an avatar configuration panel. The HUD look is a theme; the settings axes feed the schema engine; avatar animations need the recorder.                                                                                              |\n| [deepcase](research/deepcase.md)                                                             | `deep-foundation/deepcase`, `deepcase-app`, `perception-*`, `deepcase.github.io`, `deep`                                  | Associative OS UI: graph view (Cytoscape), tabbed editors (Monaco, CodeMirror), windowing, handlers that render links. Three generations with different looks (Chakra v2, perception, MUI 6), which is the reason for \"classic UIs as themes\".                                                                                                                       |\n| [Links Notation ecosystem](research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)                             | `link-foundation/links-notation` and the `lino-*` packages                                                                | The grammar, the implementations (JS, Rust, C#, Python, Go and C++ at 0.27.1; Java and PHP unpublished; no Swift port), round-trip limits (comments, layout and quoting are not kept), syntax traps (`#` starts a comment after whitespace, so hex colours must be quoted), and the related packages (`lino-objects-codec`, `lino-i18n`, `lino-arguments`).      |\n| [meta-sovereign chat](research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)                                       | `link-foundation/meta-sovereign`                                                                                          | The best chat UI in the organisation: 215 `chat-*.js` files, React 19 without JSX, one 13,794-line stylesheet, data already stored as links with `lino-objects-codec`. Its chat components become the chat UI kit.                                                                                                                                                  |\n| [formal-ai](research/formal-ai.md)                                                           | `link-assistant/formal-ai`, its `docs/associative-tech-stack.md`                                                          | Many UI needs (chat, settings, themes, `lino-i18n`, IndexedDB memory, trace and network views, desktop and VS Code hosts) with an admittedly weak UI. Its associative tech stack maps directly onto framework layers (see `ARCHITECTURE.md`).                                                                                                                      |\n| [UI projects inventory](research/ui-projects-inventory.md)                                   | All repositories of `konard`, `deep-foundation`, `link-foundation`, `link-assistant`                                      | About 95 first-party UI repositories. Two app shells are copied everywhere (the template's universal app into 15 repositories, the Deep scaffold into about 8). Theme toggles, settings panels, four i18n implementations, links views and chat UIs are duplicated. Migration waves 0–6 and a ranked top 15.                                                    |\n| [Existing solutions](research/existing-solutions.md)                                         | Online research                                                                                                           | What to build on (DTCG tokens, Web Components, Zag-style state machines, Floating UI, WAAPI, Cytoscape/Sigma/d3-force, ECharts, Mermaid, Lucide, REUSE/SPDX), what to only interoperate with (MUI, Figma, A2UI, Adaptive Cards, Lottie, ELK), and what to avoid for licence or maintenance reasons (GSAP, tldraw SDK, Theatre.js Studio, Remix Icon, SF Symbols, Material Web). |\n\n## Key findings\n\n### 1. Links Notation can carry the whole UI dialect, with three caveats\n\nAll seven samples in [`samples/`](samples/) parse with `links-notation` 0.27.1\nand format back to an equal links network. The experiments found three\nthings the framework has to design around:\n\n1. **One element, several link shapes.** The same element gives different\n   link structures depending on how it is written\n   ([`data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt`](data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt)):\n\n   ```text\n   single line       -> (ok: button (label OK) (on press (navigate home)))\n   multi-line parens -> ((ok: button) ((ok: button) (label OK)) ((ok: button) (on press (navigate home))))\n   indented parse()  -> (ok: button), ((ok: button) (label OK)), ...\n   parseGroups()     -> a tree: (ok: button) with children (label OK), (on press) -> (navigate home)\n   ```\n\n   So `ui-core` needs one **tree projection** that maps all forms to the same\n   element tree. The dialect specification (roadmap issue F03) fixes it with\n   conformance fixtures that every implementation must pass.\n\n2. **Round trip loses source details.** `Link.format()` does not keep\n   comments, layout or the original quoting. The designer must edit files\n   without destroying them, so source-preserving edits are a separate issue\n   (F14).\n\n3. **Syntax traps.** `#` after whitespace starts a comment, so colours like\n   `'#6750A4'` must be quoted, and `:` cannot appear in bare values (URLs and\n   times must be quoted). The specification and the error messages of\n   `ui-core` must say so.\n\n### 2. Swift and Kotlin need parsers first\n\nThere is no Swift port of `links-notation`, and the Java port is not published\n([links-notation#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)).\nThe roadmap therefore has a parser issue before each native renderer (F21 and\nF23). Both are driven by the shared fixtures.\n\n### 3. The same UI pieces are rebuilt again and again\n\nThe inventory found the same patterns in many repositories:\n\n- theme toggles in about 16 repositories;\n- settings panels in 7;\n- four different i18n implementations;\n- links or graph views in 10 (d3-force, Cytoscape, canvas/SVG, doublets-web);\n- chat UIs in 9.\n\nEach of these is a framework package in the roadmap. That is what makes\n\"project code gets simpler for humans and agents\" (R23) measurable: a migrated\nrepository deletes its local copy.\n\n### 4. The architecture follows from the requirements\n\nThe requirements are: runtime editing on any site (R9, R11), \"every other\nframework is just LiNo\" (R6), and five platforms (R18–R22). Together they rule\nout a code-generation-first design (the lesson of Airbnb Lona and Mitosis).\nThe proposal in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) is:\n\n- a LiNo **runtime interpreter** with stable link IDs, and thin renderers per\n  platform;\n- **Web Components** as the reference renderer;\n- **configuration layers** (defaults < theme < site < user < session), so dev\n  mode edits only the top layers, and \"make these the defaults\" (R12) is a\n  diff exported as a LiNo patch for an agent;\n- **themes** as LiNo packages of tokens, style rules and control templates.\n  This is the XAML idea, and it covers both \"classic UIs as themes\" (R14) and\n  Material, Fluent and Apple alignment (R15).\n\n### 5. Licensing narrows the library choice\n\nThe public-domain goal (R25–R27) excludes several popular options:\n\n- GSAP (proprietary terms that forbid visual animation builders);\n- the tldraw SDK (licence key);\n- Theatre.js Studio (AGPL);\n- Remix Icon (custom licence since 2026);\n- SF Symbols (restricted).\n\nELK and Graphviz (EPL) are allowed only as optional plugins. Every asset needs\na record with its SPDX licence, which the licensing issue (F02) implements with\nREUSE 3.3.\n\n## Defects found in the repository\n\nThe repository was created from a template, and several things on `main` are\nbroken or still describe the template. Issue #1 is a planning issue, so these\nare not fixed in this pull request. Each one is a **Bug** issue in phase 0 of\nthe roadmap, scheduled before every feature.\n\n| Key | Defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Evidence                                                                                                                                         | Who can fix it                                         |\n| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |\n| B01 | The repository still calls itself the template: the package is `@link-foundation/example-package-name` with a template description, `bin` and keywords; README and CONTRIBUTING have template titles; `src/index.js` exports demo `add`, `multiply` and `delay` functions; 7 template changesets are pending.                                                                                               | `package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`, `.changeset/`                                                                                       | Pull request                                           |\n| B02 | 19 template case-study folders (`docs/case-studies/issue-3` … `issue-212`) and 6 template analyses (`docs/ISSUE-*.md`) describe template issues, but their numbers will collide with this repository's issues. Defects became bug issues.                                                                                               |\n| LiNo is the only source of truth; other formats are import or export only.                                       | R6, R8. Every domain still maps losslessly to its closest standard (DTCG, WAAPI/Lottie, Vega-Lite, Mermaid, A2UI).                                            |\n| Runtime interpreter with thin renderers, not code generation first.                                              | Runtime editing (R9, R11) needs the links network at run time. Code generation is kept for wrappers and optional exports (F52).                                 |\n| Web Components are the reference renderer; React and Vue are adapters.                                           | One implementation serves plain JS, React and Vue (R18–R20).                                                                                                    |\n| JavaScript first; Swift and Kotlin follow the shared fixtures.                                                   | `docs/javascript-first.md`. The native ports need parsers first (F21, F23).                                                                                     |\n| Issue sources are files in `roadmap/issues/`, and a script creates the issues.                                   | The plan is reviewable in the pull request. Knowledge-only links are written as references in the body.                                                               |\n| Repositories outside `link-foundation/ui` are migrated through issues opened in those repositories (F65).        | Their code changes belong to their own pull requests.                                                                                                           |\n\n## Open questions and uncertainty\n\n- **Package names.** They are working names. The monorepo issue (F01) decides\n  the final ones.\n- **The tree projection rules.** They are only sketched here (finding 1). F03\n  turns them into a specification. If `links-notation` changes how it parses\n  multi-line forms, the fixtures will show it.\n- **Some library facts change quickly.** These include the A2UI version,\n  Compose Multiplatform for Web stability and the licence of the Skip engine.\n  [`research/existing-solutions.md`](research/existing-solutions.md#d-open-questions-to-verify-before-writing-issues)\n  lists them, and the issues that depend on them ask the implementer to\n  re-check.\n- **The inventory is incomplete in places.** GitHub code search was\n  rate-limited during the inventory, so some pattern counts are lower bounds.\n  The `deep-assistant` organisation was not in scope and was not scanned.\n"

Links Notation can carry the whole UI dialect, with three caveats\n\nAll seven samples in [`samples/`](samples/) parse with `links-notation` 0.27.1\nand format back to an equal links network. The experiments found three\nthings the framework has to design around:\n\n1. **One element, several link shapes.** The same element gives different\n   link structures depending on how it is written\n   ([`data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt`](data/lino-parse-shapes-output.txt)):\n\n   ```text\n   single line       -> (ok: button (label OK) (on press (navigate home)))\n   multi-line parens -> ((ok: button) ((ok: button) (label OK)) ((ok: button) (on press (navigate home))))\n   indented parse()  -> (ok: button), ((ok: button) (label OK)), ...\n   parseGroups()     -> a tree: (ok: button) with children (label OK), (on press) -> (navigate home)\n   ```\n\n   So `ui-core` needs one **tree projection** that maps all forms to the same\n   element tree. The dialect specification (roadmap issue F03) fixes it with\n   conformance fixtures that every implementation must pass.\n\n2. **Round trip loses source details.** `Link.format()` does not keep\n   comments, layout or the original quoting. The designer must edit files\n   without destroying them, so source-preserving edits are a separate issue\n   (F14).\n\n3. **Syntax traps.** `#` after whitespace starts a comment, so colours like\n   `'#6750A4'` must be quoted, and `:` cannot appear in bare values (URLs and\n   times must be quoted). The specification and the error messages of\n   `ui-core` must say so.\n\n### 2. Swift and Kotlin need parsers first\n\nThere is no Swift port of `links-notation`, and the Java port is not published\n([links-notation#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/192)).\nThe roadmap therefore has a parser issue before each native renderer (F21 and\nF23). Both are driven by the shared fixtures.\n\n### 3. The same UI pieces are rebuilt again and again\n\nThe inventory found the same patterns in many repositories:\n\n- theme toggles in about 16 repositories;\n- settings panels in 7;\n- four different i18n implementations;\n- links or graph views in 10 (d3-force, Cytoscape, canvas/SVG, doublets-web);\n- chat UIs in 9.\n\nEach of these is a framework package in the roadmap. That is what makes\n\"project code gets simpler for humans and agents\" (R23) measurable: a migrated\nrepository deletes its local copy.\n\n### 4. The architecture follows from the requirements\n\nThe requirements are: runtime editing on any site (R9, R11), \"every other\nframework is just LiNo\" (R6), and five platforms (R18–R22). Together they rule\nout a code-generation-first design (the lesson of Airbnb Lona and Mitosis).\nThe proposal in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) is:\n\n- a LiNo **runtime interpreter** with stable link IDs, and thin renderers per\n  platform;\n- **Web Components** as the reference renderer;\n- **configuration layers** (defaults < theme < site < user < session), so dev\n  mode edits only the top layers, and \"make these the defaults\" (R12) is a\n  diff exported as a LiNo patch for an agent;\n- **themes** as LiNo packages of tokens, style rules and control templates.\n  This is the XAML idea, and it covers both \"classic UIs as themes\" (R14) and\n  Material, Fluent and Apple alignment (R15).\n\n### 5. Licensing narrows the library choice\n\nThe public-domain goal (R25–R27) excludes several popular options:\n\n- GSAP (proprietary terms that forbid visual animation builders);\n- the tldraw SDK (licence key);\n- Theatre.js Studio (AGPL);\n- Remix Icon (custom licence since 2026);\n- SF Symbols (restricted).\n\nELK and Graphviz (EPL) are allowed only as optional plugins. Every asset needs\na record with its SPDX licence, which the licensing issue (F02) implements with\nREUSE 3.3.\n\n## Defects found in the repository\n\nThe repository was created from a template, and several things on `main` are\nbroken or still describe the template. The usual pattern is\n     stop 80 for light and stop 100 for dark, but verify it.\n4. High contrast.\n   - The `mode high-contrast` values come from Fluent's high-contrast theme.\n   - In forced-colours mode, map surfaces to `Canvas`, text to `CanvasText`,\n     the brand colour to `Highlight` and borders to `CanvasText`.\n   - Every focusable control keeps a visible 2px focus outline.\n5. Write `themes/fluent2/styles.lino` and `templates.lino` for the in-scope\n   controls. Use Fluent's `(state hover)`, `(state pressed)` and\n   `(state disabled)` alias tokens, not opacity layers. Fluent shows state\n   with colour changes, while {{F40}} uses state layers.\n6. Write `themes/fluent2/fluent-mapping.lino` in the same row format as\n   {{F40}}:\n   ```lino\n   (map Button (kind button)\n     (prop appearance primary (variant filled))\n     (prop appearance outline (variant outlined))\n     (prop appearance subtle (variant text))\n     (status mapped))\n   ```\n   - Cover at least these components: Button, ToggleButton, Input, Textarea,\n     Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider, Dropdown, Combobox, Dialog, Menu,\n     Tooltip, Toast, Drawer, TabList, Card, Avatar, Badge and Spinner.\n   - Reuse the mapping loader and Markdown generator from {{F40}}. If {{F40}}\n     has not merged yet, move them to `src/mapping.js` in this issue.\n7. In `examples/themes/fluent2.html`, build a gallery in light, dark and\n   high contrast. Add Playwright screenshots (including a run with\n   `forcedColors: 'active'`), tests, `docs/themes/fluent2.md` and a\n   changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/fluent2/{theme,colors,shape,spacing,type,shadow,motion,styles,templates,fluent-mapping}.lino`\n- `packages/ui-themes/src/fluent2/brand.js`, exported from `src/index.js`\n- `packages/ui-themes/src/mapping.js`, the shared mapping loader (if it is not\n  already there)\n- `packages/ui-themes/scripts/generate-fluent2.mjs`\n- `packages/ui-themes/tests/{fluent2-theme,fluent2-brand,fluent2-mapping}.test.js`\n- `docs/themes/fluent2.md`, `examples/themes/fluent2.html`\n- `tests/e2e/theme-fluent2.spec.js`, `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `fluent2-theme.test.js`: the package loads with no error diagnostics,\n      and every `pair` passes 4.5:1 (text) or 3:1 (non-text UI, marked\n      `(pair ... (min 3))`) in light, dark and high contrast.\n- [ ] Every generated token keeps its original Fluent name, so a test can\n      rebuild a `{ colorNeutralBackground1: ... }` object identical to the\n      generator input for the light theme.\n- [ ] `generate-fluent2.mjs` is deterministic: two runs produce identical files.\n- [ ] `fluent2-brand.test.js`: the default brand ramp reproduces the light\n      and dark brand aliases of the generator output, and a seed colour\n      produces 16 stops with monotonic lightness.\n- [ ] `fluent2-mapping.test.js`: every listed component has a row, every\n      mapped kind exists, and `docs/themes/fluent2.md` is up to date.\n- [ ] `npm ls --omit=dev` for `@link-foundation/ui-themes` lists no\n      `@fluentui/*` package, and no font files are added.\n- [ ] Playwright screenshots in light, dark, high contrast and\n      `forcedColors: 'active'` are attached to the pull request. Focus\n      outlines are visible in all four, and axe reports no violations.\n- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication` and\n      `npm test` pass.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnode packages/ui-themes/scripts/generate-fluent2.mjs && git diff --exit-code packages/ui-themes/themes/fluent2\nnode --test packages/ui-themes/tests/fluent2-*.test.js\nnpx playwright test tests/e2e/theme-fluent2.spec.js\nnpm test\n```\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- Fluent 2 design: [REDACTED]\n- Fluent UI repositories (MIT): https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui. Each step is one pull request\nand leaves the app deployable.\n\n1. Copy the {{F57}} checklist template into the tracking pull request.\n2. **Freeze the contracts.** Add tests for:\n   - `data-theme-mode`, `data-theme`, `data-skin` on `<html>`;\n   - the token names `--bg --bg-elev --text --accent --control-h --radius\n     --chat-bg --bubble-in --bubble-out --bubble-radius`;\n   - `--bubble-radius` of 15px (telegram), 7.5px (whatsapp) and 18px\n     (signal);\n   - localStorage `metaSovereignTheme` and `metaSovereignSkin`.\n3. **Baseline screenshots.** Use the existing Playwright Chromium and WebKit\n   suites, axe-core `stepAxeAudit`, and the pixel and contrast checks in\n   `docs/DELIVERY-AUDIT.md`. Cover four skins × light/dark × three widths\n   (≤640, 641–1023, ≥1024).\n4. **Tokens, with zero visual change.** Write `themes/{t3,telegram,whatsapp,signal}.lino`\n   with unchanged token names, for example\n   `(telegram: theme (extends t3) (token bubble-radius 15px))`. Generate the\n   `:root[data-skin=...][data-theme=...]` CSS from them. Delete the old skin\n   blocks, including the out-of-place override near `app.css` line 13,589.\n5. **Settings as LiNo.** Store one settings link (theme, skin, scale,\n   effects, locale) in the existing lino store. Keep localStorage as a cache,\n   and read the old keys once.\n6. **Leaf modules.** Replace `message-text.js`, `chat-model.js` and\n   `panel-resize.js`, the virtual list and `menuPlace` with the framework\n   versions. Use thin re-exports, so imports elsewhere do not change in the\n   same pull request.\n7. **Bubble and composer.** Put them behind the provider-neutral contract.\n   Telegram specifics move into an adapter in meta-sovereign. The composer\n   must keep the reserved-space contract (`--composer-space`) and the\n   WebKit-safe `ResizeObserver` deferral.\n8. **i18n.** Convert `locales/*` to lino-i18n catalogs with its CLI. Keep the\n   `t()` signature.\n9. **Screens.** Declare the shell and chat layout in LiNo, for example\n   `(chat: split (list chat-list) (stream message-stream) (behavior chat-window))`,\n   rendered by `@link-foundation/ui-react`.\n10. **Constraints check, after every step:**\n    - no JSX required and no `eval` (CSP);\n    - axe passes;\n    - Chromium and WebKit e2e pass;\n    - reduced-motion, transparency and effects switches still work;\n    - rem scaling at 100–200 %;\n    - offline-first behaviour.\n11. **Delete** the replaced modules and CSS. Record the line counts of\n    `app.css` and of `chat-*.js` before and after.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\nAll paths are in link-foundation/meta-sovereign:\n\n- Add: `js/src/web/themes/*.lino`, `js/src/web/locales/*.lino`,\n  `js/src/web/chat/telegram-adapter.js`,\n  `tests/e2e/framework-migration.spec.js`.\n- Change: `js/src/web/app.css`, `appearance.js`, `chat-view.js`,\n  `chat-message.js`, `chat-state.js`, `i18n.js`, `package.json`, the esbuild\n  config.\n- Delete after the switch: the replaced parts of `chat-window.js`,\n  `chat-follow.js`, `chat-days.js`, `chat-list-window.js`,\n  `panel-resize.js`, `message-text.js`, `rich-text-nodes.js` and the skin\n  blocks in `app.css`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The contract tests from step 2 pass before and after every step.\n- [ ] Screenshot diffs (four skins × two modes × three widths) are below 0.1 %,\n      or each difference is explained in the pull request.\n- [ ] axe-core reports no new violations; the Chromium and WebKit e2e pass.\n- [ ] `app.css` is at least 30 % shorter (`wc -l`), and the skin rules live\n      only in `themes/*.lino`.\n- [ ] No module under `js/src/web/` duplicates a {{F30}} module (checked with\n      `npm run check:duplication` or the target repository's equivalent).\n- [ ] No Telegram-specific import remains in the framework-facing components\n      (grep).\n- [ ] Old localStorage values are migrated on first load (e2e).\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm ci && npm test\nnpx playwright test --project=chromium --project=webkit\nwc -l js/src/web/app.css js/src/web/chat-*.js | tail -1\ngrep -rn \"data-skin=\" js/src/web/app.css | wc -l\n```\n\nCompare the screenshots with the baseline, and run `stepAxeAudit` on the chat\nscreen in each skin.\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- meta-sovereign `docs/CHAT-REFERENCES.md`: behaviour is \"learned, never\n  copied\" from GPL and AGPL clients. The store from {{F08}} is in-memory only. The links platform\nstores data as **doublets**: every link is a triple `(index, source, target)`\nof unsigned integers. [`doublets-web`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)\n(Unlicense, npm 0.1.3 at planning time) exposes the Rust doublets engine to\nthe browser through WebAssembly:\n\n```js\nimport { Link, LinksConstants, UnitedLinks } from 'doublets-web';\nconst links = new UnitedLinks(new LinksConstants());\nconst link = links.create();\nlinks.update(link, link, link); // a \"point\": source = target = itself\n```\n\nIts README shows an in-memory API only (no IndexedDB layer). Prior art:\n\n- formal-ai persists an append-only LiNo event log in IndexedDB (database\n  `formal-ai-demo`, store `events`), exports `formal-ai-memory.lino`, puts\n  import/reset/purge behind confirmations and reports doublets-web only if the\n  global is present\n  ([formal-ai.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md)).\n- meta-sovereign-chat mirrors its LiNo records into a doublets store\n  (`js/src/storage/doublets-store.js`, `dual-store.js`,\n  [meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`@link-foundation/ui-store` gains `openPersistentStore()` that saves a store to\nIndexedDB as a doublets table (`index`, `source`, `target`) plus names and an\noperation log, restores it after reload, and can copy the same table into a\n`doublets-web` `UnitedLinks` instance.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Encoding a `UiDocument` into doublets and back (`src/doublets/encode.js`).\n- IndexedDB schema, write-through on every committed transaction, load,\n  compaction, export/import of a `.lino` bundle, `destroy()`.\n- Optional adapter to `doublets-web` (`src/doublets/web-adapter.js`) loaded by\n  dynamic `import()` only when requested.\n- Multi-tab notification through `BroadcastChannel`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Server sync, conflict resolution between tabs (last writer wins, documented).\n- Making `doublets-web` itself persist (that belongs upstream).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F08}} (blocker): `createStore`, `subscribe`, `log()`, `logToLino`,\n  `logFromLino`, `toLino`. [2026-11-01T11:54:10.090Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F50\ntitle: 'Development mode for pages not built with the framework'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 7\nblocked_by: [F46, F17]\nrequirements: [R9, R23]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nIssue #1 asks to \"modify the UI/UX on the fly on any of our websites\" (R9) and\nto make migration of existing projects easy (R23). Dev mode ({{F46}}) works on\npages rendered by `ui-dom`, where every element already has a `data-link-id`.\nMost of our sites are not built with the framework yet. This issue brings dev\nmode to them: import the live DOM into the UI dialect with the HTML/DOM\nimporter from {{F17}}, show it in the same inspector, apply edits to the\nforeign page, and export the edits as LiNo so they can drive a migration.\n\nTwo delivery channels:\n\n- **Bookmarklet**: a `javascript:` URL that injects a loader script. Zero\n  install, but a page's Content Security Policy (CSP) can block the injected\n  script.\n- **Browser extension** (Manifest V3): injects the same bundle with the\n  `scripting` API on user action. Code injected by an extension is not\n  subject to the page's CSP for script loading, so it works on more sites.\n\nThe deepcase application shell already shipped a Chrome extension target\n([deepcase research, section 1](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)).\nclick-to-component, LocatorJS and Onlook are prior art for \"select an element\non a running site\"\n([existing-solutions.md section 3](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA user on any web page clicks the bookmarklet or the extension button, the dev\nmode inspector opens over the page, shows the page as a LiNo element tree,\nlets the user change text, attributes and inline styles, and exports the\nchanges as an `overrides` document plus the imported LiNo of the selected\nsubtree.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- A foreign-page adapter in `@link-foundation/ui-devmode`\n  (`src/foreign/`): uses `importDom(root, options)` from {{F17}} to build the\n  element tree and its `nodeMap` (link ID to DOM node), and implements the same\n  adapter interface that {{F46}} uses for `ui-dom` pages: `tree()`,\n  `nodeFor(id)`, `idFor(node)`, `applyProperty(id, name, value)`,\n  `observe(callback)`.\n- Deterministic IDs from {{F17}} (`id` attribute, else structural path). The\n  adapter never adds attributes to the page; it keeps mappings in a `WeakMap`.\n- Editable properties: text content of leaf elements, attributes (except\n  `on*`, `src`/`href` with `javascript:`), inline style declarations.\n  Applying writes to the DOM and records an override in the `session` layer.\n- Re-import on DOM changes (`MutationObserver`, debounced 200 ms), keeping the\n  selection when the ID is stable.\n- Persistence per origin: overrides saved under a key such as\n  `link-ui-devmode:<origin>:<pathname>` in `localStorage` (bookmarklet) or\n  `chrome.storage.local` (extension); re-applied when dev mode is opened again.\n- Export: the `overrides` document (with {{F47}} if merged) and \"Copy subtree as\n  LiNo\" (the {{F17}} output for the selected element), useful for migrations\n  ({{F57}}).\n- Bookmarklet: `packages/ui-devmode/dist/bookmarklet.txt` built from a tiny\n  loader that injects `<script type=\"module\" src=\"{bundleUrl}\">`; the bundle\n  URL is configurable at build time (default: the documentation site from\n  {{F54}} when it exists).\n- Extension: `packages/ui-devmode-extension/` (private workspace, not\n  published to npm) with `manifest.json` (Manifest V3, permissions\n  `activeTab` and `scripting`, `storage`), a toolbar action that calls\n  `chrome.scripting.executeScript` with the bundled dev mode file, and a\n  packaging script that writes a zip.\n- The inspector is mounted in a shadow root inside a fixed host element so\n  the page's CSS does not change it and it does not change the page.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Publishing to the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons (needs accounts; a\n  follow-up).\n- Writing changes back to the foreign site's source code (Onlook-style).\n- Pages inside cross-origin iframes; closed shadow roots are skipped and shown\n  as a single opaque node.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F46}} (blocker): inspector, overlay, property grid, policy and the adapter\n  interface (if {{F46}} did not define an explicit adapter interface, extract\n  it in this issue without changing behaviour for `ui-dom` pages).\n- {{F17}} (blocker): `importDom(root, options)` returning\n  `{ text, tree, nodeMap, diagnostics }`, deterministic IDs and the security\n  rules (scripts and `on*` attributes dropped).\n- Related: {{F47}} (export and share), {{F54}} (hosting of the bookmarklet\n  bundle), {{F57}} (migration playbook uses the subtree export), {{F05}}\n  (Playwright).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. `src/foreign/adapter.js`:\n   `createForeignAdapter({ root = document.body, importDom, ignore })`\n   returns the adapter. `ignore` excludes the dev mode host element.\n2. `src/foreign/apply.js` (pure helpers plus DOM writes):\n   `applyProperty(node, name, value)` for `text`, `attr <name>`,\n   `style <property>`; refuses `on*` attributes and `javascript:` URLs.\n3. `src/foreign/persist.js`: `loadOverrides(storage, location)`,\n   `saveOverrides(storage, location, overrides)`, with `storage` either a\n   `localStorage` wrapper or a `chrome.storage.local` wrapper (both async).\n4. `src/foreign/entry.js`: the injected entry. If dev mode is already mounted\n   it toggles it; otherwise it creates the host element, imports the DOM,\n   mounts the inspector with the foreign adapter and re-applies saved\n   overrides.\n5. `scripts/build-bookmarklet.mjs`: bundles `entry.js` (Vite library mode,\n   ES module) and writes `dist/bookmarklet.txt` containing\n   `javascript:(()=>{...})()` that loads the bundle. Document the CSP\n   limitation in the README.\n6. `packages/ui-devmode-extension/`: `manifest.json`, `background.js`\n   (action click → `executeScript({ target: { tabId }, files: ['devmode.js'] })`),\n   `scripts/package.mjs` that copies the bundle and zips the folder.\n7. Fixture page `packages/ui-devmode/tests/fixtures/foreign.html`: plain HTML\n   with a nav, two cards, a form, an inline `style` and a strict CSP `meta`\n   variant `foreign-csp.html`.\n8. Tests: unit tests for apply and persist; Playwright tests that load the\n   fixture, inject the bundle with `page.addScriptTag`, select a card title,\n   change its text and colour, reload and re-open dev mode.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-devmode/src/foreign/{adapter,apply,persist,entry}.js`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/scripts/build-bookmarklet.mjs`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/tests/foreign-{apply,persist}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/tests/fixtures/{foreign,foreign-csp}.html`\n- `packages/ui-devmode-extension/{package.json,manifest.json,background.js,README.md}`\n- `packages/ui-devmode-extension/scripts/package.mjs`\n- `packages/ui-devmode/README.md` (bookmarklet and extension sections)\n- Browser test in the {{F05}} location; `.changeset/*.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] On `foreign.html` the Outline shows the imported tree with the same IDs\n      as `importDom` from {{F17}} returns for that page.\n- [ ] Changing a card title text and `color` updates the page; reload and\n      re-open restores both from storage.\n- [ ] The page DOM has no attributes added by dev mode (Playwright compares\n      `outerHTML` of `body` without the host element before and after opening).\n- [ ] `applyProperty` refuses `onclick` and `javascript:` values (unit test).\n- [ ] The overrides export of the session parses as LiNo and contains one\n      `set` link per change.\n- [ ] `dist/bookmarklet.txt` is produced by `npm run build` in the package and\n      starts with `javascript:`.\n- [ ] The extension folder loads unpacked in Chromium in a Playwright test\n      (persistent context with `--load-extension`) or, if that is not possible\n      in CI, the manual steps and a screenshot are in the pull request.\n- [ ] The README states that the bookmarklet fails under strict CSP and the\n      extension should be used there (checked with `foreign-csp.html`).\n- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`,\n      `npm test` pass.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnode --test packages/ui-devmode/tests/foreign-*.test.js\nnpm run build --workspace @link-foundation/ui-devmode\nnpm test\nnpm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run check:duplication\n```\n\nThen run the Playwright test from the {{F05}} infrastructure on\n`foreign.html` and attach a screenshot of the inspector over the plain page.\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- click-to-component, LocatorJS (MIT, verify each): select an element on a\n  running page.\n- Onlook (Apache-2.0, verify): visual edits of a running app, writes code.\n- React DevTools and Vue DevTools extensions: content script plus panel.\n- Chrome extension docs: Manifest V3, `chrome.scripting.executeScript`,\n  `activeTab`. Cover the version string `ui-dialect/0`, the RFC 2119 keywords, the list of documents, and how fixtures are named.\n2. Write `docs/spec/elements.md`. An element is a link whose id is the element id and whose first value is its kind. Then define how the remaining values are read:\n   - atoms after the kind are positional values (`(greeting: text 'Hello, links')`);\n   - a sublink with an id (`(body: stack ...)`) is a child element;\n   - a sublink without an id is a **property** when its head is declared for the parent kind in `vocabulary.lino`;\n   - otherwise it is an **anonymous child** when its head is a registered kind;\n   - otherwise it is kept verbatim with the diagnostic `unknown-sublink` (warning).\n\n   Decide, and write down, that the kind is the first value, never an id prefix (`button.save:` is just an id with a dot).\n3. It must say:\n   - Implementations MUST project `parse()` output by **path folding**: a link without an id whose first value is a link structurally equal to an already-seen element head (or to a path made of them) appends its other values to that element or sublink.\n   - `parseGroups()` MAY be used where available; the result MUST be identical.\n   - Give the algorithm in pseudocode, plus the worked example of the four links `(ok: button)`, `((ok: button) (label OK))`, `((ok: button) (on press))` and `(((ok: button) (on press)) (navigate home))`.\n4. Write `docs/spec/values.md`:\n   - **Typing is schema-driven:** the vocabulary declares each property type. Quoting never changes a type, because the parser loses it.\n   - **Types:** `string`, `number` (`-1`, `1.5e3`), `dimension` (`16px`, `1.5rem`, `50%`; units px, rem, em, %, vw, vh), `duration` (`150ms`, `0.2s`), `color`, `enum`, `token-ref`, `element-ref` and `action`.\n   - **Colours** are quoted hex (`'#6750A4'`, `'#6750A4CC'`) or `(oklch 0.6 0.2 300)` / `(rgb 103 80 164)`. A bare `#` is invalid.\n   - **No `:` in bare values.** Use structured links instead: `(state hover)`, `(media (max-width 640px))`, `(aspect 16 9)`. Quote URLs.\n5. Decide the **reference form** in `values.md`. Canonical v0 is the structured form used by the samples: `(token color.primary)`, `(param draft.text)` and an element id as a bare reference. The prefixes `@` and `$` are reserved: a value starting with them gives the diagnostic `reserved-sigil` until a later version defines them as shorthand. Also document:\n   - resolution order: theme chain, then base;\n   - a cycle gives the error `reference-cycle`;\n   - fallbacks use `(or (token a) (token b) 8px)`.\n6. Write `docs/spec/ordering-and-ids.md`:\n   - Children and multi-valued properties (`on`, `token`, `track`, `key`, `event`, `set`) are ordered sequences.\n   - Single-valued properties are a set: a repeated property means the last one wins, with a `duplicate-property` warning.\n   - Element ids are unique per document; a duplicate gives the error `duplicate-id`.\n   - A dot in a token name is a path separator. A dot in an element id has no meaning.\n   - Cross-document references are deferred to `open-questions.md`.\n7. The Iconify per-set metadata\n(`license.spdx`, author, url) is the model for asset records, and REUSE 3.3\n(`REUSE.toml`, `reuse lint`) is the compliance check.\n\nThe asset record format is already sketched in\n[`samples/assets.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/assets.lino):\n\n```lino\n(lucide-check: asset\n  (kind icon)\n  (source 'https://lucide.dev/icons/check')\n  (license ISC)\n  (copyright 'Lucide Contributors')\n  (notice 'https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/blob/main/LICENSE'))\n```\n\n## Goal\n\nThe repository ships its own CC0 icon set under `assets/icons/`, an `icon`\nelement that renders any registered icon with `currentColor`, adapters for\nLucide, Tabler and Material Symbols that create asset records automatically,\nand a build step that refuses any icon without a valid record.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- About 32 own icons needed by {{F26}}–{{F38}} (list in step 2), drawn from\n  scratch on a 24×24 grid with a 2 px stroke, CC0-1.0.\n- `icon-registry.js`: icon sets, lookup, fallbacks.\n- `icon` element: decorative by default (`aria-hidden=\"true\"`), labelled when\n  `label` is set, optional mirroring in right-to-left layouts.\n- Adapters `lucide`, `tabler`, `material-symbols` as optional peer\n  dependencies, each emitting asset records.\n- `scripts/build-icons.mjs`: reads `assets.lino`, checks every record, writes\n  an ES module per set and a sprite.\n- A generated `ATTRIBUTION.md`-style notice list in the package output.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Fonts (OFL, shipped separately) and images other than icons.\n- Native Swift and Kotlin icon loading.\n- The licence policy itself and REUSE CI ({{F02}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **Blocked by {{F02}}**: the asset record fields, the SPDX allow list and the\n  CI check (`reuse lint`). [2026-11-01T11:54:30.732Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F42\ntitle: 'Apple HIG theme'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 5\nblocked_by: [F39, F04]\nrequirements: [R14, R15]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nR15 asks us to follow the Apple guidelines as well as Google's and\nMicrosoft's. Apple handles this differently from the other two: the Human\nInterface Guidelines (HIG) are published as **guidance only**, and Apple's\nfonts and symbols carry restrictive licences. The research files the HIG\nunder LEARN. It says never to bundle SF Pro or SF Symbols, and on Apple\nplatforms to use system fonts and symbols at runtime\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n\nThis issue therefore builds a **HIG-guided** theme with our own values. It\ndoes not copy Apple assets. Its job is to make web and cross-platform UIs\nfeel at home on iOS and macOS, and to give the Swift renderer ({{F21}},\n{{F22}}) a theme whose semantics match SwiftUI's. Material 3 ({{F40}}) and\nFluent 2 ({{F41}}) are the sibling themes.\n\n## Goal\n\nShip `hig`, a theme package with two platform variants, `hig-ios` and\n`hig-macos`, and light, dark and increased-contrast modes. It must:\n\n- follow the HIG section of the {{F04}} digest, covering semantic colours,\n  text styles that scale like Dynamic Type, hit targets, materials and\n  motion;\n- use only the system font stack and no Apple-owned assets;\n- include a mapping table from SwiftUI views to our kinds.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/hig/` with:\n  - semantic colour roles: label, secondary label, background, grouped\n    background, separator, tint, and the system accent colours;\n  - text styles: large title, title 1–3, headline, body, callout,\n    subheadline, footnote and caption 1–2;\n  - corner radii, spacing, minimum hit target, and motion durations and\n    springs.\n- Variants `hig-ios` and `hig-macos`, each declared with `(extends hig)`.\n  They differ in base text size, control height and density, with values\n  taken from the {{F04}} digest.\n- Modes `dark`, `high-contrast` (the analogue of \"Increase Contrast\") and\n  `motion reduced`, which turns movement into cross-fades as the HIG\n  recommends.\n- Text that scales with the user's preferred text size. On the web, text\n  sizes are `rem`-based from the root font size.\n- Translucent materials as an optional style,\n  `(material regular | thin | thick)`. It uses `backdrop-filter` and falls\n  back to an opaque surface under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` and\n  under the user's transparency comfort key from {{F39}}.\n- Style rules and templates for the {{F26}} controls: button (bordered,\n  borderless, prominent), toggle (switch), text field, slider, stepper,\n  segmented control and picker.\n- `swiftui-mapping.lino`, which maps SwiftUI view names and modifiers to our\n  kinds and props.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- SF Pro, SF Mono, New York, SF Symbols, or any Apple font or image file.\n  Nothing is bundled or downloaded, and no URL points to Apple-hosted fonts.\n- Native SwiftUI rendering and native symbol lookup, which belong to {{F21}}\n  and {{F22}}.\n- Copying HIG text or images into the repository. Link to the HIG instead.\n- Any claim of Apple endorsement. The README states that the theme is\n  \"guided by\" the HIG and not affiliated with Apple.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F39}} (blocker). Supplies the theme format, `extends`, the modes, the\n  comfort keys (transparency, motion), contrast pairs and templates.\n- {{F04}} (blocker). Supplies the HIG section of the digest: colour roles,\n  text-style sizes, hit-target size, motion guidance and accessibility\n  settings, each with a source link. To start before {{F04}} merges, read\n  https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines and record\n  the URLs. Choose our own colour values that meet the stated contrast.\n- Related: {{F21}}, {{F22}} (native consumers of the SwiftUI mapping), {{F26}},\n  {{F36}} (icons; this theme uses our own icon set), {{F40}}, {{F41}}, {{F57}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Write `themes/hig/type.lino`. The font stack is:\n   ```lino\n   (hig-type: theme\n     (token font.family.text 'system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif')\n     (token font.family.mono 'ui-monospace, monospace')\n     (token text.body.size 1rem)\n     (token text.headline.weight 600))\n   ```\n   - The stack is a quoted string, because `,` and `-` must stay intact.\n   - Express each text style relative to `body`, so that changing the root\n     size scales all of them, as Dynamic Type does.\n   - Take the ratios from the {{F04}} digest.\n2. Write `themes/hig/colors.lino`.\n   - Name the roles with our semantic names (`color.surface`,\n     `color.on-surface`, `color.on-surface-variant`, `color.separator`,\n     `color.primary` for the tint) and record the HIG role name, for example\n     `(hig label)`.\n   - Pick values that are our own and pass the {{F39}} contrast pairs in\n     light, dark and high contrast.\n   - `system` is the default scheme, because the HIG follows the device\n     appearance.\n3. Write `themes/hig/{shape,spacing,motion,materials}.lino`.\n   - The minimum hit target is a token, `size.target.min` (check the value\n     against the digest), and the {{F26}} templates enforce it with\n     `min-width` and `min-height`.\n   - Motion uses springs, for example\n     `(token motion.spring.default (spring (response 0.35s) (damping 0.85)))`.\n     {{F44}} consumes that format. Until {{F44}} lands, compile springs to a\n     CSS `linear()` easing approximation.\n4. Write `themes/hig-ios/theme.lino` and `themes/hig-macos/theme.lino` with\n   `(extends hig)`. Each overrides only density tokens: [REDACTED] text size,\n   control height and list row height.\n5. Write `styles.lino` and `templates.lino` for the in-scope controls.\n   - The segmented control and stepper templates use {{F26}} parts. If\n     {{F26}} has no segmented control, implement it as a `radio-group`\n     template with `(appearance segmented)`.\n   - Under `(motion reduced)`, the switch thumb fades instead of sliding.\n6. Implement `(material ...)` in `styles.lino`, using `backdrop-filter`\n   with a fallback rule. Add a test that sets the transparency comfort key to\n   `off` and asserts an opaque background.\n7. Write `themes/hig/swiftui-mapping.lino` in the {{F40}} row format, using\n   the shared loader in `src/mapping.js`:\n   ```lino\n   (map Toggle (kind switch) (status mapped))\n   (map VStack (kind stack) (prop axis vertical (direction column)) (status mapped))\n   (map NavigationStack (kind navigation) (status none))\n   ```\n   Cover at least Button, Toggle, TextField, SecureField, Slider, Stepper,\n   Picker, List, Form, Section, VStack, HStack, ZStack, ScrollView,\n   TabView, NavigationStack, Sheet, Alert, Menu, ProgressView, Label and\n   Image.\n8. In `examples/themes/hig.html`, build a gallery showing iOS and macOS\n   variants in light, dark and high contrast. Add Playwright screenshots,\n   `docs/themes/hig.md` (with the non-affiliation note), tests and a\n   changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/hig/{theme,colors,type,shape,spacing,motion,materials,styles,templates,swiftui-mapping}.lino`\n- `packages/ui-themes/themes/hig-ios/theme.lino`, `packages/ui-themes/themes/hig-macos/theme.lino`\n- `packages/ui-themes/tests/{hig-theme,hig-materials,swiftui-mapping}.test.js`\n- `docs/themes/hig.md`, `examples/themes/hig.html`\n- `tests/e2e/theme-hig.spec.js`, `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `hig-theme.test.js`: `hig`, `hig-ios` and `hig-macos` load with no\n      error diagnostics, and every `pair` passes in light, dark and high\n      contrast.\n- [ ] `hig-ios` differs from `hig` only in density tokens, which the test\n      checks against an allow-list.\n- [ ] No file in the repository
