[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+blocked_by: [F39, F04]",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+requirements: [R14, R15]",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+---",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+## Context",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+R15 asks us to follow the Apple guidelines as well as Google's and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+Microsoft's. Apple handles this differently from the other two: the Human",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+Interface Guidelines (HIG) are published as **guidance only**, and Apple's",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+fonts and symbols carry restrictive licences. The research files the HIG",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+under LEARN. It says never to bundle SF Pro or SF Symbols, and on Apple",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+platforms to use system fonts and symbols at runtime",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+This issue therefore builds a **HIG-guided** theme with our own values. It",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+does not copy Apple assets. Its job is to make web and cross-platform UIs",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+feel at home on iOS and macOS, and to give the Swift renderer ({{F21}},",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+{{F22}}) a theme whose semantics match SwiftUI's. Material 3 ({{F40}}) and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+Fluent 2 ({{F41}}) are the sibling themes.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+## Goal",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+Ship `hig`, a theme package with two platform variants, `hig-ios` and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+`hig-macos`, and light, dark and increased-contrast modes. It must:",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- follow the HIG section of the {{F04}} digest, covering semantic colours,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  text styles that scale like Dynamic Type, hit targets, materials and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  motion;",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- use only the system font stack and no Apple-owned assets;",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- include a mapping table from SwiftUI views to our kinds.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+## Scope",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+### In scope",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- `packages/ui-themes/themes/hig/` with:",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  - semantic colour roles: label, secondary label, background, grouped",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+    background, separator, tint, and the system accent colours;",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  - text styles: large title, title 1–3, headline, body, callout,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+    subheadline, footnote and caption 1–2;",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  - corner radii, spacing, minimum hit target, and motion durations and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+    springs.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Variants `hig-ios` and `hig-macos`, each declared with `(extends hig)`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  They differ in base text size, control height and density, with values",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  taken from the {{F04}} digest.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Modes `dark`, `high-contrast` (the analogue of \"Increase Contrast\") and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  `motion reduced`, which turns movement into cross-fades as the HIG",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  recommends.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Text that scales with the user's preferred text size. On the web, text",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  sizes are `rem`-based from the root font size.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Translucent materials as an optional style,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  `(material regular | thin | thick)`. It uses `backdrop-filter` and falls",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  back to an opaque surface under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  under the user's transparency comfort key from {{F39}}.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Style rules and templates for the {{F26}} controls: button (bordered,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  borderless, prominent), toggle (switch), text field, slider, stepper,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  segmented control and picker.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- `swiftui-mapping.lino`, which maps SwiftUI view names and modifiers to our",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  kinds and props.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+### Out of scope",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- SF Pro, SF Mono, New York, SF Symbols, or any Apple font or image file.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  Nothing is bundled or downloaded, and no URL points to Apple-hosted fonts.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Native SwiftUI rendering and native symbol lookup, which belong to {{F21}}",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  and {{F22}}.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Copying HIG text or images into the repository. Link to the HIG instead.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Any claim of Apple endorsement. The README states that the theme is",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  \"guided by\" the HIG and not affiliated with Apple.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+## Dependencies",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- {{F39}} (blocker). Supplies the theme format, `extends`, the modes, the",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  comfort keys (transparency, motion), contrast pairs and templates.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- {{F04}} (blocker). Supplies the HIG section of the digest: colour roles,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  text-style sizes, hit-target size, motion guidance and accessibility",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  settings, each with a source link. To start before {{F04}} merges, read",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines and record",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  the URLs. Choose our own colour values that meet the stated contrast.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+- Related: {{F21}}, {{F22}} (native consumers of the SwiftUI mapping), {{F26}},",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+  {{F36}} (icons; this theme uses our own icon set), {{F40}}, {{F41}}, {{F57}}.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+## Step-by-step plan",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+1. Write `themes/hig/type.lino`. The font stack is:",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   ```lino",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   (hig-type: theme",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     (token font.family.text 'system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif')",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     (token font.family.mono 'ui-monospace, monospace')",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     (token text.body.size 1rem)",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     (token text.headline.weight 600))",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   ```",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - The stack is a quoted string, because `,` and `-` must stay intact.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Express each text style relative to `body`, so that changing the root",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     size scales all of them, as Dynamic Type does.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Take the ratios from the {{F04}} digest.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+2. Write `themes/hig/colors.lino`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Name the roles with our semantic names (`color.surface`,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     `color.on-surface`, `color.on-surface-variant`, `color.separator`,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     `color.primary` for the tint) and record the HIG role name, for example",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     `(hig label)`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Pick values that are our own and pass the {{F39}} contrast pairs in",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     light, dark and high contrast.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - `system` is the default scheme, because the HIG follows the device",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     appearance.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+3. Write `themes/hig/{shape,spacing,motion,materials}.lino`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - The minimum hit target is a token, `size.target.min` (check the value",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     against the digest), and the {{F26}} templates enforce it with",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     `min-width` and `min-height`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Motion uses springs, for example",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     `(token motion.spring.default (spring (response 0.35s) (damping 0.85)))`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     {{F44}} consumes that format. Until {{F44}} lands, compile springs to a",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     CSS `linear()` easing approximation.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+4. Write `themes/hig-ios/theme.lino` and `themes/hig-macos/theme.lino` with",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   `(extends hig)`. Each overrides only density tokens: [REDACTED] text size,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   control height and list row height.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+5. Write `styles.lino` and `templates.lino` for the in-scope controls.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - The segmented control and stepper templates use {{F26}} parts. If",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     {{F26}} has no segmented control, implement it as a `radio-group`",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+     template with `(appearance segmented)`.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   - Under `(motion reduced)`, the switch thumb fades instead of sliding.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+6. Implement `(material ...)` in `styles.lino`, using `backdrop-filter`",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   with a fallback rule. Add a test that sets the transparency comfort key to",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   `off` and asserts an opaque background.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+7. Write `themes/hig/swiftui-mapping.lino` in the {{F40}} row format, using",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   the shared loader in `src/mapping.js`:",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   ```lino",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   (map Toggle (kind switch) (status mapped))",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   (map VStack (kind stack) (prop axis vertical (direction column)) (status mapped))",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   (map NavigationStack (kind navigation) (status none))",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   ```",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   Cover at least Button, Toggle, TextField, SecureField, Slider, Stepper,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   Picker, List, Form, Section, VStack, HStack, ZStack, ScrollView,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   TabView, NavigationStack, Sheet, Alert, Menu, ProgressView, Label and",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   Image.",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+8. In `examples/themes/hig.html`, build a gallery showing iOS and macOS",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   variants in light, dark and high contrast. Add Playwright screenshots,",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   `docs/themes/hig.md` (with the non-affiliation note), tests and a",
[2026-11-01T11:54:35.471Z] [INFO]                 "+   changeset.",

[2026-11-01T11:54:49.440Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F02\ntitle: 'Licensing and third-party asset records (REUSE, SPDX, CI)'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 1\nblocked_by: []\nrequirements: [R25, R26, R27]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nThe code is public domain (Unlicense, R25), and our own assets must be public domain too (R26, CC0-1.0 in practice). Third-party icons and assets are allowed, but each one must link to its source and state copyright, licence and attribution (R27). Principle 7 of [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) asks for a machine-readable record per third-party asset. The layer table places assets in `assets/` plus `assets.lino`.\n\nKnown problem sources found by the research:\n\n- **Remix Icon** moved to a custom \"Remix Icon License v1.0\" in January 2026; Fedora flagged it as not free, and older versions are Apache-2.0. **SF Symbols, SF Pro and Segoe** have restricted terms and must never be bundled. See sections 6–7 of [existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md).\n- **anime-avatar** problems ([immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md), sections 4.2 and 7):\n  - `ACS_GF2_MMD_MODEL_ARCHIVES` hot-links about 70 proprietary SUNBORN Girls' Frontline 2 archives;\n  - the DamagedHelmet model is CC-BY-NC;\n  - some licence strings are not identifiers: \"See repository\" and \"CC-ish\";\n  - prior art: `attributionRequired()` and `AttributionOverlay` (https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19).\n- **konard.github.io** has no LICENSE file (GitHub reports `license: null`), so nothing may be copied from it until it is relicensed ([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)).\n- **meta-sovereign-chat** draws its icons in `icons.js` from Lucide shapes, which are ISC: permissive, but not public domain ([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md), \"Licensing\").\n\nThe record format is sketched in [`samples/assets.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/assets.lino):\n\n```lino\n(lucide-check: asset\n  (kind icon)\n  (source 'https://lucide.dev/icons/check')\n  (license ISC)\n  (copyright 'Lucide Contributors')\n  (notice 'https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/blob/main/LICENSE'))\n```\n\n## Goal\n\nMake the repository REUSE 3.3 compliant, define the `assets.lino` record format, and add a CI check. The check fails when any file under `assets/` lacks a record, or when a record has a missing or disallowed licence. It also renders attribution text from the records.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `REUSE.toml`, plus `LICENSES/` with the texts of every licence in use (Unlicense, CC0-1.0, and each third-party licence).\n- `assets/README.md`, `assets/assets.lino` and `assets/links-ui-logo.svg` (our own CC0 placeholder).\n- `docs/licensing.md`: the policy, the allow and deny lists, the record format, and the known problem sources above.\n- `scripts/check-assets.mjs`: a record per file, licence policy, and `REUSE.toml` kept in sync.\n- `scripts/render-attributions.mjs`: generates `assets/ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, and exports a function for later UI use.\n- A CI job (a new `.github/workflows/licensing.yml`) that runs both scripts and `reuse lint`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The icon registry and the asset pipeline ({{F36}}), which consume this format.\n- The in-app attribution component (part of {{F36}}, or the components issues).\n- Relicensing konard.github.io, which the owner must do upstream.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nNo blockers. Parse records with `links-notation` (add it as a root devDependency; check the current version). This issue does not need `ui-core`.\n\nRelated:\n\n- {{F36}} turns these records into an icon and asset pipeline.\n- {{F03}} adds `asset` to the dialect vocabulary.\n- {{B06}} fixes the security workflow, whose dependency review complements this check.\n- {{F56}} links `docs/licensing.md` from the contributor guide.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Write `docs/licensing.md`:\n   - **Allowed by default:** `Unlicense`, `CC0-1.0`, `MIT`, `ISC`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `Apache-2.0`.\n   - **Allowed only as an explicit opt-in**, with an `(opt-in true)` field and attribution: `CC-BY-4.0`, `CC-BY-3.0`, `CC-BY-SA-4.0`.\n   - **Denied:**\n     - any `*-NC-*` or `*-ND-*` licence;\n     - `LicenseRef-*`, unless listed in `docs/licensing.md`;\n     - Remix Icon v1.0 or later;\n     - SF Symbols, SF Pro and Segoe;\n     - unlicensed sources.\n   - Add the table of known problem sources from the Context, with the decision for each.\n2. Define the record format in `docs/licensing.md`. One link per asset or asset group: `(<id>: asset (field value)...)`.\n   - Required fields: `kind` (icon, image, font, sound, model, animation, data), `files` (one or more repository paths or globs under `assets/`, quoted), `license` (an SPDX expression; quote it if it contains spaces) and `copyright` (quoted text, or `none` for our own CC0 assets).\n   - Required for third-party assets: `source` (a quoted URL) and `notice` (a quoted URL of the licence text).\n   - Optional fields: `attribution` (`required` or `none`), `attribution-text` (quoted), `commercial-use` (`yes` or `no`), `modified` (`yes` or `no`) and `opt-in` (`true`).\n3. Create `assets/assets.lino` with a record for `assets/links-ui-logo.svg`: `(license CC0-1.0)`, `(copyright none)`, `(files 'assets/links-ui-logo.svg')`.\n4. Implement `scripts/lib/asset-records.mjs` with these functions:\n   - `/** @param {string} text @returns {AssetRecord[]} */ parseAssetRecords(text)`. It returns `{id, kind, files, license, copyright, source?, notice?, attribution, attributionText?, commercialUse?, modified?, optIn}`.\n   - `/** @returns {{errors: string[]}} */ validateAssetRecords(records, files, policy)`.\n5. Implement `scripts/check-assets.mjs`. It must:\n   - list the files under `assets/`, except `assets.lino`, `README.md` and `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`;\n   - fail if a file matches no record, or more than one record;\n   - fail if a record matches no file, or a field is missing;\n   - fail if a licence is denied, or opt-in without `(opt-in true)`;\n   - fail if a third-party record has no `source`;\n   - fail if `REUSE.toml` is not what `--write` would generate.\n6. In the same script, generate `REUSE.toml` from the records with `--write`:\n   - one `[[annotations]]` block per record, with `path`, `precedence = \"aggregate\"`, `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` and `SPDX-License-Identifier`;\n   - one block that marks the rest of the repository as `Unlicense`, with the copyright \"Link Foundation contributors\" (check the wording with the maintainer).\n7. Implement `scripts/render-attributions.mjs`, exporting `/** @returns {string} */ renderAttributions(records, {format: 'markdown' | 'html' | 'lino'})`. Write `assets/ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, grouped by licence: name, source link, copyright, licence link, attribution text. Records with `(copyright none)` and CC0 are listed as \"public domain\".\n8. Add `LICENSES/Unlicense.txt` and `LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt` (texts from https://spdx.org/licenses/). `reuse download --all` creates the missing ones.\n9. Add `.github/workflows/licensing.yml`, triggered on pull requests and on pushes to main. It runs:\n   - `node scripts/check-assets.mjs`;\n   - `node scripts/render-attributions.mjs --check`;\n   - `pipx run reuse lint` (the `reuse` tool is GPL-3.0; it is used in CI only and never shipped or imported).\n\n   Pin the action SHAs as the other workflows do.\n10. Add the tests `tests/asset-records.test.js` and `tests/check-assets.test.js`. Use temp-dir fixtures: a file without a record, a `CC-BY-NC-4.0` record, a Remix Icon `LicenseRef`, a missing `source`, a valid Lucide ISC record, and our own CC0 file.\n11. Add npm scripts: `\"check:assets\": \"node scripts/check-assets.mjs\"` and `\"assets:attributions\": \"node scripts/render-attributions.mjs\"`.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `REUSE.toml`, `LICENSES/*.txt`, `docs/licensing.md`\n- `assets/README.md`, `assets/assets.lino`, `assets/links-ui-logo.svg`, `assets/ATTRIBUTIONS.md`\n- `scripts/lib/asset-records.mjs`, `scripts/check-assets.mjs`, `scripts/render-attributions.mjs`\n- `tests/asset-records.test.js`, `tests/check-assets.test.js`\n- `.github/workflows/licensing.yml`, `package.json` (scripts and devDependency)\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `pipx run reuse lint` reports the repository as compliant.\n- [ ] `npm run check:assets` exits 0 on main, and exits 1 (naming the file) when you add `assets/tmp.svg` without a record.\n- [ ] The tests reject `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, a Remix Icon `LicenseRef`, opt-in licences without `(opt-in true)`, and third-party records without `source`. They accept Lucide ISC and own CC0 records.\n- [ ] `assets/ATTRIBUTIONS.md` is generated, and `render-attributions.mjs --check` fails when it is stale.\n- [ ] `docs/licensing.md` lists Remix Icon, SF Symbols/SF Pro/Segoe, the GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, konard.github.io (no licence) and Lucide (ISC) with a decision for each.\n- [ ] The `licensing.yml` workflow is green on the PR. `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` pass.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnpm run check:assets\nnode scripts/render-attributions.mjs --check\npipx run reuse lint\nnode --test tests/asset-records.test.js tests/check-assets.test.js\ntouch assets/tmp.svg && npm run check:assets; echo \"exit=$?\"; rm assets/tmp.svg   # expect exit=1\n```\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- REUSE Specification 3.3 and `REUSE.toml`: https://reuse.software. Most of our UI code is React JSX (konard.github.io,\nformal-ai, immortality, anime-avatar) and some sites use MUI components\n([ui-projects-inventory.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/ui-projects-inventory.md)).\n\n{{F17}} creates `@link-foundation/ui-convert` with an HTML/DOM importer: a\nshared intermediate form `{ tag, attrs, children, text, span }`, a mapping\ntable to dialect kinds, deterministic IDs and security rules. This issue adds\ntwo more front ends that produce the same intermediate form:\n\n- **JSX** (`.jsx`, `.tsx` markup), with a mapping for **MUI** components;\n- **Vue single-file components** (`.vue`), whose `<template>` is HTML-like.\n\n[meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language) (npm\n0.46.0 at research time) is \"a self-describing language over a links network:\ngrammars and translation rules\" with a native HTML import and a CSS import\nwith a lossless CST\n([links-notation-ecosystem.md section 3](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)).\nThe research did **not** confirm a JSX or Vue grammar in meta-language. The\n[transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer) project (Rust)\ndefines LiNo rewrite rules (match / replace with `$vars`); we use the same\nrule shape for the MUI mapping so it is data, not code.\n\n## Goal\n\n`importJsx(text, options)` and `importVue(text, options)` in\n`@link-foundation/ui-convert` turn a component file into a UI dialect LiNo\ndocument plus diagnostics, with MUI components mapped to dialect kinds through\na LiNo rule file. Anything that cannot be mapped is kept, marked and reported,\nnever silently dropped.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- JSX parsing: first check the current meta-language version for a JSX\n  grammar; if it is missing or unusable, use `acorn` with `acorn-jsx` (both\n  MIT) or `@babel/parser` (MIT) for `.tsx`, and open an issue in\n  meta-language asking for a JSX grammar (link it in the pull request).\n- Vue SFC: split blocks; parse `<template>` with the meta-language HTML import\n  (as {{F17}} does); `<script>` and `<style>` are kept as raw links and\n  reported. Directives: `v-if` / `v-else` → `(when ...)`, `v-for` → `(each ...)`,\n  `@click` → `(on press (action <name>))`, `:prop` bindings → `(bind ...)`,\n  static attributes → props. Use the names fixed by {{F03}}; if it has no\n  binding vocabulary, keep `(unsupported vue-directive '...')`.\n- JSX: elements, fragments, string and number props, `className`, `style`\n  objects with literal values, text children. `onClick={save}` becomes\n  `(on press (action save))` when the handler is an identifier; anything else\n  is `(unsupported jsx-expression '<source text>')`.\n- MUI mapping rules in `src/mappings/mui.lino` for at least: `Button`\n  (`variant` contained/outlined/text), `IconButton`, `TextField`,\n  `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Typography` (`variant` h1–h6/body1/body2),\n  `Stack` (`direction`, `spacing` → `gap` token), `Box`, `Card`,\n  `CardContent`, `Dialog`, `Tabs`/`Tab`, `List`/`ListItem`, `AppBar`,\n  `Toolbar`.\n- `sx` props with literal values become `(style ...)`; theme callbacks are\n  unsupported. Importing the MUI theme object is {{F40}}.\n- Diagnostics `{ code, message, span }` for every unsupported construct;\n  output always parses.\n- A CLI entry if {{F17}} added one: `ui-convert import --from jsx|vue <file>`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Executing component code, hooks, state or data fetching.\n- Importing MUI themes ({{F40}}) and the human migration guide ({{F57}}).\n- Exporting back to code: {{F52}}.\n- Angular, Svelte and other frameworks (follow-ups using the same rule files).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F17}} (blocker): package `@link-foundation/ui-convert`, the intermediate\n  form, `mapping.js`, `ids.js`, `style.js`, security rules and the formatter\n  path through `formatLinks`. [2026-11-01T11:55:11.142Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F10\ntitle: 'ui-config: layered configuration and override patches'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 2\nblocked_by: [F08]\nrequirements: [R2, R9, R12]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nEvery UI built with the framework must be configurable through LiNo (R2) and\nchangeable on the fly on our sites (R9). Changes made in dev mode ({{F46}})\nmust be explainable to people and AI agents (R12). The architecture\n([ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md))\nfixes the order of configuration layers:\n\n```\ndefaults < theme < site < user < session\n```\n\nDev mode writes only the `user` and `session` layers. \"Make these the\ndefaults\" ({{F47}}) exports the difference between the top layers and `site`\nas an `overrides` LiNo document. The sample\n[samples/overrides.lino](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/overrides.lino)\nshows the patch format:\n\n```lino\n(user-overrides: overrides\n  (layer user)\n  (base app)\n  (set greeting text 'Hello, agents')\n  (set material3 token color.primary '#00639B'))\n```\n\nOur sites already do this by hand: konard.github.io keeps only the difference\nfrom the defaults in `localStorage` and immortality keeps\n`immortality.ui-settings.v2` diffs\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md),\n[immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-config` (`@link-foundation/ui-config`) resolves every property\nthrough the five layers, tells which layer won, writes user/session overrides,\nand imports/exports layers as `overrides` LiNo patches.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Patch format: `(<name>: overrides (layer L) (base DOC) (set ...) (unset ...))`.\n- `set` semantics: `(set ID NAME VALUES...)`. If `NAME` equals the element's\n  kind, it replaces the positional `args` (`(set greeting text 'Hello, agents')`\n  changes the text). If `NAME` is a keyed prop (`token`, declared in a list\n  `keyedProps`, default `['token', 'state']`), the first value is the key\n  (`token color.primary`). Otherwise it replaces the prop (last wins).\n- `(unset ID NAME [KEY])` removes the override in that layer.\n- `resolve`, `explain`, `set`, `unset`, `clear`, `exportPatch`, `importPatch`,\n  `subscribe`, `bindStore`.\n- Persistence adapters for `user` (localStorage) and `session` (sessionStorage).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Structural overrides (insert/remove/move elements) — later; dev mode records\n  those through {{F08}} and {{F14}}.\n- Settings schemas, presets and share links ({{F15}}); the dev mode UI\n  ({{F46}}); the hand-off flow ({{F47}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F08}} (blocker): store transactions and events. Consumed: `bindStore`\n  applies the resolved values as one transaction with `origin: 'config'`.\n  Before it merges, test `resolve` and patches against plain `UiDocument`\n  objects from {{F06}}.\n- Related: {{F07}} (typed values; `defaults` layer is built from kind schema\n  `default` entries), {{F11}} (theme layer), {{F13}} (locale setting),\n  {{F15}}, {{F46}} (expects `resolve(id, name) -> { value, layer }`), {{F47}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-config/package.json`\n   (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-config\"`), dependencies\n   `@link-foundation/ui-core`, `@link-foundation/ui-store` (workspace).\n2. `src/layers.js`: `export const LAYERS = ['defaults', 'theme', 'site', 'user', 'session'];`\n   Each layer is `Map<string, Override>` keyed by `id + '\\u0000' + name + '\\u0000' + key`.\n3. `src/patch.js`: `readPatch(text) → { name, layer, base, ops, diagnostics }`\n   using `parse` from `ui-core`; `writePatch({ name, layer, base, ops }) → string`\n   using `format`. Unknown op names, missing ids or values become diagnostics.\n   Limits: max 64 KiB of text, max 2,000 ops (configurable).\n4. `src/config.js`:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {{ document: UiDocument, layers?: Partial<Record<Layer, string>>, keyedProps?: string[] }} options */\n   export function createConfig(options) {}\n   // config.resolve(id, name, key?) -> { value: unknown[], layer: Layer } | undefined\n   // config.explain(id, name, key?) -> Array<{ layer: Layer, value: unknown[] }>  (lowest first)\n   // config.set(layer, id, name, values, key?)   only 'user' | 'session', else throws\n   // config.unset(layer, id, name, key?); config.clear(layer)\n   // config.loadLayer(layer, patchText)           any layer (site/theme are loaded, never edited)\n   // config.effective() -> UiDocument             base document with all layers applied\n   // config.exportPatch({ layers: ['user', 'session'], against: 'site', name }) -> string\n   // config.importPatch(text, layer)\n   // config.subscribe(listener) -> unsubscribe    events { layer, id, name, key, before, after }\n   // config.bindStore(store) -> unbind\n   ```\n5. `exportPatch` is diff-only: an override is written only if its value differs\n   from the value resolved from the layers below `against` and including it.\n   Output for the sample after `set('user', 'greeting', 'text', ['Hello, agents'])`\n   must equal the sample (`samples/overrides.lino`) except for the name.\n6. `src/explain.js`: `describeChanges(config, layers)` returns plain English\n   lines for agents (R12), e.g.\n   `greeting: text changed from 'Hello, links' (site) to 'Hello, agents' (user)`.\n7. `src/storage.js`: `persistLayer(config, layer, storage, key)` writes the\n   patch text diff-only on every change and restores it on start; default keys\n   `link-ui.config.user.v1` and `link-ui.config.session.v1`. Invalid stored text\n   is ignored with a diagnostic (never crashes the page).\n8. README with the layer table, patch grammar and examples; changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-config/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`, `src/index.d.ts`\n- `packages/ui-config/src/{layers.js,patch.js,config.js,explain.js,storage.js}`\n- `packages/ui-config/tests/{patch,resolve,export,explain,storage,bind-store}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-config/tests/fixtures/{site.lino,theme.lino,user.lino}`\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `resolve.test.js`: with a value in all five layers, `resolve` returns the\n      `session` value; Teams also need an \"eject to code\"\npath: turn a LiNo document into source files they can commit, read and edit\nin their usual tools.\n\nThe research warns against **heavy code generation as the primary\narchitecture** (lessons from Airbnb Lona and Mitosis) and recommends \"a\nruntime LiNo interpreter plus thin native renderers, and codegen only for\nwrappers and types\"\n([existing-solutions.md, recommendations C](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\nSo exporters are a one-way convenience, never the source of truth. The\n[transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer) project\ndescribes \"dialect lowering (LiNo UI to React / SwiftUI / Compose)\" with LiNo\nrewrite rules\n([links-notation-ecosystem.md section 3](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md));\nthe importer {{F51}} adds a JS rule engine with the same shape that this\nissue can reuse when it is merged.\n\n## Goal\n\n`exportDocument(source, { target, mode, componentName })` in\n`@link-foundation/ui-convert` that produces readable, formatted source files\nfor `react`, `vue`, `swiftui` and `compose`, with golden tests, and a CLI\ncommand to run it.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Two modes for web targets:\n  - `wrapper` (default): a component file that imports `UiView` from\n    `@link-foundation/ui-react` or `@link-foundation/ui-vue`, inlines the LiNo\n    source as a string constant and declares one stub handler per action used\n    in the document (`(on press (navigate home))` → handler `navigate`).\n  - `eject`: plain JSX / Vue `<template>` with semantic HTML elements\n    (`<button>`, `<p>`, flex `<div>`), class names and CSS custom properties\n    for tokens, plus a CSS file. Use the reverse of the {{F17}} HTML mapping\n    table so import and export agree.\n- Native targets (source only):\n  - `swiftui`: a `struct <Name>: View` with `VStack`/`HStack`, `Text`,\n    `Button`, `Toggle`, `TextField`, `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` for\n    `(variant filled)`;\n  - `compose`: a `@Composable fun <Name>()` with `Column`/`Row`,\n    `Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`, `Text`, `Button`, `Switch`, `TextField`.\n  - Token references use the identifiers generated by the Swift and Kotlin\n    outputs of {{F11}}; if F11 is not merged, emit literal values and a\n    `// TODO token space.medium` comment.\n- Unsupported kinds or props produce a comment in the output and a diagnostic\n  `{ code: 'unsupported', id, target }`; the export never fails silently.\n- Deterministic output, formatted (Prettier for JS/Vue; fixed 4-space\n  indentation for Swift and Kotlin).\n- CLI: `ui-convert export --target react|vue|swiftui|compose [--mode wrapper|eject] <file.lino>`\n  writing to `--out <dir>` or stdout.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Round-trip editing (code is not read back automatically; {{F51}} imports\n  JSX/Vue separately).\n- React Native, Flutter and other targets (follow-ups).\n- Building or running the native outputs in CI (optional check only).\n- Runtime renderers ({{F22}} SwiftUI, {{F24}} Compose) — those interpret\n  LiNo; this issue writes source.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F18}} (blocker): the public API of `@link-foundation/ui-react`\n  (`UiView` props `source`, `actions`, `onAction`) used by the React wrapper\n  output; its example app is used to compile-check the output.\n- {{F19}} (blocker): the same for `@link-foundation/ui-vue`.\n- Related: {{F17}} (package, HTML mapping table), {{F51}} (rule engine,\n  round-trip test), {{F11}} (token identifiers for Swift and Kotlin),\n  {{F22}}, {{F24}} (native naming conventions), {{F03}} (kind list).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Wrapper example for\n   `samples/document.lino`:\n\n   ```jsx\n   import { UiView } from '@link-foundation/ui-react';\n\n   const source = `(app: document ...)`; // full LiNo text\n\n   export function App({ actions = {} }) {\n     return <UiView source={source} actions={{ navigate: () => {}, ...actions }} />;\n   }\n   ```\n\n   Escape backticks and `${` in the inlined text.\n4. `vue.js`: wrapper SFC (`<script setup>` + `<UiView :source=\"source\" />`)\n   and eject SFC.\n5. `swiftui.js` and `compose.js`: a kind-to-view table kept as data\n   (`src/export/targets/swiftui.lino`, `compose.lino`) and a small printer.\n   Expected SwiftUI shape for the sample:\n\n   ```swift\n   struct App: View {\n       var body: some View {\n           VStack(spacing: 16) { // TODO token space.medium\n               Text(\"Hello, links\")\n               Button(\"OK\") { actions.navigate(\"home\") }\n                   .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)\n           }\n       }\n   }\n   ```\n\n   Do not claim exact Swift/Kotlin API details beyond the basic views above\n   without checking current Apple and Android documentation.\n6. `cli.js`: add the `export` command next to the importer commands.\n7. [2026-11-01T11:55:52.245Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\nA comprehensive template for AI-driven JavaScript/TypeScript development with full CI/CD pipeline support.\n\nThis repository publishes the real test package\n`@link-foundation/example-package-name` so the template release pipeline is\nvalidated end to end with npm trusted publishing.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Multi-runtime support**: Works with Bun, Node.js, and Deno\n- **Universal testing**: Uses [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) for cross-runtime tests\n- **Automated releases**: Changesets-based versioning with GitHub Actions\n- **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Docker images can be published after the matching npm version is visible\n- **Universal app example**: React UI for the package API with GitHub Pages, Electron, and Capacitor build paths\n- **Code quality**: ESLint + Prettier with pre-commit hooks via Husky\n- **Package manager agnostic**: Works with bun, npm, yarn, pnpm, and deno\n- **Broken link checks**: Automated link validation with [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action) and Web Archive fallback suggestions\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Using This Template\n\n1. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `package.json` with your package name and description\n4. Install dependencies: `bun install`\n5. Start developing!\n\n### Development\n\n```bash\n# Install dependencies\nbun install\n\n# Run tests\nbun test --timeout 30000\n\n# Or with other runtimes:\nnpm test\ndeno test -A --parallel\n\n# Lint code\nbun run lint\n\n# Format code\nbun run format\n\n# Check all (lint + format + file size)\nbun run check\n\n# Build the universal React example app\nnpm install --prefix examples/universal-app\nnpm run example:web:build\nnpm run example:desktop:package\n\n# Try the CLI locally\nnode bin/example-package-name.js add 2 3\n```\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .changeset/           # Changeset configuration\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD\n├── .husky/               # Git hooks (pre-commit)\n├── examples/             # Usage examples\n│   └── universal-app/    # React + GitHub Pages + Electron + Capacitor app\n├── scripts/              # Build and release scripts\n├── src/                  # Source code\n│   ├── index.js          # Main entry point\n│   └── index.d.ts        # TypeScript definitions\n├── tests/                # Test files\n├── .eslintrc.js          # ESLint configuration\n├── .prettierrc           # Prettier configuration\n├── bunfig.toml           # Bun configuration\n├── deno.json             # Deno configuration\n└── package.json          # Node.js package manifest\n```\n\n## Design Choices\n\n### Multi-Runtime Support\n\nThis template is designed to work seamlessly with all major JavaScript runtimes:\n\n- **Bun**: Primary runtime with highest performance, uses native test support (`bun test`)\n- **Node.js**: Alternative runtime, uses built-in test runner (`node --test`)\n- **Deno**: Secure runtime with built-in TypeScript support (`deno test`)\n\nThe [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) framework provides a unified testing API that works identically across all runtimes.\n\n### Package Manager Agnostic\n\nWhile `package.json` is the source of truth for dependencies, the template supports:\n\n- **bun**: Primary choice, uses `bun.lockb`\n- **npm**: Uses `package-lock.json`\n- **yarn**: Uses `yarn.lock`\n- **pnpm**: Uses `pnpm-lock.yaml`\n- **deno**: Uses `deno.json` for configuration\n\nNote: `package-lock.json` is not committed by default to allow any package manager.\n\n### Universal App Example\n\nThe template includes `examples/universal-app`, a Vite React app that imports\n`add` and `multiply` from `src/index.js` and renders a visual calculator UI.\nThe same static build is used by:\n\n- GitHub Pages (`npm run example:web:build`)\n- Electron desktop packaging (`npm run example:desktop:package`)\n- Capacitor Android/iOS sync (`npm run example:mobile:sync`)\n\nThe example app has its own `package.json` and lockfile so template users can\nopt into the frontend stack without adding React, Electron, or Capacitor to the\nlibrary package itself.\n\nSee [examples/universal-app/README.md](examples/universal-app/README.md) for\nlocal web, desktop, Android, and iOS testing instructions.\n\n### Code Quality\n\n- **ESLint**: Configured with recommended rules + Prettier integration\n- **Prettier**: Consistent code formatting\n- **Husky + lint-staged**: Pre-commit hooks ensure code quality\n- **File size limit**: Files must stay under 1500 lines for maintainability (enforced via ESLint and CI)\n\n### Release Workflow\n\nThe release workflow uses [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) for version management:\n\n1. **Creating a changeset**: Run `bun run changeset` to document changes\n2. **PR validation**: CI checks for valid changeset in each PR\n3. **Automated versioning**: Merging to `main` triggers version bump\n4. **npm publishing**: Automated via OIDC trusted publishing (no tokens needed)\n5. **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: When configured, waits for the exact npm version and tags the Docker image with that version\n6. **GitHub releases**: Auto-created with formatted release notes\n\n> **First release of a brand-new package**: OIDC trusted publishing cannot\n> create a package that does not exist yet (the first publish fails with\n> `E404`, because a trusted publisher can only be configured for an existing\n> package). To bootstrap, add a repository secret named `NPM_TOKEN` (a\n> granular/automation token with publish access). The release workflow passes\n> it as `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` automatically. Once the package exists and OIDC\n> trusted publishing is configured on npmjs.com, the token becomes optional and\n> can be removed.\n\n#### Manual Releases\n\nTwo manual release modes are available via GitHub Actions:\n\n- **Instant release**: Immediately bump version and publish\n- **Changeset PR**: Create a PR with changeset for review\n\n### CI/CD Pipeline\n\nThe GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) implements a fast-fail pipeline:\n\n**Fast checks** (~7-30s each, run first for fastest feedback):\n\n1. **Test compilation**: Syntax-checks all `.mjs` files with `node --check`\n2. **Lint, format & secrets scan**: ESLint, Prettier, jscpd, and [secretlint](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint) for credential leak detection\n3. **File line limits**: Enforces the 1500-line limit on JavaScript (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`) and Markdown (`.md`) files plus `release.yml`\n4. **Changeset check**: Validates PR has exactly one changeset (added by that PR)\n5. **Version check**: Blocks manual version changes in `package.json`\n6. **Documentation validation**: Checks required doc files (doc line limits are enforced by the file line limits check)\n\n**Slow checks** (only run after all fast checks pass):\n\n7. **Test matrix**: 3 runtimes × 3 OS = 9 test combinations\n8. **Broken link checks**: Validates all links in Markdown/HTML files (separate workflow)\n\n**Release** (on merge to main):\n\n9. **Changeset merge**: Combines multiple pending changesets at release time\n10. **Release**: Automated versioning and npm publishing\n11. **Optional Docker publish**: Publishes Docker Hub `latest` and npm-version tags after the npm package is visible\n\n#### Reasonable Timeouts\n\nEvery CI job declares an explicit `timeout-minutes` so hung steps fail\nin minutes instead of reaching the GitHub Actions default of six hours.\nFast checks use 5-10 minute caps, release jobs use 50 minutes, and the\nlink checker uses 10 minutes for external network variance.\n\nThat cap is a backstop, never the deadline: GitHub reports a job it\nkills as **cancelled**, not **failed**. Long steps therefore own an\nexplicit budget via `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`, which warns at\n70% of the budget and fails the step with exit code 124 when it expires.\nSee [CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md](docs/CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md).\n\nIndividual tests are also capped inside supported runners:\n`npm test` runs `node --test --test-timeout=30000`, and the CI Bun\nrunner uses `bun test --timeout 30000`. Both bound a _single test_, not\nthe suite, which is why the suite budget above exists. Deno does not\nprovide a single global per-test timeout flag, so Deno tests are\nprotected by their step budget and the matrix job backstop.\n\nSee [BEST-PRACTICES.md](docs/BEST-PRACTICES.md) for detailed explanations of each practice.\n\n#### Robust Changeset Handling\n\nThe CI/CD pipeline is designed to handle concurrent PRs gracefully:\n\n- **PR Validation**: Only validates changesets **added by the current PR**, not pre-existing ones from other merged PRs. This prevents false failures when multiple PRs merge before a release cycle completes.\n\n- **Release-time Merging**: If multiple changesets exist when releasing, they are automatically merged into a single changeset with:\n  - The highest version bump type (major > minor > patch)\n  - All descriptions preserved in chronological order\n\nThis design decouples PR validation from the need to pull changes from the default branch, reducing conflicts and ensuring that even if CI/CD fails, all unpublished changesets will still get published when the error is resolved.\n\n### Deploying the example app\n\nThe `example-app.yml` workflow deploys the universal example app to GitHub\nPages on every push to `main`. Before the first run on `main` in a new\nrepository created from this template, open **Settings → Pages** and set\n**Source = GitHub Actions**. This is a one-time manual step and cannot be\nconfigured from a workflow because the Pages source defaults to\n_Deploy from a branch_. Without it, the `pages-deploy` job fails on\n`actions/deploy-pages` with `Get Pages site failed` /\n`Failed to create deployment`. After flipping the source, the workflow\nprovisions the Pages site on its first run.\n\n### Auto-regenerated preview screenshots\n\nThe same `example-app.yml` workflow contains a `preview-regen` job that boots\nthe built example app in a headless Chromium via\n[`browser-commander`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/browser-commander) +\nPlaywright and writes fresh screenshots to\n`docs/screenshots/example-app/example-app-{locale}-{theme}.png` on every\npush to `main` (and on `workflow_dispatch`). Any drift is committed back to\n`main` so README/site images never go stale between releases. Screenshot-only\npushes do not match this workflow's path filter, while a protected-branch\nfallback PR remains eligible for its required checks. The job runs in the\nofficial Playwright container with the browser already installed, avoiding CI\nstalls from live Chromium downloads.\n\nThe same script is available locally:\n\n```bash\nnpm install --prefix examples/universal-app\nnpm run example:web:preview-images\n# Verbose probe of <html data-theme>, <html lang>, and PNG signatures:\nPREVIEW_VERBOSE=1 npm run example:web:preview-images\n```\n\nThe matrix defaults to `{en, ru} × {light, dark}`. The shipped example app\nhas no localization or theme toggle yet, so every cell currently renders\nthe same UI — when a fork adds either, the matrix produces real per-cell\nvariants without script edits.\n\n### Broken Link Checker\n\nThe link checker workflow (`.github/workflows/links.yml`) validates all links in Markdown and HTML files:\n\n1. **Detection**: Uses [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action) to scan all `*.md` and `*.html` files\n2. **Web Archive fallback**: For any broken links found, automatically checks the [Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org) for archived versions\n3. **Actionable suggestions**: Reports one of three outcomes for each broken link:\n   - **Archived**: Suggests the Web Archive URL as a replacement\n   - **Not archived**: Clearly reports the link is unrecoverable\n4. **Scheduled checks**: Runs weekly to catch links that break over time (even if no files changed)\n5. **Issue creation**: On scheduled runs, creates a GitHub Issue with the full broken links report\n\nAdd regex patterns to `.lycheeignore` to exclude URLs from checks (e.g., local dev URLs, example.com, known rate-limited sites).\n\n## Configuration\n\n### Updating Package Name\n\nAfter creating a repository from this template, update the package name in:\n\n1. `package.json`: replace `\"@link-foundation/example-package-name\"` with your package name\n2. `.changeset/config.json`: Package references\n\nRelease scripts derive the package name from `package.json` at runtime, so no\nscript-level package-name constants need to be edited during template adoption.\n\n### Protected-Branch Release Pull Requests\n\nIf `main` requires pull requests and the `Pipeline Status` check, the release\nand instant-release jobs can use their built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` to open a release\nPR. Enable **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** in\nrepository Actions settings. The helper verifies that the version commit is a\ndirect child of the validated workflow SHA and contains only package metadata\nand consumed changesets. It then creates a successful `Pipeline Status` check\non that exact commit, linked to the validating run, waits for every required\ncheck, and merges the PR only after they pass. The release jobs alone receive\n`checks: write`. Set `RELEASE_METADATA_PATHS` to a comma-separated list of\nadditional exact metadata paths for other package layouts.\n\nAn optional `RELEASE_PR_TOKEN` secret keeps the existing dedicated-token path\nand takes precedence when set. Give that actor Contents and Pull requests write\naccess and Checks read access. The manual changeset-PR and generated-preview\npaths still require the dedicated token. A short-lived GitHub App installation\ntoken can be wired to the same inputs instead of a PAT.\n\n### Optional Docker Hub Publishing\n\nDocker publishing is disabled by default. To enable it for a project that ships\na Docker image, add a `Dockerfile` and configure these GitHub Actions settings:\n\n| Setting              | Type               | Description                                                                           |\n| -------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE`    | Variable           | Docker Hub image name, for example `namespace/image`. This enables Docker publishing. |\n| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` | Variable           | Docker Hub username used by `docker/login-action`.                                    |\n| `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`    | Secret             | Docker Hub access token used for registry authentication.                             |\n| `DOCKER_CONTEXT`     | Variable, optional | Docker build context. Defaults to `.`.                                                |\n| `DOCKERFILE`         | Variable, optional | Dockerfile path. Defaults to `./Dockerfile`.                                          |\n\nWhen enabled, the release workflow waits until the exact published npm version\nis visible in the npm registry, then publishes Docker Hub tags for `latest` and\nthat same version. The Docker build also receives `NPM_PACKAGE_VERSION` as a\nbuild argument so Dockerfiles can install the matching published package.\n\n### ESLint Rules\n\nCustomize ESLint in `eslint.config.js`. Current configuration:\n\n- ES Modules support\n- Prettier integration\n- No console restrictions (common in CLI tools)\n- Strict equality enforcement\n- Async/await best practices\n- **Strict unused variables rule**: No exceptions - all unused variables, arguments, and caught errors must be removed (no `_` prefix exceptions)\n\n### Prettier Options\n\nConfigured in `.prettierrc`:\n\n- Single quotes\n- Semicolons\n- 2-space indentation\n- 80-character line width\n- ES5 trailing commas\n- LF line endings\n\n## Scripts Reference\n\n| Script                               | Description                                           |\n| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |\n| `bun test --timeout 30000`           | Run tests with Bun and a 30s per-test cap             |\n| `npm test`                           | Run tests with Node.js and a 30s per-test cap         |\n| `bun run lint`                       | Check code with ESLint                                |\n| `bun run lint:fix`                   | Fix ESLint issues automatically                       |\n| `bun run format`                     | Format code with Prettier                             |\n| `bun run format:check`               | Check formatting without changing files               |\n| `bun run check`                      | Run all checks (lint + format)                        |\n| `npm run example:web:dev`            | Start the universal app Vite dev server               |\n| `npm run example:web:build`          | Build the universal app static web bundle             |\n| `npm run example:web:preview-images` | Regenerate preview screenshots via browser-commander  |\n| `npm run example:desktop:package`    | Package the Electron desktop app locally              |\n| `npm run example:mobile:sync`        | Build and sync the app bundle into Capacitor projects |\n| `bun run changeset`                  | Create a new changeset                                |\n\n## Contributing\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed contribution guidelines.\n\nQuick steps:\n\n1. The research\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md))\ndecided: **LiNo is the source, DTCG 2025.10 is the exchange format**, with a\nthree-layer token model (reference → semantic → component). The W3C Design\nTokens Community Group Format Module 2025.10 (published 2025-10-28) is JSON\nwith `$value`, `$type`, `$description`, aliases `{group.token}` and composite\ntypes, with companion Color and Resolver modules. Style Dictionary (v4/v5,\nApache-2.0) already transforms DTCG to CSS, Swift and Kotlin.\n\nThe token sample\n[samples/tokens.lino](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/tokens.lino):\n\n```lino\n(material3: theme\n  (extends base)\n  (token color.primary '#6750A4')\n  (token color.on-primary '#FFFFFF')\n  (token space.medium 16px)\n  (token shape.corner.medium 12px)\n  (token motion.duration.short 150ms))\n```\n\nmeta-sovereign-chat already uses about 60 hand-written CSS custom properties\n(`--bg`, `--accent`, `--bubble-radius`, `--control-h`, ...)\n([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md))\nthat should become tokens.\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-tokens` (`@link-foundation/ui-tokens`) reads token sets written in\nLiNo (with inheritance, aliases and modes), validates them, and exports CSS\ncustom properties, DTCG 2025.10 JSON, Swift and Kotlin constants; it also\nimports DTCG JSON back to LiNo.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Token grammar: `(token PATH VALUE (description '...') (type T))`, aliases as\n  values (`(token color.action (token color.primary))` or `@color.primary`,\n  from {{F07}}), `(extends OTHER)`, modes `(mode dark (token ...))`.\n- Types: `color`, `dimension`, `duration`, `number`, `fontFamily`,\n  `fontWeight`, `cubicBezier`; composites `shadow` and `typography`.\n- `resolveTokens` (inheritance, modes, aliases, cycle detection).\n- Exporters: CSS, DTCG JSON, Swift, Kotlin; importer: DTCG JSON → LiNo.\n- Optional Style Dictionary backend via a subpath export.\n- CLI `link-ui-tokens`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Real Material/Fluent/HIG token sets ({{F40}}–{{F42}}); theme switching UI\n  ({{F39}}); style rules ({{F12}}).\n- Figma/Penpot sync (later interop issue {{F53}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F07}} (blocker): typed values — dimension, duration, colour (hex and\n  `oklch`), refs, `toCss`, `toHex`. Aliases stay as\n   `var(--color-primary)` so runtime changes cascade. Module\n   `ui-kotlin`, package `foundation.link.ui` (or the group used by F23).\n2. `commonMain/.../Model.kt`:\n   ```kotlin\n   data class UiNode(val id: String?, val kind: String, val props: List<UiProp>, val children: List<UiNode>)\n   data class UiAction(val source: String, val event: String, val action: List<String>)\n   ```\n   Field names follow the F03 `.tree.json` shape.\n3. `RenderTree.kt`: platform-neutral mapping, used by the composables and by\n   tests:\n   ```kotlin\n   data class RenderNode(val id: String?, val primitive: String,\n       val props: List<Pair<String, String>>, val children: List<RenderNode>)\n   fun renderTree(node: UiNode, theme: UiTheme): RenderNode\n   ```\n   Mapping: `document` to `LazyColumn` or scrollable `Column`, `stack` to\n   `Column`/`Row` with `Arrangement.spacedBy(gap)`, `text` to `Text`,\n   `button` to Material 3 `Button` with a `Text` child, `image` to `Image`\n   (the loader is a pluggable lambda; no network library in core) with\n   `contentDescription` from `alt`, unknown to `Box`.\n4. `Theme.kt`: `UiTheme` resolves `(token space.medium)` to `Dp` or a colour;\n   built from the F11 file or from a theme `.lino`.\n5. `Snapshot.kt`: `fun dumpLino(node: RenderNode): String`, the same format\n   as {{F22}}:\n   ```lino\n   (app: Column (scroll vertical)\n     (body: Column (spacing 16)\n       (greeting: Text 'Hello, links')\n       (ok: Button (label 'OK'))))\n   ```\n   Use the F23 formatter for quoting.\n6. `UiView.kt`:\n   `@Composable fun UiView(document: UiDocumentState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, theme: UiTheme = UiTheme.Default, onAction: (UiAction) -> Unit = {})`.\n   `UiDocumentState` keeps one `mutableStateOf` per element so `setProp`\n   recomposes only that element. Every node gets `Modifier.testTag(id)`.\n7. Actions: `Button(onClick = { onAction(...) })` with the parsed\n   `on press` link. Strings are never executed; `javascript:` navigate targets\n   are rejected.\n8. Tests in `jvmTest` / `desktopTest`: `RenderTreeTest`, `ThemeTest`,\n   `ActionTest`, `FixtureTest` (same rules as F22, snapshots in\n   `src/commonTest/resources/snapshots/<area>/<name>.render.lino`; reading\n   fixtures from `../../docs/spec/fixtures`), and `UiViewTest` with\n   `runComposeUiTest { setContent { UiView(...) }; onNodeWithTag(\"ok\").performClick() }`\n   asserting the action (check that the Compose UI test API is available for\n   the desktop target in the chosen version).\n9. Example: a desktop `main()` in `examples/kotlin/` (`./gradlew run`)\n   rendering `docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/document.lino`.\n10. `.github/workflows/kotlin.yml`: `ubuntu-latest`, `actions/setup-java`\n    (Temurin 17 or newer, check what the Compose version needs),\n    `gradle/actions/setup-gradle`, `./gradlew check` in `packages/ui-kotlin`;\n    path filters `packages/ui-kotlin/**`, `docs/spec/**`.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-kotlin/{settings.gradle.kts,build.gradle.kts,gradle.properties,gradlew,gradlew.bat,gradle/wrapper/*}`\n- `packages/ui-kotlin/src/commonMain/kotlin/foundation/link/ui/{Model,Projection,RenderTree,Theme,Snapshot,UiView,UiDocumentState}.kt`\n- `packages/ui-kotlin/src/desktopTest/kotlin/foundation/link/ui/{RenderTreeTest,ThemeTest,ActionTest,FixtureTest,UiViewTest}.kt`\n- `packages/ui-kotlin/src/commonTest/resources/snapshots/**/*.render.lino`\n- `packages/ui-kotlin/README.md`, `examples/kotlin/Main.kt`\n- `.github/workflows/kotlin.yml`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes in `packages/ui-kotlin` on the CI job.\n- [ ] `FixtureTest`: every supported fixture in `docs/spec/fixtures/` has a\n      `.render.lino` snapshot; adding a fixture without one fails the test.\n- [ ] For those fixtures, IDs and parent/child pairs equal those in the\n      `.tree.json`.\n- [ ] Each fixture's `.render.lino` is identical to {{F22}}'s for kinds that\n      map to the same primitive name, or the differences are listed in\n      `packages/ui-kotlin/README.md` (for example `ScrollView` vs `Column`).\n- [ ] `UiViewTest`: `onNodeWithTag(\"ok\").performClick()` produces\n      `UiAction(\"ok\", \"press\", listOf(\"navigate\", \"home\"))`; every element\n      with an ID has a node with that test tag.\n- [ ] `ThemeTest`: token references resolve; missing tokens give a\n      diagnostic, not an exception.\n- [ ] `javascript:` targets are rejected (`ActionTest`).\n- [ ] Screenshot of the desktop example (light and dark) attached to the\n      pull request.\n- [ ] Every dependency is Apache-2.0, MIT or BSD (reviewed in the PR).\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\ncd packages/ui-kotlin\n./gradlew check\n./gradlew desktopTest --tests '*FixtureTest*'\ncd ../../examples/kotlin && ../../packages/ui-kotlin/gradlew run   # screenshot\n```\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform (Apache-2.0): ADOPT\n  (existing-solutions.md section 8).\n- Jetpack Compose Material 3 (Apache-2.0): native controls.\n- Roborazzi and Paparazzi (Apache-2.0, verify) for optional screenshot tests.\n- Flutter Material and Cupertino widgets as a reference for one tree with\n  two looks (learn).\n\n## References\n\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md\n- https://www.jetbrains.com/compose-multiplatform/\n- https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/testing\n"

Each component issue ({{F26}}–{{F30}}) and each theme ({{F40}}–{{F43}}) needs two checks in CI: a screenshot comparison per theme and locale, and an automated accessibility audit.\n\nWhat exists already:\n\n- `scripts/update-preview-images.mjs` uses `browser-commander` and the Playwright Chromium. It serves `examples/universal-app/dist` at 1280×800 and writes `docs/screenshots/example-app/example-app-{en,ru}-{light,dark}.png`.\n- The `preview-regen` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` runs in the pinned container `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright@sha256:b0ab6f3c…` (v1.59.1-noble), with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`. It installs `playwright@1.59.1` with `--no-save`. The job currently fails because `gh` is missing in that container ({{B04}}).\n\nPrior art in our other repositories:\n\n- meta-sovereign-chat runs Playwright end-to-end tests in Chromium and WebKit, a WCAG 2.0 A/AA axe-core audit (`stepAxeAudit`), and pixel and contrast checks ([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n- formal-ai produces per-locale and per-theme CI screenshots `app-preview-{en,hi,ru,zh}-{dark,light}.png` with `data-testid` hooks, but has no axe audit ([formal-ai.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/formal-ai.md)).\n- konard.github.io tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit ([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nAdd one reusable Playwright Test setup with axe-core that any package under `packages/*` and the demo site can use. It provides:\n\n- screenshot baselines per browser, theme and locale;\n- a WCAG 2.1 A/AA audit;\n- a pinned container so that baselines are reproducible;\n- a CI workflow that uploads diffs when it fails.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Root devDependencies:\n  - `@playwright/test` (Apache-2.0), at the same version as the container tag;\n  - `@axe-core/playwright` and `axe-core` (MPL-2.0). These are allowed only as dev/CI tools, never imported by a published package; record this in `docs/testing-ui.md`.\n- `playwright.config.mjs` with the `chromium` and `webkit` projects (`firefox` optional), a `webServer` that serves static fixtures, and a fixed viewport, locale and timezone.\n- Helpers in `tests/ui/helpers.mjs`: an accessibility assertion and a theme × locale screenshot matrix.\n- Fixture pages, a smoke test, and a negative test proving that axe catches violations.\n- A test for the existing example app (`examples/universal-app/dist`), replacing nothing in `update-preview-images.mjs`.\n- A `ui-tests.yml` workflow in the pinned Playwright container, with a manual \"update snapshots\" mode.\n- `scripts/check-playwright-version.mjs`, which keeps the npm version and the container tag in sync.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Fixing `gh` in `preview-regen` ({{B04}}).\n- Component tests themselves (each component issue adds its own `*.e2e.mjs`).\n- The docs site ({{F54}}), which adds its own tests using these helpers.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **{{F01}}** (blocker) provides the `packages/*` workspace layout, the root devDependency location and the test globs. Playwright must discover `packages/*/e2e/**/*.e2e.mjs`. You can start before F01 merges by writing only `tests/ui/`, and adding the `packages/*` glob after the rebase.\n\nRelated:\n\n- {{B04}} fixes the container `gh` problem in a sibling job; reuse the same image digest.\n- {{F16}} provides the first real renderer to test.\n- {{F25}} uses `expectAccessible()` as the a11y acceptance gate.\n- {{F39}} provides the theme switch used by the screenshot matrix.\n- {{F54}} adds the demo site tests.\n- {{F56}} documents the workflow for agents.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Add the devDependencies. Pin `@playwright/test` to exactly the version in the `example-app.yml` container comment (1.59.1 at the time of writing; check the current pin).\n2. Write `scripts/check-playwright-version.mjs`. It reads the `@playwright/test` version from `package.json`, finds every `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright@sha256:… # vX.Y.Z-noble` comment in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, and exits 1 on a mismatch. Add it to `npm run lint` or as `npm run check:playwright`.\n3. Write `playwright.config.mjs` with these settings:\n   - `testMatch: ['tests/ui/**/*.e2e.mjs', 'packages/*/e2e/**/*.e2e.mjs']`. Use the `.e2e.mjs` suffix so that `node --test`, `bun test` (which matches `*.spec.*`) and `deno test` never pick these files up.\n   - `snapshotPathTemplate: '{testDir}/__screenshots__/{projectName}/{testFilePath}/{arg}{ext}'`.\n   - `use: {viewport: {width: 1280, height: 800}, locale: 'en-US', timezoneId: 'UTC', colorScheme: 'light'}`.\n   - `expect.toHaveScreenshot: {maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.001, animations: 'disabled'}`.\n   - `webServer: {command: 'node scripts/serve-static.mjs --port 4173', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:4173/'}`.\n   - `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`.\n   - `reporter: [['list'], ['html', {open: 'never'}]]`.\n4. Write `scripts/serve-static.mjs`, a dependency-free `node:http` server for `tests/ui/pages/`, `packages/*/e2e/pages/` and `examples/universal-app/dist/`. Reuse the server code of `update-preview-images.mjs` by moving it into `scripts/lib/static-server.mjs` (do not duplicate it, because jscpd runs in CI).\n5. Write `tests/ui/helpers.mjs` with two exports:\n   - `/** @param {import('@playwright/test').Page} page @param {{include?: string, exclude?: string[], tags?: string[]}} [opts] */ export async function expectAccessible(page, opts)`. It runs `new AxeBuilder({page}).withTags(opts.tags ?? ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa'])`, and fails with a readable list of `id`, `impact` and target selectors.\n   - `/** @param {Page} page @param {string} name @param {{themes?: string[], locales?: string[], apply: (page, {theme, locale}) => Promise<void>}} opts */ export async function screenshotMatrix(page, name, opts)`. It produces `<name>-<locale>-<theme>.png`.\n6. Add the fixture pages:\n   - `tests/ui/pages/smoke.html`: a heading, a labelled input, a button, and a light/dark switch through `data-theme`;\n   - `tests/ui/pages/inaccessible.html`: an unlabelled input and a low-contrast button.\n7. Add the tests:\n   - `tests/ui/smoke.e2e.mjs`, which runs `expectAccessible` and `screenshotMatrix` on `smoke.html`, with en and ru × light and dark;\n   - `tests/ui/negative.e2e.mjs`, which asserts that axe reports `label` and `color-contrast` violations on `inaccessible.html`;\n   - `tests/ui/example-app.e2e.mjs`, which builds nothing itself; it expects `npm run example:web:build` to have run, and audits `examples/universal-app/dist/index.html`. Existing violations go into an explicit `knownViolations` list, each with a linked issue, rather than being ignored silently.\n8. Add the npm scripts:\n   - `\"test:ui\": \"playwright test\"`;\n   - `\"test:ui:update\": \"playwright test --update-snapshots\"`;\n   - `\"test:ui:docker\": \"docker run --rm -v \\\"$PWD\\\":[REDACTED] -w /work -e CI=1 mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.59.1-noble sh -c 'npm ci && npx playwright test'\"`. Use the same tag as the pin.\n9. Add `.github/workflows/ui-tests.yml`:\n   - it runs on PRs and on main;\n   - one job in the same container digest as `preview-regen`, with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`;\n   - steps: `git config --global --add safe.directory \"$GITHUB_WORKSPACE\"`, `npm ci`, `npm run example:web:build`, then `npx playwright test`;\n   - on failure, upload `playwright-report/` and `test-results/` as artifacts;\n   - a `workflow_dispatch` input `update-snapshots` runs `--update-snapshots` and uploads `**/__screenshots__/**` as an artifact for a human to commit. It does not push and does not need `gh`.\n\n   Pin the actions by SHA, as the other workflows do.\n10. Commit the baselines that the container generates, never baselines from a local macOS or Windows run. Add `playwright-report/` and `test-results/` to `.gitignore`.\n11. Write `docs/testing-ui.md`. It explains how to add an `e2e/` folder to a package, update baselines with `npm run test:ui:docker -- --update-snapshots`, read the diff artifacts, and handle the `knownViolations` policy. It also records the MPL-2.0 note for axe-core.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.gitignore`, `eslint.config.js` (globals for `*.e2e.mjs`)\n- `playwright.config.mjs`, `scripts/serve-static.mjs`, `scripts/lib/static-server.mjs`, `scripts/update-preview-images.mjs` (use the shared server), `scripts/check-playwright-version.mjs`\n- `tests/ui/helpers.mjs`, `tests/ui/pages/{smoke,inaccessible}.html`, `tests/ui/{smoke,negative,example-app}.e2e.mjs`, `tests/ui/__screenshots__/**`\n- `.github/workflows/ui-tests.yml`, `docs/testing-ui.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `npx playwright test` in the pinned container passes for the `chromium` and `webkit` projects.\n- [ ] The smoke test produces 4 baselines per browser (`en`/`ru` × `light`/`dark`), and they are committed.\n- [ ] `tests/ui/negative.e2e.mjs` passes, which proves that axe detects the `label` and `color-contrast` violations.\n- [ ] Changing one colour in `smoke.html` makes `toHaveScreenshot` fail, and the CI artifact contains the diff image.\n- [ ] `node scripts/check-playwright-version.mjs` exits 0, and exits 1 after you edit the version in `package.json`.\n- [ ] `npm test`, `bun test` and `deno test -A --parallel` do not execute any `*.e2e.mjs` file.\n- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication` pass, and `ui-tests.yml` is green.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnode scripts/check-playwright-version.mjs\nnpm run example:web:build\nnpm run test:ui:docker                       #
