[2026-11-01T11:56:36.992Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F12\ntitle: 'ui-style: style rules, states and responsive conditions'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 2\nblocked_by: [F07, F11]\nrequirements: [R2, R6, R14]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nThemes must restyle any control without code changes (R14), and the same style\ndescription must work for every target framework (R6): the DOM renderer\n({{F16}}) needs CSS; React Native, SwiftUI and Compose ({{F20}}, {{F22}},\n{{F24}}) need resolved values per element. The architecture defines `ui-style`\nas \"style rules as links resolved against tokens\"\n([ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).\nThe sample\n[samples/styles.lino](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/styles.lino):\n\n```lino\n(button-style: style\n  (selector (type button) (variant filled))\n  (background (token color.primary))\n  (color (token color.on-primary))\n  (radius (token shape.corner.medium))\n  (state hover (elevation 2))\n  (state pressed (scale 0.98)))\n```\n\nBecause `:` separates an id from a link in LiNo, CSS syntax such as `:hover`\nor `max-width: 640px` cannot appear in bare values. The ecosystem research\n(section 5) prescribes structured links instead: `(state hover)`,\n`(media (max-width 640px))`\n([links-notation-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-style` (`@link-foundation/ui-style`) reads style rules written in\nLiNo, matches them to UI elements, resolves token references through\n`ui-tokens`, and produces either a CSS stylesheet or a resolved style object\nfor one element in a given state and environment.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Rule grammar (below): selectors, declarations, `state`, `media`,\n  `container` blocks, nesting of `state` inside `media`.\n- States: `hover`, `focus` (focus-visible), `pressed`, `disabled`, `selected`,\n  `checked`.\n- Conditions: `(media (max-width 640px))`, `(media (min-width ...))`,\n  `(media (prefers-color-scheme dark))`, `(media (prefers-reduced-motion reduce))`,\n  `(container (min-width 400px))`.\n- Property vocabulary with CSS mapping and types (from {{F07}}).\n- Cascade: specificity, then source order (later wins).\n- `compileCss()` and `resolveStyle()`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Animations and transitions ({{F44}}); layout algorithms ({{F28}}); complete\n  themes ({{F39}}–{{F43}}).\n- Arbitrary CSS selectors (combinators other than `within`, pseudo-elements).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F07}} (blocker): typed values and `toCss` for declaration values.\n- {{F11}} (blocker): `resolveTokens` and CSS variable naming\n  (`color.primary` → `--color-primary`). Consumed: names for `var(...)` in CSS\n  output and concrete values for `resolveStyle`. Before F11 merges, use a stub\n  `Map` of resolved tokens and the same naming rule.\n- Related: {{F16}} (expects selectors such as `ui-button[variant=\"filled\"]`),\n  {{F20}}, {{F22}}, {{F24}}, {{F25}} (state machines provide the current\n  state), {{F39}}, {{F46}} (Styles tab).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-style/package.json` (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-style\"`),\n   dependencies `@link-foundation/ui-core`, `@link-foundation/ui-tokens`.\n2. Grammar, documented in the README:\n   ```lino\n   (card-style: style\n     (selector (type card) (within (type dialog)))\n     (padding (token space.medium))\n     (media (max-width 640px)\n       (padding (token space.small)))\n     (container (min-width 400px)\n       (direction horizontal))\n     (state disabled (opacity 0.38)))\n   ```\n   Selector parts: `(type KIND)`, `(id ID)`, `(PROP VALUE)` for prop equality,\n   `(within SELECTOR)` for an ancestor.\n3. `src/properties.js`: table `name → { css, type }`, at least `background →\n   background-color (color)`, `color (color)`, `radius → border-radius\n   (dimension)`, `padding`, `gap`, `opacity (number)`, `elevation → box-shadow`\n   (value is `var(--elevation-N)` from tokens), `scale → transform: scale()`,\n   `font-size`, `font-weight`, `border-width`, `border-color`, `direction →\n   flex-direction`. Unknown property → diagnostic `unknown-property`.\n4. `src/read.js`: `readStyles(text) → { rules: StyleRule[], diagnostics }`:\n   ```js\n   /** @typedef {{ id: string, order: number, selector: Selector, declarations: Decl[],\n    *   blocks: Array<{ kind: 'state'|'media'|'container', condition: unknown, rule: StyleRule }> }} StyleRule */\n   ```\n5. `src/match.js`: `matches(selector, node, ancestors)`; specificity tuple\n   `[ids, props + states, types]`.\n6. `src/resolve.js`:\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @param {UiNode} node @param {UiNode[]} ancestors\n    * @param {{ states?: string[], viewport?: { width: number }, container?: { width: number },\n    *           colorScheme?: 'light'|'dark', reducedMotion?: boolean }} env\n    * @returns {{ style: Record<string, TypedValue>, sources: Record<string, string> }}  sources = rule id per property\n    */\n   export function resolveStyle(rules, tokens, node, ancestors, env) {}\n   ```\n   `sources` lets dev mode show which rule won (R12).\n7. `src/css.js`: `compileCss(rules, { tagFor = (k) => 'ui-' + k })`. Mapping:\n   `hover → :hover`, `focus → :focus-visible`, `pressed → :active`,\n   `disabled → :is(:disabled, [disabled], [aria-disabled=\"true\"])`,\n   `selected → [aria-selected=\"true\"]`, `checked → [aria-checked=\"true\"]`;\n   `(max-width 640px)` → `@media (max-width: 640px)`; container →\n   `@container (min-width: 400px)`. Expected output for the sample:\n   ```css\n   ui-button[variant='filled'] {\n     background-color: var(--color-primary);\n     color: var(--color-on-primary);\n     border-radius: var(--shape-corner-medium);\n   }\n   ui-button[variant='filled']:hover { box-shadow: var(--elevation-2); }\n   ui-button[variant='filled']:active { transform: scale(0.98); }\n   ```\n   Escape all attribute values; never emit `url(` from unvalidated text.\n8. 19, 25, 26, 28, 31, 36, 39, 41).\n\n### 1.3 Links Notation usage\n\nNeither repo uses Links Notation. There are no `.lino` files and no `links-notation` dependency or reference in either repo. All configuration is TypeScript/JS objects, serialized as JSON to localStorage, to a URL hash (immortality) or to a downloaded `acs-config.json` (anime-avatar). Both formats are flat or two-level key/value maps, so they map directly to links (see section 9).\n\n## 2. Configurability model\n\n### 2.1 immortality: a typed axis schema as the single source of truth\n\n`settings.ts` declares the whole configurable surface as data:\n\n- **Option catalogs.** Each is a `readonly OptionDef[]` with `OptionDef = {id, label, description?, source?: ReferenceId}`. Examples: `PALETTES` (12), `SURFACES` (13 panel materials), `FRAME_STYLES` (9), `BACKGROUNDS` (21), `BACKDROP_GRADIENTS` (7), `FONTS`, `TITLE_STYLES`, `TEXT_EFFECTS`, `INTROS`, `CHART_STYLES`, `CURSORS`, `TABLE_STYLES`, `SCROLLBAR_STYLES`, `ENTRANCES`, `SOUNDS` (26). Id union types are derived with `(typeof X)[number]['id']`, so adding an option updates the types.\n- **Reference registry.** `REFERENCES: Record<ReferenceId, {label, url}>` cites the design source of each option (Arwes, thegridcn, Soul Extract, glitchy.website and others). The panel renders these as links next to each axis.\n- **Axes.** `AXES` has 49 entries:\n  `Axis = ChoiceAxis {kind:'choice', options, display?:'buttons'|'select'} | ToggleAxis {kind:'toggle'} | RangeAxis {kind:'range', min, max, step, unit}`.\n  The shared base is `{key, label, group, description?, sources?}`. `SETTING_GROUPS` defines 8 groups: Color, Panels, Type & text, Scene, HUD & charts, Controls & data, Motion, Audio.\n- **Pure functions over the schema:**\n  - `coerceAxisValue` and `coerceSoundList` validate one value.\n  - `mergeSettings(base, raw)` accepts untrusted input and drops invalid keys.\n  - `diffSettings` and `diffFromDefaults` compute what changed.\n  - `parseStoredSettings` and `migrateLegacySettings` handle storage. Migration from v1 keeps only values the user changed from the v1 defaults.\n  - `loadSettings(storage)` and `saveSettings(storage)` take the storage as a parameter, so they are testable.\n  - `encodeShareHash` and `decodeShareHash` write `#ui=` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON{v:2, ...diff})`. Only the diff from defaults is shared.\n  - `applySharedLook` applies a shared look but keeps the viewer's comfort settings (animations, sound, volume).\n  - `applyPreset`, `isPresetActive`, `countCustomized`.\n  - `randomizeSettings(current, random)` takes an injected RNG and skips locked keys (animations, intro, cursor, and all audio).\n- **Presets.** There are 12 (Poseidon default, Mission, Grid, Ares, Arwes, Soul Extract, Glitchy, ZK matrix, Foundry, Study, Quiet, Resonance). Each is `{id, label, description, sources, settings}`, built by `preset()` as a partial override over a base.\n- **Versioned storage key.** `immortality.ui-settings.v2`, with the v1 key read once for migration.\n- **Rendering.** `Shell` in `App.tsx` writes every visual axis to a `data-*` attribute (`data-palette`, `data-frame`, `data-surface`, `data-glow` and so on) and to CSS custom properties (`--corner`, `--border-width`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`, `--font-scale`, `--chart-line`, `--bg-speed`, `--motion-scale`, `--bg-opacity`). CSS selects on `[data-x='id']`, so theme switching does not re-render React. Palette variables are mirrored to `<html>` for scrollbars. The cursor is generated as an SVG data URI.\n- **Settings UI.** `SettingsPanel.tsx` has one generic `AxisControl`:\n  - A toggle is a switch button with `aria-pressed`.\n  - A range is `<input type=range>` with `<output>` and a `--fill` variable.\n  - A choice is a set of swatch buttons in a `<fieldset>`, or the custom `Select` when `display:'select'`.\n  - The drawer is docked and non-modal (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=false`). Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener. Group tabs support arrow keys.\n  - It offers presets, Randomize, \"Copy share link\" (falls back to the address bar if the clipboard is blocked) and Restore defaults. An `aria-live` region announces the number of customized settings.\n- **Context.** `uiContext.ts` provides `useUiSettings` and `motionAllowed(settings)`, which combines the user toggle with `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\n### 2.2 anime-avatar studio: flat cfg plus a hand-written editor\n\n- `defaults.js` defines `window.ACS_DEFAULTS`, a flat object with about 150 keys, many commented. It covers:\n  - Model: `vrmUrl`, `modelPresetId`, `modelUrl`, `modelFormat`, `modelKind`, `pose`.\n  - Rig: nested `rot{bone:{x,y,z}}`, `scale{}`, `expr{}`.\n  - Gaze: about 20 `look*` keys for follow target, eye and head amounts, smoothing, cone, saccades.\n  - Materials: `mat*`, including `matPerMesh`.",

Animation and 3D\n\n### 3.1 immortality (2D UI motion)\n\n- **Text effects** (`textEffects.ts`): `revealOrder`, `decipherFrame` and `sequenceFrame` are pure functions of `(text, t, seed)`. A component only supplies the clock. This makes them deterministic, testable and easy to record. Ported from Arwes (MIT) and re-implemented from Soul Extract ideas (GPL, ideas only).\n- **Entrances and staggering** are CSS animations scaled by `--motion-scale`. A fixed bug is documented in [case study issue-7](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7): `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels after the animation and made borders look glitchy. It is now `backwards`.\n- **Backgrounds** (`Starfield.tsx`): 21 canvas renderers with `seededRandom`, `parseColor` and `useReducedMotion`. One background (\"resonance\") reacts to sound cues via `onSoundCue`, an event bus from `sound.ts`.\n- **Pointer-reactive glow** in `Frame.tsx` writes `--mx/--my` directly on the element, with no React state.\n- **Overlays** (scanlines, vignette, flicker, grain, illuminator) use `pointer-events:none`. The old `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was replaced with a smooth breathing glow, a photosensitivity fix.\n- **Sound as part of motion**: `sound.ts` has 10 UI events (hover, click, toggle, select, scan, open, close, type, intro, notify), up to 6 sounds per event, and random, cycle or layer modes. The bus is tone shelf, then compressor/limiter, then convolution reverb send, with pointer-positioned stereo. The AudioContext is created lazily because of autoplay rules. `throttledScan` limits repeated scan sounds.\n- No recording or timeline. All motion is either CSS or a clock-driven pure function.\n\n### 3.2 anime-avatar (3D character motion)\n\n- **Clip playback**: three.js `AnimationMixer`. `retargetMixamoToVRM(asset, vrm)` in `animations.js` maps Mixamo bone names through `ACS_MIXAMO_RIG_MAP`, rebuilds `QuaternionKeyframeTrack` and `VectorKeyframeTrack` data, scales hips by rig height, and flips axes for VRM0.\n- **Procedural gestures**: `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` in `gestures.js` is stateless and returns `{rot, exprs}` deltas.\n  - Gestures are `ACS_GESTURE_PRESETS` (wave, nod, shake, bow, each with duration, expression and peak).\n  - Moods are `ACS_MOOD_PRESETS` (`ampScale`, `speedScale`, expression, weight).\n  - Easings are `ACS_EASINGS` (linear, sine, quad, cubic, easeOut, easeInOut, backOut).\n  - Bell and sustained envelopes shape each gesture.\n- **Additive layering**: [case study issue-28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28) established that all motion sources (pose, idle, gestures, look-at, text-motion, mouse force) add relative deltas each frame instead of replacing each other, which removes snaps at gesture start and end. `ACS_mergePose` sums pose and manual rotations, and `mergeExpressionDeltas` sums expressions.\n- **Anatomical constraints**: `ACS_BONE_LIMITS` gives per-bone, per-axis ranges in degrees, citing range-of-motion references. `ACS_clampBoneRad` applies them, and sliders show degrees.\n- **Gaze**: smoothed look-at follows the camera, the mouse or random targets, with a cone, saccades and separate eye and head shares.\n- **Text to motion** (`textMotion.js`): a regex command table (slowWalk, run, happyWalk, stealth and others) maps to GR00T modes and procedural bone deltas, and declares resource requirements. `gearSonic.js` fetches real GEAR-SONIC reference motions (joint_pos, root_pos, root_quat at 50 fps) and a Unitree G1 MJCF/STL robot, and can call a backend.\n- **Speech** (`ipaSpeech.js`): an English-to-IPA lexicon produces a phoneme timeline, which drives VRM mouth expressions and the jaw.\n- **Text to model** (`textToModel.js`): a TRELLIS backend client. With no URL configured it returns `{status:'no-backend'}`, so the feature degrades cleanly.\n- **Editing**: an experimental TransformControls joint gizmo (one joint at a time, hover or tap to switch, off by default).\n- **Export**: GLB (`-edited.glb` via GLTFExporter) and SVG (`ACS_vrmToSVG` projects triangles with back-face culling and depth sort). The SVG export has its own camera settings.\n- **Loading**: `modelLoader.js` handles glTF/VRM, FBX, OBJ, STL, PLY and MMD (PMX/VMD), including zip, rar and 7z archives (fflate and libarchive WASM). `ACS_normalizeModelURL` rewrites GitHub `blob/` and `raw/refs/heads/` URLs to raw download URLs, and `ACS_detectModelFormat` infers the format.\n- **Archive demo**: CSS `@keyframes` (talk, breathe, headSway) on SVG parts, plus a parallel three.js part tree.\n- **Recording**: absent. Screenshot or video export, custom pose saving and a scene editor are only listed in `ROADMAP.md`. There is no MediaRecorder use and no user-editable keyframe timeline.\n\n## 4. Assets and licensing\n\n### 4.1 immortality: zero-asset, cite-everything\n\n- It ships no images or audio. Everything is generated: canvas, SVG, CSS gradients, `feTurbulence` noise and Web Audio. Fonts are OFL `@fontsource` packages.\n- Each option and each sound carries provenance. `OptionDef.source` points into `REFERENCES {label,url}`, and `SOUNDS` entries have `{character, sourceLabel, sourceUrl}`. Sounds have neutral names; the source names say what inspired them.\n- License decisions are recorded per source in [`docs/case-studies/issue-7`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7):\n  - Arwes is MIT, so code was ported with attribution in comments (`frameShapes.ts`, `textEffects.ts`).\n  - Soul Extract is GPL-3.0, so only ideas were re-implemented and no code was copied.\n  - thegridcn has no license, so it was used as a visual reference only.\n- Library choices were weighed by size. Tone.js (about 77 KB) was rejected for plain Web Audio, and the Select was hand-rolled with downshift as the fallback. The framework should keep this habit of recording rejected alternatives.\n\n### 4.2 anime-avatar: per-asset metadata and conditional attribution\n\n  - None of these assets may enter a public-domain framework asset set.\n\n## 5. Problems, bugs and limitations\n\n### 8.1 immortality\n\n1. **Monolithic stylesheet**: `styles.css` is 3359 lines, mixing all themes, components and axes. It cannot be tree-shaken per theme or reused outside the app.\n2. **Hand-duplicated mapping**: the list of axes rendered as `data-*` attributes in `App.tsx` `Shell` is repeated by hand as `CSS_AXES` in `styling.test.ts`. The schema should declare `render: 'data-attr' | 'css-var'` so both are derived.\n3. **React-bound**: the schema is portable TS, but rendering (`Shell`, `SettingsPanel`) is React-only. Nothing is available for plain JS, Vue or native.\n4. **JSON in the URL hash**: share links are percent-encoded JSON, which is long and unreadable. Links Notation would be both shorter and human-readable.\n5. **`isPresetActive` uses `JSON.stringify` comparison**, which depends on key order.\n6. **No i18n**: labels and descriptions are English literals inside the schema.\n7. **Theme ids are flat**: palettes, materials and frames combine freely, but there is no notion of a named \"theme\" bundle beyond presets, and no inheritance between presets beyond one base.\n8. **Past animation bugs** worth adding to the framework's regression list: `animation-fill-mode: both` leaving `clip-path` on panels, a `steps(1)` white flash flicker (photosensitivity), and content hidden only inside `<details>`.\n\n### 8.2 anime-avatar\n\n1. **No build step in production**: Babel standalone transpiles JSX in the browser on every load, React runs in its development UMD build, and dependencies come from unpkg without SRI. This is slow, fragile and unsafe for a framework.\n2. **Global namespace modules** (`window.ACS_*`, `window.Studio`, `window.__acs`) with implicit load order in `index.html`.\n3. **Monoliths**: `Editor.jsx` is 2381 lines in one component, and `apply.js` is 1316 lines. All styling is inline style objects, so there is no theming.\n4. **Two divergent apps** in one repo (studio in `public/` and the archived Vite app in `src/`). The README mostly documents the archive, and the archive's 2D and 3D part trees (`components/svg/*`, `components/three/*`) duplicate each other.\n5. **Weak config validation**: import does a shallow `{...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse}`. Nested `rot/scale/expr` are not validated, unknown keys persist, errors use `alert`. There is no storage version or migration, and the key `acs_B` is opaque.\n6. **No schema**: ranges and labels are duplicated between `Editor.jsx` and `randomizers.js`.\n7. **Licensing**: the proprietary GF2 archives, the CC-BY-NC DamagedHelmet, and vague license strings (\"See repository\", \"CC-ish\"). The license-string heuristic in `attributionRequired` can miss cases.\n8. **Bugs called out in [issue #19](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/19)** (since addressed): the Alicia model loaded back-to-front, GitHub `blob/` URLs failed, loading errors never auto-hid, tests autostarted and could not be stopped, the test log forced scroll to the bottom, split view was shown on mobile, and copyright was shown unconditionally.\n9. **Bugs called out in [issue #28](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/28)**: an unnatural wave, non-anatomical slider ranges shown in radians, and gestures replacing look-at instead of adding to it, which caused snaps.\n10. **No animation recording** and no keyframe editing. The Mixamo retarget only plays existing clips. Pose, scene editor and video export are only on the roadmap.\n11. **Open requests** show demand for more model sources and mocap: [#18](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/18) (VRoid Hub, CharacterStudio), [#21](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/21) (kalidokit), [#22](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/22) (webaverse), [#23](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/23) (airi), [#24](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/24) (GitHub miner), [#38](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/issues/38) (feature parity with TheSashaDev/girl-agent). [PR #17](https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/pull/17) (image-comparison e2e) is still open.\n\n## 9. Use {{F13}} if merged, else `lino-i18n` directly.\n- Theme switcher: themes and schemes from {{F39}} (`light`, `dark`, `system`);\n  the choice is stored in the `user` configuration layer.\n- Dev mode: if {{F46}} is merged, the site enables it (`?ui-dev` and the\n  shortcut); otherwise {{F55}} enables it.\n- Deployment: a new workflow `.github/workflows/site.yml` that builds and\n  deploys the site, and removal of the Pages steps from `example-app.yml`, so\n  that exactly one workflow deploys Pages.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Enabling Pages in repository settings: maintainer action in {{B03}}.\n- Component gallery and playground: {{F55}}. Directory names\nadd no prefix to translation keys. Recursive traversal sorts entries by name in\nUTF-16 code-unit order (case-sensitive and independent of the host locale), then\nvisits them depth first: a directory's contents are processed at that directory's\nposition among its siblings. Later files and later locale blocks overwrite earlier\nvalues for duplicate keys in the same locale. For example, `en.lino` is read before\n`prompts/`, and `z.lino` after it. Other keys are preserved.\n\nOnly regular `.lino` files are loaded; symbolic links and other files are skipped.\nRead and parse errors reject the load. Compatibility aliases (including the\n`mode` shortcut) are expanded once after the entire tree is merged, preserving\nexplicit keys. [2026-11-01T11:57:21.317Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F44\ntitle: 'ui-animation: animation model and player'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 6\nblocked_by: [F12, F16]\nrequirements: [R4, R6]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nR6 says any UI framework is \"just\" a LiNo document, and that includes its\nanimations. R4 asks for recordable animations, which {{F45}} builds on this\nissue. `@link-foundation/ui-animation` is the package that holds the\nkeyframe, spring and timeline model and a player built on the Web Animations\nAPI (WAAPI)\n([`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).\nThe verified sample\nhttps://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/animation.lino\ncontains this link:\n\n```lino\n(press-feedback: animation\n  (target ok)\n  (duration (token motion.duration.short))\n  (easing standard)\n  (track scale (key 0 1) (key 0.5 0.96) (key 1 1)))\n```\n\nLessons from our repositories\n([immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)):\n\n- **Pure functions of time.** In immortality, `decipherFrame(text, t, seed)`\n  is a pure function of time. In anime-avatar,\n  `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` is stateless. Animations built\n  this way are deterministic, so they can be scrubbed, recorded and tested.\n- **Additive layering.** anime-avatar sums deltas from every motion source\n  and applies bell or sustained envelopes, so nothing snaps\n  (https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28).\n- **Regressions to guard against.**\n  - `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels\n    after the animation ended\n    (https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7).\n  - A `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was a photosensitivity hazard and was\n    replaced by a breathing glow.\n- **Reduced motion.** `motionAllowed()` combines the user toggle with\n  `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\nOn libraries: WAAPI is ADOPT. Motion is MIT and optional. **GSAP is\nforbidden**, because its licence bans competing no-code animation tools\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-animation/` with four parts:\n\n1. a LiNo animation model: tracks of keyframes, easings, springs, timelines,\n   stagger, additive composition, state triggers and named procedural\n   effects;\n2. a pure evaluator `sample(animation, t)`;\n3. a compiler to WAAPI keyframes and options;\n4. a player driven by an injectable clock.\n\nReduced motion and flash safety are enforced by the model itself.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- The `animation` link with:\n  - `target`, `duration`, `delay`, `iterations`, `direction`, `fill`\n    (default `none`), `composite` (`replace`, `add` or `accumulate`) and\n    `easing`;\n  - easings: named tokens, `(cubic-bezier a b c d)`, `(steps n)` and\n    `(spring (stiffness) (damping) (mass))`;\n  - `(track <property> (key <offset> <value> [easing]))`;\n  - `(reduced-motion ...)` overrides.\n- The `timeline` link, with `(at <time> (play <id> ...))`, `(sequence ...)`,\n  `(parallel ...)` and `(stagger <step> ...)`.\n- State triggers. `(on pressed (play press-feedback))` binds to the\n  {{F12}} states `hover`, `focus`, `pressed` and `disabled`. This follows\n  the XAML VisualState pattern.\n- Value interpolation for numbers, lengths with units, colours (OKLCH, via\n  {{F07}}), opacity, `translate`, `scale` and `rotate`.\n- Effects registry. `registerEffect(name, fn)` takes pure\n  `(input, t, seed) => output` functions. The first one is `decipher`,\n  ported from immortality `textEffects.ts`, which is Unlicense.\n- Additive layers with `envelope bell` and `envelope sustain`.\n- The player: WAAPI for CSS-animatable properties, and a clock-driven frame\n  loop for effects and non-CSS properties.\n- The safety validator, which covers the fill-mode rule and photosensitive\n  flashes.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The recorder and replay ({{F45}}), the timeline editor UI ({{F49}}) and\n  Lottie import ({{F53}}).\n- Native animation output (SwiftUI, Compose and React Native `Animated`),\n  which belongs to {{F21}}, {{F23}} and {{F20}}. Keep the model\n  platform-neutral so those renderers can map it.\n- A Motion (MIT) adapter. It may come later as an optional peer dependency.\n  GSAP is never used.\n- View Transitions and scroll-driven timelines, which come in a follow-up.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F12}} (blocker). Supplies style states (`hover`, `pressed` and so on) and\n  token resolution, so `(token motion.duration.short)` and `(easing standard)`\n  resolve from the active theme.\n- {{F16}} (blocker). Supplies `handle.nodeFor(id)`, which resolves `(target ok)`\n  to a DOM node, and the store change events that fire state triggers.\n- Indirect: {{F07}}, which provides typed durations, lengths and colours.\n- Related: {{F25}} (behaviour machines can `play` animations), {{F39}}\n  (`data-motion` and the comfort keys), {{F45}}, {{F49}}, {{F53}}, {{F63}},\n  {{F64}}.\n- The model, evaluator and validator (steps 1–5) need no DOM. Start there;\n  steps 6–7 need F16, and a test can stub `nodeFor` until it merges.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Create `packages/ui-animation/package.json` (`@link-foundation/ui-animation`,\n   ESM) with no runtime dependencies besides the workspace packages and\n   `links-notation`. Add a README.\n2. `src/model.js` exposes\n   `/** @returns {{ animations: Map<string, Animation>, timelines: Map<string, Timeline>, diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }} */ loadAnimations(linoText)`.\n   It accepts this input (the final syntax is fixed by {{F03}}):\n   ```lino\n   (panel-enter: animation\n     (duration 300ms)\n     (easing (cubic-bezier 0.2 0 0 1))\n     (fill backwards)\n     (track opacity (key 0 0) (key 1 1))\n     (track translate (key 0 '0 8px') (key 1 '0 0'))\n     (reduced-motion (duration 0ms)))\n   (bounce: animation\n     (duration 600ms)\n     (easing (spring (stiffness 300) (damping 20) (mass 1)))\n     (track scale (key 0 0.9) (key 1 1)))\n   (title-reveal: animation (target title) (duration 900ms) (effect decipher (seed 42)))\n   (intro: timeline\n     (at 0ms (play panel-enter (target sidebar)))\n     (at 120ms (stagger 50ms (play bounce) (targets item-1 item-2 item-3))))\n   ```\n   Keyframe offsets must be in the range 0–1 and sorted. Each violation is a\n   diagnostic.\n3. `src/easing.js` provides `cubicBezier(a, b, c, d)` and `steps(n)`, which\n   return `(x) => y`. `spring({ stiffness, damping, mass })` returns\n   `{ at(t), settleTime }`, a closed-form damped oscillator.\n   `toCssLinear(fn, samples = 40)` returns a CSS `linear()` string, so\n   springs can run on WAAPI.\n4. `src/sample.js` provides\n   `/** Pure. @returns {Record<string, unknown>} */ sample(animation, tMs, { seed })`,\n   which handles keyframe interpolation, delay, iterations, direction and\n   effects. `sampleLayers(layers, tMs)` sums `composite add` layers with\n   their envelopes.\n   - Effects are pure functions; `decipher` returns the same string for the\n     same `(text, t, seed)`.\n   - Randomness only comes from `seededRandom(seed)`, never from\n     `Math.random`.\n5. `src/validate.js` provides `validateAnimation(animation) -> Diagnostic[]`,\n   with these rules:\n   - **fill.** `fill both` or `fill forwards` on `clip-path`, `transform`,\n     `translate`, `scale` or `rotate` is an error unless the animation\n     declares `(persist true)`. This is the immortality issue-7 regression.\n   - **flash.** Sample at 60 Hz. Over any one-second window, more than 3\n     luminance changes of at least 10 percent of relative luminance, in an\n     `opacity`, `background-color` or `color` track, is an error. This\n     follows WCAG 2.3.1, and it catches the `steps(1)` white-flash\n     regression.\n   - **reduced-motion.** Any movement track (`translate`, `scale` or\n     `rotate`) longer than 0ms with no `(reduced-motion ...)` block gets a\n     warning, because the default reduced behaviour is a cross-fade.\n6. `src/compile-waapi.js` provides\n   `toWaapi(animation, { resolveToken }) -> { keyframes, options }`. For the\n   sample `press-feedback`, it must produce:\n   ```js\n   ({\n     keyframes: [\n       { offset: 0, scale: '1' },\n       { offset: 0.5, scale: '0.96' },\n       { offset: 1, scale: '1' },\n     ],\n     options: { duration: 150, easing: '<resolved standard easing>', fill: 'none', composite: 'replace' },\n   });\n   ```\n   The duration of 150 comes from the sample token `motion.duration.short`\n   in https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/tokens.lino.\n7. `src/player.js` provides:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {{ nodeFor(id: string): Element | null }} handle\n    * @param {{ clock?: { now(): number, requestFrame(cb: () => void): number },\n    *   motion?: () => 'full' | 'reduced', animate?: Function }} [options] */\n   export function createPlayer(handle, options) {}\n   // player.play(id, { target }) -> { finished: Promise<void>, pause(), seek(ms), cancel() }\n   // player.bindTriggers(store) -> unsubscribe\n   ```\n   - When `motion()` returns `'reduced'`, apply the `(reduced-motion ...)`\n     block. Without one, use opacity-only tracks with duration 0.\n   - `motion` defaults to reading `data-motion` on the target's theme\n     boundary ({{F39}}) and `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n8. Write `examples/animation/index.html`, which plays `intro` and has a\n   reduced-motion toggle. Add the README (model reference, safety rules and\n   the GSAP ban), tests and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-animation/package.json`, `README.md`, `src/index.js`, `src/index.d.ts`\n- `packages/ui-animation/src/{model,easing,sample,layers,effects,validate,compile-waapi,player,random}.js`\n- `packages/ui-animation/src/effects/decipher.js` (port from immortality; keep the source URL in a comment)\n- `packages/ui-animation/tests/{model,easing,sample,layers,effects,validate,compile-waapi,player}.test.js`\n- `examples/animation/index.html`, `examples/animation/main.js`\n- `tests/e2e/animation.spec.js`, `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `model.test.js`: `samples/animation.lino` and the step 2 example load\n      with no error diagnostics, and unsorted or out-of-range offsets give\n      diagnostics.\n- [ ] `sample.test.js`: `sample(press-feedback, 75)` gives `scale` 0.96\n      under linear easing, and 1000 calls with the same arguments return\n      identical results.\n- [ ] `effects.test.js`: `decipher` with `seed 42` gives a snapshot-stable\n      frame sequence, and `grep -rn \"Math.random\" packages/ui-animation/src`\n      is empty.\n- [ ] `easing.test.js`: a spring settles within 0.1 percent of its target by\n      `settleTime`, and `toCssLinear` returns a valid `linear(...)` string.\n- [ ] `validate.test.js` (regression): `fill both` on `clip-path` is an\n      error, and an opacity flicker of `0 → 1` with `(steps 1)` at 8 Hz is a\n      flash error. A breathing glow at 0.5 Hz passes.\n- [ ] `compile-waapi.test.js`: the `press-feedback` output equals the object\n      in step 6.\n- [ ] `player.test.js`: with a manual clock and a fake `animate`, `seek(75)`\n      and `finished` behave deterministically, and reduced motion switches to\n      the reduced variant.\n- [ ] Playwright `animation.spec.js` (Chromium): after `panel-enter`\n      finishes, the computed `translate` and `clip-path` equal their values\n      before the animation, so nothing is left behind.\n- [ ] `npm ls gsap` finds nothing.\n- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication` and\n      `npm test` pass.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnode --test packages/ui-animation/tests/*.test.js\nnpx playwright test tests/e2e/animation.spec.js\ngrep -rn \"Math.random\" packages/ui-animation/src || echo clean\nnpm test\n```\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- Web Animations API (ADOPT): https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Web_Animations_API\n- Motion (MIT, optional later; do not use Motion+): https://github.com/motiondivision/motion\n- Theatre.js: the core is Apache-2.0 and Studio is AGPL, so use it as a\n  design reference only: https://github.com/theatre-js/theatre\n- Rive state machines and XAML VisualStates, models for state triggers.\n- Why GSAP is forbidden: https://gsap.com/community/standard-license/\n- WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.3.1, three flashes or below threshold.\n\n## References\n\n- Animation sketch in\n  [links-notation-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md)\n  section 6.4.\n- immortality `textEffects.ts`: https://github.com/konard/immortality/blob/main/app/src/textEffects.ts\n- Requirements R4, R6:\n  https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/requirements.md\n"

[2026-11-01T11:57:25.939Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F25\ntitle: 'Behaviour state machines, actions registry and accessibility'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 4\nblocked_by: [F16]\nrequirements: [R13, R15]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nEvery control needs the same three things: behaviour (open/closed, checked,\nfocused item), keyboard and focus handling, and ARIA semantics. The research\nrecommends describing behaviour as serialisable state machines, as Zag.js\n(MIT) does, so that \"behaviour and accessibility live once\" and only a thin\nbinding differs per platform; React Aria (Apache-2.0) is the quality bar\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)\nsection 4 and Recommendations A).\n\nHandlers must be data. deepcase stores UI as TSX strings and runs them with\n`eval` in `evalClientHandler`; the `require` whitelist does not sandbox\nanything ([deepcase.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)\nsections 2.1 and 10). The spec ({{F03}}, `docs/spec/behaviour.md`) already\nfixes `(on <event> <action>...)`, with actions from the vocabulary\n(`navigate`, `emit`, `set`, `toggle`, `focus`) that are never evaluated.\n\nOur apps re-implement the same accessibility pieces: dialog focus traps and\n\"shortcuts never steal plain keys from fields\" in meta-sovereign\n([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)\nsection 3.4), the APG listbox with typeahead and `numericKeys.js` in\nkonard.github.io\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)\nsection 4.1), arrow-key tab groups and `aria-live` counters in immortality\n([immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md)\nsection 5).\n\n## Goal\n\nShip a DOM-free state machine interpreter whose machines are written in LiNo,\nan actions registry that maps names to host functions, and DOM accessibility\nhelpers (focus, roving tabindex, typeahead, key bindings, live region) that\n{{F26}} and {{F27}} build on.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Machine format in LiNo: `initial`, `context`, flat `state`s, `on` with\n  `target`, `do` (action names) and `when` (guard names), `entry`, `exit`,\n  `after` (timers with an injected clock).\n- Interpreter `createMachine` / `interpret` with no DOM dependency\n  (`@link-foundation/ui-components/behavior`, also used later by {{F20}}).\n- Part bindings in LiNo: ARIA attributes and keys per part, derived from\n  state and context.\n- `createActionRegistry()`: register, lookup and dispatch by name; unknown\n  names produce diagnostics, never code execution.\n- DOM helpers in `src/a11y/`: focus trap and restore, roving tabindex,\n  typeahead, key binding map, live-region announcer, `bindMachine`.\n- Integration with `ui-dom` ({{F16}}): `(on press ...)` dispatch goes through\n  the registry; components declare `(machine ...)`.\n- Two reference machines: `toggle` and `disclosure`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Nested and parallel states, history states (record in the README as\n  future work).\n- The controls themselves ({{F26}}) and overlays ({{F27}}).\n- Expressions in guards (`when` takes a guard name only, as the spec defers\n  expressions).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F16}} (blocker): `defineKind`, the `ui-action` event and `onAction`, and\n  `handle.nodeFor(id)` used by `bindMachine` to find parts.\n- Indirect: {{F06}} `parse` (machines are LiNo documents), {{F03}}\n  `behaviour.md` and `vocabulary.lino` (add the `machine` kind there by a\n  spec pull request if missing).\n- Related: {{F04}} (APG keyboard summaries per kind are the acceptance\n  reference), {{F05}} (`expectAccessible(page)` is the axe gate), {{F18}},\n  {{F19}}, {{F20}}, {{F28}} (move its keyboard logic onto these helpers).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. In `packages/ui-components/` (create the package if {{F28}} has not:\n   `@link-foundation/ui-components`, `\"type\": \"module\"`), add `src/behavior/`\n   and an `exports` entry `\"./behavior\"` that imports nothing from the DOM or\n   `ui-dom`.\n2. Machine format (`src/behavior/machines/toggle.lino`):\n   ```lino\n   (toggle-machine: machine\n     (initial off)\n     (context (pressed false))\n     (state off\n       (on toggle (target on) (do set-pressed) (when not-disabled)))\n     (state on\n       (on toggle (target off) (do clear-pressed) (when not-disabled)))\n     (part root\n       (attr aria-pressed (context pressed))\n       (key Enter toggle)\n       (key Space toggle)))\n   ```\n   `disclosure.lino` adds `(entry focus-content)`, `(exit restore-focus)` and\n   `(after 500ms (target closed))` to show timers.\n3. `src/behavior/parse-machine.js`:\n   `parseMachine(text | UiNode) -> { machine, diagnostics }`; diagnostics for\n   unknown targets, duplicate states, missing `initial`.\n4. `src/behavior/interpret.js`:\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @param {Machine} machine\n    * @param {{ actions: ActionRegistry, guards?: Record<string, (ctx, event) => boolean>,\n    *   clock?: { setTimeout, clearTimeout }, context?: object }} options\n    * @returns {{ state: string, context: object, send(event: string | {type: string}): void,\n    *   subscribe(fn: (snapshot) => void): () => void, stop(): void, attrs(part: string): object }}\n    */\n   export function interpret(machine, options) {}\n   ```\n   Built-in context actions: `(do (set pressed true))` and `(do (toggle pressed))`\n   are data operations on context; everything else is a registry lookup.\n5. `src/behavior/actions.js`: `createActionRegistry({ onUnknown })` with\n   `register(name, fn)`, `has(name)`, `dispatch(name, args, meta)`. The\n   vocabulary actions `navigate`, `emit`, `set`, `toggle`, `focus` have\n   default implementations; `navigate` rejects the `javascript:` scheme.\n6. [2026-11-01T11:58:17.609Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F45\ntitle: 'Animation and interaction recorder, replay'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 6\nblocked_by: [F44, F08]\nrequirements: [R4, R7]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nR4 asks for animation recording, with recordings stored as Links Notation.\nR7 asks for the simplest description, sharable by default. The verified\nsample\nhttps://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/samples/animation.lino\nshows the target shape:\n\n```lino\n(recording-1: recording\n  (started '2026-11-01T12:00:00Z')\n  (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n  (event 840ms (input pointer down ok))\n  (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved')))\n```\n\nNone of our repositories records anything today: immortality and\nanime-avatar have no recording or timeline. Their animations are pure\nfunctions of time, though, and that makes the design simple: **record the\nclock, the inputs, the state changes and the seed, not the pixels**.\nPlayback re-evaluates the pure functions, so recordings are small, diffable\nand reproducible\n([immortality-and-anime-avatar.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/immortality-and-anime-avatar.md),\nmigration note 6).\n\ndeepcase points the same way. Its window and focus state\n(`Opened`, `Focus`, `Traveler`) is links, so timestamped changes to it are a\nrecording too\n([deepcase.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/deepcase.md)\nsection 11).\n\nrrweb (MIT) records DOM mutations. It is useful for comparison, but it is not\nour format\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nAdd a recorder and a deterministic replayer to `@link-foundation/ui-animation`.\n\n- The recorder captures store diffs, user input events and animation starts\n  as timestamped LiNo events, together with the seed, the clock origin and\n  the viewport.\n- Replay reproduces the same state at every time `t`, and it can seek both\n  forward and backward.\n- A verifier replays only the inputs and proves that they regenerate the\n  recorded state changes.\n- A recording can be exported as a Playwright test.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- The recording format:\n  - header fields `started`, `seed`, `viewport`, `document` (the id of the\n    recorded document), `snapshot` (the initial state as LiNo) and\n    `redacted`;\n  - `event` links with a relative time in ms;\n  - event kinds `set`, `insert`, `remove` and `move` (from {{F08}}),\n    `input` (pointer, key, wheel, text, focus), `play` and `cancel` (from the\n    {{F44}} player), and `mark` (a user label).\n- `createRecorder(...)`, `replay(...)`, `stateAt(recording, t)` and\n  `verifyReplay(recording, ...)`.\n- Coalescing. Pointer moves are throttled to at most 60 per second, text\n  input is merged per field, and every timestamp is an integer in ms.\n- Redaction is on by default. Values from `password` fields and from fields\n  marked `(sensitive true)` are recorded as `'***'`.\n- `toPlaywright(recording)`, which generates a Playwright spec.\n- Optional comparison script: `experiments/recorder/vs-rrweb.mjs`. It\n  records the same scripted session with rrweb (a devDependency of the\n  experiment only) and prints both sizes.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Video, screen or MediaRecorder capture, which is pixels, not links.\n- The timeline editor UI ({{F49}}) and the dev mode recording button\n  ({{F46}}).\n- Persisting recordings to IndexedDB ({{F09}}). This issue returns text, and\n  the caller saves it.\n- rrweb as a runtime dependency, and any rrweb import or export in the\n  shipped package.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F44}} (blocker). Supplies the player's `play`/`cancel` hooks, used to\n  record animation starts; `sample(animation, t, { seed })`, used to\n  re-evaluate animations during replay; and `seededRandom`.\n- {{F08}} (blocker). Supplies the store change events (insert, update,\n  remove, move), transactions, `snapshot()` and `restore()`, and stable IDs.\n  Use the event shape actually merged. Until then, a stub store with\n  `subscribe` and `apply(diff)` in `tests/helpers/fake-store.js` is enough.\n- Indirect: {{F06}} (parse and serialise LiNo) and {{F16}}\n  (`handle.idFor(node)`, which maps DOM input targets to link IDs).\n- Related: {{F09}}, {{F46}}, {{F49}}, {{F63}} (anime-avatar gestures),\n  {{F64}}, {{F05}} (the Playwright harness for generated specs).\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Write `src/recorder/format.js`, which provides\n   `parseRecording(text) -> Recording` and\n   `serializeRecording(recording) -> string`. Both use `links-notation`;\n   never use regular expressions. This is the full form:\n   ```lino\n   (session-7: recording\n     (started '2026-11-01T12:00:00Z')\n     (seed 42)\n     (viewport 1280 800)\n     (document app)\n     (redacted true)\n     (event 0ms (set ok label 'OK'))\n     (event 840ms (input pointer down ok (at 12 8)))\n     (event 841ms (play press-feedback (target ok)))\n     (event 990ms (set ok label 'Saved'))\n     (event 1500ms (input key down Enter (target ok)))\n     (event 2100ms (mark 'saved once')))\n   ```\n   `serializeRecording(parseRecording(x))` must equal `x` for the canonical\n   form.\n2. Write `src/recorder/recorder.js`:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {{ store: Store, player?: Player, root?: Element, handle?: DomHandle,\n    *   clock?: { now(): number }, seed?: number, redact?: boolean,\n    *   maxEvents?: number }} options\n    * @returns {{ start(): void, stop(): string, mark(label: string): void, size(): number }} */\n   export function createRecorder(options) {}\n   ```\n   - `start()` snapshots the store and stores the snapshot.\n   - The recorder subscribes to the store, the player and DOM input events on\n     `root`, which are captured in the capture phase and passive.\n   - Each DOM target maps to a link ID with `handle.idFor`. Pointer\n     coordinates are recorded relative to the target box.\n   - `maxEvents` (default 100,000) turns the buffer into a ring buffer and\n     adds a `(truncated true)` header.\n3. Write `src/recorder/state-at.js`, which provides\n   `/** Pure. */ stateAt(recording, tMs) -> Snapshot`. It restores the\n   initial snapshot and applies every diff with time `<= tMs`.\n   `animationsAt(recording, tMs)` lists the running animations with their\n   local time, so the {{F44}} `sample()` can give the exact visual values.\n4. Write `src/recorder/replay.js`:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {string | Recording} recording\n    * @param {{ store: Store, player?: Player, clock?: ManualClock }} options\n    * @returns {{ play(): Promise<void>, pause(): void, seek(ms: number): void,\n    *   readonly time: number, readonly duration: number }} */\n   export function replay(recording, options) {}\n   ```\n   - Seeking backward uses `stateAt` from the snapshot, not undo.\n   - The clock is injected. Tests use `createManualClock()`, where\n     `advance(ms)` runs due events in order, and ties keep file order.\n   - A player seeded with the recording's `seed` reproduces procedural\n     effects such as `decipher`.\n5. Write `src/recorder/verify.js`, which provides\n   `verifyReplay(recording, { createApp }) -> { ok: boolean, mismatches: Array<{ time, expected, actual }> }`.\n   It builds a fresh app with `createApp(seed)`, dispatches only the `input`\n   events at their times on a manual clock, records again, and compares the\n   resulting `set`, `insert`, `remove` and `move` events.\n6. Write `src/recorder/to-playwright.js`, which provides\n   `toPlaywright(recording, { url }) -> string`. It generates a spec that\n   opens `url`, clicks and types at the recorded targets using\n   `[data-link-id=\"ok\"]` selectors, and asserts the recorded `set` values.\n   `mark` events become `test.step` names.\n7. Wire `examples/animation/` from {{F44}}: add Record, Stop, Replay and a\n   scrubber (`<input type=\"range\">`) that calls `seek`. Show the LiNo\n   recording in a `<pre>`.\n8. Add the optional `experiments/recorder/vs-rrweb.mjs`, the README section\n   \"Recording format\", tests and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-animation/src/recorder/{format,recorder,state-at,replay,verify,to-playwright,clock,redact}.js`\n- `packages/ui-animation/src/index.js` (exports), `src/index.d.ts`, `README.md`\n- `packages/ui-animation/tests/{recording-format,recorder,state-at,replay,verify,redact,to-playwright}.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-animation/tests/helpers/fake-store.js`, `tests/fixtures/recording-*.lino`\n- `examples/animation/{index.html,main.js}` (record and replay controls)\n- `tests/e2e/recorder.spec.js`, `experiments/recorder/vs-rrweb.mjs` (optional)\n- `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `recording-format.test.js`: `recording-1` from `samples/animation.lino`\n      and the step 1 example parse, and serialising them round-trips to\n      identical text.\n- [ ] `recorder.test.js`: a scripted session with a manual clock\n      (`set`, a pointer down on `ok`, `play`, `set`) produces exactly the\n      events and timestamps of the step 1 example.\n- [ ] 1,000 pointer moves within one second are coalesced to at most 60\n      `input pointer move` events.\n- [ ] `redact.test.js`: text typed in a `password` field is stored as `'***'`\n      by default and stored as typed when `redact: false`.\n- [ ] `state-at.test.js`: `stateAt(r, 900)` has label `'OK'` and\n      `stateAt(r, 990)` has label `'Saved'`. If every edit goes through\n`parse` → change → `format`, all comments, blank lines, indentation choices and\nthe choice between one-line, multi-line and indented forms are lost, and the\ndiff that an agent has to review (R12) becomes the whole file.\n\nThe ecosystem research names this \"gap 4: comments and layout are lost on round\ntrip\" and lists three options: (a) a concrete syntax tree (CST) upstream,\n(b) comments as links such as `(note '...')`, (c) patch-in-place using source\npositions\n([links-notation-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/links-notation-ecosystem.md),\nsection 5). Facts checked with `links-notation` 0.27.1 during planning:\n\n- Parsed `Link` objects have only `id` and `values` — **no source positions**.\n- `ParseError` has `offset`, `line`, `column` and `location { start, end }`.\n- `stripComments(text)` blanks comments but keeps every offset, so positions\n  in the stripped text equal positions in the original.\n- `StreamParser` reports positions only coarsely (a link is emitted when the\n  next record starts), so it cannot give exact spans.\n- A bare `#` starts a comment; `//` does not (it is a normal reference).\n- The formatter does not reflow nested links to fit `maxLineLength`.\n\n## Goal\n\nA JavaScript module that applies structural edits (set a prop, change text,\ninsert/remove/move a child, rename an id) to the **original text** with the\nsmallest possible text change, keeping comments and layout everywhere else,\nplus an upstream proposal for real source positions.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `indexSource(text)` → span tree that maps every element and prop of the\n  {{F06}} tree to `{ start, end }` offsets, for all three document forms.\n- Edit functions that return the new text and the list of text edits.\n- `applyOpsToSource(text, ops)` for the {{F08}} operation shape.\n- Self-check after every edit: the new text must parse to the expected tree;\n  otherwise return an error and leave the text unchanged.\n- Convention (b): `(note '...')` props are kept as data by `ui-core` and the\n  store, so comments that must survive any tool can be written as links.\n- Upstream issue draft (option a).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Writing our own full LiNo parser. [2026-11-01T11:59:28.786Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nkey: F53\ntitle: 'Interop with A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms and Lottie'\ntype: Feature\nlabels: [enhancement]\nphase: 8\nblocked_by: [F06]\nrequirements: [R6]\n---\n\n## Context\n\nR6 says any UI framework is \"just\" a LiNo document. Four JSON formats\ndescribe UIs or animations declaratively, and supporting them makes the\nframework useful to agents and existing hosts on day one\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md),\ninterop section):\n\n- **Google A2UI** (Apache-2.0) is the agent-to-UI protocol. An agent streams\n  JSON messages that describe components from a catalog as a flat list with\n  IDs, plus data-model updates. v0.8 is listed as stable and v0.9 as a draft,\n  so check the current version before starting.\n- **Microsoft Adaptive Cards** (MIT; check the repository licence) are JSON\n  cards built from `body` elements, inputs and `actions`.\n  - Schema 1.6 is current, and Teams supports up to 1.5.\n  - The host config acts as a theme.\n  - `fallback` and `fallbackText` handle versioning.\n- **JSON Forms** (MIT) pairs a JSON Schema for the data with a UI schema of\n  layouts and controls (`VerticalLayout`, `HorizontalLayout`, `Group`,\n  `Categorization`, `Control` with a `scope`, and `rule`s).\n- **Lottie** has a spec, version 1.0 from September 2024, maintained by the\n  Lottie Animation Community at the Linux Foundation. lottie-web is MIT.\n  Spec 1.0 excludes text layers, effects and expressions.\n\nThe research concludes that the dialect should be lossless to and from JSON,\nso importing these formats is mechanical. meta-sovereign already plays\nTelegram `.tgs` stickers, which are Lottie, through the lottie-web light\nbuild with no `eval`\n([meta-sovereign-chat.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/meta-sovereign-chat.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nAdd four import and export pairs to `@link-foundation/ui-convert`. Each one\nturns a format into UI-dialect LiNo and back:\n\n- A2UI messages become document diffs.\n- Adaptive Cards become documents, and host configs become themes.\n- JSON Forms become form documents.\n- Lottie becomes shapes plus animations.\n\nWithin the supported subset each pair is lossless, and outside it the pair is\nexplicit about what it lost. Actions are always data, never code.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- `importA2ui(messages)` and `exportA2ui(doc)`. A pure\n  `a2uiMessagesToDiffs(messages)` turns streamed messages into incremental\n  `set`, `insert` and `remove` diffs.\n- Adaptive Cards:\n  - `importAdaptiveCard(json)` and `exportAdaptiveCard(doc, { targetVersion })`;\n  - `hostConfigToTheme(hostConfig)`.\n- JSON Forms: `importJsonForms({ schema, uischema })` and `exportJsonForms(doc)`.\n- Lottie: `importLottie(json)` and `exportLottie(doc, animationId)`, for\n  shape layers (rect, ellipse, path, fill, stroke, group), the transform\n  properties (position, scale, rotation, opacity, anchor) and bezier\n  keyframe easing.\n- Unknown properties are preserved as `(extra <format> '<json>')`, so a round\n  trip does not drop them. Every lossy step produces a diagnostic.\n- A mapping table for each format: `src/interop/<format>/mapping.lino`.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- A2UI transport (A2A, SSE or WebSocket) and agent hosting. This issue\n  converts messages only.\n- The Adaptive Cards templating language (`${...}`). Expressions are kept as\n  literal strings and are never evaluated.\n- Lottie text layers, effects, expressions, image and audio assets, and\n  precomps beyond one level. They are rejected with a diagnostic, and\n  expressions are never evaluated.\n- Rendering. The output is LiNo; {{F16}} renders it, and {{F44}} plays the\n  animations.\n- DivKit and json-render. They could be added later in the same layout.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F06}} (blocker). Supplies the parser, the element tree and the\n  serialiser. Every importer builds a tree and serialises it with\n  `links-notation`, and every exporter walks a parsed tree.\n- Related:\n  - {{F26}}, {{F27}}, {{F29}}: the target kind names (`text`, `image`,\n    `stack`, `button`, `text-field`, `checkbox`, `select` and so on). Use\n    the names actually merged, and keep them in the `mapping.lino` files.\n  - {{F44}}: the animation format Lottie maps to.\n  - {{F39}}: the theme format for host configs.\n  - {{F17}} and {{F51}}: the other `ui-convert` importers. Share their\n    package layout and diagnostics type.\n  - {{F52}}: code exporters.\n- If `packages/ui-convert/` does not exist yet, create it with\n  `src/index.js` and `src/diagnostics.js`, and use the same layout {{F17}}\n  describes.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. Collect fixtures in `packages/ui-convert/tests/fixtures/interop/`:\n   - official sample cards from the Adaptive Cards repository;\n   - A2UI sample message streams from the A2UI repository;\n   - two JSON Forms examples (person, with a rule);\n   - three small Lottie files that use only in-scope features.\n\n   Record the source URL and licence of every fixture in `fixtures/interop/SOURCES.md`.\n2. Adaptive Cards (`src/interop/adaptive-cards/`). Map\n   `TextBlock`, `Image`, `Container`, `ColumnSet`, `Column`, `FactSet`,\n   `ActionSet`, the `Input.*` elements, `Action.Submit`, `Action.OpenUrl`,\n   `Action.ShowCard` and `Action.ToggleVisibility`.\n   - Read the version from the card's `version`.\n   - On export with `targetVersion: '1.5'`, replace newer elements with\n     their `fallback`, or drop them and keep `fallbackText`, with a\n     diagnostic.\n   - Here is the output for a card with one `TextBlock`, one `Input.Text`\n     and one `Action.Submit`:\n     ```lino\n     (card: document\n       (source adaptive-cards '1.6')\n       (body: stack\n         (title: text 'Hello' (size large) (weight bold))\n         (name: text-field (label 'Name') (bind name)))\n       (actions: stack (direction row)\n         (submit: button (label 'OK') (on press (submit card)))))\n     ```\n   - `Action.OpenUrl` becomes `(on press (open-url 'https://example.com'))`.\n     The URL is quoted because it contains `:`.\n3. `hostConfigToTheme(hostConfig) -> string`. It maps default container\n   colours, foreground colours, spacing, font sizes and font weights to\n   tokens in the {{F39}} theme format, and lists unmapped paths.\n4. A2UI (`src/interop/a2ui/`). Implement:\n   ```js\n   /** @param {object[]} messages A2UI protocol messages, in stream order\n    * @returns {{ diffs: Array<{ op: 'insert' | 'set' | 'remove', id: string, parent?: string, kind?: string, props?: object }>, diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }} */\n   export function a2uiMessagesToDiffs(messages) {}\n   ```\n   - The A2UI flat component list with child IDs maps directly onto links.\n   - Bind data-model paths as `(bind <path>)`.\n   - Read the message names and the catalog schema from the current spec,\n     and pin the supported version in `A2UI_VERSION`.\n   - `importA2ui` applies all diffs to an empty tree. `exportA2ui` produces\n     one full surface message sequence.\n5. JSON Forms (`src/interop/json-forms/`).\n   - `Control` scopes such as `#/properties/name` become `(bind name)`. In\n     LiNo the raw scope must be quoted, because `#` starts a comment.\n   - Labels, `required`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum` and `format` come from\n     the data schema.\n   - A `rule` with effect HIDE, SHOW, ENABLE or DISABLE and a `condition`\n     becomes `(rule (hide (when (bind vegetarian) (equals false))) (target diet))`.\n   - Layouts map to `stack` with `(direction column)` or `(direction row)`.\n     `Group` becomes a titled section, and `Categorization` becomes tabs.\n6. Lottie (`src/interop/lottie/`).\n   - Frame times convert to ms with `fr`.\n   - Each in-scope layer becomes a shape element.\n   - Animated transform properties become {{F44}} tracks, and bezier\n     `i`/`o` handles become `(cubic-bezier ...)` easings per key:\n     ```lino\n     (dot: shape (path 'M0 0 L10 0 L10 10 Z') (fill '#FF5500'))\n     (dot-pulse: animation\n       (source lottie '1.0')\n       (target dot)\n       (duration 1000ms)\n       (track opacity (key 0 0) (key 0.5 1) (key 1 0))\n       (track translate (key 0 '0px 0px') (key 1 '100px 0px')))\n     ```\n   - `exportLottie` writes the spec 1.0 subset. Check whether the Lottie spec\n     publishes a JSON Schema; if it does, validate the output against it in\n     the test.\n7. `src/interop/index.js` provides `detectFormat(json)`, which returns\n   `'a2ui' | 'adaptive-cards' | 'json-forms' | 'lottie' | null`. Also add\n   the CLI subcommand\n   `npx ui-convert import <file.json> [--format <name>] > out.lino` and the\n   matching `export <file.lino> --format <name>`.\n8. Write the README section with a capability matrix per format (supported,\n   partial or unsupported elements), the tests and a changeset.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- R35 asks for issues that are detailed enough for such agents. `select` uses a minimal\n  positioned listbox here and moves onto the {{F27}} popover when it merges.\n- Lists, trees, tables ({{F29}}), date and time pickers (later issue).\n- Theme packs ({{F40}}–{{F43}}) and the theme engine ({{F39}}); this issue\n  uses the default token values only.\n- Icons themselves ({{F36}}); `icon-button` takes an icon name and renders a\n  placeholder until {{F36}} merges.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F25}} (blocker): `parseMachine`, `interpret`, `createActionRegistry`,\n  `bindMachine`, `createRovingTabindex` (radio group), `createTypeahead`\n  (select), `bindKeys`, `announce`. In anime-avatar,\n  `ACS_gestureDelta(name, t, mood, easing)` is stateless. Animations built\n  this way are deterministic, so they can be scrubbed, recorded and tested.\n- **Additive layering.** anime-avatar sums deltas from every motion source\n  and applies bell or sustained envelopes, so nothing snaps\n  (https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-28).\n- **Regressions to guard against.**\n  - `animation-fill-mode: both` left `clip-path` and transforms on panels\n    after the animation ended\n    (https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/main/docs/case-studies/issue-7).\n  - A `steps(1)` white-flash flicker was a photosensitivity hazard and was\n    replaced by a breathing glow.\n- **Reduced motion.** `motionAllowed()` combines the user toggle with\n  `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\nOn libraries: WAAPI is ADOPT. Motion is MIT and optional. **GSAP is\nforbidden**, because its licence bans competing no-code animation tools\n([existing-solutions.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/existing-solutions.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nCreate `packages/ui-animation/` with four parts:\n\n1. a LiNo animation model: tracks of keyframes, easings, springs, timelines,\n   stagger, additive composition, state triggers and named procedural\n   effects;\n2. a pure evaluator `sample(animation, t)`;\n3. a compiler to WAAPI keyframes and options;\n4. a player driven by an injectable clock.\n\nReduced motion and flash safety are enforced by the model itself.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- The `animation` link with:\n  - `target`, `duration`, `delay`, `iterations`, `direction`, `fill`\n    (default `none`), `composite` (`replace`, `add` or `accumulate`) and\n    `easing`;\n  - easings: named tokens, `(cubic-bezier a b c d)`, `(steps n)` and\n    `(spring (stiffness) (damping) (mass))`;\n  - `(track <property> (key <offset> <value> [easing]))`;\n  - `(reduced-motion ...)` overrides.\n- The `timeline` link, with `(at <time> (play <id> ...))`, `(sequence ...)`,\n  `(parallel ...)` and `(stagger <step> ...)`.\n- State triggers. `(on pressed (play press-feedback))` binds to the\n  {{F12}} states `hover`, `focus`, `pressed` and `disabled`. This follows\n  the XAML VisualState pattern.\n- Value interpolation for numbers, lengths with units, colours (OKLCH, via\n  {{F07}}), opacity, `translate`, `scale` and `rotate`.\n- Effects registry. `registerEffect(name, fn)` takes pure\n  `(input, t, seed) => output` functions. The first one is `decipher`,\n  ported from immortality `textEffects.ts`, which is Unlicense.\n- Additive layers with `envelope bell` and `envelope sustain`.\n- The player: WAAPI for CSS-animatable properties, and a clock-driven frame\n  loop for effects and non-CSS properties.\n- The safety validator, which covers the fill-mode rule and photosensitive\n  flashes.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The recorder and replay ({{F45}}), the timeline editor UI ({{F49}}) and\n  Lottie import ({{F53}}).\n- Native animation output (SwiftUI, Compose and React Native `Animated`),\n  which belongs to {{F21}}, {{F23}} and {{F20}}. that file with exactly F28's signature and the\n  minimal behaviour, and F28 extends it), {{F30}} (message context menu),\n  {{F36}} (icons), {{F37}} (drawer), {{F38}} (tabs), {{F43}} (radial menu in\n  the deepcase theme), {{F57}}.\n\n## Step-by-step plan\n\n1. `src/overlays/position.js`:\n   ```js\n   /**\n    * @param {HTMLElement} anchor  or a virtual element { getBoundingClientRect }\n    * @param {HTMLElement} floating\n    * @param {{ placement?: string, offset?: number, onUpdate?: (pos) => void }} options\n    * @returns {() => void} cleanup from autoUpdate\n    */\n   export function positionFloating(anchor, floating, options) {}\n   ```\n   A virtual element at the pointer position is used by context menus.\n   CSS anchor positioning may be added as progressive enhancement (check\n   current browser support first).\n2. `dialog`: native `<dialog>`, `showModal()`, `aria-labelledby` from its\n   `title` part, the `cancel` event (Escape) dispatches `(on close ...)`,\n   focus returns to the opener. `alert-dialog` adds `role=\"alertdialog\"` and\n   no light dismiss. Example:\n   ```lino\n   (confirm: dialog\n     (title 'Delete message?')\n     (body (text 'This cannot be undone.'))\n     (actions\n       (cancel: button (label 'Cancel') (on press (close confirm)))\n       (delete: button (label 'Delete') (variant filled) (on press (emit delete)))))\n   ```\n3. `popover` and `tooltip`: `popover=\"auto\"` (light dismiss) for popovers,\n   `popover=\"manual\"` for tooltips. The tooltip opens after a delay on hover\n   or focus (timers through the {{F25}} injected clock), stays while the\n   pointer is over it and closes on Escape (WCAG 1.4.13).\n4. `menu` and `context-menu`: APG menu button pattern; arrows, Home/End,\n   typeahead, Enter/Space activate, Escape closes and returns focus, one level\n   of submenus with ArrowRight/ArrowLeft. `contextmenu` calls\n   `preventDefault()` only when the target declares a menu. The menu receives\n   the target ID separately from the current selection.\n5. `tabs`: APG tabs; roving tabindex, automatic activation by default,\n   `(activation manual)` option; `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` pairs\n   generated from link IDs.\n6. `toast` and `toaster`: a queue in a polite live region (`role=\"status\"`),\n   `(politeness assertive)` for errors, auto-dismiss duration from a token,\n   paused on hover and focus, never moves focus, at most `(max 3)` visible,\n   every toast closable (WCAG 2.2.1). `popover=\"manual\"` keeps it on top.\n7. `drawer`: `(modal true)` uses `showModal()` with a side placement;\n   `(modal false)` is a docked panel with `role=\"dialog\"` and\n   `aria-modal=\"false\"`; Escape closes both and focus returns.\n8. `radial-menu`: pure geometry in `src/overlays/radial-geometry.js`:\n   `radialLayout(count, { radius, startAngle }) -> [{ x, y, angle }]` and\n   `sectorAt(dx, dy, count, startAngle) -> index | -1`. Labels are never\n   rotated; each item shows an icon and a horizontal label. `role=\"menu\"` with\n   `menuitem` children, arrow keys move clockwise/counter-clockwise, Enter\n   activates, Escape closes. `(presentation linear)` renders the same items\n   as a normal `menu`; choose it automatically when the circle does not fit\n   the viewport. Transitions respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Story example:\n   ```lino\n   (node-menu: radial-menu\n     (radius 108)\n     (item editor (label 'Editor') (icon edit) (on select (emit open-editor)))\n     (item insert (label 'Insert') (icon plus) (on select (emit insert)))\n     (item delete (label 'Delete') (icon trash) (on select (emit delete))))\n   ```\n9. Register non-top-layer surfaces (docked drawer, toaster fallback) with the\n   layer manager.\n10. Stories in `packages/ui-components/stories/<kind>.lino` (a menu story uses\n    the Telegram Desktop message menu set: Reply, Quote and Reply, Edit, Pin,\n    Copy, Forward, Delete, Select), catalog entries in\n    `src/overlays/catalog.lino`, gallery page `e2e/pages/overlays.html`.\n\nSuggested pull requests: A popover, tooltip, dialog, drawer; B menu, context\nmenu, radial menu; C tabs, toast.\n\n## Files to create or change\n\n- `packages/ui-components/src/overlays/{index,position,dialog,popover,tooltip,menu,context-menu,radial-menu,radial-geometry,tabs,toast,drawer}.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/src/overlays/{kinds,catalog}.lino`,\n  `src/overlays/machines/*.lino`, `src/overlays/styles.css`\n- `packages/ui-components/stories/*.lino`\n- `packages/ui-components/tests/overlays/*.test.js`\n- `packages/ui-components/e2e/pages/overlays.html`,\n  `packages/ui-components/e2e/overlays.e2e.mjs`\n- `packages/ui-components/package.json` (add `@floating-ui/dom`),\n  `docs/spec/vocabulary.lino` (spec PR), `.changeset/<name>.md`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `radial-geometry.test.js`: positions for 1, 3 and 11 items, sector\n      hit tests at the boundaries, and no label transform contains `rotate`.\n- [ ] `position.test.js` (with a stubbed `computePosition`): cleanup stops\n      `autoUpdate`; a virtual anchor is supported.\n- [ ] `dialog`: e2e test shows focus inside on open, Tab cycles inside,\n      Escape closes, focus returns to the opener, background is inert.\n- [ ] A {{F28}} window raised while a modal dialog is open stays visually\n      below it (e2e reproduction of deepcase-app issue 290).\n- [ ] `menu` and `context-menu`: keyboard-only e2e (Shift+F10, arrows,\n      typeahead, Escape); right click outside declared targets keeps the\n      browser menu; the handler receives the target ID, not the selection.\n- [ ] `tooltip` stays open while hovered and closes on Escape (e2e).\n- [ ] `tabs`: arrows move focus; manual mode activates only on Enter/Space.\n- [ ] `toast`: announced through the live region, never takes focus, pauses\n      on hover, closes with its close button (e2e).\n- [ ] `radial-menu`: keyboard-only e2e, and the linear fallback is used in a\n      320 px wide viewport.\n- [ ] `expectAccessible(page)` reports no violations on `overlays.html` in\n      each opened state; `screenshotMatrix` baselines (light, dark) committed.\n- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`,\n      `npm run check:duplication` pass; `@floating-ui/dom` is MIT.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\nnode --test packages/ui-components/tests/overlays/*.test.js\nnpx playwright test packages/ui-components/e2e/overlays.e2e.mjs\nnpm test && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run check:duplication\n```\n\nAttach screenshots of each open overlay (light and dark) to the pull request.\n\n## Prior art and libraries\n\n- Floating UI (MIT, https://floating-ui.com): ADOPT for positioning.\n- HTML `<dialog>` and the Popover API; The\nframework should generalise them so that every app gets the same behaviour\nfrom one LiNo schema (R2, R9, R11), and the settings panel ({{F37}}) can be\nbuilt on top.\n\nimmortality (`app/src/settings.ts`, 1560 lines, Unlicense — code may be\nported) has 49 typed settings (choice, toggle, range with\n`min`/`max`/`step`/`unit`) in 8 groups, `coerceAxisValue`, `mergeSettings`\nfor untrusted input, `diffFromDefaults`, `migrateLegacySettings` (keeps only\nvalues the user changed in v1), 12 presets, `randomizeSettings` with an\ninjected random function and locked keys, a diff-only share hash\n`#ui=<JSON {v:2,...}>`, and `applySharedLook`, which keeps the viewer's\ncomfort settings (animations, sound, volume). Known bugs: `isPresetActive`\ncompares with `JSON.stringify` (key order matters) and the list of CSS axes is\nduplicated by hand in a only, do not copy code**) uses flat\ndotted keys (`liquid.blur`, `skin.name`), a rule table (`d`, `min`, `max`,\n`u`, `o`, `c`), diff-only persistence in `localStorage`, CSS variables and\n`data-*` attributes applied **before first paint** by an injected script,\n`#settings=<JSON>` share links, comfort keys (`motion.mode`, `sound.on`,\n`sound.volume`, ...) and a test (`applied.test.js`) that every setting is used\n([konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research/konard-github-io-and-links-visuals.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`packages/ui-settings` (`@link-foundation/ui-settings`) reads a settings schema\nwritten in LiNo and provides pure functions for coercion, untrusted merging,\ndiffing, migration, presets, randomisation and share links, plus DOM\napplication before first paint and a test helper that proves every setting is\nused.\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n- Schema format (agreed with {{F37}}):\n  ```lino\n  (settings-schema: schema (version 2))\n  (appearance: section (label 'Appearance'))\n  (liquid.blur: (type range) (default 18) (min 0) (max 40) (step 1) (unit px)\n    (section appearance) (label 'Blur') (apply (css-var --liquid-blur)))\n  (theme.mode: (type choice) (default auto) (options auto light dark)\n    (section appearance) (apply (data-attr theme-mode)))\n  (motion.reduce: (type toggle) (default false) (section appearance) (comfort))\n  (accent: (type color) (default '#3390EC') (apply (css-var --accent)))\n  (preset calm (label 'Calm') (set liquid.blur 24) (set theme.mode dark))\n  (migration (from 1) (to 2) (rename blur liquid.blur) (old-default liquid.blur 12))\n  ```\n- Field types `range`, `number`, `toggle`, `choice`, `color`, `text`, and\n  `defineFieldType(name, { coerce, equals, random, format })` so apps can add\n  `vector3`, `map` or `asset` (requested by {{F63}}).\n- Values document (diff-only): `(settings (version 2) (liquid.blur 24))`.\n- Share links `#settings=<encodeURIComponent(values LiNo)>`, plus readers for\n  the old JSON formats (`#ui=` of immortality, `#settings=` of konard.github.io).\n- `(comfort)` fields: kept from the viewer when applying presets or shared\n  looks, and never randomised.\n- Binding to {{F10}}: values are overrides of element `settings` in the\n  `user` layer (diff-only by construction).\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- The settings panel UI ({{F37}}); per-site migrations ({{F58}}, {{F64}}).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- {{F10}} (blocker): `createConfig`, `set('user', 'settings', Create `packages/ui-settings/package.json`\n   (`\"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-settings\"`), dependencies `ui-core`,\n   `ui-config` (workspace).\n2. `src/schema.js`: `readSchema(text) → { schema, diagnostics }`;\n   ```js\n   /** @typedef {{ key: string, type: string, default: unknown, label?: string, section?: string,\n    *   min?: number, max?: number, step?: number, unit?: string, options?: string[],\n    *   comfort: boolean, apply: Array<{ cssVar?: string, dataAttr?: string }> }} SettingField */\n   /** @typedef {{ version: number, fields: Map<string, SettingField>, sections: Section[],\n    *   presets: Map<string, Preset>, migrations: Migration[] }} SettingsSchema */\n   ```\n   Report unknown types, defaults that fail their own coercion, duplicate keys.\n3. `src/coerce.js`: `coerce(field, raw) → { ok, value }` — clamp ranges, round\n   to `step`, choices must be members, colours must be `#rrggbb`, toggles accept\n   `true`/`false`. Port from immortality `coerceAxisValue`.\n4. `src/values.js`: `defaults(schema)`, `merge(schema, base, untrusted) →\n   { values, rejected: string[] }` (drops unknown keys and invalid values, never\n   throws), `diff(schema, values)`, `isDefault`, `reset(schema, values, keys?)`,\n   `countCustomized`, `equalValues` (structural, order-independent).\n5. `src/presets.js`: `applyPreset(schema, values, id)` (keeps comfort fields),\n   `activePreset(schema, values)` using `equalValues` (fixes the key-order bug).\n6. `src/random.js`: `randomize(schema, values, { random, locked = new Set() })`;\n   `random` is required (no `Math.random` inside); comfort and locked fields\n   are unchanged.\n7. `src/migrate.js`: `migrate(schema, stored)` applies `rename`, then drops\n   values equal to the `old-default` of their version (so users get new\n   defaults, as immortality does), then `merge`.\n8. `src/codec.js`: `toLino(schema, values)` (diff only, sorted by schema\n   order), `fromLino(schema, text)`, `fromLegacyJson(schema, json)`,\n   `toShareHash(schema, values)`, `fromShareHash(schema, hash, viewerValues)`\n   — rejects input over 8 KiB, merges as untrusted, keeps viewer comfort\n   values.\n9. `src/dom.js`: `applyToRoot(schema, values, root)` sets\n   `--liquid-blur: 18px` and `data-theme-mode=\"auto\"`;\n   `beforePaintScript(schema, { storageKey })` returns the source of a small\n   inline script that reads stored values, validates them with the serialised\n   rule table and applies them before first paint; `beforePaintScriptHash()`\n   returns its `sha256-...` for a Content Security Policy.\n10. `src/testing.js`: `assertEverySettingUsed(schema, { css, sources })` —\n    each field has an `apply` target found in the CSS text, or its key appears\n    in one of the given source strings; the error lists unused keys.\n11. `src/config.js`: `bindConfig(config, schema, { target = 'settings' })`.\n12.
